- Analysis Codes are used to group related Pay Codes that share similar characteristics (for example, grouping all absence-related pay codes under "Absence Management" or all basic pay elements under "Basic Pay")
- Every Pay Code must be assigned to an Analysis Code
- Analysis Codes are organised by Analysis Types, which are the main categories used for payroll reporting and financial system integration

**The eight Analysis Types are:**
- GP (Gross Pay)
- NT (Non-Taxable)
- DN (Deduction)
- TR (Tax Relief)
- NP (Nett Pay)
- EN (Employer Pension)
- ER (Employer NI/PRSI)
- AL (Apprentice Levy)

## What you'll be able to do:

1. **Access the Analysis Code screen** — Navigate to the right location in the system and view all existing codes and their details
2. **Filter Analysis Codes** — Use filtering options to search by code, description, analysis type, or pay type
3. **Add new Analysis Codes** — Create custom codes (up to 4 digits) with descriptions to suit your organisation's needs
4. **Delete Analysis Codes** — Remove codes that are no longer needed

The guide also explains that PeopleXD comes with pre-configured Analysis Codes that can be customised, and that these codes are essential for payroll reporting, data extraction, and posting information to your financial management system.
ss: Analysis Codes in PeopleXD's payroll system group related Pay Codes by their characteristics—such as Basic Pay or Absence Management—and must be assigned to a specific Analysis Type (Gross Pay, Deduction, Tax Relief, etc.) that determines how payroll data posts to your Financial Management System and appears on reports. Open this guide when you need to add, duplicate, or delete Analysis Codes within the Settings menu, or when configuring how pay elements are categorized for payroll processing, reporting, and General Ledger posting. This document covers the Analysis Code screen interface, filtering options, and step-by-step instructions for managing codes in CorePortal.
sl: This user guide explains how to configure Analysis Codes within a payroll system, covering the fundamental purpose of these codes and the specific processes required to manage them. Analysis Codes are organizational tools that group Pay Codes with similar characteristics—such as grouping adoption leave under "Absence Management" or basic hours under "Basic Pay"—and every Pay Code must be assigned to an Analysis Code associated with one of nine specific Analysis Types (including GP for Gross Pay, DN for Deductions, TR for Tax Relief, EN for Employer Pension, and others). To access and manage Analysis Codes, users navigate to Settings > Codes > Analysis Code, where they can view the Analysis Code Screen displaying fields for the code itself, its description, Analysis Type, Pay Type, and an Overtime Indicator. The document provides step-by-step instructions for adding new Analysis Codes by entering a unique 4-digit code and a description (maximum 30 characters), selecting the appropriate Analysis Type from the defined list, and optionally enabling the Overtime Indicator for overtime-related codes. Users can also filter the Analysis Code Screen by Analysis Code, Description, Analysis Type, or Pay Type to locate specific entries, and can delete codes through the three-dot menu. Analysis Types serve the critical function of organizing major headings on the Payroll Update Control Report and enabling payroll journal posting to the Financial Management System (FMS), while the codes themselves support data extraction for management reporting and General Ledger posting. Access to these configuration screens requires the specific menu permission "Pay Settings - Analysis Code" within CorePortal, making this guide essential for payroll administrators and system configuration specialists who need to set up or maintain custom Analysis Codes beyond PeopleXD's pre-configured defaults.

t: Configure Auto Enrolment
s:
# Summary of "Configure Auto Enrolment" Guide

This guide teaches users how to set up and configure the auto enrolment feature in the PeopleXD HR system's payroll module. 

**What you'll learn:**

The guide explains auto enrolment, which is a UK government requirement for employers to automatically enrol eligible employees into a workplace pension scheme and make pension contributions. It covers who qualifies (employees aged 22 to State Pension Age who earn above the threshold and work in the UK).

**What you'll be able to do:**

After reading this guide, you'll be able to:

- Access and configure the core auto enrolment settings in the system (via Settings > UK Tax Rates > General > Auto Enrolment)
- Set up key auto enrolment parameters including the staging period (when auto enrolment starts), minimum and maximum ages, and minimum eligibility ages
- Configure pay codes, pay groups, and pension schemes for auto enrolment purposes
- Set State Pension Ages
- Configure earnings parameters and pension contribution rules
- Set up default pension scheme rules
- Configure postponement options (delaying auto enrolment for employees)
- Set exclusion rules (preventing certain employees from being auto-enrolled)
- Configure company-level auto enrolment parameters

The guide provides step-by-step instructions for each configuration task, helping payroll administrators ensure their organisation complies with UK auto enrolment regulations through the system.
ss: Auto Enrolment is a UK government requirement that automatically enrolls eligible employees into a workplace pension scheme, and this guide explains how to configure it in your payroll system. You'll learn how to set up auto enrolment parameters including staging periods, age thresholds, earnings eligibility, pension schemes, and pay codes—all within the Settings > UK Tax Rates > General menu. Open this document if you need to configure which employees qualify for auto enrolment, define pension scheme rules, set up postponement or opt-out periods, or exclude specific pay codes and pay groups from earnings calculations. This is essential for payroll administrators setting up auto enrolment compliance for the first time or adjusting existing configurations.
sl: This document is a user guide that provides comprehensive instructions on configuring auto enrolment within a CoreHR payroll system, covering the setup of parameters required to manage the UK government's mandatory workplace pension scheme initiative. The guide explains that auto enrolment requires eligible UK employers to automatically enrol qualifying staff into a workplace pension scheme and make contributions, with eligible employees being those aged 22 to State Pension Age who earn above the earnings threshold and work in the UK. The main configuration tasks are accessed through Settings > UK Tax Rates > General > Auto Enrolment, where administrators complete fields such as Staging Period, Auto Enrolment Min Age, Auto Enrolment Max Age, Minimum Eligible Jobholder Age, Re Enrolment Years, and Default Pension Scheme, along with toggles for Multipost Aggregate Earnings and Postpone Pension Enrolment based on Employee Start Date. The document then details seven additional configuration screens accessible via an Options dropdown list, including Configure Pay Code Options (section 2.2, which involves enabling Non-Qualifying indicators on pay codes to exclude them from earnings calculations), Configure Pay Group Options (section 2.3, relevant for multi-country companies), Configure Pension Scheme Options (section 2.4, which references verification against the Pension Regulator's criteria), Configure State Pension Ages, Configure Earnings Parameters, Configure Pension Rules (including subsections for Setting Default Pension Scheme Rules, Postponing Pension, and Excluding employees), and Configure Company Parameters. The guide is designed for payroll administrators and HR professionals responsible for implementing auto enrolment compliance within their organization, helping them resolve configuration issues such as handling negative allowances or multi-post employee earnings aggregation.

t: Configure Cost Centres
s:
# Summary: Configure Cost Centres Guide

This guide teaches users how to set up and manage cost centres in the PeopleXD HR system's payroll module.

**What you'll learn:**

- **What cost centres are:** Organizational units (typically departments) used to allocate and track employee costs such as salaries and expenses for accounting purposes. These codes link to your company's financial management system.

- **How to add a new cost centre:** Navigate to Settings > General Ledger Costing > Cost Centres, then enter a unique cost code (up to 13 characters), a description (up to 30 characters), and optional details like activity codes, client references, and sub-headings.

- **How to edit an existing cost centre:** Modify cost centre details as needed.

- **How to disable a cost centre:** Deactivate cost centres that are no longer in use.

- **How cost centres work in practice:** Each employee is assigned a default cost centre through their contract, but the system allows you to temporarily reassign costs to different cost centres as needed (for example, if an employee covers for someone in another department).

- **Where to access cost centre management:** Through the Settings menu under General Ledger Costing, and how cost centres can also be managed through employee cost allocations in People Management.

The guide essentially provides step-by-step instructions for creating, modifying, and managing the organizational cost codes that the payroll system uses to allocate employee expenses across different departments or business units.
ss: Cost Centres in PeopleXD are organizational units used to allocate employee costs and salaries for accounting purposes, and they must align with your Financial Management System setup. This guide covers how to add, edit, and disable cost centres through the Settings > General Ledger Costing menu, including optional fields like activity codes and client references. Open this document if you need to configure new cost centres for different departments, manage existing centre codes, or understand how employee costs are charged to specific business units. You'll also find the required menu permissions needed to access the Cost Centre screen from CorePortal.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions on configuring cost centres within the PeopleXD payroll system, which are units within a company to which employee costs such as salary and expenses are allocated for cost accounting purposes. The document explains that cost centre codes are interfaced into the Financial Management System (FMS) and can be accessed through the Settings > General Ledger Costing > Cost Centres menu path. The guide covers three main maintenance tasks: adding a new cost centre by entering a unique cost code (maximum 13 characters) and description (maximum 30 characters) along with optional fields such as Activity Code, Client Reference, and Sub Heading; editing an existing cost centre by accessing the three-dot menu and updating relevant data; and disabling a cost centre by toggling the Active Indicator. Each cost centre record displays multiple fields including Cost Centre code and description, Activity code and description, Client Reference, Subhead, Active Indicator, and BIK Indicator, allowing organizations to configure cost centres for different departments and allocate employee costs accordingly. The system also enables flexible cost allocation through features like Cost Allocations, Timesheet Current Period, and Pay Code configuration, allowing companies to temporarily reassign an employee's costs to different departments—for example, reallocating a marketing executive's salary to a sales cost centre during periods of leave coverage. Payroll administrators and HR personnel who need to set up and maintain cost centre structures for accurate financial tracking and employee cost allocation would typically use this document.

t: Configure Expense Codes
s:
# Summary: Configure Expense Codes Guide

This guide teaches users how to set up and manage Expense/GL Codes in the PeopleXD HR system's payroll module.

**What you'll learn:**

- **What Expense Codes are**: These are accounting codes used to categorize and group employee pay transactions so they can be recorded in the general ledger (GL) as debits and credits on profit & loss and balance sheet accounts. They're 8-digit numbers that aren't tied to individual employees but rather to types of pay and employee categories.

- **How to add a new Expense Code**: Navigate to Settings > General Ledger Costing > Expense/GL Codes, then click Add. You'll enter an 8-digit code, provide a description (up to 30 characters), optionally assign a tax code, and activate the code. You can also choose to hide it from employee timesheets if needed.

- **How to edit an existing Expense Code**: Access the code through the same menu path, use the three-dot menu to select Edit, update the relevant fields, and save your changes.

- **How to disable an Expense Code**: Deactivate codes by turning off the "Active Indicator" — though the guide warns you should only do this if the code isn't currently in use.

- **Key context**: Expense Codes work alongside Cost Centres and can be used across multiple departments. The same Expense Code can apply to different employee types and pay elements.
ss: Expense/GL Codes in CoreHR's payroll module are used to categorize and post employee pay elements to the general ledger as debits and credits for accounting purposes. This guide covers how to add, edit, and disable expense codes within the Settings > General Ledger Costing menu, including how to configure fields like description, tax code, and visibility settings. Open this document if you need to set up new expense codes, modify existing ones, or understand how expense codes work with cost centres in your payroll system. You'll also find the required menu permissions needed to access the Expense/GL Codes configuration screen.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions on configuring Expense/GL Codes within the CoreHR payroll system, which are numerical codes used to categorize and post employee salary transactions to the general ledger as debits and credits. The document explains that Expense Codes are 8-digit number fields (up to 12 digits maximum) that summarize transactions into expense and liability groups for P&L and Balance Sheet postings, and can be used across multiple Cost Centres regardless of individual employee assignment. To access and manage these codes, users navigate to Settings > General Ledger Costing > Expense/GL Codes, where they can add new codes by entering the code itself, a description (maximum 30 characters), an optional Tax Code, and toggling the Active Indicator and "Do Not Display on ESS Timesheet" indicator as needed. The guide details three key operational tasks: adding new Expense/GL Codes via the Add button, editing existing codes through the three-dot menu option, and disabling codes by toggling the Active Indicator off (with a caution to verify codes are not in use before deactivation). Each Expense/GL Code record displays standardized fields including Expense Code, Description, Tax Code, Active Indicator, and the ESS Timesheet display setting, and the system supports data mapping to align CoreHR output with Financial Management System (FMS) requirements. Payroll administrators and system configuration users typically use this document when setting up or maintaining the chart of accounts structure and cost allocation framework within their organization's CoreHR instance, requiring the "Settings - Expense/GL Codes" menu option for access.

t: Configure Organisations
s:
# Summary: Configure Organisations Guide

This guide teaches users how to set up and manage organisations and companies within the PeopleXD Payroll system.

**What users will learn:**

- **Understanding organisations**: An organisation can contain multiple independent companies, each with unique company codes. Companies are linked to pay groups, and users must have access to a company to access its associated pay groups.

- **Core organisation management tasks**: The guide covers four main operations:
  - Adding a new company/organisation
  - Editing existing company details
  - Copying (duplicating) an existing company
  - Deleting a company

- **What can be configured for each organisation**: Name, address and contact details, company registration number, revenue details, pay periods, associated pay codes, bank details, and payroll calendar.

- **Copying companies as best practice**: Users learn that copying an existing company is the most efficient way to create a new company, as it pre-populates most settings and requires only updating a few key fields such as company code and contact information, rather than configuring everything from scratch.

- **Company-specific details to configure**: When setting up or copying a company, users learn how to enter optional fields including registered number, contact person, phone/fax numbers, interface company code, email address, currency code, and payroll provider.

- **System navigation**: Users learn where to access these functions (Settings tab on the Payroll Dashboard, then the Organisations section).
ss: Configuring Organisations in PeopleXD Payroll covers how to set up and manage companies within your payroll system, including adding, editing, copying, and deleting organisations. The guide walks you through maintaining essential details like company codes, payroll parameters, pay periods, bank details, and payroll calendars that control how each company operates independently. You'd open this document when setting up a new company in your payroll system, duplicating an existing company structure to save time, or updating organisational settings like pay codes, banking information, or PAYE rates. It's essential reading for payroll administrators responsible for establishing the foundational company structure in PeopleXD before processing payroll.
sl: This document is a user guide for configuring organisations within the PeopleXD Payroll system, providing comprehensive instructions on how to set up and maintain company structures within the platform. The guide explains that an organisation may consist of multiple independent companies, each with unique company codes and linked pay groups, accessible through the Payroll Dashboard by clicking the Settings tab and then the Organisations option. The document covers four main operational tasks: adding a new organisation, editing an existing one, copying a company (which is recommended as best practice to save processing time), and deleting organisations, with copy operations allowing users to amend specific fields such as Company Code, Contact Details, Registered Number, Currency Code, and Country Code. The guide details the mandatory and optional fields that must be configured during company setup, including general settings like Company Code, Payroll Period, and Pay Periods, as well as critical pay codes for PAYE, National Insurance/PRSI, salary, and nett pay deductions. Additional configuration sections accessible through the Select Detail dropdown menu include Payroll Parameters (covering banking details, academic year settings, tax rates, and cost centre validation), Payroll Calendar, and Miscellaneous Parameters, with Payroll Parameters also accessible independently from the Payroll Dashboard under General Settings. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and system configuration specialists who need to establish the foundational organisational structure and company parameters that support all downstream payroll processing activities in PeopleXD.

t: Configure Pay Group Access
s:
# Summary: Configure Pay Group Access

This guide teaches users how to manage payroll administrator access to specific pay groups within the PeopleXD HR system.

## What You'll Learn:

**Understanding User Access in Payroll**
The guide explains that user access in the payroll system operates on two separate levels:
1. **Menu Profiles** — which control what functionality and features a user can see (dashboards, screens, buttons, menu options)
2. **Data Access** — which controls what actual records a user can view and work with (employees, pay groups, salaries)

Both are required for payroll administrators to do their jobs effectively.

**Pay Group Access Basics**
Pay Group Access is the data-level control that restricts payroll administrators to only see employees and process payrolls for specific pay groups they've been granted access to. This is useful when organizations have multiple pay groups and need to limit what different staff members can manage. For example, an administrator might have access to only one pay group, while another has access to all three, or temporary access might be granted to cover for absent colleagues.

**Practical Tasks You Can Perform**
The guide covers step-by-step instructions for:
- Granting users access to specific pay groups
- Removing pay group access from users
- Accessing the Pay Group Access configuration screen through the Settings tab

The guide also notes that Pay Group Access applies to HR Administrators on the People Management Dashboard as well, for controlling access to employee salary information.
ss: Pay Group Access controls which payroll data payroll and HR administrators can view and manage in CoreHR, allowing organizations to restrict user access to specific pay groups on the Payroll and People Management Dashboards. This guide walks you through granting individual users access to one or more pay groups and removing access when no longer needed. Use this document when you need to set up payroll administrator permissions, temporarily grant access to cover staff absences, or revoke pay group access from users. The process involves navigating to Settings > Codes > Pay Groups Access and using filters to assign or remove pay group permissions at the individual user level.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for managing Pay Group Access within the CoreHR Payroll system, enabling administrators to control which payroll data individual users can access and modify. The document explains that user access in CoreHR operates across two categories—Menu Profiles (which control system functionality and navigation) and Data Access (which controls visibility of actual records including employees, pay groups, and salaries)—and that Payroll Dashboard users require configuration in both areas. Pay Group Access specifically operates at the pay group level, allowing payroll administrators to be granted access to all pay groups in an organization or restricted to specific pay groups, including temporary assignments to cover absences. To configure Pay Group Access, administrators navigate to Settings > Codes > Pay Groups Access in the CorePortal and must ensure the "CorePortal Pay Settings - Pay Groups Access" menu option is enabled for the user, along with specific webservice menu options for getting and managing paygroup data. The guide provides step-by-step procedures for granting user access by filtering by username, adding new rows, selecting the required pay group from a dropdown menu, specifying the username and Input Location (mandatory field), and saving the configuration so the pay group becomes available on the user's Payroll Dashboard. The document also covers the process for removing pay group access, though the specific removal steps are truncated in the provided text, and notes that Pay Group Access configuration is similarly applicable for HR Administrators managing employee salary and allowance records on the People Management Dashboard.

t: Configure Pay Groups
s:
# Summary: Configure Pay Groups Guide

This guide teaches users how to manage pay groups in the PeopleXD HR system. 

**What is a Pay Group?**
A pay group is a grouping mechanism used to organize employees who share the same pay frequency (weekly, fortnightly, monthly, etc.). All employees within a pay group are processed together for payment. Every employee must be assigned to a pay group, and each pay group must be linked to a company.

**What You'll Learn to Do:**

1. **Set up access permissions** — Enable or disable user access to the Pay Group configuration screen through the system menu option "CorePortal Pay Settings - Pay Groups"

2. **Add a new pay group** — Create a pay group by entering required information including:
   - A unique code for the pay group
   - A description (up to 30 characters)
   - Pay frequency (weekly, fortnightly, monthly, 4-weekly, or bi-monthly)
   - Wages or salary indicator
   - Tax year start period
   - Input periods and completed periods for payroll tracking
   - Current payroll period
   - Maximum hours threshold for employees in that group

3. **Edit an existing pay group** — Modify pay group settings

4. **Duplicate a pay group** — Copy an existing pay group to create a similar one

5. **Delete a pay group** — Remove a pay group from the system

All these tasks are performed through the Settings > Codes > Pay Groups menu in the system.
ss: Pay Groups in CorePortal organize employees who share the same pay frequency so they can be processed together during payroll runs. This guide covers the complete setup process: adding new pay groups, editing existing ones, duplicating configurations, and deleting them from Settings > Codes > Pay Groups. You'll need this document when configuring payroll parameters like pay frequency (weekly, fortnightly, monthly), maximum hours and gross/net pay thresholds, pay period hours, and other mandatory fields required to link employees to a pay group. Open this if you're responsible for payroll administration and need to create or modify how your employees are grouped for payment processing.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for configuring pay groups within the Access payroll system, covering the complete lifecycle of pay group management from creation through deletion. The document explains that a pay group is used to organize employees who share the same pay frequency, ensuring they are processed together for payment, and clarifies that every employee must be linked to a pay group and each pay group must be linked to a company. Users access pay group configuration through Settings > Codes > Pay Groups menu path, with access controlled by the CorePortal Pay Settings - Pay Groups system menu option that, when enabled, provides full view and edit access to the Pay Groups screen. The guide walks through four key maintenance tasks: adding a new pay group (which requires completing mandatory fields marked with red asterisks including unique code, description, pay frequency indicator, wages/salary indicator, and various period fields), editing existing pay groups, duplicating pay groups, and deleting pay groups. The document details critical configuration fields such as Pay Frequency Indicator (W, F, M, 4, or B), Start Period, Input Period, Completed Input period, Completed Update period, Payroll Period, and threshold limits including Maximum Hours, Maximum Gross, and Maximum Nett that trigger alerts on the payroll observation report. Additional configurable parameters include Pay Period Hours, Pay Period Days, Days in Year (used for converting annual rates to hourly equivalents using a specific formula), and optional indicators for Annual Allowance, Validation Bypass, and Pay on Timesheet Only. This document is intended for payroll administrators and system configuration users who need to establish and maintain the foundational pay group structures that govern how employee payments are processed within the organization.

t: Configure Payslip Locations
s:
# Summary: Configure Payslip Locations Guide

This guide teaches users how to set up and manage payslip locations in the PeopleXD HR system's payroll module.

**What payslip locations are:** For organisations with employees across multiple locations, payslip locations allow employers to automatically generate and organise payslips by location. This eliminates the need to manually sort payslips after printing. Payslips can be distributed to employees' home addresses, work locations, cost centres, or other defined locations.

**What users will learn to do:**

- **Add a new payslip location** — Navigate to Settings > Codes > Payslip Location, click Add, and enter a unique location code (up to 8 digits), a description (up to 30 characters), and up to three address lines, then save.

- **Edit an existing payslip location** — Access the same menu, click on the field to be changed, overwrite the data with new information, and save.

- **Delete a payslip location** — Select the location to be deleted, click the delete button, and save. The guide emphasises checking that no employees are currently assigned to that location before deleting, as this will cause error messages in employee records.

- **Sort and customise the payslip location screen** — Click column headers to sort the list in ascending or descending order, and optionally show or hide columns. Note that these changes apply only to the current session and will not be saved.
ss: Payslip Locations in the Payroll system allow employers with multiple employee locations to generate and distribute payslips organized by location, eliminating the need for manual sorting after printing. This guide walks you through adding, editing, deleting, and sorting payslip location codes in the Settings > Codes > Payslip Location menu, where each location includes a code, description, and address details. Open this document if you need to set up new payslip distribution locations, modify existing location information, or remove locations that are no longer in use. You'll also find instructions for organizing the payslip location list by different columns to suit your workflow.
sl: This document is a user guide for configuring payslip locations within the Payroll system, designed for employers who need to organize payslip distribution across multiple employee locations. The guide explains that payslip locations enable employers to generate and sort payslips by location rather than manually sorting them after printing, with payslips distributable to an employee's home address, work location, cost centre, or other defined locations. All configuration tasks—adding, editing, deleting, and sorting payslip locations—are performed by navigating to Settings > Codes > Payslip Location on the Payslip Location screen. When adding a new location, users must enter a unique location code (maximum 8 digits), a description (maximum 30 characters), and three address line fields, then save using the green Save button; editing requires clicking the specific field to modify and saving changes. The guide addresses an important error scenario: deleting a payslip location that is still assigned to employees will generate an error message in the employee record indicating the location is invalid or missing, so users must verify that no employees are assigned to a location before deletion. Additionally, users can sort the payslip location list by any column header in ascending or descending order and can customize which columns display, though these sorting preferences reset to default settings when the screen is reopened. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and managers who manage multi-location employee payroll operations.

t: Configure Payslip Logos
s:
# Summary: Configure Payslip Logos Guide

This guide teaches HR administrators how to add company logos to payslips in the PeopleXD Payroll system. 

**What you'll learn:**

- **Logo technical requirements** — Logos must be in JPEG format with specific dimensions: 200px wide by 100px tall for portal payslips, and 275px wide by 50px tall for copy payslips. They must also meet specific resolution (96 dpi) and bit depth (24) requirements. Files exceeding these specifications will cause payslip generation to fail.

- **System setup** — How to configure the Logo Upload widget on a dashboard (typically the Administrator Dashboard) and how to grant the necessary security access so that users can upload logos by enabling the "Employee Document Upload" menu option in security settings.

- **Upload process for portal payslips** — Step-by-step instructions for uploading a logo that will appear on payslips employees view in the portal, including selecting the correct options from dropdown menus, assigning the logo to specific companies and pay groups, and locating the image file to upload.

- **Upload process for copy payslips** — How to upload a separately formatted logo for printed payslip copies.

The guide emphasizes that only system administrators should have access to perform these configurations, and that the process must be repeated for each company using the system.
ss: Payslip logos in PeopleXD Payroll are company-specific images that appear on both portal and copy payslips generated for employees. This guide covers uploading logos through the Administrator Dashboard, setting up the required Logo Upload widget, granting security permissions, and meeting strict file requirements (JPEG format only, specific pixel dimensions per payslip type). Open this document when you need to add your organization's branding to payslips or troubleshoot logo upload issues in PeopleXD.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive user guide for configuring and uploading company logos within the PeopleXD Payroll system to display on employee payslips. The guide covers the entire setup process, including configuring a Logo/Template Upload widget (typically added to the Administrator Dashboard), granting security access through the Quick Jump > Security > Menu Profiles section by enabling the "Employee Document Upload" menu option, and uploading logos to two distinct payslip formats. Logo files must meet specific technical requirements: JPEG format only, with dimensions of 200px width by 100px height for portal payslips and 275px width by 50px height for copy payslips, along with 96 dpi resolution and 24-bit color depth, as oversized files will cause payslip generation to fail. The document details two separate upload processes accessed via Administrator Dashboard > Logo Upload, where users select the Image Type as "Logo," choose either "Portal Payslip Logo" or "Copy Payslip Logo" from the Location dropdown, assign a unique name to each logo, select the relevant company, optionally specify a Pay Group, and locate the image file to upload. System administrators are the primary users of this document, as they are responsible for managing logo uploads and must complete the process individually for each company within the organization. The guide also warns that duplicate logo names will generate error messages and that security access restrictions may result in "Access Denied" errors if proper permissions are not configured beforehand.

t: Configure Pension Schemes
s:
# Summary: Configure Pension Schemes Guide

This guide teaches users how to set up and configure pension schemes in the PeopleXD CoreHR payroll system.

**What you'll learn to do:**

- Understand the basics of pension scheme configuration and how pension schemes work within the organisation
- Access pension scheme settings in the system (via the Settings tab in CorePortal Pay)
- Create new pension schemes by adding and configuring all necessary pension scheme parameters

**Key configuration details covered:**

The guide walks through the step-by-step process of setting up a pension scheme, including how to:
- Enter a unique pension code and description
- Select a pension scheme type (such as Group Defined Benefit, Group Defined Contribution, Salary Sacrifice, or Non-Standard Contribution schemes)
- Configure mandatory settings like the renewal period (tax week when the pension year starts)
- Set up optional deduction details, including:
  - Fixed deduction values for employees
  - Percentage-based deductions (with the option to use up to 3 different employee percentage rates)
  - Employer contribution percentages and multipliers
  - Social welfare deduction rules
- Specify reckonable days of service

**Additional context:**

The guide notes that employees can be assigned to multiple pension schemes, and that pensions can be assigned either through the HR or Payroll function depending on organisational requirements. It also explains how system access permissions affect user access to the pension scheme configuration screens.
ss: Pension Schemes in CoreHR are configured through the Settings > Codes > Pension Scheme menu to set up different pension types such as Group Defined Benefit, Group Defined Contribution, Salary Sacrifice, and Additional Voluntary Contribution (AVC) schemes. The configuration requires defining mandatory fields like Renewal Period (Tax Week), Scheme Type (Contributory or Non-Contributory), and Calculate Only settings, along with optional fields for deduction percentages, employer contributions, and social welfare deductions. You would open this guide when setting up new pension schemes for your organization or assigning multiple schemes to employees, whether through HR or Payroll depending on your requirements. Use this document to understand how to configure employee and employer deductions, pay codes, and scheme-specific parameters that align with your organization's pension rules.
sl: This document is a user guide for setting up and configuring pension schemes in the CoreHR payroll system, designed for payroll administrators and HR professionals who need to establish pension arrangements according to organizational requirements. The guide explains that pension schemes can include various types such as Additional Voluntary Contribution (AVC) schemes, Group Defined Benefit or Contribution schemes, and Salary Sacrifice arrangements, with employees potentially assigned to multiple schemes simultaneously. To access pension scheme configuration, users must navigate to Settings > Codes > Pension Scheme in CorePortal Pay, where the Pay Settings - Pension Scheme menu option controls whether users have full view and edit access or receive a restricted access message. The configuration process requires entering mandatory fields including a unique Pension Code, Description (maximum 50 characters), Company name (maximum 40 characters), Renewal Period in Tax Weeks, and Scheme Type (Contributory or Non-Contributory), along with numerous optional fields such as Pension Scheme Type, employee and employer deduction percentages, reckonable days, and employer contribution multipliers. The document provides detailed field-by-field guidance for configuring Employee Pay Codes (Deduction 1-3, Pre-Tax Adjustment, and Pre-Tax AVC) and Employer Pay Codes (Adjustment and Deduction), explaining how these map pension calculations to specific pay codes for reporting and analysis. Additional features covered include the ability to set Primary schemes that prevent employees from joining other schemes, enable PRSA schemes, apply Social Welfare Deductions to pensionable pay, and configure whether pension values should be calculated only or both calculated and deducted from employee pay.

t: Configure Project Codes
s:
# Summary of "Configure Project Codes" Guide

This guide teaches users how to set up and manage Project Codes in the PeopleXD HR system's payroll module.

**What you'll learn:**

The guide explains that Project Codes are used to assign employee salary costs to specific projects for accounting and cost tracking purposes. It covers the practical steps for three main tasks:

1. **Adding a new Project Code** — Users learn how to create a Project Code by entering a unique code (up to 12 digits) and description (up to 30 characters), plus optional information like client reference, analysis code, activity code, rate, cost centre, and budget value. Users must activate the code to make it available.

2. **Editing an existing Project Code** — Users can update any Project Code's details by accessing it through the Projects menu, using the edit option, making changes, and saving.

3. **Disabling a Project Code** — Users can deactivate codes they no longer need, though the guide warns that deactivating codes with currently assigned employees will cause system errors.

The guide also explains that Project Codes work alongside employee contract assignments, allowing organisations to flexibly allocate pay to different projects and track costs in their Financial Management Systems. The information is practical and task-focused, aimed at HR administrators who need to maintain project coding structures in the system.
ss: Project Codes in the payroll system allow organizations to charge employee costs to specific projects for cost centre sub-analysis in Financial Management Systems. Use this guide to add, edit, or disable Project Codes through Settings > General Ledger Costing > Projects, including how to assign optional details like client references, analysis codes, and budget values. Open this document when you need to set up new projects that employees will be assigned to, update existing project information, or deactivate projects (with caution, as this can trigger payroll errors if employees are still assigned). The guide covers the complete configuration process and the menu permissions required for payroll staff to access the Project Code screen.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for configuring Project Codes within a payroll system, enabling organizations to charge employee costs to specific projects for financial tracking and analysis. Project Codes allow temporary project assignments to be tracked separately from an employee's primary cost centre, and are typically used for cost centre sub-analysis in Financial Management Systems (FMS), with assignments made through the HR employee contract or via Cost Allocations, Timesheet Current Period, and Pay Code configuration. The document walks users through accessing the Projects screen via Settings > General Ledger Costing > Projects, where they can view all configured codes and their associated fields including Project Code, Description, Client Reference, Analysis Code, Activity, Rate, Cost Centre, Budget Value, Recoup Indicator, and Active Indicator. The guide details three primary maintenance tasks: adding a new Project Code (which requires a unique code up to 12 digits and description up to 30 characters, with optional fields for client reference, analysis code, activity code, rate, cost centre, and budget value), editing an existing code through the three-dot menu, and disabling codes via the Active Indicator toggle. The document explicitly warns that deactivating a Project Code while employees are still assigned to it will generate errors on employee records, during payroll validation, and when generating the General Ledger, requiring careful management of the Active Indicator status. Payroll administrators and HR configuration users who manage project-based cost allocation and need access to the Pay Settings - Project Code menu option in CorePortal will use this document.

t: Configure Statutory Payments (UK)
s:
# Summary: Configure Statutory Payments (UK)

This guide teaches users how to set up and manage UK statutory payment types within the PeopleXD Payroll system. After reading it, users will be able to:

**Configure Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) Rates:**
- View, edit, and add new SSP rates in the system
- Manage rate types, weekly rates, and upper/lower limits
- Update rates as they change each year

**Configure Multiple Types of Statutory Payments:**
The guide covers setup for six main statutory payment schemes:
- Statutory Maternity Pay (SMP)
- Statutory Paternity Pay (SPP) and Additional Statutory Paternity Pay (ASPP)
- Statutory Adoption Pay (SAP)
- Statutory Sick Pay (SSP)
- Shared Parental Leave
- Redundancy payments

**Configure Payment Parameters and Settings:**
Users will learn how to establish parameters for:
- Ordinary Statutory Parental Pay (OSSP)
- Keep In Touch Days
- Average pay calculations and pay days
- Statutory recovery parameters
- Redundancy-specific parameters
- Other general statutory payment settings

The guide provides step-by-step instructions for accessing configuration screens through the Payroll Dashboard Settings tab, where users can input and maintain all the necessary parameters to ensure the payroll system correctly calculates and processes statutory payments for employees on leave or facing redundancy.
ss: Statutory Payments (UK) in PeopleXD Payroll covers the configuration of all UK-mandated employee payments including Statutory Maternity Pay (SMP), Paternity Pay (SPP), Adoption Pay (SAP), Sick Pay (SSP), and Redundancy. This guide walks you through setting up SSP rates, configuring parameters for each payment type, establishing qualifying days and waiting periods, and managing thresholds like maximum SSP weeks and PIW (Period of Incapacity for Work) limits. Open this document when you need to initially set up or update statutory payment rules in your payroll system, or when UK legislation changes and you need to adjust payment rates or eligibility criteria.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive guidance for configuring statutory payments in PeopleXD Payroll, a system used by UK payroll administrators to manage employee payments during absences due to illness or parental reasons. The document covers configuration of multiple statutory payment types including Statutory Maternity Pay (SMP), Statutory Paternity Pay (SPP), Statutory Adoption Pay (SAP), Ordinary Statutory Parental Pay (OSSP), Shared Parental Leave, Redundancy, and Statutory Sick Pay (SSP). For SSP rates, users access the Payroll Dashboard Settings tab and use the Maintain SSP Rates screen to view pre-configured annual rates, edit existing rates by entering data in fields such as Weekly Rate, Lower Limit, Upper Limit and Standard Rate, or add new rate types by clicking Add. For statutory pay parameters, all configuration is performed on the General screen accessed via Settings > UK Tax Rates > General, where users complete mandatory fields (marked with red asterisks) specific to each payment type. The OSSP configuration section specifically addresses fields such as CoreTime Work Pattern override, Qualifying Days, Period of Incapacity for Work (PIW) settings including minimum days, maximum link days, and years limit, SSP weeks limit (defaulting to 28 weeks but adjustable if legislation changes), retirement ages by gender, SSP pay code selection, and Timesheet Interface integration settings. This document is essential for payroll professionals responsible for setting up and maintaining accurate statutory payment calculations within the PeopleXD Payroll system to ensure compliance with UK employment legislation.

t: Configure the Payroll Calendar
s:
# Summary: Configure the Payroll Calendar Guide

This guide teaches users how to set up and manage payroll calendars in the PeopleXD HR system. After reading it, users will understand and be able to:

**Core Concepts:**
- What a payroll calendar is and why each company needs one
- How payroll calendars break the year into numbered weeks (formatted as YYYYWW) and track period end dates for different pay frequencies (weekly, fortnightly, four-weekly, and monthly)
- That payroll calendars do not track payment dates but can have period end dates offset at the pay group level

**Key Tasks:**
- Add a new payroll calendar
- Edit an existing payroll calendar
- Duplicate a payroll calendar
- Amend dates within a calendar
- Build or rebuild a calendar for a year

**Administrative Setup:**
- How to grant users access to the calendar configuration screens through the Settings tab using the "Pay Settings - Calendars" menu option
- The difference between enabled access (full view and edit) and disabled access

**Technical Details:**
- How to navigate to the Payroll Calendars screen (Settings > Company Parameters > Payroll Calendars)
- Understanding the data fields displayed: week numbers, tax periods, calendar periods, and week end dates
- Knowledge that calendars come pre-configured during software setup but may need editing, and that additional week 53/fortnight 27 entries can be added when needed
ss: Payroll calendars in PeopleXD must be generated and configured for each company to track period end dates for weekly, fortnightly, four-weekly, and monthly pay groups. This guide covers how to add, edit, and duplicate payroll calendars, as well as how to amend dates and build calendars for new years. Open this document if you need to set up a new payroll calendar, modify existing calendar dates for special circumstances like leap years or week 53, or copy a calendar structure from one year to the next. You'll also find details on user access permissions required to manage calendars through the CorePortal Settings tab.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions on configuring and maintaining payroll calendars in the Access payroll system, specifically covering how to add, edit, and duplicate payroll calendars for companies within an organisation. The document explains that payroll calendars must be generated for each company and consist of the year broken into week numbers (formatted as YYYYWW), tracking period end dates for weekly, fortnightly, and four-weekly pay groups, while monthly pay groups always end on the last day of the month. Users access the Calendar configuration screen via Settings > Company Parameters > Payroll Calendars and require the CorePortal Pay Settings - Calendars menu option to have full view and edit access, otherwise a restricted access message will appear. The guide details multiple calendar fields including Week Number, Tax Period, Calendar Period, Week End Date, Production Week, Monthly Sequence, Quarterly Sequence, and specific indicators (FNtly Ind., 4 Wkly Ind., Monthly Ind., and Multi Run) that designate when payroll runs occur and whether multiple pay periods should be processed together. The document addresses common scenarios such as leap years or years requiring week 53/54 by explaining the Amend Dates function, which allows users to add or subtract days across specified periods, and the Build/Rebuild Year function, which enables copying a calendar from one year to the next using a base year as a template. This guide is typically used by payroll administrators and system configuration staff who need to set up and maintain accurate payroll calendars in PeopleXD software.

t: Configure the Payroll Dashboard
s:
# Summary: Configure the Payroll Dashboard Guide

This guide teaches users how to set up and configure the Payroll Dashboard in the PeopleXD HR system.

**Key topics covered:**

**Access and Permissions:**
- Understanding default menu profiles that grant full payroll admin access
- Creating custom menu profiles to control what different users can see and do
- Setting up read-only access for specific users
- Duplicating existing profiles to speed up configuration

**Dashboard Navigation and Features:**
The guide explains how to configure access to all major sections of the Payroll Dashboard:
- **Manage Payroll Tab** — options for running payroll using either a 5-step or 3-step process, plus managing payroll inputs, checking payroll data, and viewing outputs
- **Employee Tab** — accessing employee-related functions
- **Enquiry Tab** — running queries and lookups
- **Uploads Tab** — importing payroll data in bulk
- **Predefined Reports Tab** — accessing pre-built reports
- **Settings Tab** — configuring company parameters, payroll codes, pay rates (for both UK and Ireland), banking details, and general settings
- **Pay Rates section** — viewing, adding, and bulk updating pay rates by employee or position, plus updating allowances scale rates
- **Year End Tab** — end-of-year payroll functions

After reading this guide, users will understand how to configure user access levels, customize which dashboard features are available to different roles, and manage the various payroll configuration settings within the system.
ss: The Payroll Dashboard in CorePortal uses Security Menu Profiles to control user access to payroll functions, tabs, and screens—it cannot be configured through the standard Dashboard Configuration screen. This guide provides detailed instructions for assigning and customizing Menu Profiles for CorePortal users, including how to use the default "CorePortal_Pay_Admin" profile or build custom profiles from scratch. You'll open this document when you need to set up user permissions for payroll tasks like running payroll, managing employee information, accessing reports, or configuring tax rates and pay scales. Use it whenever you're onboarding payroll users or need to adjust what dashboard features and menu options specific users can see.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions on configuring access to the Payroll Dashboard within the CorePortal system for different user roles and permission levels. The document explains that Payroll Dashboard configuration is managed entirely through Security Menu Profiles rather than the Dashboard Configuration screen, as the dashboard is functional with fixed tabs that cannot be reordered or removed. The guide covers the default menu profile "CorePortal_Pay_Admin," which grants full access to all Payroll Dashboard options, and explains how administrators can build custom menu profiles by duplicating and editing existing profiles or creating new ones from scratch. It details all available menu options across multiple tabs including Manage Payroll (with 5-step and 3-step payroll processing options, Inputs, Payroll Checking, and Outputs tabs), Employee, Enquiry, Uploads, Predefined Reports, Settings (covering Company Parameters, Codes, Pay Rates, UK Tax Rates, Ireland Tax Rates, Banking, and General settings), and Year End tabs. The document specifically addresses menu configuration for running payroll processes, managing pay rates through bulk updates by employee or position, handling allowances scale rates, and performing year-end legislative tasks and system rate updates. This guide is intended for payroll administrators and system configuration specialists who need to set up appropriate access levels for CorePortal users while controlling visibility of specific payroll functions and data entry screens.

t: Configure the Task List
s:
# Summary: Configure the Task List Guide

This guide teaches users how to set up and customize the Task List feature in the PeopleXD HR system's Payroll module.

**What you'll learn:**

- **Understanding the Task List**: The Task List is a workflow system built around two pre-configured payroll schedules — a 3-step process and a 5-step process. These contain mandatory system tasks (like Salaries & Allowances, Payroll Validation, and Confirm Timesheets) that must be completed in a specific order.

- **Adding custom tasks**: You can add additional manual tasks to your task list beyond the pre-configured system tasks. Examples include "View Gross to Net" or "Print Payslips." These custom tasks appear on your checklist but don't become part of the main automated payroll process.

- **Managing access**: You'll learn how to grant users permission to access and modify the Task Manager through system menu options.

- **Editing the Task List**: The guide covers practical configuration tasks including how to add new tasks, reorder existing tasks, rename tasks, and delete tasks from your list.

In essence, this guide enables payroll administrators to customize their payroll workflow by adding manual checkpoints and organizational steps while maintaining the integrity of the required system-driven payroll processes.
ss: The Payroll Task List in CorePortal allows you to customize the sequence of payroll processing steps by adding manual tasks to the pre-configured 3-Step or 5-Step Payroll Schedule. You can add new tasks like "View Gross to Net" or "Print Payslips," reorder them, rename them, or delete custom tasks through Settings > General > Task Manager—though system tasks cannot be modified. Open this guide when you need to set up additional checkpoints in your payroll workflow, configure task notifications for multiple payroll administrators, or manage the order of manual tasks that require sign-off before closing a payroll period.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for configuring the Payroll Task List within the Access payroll system, specifically detailing how to customize task workflows and manage payroll processing sequences. The document explains that the system offers two pre-configured payroll schedules (3 Step and 5 Step Payroll Schedule) with mandatory system tasks such as Salaries & Allowances, Payroll Validation, and Confirm Timesheets that must be processed in a fixed sequence and cannot be modified. Users can add custom manual tasks to the task list by navigating to Settings > General > Task Manager, selecting a pay group, and using the Add button to create new entries with specified positions and task descriptions, with an optional notification email address field for multi-user payroll environments. The document covers the impact of adding new tasks, including how they appear in the Manage Payrolls tab and affect the payroll completion progress indicator, and explains that while system tasks complete automatically, additional manual tasks require manual completion through enabled indicators on the task checklist. Configuration access is controlled through the CorePortal Pay Settings - Task Manager menu option, which must be enabled to allow full view and edit access to the Task Manager screen. The guide also provides detailed editing procedures for manually created tasks, including how to reorder tasks using position numbers or arrow buttons, rename task descriptions, and delete custom tasks—all operations that are restricted for system-defined tasks. Once all tasks are marked complete, the Overall Signoff button becomes active and closes the current payroll period, automatically opening a new payroll period in the task list.

t: Disk Exchange
s:
# Summary of "Disk Exchange" Guide

This guide teaches users how to use the Disk Exchange module within the PeopleXD Payroll back office system to manage deduction and pension data transfers with third parties.

After reading this guide, users will be able to:

- **Maintain Data Load Control** — set up and manage the framework for data imports
- **Load deduction files** — import deduction details and pension/AVC scheme information from external sources in a specified format into the payroll system
- **Amend loaded data** — make corrections and modifications to imported data, including performing global deletions where needed
- **Update deduction and pension details** — modify both normal deductions and pension scheme information after they've been loaded
- **Validate loaded data** — run validation checks to ensure the imported data is accurate and complete before processing
- **Generate output files** — create and export files containing deductions taken from employees to send back to third parties in the required format

The guide also provides technical specifications including file naming conventions, file format requirements, and information about the specific forms and reports used in the Disk Exchange process.

In essence, this is a tool for managing bidirectional data exchange — receiving deduction information from external providers and sending deduction records back out in a standardized format.
ss: Disk Exchange in PeopleXD Payroll enables you to load deduction and pension scheme files from external sources into the payroll system and generate deduction output files to return to third parties. The process involves loading data files, validating the information, amending any errors, and updating employee deduction or pension details in a controlled manner. Open this guide when you need to import or export employee deduction data, set up pay codes for batch processing, or troubleshoot data validation errors during the deduction file exchange process. It covers all steps from initial data load through final validation and output file generation.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for using the Disk Exchange module within PeopleXD Payroll's back office system, which handles the import and export of deduction and pension data files. The document covers six main operational processes: Maintain Data Load Control, Load Deductions File, Amend Loaded Data, Update Deduction/Pension Details, Run Data Load Validation, and Generate Output Deductions File. To access Disk Exchange, users navigate to CorePay > Employee > Employee Deductions > Disk Exchange and can then configure pay codes and pension schemes through the Maintain Data Load Control function, which requires setting a Department ID, specifying valid Pay Codes or Pension Schemes, and designating whether values are periodical or weekly amounts through the Value Status field. The Load Deductions File process accepts two types of deduction files—normal deductions and pension schemes—from third-party systems in a specified format, loading them into an intermediate payroll table while generating validation reports, though users must keep Pay Codes and Pension Schemes on separate records to avoid system errors. The guide is primarily used by payroll administrators and back-office staff who need to manage employee deductions, pension contributions, and deduction-related data transfers between external systems and the PeopleXD Payroll platform. The appendix provides essential technical specifications including file naming conventions, file format requirements for both input deduction files and output deduction files, and lists of relevant forms and reports used throughout the processes.

t: Employee Self-Service Widgets
s:
# Employee Self-Service Widgets Guide Summary

This guide teaches HR administrators and users how to manage and use the Employee Self-Service (ESS) payroll widgets in the PeopleXD system. Here's what you'll learn:

## Dashboard Setup
How to customize the employee dashboard by creating, editing, and deleting tabs, plus how to add payroll widgets to those tabs for easy employee access.

## Payslip Management (My Payslip Widget)
How employees can view their payslips and current pay rates through a dedicated widget. The guide covers both user-facing features and administrator configuration options for controlling access and display settings.

## Bank Account Details (My Bank Account Widget)
How employees can view and update their bank account information through the system. This section includes extensive configuration options for administrators, such as:
- Controlling whether bank account numbers are visible or hidden
- Managing display of building society details
- Setting up password authentication requirements for changes
- Configuring email notifications when bank details are updated

## Tax Information (Tax Details Widget)
How employees can access their tax details through a dedicated widget, along with configuration instructions for administrators.

## P60 Documents (P60 Documents Widget)
How employees can access their P60 annual tax documents (section appears to continue beyond the provided text).

Overall, the guide serves as both a user manual for employees navigating these payroll self-service features and a configuration guide for HR administrators setting up and controlling these widgets.
ss: Employee Self-Service (ESS) Widgets enable payroll self-service functionality through CorePortal, allowing employees to view and manage their own payroll information without HR intervention. The guide covers six key widgets: My Payslip (for viewing payslips and current pay rates), My Bank Account (for editing bank details), Tax Details, P60 Documents, PRD60 Certificates, and Important Dates. Open this document if you need to configure these widgets on employee dashboards, understand how employees use them to access payroll data, or set up specific features like bank account visibility and password authentication. This is essential for payroll administrators and system implementers managing employee self-service capabilities in CorePortal.
sl: This user guide provides a comprehensive overview of Employee Self-Service (ESS) widgets available in the CorePortal payroll system, designed to enable employees to access and manage their payroll information through a self-service portal. The document covers configuration of the Employee Dashboard, including how to edit, delete, and add tabs, as well as how to add widgets to those tabs through the dashboard interface. It details six primary payroll widgets: the My Payslip Widget (for viewing payslips and current rates of pay), the My Bank Account Widget (for editing bank details with options to hide or show account numbers and display building society details), the Tax Details Widget, the P60 Documents Widget (including language customization), the PRD60 Certs Widget, and the Important Dates Widget. For each widget, the guide provides both user instructions and configuration guidance, including access controls, CorePortal parameters, and in the case of bank account changes, password authentication settings and email notification options. The document references CorePortal as the underlying system and includes configuration details such as payslip parameters and bank account parameters that administrators need to implement to enable widget functionality. This guide is intended for both end users who need to navigate these widgets and administrators responsible for configuring access and parameters within the payroll system.

t: Ireland
s:
# Summary of the Ireland HR Guide

This guide teaches users how to manage the Enhanced Joiners and Rejoiners payroll process in the PeopleXD HR system, specifically for Irish payroll operations.

**Key areas covered:**

**Salary Approvals** — Users will learn how to view salaries awaiting approval and either approve or reject salary and allowance information.

**Processing New Joiners** — The guide explains how to identify employees awaiting joiner processing, use the Joiners screen, and filter or search for specific joiners. Users will learn how to process individual joiners or handle multiple joiners in bulk, as well as how to export joiner lists to Excel, set default values, and view Irish tax details for new employees.

**Processing Rejoiners** — Similar to joiners, this section covers identifying and processing employees returning to the organisation. Users will learn how to access the Rejoiners screen, use filters and search functions, amend pay group information, and process individual rejoiners or multiple rejoiners in bulk.

**System Administration** — The guide includes information on granting user access to these screens and which menu profiles and options need to be enabled.

**Overall outcome** — After reading this guide, users will be able to manage the complete enhanced payroll onboarding process for both new joiners and returning rejoiners in Ireland, including approvals, processing, filtering data, and bulk operations.
ss: The Enhanced Joiners and Rejoiners feature in PeopleXD Payroll streamlines how you onboard new employees and rehire returning staff into your payroll system after they've been set up in People Management. This guide covers processing salary approvals, joining employees individually or in bulk, and rejoining employees while managing their pay group assignments. Use this document when you need to process new starters, returning employees, or review outstanding salary approvals in your Irish payroll operations. You'll also find instructions on configuring the enhanced_jml_enable parameter and granting user access to these payroll processing screens.
sl: This user guide for XD Payroll describes the Enhanced Joiners and Rejoiners feature in PeopleXD Payroll, which streamlines the process of onboarding new employees and rehiring former employees into the payroll system. The document covers three primary functional areas: Salary Approvals (which provides visibility of outstanding salary approvals), Joiners (which allows individual or bulk processing of employees after setup in People Management, including the ability to set default values for mandatory fields and view tax details via the Irish Tax Details Screen), and Rejoiners (which enables bulk rejoining of former employees while also allowing amendment of their Pay Group assignments before processing). Users can filter and search employee records on the Joiners Screen and Rejoiners Screen, export lists to Excel through the Actions Menu, and process employees either individually or in bulk, with all actions tied to payroll run requirements. The enhanced process requires enabling the enhanced_jml_enable parameter through the Administrator Dashboard and Site Manager widget's Admin Settings, and inclusion of rejoiners depends on configuration of the Synchronisation of Joiner and Rejoiner Process indicator in People Management. This guide is intended for payroll administrators and HR personnel in Ireland who need to manage employee onboarding, rejoining, and salary approval workflows within the PeopleXD system, with access controlled through Menu Profile permissions and specific menu options.
