# Summary of "Occupational Absence Enhancements" Guide

This guide teaches PeopleXD HR system users how to configure and use new features for managing occupational absence (primarily sick pay) in their organisation.

## Main Topics Covered

**First Anniversary Pro Rata Enhancements**
Users will learn how to set up rules that handle absence during an employee's first year of service. Specifically, you can configure the system to:
- Ignore any sick leave taken before an employee reaches their first work anniversary, so those absences don't count against their occupational sick pay entitlement
- Set which month the first anniversary period should begin and end
- Automatically calculate pro-rata (adjusted) sick pay entitlements based on when the employee started

**Closed Periods Enhancements**
Users will learn how to create and manage occupational closure calendars within the system. This allows you to:
- Add closure calendars to define periods when your organisation is closed
- Add specific closed date periods to these calendars
- Assign categories to the calendars so the system can properly account for these non-working periods when calculating absence

## How to Use This Guide

The guide provides step-by-step instructions for accessing the relevant configuration screens in the PeopleXD Back Office system and explains what each setting does, using examples to illustrate how the rules work in practice.
ss: Occupational Absence Enhancements covers new features in the Workforce Management (WFM) system for configuring how occupational sick pay is calculated and managed. The guide walks through three main enhancements: ignoring absences that occur before an employee's first anniversary, setting pro-rata entitlement periods based on anniversary dates, and managing closed periods for absence calculations. Use this document when you need to configure occupational absence rules in CoreTime Back Office, particularly if you're setting up sick pay eligibility rules, anniversary-based entitlements, or closure calendars. It's essential for HR and payroll teams managing occupational sick leave policies in the Access Group system.
sl: This guide documents enhancements made to the Occupational Absence Configuration screens within the Access Group's Workforce Management system, specifically covering First Anniversary Pro Rata features and Closed Periods functionality. Users access these enhancements through Back Office by navigating to CoreTime/CoreRoster > System Parameters > Reference A-C > Absence Pay Parameters > Absence Rules, where they search for their company and select More against the desired rule to reach the Configuration screen. The First Anniversary Pro Rata Enhancements section explains three configurable settings: the "Ignore Absence Prior to First Anniversary" option which excludes any sick leave starting before an employee's one-year anniversary from occupational sick pay calculations, the "First Anniversary Start/End Month" fields which allow administrators to define the month range for pro-rating occupational sick entitlement from the first anniversary until the end of the sick year, and the "Service First Anniversary Entitlement Pro Rata" setting which determines when entitlement calculations occur relative to service anniversaries. The Closed Periods Enhancements section describes the Occupational Closure Calendars screen and provides step-by-step instructions for adding closure calendars, adding closed periods to those calendars, and assigning categories to them. The document includes four detailed scenarios demonstrating how the "Ignore Absence Prior to First Anniversary" setting affects employee entitlements under different date combinations, helping payroll and workforce management professionals understand the practical implications of enabling or disabling this feature. This resource is designed for HR and workforce management teams using the People XD system who need to configure occupational absence rules specific to their organizational requirements.

# Summary of "Overlapping Leave and Absence Requests" Guide

This guide teaches users how to understand and work with the Overlapping Warnings feature in the PeopleXD HR system's Time & Attendance module.

## What You'll Learn:

**Core Feature Understanding:**
The guide explains how overlapping warnings work — a system that alerts managers and approvers when they're processing leave or absence requests that conflict with other activity in their team. Specifically, the warnings notify approvers if a leave request overlaps with:
- An absence or approved leave request from another team member
- A pending (un-actioned) request from another team member  
- A previously rejected request from the same employee

**Configuration:**
You'll learn how to set up the overlapping warnings feature, including:
- How to add and configure the Time and Attendance Settings widget to your dashboard
- How to access the Absence Warning Configuration screen where settings are customized
- What security permissions are needed to access these features

**Practical Use:**
You'll understand how to view overlapping warnings in the system, specifically through the My Approvals screen, and see multiple real-world examples of different overlap scenarios (such as rejected request overlaps, team absence overlaps, and combinations of multiple overlapping conflicts).

**Important Limitations:**
The guide clarifies that overlapping warnings are informational alerts only — they don't prevent approvers from approving or rejecting requests, and they only apply to sick absences when they go through an approval process, not when directly entered on employee records.
ss: The Overlapping Warnings feature in WFM Time alerts approvers when an employee's leave or absence request overlaps with rejected requests, team absences, or pending requests for other employees in their approval scope. This guide covers how to configure the warning system through the Time and Attendance Settings widget, set security permissions, and customize which overlap scenarios trigger alerts based on absence types and pay codes. Open this document if you need to enable or disable overlapping leave warnings, configure which types of overlaps should alert approvers, or understand how the system displays these warnings during the leave request approval process.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive documentation of the Overlapping Warnings feature within WFM Time v28, a workforce management system that alerts approvers to potential scheduling conflicts during the leave and absence request approval process. The document covers configuration procedures accessed through the Time and Attendance Settings widget and Absence Warning Configuration screen, which is made available on the Administrator Dashboard by adding the Time and Attendance Settings widget and ensuring appropriate Menu Profile permissions including "CorePortal – Time and Attendance Settings" and "Absence Warning Configuration" menu options. The overlapping warnings system triggers alerts when a leave request overlaps with rejected requests for the same employee, un-actioned requests from other team members, or previously approved absences or leave requests from colleagues within the approver's remit, but importantly these warnings are informational only and do not prevent approval or rejection. Configuration is managed globally through the Absence Warning Configuration screen, where administrators can enable or disable specific warning scenarios including rejected request overlaps, different absence type or pay code overlaps, and team absence or unactioned request overlaps, with granular control available through Personalised Pay Code Groups to limit which leave types trigger warnings. The document includes five specific warning configuration indicators with detailed explanations of when each warning displays, practical examples demonstrating how overlapping scenarios function, and important notes that sick absence warnings only trigger when submitted through an approval process rather than directly entered on employee records. This guide is primarily used by system administrators configuring the warning system and approvers who encounter these warnings on the My Approvals screen during their daily operations.

# Summary of the Period Closure Configuration User Guide

This guide teaches HR administrators how to use the Period Closure feature in the PeopleXD Workforce Management system to manage company-wide closure periods.

## What you'll learn:

**Core functionality:** How to set up and manage periods when the company is closed (such as Christmas holidays or summer shutdowns). The system automatically deducts the appropriate leave from employee entitlements during these periods.

**Key tasks covered:**

1. **Setting up a Period Closure** — A four-step process involving:
   - Adding a new period closure
   - Creating criteria groups (to define which employees are affected)
   - Assigning those criteria groups
   - Retrieving the relevant employees

2. **Managing existing Period Closures** — Including:
   - Viewing and editing closures (with or without pay frequency settings)
   - Copying existing closures
   - Retrieving employee lists
   - Viewing exceptions and administrator alerts
   - Deleting closures or specific absence records
   - Notifying employees about the closure

3. **Accessing and viewing** — How to locate the Period Closure screen and view all configured closures

4. **System administration** — How to import and configure menu options

The guide also includes FAQs to answer common questions about the feature.
ss: Period Closure in Workforce Management (WFM) enables administrators to pre-book company closure periods—such as Christmas or summer shutdowns—and automatically deduct the relevant leave from employee entitlements. Open this document when you need to establish a new closure period, assign it to staff, view or edit existing closures, or notify employees of pre-booked leave deductions. sl: This user guide for Access Group's Workforce Management system provides comprehensive instructions on configuring and managing the Period Closure feature, which allows administrators to pre-book company closure periods such as Christmas or summer shutdowns and automatically deduct relevant leave from employee entitlements. This guide is designed for workforce administrators and HR personnel who need to manage company-wide closure periods while ensuring compliance with employee working schedules, preventing over-booking of leave, and maintaining accurate entitlement tracking.

s:
# Summary

This guide explains how to use the **Pro Rata Length of Service Increments** feature in PeopleXD's Time and Attendance system.

After reading this guide, you will understand:

- **What pro rata length of service increments are** — a system feature that allows anniversary-based service increments (additional annual leave days) to be calculated proportionally rather than as a full amount

- **When and how to use this feature** — it applies when employees start or leave mid-year, ensuring they receive only the portion of their service increment that corresponds to the time they actually worked that year

- **How the calculation works** — the system can calculate the pro rata amount based on:
  - Days
  - Weeks
  - Months
  
  The system takes the period between an employee's anniversary date and the end of the leave year, applies their full-time equivalent (FTE) rate, and rounds according to configured rules

- **Configuration requirements** — you need to set up the feature via the Balance Parameters screen in Backoffice, and it only works when the "Length of Service – Calculate On" parameter is set to either "Anniversary" or "Post Appointment Anniversary"

- **Practical examples** — the guide includes five worked examples showing how the calculations apply to full-time and part-time employees using different calculation bases

The guide essentially teaches HR system administrators how to configure and understand pro rata service increment calculations for fair leave entitlements.
ss: Pro Rata Length of Service Increments in CoreTime calculates anniversary-based service increment entitlements for employees on a proportional basis using dates, weeks, or months. This functionality applies the employee's FTE (full-time equivalent) to service increment awards and is configured through the Balance Parameters screen in CoreHR's Backoffice system. Use this guide when you need to understand how to set up or troubleshoot service increment calculations for part-time or full-time employees whose anniversary dates don't align with your annual leave year, or when employees leave mid-year.
sl: This user guide document explains the Pro Rata Length of Service Increments functionality within the CoreHR Time and Attendance system (version 28), which enables organizations to prorate anniversary-based length of service increments for employees. The feature allows service increment calculations to be based on dates, weeks, or months, taking into account the period between an employee's anniversary date and the end of the annual leave year, and applies the employee's full-time equivalent (FTE) to determine the actual increment awarded. Configuration occurs through the Balance Parameters screen accessed via Backoffice > CoreTime/CoreRoster > System Params > Balances > Parameters, where users enter a balance code and select Length of Service settings. The Pro Rata functionality is only applicable when the Length of Service – Calculate On parameter is set to either Anniversary (using the personnel master start date without considering contract history) or Post Appointment Anniversary (examining contract history and enabling additional parameters such as Use Service in Company and Exclude Leave for career breaks). The Anniversary Pro-Rata (Override) section on the Balance Parameters screen provides specific fields including Apply FTE to Service Increment (set to Current Appointment to capture FTE at the anniversary date) and Pro-Rata prior to Anniversary date (allowing selection of calculation basis: dates, weeks, or months). The document includes five detailed examples demonstrating how the pro rata calculation works for full-time and part-time employees using different calculation bases. This guide is primarily used by HR and payroll administrators in CoreHR implementations who need to configure and understand how service increments are calculated and prorated for employees at different appointment levels or with varying work patterns.

# Summary of the PeopleXD HR Reports User Guide

1. **Daily Clocking Hours** — tracks employee clock-in/out times and hours worked
2. **Pay Code Hours** — reports on hours associated with specific pay codes
3. **Pay Code Instance** — details individual instances of pay code usage (with an additional time-focused variant)

5. **Balance Details** — shows leave or entitlement balances

- Each report has its own "Manage Selections" section, enabling users to tailor the reports to their specific needs rather than viewing all data

**Role-Based Access:**
- The guide distinguishes between Admin and Manager menu options, indicating different users have different report access levels

**Important Limitation:**
- The reports do not currently support employees with multiple concurrent appointments

This guide is designed to help both administrators and managers generate workforce data and insights relevant to payroll, attendance, and leave management.
ss: PeopleXD Workforce Management Reports covers five customizable reports—Daily Clocking Hours, Pay Code Hours, Pay Code Instance, Pay Code Occurrence, and Balance Details—that help you track employee time, attendance, and pay code data. Use this guide when you need to access the Reports screen from either the WFM Admin Dashboard or Workforce Management Dashboard, set up report filters, and export data to Excel or print results. The guide walks you through managing report selections, running reports with mandatory and optional fields, and understanding what each report type displays. sl: This user guide for PeopleXD Workforce Management provides comprehensive instructions on accessing and utilizing the Reports screen, which contains five distinct report types: Daily Clocking Hours, Pay Code Hours, Pay Code Instance, Pay Code Occurrence, and Balance Details. Users can access the Reports screen through either the WFM Admin Dashboard or the Workforce Management Dashboard by selecting Reports from the left-hand menu, with the page defaulting to Daily Clocking Hours upon entry. The document explains how to use the Manage Selections feature at the top of each report screen, which allows users to add, save, and manage filter selections for frequently used reports by completing a Code and Name, setting mandatory and optional criteria, and saving the selection for future application. The process for running any report follows the same general workflow: selecting the report type from a drop-down menu, filling in mandatory fields, optionally refining criteria using additional fields, clicking Run Report, and then choosing to print or export the results to Excel. Each report type has a dedicated section describing its specific purpose and available fields, with Daily Clocking Hours allowing configuration by department, work group, or employee to track clocked hours. The guide also notes important limitations, such as reports not currently supporting Multi Appointments, and explains that the interface differs between Admin View (accessed via WFM Admin Dashboard with Org Role Access) and Manager View (accessed via Workforce Management Dashboard with Team Area Access), though the core functionality remains consistent across both security types. s:
# Summary of "Timesheet Claims" User Guide

**Understanding Timesheet Claims:**
- What timesheet claims are and how they are formed within the system
- Key concepts and essential information about how the system works
- How to navigate and use the Timesheet Claims summary screen

**System Setup and Configuration:**

1. **Creating and assigning organizational roles** – setting up role types and assigning them to users
2. **Setting up timesheet templates** – configuring templates, assigning managers and administrators to them, and understanding different claim statuses

By following this guide, an administrator will be able to fully configure the timesheet claims system so that employees and managers can begin recording and managing timesheet claims within PeopleXD.
ss: Timesheet Claims in PeopleXD Workforce Management covers the complete process of submitting, reviewing, and managing employee timesheets for payroll integration. This guide walks through initial setup tasks like creating organizational roles, configuring timesheet templates and pay codes, and assigning manager/administrator permissions, then explains how employees, managers, and administrators use the system to submit, approve, and process claims. Open this document when you need to configure timesheet claims for your organization, understand the submission and approval workflow, or troubleshoot claim statuses and payroll release procedures.
sl: This user guide for PeopleXD Workforce Management provides comprehensive documentation on timesheet claims processes, covering setup, configuration, and operational use across employee, manager, and administrator roles. Configuration requirements include seven main steps: creating and assigning organizational roles, creating and assigning timesheet templates (with associated manager and administrator assignments), enabling claims summary widgets on dashboards, configuring security menu access, setting up pay codes with workflow processes, completing optional configurations such as historical claims entry and behalf-of-employee submission, and generating timesheets with various claim handling scenarios. This document serves as the primary reference for system administrators setting up the timesheet claims module, managers and administrators processing claims within their approval workflows, and employees submitting their timesheet claims for approval and payroll integration.

t: Transferring Leave and Balances
s:
# Summary: Transferring Leave and Balances Guide

This guide teaches users how to use the automated leave and balance transfer feature in the PeopleXD HR system when an employee moves to a new appointment (future-dated replacement).

**What you'll learn:**

The guide explains a new automated process that eliminates manual work when transferring an employee's leave entitlements and absence records from their previous appointment to a new one. Previously, HR staff had to manually:
- Calculate remaining entitlements and assign them to new balances
- Adjust carried-over days or hours
- Re-enter future-dated absence records
- Ask employees to resubmit leave requests

**What you'll be able to do:**

After reading this guide, you'll be able to:

1. **Enable the feature** — Turn on the "Transfer Future Leave" toggle in the WFM Admin Dashboard's General Settings

2. **Transfer leave for an employee** — Navigate through People Management to access an employee's contract, select "Replace Contract," and choose the "Transfer Balance" option in the new Balance section

3. **Understand the transfer process** — Know what happens automatically when the transfer date arrives: the previous appointment's balance is pro-rata calculated, the new appointment's balance is set up, remaining entitlements are carried forward with supporting notes, and any scheduled leave or absences on or after the new start date are automatically transferred to keep employee calendars current

The guide includes practical examples to illustrate the transfer process and explains the constraints of the system.
ss: When an employee moves to a new appointment in WFM, their leave balances and future-dated absence records automatically transfer from their old contract to the new one—eliminating the need to manually recalculate entitlements, adjust carryover days, or re-enter leave requests. This guide covers how to enable the Transfer Future Leave feature in the WFM Admin Dashboard and then use the Replace Contract function in People Management to process the transfer. Open this document if you need to understand how leave and balance transfers work during an appointment replacement, or if you're setting up the automated transfer functionality for the first time.
sl: This user guide provides instructions for managing the automatic transfer of leave balances and absence records when an employee transitions from one appointment to another using the Future Dated Replacement functionality in Access's Workforce Management system. The document explains that the transfer feature eliminates manual processes previously required, such as manually calculating remaining entitlements, adjusting carried-over days or hours, re-entering absence records, and requesting employees to resubmit leave requests. To use this functionality, administrators must first enable the "Transfer Future Leave" toggle in the WFM Admin Dashboard under General Settings, then navigate to People Management > Command Centre > Employee Search to access the relevant employee record, select Contracts, and click Replace Contract followed by Apply, which reveals a new Balance section where administrators select "Transfer Balance" as the required option. When the future transfer date is reached, the system automatically calculates pro-rata entitlements on the previous appointment's balance, assigns or pro-rata calculates the new appointment's balance, applies remaining entitlements to carryforward with supporting narratives, and transfers any leave or absence records starting on or after the new appointment date. The guide includes two detailed examples showing how balances are calculated and transferred when an employee moves between appointments with different annual leave entitlements, demonstrating the pro-rata reduction of entitlements based on the portion of the year worked. HR administrators are the primary users of this document, as they manage employee appointment changes and rely on the system's automated balance transfer process to maintain accurate leave records across appointment transitions.

t: Trigger Points
s:
# Summary: PeopleXD HR System "Trigger Points" User Guide

This guide teaches users how to use the Trigger Points feature in the PeopleXD Workforce Management system, which automatically monitors and alerts people when employees' absence patterns require attention.

## Key Learning Outcomes

After reading this guide, users will understand:

**What Trigger Points Do:**
- Monitor individual employee attendance records against pre-set criteria
- Generate automatic alerts when employees reach defined absence thresholds
- Track various absence patterns including cumulative days off, number of absence spells, combinations of both, and specific patterns

**Types of Triggers:**
The system supports four main trigger types: Sum Rule, Daily Rule, Reminder Rule, and Occupational Sick Leave Rule

**Common Alert Scenarios:**
- When cumulative absences exceed a threshold within a set period
- When multiple absence spells occur within a period
- When fit notes or medical certificates are due
- When staff are returning from planned leave
- When an employee's pay rate changes due to long-term absence

**How to Use the Feature:**
- How to enable the Trigger Points widget in the system
- How to configure trigger point rules and set custom parameters
- How to organize rules into groups
- How to view, manage, and toggle trigger notifications on and off
- How to send notifications via email and through employee/manager self-service portals

**Role-Based Access:**
The guide explains different access levels and capabilities for administrators (who set up triggers), managers (who receive alerts), and employees (who are notified when triggers activate).
ss: Trigger Points in Workforce Management allows administrators to set up automated alerts that monitor employee attendance patterns and absence records. You use the Trigger Points widget to create and configure rules—such as Sum Rules, Daily Rules, Reminder Rules, and Occupational Absence Entitlements Rules—that generate notifications when employees reach predefined thresholds for sickness absence, pattern changes, or other attendance events. These notifications can be sent via email and PeopleXD to managers, HR administrators, and employees based on roles you define. Open this guide when you need to enable the Trigger Points widget, create new absence monitoring rules, or configure who receives attendance alerts in your system.
sl: This document is a comprehensive user guide for the Trigger Points feature within Access Group's Workforce Management system, designed to help administrators, managers, and employees understand how to configure and use absence monitoring alerts. The guide explains that trigger points are primarily used to highlight sickness absence levels and patterns requiring attention, with examples including cumulative days absent in a set period, number of spells, pattern-related absences, and notifications for fit notes or pay rate changes. To set up triggers, administrators must enable the Trigger Points Widget through Dashboard Configuration by selecting Administrator Dashboard, choosing the desired dashboard (such as Site Manager), and activating the Trigger Points toggle under Tab Widgets. The system supports four main rule types—Sum Rule (for cumulative absence days or combinations), Daily Rule (for pattern-based absences on particular days), Reminder Rule (for event notifications), and Occupational Absence Entitlements Rule (for pay rate change notifications)—each with different configuration settings accessible through the Trigger Point Rule Configuration Screen. Once configured, the Trigger Points Widget displays all existing rules with their Rule ID and Rule Description, and allows administrators to edit rules, copy rules, create new rules, and organize them into Rule Groupings that can be attached to employees, work groups, or set as company defaults. The notifications generated by these triggers are sent to definable roles including employees, managers, and HR administrators through both email and self-service portals in PeopleXD, with the administrator controlling who receives notifications and what information is included.

s:
# Summary: Weekly Timesheets Guide

This guide teaches users how to use the **Weekly Timesheet Configuration feature** in the PeopleXD HR system's Workforce Management (WFM) module.

## What You'll Learn:

**Key Capabilities:**
- Access the Weekly Timesheet Configuration screen through the WFM Admin Dashboard
- Configure what payroll timesheet information displays to employees, managers, and administrators
- Choose up to three lines of additional information to show on the timesheet (with one line available only in the Portal version)
- Optionally display payslip pay code descriptions alongside the standard WFM pay code descriptions
- View the number of hours worked against each pay code for a given period

**Who Can Use It:** The feature is menu-profile driven, meaning access is controlled based on user role (Admin, Manager, or Employee), and it's available in both the Portal and Native App versions.

The guide provides step-by-step instructions for navigating to the configuration screen and explains each configurable field, helping administrators set up timesheet displays customized to their organization's needs.
ss: Weekly Timesheets in Access Group's Workforce Management (WFM) system lets administrators configure what payroll timesheet information employees, managers, and admins can view after timesheets are generated. The configuration screen allows you to customize additional information fields, enable pay code descriptions, and control how timesheet data is displayed across both the Portal and Native App. Open this guide when you need to set up timesheet visibility for your workforce, control what payroll details appear to different user levels, or troubleshoot timesheet display issues. The guide covers accessing the configuration screen, configuring display options, and understanding the menu security settings required for employees, managers, and administrators.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive documentation on configuring and using the Weekly Timesheet feature within the Access Group's Workforce Management (WFM) system, explaining how administrators set up what payroll timesheet information displays to employees after the generate timesheet process is completed for a period. The document covers accessing the Weekly Timesheet Configuration screen through the WFM Admin Dashboard by selecting WFM Configuration and then the Weekly Timesheet Configuration tile, where administrators configure three additional information fields and can enable the payslip pay code description option to display WFM pay code descriptions instead of those set up in Payroll. The Weekly Timesheet screen itself displays detailed timesheet data including pay codes, descriptions, types, daily hours worked, clock in/out times, and totals, with the option to group data by pay code, and can be accessed by admins and managers through Person Maintenance while employees view timesheets via the My Calendar widget or My Calendar section. The guide is designed for WFM administrators who need to configure the system and any users—administrators, managers, and employees—who require access to view timesheet information relevant to their role.

ss: Work Groups in WFM let you organize employees into logical groupings to control supervisor access, determine payroll feeding rules, and apply different configuration settings to workers with the same shift type. You use the Work Group screen to create, copy, configure, and manage these groups—assigning them to companies, holiday schemes, and shift types while setting up payment rules, payroll hours, absences, and other workforce parameters. Open this guide when you need to set up a new work group, modify payment or absence rules for a specific employee group, or understand how to configure groups so that workers clocking in for tracking don't feed into payroll while others do. sl: This Work Groups user guide from Access Limited explains how to manage and configure work groups within a workforce management system, specifically covering the Work Group Screen accessible via WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Configuration > Work Groups. The document provides step-by-step instructions for fundamental tasks including adding new work groups, copying existing ones, marking work groups as inactive, deleting work groups, and viewing active users assigned to specific work groups. Work groups serve as personnel groupings that control supervisor access levels and determine whether employee timesheets feed into the payroll system, allowing organizations to treat workers with identical shift types differently based on operational needs—such as creating separate groups for remote data entry staff who do not clock in versus office-based day workers who do. The Work Group Screen displays key fields such as Work Group Code, Work Group Name, Company, Holiday Scheme, and Shift Type, all of which can be filtered using search and filter options based on companies, shift types, holiday schemes, calendars, timesheets, and active status. The guide covers extensive configuration sections including General Parameters, Payment Rules (with subsections for Default Payments, Basic/Salary Rules, Time Threshold Balance, and Medical Salary Rules), Default Payroll Hours, Group Codes, Trigger Points, Extra Hours Recoding, Absence Contract Days, and Advanced Configuration options covering absences, sign-off hours, stand-by hours, and additional settings. This resource is intended for system administrators responsible for setting up and maintaining work group structures to align with organizational requirements and payroll processing needs.

**Understanding the predefined tasks:** The guide covers 7 built-in year-end tasks that are essential for system maintenance:

- Extending the Company Period

- Extending the Balance Calendar

This is intended for WFM Administrators who need a centralized, organized view of all year-end tasks to ensure nothing is missed during the annual closeout process.
ss: The PeopleXD Workforce Management Year End Tasks screen centralizes critical year-end administrative activities, displaying seven predefined tasks such as extending company calendar years, updating bank holiday schemes, and completing balance period ends. WFM administrators use this screen to track task completion status, receive email notifications when actions are due, and add custom checklist items tailored to their organization's specific requirements. Open this guide when you need to set up year-end processes, understand which menu profiles are required for access, or configure notifications to ensure no critical tasks are missed.
sl: This document is a user guide for the WFM Year End Tasks functionality within PeopleXD Workforce Management, designed to help system administrators systematically manage annual year-end processes through a centralized screen. The guide explains how to access the WFM Year End Tasks screen via the WFM Admin Dashboard and outlines the seven predefined year-end tasks that keep the system current: Extend Company Calendar Year, Extend Company Period, Extend User Defined Calendar Periods, Update Bank Holiday Scheme, Extend Balance Calendar, Complete Balance Period End, and Extend Non-Cycle Shift. To use this functionality, administrators must have the WFM_Year_End menu profile enabled along with related profiles including WFM_COMPANY_SETTING_ADMIN, WFM_BANK_HOLIDAY_CONFIG, WFM_BALANCE_CONFIGURATION, WFM_BALANCE_ADMIN, and WFM_SHIFTS_TYPES, and email parameters must be configured for notifications. The document also covers threshold settings, notification logic, menu options for importing profiles, and includes FAQs to address common questions about year-end task management.

# Summary: Upload Documents Guide for PeopleXD

This guide teaches users how to set up and configure the document upload functionality within PeopleXD's Workforce Management system, specifically for use with leave requests and absence entries.

After reading this guide, users will be able to:

**Main Learning Outcomes:**

1. **Understand the Document Upload Purpose** — Learn how employees can submit required documentation (such as medical certificates for sick leave) when they return to work.

2. **Set Up Document Types** — Create and configure document types that control how documents are managed and accessed in the system. This includes:
   - Assigning a code and description to each document type
   - Deciding whether documents are linked to a person or to a specific employment contract
   - Activating document types for use

3. **Configure User Access Permissions** — Control who can view and upload documents by setting separate permissions for:
   - Managers (MSS access) — determining whether managers can only view employee documents, or both view and upload them
   - Employees (ESS access) — determining whether employees can only view their own documents, or both view and upload them

4. **Configure Pay Codes** — Set up pay codes to support document uploads (details covered later in the guide)

5. **Set Up Menu Access** — Enable the document upload feature across different user roles (employees, managers, and for absence-related functions)

The guide emphasizes that document type setup is essential for controlling which users have access to which documents and what actions they can perform with them.
ss: The Upload Documents feature in PeopleXD Workforce Management allows employees to submit documentation (such as medical certificates for sick leave) when they return to work, and managers to view or add supporting documents to leave requests and absence entries. To enable this functionality, you need to set up Document Types to control who can view and upload files, configure which pay codes require supporting documents, and activate the appropriate menu options for employees and managers. This guide covers the complete configuration process, including how to establish warning levels that either allow, warn, or block leave submissions without attached documentation. Use this document when setting up your organization's document upload workflow for leave and absence management.
sl: This user guide from Access Group provides comprehensive instructions for configuring and implementing the document upload functionality within PeopleXD Workforce Management, specifically for use with Leave Request and Absence Entry processes. The document covers three main configuration areas: Document Type Setup (accessed via People Management Dashboard > Data Centre > Reference Data > Document Type tile), Pay Code Configuration (accessed via WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Configuration > Pay Codes tile), and Menu Access setup for both employees and managers. Document Type setup involves creating document types with specific codes and descriptions, then configuring Advanced Options to determine whether documents are person-driven or contract-driven, and setting MSS (Manager Self Service) and ESS (Employee Self Service) access permissions that control whether managers and employees can view and/or add documents. Pay Code Configuration requires enabling the "Supporting Documents Required" toggle on the Leave Request Documents screen, selecting a document type from a dropdown, and choosing a Warning Level (Allow, Warning, or Stop) that determines whether the system merely permits document uploads, issues warnings if documents are missing, or prevents process completion without documentation. Menu Access configuration grants employees and managers the ability to upload and view documents by enabling specific menu options through Security > Menu Profiles, with separate menu profiles for employee and manager access. This guide is essential for HR administrators and system configuration specialists who need to implement document submission requirements for absence management, such as requiring medical certificates for sick leave or exam proof for study leave.

t: Break Recalculation - Stagger Multiple Breaks
s:
# Break Recalculation - Stagger Multiple Breaks: Guide Summary

This guide teaches users how to use the Break Recalculation feature in the PeopleXD HR system, specifically when employee work patterns are changed (extended or shortened).

## What You'll Learn

**Core Functionality:**
- How the Break Recalculation feature automatically adjusts employee breaks when their work patterns are modified
- How the system ensures breaks comply with Working Time Directive (WTD) regulations while minimizing staffing gaps

**Key Concepts Covered:**
- **Working Time Directive Rules** — the regulatory framework that governs when and how breaks must be scheduled
- **Break Recalculation Process** — how the system recalculates and repositions breaks to optimal times when patterns change
- **Edited Breaks** — how to preserve manually edited breaks during recalculation
- **Staggered Multiple Breaks** — how to handle situations where employees have multiple breaks staggered throughout a day, including managing gaps between breaks
- **Adjoining Patterns** — how break recalculation works when work patterns connect or overlap

**Practical Application:**
- Real-world examples showing break recalculation in action, such as when a shift changes from 7.5 hours to 10 hours, or when additional work patterns are added
- Configuration instructions for setting up the WTD breaks parameter in the system

The guide ensures users understand how the system automatically optimizes break scheduling to maintain compliance, company rules, and adequate staffing levels.
ss: Break Recalculation in Roster automatically adjusts employee breaks when shift patterns are extended or shortened, ensuring compliance with Working Time Directive rules while minimizing staffing gaps. The feature recalculates break timing and duration based on AutoRoster Break Rules configured at the Work Group or individual level, and triggers whenever pattern start/end times change or additional patterns are added to a working day. You'd open this document when amending employee rosters and need to understand how breaks will be automatically repositioned, or when configuring break rules in the Working Time Parameters section of Backoffice. It also covers how to preserve manually edited breaks (such as those scheduled around medical appointments) so they aren't overwritten during recalculation.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive user guide for the Break Recalculation functionality in Roster v28, explaining how the system automatically adjusts employee breaks when work patterns are amended, either extended or shortened. The Break Recalculation feature ensures compliance with Working Time Directive (WTD) regulations while scheduling breaks at optimal times to minimize staffing shortages, and it is configured through the Backoffice menu via System Params > Working Time Parameters, where administrators access the AutoRoster Break Rules section to set parameters for their Work Groups or individual employees. The document details eight specific break rules—including "No Break in the First," "No Break in the Last," "Max Consecutive Hours," "Split Break After," "Minimum Split Duration," "One Rule Only," "Multiple Rules," and "Minor Age Threshold"—that govern when and how breaks are assigned based on shift duration and employee age. Break recalculation is triggered automatically when pattern start or end times are amended, when adjoining or non-adjoining additional patterns are added to a working day, or when patterns change from Work to Rest status or vice versa, with breaks being amended to reflect the new working day duration. The guide also covers the "Keep Edited Breaks" function, which allows manually scheduled breaks (such as those fixed for medical appointments) to remain unchanged during recalculation, and includes practical examples showing how breaks are recalculated for scenarios such as roster changes to 7.5-hour and 10-hour days. This document is intended for HR and payroll professionals, roster administrators, and system configurators who need to understand and implement break recalculation rules to maintain both WTD compliance and company-specific staffing requirements in the Roster system.

t: Cost of Roster

# Cost of Roster Guide Summary

This guide teaches users how to understand and work with the **Cost of Roster** feature in the PeopleXD HR system. Here's what it covers:

## What You'll Learn

**Understanding Cost of Roster basics:**
- What the Cost of Roster feature is and where it's displayed in the system
- How to view roster costs in different formats: daily view, weekly view, and summary view
- What information is shown, including uncovered shifts, time exceptions, and sign-off hours

**Using the Cost of Roster tool:**
- How budget summaries work within the system
- Where and how to calculate **planned costs** (budgeted/forecasted staffing expenses)
- Where and how to calculate **actual costs** (real staffing expenses as they occur)
- How to access and use the Cost Summary screen to compare planned versus actual costs
- How to view detailed breakdowns of cost information

**Setting up and configuring budgets:**
- How to load budget values and hours into the system through multiple methods
- How to upload budgets using interface files
- How to configure the system interfaces for budget entry
- How to manually enter budget hours and values directly via People Hub
- The proper file formats and layouts needed for budget uploads (both table and comma-separated formats)

In essence, this guide enables HR professionals to monitor staffing budgets, compare planned versus actual roster costs, and maintain accurate budget configuration in the system.
ss: The Cost of Roster feature in CoreHR lets you view and compare budget allocations against planned and actual roster costs in real time, enabling better cost management decisions. Roster managers can monitor team budgets and spending across shifts, while administrators can configure costing for additional events like overtime. You'll use this tool to access cost summaries, break down expenses by detail, and track budget variances across day and week views. Open this guide when you need to set up budget values, configure cost allocations by employer or pay code, or understand how to interpret cost data within your roster.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive documentation for the Cost of Roster feature in CoreHR, covering its functionality, usage, and configuration for roster managers and system administrators. The document explains how to access and view Cost of Roster data across multiple screen views including Roster Details Day View, Roster Details Week View, and Cost Summary screens, which display information about uncovered shifts, time exceptions, and approved sign-off hours. The guide details two main cost calculation areas: Planned Costs and Actual Costs, along with a Cost Summary feature that includes comparison and detail breakdown functionality to help users analyze budget versus actual spending. Configuration sections cover critical setup tasks including budget value uploads and manual entry via the People Hub interface, employer cost allocation groupings with effective date updates, personal overrides, and pay code configuration within the Roster Links settings. The Cost of Roster functionality enables organizations to view real-time budget, planned cost, and actual cost data simultaneously, supporting better informed business decisions and helping roster managers keep team spending aligned with budgets. This guide is intended for roster managers who need to monitor costs effectively and system administrators responsible for configuring the feature, including setting display controls, costing types, and hours calculation parameters.
