t: Generate payroll outputs
s:
Once you complete your payroll there are several outputs you will need to generate. 

 

To learn how to do this, watch the video or follow the steps below.
​

Click Manage Payroll then highlight the relevant pay group.

Click the Outputs tab. 

To print your payslips, click Print Payslips or these ...
ss: Generating payroll outputs in PeopleXD covers the final step after completing your payroll run, including printing payslips, creating bank files for payment processing, and generating General Ledger files for accounting. Open this guide when you need to produce payslips for employees, create the bank file to process payments, or export GL data to your accounting system. The process involves accessing the Outputs tab within Manage Payroll, selecting the relevant pay group, and choosing which outputs to generate. You'll also learn where to view all generated files in the Report Centre.
sl: This document provides instructions for generating the various output files and reports that must be created after completing a payroll run in the Access Group payroll system. The process begins by navigating to Manage Payroll, selecting the relevant pay group, and then accessing the Outputs tab where all output generation options are centralized. Users can generate payslips through the Print Payslips option, which can either be printed directly or released through Portal for employee self-service access. The document describes how to create the bank file for pay path processing by clicking the Bank File button, and how to generate the General Ledger file by clicking the General Ledger button, both essential for downstream financial and banking processes. All generated files can be tracked and reviewed in the Report Centre, providing a centralized location to verify successful output creation. The document acknowledges common issues such as cost centres not outputting as expected on general ledger files and General Ledger journal report (PAYB236) not balancing, directing users to related articles for troubleshooting these specific scenarios. This guidance is typically used by payroll administrators and finance teams who need to complete the final stage of payroll processing and ensure all required outputs are properly generated for banking, accounting, and employee communication purposes.

t: Error: 'Entry at Start date as least 2 address fields must be populated'
s:
When submitting an RTI file, you may encounter the above error message in the RTI Exception Report. This error appears because the system requires at least two address fields to be populated for an employee. If these fields are missing or incomplete, the RTI file cannot be processed.

 

To resolve ...
ss: RTI file submissions require at least two populated address fields for each employee, and this error occurs when address information is missing or incomplete in the system. To resolve it, you'll need to update the employee's address details and verify that the effective dates are set correctly in the People Management section of Portal. After updating the address information, regenerate and resubmit the RTI file to process it successfully. Open this document if you're submitting RTI files and encounter validation errors related to incomplete employee address data.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre provides guidance on resolving a specific error that occurs when submitting RTI files through the Portal system. The error message "'Entry at Start date as least 2 address fields must be populated'" indicates that the RTI file submission cannot proceed because the system requires a minimum of two populated address fields for each employee record. The document outlines a step-by-step process to locate and update employee address information, beginning by accessing People Management from the dashboard menu, then navigating to the Employees section, and searching for the specific employee by name. Once the employee record is located and the Contact Information section is accessed, users must verify the effective dates of at least two address entries under the My Address Details area, and if necessary, edit these dates using the three-dot icon menu and the Edit Address Details option. The document specifies that users must select the appropriate effective date in the Date effective field and save the changes to ensure compliance with the RTI submission requirements. After updating the address effective dates, users must regenerate and resubmit the RTI file for processing to resolve the error. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and HR professionals within organizations using the Access Group Portal who need to troubleshoot RTI file submission failures related to incomplete employee address data.

t: Back Office: Add new bank details
s:
A Bank Identifier Code (BIC) is a unique code that identifies a specific bank or financial institution, facilitating international wire transfers and ensuring accurate and timely payments.

 

Adding a new BIC or updating bank details in the portal is essential for maintaining correct payment proces...
ss: Adding a new Bank Identifier Code (BIC) or updating bank details in CorePay ensures accurate payment processing and prevents transaction delays. This process is completed in the Back Office by navigating to CorePay > Reference > Bank Details, selecting BIC from the Type dropdown, and entering the required information. Open this document when you need to set up a new BIC in the reference data, particularly if it's a new bank that must also be configured in payroll. For UK banks, you can select the sort code directly from the dropdown menu instead.
sl: This document provides instructions for adding new Bank Identifier Codes (BICs) and bank details through the Portal interface in the Access Group system, which is essential for maintaining accurate payment processing and avoiding transaction delays. A BIC is a unique code that identifies specific banks or financial institutions and facilitates international wire transfers. The document guides users through the specific navigation path of clicking CorePay, then Reference, then selecting Bank Details from the Type List of Values (LOV) and choosing BIC. For UK banks, users can select the sort code directly from a drop-down menu rather than entering a full BIC. The process involves clicking a green plus icon to add new details, filling in the required fields, and then clicking the save icon to store the changes. The document notes that if adding a new BIC, users should also set up a new bank identifier in the payroll system. This resource is designed for back office and portal users who need to add or update bank information to ensure timely and accurate payment processing, and it references related articles covering foreign bank accounts, company bank details, sort codes, and bank identifiers for comprehensive bank setup guidance.

t: Disable browse button on paypath screen
s:
To disable browse button on the Paypath screen in PeopleXD Payroll and store the file in a specific file location, follow the steps below in back office.

Click CorePay then click Update.

Click Utilities then click System Configuration.

Click General.

Under the Paypath column select the Disable B...
ss: The PeopleXD Payroll system allows you to disable the browse button on the Paypath screen and configure a specific file location for payroll file storage. This configuration is managed through the back office CorePay utility under System Configuration settings. Use this guide when you need to restrict file browsing functionality in your payroll system or when setting up a custom file path for Paypath documents. The process involves navigating to General settings, enabling the Disable Browse Button checkbox, and defining your preferred file location.
sl: This document provides instructions for disabling the browse button functionality on the Paypath screen within PeopleXD Payroll's back office environment. The process involves navigating through the CorePay module by clicking CorePay then Update, followed by accessing Utilities and selecting System Configuration. Users must then navigate to the General section where they will find the Paypath column containing a "Disable Browse Button" checkbox that needs to be selected. In addition to disabling the browse button, the document explains how to specify a custom file location by entering a path in the "Paypath File Location" field, allowing administrators to control where Paypath files are stored within their system. After making these configuration changes, users must save their modifications by clicking the save icon to apply the settings. This document is typically used by PeopleXD Payroll system administrators or back office personnel who need to restrict user access to the browse functionality and enforce a standardized file storage location for Paypath operations.

t: Back Office: Reset third party paypath file
s:
Resetting a third-party paypath file involves refreshing or reconfiguring the data exchange mechanism between your payroll system and an external payroll service provider. 

 

This process is necessary when data transmission errors occur, file corruption is detected, or synchronisation issues arise...
ss: Resetting a third-party paypath file refreshes the data exchange between your payroll system and an external payroll service provider. Use this process when you encounter data transmission errors, file corruption, or synchronisation issues that prevent proper communication between systems. Open this guide when payroll data fails to transmit correctly and you need to regenerate the file before running the next payroll cycle. The reset is performed in Back Office under Core Pay > Employee > Employee deduction > Third Party EFT.
sl: This document provides instructions for resetting a third-party paypath file in the Back Office module of a payroll system, which involves refreshing the data exchange mechanism between the internal payroll system and an external payroll service provider. The reset process is necessary to resolve data transmission errors, file corruption, or synchronisation failures between the system and the third-party provider, and should be performed immediately upon detection of such issues before the next payroll cycle is processed. Users navigate through Core Pay > Employee > Employee deduction > Third Party EFT to access the reset functionality. The specific steps involve selecting "Reset Third Party EFT," entering the company and start date (which represents the processing date), ticking the "Reset toggle," and clicking Reports to re-generate the file. This document is intended for Back Office users managing payroll operations, though it notes that Portal users should follow a separate procedure outlined in a related article. If errors occur during the reset process, users are instructed to raise a case online referencing this article title and providing details including the affected pay group(s) and processing date. The document also cross-references related articles covering bank paypath file resets, third-party EFT file generation, and bank file creation for users requiring additional functionality.

t: Portal: Grant pay group access to a user
s:
A pay group is used to categorise employees with the same pay frequency. All employees within a pay group are processed together for payments.

 

If you're unable to view a pay group or an employee in a pay group, you need to grant pay group access to view specific pay groups and employees.

 

If ...
ss: Pay groups categorize employees by pay frequency, and granting pay group access allows users to view specific pay groups and their employees in the system. Use this document when you need to give a user permission to access certain pay groups—either because they're unable to view a pay group or specific employees within it. The process involves navigating to Settings, selecting Pay Groups Access, and adding the relevant pay groups for that user. Note that access must be granted in Back Office to update both Portal and Back Office accounts; Portal alone only updates Portal access.
sl: This document explains how to grant pay group access to users in the Portal system, where pay groups are used to categorize employees with the same pay frequency for batch payment processing. The document addresses the specific scenario where users are unable to view particular pay groups or employees within those groups and need access permissions to resolve this visibility issue. To grant pay group access, users navigate to Settings, select Pay Groups Access, click Add Pay Group Access, enter the user's name and employee number, select the relevant pay groups, and click OK. A critical configuration note emphasizes that to provide pay group access to both Portal and Back Office accounts simultaneously, administrators must grant access through the Back Office system rather than the Portal, as the Portal only updates Portal accounts. The document alerts users that if an "access denied" message appears after granting access, they must contact their organization's superuser to verify that the appropriate menu profile permission has been assigned to their account, as the support team cannot directly assign access. This document is typically used by Portal administrators or users with permission-management responsibilities who need to onboard new users or troubleshoot access issues related to pay group visibility and employee data access.

t: Back Office: Grant pay group access to a user
s:
A pay group is used to categorise employees with the same pay frequency. All employees within a pay group are processed together for payments.

 

If you're unable to view a pay group or an employee in a pay group, you need to grant pay group access to view specific pay groups and employees.

 

If ...
ss: Pay groups categorize employees by pay frequency in CorePay, and this document covers how to grant back office users access to view and process specific pay groups and their employees. Use this guide when you need to assign pay group permissions to a back office user account, either because they're unable to view certain pay groups or employees, or as part of setting up new user access. The process involves navigating to CorePay Pay Users through the Portal Security section and adding the relevant pay group, username, and input location for each access level needed. Note that your organization's superuser must assign the necessary menu profile to your account before access can be granted.
sl: This document provides instructions for granting pay group access to users in a back office system, where pay groups are used to categorize employees with the same pay frequency and process them together for payments. The document explains that access restrictions may prevent users from viewing specific pay groups or employees, requiring administrators to grant the necessary permissions through a defined process. To grant pay group access via the back office, users must navigate through CorePay > Reference > Pay Users, click the add icon, and populate three key fields: Pay Group, Username (employee number), and Input Location before saving. Alternatively, access can be granted through Portal by navigating to Security > Set Up, selecting CorePay Pay Users, filtering by Back Office Account type, and adding the same three required fields for each pay group and input location combination. The document notes an important distinction that portal accounts must have access granted only through the portal system, not the back office. If an access denied error message appears after granting access, users are instructed to contact their organization's superuser to verify that the relevant menu profile permission has been properly assigned to their account, as the support team cannot directly assign access. The document emphasizes that superusers within the organization are responsible for assigning the necessary menu profiles, not the external support team.

t: Back Office: Update personnel number for an employee
s:
To amend an employee's reference number, you need to adjust the Employee Reference field in back office. 

 

To do this, follow the steps below. 

📌Note: To amend the employee reference number in Portal, follow these steps.

Click CorePay then click on Employees.

Select Advanced Employee Features ...
ss: Updating an employee's personnel number in back office requires accessing the Employee Reference field through CorePay and the Advanced Employee Features menu. Use this document when you need to correct an employee's reference number by entering both the incorrect and correct personnel numbers, then saving the changes to your local file location. Open this guide if you're working in back office (rather than Portal) and need to amend an employee's identification number in the system.
sl: This document provides instructions for updating an employee's personnel number within the Back Office system, specifically targeting administrators or HR personnel who need to correct or change employee reference numbers in the payroll system. The process involves accessing the CorePay module and navigating to the Employees section, then selecting Advanced Employee Features and the Change Employee Reference option. Users must enter the incorrect personnel number in the Current Reference field and the correct personnel number in the New Reference field to perform the amendment. The document requires users to specify a file location setting, selecting Local File Location such as Desktop or another local directory before confirming the changes by clicking OK. The summary notes that there is an alternative procedure for amending employee reference numbers through the Portal interface, with related documentation available for that process. This document is typically used by back office administrators, payroll managers, or HR personnel when they need to correct data entry errors in employee records or update personnel identification numbers within the Access Group payroll system.

t: White listing IP addresses
s:
If you have changed your IP address or need to add new ones to the whitelist, please contact our support team to reach out to the optimization services team. Please note that this request will incur a charge.

 

📌Note: This must be done before adding the IP address under the Security dashboard in p...
ss: White listing IP addresses allows you to control which IP addresses can access your system through the Security dashboard in your portal. You'll need to contact the optimization services team to whitelist IPs before you can add them yourself—note that this service incurs a charge. Open this document when you've changed your IP address, need to add new ones for access, or are setting up IP restrictions for Back Office. The guide walks you through accessing the Security menu, viewing product access restrictions, and entering IP addresses in the system.
sl: This document provides instructions for whitelisting IP addresses in Access Group's portal and Back Office systems, covering both the request process and the technical implementation steps. The document explains that users who have changed their IP address or need to add new ones must first contact the support team to reach out to the optimization services team, a process that incurs a charge and must be completed before adding the IP address in the portal's Security dashboard. Once the support team has processed the whitelist request, users can implement the changes by navigating to the Security menu, selecting System Overview, and locating the Product Access Restriction Options section where they click VIEW next to the Common product. To add a new IP address entry, users click the ADD button, enter the full IP address in the IP Address field, and click OK to save the configuration. For Back Office IP whitelisting specifically, users must raise a new support case and include their relevant public IP addresses, with a note that private IPs should be masked as public IPs before sharing with the support team. This document is intended for portal and Back Office administrators or users who manage network access and security configurations and need to update IP restrictions due to address changes or new network requirements.

t: Set employee P60 to print
s:
Setting all employee P60s to print ensures that each employee receives their end of year tax summary, which is essential for tax compliance.

 

If the P60 file is blank, you will need to update or set employee P60 to print. 

 

To do this, follow the steps below in portal. 

📌Note: If this is requ...
ss: Setting employee P60s to print ensures each worker receives their end-of-year tax summary, which is required for tax compliance. Open this guide if an employee's P60 file is blank or if you need to configure P60 printing in your payroll system. The process involves navigating to an employee's Tax Details in the portal and enabling the Print P60 toggle under Payslip Options. For bulk updates across all employees, the document recommends raising a support case to run a background script instead.
sl: This document provides instructions for configuring P60 printing settings for individual employees in the Access Group payroll system to ensure end-of-year tax summaries are generated and distributed for tax compliance purposes. The guide addresses the specific problem of blank P60 files, which require the P60 print setting to be enabled before P60s can be properly produced. The document directs users to access the portal and navigate to a specific employee record by clicking the Employee menu and searching for the relevant employee name. Once the employee record is open, users must click View and scroll to the Tax Details section to locate the payroll configuration area. Within Tax Details, under the Payslip Options section, users will find a Print P60 toggle switch that must be turned on to enable P60 printing for that employee. For organizations needing to apply this setting across all employees simultaneously rather than individually, the document recommends raising a support case to request a background script that can update the setting in bulk. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and HR professionals who need to troubleshoot missing or blank P60s and ensure employees receive their required tax documentation.

t: Load position rates of pay
s:
Loading position rates of pay involves entering or updating the compensation rates assigned to various job positions within your organization. This practice is essential for ensuring accurate payroll calculations and maintaining compliance with internal pay structures and external regulations. 

 

...
ss: Loading position rates of pay in PeopleXD involves uploading compensation rates for job positions through a CSV file via the portal, ensuring employees receive correct pay based on their role and scale point. Use this process when you need to enter new rates, update existing rates in bulk, or delete incorrect uploads—all of which directly impact payroll calculations and compliance. The CSV file requires specific fields in a set order: Position, Point, Rate Sequence, Date Effective, and pay rate values (hourly, daily, weekly, or annual salary). Open this guide when setting up or modifying position-based compensation structures, as rates become effective on the system-specified date and the system automatically calculates arrears based on effective and input dates.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide to loading position rates of pay in the PeopleXD system, which is essential for ensuring accurate payroll calculations and maintaining compliance with internal pay structures and external regulations. The document covers four main processes: uploading new position rates, viewing rates, deleting rates, and performing bulk updates for employees assigned to a position rate. To upload rates, users must first create a CSV file with specific fields in a critical order, including Position, Point, Rate Sequence, Date Effective (in DDMMYYYY format), and compensation fields such as Hourly Rate, Daily Rate, Weekly Rate, and Annual Salary. Users then access the Portal, navigate to Uploads > Rate of Pay Uploads > Load Position Rates of Pay, enter a reference number, select CSV as the file type, browse to locate the file, and click OK to complete the upload. The new position rates are uploaded to PeopleXD with an effective date, and the system will automatically create new salary records for employees once the system date reaches that effective date; importantly, the system reads rates by both date effective and date input, which allows for automatic arrears calculations when multiple rates are input for the same effective date. The document also provides instructions for deleting incorrect position rate uploads by accessing the same portal location, entering the original reference number, and clicking Delete. This guide is intended for payroll administrators and HR professionals who manage employee compensation structures within the PeopleXD system.

t: Configure payslip parameters
s:
Payslip parameters are specific settings that determine how employee payslips are generated and displayed, including details such as earnings, deductions, and formatting options.

 

Configuring these parameters is essential for ensuring that payslips accurately reflect employees' compensation and c...
ss: Payslip parameters control how employee payslips are generated and displayed in your payroll system, including which earnings, deductions, and formatting options appear on each payslip. Configure these settings through System Configuration to ensure payslips accurately reflect compensation and meet legal compliance requirements. Open this document when you need to customize payslip layouts—such as adjusting the number of allowance or deduction lines, adding employer registration numbers, displaying job titles, or enabling advanced printing features. You'll also find guidance here for configuring copy payslips and ESS (Employee Self-Service) payslip display options.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide to configuring payslip parameters within the system's Settings > System Configuration > Payslip section, explaining how to access and save these settings by clicking Settings, System Configuration, Payslip, and then Save. The configuration covers three distinct payslip formats—Standard paper payslip, Copy Payslip, and ESS payslips—each with specific customizable fields that control how employee compensation information is generated and displayed. For Standard paper payslips, administrators can set the maximum number of allowance and deduction lines (up to 12 each), configure miscellaneous pay codes to group excess items, control ER remittance printing methods, customize labels for pre-tax deductions, and enable advanced printing options when payslips have been customized accordingly. The document also details numerous toggle settings that control visual and informational elements of payslips, such as displaying the payslip rate column, ER registration numbers, employer names, job titles, apprentice levy, and hourly allowances, as well as options to hide or reposition logos and restrict cheque printing based on user menu profiles. Copy Payslip configuration allows administrators to control the display of home addresses, payroll week-end dates, pay period formatting in month-year format, and historic messages from employees, pay groups, or pension schemes. This document is essential for payroll administrators and system configurators who need to ensure payslips comply with legal requirements, accurately reflect employee compensation including earnings and deductions, and match their organization's specific formatting and display preferences across different payslip versions.

t: Update to SEPA mode
s:
The Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) is the European Union's initiative aimed at integrating payment systems to standardize euro transactions across participating countries. This initiative allows for seamless electronic payments using unified formats and procedures.

 

Organizations need to update...
ss: SEPA mode in CorePersonnel determines which payment banking details (sort codes, account numbers, BIC, and IBAN) are required and displayed for euro transactions across European markets. Organizations typically start in Mode 2, which supports both legacy and new SEPA file formats, then transition to Mode 3 once SEPA files are validated and old bank details are no longer needed. Open this document when you're expanding operations into new European countries, changing banking relationships, or need to understand which banking information fields your system requires. If you need to update SEPA mode settings for your companies, this document explains the three modes available and directs you to raise a support case with the specific companies that need updating.
sl: This document explains SEPA (Single Euro Payments Area) mode configuration within CorePersonnel, which is the EU's standardized euro payment system that organizations must implement when expanding into European markets, changing banking relationships, or meeting regulatory requirements. CorePersonnel provides three distinct SEPA modes with different data requirements: Mode 1 uses bank sort code and account number only, Mode 2 includes bank sort code, account number, BIC, and IBAN, and Mode 3 uses only BIC and IBAN. The standard implementation approach begins with Mode 2 to allow clients to generate both legacy bank files and new SEPA files simultaneously; once clients validate the SEPA files, they transition to Mode 3 as the old bank details become obsolete. Portal displays vary by mode, with Mode 1 and Mode 2 showing account and sort code fields, while Mode 3 displays BIC and IBAN instead. To update SEPA mode settings for individual or multiple companies, users must submit an online case request that references this article title and specifies which companies require updating. The document references related troubleshooting articles including errors such as missing BIC and IBAN data during complete payment updates (PAY355), and provides links to procedures for resetting bank paypath files and adding new bank details in both Portal and Back Office environments.

t: Configure pay scales
s:
Pay scales are structured salary frameworks that define compensation levels within an organization. They are typically organized by job grades, experience levels, and performance criteria.

 

Scale points establish specific incremental steps within each pay scale, while rates assign actual monetary...
ss: Pay scales establish structured salary frameworks organized by job grades, experience levels, and performance criteria, with scale points defining incremental steps and rates assigning actual monetary values to each point. This document covers how to add pay scales, set up scale points, and define rates of pay within your payroll system using the Settings menu under Pay Rates. Use this guide when developing new job classifications, conducting annual pay reviews, or restructuring compensation frameworks to ensure salary equity across your workforce. Open this document if you need step-by-step instructions for creating and configuring compensation structures that align with industry standards and your internal budget.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on configuring pay scales within an organization's compensation system, covering the creation and management of structured salary frameworks that organize compensation by job grades, experience levels, and performance criteria. The document describes three core processes: adding a pay scale through Settings > Pay Rates > Position Reference (where users enter a position code and description before saving), setting up scale points via Settings > Pay Rates > Scale Point Profile (where users select a position code, add scale points with relevant codes and narratives, then save), and defining rates of pay through Pay Rates > Add Position Rates (where users select a position code, set an effective date, add scale point codes, and input compensation values including hourly rate, daily rate, annual salary, weekly rate, and unit rate). These interconnected tasks are essential for organizations implementing new job classifications, conducting annual pay reviews, or restructuring existing compensation frameworks to maintain salary equity and support career progression planning aligned with industry standards. The document serves human resources professionals, payroll administrators, and organizational leaders who need to establish fair and consistent remuneration structures across their workforce while managing internal budgets and compliance requirements.

t: Error: 'ERRMESS :ORA-01403: no data found on the SOURCEREF:s26500_council_tax'
s:
This error message:

"SOURCEREF:s26500_council_tax
EMPNO :XXXXX
ERRNO :100
ERRMESS :ORA-01403: no data found
**End UnHandled Exception - Contact Support HelpDesk."

appears in the PAY140 trace file.

 

The employee flagged in the trace file show negative net earnings, affecting their council tax ca...
ss: The ORA-01403 error in the PAY140 trace file occurs when council tax calculations fail because an employee has negative net earnings without a properly configured pay code scale. This error affects payroll processing in CorePay and requires you to verify that council tax deduction codes have valid threshold entries covering both negative earnings (from -9999 to zero) and the employee's actual positive earnings range. Open this document when payroll validation fails with unhandled exceptions related to council tax, or when an employee's deductions aren't calculating correctly due to missing or incomplete earning thresholds. The resolution involves checking employee deductions in the Portal or Back Office, then adding or updating the appropriate nett earnings scale ranges for the council tax pay code.
sl: This document provides guidance on resolving an ORA-01403 "no data found" error that appears in the PAY140 trace file when processing council tax deductions for employees with negative net earnings. The error occurs because council tax calculations require valid threshold entries starting from a net earning of zero, and employees with negative pay require special configuration to prevent the system from failing to locate matching deduction rates. The document explains that users must verify two key elements: first, they should check the tax council pay code by navigating to the employee's deductions through either the Portal (Employee > VIEW > Deductions) or Back Office (CorePay > Employee > Employee Deductions > View Employee Deductions). Second, users must ensure valid entries exist against the employee's positive monthly threshold, which involves accessing pay code settings through Portal (Settings > Pay Codes > Deductions) or Back Office (CorePay > Reference > Advanced Reference Features > Nett Deduction Rates). For employees with negative earnings specifically, users must add a threshold row with Nett Earnings From set to -9999 and Nett Earnings To set to Zero in the Scales or Nett Deduction Rates section. For employees with positive earnings, users should verify that valid entries cover the complete range of the employee's weekly or monthly earnings without gaps in the thresholds. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and support staff who encounter deduction processing failures related to council tax calculations in the Access Group payroll system.

t: Turn on PAYE reference number on payslip
s:
The PAYE (Pay As You Earn) reference number is a unique identifier assigned to employers by tax authorities. It is used to track employees' income tax and National Insurance contributions.

 

Enabling the PAYE reference number on payslips is essential for ensuring transparency and accuracy in tax r...
ss: The PAYE reference number is a unique tax identifier that tracks employees' income tax and National Insurance contributions. Enable this on payslips by activating the py_payslip_company_no parameter in your portal's Administrator Dashboard through Site Manager and Admin Settings. Open this document when you need to display the employer's PAYE reference on payslips for tax transparency and to help employees verify their tax deductions. Test the configuration change in your UAT environment first before applying it to your live system.
sl: This document explains how to enable the PAYE reference number display on payslips within the Access Group portal, providing employees with a unique tax identifier assigned by authorities that tracks income tax and National Insurance contributions. The PAYE reference number serves as critical transparency and verification information, allowing employees to confirm their tax deductions and support tax-related inquiries with accurate documentation. To implement this feature, users must activate the py_payslip_company_no parameter through a specific configuration process in the portal's administrator settings. The step-by-step process begins by accessing the Administrator Dashboard from the main dashboard menu, then navigating to Site Manager and selecting Admin Settings. Users then search for the py_payslip_company_no parameter in the Search field, click Edit to open the configuration, and change the parameter value to Y before clicking OK to save changes. The document emphasizes that configuration changes should be tested first in a UAT (User Acceptance Testing) environment to ensure the functionality works correctly before deployment to the live system. This document is primarily intended for system administrators and payroll managers who manage tax compliance settings and need to ensure accurate PAYE information appears on employee payslips.

t: Enable parameter for payroll messages
s:
Payroll messages are notifications or alerts that convey important information regarding payroll processes, such as payment confirmations, tax updates, or corrections. 

 

Enabling the parameter for payroll messages is essential for ensuring that employees receive timely and accurate information re...
ss: Payroll messages are notifications that convey important payroll information such as payment confirmations, tax updates, and corrections. Enable payroll messages by switching on the CP_USING_PAY_PORTAL parameter through Administrator Dashboard > Site Manager > Admin Settings. Open this document when you need to activate payroll message notifications in your portal to ensure employees receive timely and accurate payroll-related information. The parameter change only enables message display and does not impact your actual payroll processing.
sl: This document provides instructions for enabling payroll message notifications within an organization's payroll system through portal configuration. Payroll messages are alerts and notifications that communicate critical payroll-related information to employees, including payment confirmations, tax updates, and corrections. The core task involves activating the CP_USING_PAY_PORTAL parameter, which is the system setting that controls whether payroll messages are displayed and actionable within the platform. To complete this configuration, administrators must navigate through the portal's Administrator Dashboard, access Site Manager, select Admin Settings, and locate the CP_USING_PAY_PORTAL parameter using the search field. Once found, the parameter value must be edited and changed from its default state to "Y" to enable the functionality, then confirmed by clicking OK. The document emphasizes that this change only affects message display and does not impact actual payroll processing or calculations. This document is intended for system administrators or payroll administrators who manage portal settings and need to ensure employees receive timely and accurate payroll information through the notification system. The guide is part of a broader set of payroll configuration documentation that includes related tasks such as adjusting additional payroll message settings and reviewing displayed messages.

t: Unable to download P60s from the Report Centre
s:
A P60 is an official tax document issued by employers in the UK, summarizing an employee's total earnings and tax deductions for the financial year. 

 

Producing P60s is essential for ensuring that employees have accurate records of their income and tax contributions, which they need for personal ...
ss: P60 reports in the Report Centre may fail to download if the file times out or displays a "file too large" error. Payroll administrators can resolve this by adjusting the cp_py_split_p60 parameter in Admin Settings to split P60 reports into smaller batches based on employee count. Open this document if you're experiencing download failures when generating P60s in portal and need to configure the file-splitting setting to enable successful report generation.
sl: This document explains how to resolve issues when downloading P60 forms—official UK tax documents summarizing employee earnings and tax deductions—from the Report Centre in the portal. P60s are critical for employees to complete personal tax returns and maintain accurate financial records. The document addresses a specific technical problem: when users attempt to download P60 reports from the Report Centre, the file may time out or generate an error message stating the file is too large. The root cause is typically a configuration setting that needs adjustment by payroll administrators. To fix this issue, administrators must navigate to the portal dashboard, select Administrator, then Site Manager, then Admin Settings, and search for the parameter cp_py_split_p60. Once located, administrators edit this parameter and set the Value field to a smaller number—such as 1,000—which splits the P60 report into smaller files containing that number of employee records rather than attempting to generate one large file. After adjusting the parameter, administrators can regenerate the P60s and successfully download the reports from the Report Centre. This document is designed for payroll administrators managing employee tax documentation within Access Group's payroll portal system.

Open this document when you need to upload new individual employee pay rates, delete incorrect uploads, or understand the required CSV file format and field structure. sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on loading individual employee personal pay rates into the PeopleXD payroll system, a process essential for ensuring employees receive correct compensation based on their contract terms and adjustments. The document describes the complete workflow including uploading new rates, viewing results, deleting incorrect uploads, and performing bulk updates, with specific navigation paths through the Portal interface via Uploads > Employee New Rates of Pay. The document specifies critical technical requirements such as ensuring each CSV line contains at least 10 commas to verify all fields are present, limiting the Reference field to 10 characters maximum and ensuring uniqueness for employees with secondary appointments, and using Notepad to validate the file before upload. After uploading through the Portal's Browse function and clicking OK, the system automatically generates a report accessible in the Report Centre showing both successful and unsuccessful loaded records. The deletion process for incorrect uploads follows the same Portal navigation path (Uploads > Employee New Rates of Pay) where users enter the original reference and click Delete to remove erroneous entries. This document is typically used by payroll administrators and HR personnel who need to manage employee compensation records and ensure accurate pay rate implementation across the organization.

The document provides a straightforward resolution process accessible through the portal interface, requiring users to navigate to Settings > Codes > Pay Codes (Classic) and select the relevant pay code from the Pay Group dropdown menu. The solution involves clearing any existing content from the Hours/Days Limit field and leaving it blank, then saving the changes by clicking the Save button. This document is primarily useful for payroll administrators and HR professionals who manage pay code configurations and encounter validation errors when attempting to set time-based limits on unit-based or value-based pay codes. t: Configure the payroll calendar
s:
A payroll calendar outlines the specific periods for processing payroll, including pay and cut-off dates for timekeeping and payroll submissions.

 

Configuring the payroll calendar is essential to ensure timely and accurate employee payments while aligning with the company's financial processes an...
ss: The payroll calendar outlines pay periods and cut-off dates for timekeeping and payroll submissions, dividing the year into week numbers and tracking period end dates for different pay group frequencies. Configuring this calendar is essential to ensure accurate and timely employee payments while aligning with your company's financial processes and regulatory requirements. Open this document when you need to set up a new payroll calendar, reuse an existing calendar as a template, adjust week end dates, or add special periods like week 53. Each company within your organisation requires its own payroll calendar configured in your system's Company Parameters settings.
sl: This document provides guidance on configuring payroll calendars within an organization's payroll system, explaining that a payroll calendar outlines specific periods for processing payroll including pay and cut-off dates for timekeeping and payroll submissions. The document emphasizes that configuring the payroll calendar is essential for ensuring timely and accurate employee payments while aligning with the company's financial processes and regulations, and notes that each company within an organisation requires its own payroll calendar. Key configuration details include understanding that the calendar divides the year into week numbers (formatted as 202001, 202002, 202003, etc.) and tracks period end dates for weekly, fortnightly, and four-weekly pay groups, with monthly pay groups always having period end dates on the last day of the month, though the calendar itself does not track payment dates. The document describes three main processes: reusing an existing calendar as a template by navigating to Settings > Company Parameters > Calendars, selecting a company, and using the Build/Rebuild Year function with Base Year and New Year fields; amending week end dates through the Amend Dates option where users specify the number of days adjustment and date ranges in the From Period and To Period fields; and creating new calendars with options to update week end dates or add extra weeks such as week 53 by duplicating and modifying existing weeks. This document is typically used by payroll administrators and HR professionals who need to set up or maintain payroll calendar configurations to ensure accurate and compliant payroll processing across their organization.

sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses a specific error that occurs when running the PAY140 validation file during the final payroll period of the year, where the validation process fails or becomes stuck in the portal system. The root cause of this issue is that the payroll calendar for the upcoming year has not been configured before the user attempts to process payroll for the last period of the current year. To resolve this problem, users must rebuild next year's calendar through the portal interface by navigating to Settings, then locating Company Parameters and selecting Calendars. Within the Calendars section, users search for their relevant company in the Company field and then click the Build/Rebuild Year button beside the appropriate company entry to generate the missing calendar data. This document is intended for payroll administrators and finance teams who use the Access Group portal system and encounter validation failures during year-end payroll processing. The document also provides related article references for users who may encounter similar issues, including errors related to pay group availability, paycode deletions, and database constraint violations.

t: Bulk update salary records
s:
Bulk updating salary records involves making simultaneous changes to the salary information of multiple employees within the payroll system.

ss: Bulk update salary records in the payroll system by uploading a properly formatted CSV file containing employee salary information, effective dates, position codes, and pay rates. This process is essential when implementing company-wide salary adjustments such as annual raises or market-based changes across multiple employees simultaneously. You'll need to prepare your CSV file according to strict formatting requirements—including mandatory fields like Employee Number, Effective Date, New Position Code, and Scale Point—and remove the header row before uploading. Open this document when you need step-by-step instructions for uploading salary changes, understanding the required file format, troubleshooting upload errors, or correcting data using success and exemption reports.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on bulk updating salary records in the payroll system, enabling simultaneous changes to multiple employees' salary information during company-wide adjustments such as annual raises or market-driven changes. The document covers two distinct bulk update processes: one for loading employee new rates of pay and another for loading position new rates of pay, each with specific CSV file format requirements outlined in detailed column specifications. For employee new rates of pay, the CSV must include mandatory fields such as Employee Number, Effective Date (in DDMMYYYY format), New Position Code, Scale Point, and Rate Sequence Number, along with optional fields for Pay Multiplier, Hourly Rate, Daily Rate, Weekly Rate, Annual Salary, Reference, and conditionally the Appointment ID. The file preparation process requires users to format data as comma-separated values, remove header rows before uploading, verify all required columns are populated, ensure the Rate Sequence Number is set to 1, and then navigate to the Uploads menu to select either "Employee New Rates of Pay" or "Load Position New Rates of Pay" depending on the update type. The document addresses common errors and troubleshooting scenarios, including issues where data appears in a single spreadsheet column (resolved by re-importing with comma delimiter specification) and upload failures (resolved by verifying required columns are present and using concise references). Error correction requires using the success report to delete successfully loaded data before re-uploading and consulting exemption report messages to amend unsuccessful data entries before resubmission using the same upload steps.

t: NIC/PRSI category not changing when employee reaches SPA
s:
If the NIC category is not changing when the employee reaches SPA, it is because there are no rules set up. 

 

A rule needs to be set up to automatically change the employee's table when they reach state pension age. If the rule is added after the employee has changed codes, you will need to updat...
ss: When an employee reaches state pension age (SPA), their NIC or PRSI category should automatically change, but this only happens if rules are configured in your payroll system. This document explains how to set up NIC rules in HMRC settings and PRSI rules in either Portal or Back Office (CorePay), including how to specify the age thresholds and class codes for the transition. Open this if an employee's tax category hasn't updated at SPA and you need to configure the automation rules, or if you need to manually update an employee whose category should have already changed.
sl: This document explains how to resolve the issue where an employee's NIC or PRSI category fails to automatically change when they reach state pension age (SPA), which occurs because no rules have been configured in the system. The document provides separate configuration procedures for both HMRC and PRSI setups, allowing payroll administrators to establish the necessary rules that trigger automatic category changes at the appropriate age. For HMRC configuration in Portal, users must navigate to Settings > UK Tax Rates > NIC Rules, enable "Apply Rules in Payroll Run," and configure a NIC RULE by specifying the Age From, Age To, NI Class, and optionally enabling "Update only on from age" to apply the rule only during the period when an employee reaches the specified age and receives payment. For PRSI configuration, users can work through either the Portal (Settings > Ireland Tax Rates > Old Age Pension Rates > Pension Tax Limits) or Back Office (CorePay > Reference > Advance Reference Features > Reference K-P > Old Age Pension Rates > Pension Tax Limits), where they must highlight the relevant age and pension tax limit, then enter the From PRSI Class and To PRSI Class values. The document also notes that if a rule is added after an employee has already changed codes, manual updates to the employee record will be required since retroactive automatic changes will not occur. This guidance is intended for payroll administrators and HR professionals using the Access Group's payroll system who need to ensure proper automation of NIC and PRSI category transitions at state pension age.

t: Configure pay codes
s: Configuring pay codes is a crucial step in payroll management that ensures accurate classification of employee earnings, deductions, and benefits. This process involves defining specific codes that represent various types of compensation, such as regular pay, overtime, bonuses, and deductions for ta...
ss: Pay codes in PeopleXD classify employee earnings, deductions, and benefits—such as regular pay, overtime, bonuses, and tax deductions—and can be configured as standard value (calculated by hours, days, units, or value) or scaled value (based on employee pay scale position). This document walks you through creating and configuring pay codes via the Settings menu and Pay Code Wizard, including the option to clone existing codes for faster setup. Open this guide when you need to set up new pay codes, troubleshoot misconfigured codes causing payroll calculation errors, or ensure unit rates and other details are correctly configured before payroll runs.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide to configuring pay codes in PeopleXD, which is essential for accurate payroll management, compliance with labor laws, and generating reliable financial reports. The document explains that pay codes represent various types of compensation including regular pay, overtime, bonuses, and deductions, and can be configured as either standard value pay codes (calculated on hours, days, units, or value basis) or scaled value pay codes (based on employee position on a pay scale). The configuration process involves navigating to Settings > Codes > Pay Codes, clicking Create New Pay Code, selecting a Payment Type and Payment Subset Type from drop-down menus, entering a unique Pay Code number and Description, then completing each step in the Pay Code Wizard screen before saving. The document recommends cloning an existing pay code when a similar one exists rather than creating from scratch, and advises testing all configuration changes in the UAT environment before applying them to the live system. For troubleshooting misconfigured pay codes that result in incorrect payroll calculations or discrepancies in employee payments, the document outlines steps including identifying whether the pay code is standard or scaled value, cloning an existing correctly configured pay code, adjusting the formula as needed, and replacing the misconfigured code in future payroll periods. Additionally, the document highlights that unit rates must be properly configured for units-based pay codes, and that missing unit rates or configuration details will cause payroll calculation exceptions. This resource is designed for payroll administrators and finance professionals responsible for setting up and maintaining accurate pay code configurations within PeopleXD.

sl: This document provides guidance for resolving an ORA-01400 error that occurs when attempting to load a PeopleHUB file into the system, with the root cause being a missing or improperly positioned START_DATE field in the input data. The error indicates that the START_DATE field is either unpopulated or NULL, which prevents the system from successfully inserting records into the PSOFT_NON_TIMESHEET table in the CoreHR database. The document explains that two categories of errors can occur during PeopleHub file processing: Stop Errors, which block file uploads due to structural formatting issues, and Validation Errors, which occur when data passes format checks but fails internal system validation. To resolve the issue, users must navigate to the PeopleHub Dashboard from the main menu, access the Settings tab, locate the External HR Interface file group, and use the three-dot menu to view the Columns configuration for the appropriate file type (either Allowances/Deductions for NON_001_*** files or Employee for EMP_*** files). Users should then compare their file's column structure against the expected format displayed in the system to verify that the START_DATE field is positioned in the correct column. t: Set up a cycle to or bike to work pay code
s: Setting up a Cycle to Work or Bike to Work pay code is a crucial step in promoting a corporate initiative that encourages employees to commute by bicycle. ss: Setting up a Cycle to Work or Bike to Work pay code allows you to manage tax-efficient bicycle commuting benefits and deductions in your payroll system. This pay code is deducted before Tax, PRSI, and USC, and can be configured as either a Negative Taxable Allowance or an Income Continuance Deduction depending on your client requirements. Open this document when you need to create a new cycle-to-work pay code with the correct settings for taxable indicators, PRSI, USC, and pension parameters. You'll also find guidance on enabling reducing balance options if needed for your organization's sustainability initiative.
sl: This document provides guidance on setting up a Cycle to Work or Bike to Work pay code within a payroll system to support corporate sustainability initiatives while providing tax-efficient benefits to participating employees. The document describes two distinct configuration methods: the first uses a Negative Taxable Allowance approach with Pay Code Type set to Allowance, Taxable Indicator set to Taxable, PRSIable Indicator set to PRSIable, and checkboxes enabled for USCable and ASC Indicator while leaving Pension unchecked; the second alternative uses an Income Continuance Deduction approach with Pay Code Type set to Deduction, Taxable Indicator set to Income Continuance, PRSIable Indicator set to Non-PRSIable, and similar checkbox configurations. A key distinction of this pay code is that it is deducted before Tax, PRSI, and USC calculations, ensuring proper tax treatment. The document includes a specific tip for users implementing a reducing balance pay code to enable the reducing balance option accordingly. Both configuration methods allow administrators to check the Pension Related Deduction box where appropriate to suit individual client requirements. This guidance is intended for payroll administrators and HR professionals who manage employee benefits and need to implement compliant Cycle to Work or Bike to Work schemes within their organization's payroll system.

t: Update pay scales using the pay increase module
s:
Updating pay scales using the pay increase module involves applying systematic salary adjustments across multiple employee pay rates through an automated process. 

 

This module allows you to implement percentage or fixed amount increases to specific pay scales, grades, or employee groups simultan...
ss: The pay increase module in PeopleXD allows you to apply percentage or fixed amount salary adjustments across multiple employee pay rates and grades simultaneously, rather than updating individual records manually. Use this module to define position code ranges and exclusions, preview changes in trial mode before applying them, and set effective dates and minimum/maximum increase limits. Open this document when you need to implement organisation-wide pay scale updates while maintaining consistency and accuracy across your workforce.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on using the pay increase module to apply systematic salary adjustments across multiple employee pay rates simultaneously rather than updating individual records manually. The document covers several key processes: recording pay rate ranges by entering position codes in the Position Code From and To fields (for example, Position 1 to 9999), specifying exclusions under the Record Positions for Exclusions section, and using the Generate Report option to preview all affected position codes before implementation. The module supports two approaches to defining which positions receive increases—either through the Record Ranges and Exclusions for Rate Increases screen or by manually amending position codes on the Maintain Rate Increase Position screen—and includes a delete function to clear recorded ranges if needed. A critical feature is the trial mode under the Applying Percentage/Value Increase to Position Rates option, which allows users to preview increases before the corresponding Apply Percentage/Value Increase to Position Rates screen enforces them permanently. When applying increases, users can configure the Rate Base Date (the date before the new rate takes effect), Date Effective (the actual effective date), and choose between percentage increases with optional minimum and maximum limits or fixed amount increases entered in the Min Value field. Additional settings include selecting which rate types to adjust (annual, weekly, daily, and hourly rates are selected by default), setting decimal place rounding preferences, and assigning a custom reference for the transaction. This document is essential for payroll administrators and HR professionals responsible for managing organisation-wide salary adjustments while maintaining consistency and accuracy across all employee pay grades and groups.

f the above error appears after uploading an employee’s new pay rates, the file contains incorrect data. This may include an invalid date format, an incorrect employee reference, or an incorrect number of columns.

ss: When uploading new employee pay rates, the "Problem With Record 1 On File" error indicates your file contains formatting issues such as invalid date formats, incorrect employee references, or the wrong number of columns. Common causes include Excel removing leading zeros from dates (like changing 01052022 to 1052022), trailing commas being stripped, or missing columns in the file structure. Use Notepad to manually inspect and fix your file, ensuring dates have leading zeros, the employee reference doesn't exceed 10 characters, and the file contains at least 10 columns before re-uploading. If errors persist, try uploading the file in smaller batches or test with a single row first.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving the "Problem With Record 1 On File" error that occurs after uploading employee pay rate files to a system. The error typically indicates that the uploaded file contains incorrectly formatted or structured data, which may include invalid date formats, incorrect employee references, or an incorrect number of columns. The document addresses several specific file formatting issues: leading zeros that Excel may inadvertently remove from dates (requiring manual correction in Notepad, such as changing 1052022 to 01052022), employee reference sections that must not exceed 10 characters, and trailing commas that Excel may remove during file processing. A critical requirement is that the file must contain at least 10 columns (9 commas) when opened in Notepad, with columns 7 to 10 being optional but at least one containing data, and all columns must be present in the correct format even if blank. The document suggests resolution strategies including manually editing the file in Notepad to restore formatting, breaking large files into two parts for separate uploads, or testing with a single line upload to isolate the problem. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators, HR staff, or system users responsible for bulk uploading employee pay rate data into the Access Group's CorePay system, and it references related articles addressing similar errors in the pay rate upload process.

t: Pro Rata indicators on an allowance
s:

By understanding these indicators, you can ensure accurate adjustments and compliance with Benefits In Kind (...
ss: Pro-rata indicators on allowance pay codes determine how the payroll system calculates and applies allowances based on employee hours and availability. These settings are essential for ensuring accurate adjustments and compliance with Benefits In Kind (BIK) regulations, particularly when deductions apply for days an employee is available. Use this document when you need to configure allowance pay codes and understand how the Pro Rata Indicator, Pro Rata Element, and Pro Rata Calculation checkboxes affect payment calculations based on contract hours, timesheet hours, or days worked.
sl: This document explains the pro-rata indicators available on the Allowances/Payment tab of an allowance pay code within the Access Group payroll system, and how these settings control allowance calculation and application across different employment scenarios. The document covers three specific checkbox indicators that can be configured: the Pro Rata Indicator, which applies pro-rata calculations to permanent or recurring allowance payments based on an employee's contract hours versus actual timesheet basic hours (for example, an employee working 20 of their contracted 39 hours would receive 20/39 of the allowance value); the Pro Rata Element, which should be enabled only for hourly or daily pay codes that qualify as pro-rata elements and contribute toward the total hours calculation; and the Pro Rata Calculation checkbox, which determines whether pro-rata adjustments are based on the specific number of days the allowance is paid for or the total number of days in the pay period. Understanding and correctly configuring these indicators is essential for ensuring accurate payroll calculations and compliance with Benefits In Kind (BIK) regulations, particularly when applying BIK deductions for the days an employee is available to work. The document is intended for payroll administrators and HR professionals who configure allowance pay codes and need to ensure that allowances are calculated correctly according to employee contract terms and actual hours worked.

t: PayWise+ does not have a balance from XD
s:

The issue occurs when the WFM period closure process is incom...
ss: PayWise+ relies on balance data from PeopleXD via the WFM system to enable early wage payments, but this connection fails when the WFM period closure process is incomplete or encounters errors. Common causes include manually rejecting period closure during timesheet generation, system errors during the closure process, or synchronisation failures between WFM and PayWise+. Open this document if employees cannot access earned wages through PayWise+, or if you need to manually close WFM periods, resolve period closure errors, or regenerate timesheets after support intervention. The guide provides step-by-step instructions for automatic and manual period closure in WFM, identifying system errors, and reprocessing timesheets.
sl: This document explains how to resolve the issue where PayWise+ cannot access balance data from PeopleXD (XD), which prevents employees from retrieving their earned wages through early payment features. The problem typically stems from incomplete or failed WFM period closure processes, including scenarios where users manually reject period closure during timesheet generation, technical errors prevent proper completion, or data synchronisation fails between the WFM and PayWise+ systems. The document provides two approaches for period closure: automatic closure by selecting "Yes" when prompted during timesheet generation in WFM, which triggers PayWise+ message generation, or manual closure through the Portal by navigating to WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Configuration > Company and Calendar Config, selecting the relevant company, and toggling the "Completed" switch on for the target period. It also addresses system errors that can occur during closure, identifiable when a closed period fails to appear in the WFM Generate Timesheets - History screen, requiring users to raise a support case for investigation. If the underlying error is resolved but the payroll period remains unclosed, administrators can reopen the period by toggling the "Completed" switch off, then regenerate and close the timesheets again to restore data synchronisation. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators, WFM system users, and support personnel who manage timesheet processing and troubleshoot payment access issues in organisations using the PayWise+ and PeopleXD integrated systems.

ss: Cost centres in payroll are accounting units that allocate employee-related expenses such as salary to specific departments or cost codes, integrated with your Financial Management System (FMS). sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on managing cost centres within the payroll system, explaining that cost centres are organizational units used to allocate employee-related expenses such as salary and costs to specific departments or areas for accounting purposes, with integration into the Financial Management System (FMS). The document explains how to assign cost centres to employees through the People Management dashboard under Cost Allocations, and demonstrates the system's flexibility by noting that temporary reassignments can redirect an employee's costs between departments when coverage situations arise. ss: Payroll filters let you customize views of payroll data on the Payroll Dashboard by showing only information relevant to your role, working within your existing user and paygroup access settings. You can create multiple filters using specific criteria from reference data, then apply them as default filters (which load automatically), or apply them individually to input screens like Joiners, Rejoiners, Pay Changes, and Manage Employees. sl: This document explains how to use payroll filters in the Access Group system to streamline payroll data entry and review by displaying only relevant information to individual users while respecting existing access controls. The document covers three core processes: creating filters on the Payroll Dashboard by navigating to Settings > Payroll Filters and selecting reference data fields to include, editing existing filters through the three-dot menu to modify criteria (with changes applying to all affected users), and applying filters in three ways—as default filters that automatically load on the Joiners, Rejoiners, Pay Changes, and Manage Payroll Employees screens, as input screen filters on the Joiners, Rejoiners, Pay Changes, and Manage Employees input screens, or on the Employee tab. Payroll administrators use this functionality to customize their view of employee data without affecting other users' visibility, and the document notes that payroll filters are available only on the enhanced Joiners, Movers, and Leavers (JML) screens. The document specifies the exact menu paths and field names required for implementation, including the Core Portal Pay menu option "Settings - Payroll Filters" and multiple web services options such as "Get group criteria" and "Create group criteria details" for system administrators configuring user access. Default filters persist when users navigate away from the Manage Payroll screen or log out, ensuring consistent filtered views across sessions, while the document warns that deleting or renaming a filter removes it as a default for any users who had it applied.

t: Configure Irish Statutory Sick Pay
s:
