ss: Delegate approver nominations in your approval workflow can be removed by contacting the support team to run a required script. You'll need to raise a support case online, reference this article, and provide the employee number for the person whose nomination you want to end. Open this article if you need to remove someone from their delegate approver role or if a nomination needs to be terminated.
sl: This document provides instructions for removing delegate approver nominations from the Access Group system, a task that requires backend support intervention rather than self-service completion. The process involves contacting the support team by raising a new case through the online case management system and referencing the article title "Remove delegate approver nominations" along with the affected employee number. The support team will execute a script on the backend to end the delegate approver nominations for the specified employee. This document is intended for Access Group administrators, HR personnel, or managers who need to revoke delegation of approval authority that an employee may have previously been granted. The document appears to be part of a broader support knowledge base covering related approval and payroll processing issues, including scenarios involving non-starters, manager access permissions in ESS timesheets, salary processing errors, and payroll report reconciliation problems.

t: Error: 'Warning: NI Thresholds not equal to NIable Pay'
s:
If the above error message appears when trying to calculate and save a manual payment, this is because of a mismatch between the entered National Insurance (NI) thresholds and the total NIable pay. 

 

NIable pay= LEL + PT + ST + UE

 

When the following warning appears on the screen :

 

"Warnin...
ss: Manual payment calculations in your payroll system fail with a National Insurance threshold mismatch warning when the entered NI thresholds (LEL + PT + ST + UE) don't add up to the total NIable pay. This error occurs because the 'Above UEL' value, which represents earnings above the Upper Earnings Limit, is essential for matching the threshold breakdown to your total NIable pay. Open this document when you encounter the "Warning: NI Thresholds not equal to NIable Pay" message and need to resolve the discrepancy by verifying the employee's correct tax details in the portal.
sl: This document explains the "Warning: NI Thresholds not equal to NIable Pay" error message that appears when calculating and saving a manual payment in the Access Group payroll system, which occurs due to a mismatch between entered National Insurance thresholds and the total NIable pay. The document defines NIable pay as the sum of four components: LEL (Lower Earnings Limit), PT (Primary Threshold), ST (Secondary Threshold), and UE (Above UEL, representing earnings above the Upper Earnings Limit). The warning message specifically alerts users that the thresholds entered do not add up to the total NIable pay, with particular emphasis on ensuring the 'Above UEL' value is included to maintain an accurate breakdown. To resolve this issue, users must verify the employee's correct tax thresholds by navigating to Employee in the portal, searching for the relevant employee, selecting View, clicking Tax Details, and highlighting the appropriate year. This document is intended for payroll administrators and HR professionals who process manual payments and need to troubleshoot National Insurance calculation discrepancies within the Access Group payroll portal. The document also references related errors involving NI configurations, apprenticeship levy figures, NI letters, FPS submissions, and threshold population requirements, providing users with cross-references to similar NI-related issues they may encounter.

t: Error: 'IBAN does not match BBAN Length'
s:
If the International Bank Account Number (IBAN) provided does not match the expected length of the Basic Bank Account Number (BBAN) associated with that specific account, it may be due to one of the following reasons:

The bank identifier for the bank has not been set up.

The BBAN length is incorre...
ss: IBAN and BBAN validation in CorePay affects international bank account setup for employees. This document helps when you receive an "IBAN does not match BBAN Length" error during employee bank detail entry, which typically occurs because the bank identifier hasn't been configured or the BBAN length is set incorrectly. Open this guide if you're setting up foreign bank accounts and need step-by-step instructions to resolve validation errors in either the Portal or Back Office environment.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses the error message "IBAN does not match BBAN Length" and provides troubleshooting guidance for users working with international bank account setup in their system. The document explains that this error occurs when the International Bank Account Number (IBAN) provided does not correspond with the expected length of the Basic Bank Account Number (BBAN) for a specific account, which can result from either a missing bank identifier setup or an incorrectly configured BBAN length. The document identifies that IBAN-to-BBAN correspondence is critical for ensuring accuracy in international banking transactions and preventing fund transfer errors. For users encountering a missing bank identifier, the document provides separate step-by-step instructions for both the Portal (navigating to Settings > Bank Details > Bank Country Codes to verify BBAN Length for the BIC Country code) and the Back Office (accessing CorePay > Reference > Bank Details > Bank Identifier to add the relevant identifier). For users with an incorrect BBAN length, parallel instructions are provided across both interfaces, with the Portal route involving Settings > Bank Details > Bank Identifier and the Back Office route requiring CorePay > Reference > Bank Details > Bank County Codes, followed by verification and re-entry of employee bank details. The document emphasizes an important distinction that BBAN and IBAN lengths are not equivalent and directs users to consult the IBAN Registry document for country-specific details. This resource is primarily used by back-office administrators and payroll personnel responsible for setting up and maintaining foreign bank account information for employees within the Access Group system.

t: Back Office: Change PRSI class
s:
Changing the PRSI (Pay Related Social Insurance) class in Back Office refers to updating an employee's classification for social insurance contributions based on their employment status or earnings. 

 

This change is necessary to ensure that employees are contributing the correct amount towards th...
ss: Changing an employee's PRSI (Pay Related Social Insurance) class in CorePay Back Office ensures they're contributing the correct amount towards social security benefits, which affects their pension entitlement, unemployment benefits, and other state supports. Use this process when an employee's employment status or earnings change and their social insurance classification needs to be updated. Access the employee record in CorePay, navigate to Maintain Employee Details, update the PRSI Class field, and save your changes. Open this guide if you need step-by-step instructions for updating PRSI classifications or if you're troubleshooting contribution-related issues for individual employees.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre explains how to change an employee's PRSI (Pay Related Social Insurance) class in the Back Office system, which is essential for ensuring employees contribute the correct amount towards their social security benefits. The PRSI class classification directly impacts employee entitlement to pensions, unemployment benefits, and other state-supported benefits, making accurate classification critical for payroll administrators. The process involves navigating through the CorePay module by clicking CorePay followed by Employee, then accessing the Maintain Employee Details section where the PRSI Class field can be updated. Once the necessary changes to the PRSI Class have been made in the employee details screen, users must click the save icon to commit the changes to the system. This document is primarily used by back office and payroll professionals who manage employee records and social insurance contributions, particularly when an employee's employment status or earnings change. The document also references related issues that administrators may encounter, including PRSI/NI week overrides, problems with NIC/PRSI categories not updating when employees reach State Pension Age, discrepancies between cumulative and historical PRSI weeks on pre year-end reports, and situations where only one PRSI week is generating for an employee, as well as PRSI Class Automation functionality.

t: Update an employee's cumulative pay
s:
You may need to manually update an employee's Year-to-Date cumulative values if there was an input error for a new starter or an issue when transferring an employee between companies or pay groups. 

📌Note: Only update Year-to-Date Cumulatives at the beginning of payroll processing. Do not make thes...
ss: Manually update an employee's Year-to-Date cumulative values in the payroll system when input errors occur for new starters or during employee transfers between companies or pay groups. Access the employee record in portal, navigate to Legislative > Year to Date Cumulatives, and make corrections before running payroll updates or confirming timesheets. This task must be completed at the beginning of payroll processing to avoid data inconsistencies. Open this document when you need to correct cumulative totals that are showing incorrect amounts due to data entry mistakes or system transfer issues.
sl: This document provides guidance on manually updating an employee's Year-to-Date cumulative pay values in the payroll system when errors or data transfer issues occur, such as input mistakes for new starters or problems when moving an employee between companies or pay groups. The document emphasizes a critical timing restriction: Year-to-Date cumulative updates must only be performed at the beginning of payroll processing and must not be made after running a payroll update or confirming the timesheet job, as doing so could create data integrity issues. The process is executed through the portal by navigating to the Employee section, using the search field to locate the relevant employee, clicking the VIEW button beside their name, and then accessing the Legislative menu followed by Year to Date Cumulatives. The document is intended for payroll administrators and HR staff who need to correct cumulative pay data in the system before payroll processing begins. Additionally, the document references related articles and reports that users may find helpful, including guidance on uplifting employee tax codes, balancing data check reports, and accessing the Employee Cumulatives (ALL) report (PAYB084B) available in both Portal and Back Office versions, as well as the Detailed Observation report (PAYB300DET) for identifying incorrect totals.

t: Change an employee's pay method
s:
Changing an employee's pay method involves updating how they receive their wages, such as switching from a paper cheque to direct deposit or altering the frequency of payments.

 

This process is vital for ensuring employees receive their wages in a way that suits their preferences and aligns with ...
ss: Changing an employee's pay method updates how they receive their wages—such as switching from paper cheque to direct deposit or adjusting payment frequency. You'll use this process when an employee requests a different payment arrangement or when you need to align their pay delivery with company payroll procedures. The steps differ depending on your system: in the Portal, navigate through People Management to the employee's Bank Detail section, or in CorePay Back Office, access the employee's Payment Details to select a new pay method. A note: when switching from cheque (CH) to direct payment (PP), ensure you record the employee's BIC, IBAN, sort code, and account number for the bank file.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for updating an employee's pay method within a payroll system, covering changes such as switching from paper cheque to direct deposit or modifying payment frequency. The process is essential for aligning employee wage delivery with their preferences and organizational payroll procedures. For Portal users, the task involves navigating from the dashboard menu through People Management, locating the specific employee via the Search function, and accessing their Personnel Profile through the Actions menu, where the Bank Detail section contains the Pay Method drop-down for selecting the desired payment option before saving changes. Back Office users follow a parallel process by accessing CorePay, selecting the Employee module, entering the employee number in the Personnel Profile, and locating Payment Details in the Select Detail window to modify the pay method accordingly. A critical note highlights that when changing the pay method from "CH" (cheque) to "PP" (presumably another payment type), users must verify and record the employee's BIC and IBAN or Sort Code and Account Number to ensure accurate information is included on the bank file. The document serves HR and payroll administrators who need to process employee payment preference updates within the system.

t: NI category auto updating back to an incorrect letter
s:
The issue of the National Insurance (NI) category auto-updating to an incorrect letter occurs due to system errors, incorrect data inputs, or updates in employee status that are not reflected accurately.

 

To resolve this, check the employees' date of birth in Workforce management and compare them...
ss: NI category auto-updating in your payroll system can revert to an incorrect letter due to system errors, incorrect data inputs, or employee status changes that aren't properly reflected. You'll need to verify the employee's date of birth in Workforce Management and cross-reference it against the NIC rules configured in your Payroll settings (Settings > UK Tax Rates > NIC Rules). Open this document if an employee's NI category keeps reverting to the wrong letter despite previous updates, or when the "Update Only on From Age" indicator isn't triggering correctly based on their date of birth.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses a technical issue where National Insurance (NI) categories automatically revert to incorrect letter designations due to system errors, faulty data entries, or employee status changes that fail to update properly in the system. The document provides a troubleshooting procedure that involves verifying employee information across two key modules: Workforce management, where employee dates of birth are stored, and Payroll, where National Insurance contribution (NIC) rules are configured and applied. To resolve the issue, users must navigate to Settings, locate the UK Tax Rates section, and access the NIC Rules configuration to manually review whether the rules align correctly with each affected employee's date of birth. A critical system behavior explained in the document is that the "Update Only on From Age" indicator will only activate based on the employee's date of birth, meaning incorrect dates of birth in Workforce management can prevent proper NI category updates. This document is primarily intended for payroll administrators and HR professionals using the Access Group Back Office system who need to diagnose and correct NI category auto-update failures. The document also references related troubleshooting articles covering adjacent issues such as NIC/PRSI category changes at State Pension Age, methods for updating employee PPS or NI numbers, NI arrears calculations following category changes, and procedures for updating NI letters after employee rehire scenarios.

s:

ss: Set up exclusion orders in PeopleXD Payroll to prevent employees from paying the P35 Levy and manage their tax status after Revenue Payroll Notifications (RPNs) are generated. This involves enabling the P35 Levy Exclusion toggle on the employee's Tax Details screen and optionally adjusting their Universal Social Charge (USC) status. You may also need to enable the Enhanced Tax Exclusion system configuration setting so the system automatically generates PAYE refunds for excluded employees rather than requiring manual adjustments. Use this guide when you've received RPNs and need to place an employee on a tax exclusion order or troubleshoot why PAYE refunds aren't being generated.
sl: This document provides instructions for setting up an exclusion order for employees in the PeopleXD Payroll system after Revenue Payroll Notifications (RPNs) have been generated. The primary process involves navigating to the Employee section in Portal, searching for and viewing the relevant employee record, then accessing the Tax Details screen to enable the P35 Levy Exclusion toggle and saving the changes. The document also addresses a common issue where PAYE refunds are not being automatically generated for tax-excluded employees, which occurs due to the Enhanced Tax Exclusion system configuration setting not being enabled. To resolve this issue, users must navigate to the Payroll Dashboard, access Settings, select System Configuration, and then click on Payroll Validation/Update to enable the Enhanced Tax Exclusion toggle. The document recommends testing any significant system configuration changes in User Acceptance Testing (UAT) environments before applying them to live production environments, as enabling Enhanced Tax Exclusion will impact employee payslips and PAYE submissions to Revenue. An additional consideration mentioned is checking whether employees need to pay Universal Social Charge (USC) and updating their USC status to exempt on the Tax Details screen if applicable. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and finance professionals managing tax compliance and exclusion orders within PeopleXD Payroll.

Work pattern shift

Use this document when you need to troubleshoot missing salary offsets and follow step-by-step instructions to reassign shifts or adjust FTE settings in Back Office. sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving a specific issue in the Access Group's CoreTime and CorePay integrated system where unpaid leave is recorded in CoreTime but fails to generate a corresponding salary reduction in CorePay. The document identifies two primary causes for this problem: incorrect work pattern shift assignments and improper FTE (Full-Time Equivalent) value configurations. For the work pattern shift issue, the document provides detailed step-by-step instructions requiring users to navigate through Back Office to CoreTime, then to Pers Data, Person Maintenance, and Shift Types, where they must assign the employee to a suitable shift with properly configured default hours and set the effective date for the change. This document is designed for payroll administrators, HR personnel, and system users who manage employee leave records and salary processing in CoreTime and CorePay and need to diagnose why expected salary deductions are not appearing in payroll systems.

t: What are increments and what are the rules surrounding them
s:
What is an increment?

An increment is an increase or addition to an employee's pay, especially one that is part of a series based on a fixed scale.

 

What is the Increment Process?

This process applies only to employees who have a pay scale salary. 

 Increments cannot be automatically generated...
ss: Increments are automatic salary increases applied to employees on pay scales, managed through either CorePay (during payroll runs) or CorePersonnel (via nightly system jobs). This document explains how the increment process works, including how increment due dates are set and managed at the post appointment level, how the system automatically progresses employees through pay scale points, and what controls like increment hold indicators and bar points do. Open this if you need to understand how increments are calculated and applied, how to set or update increment due dates on employee records, or how to manage increment holds and pay scale progression rules.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive overview of salary increments in the CorePay and CorePersonnel systems, defining an increment as a fixed pay increase typically applied annually or at specified employee milestones. The increment process applies specifically to employees on pay scale salaries and eliminates the need for manual salary amendments by automatically advancing employees to the next point on their designated pay scale. Increments can be processed either through CorePay during payroll runs with reference codes starting with "PAY," or through CorePersonnel via a nightly system job that generates increments a fixed number of days before the increment due date to allow time for HR and payroll approval or rejection. The document explains key configuration elements including the increment due date (captured and updated on the pay profile screen during appointment or later as needed), the increment hold indicator (which temporarily prevents increment processing while allowing for back-dated pay if removed), and pay scale point increment rules that control progression, maximum points, tenure requirements, bar points, and age restrictions. The increment system job automatically reviews all employees' increment due dates, creates new salary records based on pay scale rules, and updates the next increment due date—typically 12 months forward—unless the employee has reached the top of the scale or other restrictions apply. The document clarifies that increment details are managed at the post appointment level rather than the employee level, making it crucial for employees with multiple post appointments to have the increment due date recorded separately for each position.

t: What are Increments and what are the rules surrounding them
s:
What is an increment?

An Increment is an increase or addition to an Employees pay, especially one of a series on a fixed scale.

 

What is the increment process?

This process is used to automatically create a new salary record for an employee, which moves them to the next point on their pay scale...
ss: Increments are automatic salary increases that move employees up a fixed pay scale point, removing the need for manual salary amendments. This process works in CorePersonnel through a nightly system job that reviews increment due dates and creates new salary records, or in CorePay during payroll runs. You'll use this document to understand how to set and manage increment due dates, configure pay scale point rules (including bar points and age restrictions), and control increments using the increment hold indicator. Open this if you need to set up automatic pay progression for employees, manage increment dates across multiple post appointments, or understand how the increment system job processes salary changes.
sl: This document explains what increments are and describes the automated process for applying salary increases within the Access Group's CorePersonnel and CorePay systems. An increment is a pay increase that moves an employee to the next point on a fixed pay scale, and the increment process automatically creates new salary records rather than requiring manual salary amendments for standard annual increases that can be applied organization-wide on a common date or on employee-specific dates such as work anniversaries. The document details how increments are managed differently depending on where they are run: when executed from CorePay, they generate during payroll runs with specific reference codes, while CorePersonnel increments are generated by a nightly system job several days before the increment due date to allow for HR/Payroll approval or rejection. Key attributes and management tasks include the Increment Due Date (which can be captured during the appointment stage or updated directly on the Pay Profile screen) and the Increment Hold Indicator (which prevents the increment job from processing on the scheduled due date, though backdating will occur if the hold is removed). The nightly increment system job automatically reviews all employees' increment due dates, moves eligible employees to the next pay scale point by creating an approved salary amendment, and generates a new increment due date typically 12 months later. The document also explains pay scale point increment rules that control progression, define alternative pay scales when maximum points are reached, set length of time requirements on each point, establish age restrictions, and use bar points to prevent progression beyond certain levels. Additionally, it clarifies that increment due dates are only removed when the increment process itself brings an employee to the top of the scale, not when manual salary amendments or bar points prevent further progression.

Common reasons for changing an employee's pay group include changes in pay frequency (such as monthly or weekly), different payment types (wages versus salary), moves to different tax jurisdictions, or contract modifications. The document emphasizes an important system constraint: employees cannot be moved to a payroll period that is earlier than their current pay group's period. t: What happens when an employee has a DEA and DEO
s: If an employee has both a DEO (Child Maintenance) and a DEA, the DEO will take priority over the DEA. The system will check the employee's net wage and ensure that it is equal to or greater than 60% before calculating the DEA. If the net wage falls below this threshold, the DEA will not be calculate...
ss: When an employee has both a DEA (Attachment of Earnings) and a DEO (Child Maintenance) order, DEO takes priority and PeopleXD protects a minimum of 60% of the employee's net wage before applying the DEA. The system evaluates net pay each period to determine if the DEA should be deducted in full, partially, or not at all, ensuring the employee never receives less than 60% of their net earnings after both deductions. Open this document if you need to understand how PeopleXD handles competing deduction orders and the protected earnings threshold that applies to DEA calculations.
sl: This document explains how the People XD payroll system handles situations where an employee is subject to both a DEO (Child Maintenance) and a DEA (Attachment of Earnings Order) simultaneously. The core process involves a priority hierarchy where the DEO takes precedence and is deducted first, with the DEA calculated only after the DEO deduction is applied. The system enforces a protected earnings threshold of 60% of the employee's net wage, meaning that if either deduction causes the net pay to fall below this 60% threshold, the DEA will not be calculated or will be calculated partially. During each pay period, People XD automatically evaluates the employee's net wage to determine whether the full DEA deduction should apply, a partial deduction should apply, or no deduction should occur, with calculations designed to comply with HMRC guidelines. The document is designed for payroll administrators and HR professionals who use People XD and need to understand the interaction between multiple earnings deductions, particularly the compliance requirement that employees must retain at least 60% of their net earnings after all deductions are applied. The document references related articles on setting up a DEA pay code, troubleshooting incorrect attachment of earnings deductions, and resolving issues with AEO protected earnings functionality.

t: Impact of periodic employee hours setting on the Minimum Wage Exception report
s:
The Minimum Wage Exception report identifies employees whose calculated hourly rate falls below the National Minimum Wage(NMW), the National Living Wage (NLW), or the minimum apprenticeship rate. The report compares the employee’s hourly rate against the statutory rate applicable to their age.

 

T...
ss: The Minimum Wage Exception report identifies employees whose hourly rate falls below the National Minimum Wage, National Living Wage, or apprenticeship minimum rate by comparing calculated hourly rates against statutory thresholds. The Periodic Employee Hours setting in Payroll Checking controls how the hourly rate is calculated—enabling it uses pay-per-period divided by contracted hours, while disabling it annualizes pay based on pay frequency multipliers and minimum wage report weeks. Open this document if your pay groups use non-weekly pay frequencies (fortnightly, monthly, etc.) where contracted hours don't represent weekly hours, or if you need to understand why minimum wage exceptions are being flagged for specific employees.
sl: This document explains the Minimum Wage Exception report, which identifies employees whose calculated hourly rate falls below the National Minimum Wage (NMW), National Living Wage (NLW), or minimum apprenticeship rate by comparing each employee's hourly rate against the statutory rate applicable to their age. The document provides step-by-step instructions for accessing and configuring the Periodic Employee Hours setting within the payroll system by navigating to Manage Payroll > Payroll Checking > View Gross to Nett > Minimum Wage tab, where users can toggle this setting on or off depending on whether contracted hours represent weekly hours or alternative pay periods. The critical function of this setting is to control how the system calculates hourly rates: when enabled, the hourly rate is calculated as Pay in Period divided by Hours at Appointment Level, while when disabled, the system uses a multi-step calculation involving annual multipliers based on pay frequency (12 for monthly, 52 for weekly, 26 for fortnightly, 4 for quarterly, and 2 for half-yearly), the Minimum Wage Report Weeks field from the Pay Group configuration, and hours at appointment level. Users can verify the Minimum Wage Report Weeks setting by navigating to Settings > Pay Groups, selecting the relevant pay group from a dropdown menu, and reviewing the field, which defaults to 52 weeks if blank. The document is designed for payroll administrators and compliance officers who need to ensure accurate minimum wage calculations and resolve discrepancies between contracted hours and pay periods, and it includes worked examples demonstrating both calculation methods along with links to related error resolution articles and the full Minimum Wage User Guide.

t: Attachment of earnings deduction incorrect
s:
If the repayment amount for the AOE or DEA deduction seems incorrect, it may be because the net earnings used in the calculation do not align with the expected formula.

 

For both AOE and DEA, the net earnings for an employee are calculated using the following formula:

Net Earnings = Gross Pay – ...
ss: Attachment of Earnings Orders (AOE) and Deduction of Earnings Administration (DEA) calculations in your payroll system depend on net earnings derived from gross pay minus specific deductions like PAYE, National Insurance, and pension contributions. If an AOE or DEA repayment amount appears incorrect, the issue likely stems from net earnings not matching the expected calculation formula, which uses tiered rates applied to earnings bands. Open this document if you need to verify why a deduction amount doesn't match what you expected, or to understand which deductions are included (and excluded) when calculating net earnings for court-ordered or administrative earnings deductions.
sl: This document explains how to troubleshoot situations where the repayment amount for Attachment of Earnings (AOE) or Deduction of Earnings Administration (DEA) deductions appears incorrect, typically due to misalignment between calculated and expected net earnings values. The document outlines the precise formula used to calculate net earnings for both AOE and DEA: Net Earnings equals Gross Pay minus Applicable Deductions, where applicable deductions include only PAYE (Income Tax), Employee NI/PRSI, and Pension contributions—notably excluding other deductions such as student loans. Once net earnings are determined, the deduction amount itself is calculated using a two-tier formula: (Lower band × lower rate%) + (Remainder of net earnings above lower band × balance rate), with the lower band, lower rate, and balance rate values stored on the specific pay code used for AOE. The document provides a worked example for a monthly employee earning £2000.00 with £350.00 in applicable deductions, demonstrating how the net earnings of £1650.00 are used to calculate a final AOE deduction of £336.60 using lower band (£1480), lower rate (17%), and balance rate (50%) parameters. This document is intended for payroll administrators, HR professionals, or finance staff who use Access Group's payroll system and need to validate or correct AOE and DEA calculations when the deduction amounts do not match expected values. The document references related setup tasks such as configuring DEA pay codes and notes other related scenarios involving DEA and Deduction of Earnings Orders (DEO).

t: When are PAYE Modernisation correction submission files generated

ss: PAYE Modernisation correction submission files are automatically generated when specific payroll changes occur, such as updating an employee's PPSN, leave date, or recording a cancel payment, or when an employee passes away. You can also manually create three types of correction submissions—normal submission, full resubmission, or delete submission—depending on the error that occurred and whether data has already been reported to Revenue. Use this document to understand which correction file type to generate for your situation and the specific scenarios where the system creates correction files automatically. Open this if you need to correct inaccurate payroll data that's already been submitted to Revenue.
sl: This document explains when and how the PAYE Modernisation (PMOD) system automatically generates correction submission files to fix inaccurate payroll data that has already been reported to Revenue, along with the three manual submission types available: Normal submission, Full resubmission, and Delete submission. The system generates correction files automatically in four specific scenarios: when an employee's PPSN (Payee Public Services Number) is updated and differs from what was previously reported to Revenue (except when only changing from a PPSN ending in "W"), when an employee's leave date is updated and differs from previously reported dates, when a cancel payment is entered for a previous period, or when an employee is recorded as deceased. A Full resubmission option is used when the original file contained errors such as an incorrect pay date, and it deletes all previously sent payslips for that pay group and period while submitting corrected ones with updated details. A Delete submission file contains only delete line IDs and is used to remove employees who were incorrectly included in a submission or to delete duplicate files by specifying the submission ID, though it should not be used if a payment needs to be cancelled—a delete cancel function should be used instead. This document serves payroll administrators and finance professionals who use the Access Group's payroll system and need to correct submission errors, access the PMOD processing interface, and understand which correction method applies to their specific situation, with related guidance available through articles on creating PAYE Modernisation files, reviewing pay group parameters, and managing deleted or resubmitted payments.

t: Impact on RPN process for leavers, rehires and temporary rejoiners
s:

This system automatically updates employee tax details as circumstances change, en...
ss: The Revenue Payroll Notification (RPN) system provides real-time tax information from Irish Revenue, and managing it correctly is critical when employees leave, rejoin, or return temporarily. This document explains the specific RPN procedures to follow in CoreHR for leavers (whose RPN details update automatically), rehires (using either existing or new employee numbers), and temporary rejoiners (with different processes depending on whether they rejoin in the same tax year or the previous year). Open this if you're processing employee departures, rehires, or temporary returns and need to ensure accurate RPN retrieval and tax compliance throughout these transitions.
sl: This document explains how the Revenue Payroll Notification (RPN) system, a real-time tax information service from Irish Revenue, is affected when employees leave, are rehired, or return temporarily, and provides specific procedures for maintaining tax compliance during these employment changes. For leavers, the payroll submission file automatically notifies Revenue during the employee's final pay period, after which the employee no longer appears in the RPN retrieval system once processed in CoreHR. When rehiring employees, the document outlines two scenarios: reactivating an existing employee record with the same employee number (recommended) or creating a new employee record (not recommended), both requiring the Retrieve New Employee RPNs process and generation of a new Employment ID with valid characters [A-Za-z0-9_\-]. For temporary rejoiners within the same tax year, users should retrieve the employee's RPN using their most recent Employment ID without treating it as new employment, whereas temporary rejoiners from the previous year are treated as new employment requiring retrieval of a new employee RPN and generation of a fresh Employment ID. The document clarifies important field-level distinctions, noting that when retrieving RPNs at the employee level the company last updated field is unavailable, but when retrieving at company level the employee reference is blank and company last updated defaults. If no RPN is returned during retrieval, the employee will be placed on emergency tax at the updated RPN step, and specific submission file details—such as start and end dates matching the pay date—inform Revenue about one-day temporary employment situations.

ss: PAYE Modernisation (PMOD) file submissions to revenue may accidentally exclude employees, preventing their payroll details from being transmitted and creating compliance gaps. Follow this when you discover an employee was mistakenly marked as excluded from PMOD and their payroll information needs to be properly submitted to revenue for earlier pay periods.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide for resolving the situation where an employee has been mistakenly excluded from the PAYE Modernisation (PMOD) file submitted to revenue, which prevents their payroll details from being transmitted and can create reporting and compliance discrepancies. The document explains that exclusions typically occur when an employee is accidentally marked as excluded during payroll processing, and the system will not automatically correct this omission in future submissions. To resolve the issue, users must follow three primary steps within the Portal system: first, unexclude the employee by navigating to Manage Payroll > relevant pay group > Outputs > ROS > PAYE Modernisation > Employee Parameters, then disabling the Exclude Employee toggle and saving the changes. Second, users must enable the Previous Periods toggle in the pay group parameters by accessing Manage Payroll > relevant pay group > Outputs > ROS > PAYE Modernisation > Pay Group Parameters to allow submissions for earlier pay periods. Third, users generate a normal submission through the PAYE Modernisation Files Process by selecting Generate Submission File, choosing Normal Submission type, selecting the relevant pay group and employee, and entering an Override Payment Date to ensure the submission reflects the original pay period. The document includes an important warning that if the employee was excluded before the payroll was finalized, users must raise a case referencing the article and providing the employee reference, payroll period, and confirmation of the erroneous exclusion. Finally, the document recommends verifying all employee details including earnings, deductions, and tax information before submission to ensure accuracy of the corrected file.

sl: This document provides instructions for transferring Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) files from PeopleXD Payroll to Revenue, which is a mandatory compliance task that must be completed on or before the date employees are paid for any payroll run containing ERR-qualifying payments. The transfer process begins by navigating to Outputs > ROS > Enhanced Reporting Requirements > ERR Files Process, where users select "Transfer Submission File" from the Select ERR Action drop-down menu, choose the relevant company, and then enable the Transfer File toggle for each pay group before clicking Transfer. The document addresses the scenario where multiple submission files (such as original and correction submissions) are transferred for the same period by recommending users also complete a Check ERR Run process to ensure accuracy. After transfer, Revenue responds with a status update displayed in the Status column indicating whether the file was successfully "Transferred," was "Rejected" with a reason provided, or remains "Pending" while Revenue processes it. Following the file transfer and completion of the Check ERR Run process, users must confirm the transfer by returning to Manage Payroll > Outputs > ROS > Enhanced Reporting Requirements > ERR Files Process, selecting "Transfer Submission File," enabling the Confirmed toggle, and clicking Yes. This document is used by payroll administrators and compliance professionals in organizations using PeopleXD Payroll who need to meet Irish Revenue reporting obligations for enhanced reporting requirements.

t: Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR)
s:
On January 2024, Revenue introduced ERR. This requires you to submit the details of the relevant employee payments to Revenue on or before each payday and applies to any payments you make to employees and directors under the following categories.

 

📌Note: Revenue has confirmed that payments you ma...
ss: Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) is a Revenue compliance process introduced in January 2024 that requires you to submit employee payment details to Revenue on or before each payday. The requirement covers specific payment categories including small benefits (vouchers), remote working allowances (up to €3.20 daily), and travel and subsistence expenses—but excludes company credit card payments and reimbursements to non-employees. For each applicable payment type, you must report specific details such as date paid, amount, and number of days worked. Open this document if you need to understand which employee payments fall under ERR and what reporting information you're required to submit to Revenue.
sl: This document provides an overview of Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR), a mandatory reporting system introduced by Revenue in January 2024 that requires employers to submit details of relevant employee payments to Revenue on or before each payday. The ERR applies to payments made to employees and directors across several specific categories: small benefits (vouchers or other tax-free benefits where you must report the benefit date paid and value), remote working daily allowances (up to €3.20 per day exempt from PAYE, PRSI, and USC, requiring reporting of total days, amount paid, and date paid), and travel and subsistence expenses (including vouched travel, unvouched travel, vouched subsistence, unvouched subsistence, site-based employee payments with country money, emergency travel, and eating on site, all requiring date paid and amount paid details). The document clarifies important exclusions: payments made via company credit card and expenses to non-employees or non-directors do not fall under ERR requirements. The document serves as introductory guidance for employers and payroll administrators who need to understand their ERR obligations, with references to more detailed configuration guides, FAQs, checklists, and procedures for generating ERR files and loading digital certificates in back office systems. For complete implementation details and software-specific instructions, users are directed to access the related user guides and supporting articles referenced at the end of the document.

sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for generating an Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) submission file in PeopleXD Payroll, which must be submitted to Revenue for every payroll run containing relevant payments on or before the employee payment date. If exceptions occur during generation, the ERR Submission Exception Report displays errors that must be reviewed and resolved within PeopleXD Payroll before regenerating the file, with this correction cycle repeated until no exceptions remain. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and compliance officers who need to ensure accurate ERR submissions to Revenue and handle error resolution workflows. The document forms part of a larger ERR configuration ecosystem in PeopleXD Payroll, with related articles addressing file transfers to Revenue, configuration settings, delete submissions, full resubmissions, and historical period submissions.

sl: This document provides guidance on excluding employees from submission files in the Back Office system, specifically during payroll or reporting submissions to PAYE Modernisation (PMOD). To exclude an employee, users navigate to CorePay > Update > PAYE Modernisation > Employee Parameters > Employee > Exclude within the Back Office interface. The document clarifies that if an employee has not yet been excluded before the period closes (complete update), users can reverse the exclusion by unticking the Exclude indicator on the same screen. However, if the exclusion was already applied during the complete update, users must submit a new support case online requesting reinclusion, and the support team will run an update to include the employee again. For excluding or including employees from previous periods or specific payroll cycles, users should raise a case online referencing the article title and providing the employee number, payroll period, and whether inclusion or exclusion is required. t: Create and transfer PAYE Modernisation files
s:
PAYE Modernisation files are digital records that contain critical payroll information, including employee details, tax deductions, and earnings.

 

Creating and transferring these files is essential for your business as it ensures accurate and timely reporting to tax authorities. This process redu...
ss: PAYE Modernisation files contain critical payroll information including employee details, tax deductions, and earnings that must be reported to tax authorities. This document covers how to generate submission files within your payroll system and transfer them to Revenue, along with how to monitor transfer status and respond to acceptance or rejection messages. Open this document when you need to create and submit payroll files to meet tax reporting requirements, or when you need to check whether Revenue has accepted your submission and understand any validation errors that need correcting.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for creating and transferring PAYE Modernisation files, which are digital records containing essential payroll information such as employee details, tax deductions, and earnings required for accurate tax authority reporting. The document describes two primary processes: generating submission files and transferring them to Revenue authorities, both of which are accessed through the Manage Payroll menu by selecting the relevant pay group, navigating to the Outputs tab, then ROS, and accessing PAYE Modernisation Files Process. To generate a submission file, users select "Generate Submission File" from the Select PAYE Action dropdown menu, choose "Normal Submission" from the Submission Type dropdown, select a pay group (which automatically populates the Period/Month), optionally override the payment date, and then review the generated file in the Report Centre tab. The transfer process follows a similar navigation path but uses the "Transfer Submission Files" option, allowing users to select a company from a dropdown menu, toggle the "Transfer File" option on, and then confirm the transfer by clicking YES. The document addresses various submission statuses and scenarios users may encounter: "Transferred" indicates Revenue has received the file, "Rejected" shows a failure reason, and "Accepted" confirms Revenue acknowledgment and generates a response file in Report Centre. For check requests, the system automatically generates results that display as either "Accepted COMPLETED: All Valid Payslips" (requiring no further action), "Accepted COMPLETED: Invalid Payslips" (requiring data correction and resubmission), "Pending" or "No Response" statuses (which require users to manually click "Run Check"). This document is essential for payroll administrators and finance professionals who need to ensure accurate and timely tax reporting while reducing errors in tax calculations and improving overall payroll management efficiency.

ss: PAYE Modernisation (PMOD) file transfers to Revenue can fail due to exceptions or expired certificates. Use the Payroll Dashboard notifications and Report Centre in Portal to identify submission errors, then verify your PMOD certificate validity in the Revenue Online Service (ROS) and update it in PeopleXD if needed. Resolve any listed exceptions, regenerate the file, and retry the transfer—or contact support if the payroll period is already closed. Open this article when a PMOD file transfer fails and you need to troubleshoot the root cause and resubmit.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving failed PAYE Modernisation (PMOD) file transfers to Revenue, and is designed for payroll administrators and finance professionals who manage tax submissions through Access Group systems. The document explains how to diagnose transfer failures by checking the notification bell on the Payroll Dashboard for status messages such as "Transfer Submission File Loaded Successfully," and then reviewing generated files in the Report Centre within Portal to identify any exception files that contain listed issues requiring resolution. A key cause of transfer failures is an expired or invalid PMOD certificate used for Revenue submissions, which the document addresses through a dedicated certificate renewal process that involves verifying expiration dates, downloading the latest certificate from the Revenue Online Service (ROS) with appropriate access permissions, and uploading the renewed certificate to PeopleXD. After resolving any identified exceptions and updating the certificate, users must regenerate the PMOD file and reattempt the transfer. If the payroll period has already closed, the document directs users to raise a support case online referencing the article title and providing specific details including the submission files from the Report Centre, the affected pay group, and a description of corrections made, which the support team will then process. The document serves as a complete reference for both self-service troubleshooting and escalation to support when immediate remediation is not possible.

ss: Digital ROS certificate uploads can fail due to file access or naming issues. Open this article if you're getting a "Certificate not loaded" error when trying to upload a .p12 or .p12.bac certificate file. The fix involves checking that your certificate file is stored locally (not in OneDrive), uses the correct file extension, and contains no spaces in the filename or file path. Use this guide to troubleshoot before contacting support.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving the "Certificate not loaded" error that occurs when uploading a new digital ROS certificate in Access Group's system. The guide addresses three primary causes of upload failures: file storage location issues, incorrect file naming conventions, and problematic file path formatting. Users must first verify that the certificate file is stored locally on their device rather than in OneDrive, as cloud storage permissions can interfere with access, and should move the file to a local folder such as their desktop if needed. The document specifies that Revenue requires certificate files to use either the .p12.bac or .p12 file extension, and provides an example of an incorrect format (XXX.p12 (1).bac) to help users identify naming mistakes. Additionally, users must ensure that both the certificate filename and its complete file path contain no spaces, as these can cause upload failures. This document is primarily used by Back Office staff or system administrators responsible for loading digital certificates for Enhanced Reporting Requirements in the ROS system. If these three troubleshooting steps do not resolve the issue, users are directed to raise a new case online and reference this article's title for support.

ss: RPNs (Revenue Personal Numbers) may fail to retrieve in your payroll system, displaying an "RPN not available for Employee" error message. This guide outlines the most common reasons why RPNs don't come through—including incorrect or outdated PPSNs, employees not registered with Revenue, missing employment links on Revenue records, active PAYE exclusion orders, and other employee-specific issues like marital status changes. Open this document when you're troubleshooting missing RPNs for employees in your payroll package and need step-by-step guidance on how to verify employee details, check Revenue records, and resolve each issue. It includes practical solutions like using the PPSN checker on ROS, confirming employment registration, and when to apply Emergency Tax rules.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive troubleshooting guide for employers and payroll administrators who encounter the error message "RPN not available for Employee" when retrieving RPNs through their payroll system or ROS (Revenue Online Service). The guide identifies multiple specific scenarios that prevent RPN availability, including incorrect or unverified PPSNs, which can be checked using the PPSN Checker tool available under Additional Services on the Employer Services tab in ROS, and outdated married women's PPSNs ending in 'W' that must be replaced with new individual PPSNs from DEASP. It addresses registration issues where employees new to Ireland must register with Revenue for PAYE through MyAccount or by contacting the National PAYE Helpline (+353) 1 738 3636, and explains that employment linkage problems occur when the employment start date was not previously notified to Revenue or when an employment has been inadvertently ceased, which can be resolved by using PMOD-enabled payroll packages for direct reporting or by manually completing a create RPN request in ROS. The document also covers additional obstacles such as active PAYE exclusion orders and technical issues like entering an incorrect date in the "Date of last RPN" field when using the Request RPNs by Online Form option in ROS. For employee-specific situations involving marital status changes, bereavement, or credit redistribution that Revenue cannot discuss due to taxpayer confidentiality, the document directs employees to contact Revenue at 01-7383636 or via MyEnquiries, while employers should apply Emergency Tax rules if timely resolution is not possible. If none of the listed scenarios apply after thorough checking, employers can apply Emergency Tax rules or contact the Employer Helpline at 01-7383638 or via MyEnquiries for further assistance.

ss: When a transfer shows ACKNOWLEDGED status with Pending submission in PeopleXD Payroll, the system has received your request but hasn't yet processed the final submission to Revenue. This typically happens when additional approvals are needed, information is missing, or batch processing is delayed. Open this document if your PAYE Modernisation transfer is stuck in Pending status and you need to run checks, verify payslips, and move the submission forward through CorePay's Transfer Submission Files process.
sl: This document explains the meaning and resolution of a specific status combination in PeopleXD Payroll where a transfer shows as ACKNOWLEDGED with a Pending submission status, indicating that the system has received the transfer request but has not yet processed the actual submission due to factors such as missing approvals, incomplete information, or batch processing delays. The document provides a step-by-step resolution process that requires users to navigate through the Back Office menu by clicking CorePay, then Update, followed by PAYE Modernisation and Transfer Submission Files. For the affected pay group with Pending submission status, users must click Run Check again, which will verify valid payslips and typically result in a COMPLETED status showing all valid payslips. After the check completes, users navigate back to Transfer Submission Files and select Confirmed to remove the row from the screen while ensuring the file is not resubmitted. The document clarifies an important distinction: a Pending status does not mean the request is queued for review, but rather that Revenue has already received the file and the Run Check process is validating its contents. This guidance is relevant for payroll administrators and finance teams working with PAYE Modernisation submissions in the Access Group's Back Office system who encounter delays or stalled transfers.

The document references related configuration guidance including PAYE Modernisation parameters amendment and the PAYE Modernisation Irish user guide for users requiring additional context. sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on amending PAYE Modernisation parameters, which are the system settings and configurations that control how employee income tax is calculated and reported in compliance with current taxation laws. s:

ss: Cancelled payments from the previous year aren't appearing on your Payroll Submission file because you need to properly flag the employee record in CorePay. This happens in Back Office when you cancel a payment without selecting the recoupment option or indicating the employee's deceased status. Open this document if you're processing payroll adjustments for employees who received payments in a prior tax year and need those cancellations to show correctly in your submission file. The fix involves either entering the date of death, selecting the deceased indicator, or properly marking previous year recoupment depending on your situation.
sl: This document addresses a specific payroll issue in the Access Group Back Office system where cancelled payments for the previous year do not appear on the Payroll Submission file when the "Recoup previous year" option is not selected for deceased employees. The document provides step-by-step procedures for two distinct scenarios: handling deceased employees from the previous year and handling living employees from the previous year, both requiring entry into CorePay > Employee > Advanced Employee Features > Set Employment Status. For deceased employees whose estates have returned recoupment funds in the current period, users must enter a negative manual payment that includes all pay elements and select the previous year recoupment option. For living employees where recoupment occurred in the current period, the process involves requesting gross pay recoupment from the employee, entering a negative manual payment for gross pay only, selecting previous year recoupment, and issuing the manual payment to the employee, after which tax liability transfers to the employee and Revenue for any refunds. The document resolves the core problem by instructing users to either enter the employee's date of death or select the deceased indicator in the system to ensure proper output on the Payroll Submission file. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and HR professionals managing employee records in the Access Group Back Office system when processing retroactive adjustments and cancellations for previous year payments.

ss: When transferring an ERR (Enhanced Reporting Requirements) certificate to Revenue Online Service (ROS), an error occurs if your user account lacks the correct permissions. This typically happens when you're accessing ROS as a sub-user rather than an administrator—the main ROS administrator must adjust your PAYE-Emp view and submission permissions through ROS admin services. You'll need at least one permission enabled for PAYE-Emp, but selecting both viewing and submitting options together can trigger an error, so ensure only one is activated for your needs. Open this article if you're receiving a certificate transfer error and need to resolve permission issues between administrator and sub-user accounts.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses a specific error encountered when attempting to transfer an ERR (Enhanced Reporting Requirements) certificate, which occurs when the loaded certificate lacks the correct permissions. The issue commonly arises when users access the Revenue Online Service (ROS) as sub-users rather than as administrators, requiring the main ROS administrator to adjust permissions through the admin services section of ROS. To gain access to Enhanced Reporting Requirements features, sub-users must have at least one view permission for PAYE-Emp, with administrators able to configure two distinct permission settings: "To View Only" (which can be set to YES to allow viewing only, or NO to allow both submitting and viewing) and "To Submit and View" (which can be set to YES to allow both submitting and viewing, or NO to allow viewing only). The document includes a critical warning that selecting Yes for both viewing and submitting options simultaneously may trigger an error message, so administrators should select only one permission option appropriate to each sub-user's specific needs. If the ROS administrator confirms that permissions are configured correctly but the error persists, the document recommends contacting ROS support for further assistance. This guidance is intended for ROS administrators managing certificate transfers and sub-user access permissions within payroll and tax reporting workflows.

sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses a specific error encountered when attempting to retrieve an RPN (Revenue and Customs Reference Number) for an employee within the system. The error message "RPN Response file has not been retrieved, response phrase is: No phrase, please check report for validation errors" typically indicates that the user has not followed the correct procedure for the RPN retrieval process. A common cause of this error is selecting an inappropriate retrieval method—for example, using the rejoiner process to retrieve an RPN for an employee who is not actually a rejoiner, which will trigger the validation error. The document directs users to resolve this issue by ensuring they select the appropriate option that matches the employee's actual status when initiating the RPN retrieval. The help article is designed for payroll administrators and HR professionals who manage employee data and RPN retrieval processes within the Access Group system, providing them with a quick troubleshooting reference when encountering this validation error. t: PAYE Modernisation deletion indicator for a cancel payment for deceased personnel

ss: Use the PAYE Modernisation deletion indicator in CorePay when cancelling payments for deceased employees who were reported to Revenue through a payroll submission file. The process differs depending on the tax year: for 2018 tax year cancellations (not previously reported), tick Previous Year Recoupment but do not tick PAYE Modernisation Deletion; for 2019 tax year cancellations (previously reported), do the opposite by ticking PAYE Modernisation Deletion and sending a DELETE instruction to Revenue. Open this document when you need to recoup a net payment from a deceased employee's estate and ensure the cancellation is correctly reflected in your payroll submission file and CorePay Control report.
sl: This document provides guidance on cancelling payments for deceased employees in a payroll system, with different procedures depending on whether the original payment was reported to Revenue through a submission file. For the 2018 tax year, when cancelling payments that were not previously reported to Revenue, users should tick the Previous Year Recoupment option but must not tick the PAYE Modernisation Deletion option, allowing the cancellation to be reflected in the payroll submission file through negative values that appear in the CorePay Control report. For the 2019 tax year and later, when cancelling payments that were already reported to Revenue via a submission file, users should tick the PAYE Modernisation Deletion option instead and avoid using Previous Year Recoupment, which sends a required DELETE instruction to Revenue in the submission file without generating negative values in the CorePay Control report. The document explains that deceased employees are identified by either checking a populated Date of Death field or by ticking a Deceased indicator within the system. In both scenarios, the net payment must be recouped from the deceased individual's estate, and users should ensure that the previous payment in the current tax year is cancelled in the current period when viewing submission file details. This guidance applies to payroll administrators or finance personnel who handle payment cancellations and estate recoupments for deceased staff members within the Access Group payroll system.

Conversely, when the PAYE Modernisation Deletion option is disabled, the cancelled values are netted off within the Payroll Submission file for the current period rather than creating a separate deletion record. The document also directs users to consider the impact of not selecting the recoup indicator when processing cancellations. This guidance is relevant for payroll administrators and finance professionals using Access Group's payroll system who need to understand how payment cancellations are processed and recorded in PAYE submissions. The document references related scenarios including cancelled payments from previous years, cancellations involving deceased personnel, payslip status issues after submission file transfers, and provides links to portal resources for PAYE Modernisation deletion files and resubmission procedures.

sl: This document explains a specific issue that occurs in payroll processing when payslips display an "Invalid Payslip" status after transferring submission files following a cancelled or manual payment. The document emphasizes that the PAYE Modernisation Deletion feature should be used sparingly and only in situations where an employee was erroneously reported to revenue and should not have been submitted, as this option deletes the payslip previously sent from the revenue system. To troubleshoot invalid status errors, users should review the response file from Revenue, where common error messages such as "Unable to delete line item because it has already been deleted" may indicate that the software attempted to delete the same payslip or line ID multiple times due to both recoupment and deletion indicators being selected together. t: Processing non-taxable advances
s:
Revenue have recently announced that non-taxable advances will be allowed in certain scenarios. 

 

This change is being implemented following feedback on the ERR release in relation to advanced not being allowed.

 

What this means?

Irish Revenue will introduce an optional administrative practic...
ss: Non-taxable advances for travel and subsistence expenses are now allowed under Irish Revenue's optional administrative practice, following changes to Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR). This document explains the conditions employers must meet—including reasonable estimates, timely reconciliation with actual claims, and proper controls—plus how to report advance payments to Revenue using the new "Advances" subcategory in ERR. Open this if you need to understand whether your organisation should opt into processing non-taxable advances, what governance controls are required, and how PeopleXD (or your payroll system) will handle the reporting. The document also clarifies that advance payments must be manually reported via Revenue screens until PeopleXD's software update is released in approximately two months.
sl: This document explains the process for handling non-taxable advances following Irish Revenue's new optional administrative practice, which was introduced in response to feedback on the Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) release regarding restrictions on advance payments. The document covers the conditions under which non-taxable advances are permitted, specifically for anticipated travel and subsistence expenses only, and requires employers to establish appropriate controls to track and reconcile all advance payments. Advances must be reported to Revenue under ERR using a designated "Advances" subcategory, and as the advance is drawn down, this drawdown activity must also be reported under ERR to maintain compliance. The document emphasizes that advance payments must represent reasonable estimates of expected claim amounts and qualify for relief under section 114 TCA 1997, with employers required to promptly reconcile advances against actual claims and recoup or tax any excess payments without delay. While employers have discretion to opt into this practice with no advance notification to Revenue required, they must maintain appropriate governance and controls; those choosing not to participate will have standard tax rules apply, with advance payments taxed through payroll instead. The document explains the implementation timeline, noting that Revenue ROS screens will be updated within approximately two months to allow manual capture and reporting of advance payments, and that the Access Group's PeopleXD software solution will be updated to accommodate ERR reporting requirements, with manual reporting via Revenue screens required until that update is released. Employers using non-PeopleXD systems are advised to discuss new functionality plans with their respective software vendors, and further guidance can be found in Revenue Tax Duty Manual (TDM) part 38-03-33.

sl: This document provides instructions for excluding an employee from the Revenue submission file within a payroll portal system. The process involves navigating through the Manage Payroll section, selecting the relevant pay group, and then accessing the Outputs menu to reach ROS and PAYE Modernisation settings. Once in the PAYE Modernisation area, users must click on Employee Parameters, locate the specific employee through a search function, and enable the "Exclude employee" toggle to remove them from submission. For employees who need to be excluded from previous payroll periods or files that have already been submitted, the document directs users to raise a new support case online and reference this article while providing key details including the employee number, the relevant payroll period, and clarification on whether the employee should be included or excluded. This task is typically performed by payroll administrators or managers who need to manage employee participation in PAYE Modernisation (PMOD) file submissions to Revenue authorities.

s:

ss: Generating a Full Resubmission ERR file in PeopleXD is required when you've amended an employee's pay date after already submitting the original ERR file to Revenue. This process resubmits only the amendments you've made since Revenue accepted your normal ERR file for that period. You'll use the Manage Payroll section to access ROS outputs and select Full Resubmission from the submission type dropdown, with separate procedures for the current period versus previous periods. Open this document when you need to correct pay date changes that have already been reported to Revenue.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for generating a Full Resubmission ERR (Enhanced Reporting Requirements) file when an employee's pay date has been amended after the initial ERR file has already been submitted to Revenue. The Full Resubmission file contains only amendments made since Revenue accepted the normal ERR file for that period, and the document distinguishes between processes for the current period and previous periods. For the current period, users navigate through Manage Payroll > Outputs > ROS > Enhanced Reporting Requirements > ERR Files Process, then select "Generate submission file" from the Select ERR action dropdown, choose "Full Resubmission" from the Submission type dropdown, select the pay group, and enter an override payment or cheque date. The document explains a specific error scenario—the message "You cannot generate a file for this pay group and periods as the last file sent got no response from Revenue - Please run a Check ERR Run"—which indicates either that no normal file was submitted for the period or that Revenue rejected the normal file. To resolve this, users can follow steps to check file submission status by selecting "Transfer submission file" from the Select ERR action dropdown and reviewing the Status column. For previous periods, the process is similar but requires first enabling the Previous periods toggle in Pay Group Parameters before accessing ERR Files Process. This document is used by payroll administrators and finance teams who need to correct pay date information that was already submitted to Revenue through the Irish ROS (Revenue Online Service) system.

t: Generate the Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) file for a previous period
s:
You need to submit an ERR return to Revenue in every payroll run where you make any relevant payments, regardless of what system you use to make the payment, on or before the date the employees are paid.
​
For full details of what's included in the ERR submission file, check our user guide.

There...
ss: The Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) file is a mandatory Revenue submission that must accompany every payroll run where relevant payments are made. This document covers how to regenerate ERR files for previous payroll periods in PeopleXD Payroll—specifically when you haven't already generated a file for that period or when Revenue rejected the original submission. You would use this guide when you need to resubmit ERR data by enabling the Previous periods toggle, selecting your pay group and period, and running the ERR Files Process. The document also explains how to review and resolve any exceptions that appear in the ERR Submission Exception Report before transferring the corrected file to Revenue.
sl: This document provides instructions for generating Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) submission files for previous payroll periods within the PeopleXD Payroll system. The process is necessary when ERR files have not yet been generated for a particular period or when Revenue has rejected a previously submitted file. Users navigate through specific menu paths—Manage Payroll, Outputs, ROS, Enhanced Reporting Requirements, and Pay Group Parameters—to access the file generation functionality. The procedure involves enabling the Previous periods toggle for the relevant pay group, then using the ERR Files Process with the Generate submission file action, selecting Normal Submission type, choosing the appropriate pay group, and specifying the target period, with an optional field to override the payment date. After generating the file, users may encounter an ERR Submission Exception Report that identifies errors requiring correction directly in PeopleXD Payroll, after which a new submission file must be regenerated. This iterative error-checking and resolution process should continue until no exceptions remain, and Access Group strongly recommends resolving all errors before transferring the completed file to Revenue. The document is typically used by payroll administrators and finance professionals who need to resubmit or generate corrected ERR files for compliance with Revenue requirements when initial submissions fail or have not yet been created.

ss: When you need to correct pay dates or Shadow Payroll indicator changes in PeopleXD Payroll, use this guide to generate and resubmit full PAYE Modernisation files through Portal. The process covers resubmitting at the pay group level, for individual employees, or for previous periods—each with step-by-step instructions for navigating the Payroll Dashboard and PAYE Modernisation Files Process. Open this document when you've made amendments to employee pay information that requires Revenue notification, or when you need to transfer corrected submission files and check their status. It also includes troubleshooting steps for enabling previous periods and interpreting Revenue responses.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide for creating and processing full resubmission files in PeopleXD Payroll's Portal when amendments are needed for PAYE Modernisation submissions. The full resubmission file is generated when specific changes have been made, specifically corrections to the pay date or the Shadow Payroll indicator for employees, and can be created at either the pay group level or for individual employees, with only changes made since the last accepted submission included in the new file. Users access the resubmission process through the Portal dashboard by navigating to Payroll Dashboard > Manage Payroll > Outputs > ROS > PAYE Modernisation > PAYE Modernisation Files Process, then selecting "Generate Submission File" and "Full Resubmission" from their respective dropdown menus, along with specifying the relevant pay group, employee (if applicable), and Override Payment Date and Override Cheque Pay Date fields. The document addresses three specific scenarios: generating resubmission files for entire pay groups, creating files for individual employees, and resubmitting for previous periods (which requires first enabling the previous period through the Pay Group Parameters screen). After generation, users can download the submission file from the Report Centre and transfer it to Revenue using the "Transfer Submission Files" option, where the Status field indicates outcomes such as "Transferred," "Rejected," or "Accepted COMPLETED." The document also covers error handling, including the scenario where a previous submission received no response from Revenue, and explains how to interpret Revenue's responses, with statuses indicating whether payslips are valid or require correction before transferring a new submission file.

s:
