This document walks you through the step-by-step process in Portal, including how to enable previous periods if needed and how to transfer the corrected file to Revenue. Open this guide when you've made amendments to employee pay dates or Shadow Payroll settings and need to resubmit corrected payroll data.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on creating and processing full resubmission files within PeopleXD Payroll when amendments to pay dates or Shadow Payroll indicators are necessary for PAYE Modernisation compliance. The document covers four distinct scenarios: generating resubmission files at the pay group level, for individual employees, for previous periods, and transferring completed resubmission files to Revenue. For pay group-level resubmissions, users navigate to CorePay > Update > PAYE Modernisation, select "Generate Submission File" from the Generate/Transfer dropdown, choose "Full resubmission" as the submission type, enter the pay group, select the period and payment date, then verify the generated file displays the correct date. Individual employee resubmissions follow the same path but require entering both the pay group and specific employee in their respective fields. To process resubmissions for previous periods, users must first enable the Previous periods toggle within Pay Group Parameters before generating the submission file, then disable this toggle afterwards. The document addresses two specific correction scenarios: when pay dates are incorrectly reported, the resubmission file includes deleted line items from the previous submission and new line items with updated dates; when Shadow Payroll indicator status changes, the file reflects the amended status with corresponding delete and new line items. A critical note advises that if an incorrect payment date has been used for PAYE Modernisation, Revenue must be contacted directly before submitting any correction file. This document is essential for payroll administrators and back office staff in the Access Group system who need to correct previously submitted PAYE data to Revenue.

t: Arrears not calculating correctly in salary processing
s:
When processing salaries, arrears may not generate correctly for an employee due to several factors.

 

Below, we outline common scenarios that can cause inaccuracies in arrears calculations.

 

 

Null or zero multiplier for previous rate

If the multiplier for the employee's previous rate is nul...
ss: Salary arrears may fail to calculate correctly during payroll processing in your system due to issues such as null multipliers on previous rates, incorrect pay group assignments, multiple salary changes in one period, or missing net pay rows. This document outlines over a dozen common scenarios that prevent arrears generation and provides specific fixes for each—including when to enter manual timesheet entries, run retrospection jobs, or contact support. Open this if your employees' arrears are not appearing as expected after a salary change, pay group transfer, or during standard payroll runs. It's also useful if you need to troubleshoot why the system isn't automatically calculating back-pay owed to staff.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre provides a comprehensive troubleshooting guide for resolving arrears calculation errors in salary processing, detailing multiple scenarios where arrears fail to generate correctly and offering specific remediation steps for each. The document covers common configuration and data entry issues including null or zero multipliers for previous rates, incorrect pay group assignments, incorrectly entered new rates with wrong effective dates, and transaction dates that fall outside the payroll period. It addresses complex payroll scenarios such as multiple salary changes within the same period, timing misalignments between input dates and complete update dates, discrepancies between configured pay days and calculated days, and employees transitioning between pay groups (e.g., from weekly to fortnightly pay cycles). The guide explains that many of these issues require manual timesheet entry as the system cannot automatically accommodate them, and provides specific configuration instructions such as enabling the Retrospection toggle under Settings > Codes > Pay Groups for individual pay groups. For certain issues involving incorrect units on net pay rows, incorrect rejoin dates, or other data anomalies, the document directs users to raise support cases for analyst intervention, while for hourly pay codes it specifies that the positive input retro (PIR) job must be run to generate retrospection payments. This resource is designed for payroll administrators and HR professionals who process salaries and need to diagnose and correct arrears calculation failures within the Access Group payroll system.

t: Portal: Issue a manual payment
s:
There may be times when you need to make changes to an employee's pay after you've closed the payroll period. In this case, you need to issue a manual payment.

 

⚠️Important: When correcting errors from previous periods near the Financial Year End, ensure you verify that payroll corrections are ac...
ss: Issuing a manual payment in PeopleXD Payroll lets you adjust an employee's pay after the payroll period has closed, which is essential for correcting errors or making changes that weren't captured in the regular pay run. The process involves navigating to Issue Manual Payments, entering employee and payment details (including reference number, period, PAYE code, and appointment information), and ensuring all pay codes and National Insurance details are accurate before saving. Open this document when you need to make post-payroll adjustments, especially near Financial Year End when HMRC compliance is critical, or when you need to correct previous tax year payments by submitting a Previous Year Full Payroll Submission (PYFPS).
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on issuing manual payments in PeopleXD Payroll when corrections or adjustments to employee pay are needed after a payroll period has been closed. The process begins by navigating to Manage Payroll, selecting the relevant pay group, then accessing General and Issue Manual Payments, where users must enter specific details including employee reference number, payroll period, issue date, PAYE code, and number of days. The document emphasizes the critical importance of HMRC compliance when making corrections near Financial Year End, requiring verification of pension adjustments, overpayments, and accuracy of employee records for payslips and P60s. Users must ensure appointment IDs and expense codes are entered for all fields, verify that employer NI or PRSI amounts are correctly entered (with the option to enter 0 if there is no NIable or PRSIable pay), and carefully check all Manual Payment Pay Codes before saving, as these cannot be amended after entry. The document also addresses corrections made in previous tax years, explaining that year-end must be completed before cancelling and reissuing manual payments, after which users must submit a Previous Year Full Payroll Submission (PYFPS) to HMRC and update P60 cumulative details through either the Portal (Year End > Manage > Post Cleardown Activities > Maintain Cumulatives) or Back Office (CorePay > Update > Advanced Update Features > Year End > Maintain Year End Cumulative Details). This document is typically used by payroll administrators and finance teams who need to correct pay errors, process additional payments outside standard payroll cycles, or ensure compliance with HMRC regulations for year-end adjustments.

t: Portal: Update P60
s:
A P60 is an official document issued to employees at the end of the tax year, summarising their total pay and tax deductions. 

 

It is important for tax returns and proof of income. P60S are processed after the final payroll of the tax year, but you may need to update the details if there are corr...
ss: P60 documents summarise an employee's total pay and tax deductions at the end of the tax year and are essential for tax returns and proof of income. After the final payroll run, you may need to update P60 details in Portal if there are corrections to earnings, tax paid, or employee information. Use this guide when you need to amend P60 records through the Payroll Dashboard by accessing Year End settings and the Maintain Cumulatives section. Open this document if your organisation has identified errors on P60s that require correction before they're released to employees.
sl: This document provides guidance on updating P60 details in the Portal system after the final payroll of the tax year has been processed. P60s are official end-of-year documents issued to employees that summarise their total pay and tax deductions, making them essential for tax returns and proof of income. The document explains that updates may be necessary when there are corrections needed to earnings, tax paid, or employee information following initial P60 generation. Users access the update process by navigating from the dashboard menu to Payroll Dashboard, then selecting Year End and highlighting the relevant company before clicking Manage. Within the Manage section, users locate and click Maintain Cumulatives under the Post Cleardown Activities area to make the required P60 updates. This process is typically used by payroll administrators or finance teams who need to correct P60 records after the year-end payroll cycle and before P60s are released to employees. The document also provides references to related articles covering back office P60 updates, P60 production and release procedures, troubleshooting for employees on absence, and P60 access controls.

The process involves navigating through CorePay to Advanced Update Features and Year End settings to maintain cumulative year-end details. sl: This document provides guidance on updating P60 records in the Back Office system, which are official year-end tax documents issued to employees that summarize total pay and tax deductions. P60s are essential for employee tax returns and proof of income, and while they are typically generated after the final payroll run of the tax year, updates may be necessary to correct errors or changes in earnings, tax paid, or employee information. The document outlines the specific menu navigation required to access the update function: users must click CorePay, then click Update, followed by selecting Advanced Update Features and Year End, and finally clicking Maintain Year End Cumulative Details to access the screen where P60 data can be modified. This process is used by payroll administrators and back office staff who need to make corrections or adjustments to P60 records after the initial generation but before they are issued or released to employees. The document references related functionality including Portal-based P60 updates, P60 production processes, manual payment issuance, P60 release procedures, and the ability to produce blank P60 forms from Back Office, all of which are interconnected with the update process described.

t: Cancel a manual payment
s:
Cancelling a manual payment is necessary when a payment has been made in error or contains incorrect details. 

 

If you’ve recorded an incorrect manual payment and wish to cancel it, your options depend on whether a payment has already been cancelled in the payroll period.
​
If you've cancelled a ...
ss: Manual payment cancellation in your payroll system becomes necessary when a payment has been recorded in error or contains incorrect information. Your approach depends on your payroll period status: if you've already cancelled a payment in the current period, you'll need to issue a negative manual payment matching the incorrect amount; if no cancellations have been processed yet, you can cancel all payments for that period and then reissue with correct details. Open this document when you've made a payroll error and need to correct it while understanding the constraints of your current payroll cycle.
sl: This document provides guidance on cancelling manual payments that have been recorded incorrectly or with inaccurate details. The document outlines two distinct scenarios for cancelling manual payments, depending on whether a payment has already been cancelled within the current payroll period. In the first scenario, if a payment has already been cancelled during the payroll period, users must issue a negative manual payment with identical values to the incorrect payment rather than performing a full cancellation. In the second scenario, if no payment has been cancelled during the payroll period, users can perform a cancel payment action, which will cancel all payments for that period including both the incorrect manual payment and any other payments that were made. After completing either cancellation option, users can then issue a new manual payment containing the correct details. The document is designed for payroll administrators and finance users who need to correct manual payment errors within their payroll processing workflows. The guidance references related processes including issuing manual payments, cancelling payments, correcting figures reported to HMRC, and resolving payslip display issues that may occur following manual payment cancellation.

t: Change payment type after the complete update
s:
Changing the payment type after the complete update job has been run typically occurs when an employee has received an incorrect payment method, such as a bank transfer or cheque, during payroll processing and needs an update.

 

However, users cannot update the payment type once the complete updat...
ss: Changing an employee's payment type (such as bank transfer or cheque) in payroll becomes restricted once the complete update job has been run. If an employee received an incorrect payment method during processing, you'll need to contact support rather than making the change yourself, as the system prevents direct updates after this point. Open this document when you need to correct a payment type error and discover you can't modify it through normal channels. Have your employee number, payroll period, and desired payment type ready when you submit your support request.
sl: This document explains the process for addressing payment type errors that occur after the Complete Update payroll job (PAY355) has been executed in the system. It describes a common scenario where employees receive incorrect payment methods—such as bank transfers or cheques—during payroll processing and require correction. The document identifies a significant system limitation: users cannot directly update the payment type through standard functionality once the Complete Update job has been completed. To resolve this issue, the document directs users to contact support, who will need to run specific database scripts to manually correct the payment type. Users requesting assistance are instructed to raise a new case online and reference this article's title while providing three essential pieces of information: the employee number, the payroll period affected, and the correct payment type that needs to be applied. The document also provides cross-references to related articles covering similar post-Complete Update issues, such as incorrect expense codes, incorrect cost centres, and BIC/IBAN errors, as well as articles about Complete Update job failures and payroll report retrieval.

t: Allowances not generating
s:
Allowances are a crucial part of employee compensation and must be accurately reflected in payroll to ensure correct payments and compliance.

 

If an assigned allowance does not appear or calculate correctly, several reasons may be responsible.

We’ve compiled a list of possible causes and how to ...
ss: Allowances in PeopleXD Payroll may fail to generate or calculate correctly due to several configuration and processing issues. This document covers the most common causes—including the Generate Salaries and Allowances job not being rerun, incorrect allowance setup, positive input timesheet gaps, zero multiplier settings, and GL posting errors—along with specific steps to resolve each one. Open this guide when an assigned allowance isn't appearing in payroll or is calculating an incorrect amount, and you need to identify and fix the underlying cause quickly.
sl: This document provides comprehensive troubleshooting guidance for resolving issues when allowances fail to appear or calculate correctly in payroll processing within the PeopleXD Payroll system. The document identifies multiple specific causes and their solutions, including scenarios where the Generate Salaries and Allowances job has not been re-run after allowance configuration changes, allowance configuration errors such as missing Balance Due fields for reducing balance allowances or unset percentage pay codes, and situations where employees on positive input lack timesheet entries or are on zero multipliers without the Pay in Full indicator enabled. It details step-by-step procedures for accessing relevant screens in both the Portal and Back Office interfaces—such as navigating to Settings > Codes > Pay Codes to enable the Pay in Full rule, or CorePay > Employee to amend employee sundry profiles for those who have moved from quarterly pay groups. The document also addresses advanced scenarios including zero multipliers with date-effective entries, incorrect end period settings for 54-week years requiring support analyst intervention, GL posting override errors in the pay290.logXXXX file when cost centers are not configured, and salary lines that have not been commenced before pay period completion. This resource is essential for payroll administrators and HR professionals in organizations using PeopleXD Payroll who need to diagnose and resolve allowance generation failures and ensure accurate employee compensation processing.

t: Payslip with negative net pay
s:
A payslip with negative net pay occurs when an employee’s total deductions exceed their earnings, resulting in a negative amount payable.

 

The payroll system cannot process employees with negative net pay amounts.

 

 HMRC regulations prohibit the submission of negative payment amounts through t...
ss: Negative net pay occurs when an employee's total deductions exceed their earnings, creating a negative amount payable to the employee. Both the payroll system and HMRC regulations prohibit processing these transactions, so you'll need to resolve the issue before submitting payroll. Open this article if you encounter negative net pay calculations in your payroll processing and need to understand why the system is blocking submission or how to recover from this situation.
sl: This document explains the issue of payslips with negative net pay, which occurs when an employee's total deductions exceed their earnings, resulting in a negative amount payable to the employee. The payroll system is designed to block and cannot process employees with negative net pay amounts due to regulatory constraints, as HMRC regulations explicitly prohibit the submission of negative payment amounts through their systems. To maintain compliance with both HMRC requirements and software restrictions, the system actively blocks any attempts to process negative net pay calculations. Users must resolve any negative net pay issues before submitting payroll data, as both HMRC and the payroll software will reject these transactions if they proceed. The document references several related topics including the error message "*** Negative Pay After Processing Pre-Tax Deductions **", guidance on making negative payslips, steps for setting up negative net pay recovery, instructions for removing a pay code from a payslip, and configuration of Intelligent Payslips. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and HR professionals who encounter negative net pay scenarios during payroll processing and need to understand both the system limitations and the regulatory reasons behind them.

t: End an allowance in CorePay
s:
An allowance represents additional payments provided to employees for specific purposes, such as travel, housing, or professional expenses. 

 

Ending an allowance is important to ensure that payroll records accurately reflect current compensation structures and prevent overpayment, and maintain co...
ss: Ending an allowance in CorePay removes additional employee payments (such as travel, housing, or professional expenses) from active compensation records. Use this process to prevent overpayment, maintain accurate payroll records, and comply with company policies—and as best practice, end an allowance before assigning a replacement rather than modifying an existing one. You can end an allowance either in CorePay back office by searching for the employee and pay code, then entering an end date, or through People Management on Portal via the Allowances tab. Open this document when you need to stop a current allowance for an employee or when making changes to allowance values.
sl: This document explains how to end an allowance in CorePay, which is essential for maintaining accurate payroll records, preventing employee overpayment, and ensuring compliance with company policies. An allowance represents additional payments provided to employees for specific purposes such as travel, housing, or professional expenses, and the document emphasizes that when amending an allowance, best practice is to end the existing allowance and assign a new one rather than modifying the current allowance value. The document provides two distinct procedures: the first is the back office method in CorePay, which requires navigating to CorePay > Employee > Employee Allowances > Amend An Existing Allowance and entering the Employee Reference (personnel number), Pay code, and Start date to retrieve the allowance, then entering the Allowance End Date and saving. The second procedure uses the People Management portal, where users access the dashboard, navigate to an employee's Current salary section, select the Allowances tab, highlight the relevant allowance, and update the Payroll End Date field before saving. The document includes important warnings that the allowance end date cannot be updated after saving from the back office screen, and that entering a past end date may generate arrears. This document is intended for payroll administrators and HR personnel who manage employee compensation in CorePay or use the People Management portal to administer allowances.

t: Salary offset deduction is incorrect
s:
A salary offset deduction reduces an employee's salary to account for their absences, aiming to ensure fair compensation during periods of sick leave.

 

Incorrect salary offset deductions can happen for the following reasons:

 

Cause 1: The daily rate looks incorrect.

The daily rate is determin...
ss: Salary offset deductions in payroll reduce an employee's pay to account for absences like sick leave, but they can calculate incorrectly due to wrong daily rates or pay group settings. The most common causes are an incorrect "Days in Year" value at the pay group level, or the employee's pay group being set to daily rate when they should be on an hourly rate. Open this document if your payslip shows an unexpected deduction amount for absences, or if the deduction doesn't match the number of sick days taken. Follow the troubleshooting steps to verify your pay group settings in the portal and recalculate what the correct deduction should be.
sl: This document provides guidance on troubleshooting incorrect salary offset deductions, which are reductions applied to an employee's salary to account for absences such as sick leave and ensure fair compensation. The document identifies two main causes of incorrect deductions: an incorrect daily rate calculation and pay group configuration mismatches between hourly and daily rate settings. For the daily rate issue, users access the portal by navigating to Settings > Codes > Pay Groups, selecting the relevant pay code from the Pay Group Code drop-down menu, and verifying the Days in Year field value; the daily rate should be calculated by dividing the employee's salary by the number of days in the year and then multiplying by the actual sick days taken, with reference to override settings in the sickness category if needed. The second cause occurs when an employee's pay group is incorrectly configured to apply a daily rate instead of an hourly rate, resulting in doubled deductions—for example, deducting 80 hours instead of 40 hours when an hourly employee takes 10 sick days. To resolve hourly employee deductions, users must check the pay group settings assigned to the employee and ensure the pay group is set to HOURLY rather than a daily rate setting. This document is intended for payroll administrators and HR professionals who need to investigate and correct payslip discrepancies related to absence deductions in the Access Group payroll system.

t: Populate Scottish arrestment order rates
s: Scottish Arrestment Order rates specify the statutory deduction amounts that employers must apply when court orders instruct them to withhold money from an employee's wages to satisfy debts or legal obligations. Set by Scottish legislation, these rates determine the maximum amounts that can be deduc...
ss: Scottish Arrestment Order rates are the statutory deduction amounts employers must withhold from employee wages when court orders are issued to recover debts such as unpaid council tax or maintenance payments. You'll need to configure these rates in Portal by navigating to Settings > Pay Codes, then entering the earnings bands and deduction amounts in the Payment Orders section according to government-specified banding. Open this guide when you receive formal court instructions to set up wage deductions, or when you need to understand which earnings thresholds and deduction percentages apply to Scottish arrestment orders. The configuration ensures you withhold the correct amounts while allowing employees to retain sufficient income for essential living expenses.
sl: This document provides instructions for configuring Scottish Arrestment Order rates in the Access Group Portal system, which are statutory deduction amounts that employers must apply to employee wages when complying with court orders for debt recovery. The document explains that Scottish Arrestment Order rates determine the maximum amounts that can be deducted from earnings while ensuring employees retain sufficient income for essential living expenses, and are used when receiving formal court instructions to recover debts such as unpaid council tax or maintenance payments through salary deductions. To implement these rates, users must navigate to Settings > Codes > Pay Codes in Portal, search for the relevant pay code, click the three-dot icon, and select Edit to access the configuration screen. Within the Pay Code section under Payment Orders, users must populate several fields including Nett Earnings Week From and To dates (drawn from government banding), Lower Band Week, Lower value, Balance the %, and The Sum, with specific instructions to follow government deduction guidance when determining whether toggles should be enabled for "value OR %" versus "value PLUS %" calculations. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and compliance personnel who process court-ordered wage deductions in Scottish jurisdictions and need to ensure their payroll system correctly reflects the statutory rates and banding requirements set by government legislation.

t: Adjust or refund a deduction
s:
Adjusting or refunding a deduction is carried out when an incorrect amount has been deducted from an employee’s pay or when a deduction needs to be reversed.

 

To adjust a deduction for an employee or process a refund, follow the steps below in portal.

ss: Correcting payroll deductions in your portal covers situations where an employee has been charged an incorrect deduction amount or a deduction needs to be cancelled entirely. You'll navigate to the employee's record, locate the specific deduction, and use the Adjust Normal Amount section to either modify the deduction value or process a refund across one or more payroll periods. Open this document when you need to reverse an erroneous deduction, adjust a deduction amount retroactively, or refund an employee for an overpayment.
sl: This document provides instructions for adjusting or refunding employee deductions within the Access Group portal when incorrect amounts have been deducted from pay or when a deduction needs to be reversed entirely. The process involves navigating to the Employee section of the portal, searching for and viewing the relevant employee record, then accessing the Deduction area to highlight and edit the specific deduction requiring adjustment. Users must enter the number of payroll periods for the adjustment in the "Number of Periods" field, with the example that entering "1" applies the adjustment value only to the current payroll period while restoring the normal deduction value in subsequent periods. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and HR professionals who need to correct deduction errors or reverse deductions that were applied in error or are no longer due. The guide references related portal-based processes including loading new deduction details, placing deductions on hold, and resolving scenarios such as AVC deductions being applied when not due, providing context for when this adjustment process fits within broader deduction management workflows.

t: Error: 'An error has occurred, please try again. If the issue persists please contact support…'
s:
Loading rates of pay in bulk involves entering multiple employee pay rates at once into a payroll system. This method streamlines payroll management by enabling administrators to efficiently update compensation rates for a group of employees, rather than processing each change individually.

ss: Bulk loading of pay rates in your payroll system allows administrators to update compensation for multiple employees at once rather than individually. ss: PRSI refunds for previous tax years cannot be processed through the payroll system in PeopleXD—the system only handles current tax year PRSI refunds and does not support backdated refunds regardless of the timesheet transaction date recorded. Any PRSI refunds for prior years must be managed directly between the employee/employer and the Department of Social Protection outside of payroll. Processing these refunds via payroll is not recommended because it requires extensive manual amendments that increase the risk of errors. Open this document if you need to understand why a previous tax year PRSI refund cannot be completed in the system and where responsibility for handling it should lie.
sl: This document clarifies the limitations and recommendations for handling PRSI (Pay Related Social Insurance) refunds within the Access Group payroll system. The document warns that if a timesheet is recorded for a refund, the Validation report will only display PRSI paid in the current tax year, and supplementary runs will not work for National Insurance (NI) arrears. It emphasizes that refunding PRSI via payroll is not recommended because it requires extensive manual amendments that may introduce errors into payroll records. Instead, the document advises that any PRSI refund should be handled as a matter between the employee or employer and the Department of Social Protection, managed entirely outside the payroll system. The document is designed for payroll administrators and finance professionals who need to understand the proper procedures and system limitations when employees or employers request PRSI refunds, particularly for prior tax years. sl: The General Ledger journal report (PAYB236) is a critical payroll processing tool that ensures all financial transactions are accurately recorded and balanced within the general ledger, and this document provides systematic troubleshooting guidance for resolving instances when the report fails to balance. s:

ss: Overtime calculations in Access Group's payroll system depend on three key settings: pay code multipliers, pay group pay periods, and employee FTE hours. sl: This document provides guidance on diagnosing and resolving incorrect overtime calculations within a payroll system, addressing a common issue that affects employee compensation accuracy. ss: Setting up a reducing balance allowance in PeopleXD lets you create deductions that decrease over time from a set capital sum, paid out in regular installments until the balance reaches zero. You can configure this allowance either through the Portal (via Payroll Dashboard > Pay Codes) or the Back Office (via CorePay > Reference > Pay Codes), with the key requirement of setting a minus multiplier value and enabling the Reducing Balance toggle. This is useful when you need to deduct a fixed total amount from an employee's pay across multiple payroll periods—such as loans, advances, or other installment-based deductions. Note that the system calculates reducing balance deductions from the current or future period only, not retrospectively.
sl: This document provides a complete guide to setting up a reducing balance allowance in the PeopleXD system, which is a type of allowance that deducts from an employee's pay by reducing a capital sum with each payroll run until the balance reaches zero. The document explains the foundational concept that a reducing balance allowance requires both a capital sum (the total annual value to be deducted) and a periodic value or percentage assigned to the employee, with the balance automatically decrementing each payroll period until it reaches zero and the allowance ceases. It includes step-by-step instructions for setting up this allowance through two different interfaces: the Portal method (accessed via Payroll Dashboard > Settings > Pay Codes under Codes) and the Back Office method (accessed via CorePay > Reference > Pay Codes), both of which require creating or duplicating a pay code and configuring specific settings. Both setup methods require configuring the multiplier as a minus value (such as -1) on the General tab and enabling or selecting the Reducing Balance toggle or indicator on the Allowances/Payments tab before saving and completing employee-level setup. The document also highlights an important limitation: the system will not process retrospective arrears for a reducing balance pay code with a past date, and these allowances will only calculate from the current period or future start dates onward. This guide is typically used by payroll administrators and HR professionals in the Access Group system who need to implement allowances that systematically reduce an employee's entitlements over multiple pay periods.

Open this document when you need to set up third-party payments, generate bank files for deductions, or configure HMRC payments.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on generating Third Party Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) files within the Access Group payroll system, enabling users to transfer deduction payments electronically to external organisations such as healthcare providers, credit unions, and pension schemes. The document outlines four main configuration and operational processes: configuring pay codes with bank account details and Third Party Returns rules via the Settings tab, configuring payment percentages and discounts on the Payroll Dashboard's Manage Payroll > Outputs > Third Party EFT section, extracting deduction data from payroll history into the Third Party EFT module for a specified period, and generating bank files for payment through the Generate/Reset tab. It addresses common scenarios such as the need to reset extracted data before making amendments and regenerating files, with an important warning that extracting data multiple times will overwrite all previously extracted information. sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre explains the error message that appears when users attempt to set up a deduction on the Maintain Employee Deduction screen and encounter the notification "Deduction already exists with this Pay Code and Reference" or "Deduction with same reference already exists for." The document specifies important formatting requirements for the new reference: it must contain no spaces and cannot exceed 12 characters in length. This guidance is relevant for payroll administrators and HR personnel who manage employee deductions within the Access Group system and need to understand the constraints around deduction configuration and reference naming conventions.

t: Back Office: Issue a manual payment
s:
If the payroll period is closed, you may need to issue a manual payment. When canceling a payment, first record an alternative payment in the accounts system, then enter the manual payment in PeopleXD to update the employee's cumulatives and reflect the adjusted figures on the next FPS.

 

To issue...
ss: Use this guide when you need to issue a manual payment for a closed payroll period in PeopleXD's CorePay system. It covers the step-by-step process for entering mandatory fields (employee reference, payroll period, PAYE code, pay codes, and NI/PRSI details), ensuring cumulative records and FPS figures are updated correctly. Open this document if you're processing a late or corrective payment, canceling an existing payment, or need to adjust employee pay records after payroll has closed. Note that manual payments require manual entry of all values—the system won't automatically calculate salary or PAYE, and physical cheques or bank files aren't generated.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for issuing manual payments in the Back Office system when a payroll period has been closed, a process that requires updating both the accounts system and PeopleXD to maintain accurate employee cumulatives and FPS reporting. The primary workflow involves navigating to CorePay > Update > Advanced Updated Features > Issue a Manual Payment, then completing mandatory fields including Employee Reference number, Payroll Period, Issue Date, PAYE Code, and Number of Days, along with optional PO Number entry. Users must accurately enter pay codes, values, and Appointment_ID in the Manual Payment Pay Codes section, ensure positive figures are used (as multipliers are applied automatically), and populate the Employer NI/PRSI section as applicable, while deliberately avoiding manual entry of Nett Pay as it generates automatically. The document addresses the limitation that the system cannot create cheques or bank files for manual payments, requiring alternative payment methods such as cheques or manual credit transfers if additional payments are needed, and notes that only copy payslips are available through this process, not printed payslips. For manual payments recorded in previous tax years, specific procedures are outlined to update P60 details through either the Back Office path (CorePay > Update > Advanced Update Features > Year End > Maintain Year End Cumulative Details) or the Portal path (Payroll Dashboard > Year End > Manage > Post Cleardown Activities > Maintain Cumulatives). This document is typically used by payroll administrators and back office staff who need to correct payments after period closure or address payment adjustments for employee pay group changes.

ss: Redundancy and sporting testimonial payments require specific tax treatment in PeopleXD payroll, with different rules depending on whether payments fall under or over £30,000. Payments under £30,000 are generally tax-free, while amounts exceeding £30,000 become taxable and subject to Employer Class 1 National Insurance contributions. You'll need to set up separate pay codes in PeopleXD Portal to ensure HMRC compliance and correct tax handling for each payment threshold. Open this document when configuring redundancy or testimonial payments to learn the step-by-step process for creating and enabling the appropriate pay codes.
sl: This document explains how to handle taxable redundancy payments and sporting testimonials within the PeopleXD payroll system, detailing the tax treatment requirements under UK legislation and the configuration steps needed for compliance. The document covers two distinct payment scenarios based on HMRC rules: payments under £30,000, which are generally tax-free but may have specific National Insurance implications requiring one pay code setup, and payments exceeding £30,000, where the amount over the threshold becomes taxable and subject to Employer Class 1 National Insurance contributions, necessitating a separate dedicated pay code. To configure these payments in the system, users must navigate to the Portal's Settings section, access Pay Codes under the Codes menu, locate the relevant pay code, click the three-dot icon, select Edit, and then click Rules to add the taxable redundancy configuration from the dropdown menu before saving changes via the OK button. This document is designed for payroll administrators and HR professionals using PeopleXD who need to ensure their organization correctly processes redundancy and testimonial payments while maintaining full HMRC compliance and avoiding tax treatment errors. The document also references related configuration tasks such as setting up DEA pay codes, salary sacrifice pensions, manual rate changes, statutory pay parameters, and processing non-taxable advances, indicating it is part of a broader payroll setup and management guide.

sl: This document explains how to troubleshoot an issue in payroll systems where an employee's allowance fails to split across multiple cost centres even though their salary is properly configured to do so in the Cost Allocations screen. ss: Loading new employee deductions in CorePay uses the Disk Exchange feature to import deduction data from a file into an intermediate payroll table and generate a validation report. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators or back office users who need to batch-load deduction records from external files rather than entering them manually, and it serves as a reference guide for troubleshooting file validation issues during the import process.

t: New LPT deduction doesn't take into account existing LPT deduction amount
s: If you load a new tax certificate or RPN, the system may set up a new LPT deduction without recognizing previous deductions. This issue often occurs when the tax year on the old LPT deduction is incorrect. As a result, the system does not add the amount already deducted to the new deduction, leading...
ss: When loading a new tax certificate or RPN in the payroll system, a duplicate LPT (Low Profit Threshold) deduction may be created instead of updating the existing one, especially if the previous deduction has an incorrect tax year. This causes the system to fail recognizing prior deductions and results in payroll miscalculations where previously deducted amounts aren't carried forward. Open this article if you've discovered duplicate LPT deductions after uploading a new tax certificate or RPN, or if an employee's deduction amounts appear incorrect following a certificate update. You'll need to submit a support case with the affected employee numbers and LPT pay code to resolve the issue.
sl: This document describes a specific issue that occurs in the Access Group payroll system when users load a new tax certificate or RPN (Revenue Program Number), where the system creates a new LPT (Local Property Tax) deduction without accounting for any existing LPT deductions that have already been applied. The problem typically arises when the tax year recorded on the old LPT deduction is incorrect, causing the system to fail to recognize and carry forward the previously deducted amount to the new deduction, which results in calculation errors and potential payroll inaccuracies. The document provides guidance for resolving this issue by instructing users to submit a new support case online, and specifies that they should reference the article title, provide the affected employee numbers, and identify the LPT pay code associated with the problematic deduction. This document is intended for payroll administrators and HR professionals who manage tax deductions and handle RPN or tax certificate uploads within the Access Group system, particularly those who encounter discrepancies in local property tax deduction amounts after processing new tax documentation. The related articles referenced suggest that users can access further information about loading new deduction details through both the Portal and Back Office interfaces, as well as troubleshooting steps for RPN retrieval errors.

ss: The PAYE Modernisation (PMOD) deletion file process handles canceled payments for deceased employees in payroll systems. This check must be repeated until the submission status changes to COMPLETED for all valid payslips associated with the original submission. Once the status has been updated to COMPLETED, users must re-generate and transfer the submission file for the cancelled payment to ensure the deletion file is properly created. This document is intended for payroll administrators and Back Office users who manage PAYE submissions and need to process cancellations for deceased personnel within their organisation.

t: Enhanced Holiday Pay annual leave dates
s:

ss: Enhanced Holiday Pay calculates holiday pay based on average earnings, but requires you to update your annual leave start and end dates each year to ensure the correct entitlement period is applied. The system provides a 12-month grace period during which dates roll forward automatically, but if you don't update them within this window, it will continue deducting from the previous year's entitlement, causing employees to exhaust holidays incorrectly and requiring manual payment corrections. Open this document if you need to update your holiday year dates in the Payroll Dashboard, or if you're experiencing issues with employees' holiday balances or Enhanced Holiday Pay calculations referencing the wrong year. Update your dates in the Pay Group Parameters tab during the first or second pay period of your new holiday year to prevent processing errors.
sl: This document explains the Enhanced Holiday Pay feature in the Access Group system, which calculates holiday pay based on average earnings and requires annual maintenance of entitlement dates. The core process involves navigating to Payroll Dashboard > Settings > Enhanced Holiday Pay > Pay Group Parameters tab, where users must update the annual leave start date and annual leave end date fields for each pay group to reflect the current holiday year. The system operates with a 12-month grace period that automatically rolls forward entitlement dates by one year, allowing employees to transition smoothly between holiday years—for example, automatically switching from 2024 to 2025 entitlements—but this automatic roll-forward only functions once, meaning a second manual update is required to prevent the system from incorrectly deducting from outdated entitlements. Failing to update these dates causes critical processing errors, including employees exhausting their holiday entitlement incorrectly, Enhanced Holiday Pay calculations referencing the wrong entitlement year, and the need for manual payment corrections. Users should perform this update during the first or second pay period of their new holiday year, though the system allows up to 12 months from the end of the old holiday year to make the change. The document is designed for payroll administrators and HR professionals who manage Enhanced Holiday Pay in their organization and need to ensure accurate holiday entitlement tracking and payment calculations across multiple pay groups.

ss: Prepare your PeopleXD payroll environment for Year End by cloning your Production data to UAT for testing and validation purposes. Before requesting a clone, verify internally that no other teams are using UAT and that you won't lose any in-progress project data, since the clone process deletes UAT data that doesn't exist in Production. Depending on your hosting setup, arrange appropriate backups—PeopleXD-hosted solutions back up automatically, while non-hosted solutions require coordination with your IT department. Open this document when preparing for Year End cleardown to understand cloning procedures, backup requirements, and the critical steps needed before running the Year End process.
sl: This document provides guidance for preparing non-production environments ahead of Payroll Year End processing, specifically covering environment cloning and backup procedures. A clone copies the Production environment to the UAT environment, allowing organizations to test and validate Year End processes with current employee and payroll data; however, any UAT data not present in Production (such as configuration or test data from in-progress implementation projects) will be permanently deleted during this process. The document recommends timing the clone after the last payroll run of the year to ensure testing occurs on the most recent data, and requires organizations to email peoplexd.professionalservices@theaccessgroup.com to arrange the clone, with potential additional charges depending on contractual entitlements. Before requesting a clone, users must verify internally whether other teams use UAT, whether any projects are in progress, and whether non-Production data exists that should be preserved, as these factors may make cloning inappropriate. For backup requirements, the document distinguishes between two hosting scenarios: organizations using the PeopleXD-hosted exdata platform receive automatic backups and need not request one separately, while those not on the exdata platform must coordinate backups through their internal IT department. The document emphasizes that while restores are technically possible after Year End cleardown, they should be considered emergency measures only, as they incur significant costs and should be avoided through careful Year End process execution.

t: P60 NI Figure does not match March payslip
s:
When the P60 figure differs from the March payslip, check whether there was a break in the employee’s service. The P60 reflects only the National Insurance (NI) contributions for the current period of employment.

 

For example, if the employee left in April and rejoined in May, the P60 will only d...
ss: P60 figures can differ from March payslips when an employee has had a break in service, as the P60 only reflects National Insurance contributions for the current employment period. If an employee left and rejoined within the same tax year, the P60 shows NI only from their return date, while the payslip may show the full year's total depending on your system settings. Open this article if your P60 NI amounts don't match what appears on the March payslip, or if you need to adjust how National Insurance is displayed across multiple employment periods. You'll learn how to enable the Multiple Periods of Employment toggle in Company Parameters to control whether payslips show partial or full-year NI contributions.
sl: This document addresses discrepancies between P60 National Insurance figures and March payslip amounts, particularly in situations involving breaks in employee service. The P60 form displays NI contributions only for the current continuous period of employment, whereas the payslip may show the full tax year NI total (April to March) depending on system configuration. The document explains that if an employee left and rejoined during the same tax year—for example, departing in April and returning in May—the P60 will only reflect contributions from the return date onwards. To resolve this discrepancy, users must navigate to Settings > Company Parameters > General Settings within the portal and select the appropriate company code from the dropdown menu. The document then instructs users to click Next and enable the "Multiple Periods of Employment" toggle to allow the system to display cumulative NI contributions across multiple employment periods on payslips. Changes must be saved by clicking the Save button to take effect. This guidance is primarily used by payroll administrators and HR professionals who need to reconcile P60 figures with payslip records and configure system settings to accurately reflect employee NI contributions across interrupted employment terms.

t: Who can defer their State Pension Contributory
s:
Individuals who qualify to defer their State Pension Contributory are those born on or after January 1st, 1958. They can claim the Contributory State Pension between ages 66 and 70. 

 

However, once you begin claiming your Contributory State Pension, you can no longer choose to defer your pension ...
ss: State Pension Contributory deferral eligibility applies to individuals born on or after January 1st, 1958, who can delay their pension claim between ages 66 and 70. Once you begin claiming your Contributory State Pension, deferral is no longer an option, even if you continue working, because PRSI contributions stop upon pension receipt. Open this document if you need to understand who qualifies to defer their State Pension, the age window for deferral decisions, and the permanent nature of claiming once you start receiving payments.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre outlines eligibility criteria and key constraints for deferring State Pension Contributory benefits. It specifies that individuals born on or after January 1st, 1958 are eligible to defer their State Pension Contributory and have the option to claim between ages 66 and 70. The document clarifies an important limitation: once an individual begins claiming their Contributory State Pension, they can no longer choose to defer their pension claim, regardless of whether they continue working. This restriction exists because PRSI (Pay Related Social Insurance) payments cease once pension payments commence, preventing further deferral options. The document serves as a reference guide for pension administrators, HR professionals, and individuals managing State Pension claims within the Access Group system who need to understand deferral eligibility and the permanent nature of the claiming decision. Related functionality in the system includes processes for deferring the start date of State Pension Contributory and PRSI Class Automation, which are referenced as connected topics for users seeking more comprehensive pension management information.

The State Pension Contributory is available to those who are at leas...
ss: Deferring your State Pension Contributory allows you to delay claiming your pension between ages 66 and 70, giving you flexibility in when to start receiving payments. Use this guide if you're deciding whether to defer your State Pension to continue working, build additional PRSI contributions, qualify for eligibility, or secure a higher pension rate. This is particularly relevant if you're approaching State Pension age and want to understand how deferral can improve your long-term pension benefits or help you meet the 520-contribution requirement.
sl: This document explains the new State Pension Contributory deferral option available from January 2024, which allows individuals aged 66 to 70 to choose when to begin claiming their pension within that age range. The State Pension Contributory is available to those who are at least 66 years old and have made sufficient Pay Related Social Insurance (PRSI) contributions, specifically requiring a minimum of 520 contributions equivalent to 10 years of service. The document outlines three primary reasons individuals might consider deferring their pension start date: the ability to continue working and contributing to PRSI during the deferral period, which can increase their personal rate of payment or help them meet the 520-contribution qualifying threshold; the opportunity to become eligible for State Pension if they did not qualify at age 66; and the potential to receive a higher State Pension rate by waiting rather than claiming at 66. The document is designed for pension administrators, HR professionals, and system users working with the Access Group payroll or pension management system who need to understand and implement this deferral functionality. Related topics covered include guidance on employees assessed but postponed for auto-enrolment who wish to start their pension earlier, general State Pension Contributory information, and PRSI Class Automation configuration, all of which provide context for managing pension deferrals within the broader pension administration framework.

t: Manage corrections during year end process
s:
This explains how to process payroll corrections when the year end cleardown job affects your payroll data. Following these procedures ensures that payroll corrections are applied correctly and maintains data integrity during the year end transition period.

 

You should apply these procedures when...
ss: Managing payroll corrections in your system requires different approaches depending on where you are in the year end cycle—before the last tax period closes, after it closes but before year end cleardown, or after cleardown completes. This document outlines which correction methods (supplementary runs, cancel payments, manual payments) are allowed at each stage, since timing significantly impacts what you can do and your reporting requirements. Open this guide when you've discovered payroll errors that need correcting and need to understand whether you can process them immediately or must wait until after the year end cleardown job runs. The procedures differ for Ireland (December/January tax year) and the UK (March/April tax year).
sl: This document provides guidance on how to manage and process payroll corrections within the Access Group payroll system when they are affected by the year end cleardown job, ensuring data integrity is maintained throughout the year end transition period. The document addresses the critical timing issue that corrections must follow different procedures depending on whether they are discovered before or after the year end cleardown job is executed, and it outlines the specific allowable correction actions at each stage of the year end process. Before the last period of the tax year is closed (December for Ireland, March for the UK), users can perform supplementary runs for the last closed period and process cancel and manual payments as normal. After the last period closes but before year end cleardown runs, supplementary runs for the final tax year period are permitted, but cancel and manual payment processing are restricted until after cleardown completes. Following the year end cleardown execution, in the first period of the new tax year (January for Ireland, April for the UK), users may cancel and process manual payments for any previous period, though supplementary runs are not available since no previous period exists within the new tax year. After the first period of the new tax year has been completed, both supplementary runs for the previous period and standard cancel and manual payment processing become available again. The document references related articles including procedures for canceling year end cleardown status on UAT or Live environments, required reports before supplementary runs, pre-year end data checks, and comprehensive year end FAQs to support users through the full correction and cleardown process.

s:

ss: P60s are official UK tax documents that summarize an employee's annual earnings and tax deductions, which employees need for personal tax returns and financial planning. This document covers how to generate and distribute P60s in your payroll system for employees who were employed on or after 5 April, with a deadline of 31 May. You'll use this guide if you need to print P60s for distribution or release them to employees through the ESS portal, with options to filter by company, pay group, employee, or location. The process includes configurable print settings such as duplex printing, labels, and a toggle for including zero-paid employees.
sl: This document provides comprehensive instructions for producing P60s, which are official UK tax documents that employers must issue to employees summarizing their annual earnings and tax deductions for the financial year. P60s must be provided to any employee still working on or after 5 April by 31 May, making this process essential for ensuring employees have accurate records for personal tax returns and financial planning. The document describes two primary methods for generating P60s: printing physical copies and releasing them online through the Employee Self-Service (ESS) portal. For the print method, users navigate to Year End > Manage > Print P60s and configure settings including Company, Pay Group, Employee reference, Location, and the relevant tax year, with optional toggles for Extra Pay Days (if week 53 was processed), Generate Labels, and the Print Zero Paid Employees option for employees with no annual pay. Within P60 Print Options, users must ensure Duplex is selected and can choose to release P60s to employees through the ESS portal. For the online method, users follow a streamlined path through Year End > Manage > Print P60s > Release to Employees, then select the company and enter the tax year before clicking OK. This document serves HR, payroll, and finance teams responsible for end-of-year compliance and employee record management, helping them navigate the specific system workflows and configuration options needed to produce compliant P60 documents efficiently.

ss: The apprenticeship levy is a mandatory employer tax that funds apprenticeship training, and this document covers how to configure it in PeopleXD Payroll. You'll learn how to set up company parameters (including levy thresholds and pay codes), create analysis codes and pay codes, configure GL matrices, and exclude specific companies, pay groups, or employees from levy calculations. Open this document when you need to establish apprenticeship levy settings for your organization, allocate thresholds across connected companies, or adjust which employees and pay groups are subject to the levy during payroll processing.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on configuring the apprenticeship levy within the PeopleXD Payroll system, explaining that the levy is a government tax paid by employers and stored in a fund to support apprenticeship training costs. The configuration process involves multiple sequential steps accessible through the Settings menu, beginning with reviewing company parameters by navigating to Settings > General > Other, selecting Apprentice Levy from the Select Detail dropdown, and then configuring the Apprentice Levy Threshold and Apprentice Levy Pay Code for each company in the organisation. The document details how to set up new analysis codes and pay codes for apprentice levy tracking, including cloning the Employer NI pay code, assigning it analysis type AL, and ensuring specific toggles are correctly configured such as leaving the Inland Revenue pay path toggle disabled and not marking it as an RTI statutory payment. For organisations implementing employee-level apprentice levy costing during payroll validation, users must review and update the GL matrix and configure company costing elements including cost centre, location, expense, and project fields through Settings > General Settings. The document also addresses exclusion scenarios, allowing administrators to exclude entire companies, specific pay groups, or individual employees from apprentice levy calculations by toggling the relevant Exclude options found in Settings > General > Other > Apprentice Levy, while offering the option to include Benefits in Kind (BIK) pay codes in apprentice levy calculations. This configuration document is primarily used by payroll administrators and system implementers who need to set up apprentice levy compliance within their organisation's payroll system.

ss: Reconcile your payroll year end data by comparing the pre year end data check report against the employee cumulatives (PAY084B) report and final control report (PAY355CT) across each pay group. Match specific figures: taxable pay less pension, PAYE, and National Insurance (both employee and employer) must balance between reports, accounting for the fact that pre year end figures split current and previous employment while the control reports combine them. Open this document when you're running your payroll year end process and need to verify that all tax, PAYE, and NI totals are correct before proceeding to year end cleardown.
sl: This document provides guidance on reconciling pre year end reports as part of the payroll year end process in the Access Group system. The core task involves comparing three key reports: the pre year end data check report, the employee cumulatives (all) (PAY084B) report, and the final control report (PAY355CT), reconciling them for each pay group across the company. The document specifies four main reconciliation checks: current taxable plus previous P45 taxable must equal taxable pay less pension on the final control report; current PAYE plus previous P45 taxable must equal PAYE on the final control report; NIC EE all employment must equal NI employee on the final control report; and NIC ER all employment must equal NI employer on the final control report. It clarifies important technical distinctions, such as that taxable pay figures on the pre year end data check report are net of pension (aligned with P35 and P60 returns), while the employee cumulatives and final control reports combine current and previous employment figures rather than splitting them. The document also addresses reconciliation of the pre year end statutory pay report by comparing the other statutory all employments report to figures on the detailed observation report for relevant pay codes, and notes that post year end taxable pay figures (including P60s) are always whole numbers, requiring allowance for rounding when reconciling totals. ss: Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) is a mandatory reporting process in PeopleXD Payroll that requires you to report relevant payments to Revenue by the date you pay employees. This FAQ addresses common implementation questions, including how to handle ERR if you use a separate expense system, manage employee pay group changes, process expense advances, and report non-monetary items like gifts. Open this document when you're setting up ERR in PeopleXD Payroll or need quick answers about specific scenarios—such as whether external claimants must be included or how to configure pay codes for physical items. It's especially useful if you're integrating PeopleXD Payroll with third-party systems or need clarification on what triggers an ERR return to Revenue.
sl: This FAQ document addresses common questions about Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) implementation within the PeopleXD Payroll system, designed to help users understand mandatory compliance processes and system configurations. The document clarifies that organizations using PeopleXD Payroll with separate third-party expense systems must report relevant payments to Revenue by the employee pay date, and should consult their expense vendor for integration guidance, while warning against directly connecting PeopleXD Payroll to third-party software to share employment IDs for data protection reasons. It explains operational scenarios such as the requirement to complete an ERR return to Revenue before moving an employee between payroll companies as of January 2024, and provides guidance on processing non-taxable expense advances through the system. The document specifies technical behaviors including how PeopleXD Payroll automatically excludes external claimants (identified by X prefix employee numbers) from ERR file generation, while including regular employees (C prefix), since external claimants are not employees of the employer. It also provides configuration instructions for handling non-payment items such as gifts by requiring users to create two offsetting payments—one for the item's value and one to reverse it—so these benefits appear in ERR returns as required by Revenue. This resource is primarily used by PeopleXD Payroll administrators and HR professionals responsible for ERR compliance, payroll configuration, and managing employee expense and payment reporting to tax authorities.

The document addresses two specific tax scenarios that require special handling: employees with exemption orders who revert to emergency tax and USC rates until their 2026 RPN is retrieved (reviewed via Employee > search > VIEW > Tax Details), and employees with exclusion orders who must remain on emergency basic rates until their new RPN is received (managed through Manage Payroll > pay group > Outputs tab > ROS > PAYE Modernisation > Employee Parameters > Exclusion Order). This guidance is essential for payroll administrators and HR professionals who need to ensure compliance with Irish revenue requirements before processing payroll for the new tax year.

ss: Payroll and HR teams in Ireland need to review and configure tax year 2026 rate changes, including preloaded updates to PAYE, PRSI, USC, SSP entitlement days, and ASC, plus manually configure OAP rates, social welfare rates, and national minimum wage. The document also covers important software changes affecting your payroll system: statutory sick pay remains at five days (not increasing to ten as previously planned), new zero-emission vehicle benefit-in-kind categories are introduced, temporary OMV reductions extend through 2028, and auto enrolment begins in January 2026. Additionally, new Single Pension Scheme reporting requirements via payroll submissions will be reportable from 2027 and mandatory from 2028. Open this document during your year-end process to understand what rate updates are automatic versus manual, and which compliance and payroll configuration changes take effect in 2026.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive overview of tax rate changes and software updates applicable to the 2026 tax year in Ireland, designed for payroll administrators and HR professionals conducting year-end processes. The document outlines two categories of rate updates: preloaded rates that are automatically configured as part of the year-end software update (including PAYE, PRSI, USC, SSP Entitlement Days, and ASC) and customer-configurable rates that require manual setup (OAP rates, Social Welfare Rates, and National Minimum Wage). Several significant software changes are introduced for 2026, including the continuation of statutory sick pay entitlement at five days per calendar year despite previous legislative plans for expansion, and the introduction of a new vehicle category (A1) for zero-emission cars under Benefit in Kind calculations with rates between 6% and 15% of original market value. The document confirms that temporary reductions to the original market value threshold will be extended through 2028, decreasing from €10,000 in 2026 to €5,000 in 2027 and €2,500 in 2028, while the lower mileage limit for employer-provided vehicles remains permanently set at 48,001 miles. Auto enrolment in Ireland will commence in January 2026, and a new reporting requirement for Single Pension Scheme data through the Payroll Submission Return will be reportable from 2027 and mandatory from 2028, requiring employers to submit five new data items including Gross Pensionable Remuneration, Net Pensionable Remuneration, Full Time Equivalent/Work Pattern, and accrued lump sum and pension referable amounts. The document also confirms that the small benefit exemption remains unchanged at €1,500 per annum per employee.

The document also covers specific payroll scenarios including how to handle employee start and leave dates that fall in previous tax years but involve payments in subsequent periods, how tax credits and USC COPs are calculated during emergency weeks (53, 54, and 56) on a week-one basis, and how to verify that salary sacrifice pay codes have the Salary Sacrifice indicator enabled in Portal under Settings > Codes > Pay Codes to ensure accurate gross pay reporting on Payroll Submission Files. This guidance is intended for payroll administrators and finance professionals responsible for managing year-end payroll processes and ensuring compliance with Revenue requirements, particularly in an Irish payroll context.

ss: State Pension Contributory (SPC) is a new indicator added to the Revenue Payroll Notification (RPN) that flags employees receiving their State Pension Contributory. You can view this indicator in Portal either through the Employee PAYE Certificates upload screen or by navigating to an individual employee's record and viewing their certificates. Open this document when you need to identify which employees are receiving SPC, retrieve RPN information for the new tax year, or understand deferral options for State Pension Contributory.
sl: This document describes the State Pension Contributory (SPC) indicator, a new field added to the Revenue Payroll Notification (RPN) for employees who are receiving State Pension Contributory payments. The document explains where users can access and view this indicator within the Portal system through two primary navigation paths: either by clicking Uploads and then Load Employee PAYE Certificates, or by clicking Employee, then View, followed by View Certs. The SPC indicator helps payroll and HR professionals identify which employees are in receipt of State Pension Contributory, which is critical information for accurate payroll processing and tax compliance. Users may encounter scenarios requiring them to check SPC status, defer SPC start dates, or determine employee eligibility to defer their State Pension Contributory, all of which are addressed through related support articles referenced in the document. The document also references PRSI Class Automation functionality and provides guidance on retrieving RPNs for the new tax year, which are processes that interact with the SPC indicator. This document is typically used by payroll administrators, HR professionals, and finance teams working within the Access Group system who need to manage employee pension contributions and ensure proper tax and pension deductions are applied.
