ss: Ireland payroll administrators use this checklist to manage critical year-end tasks in their payroll system, covering everything from finalizing the current tax year's payroll to preparing for the new tax year. The checklist breaks down pre year end activities (completing payroll, submitting to Revenue, configuring rates), the year end cleardown itself, and post year end steps (retrieving RPNs, reviewing PAYE Modernisation configuration, and posting ASC returns). Open this document in the weeks leading up to your payroll year end to ensure you don't miss essential compliance and configuration tasks. It includes specific guidance for public sector employers managing ASC data checks and work-sharing arrangements.
sl: This document is a practical checklist designed to guide Irish payroll administrators through the year-end process in the Access Group payroll system, organized into three distinct stages: pre year end, run year end, and post year end activities. The pre year end stage requires completing payroll for the current tax year, ensuring all payroll submissions and returns have been sent to Revenue and reconciled, reviewing rate and software changes, and configuring manual rates, with an additional public sector requirement to generate an ASC pre year end data check report. The run year end stage involves completing the year end cleardown process, which is a critical step in closing out the tax year in the system. The post year end stage encompasses retrieving RPNs (Revenue Personal Numbers) for the new tax year, reviewing the company calendar settings, reviewing PAYE Modernisation configuration, and posting Additional Superannuation Contribution (ASC) returns, with sector-specific tasks for public sector employees including reviewing work sharing setup and shorter working year or parental leave configuration. This checklist helps resolve common year end challenges by providing a structured approach to ensure no critical tasks are missed and all regulatory requirements with Revenue are met. The document is primarily used by payroll administrators and HR professionals in Irish organizations who need to properly close out one tax year and prepare systems for the next, with specific applicability to public sector organizations that have additional configuration and reporting requirements.

t: Configure auto enrolment
s:
Before you configure auto enrolment in PeopleXD, ensure that you have completed the following steps:

Register your organization with NAERSA via the Employer Portal and provide bank details for direct debit.

Obtain a valid ROS digital certificate for API authentication; this is the same certificate...
ss: Auto enrolment in PeopleXD requires prerequisite setup including NAERSA registration, ROS digital certificates, and user profile assignments before processing your first auto enrolment payroll. This document walks you through creating the necessary pay codes (employee and employer contributions), setting up Irish auto enrolment pension schemes, and configuring default pension rules in the ROS outputs section. You'll also find instructions for optional configurations like excluding specific pay groups or employees, assigning multiple schemes by reference data, and enabling salary sacrifice indicators. Open this guide when you're ready to implement auto enrolment for your organisation or need step-by-step help configuring any component of the system in PeopleXD.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on configuring auto enrolment for Irish pension schemes within the PeopleXD payroll system. It covers prerequisite setup requirements including NAERSA organization registration via the Employer Portal, obtaining a valid ROS digital certificate for API authentication, and assigning the AUTO_ENROL_IE_MENU profile to relevant users. The core configuration involves creating two separate pay codes (one for employee contributions and one for employer contributions) through the Settings > Pay Codes menu, cloning existing pension deduction codes, and ensuring the employee pension deduction code is configured as Pre-Taxable, Non-PRSIable, and Non-USCable. The document details how to create an auto enrolment pension scheme by duplicating an existing Irish pension scheme through Settings > Pension Scheme, linking the employee pay code created above, and activating the Irish Auto Enrolment indicator. It explains how to establish default pension scheme rules globally or assign multiple schemes by reference data through the Manage Payroll > Outputs > ROS > Auto Enrolment Submissions menu path. The guide also covers optional configurations including excluding specific pay groups or individual employees from auto enrolment assessments (with warnings that NAERSA does not recognize valid reasons for employee exclusions once instructions are issued), setting up proxy server credentials for internet connectivity, and enabling salary sacrifice indicators on relevant pay codes. This document is essential for payroll administrators and finance teams implementing auto enrolment in Irish organizations using PeopleXD before processing their first auto enrolment payroll.

t: Retrieve and manage AEPN instructions for Auto Enrolment
s:
An AEPN is an official instruction from NAERSA that specifies which employees to enroll, which employees to stop deductions for, the contribution rates to apply, and any status changes, such as opt-outs or suspensions. 

⚠️Important: Always retrieve AEPNs before every payroll run, even if you believ...
ss: Auto Enrolment Pin Notices (AEPNs) are official instructions from NAERSA that tell you which employees to enroll in pensions, stop deductions for, and what contribution rates to apply. This document walks you through retrieving the latest AEPN files into PeopleXD before every payroll run, printing the NAERSA exceptions report to catch data mismatches, and viewing AEPN details on individual employee records. You'll also learn how to clear interim AEPN records, check AEPN history, and review validation reports after payroll processing. Open this guide whenever you need to manage pension auto-enrollment instructions or troubleshoot employee enrollment issues in your payroll system.
sl: This document provides comprehensive instructions for retrieving, managing, and validating Auto Enrolment Pension Network (AEPN) instructions in the Portal system, which are official directives from NAERSA that specify employee enrollment status, deduction cessation, contribution rates, and status changes such as opt-outs or suspensions. The core retrieval process involves navigating to the Uploads tab, selecting Load Employee AEPN Certificates, choosing the company reference number from a dropdown menu, and clicking OK, which downloads a CSV file of all AEPNs linked to your tax registration number into the Report Centre. The document emphasizes that AEPNs must be retrieved before every payroll run regardless of whether changes are anticipated, as NAERSA updates these instructions nightly. Users can print the NAERSA exceptions report through the same Load Employee AEPN Certificates screen to identify employees in the NAERSA file who are missing from PeopleXD, uncover duplicate PPS numbers, and resolve employee ID mismatches, with a critical requirement to investigate and resolve all exceptions before proceeding with payroll. The document describes how to clear interim holding table records if re-retrieval or data issue resolution is needed, view active AEPN details on individual employee pension records through the Employee menu and Pension tab, and access historical AEPN information via the AEPN Certs Enquiry screen. After payroll validation (Pay140) is executed, users can review results through the Manage Payroll section's Control Reports, selecting either the AEPN Update Report to track updated instructions and exceptions or the Auto Enrolment Report to review revenue gross pay and calculated contributions.

t: Generate and submit auto enrolment contributions
s:
Before generating your submission files, follow these steps:

Retrieve the latest AEPN instructions.

Complete the payroll processing for your pay group.

Review the Auto Enrolment Contribution Report to ensure its accuracy.

⚠️Important: Submit your contribution files on or before the employee's pa...
ss: Auto Enrolment Contribution Report and submission file generation in PeopleXD Portal allows you to prepare pension contribution data for NAERSA (the pension regulator). Follow this process to generate JSON and CSV submission files, override employee contribution data if needed, transfer files to NAERSA before the 6:30 PM pay date deadline, and reconcile contributions afterward. Open this document when you need to submit Auto Enrolment pension contributions after completing payroll processing, or when you must correct submissions, resubmit data, or verify that contributions were processed correctly.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on generating, submitting, and reconciling auto enrolment pension contributions within the Portal system, covering the complete workflow from preparation through final reconciliation with NAERSA. Before generating submission files, users must retrieve the latest AEPN instructions, complete payroll processing for their pay group, and review the Auto Enrolment Contribution Report, with a critical deadline of submitting contribution files on or before the employee's pay date when NAERSA must receive funds by 6:30 PM. The document details the generation process accessed via Manage Payroll > Outputs tab > ROS > Auto Enrolment Submissions, where users select from the Auto Enrolment Pension dropdown to Generate Submission File and choose submission types including Normal Submission (O), Full Resubmission (F), Delete Submission (D), or Previous Period Submission (P), with the system automatically generating JSON and CSV files plus control and exception reports. For submission types beyond standard submissions, users must first enable their respective indicators in Pay Group Parameters by activating settings such as Allow Full Resubmission, Allow Deletes, or Previous Periods. The Override Submission function allows manual corrections of specific fields including Gross Pay, contribution amounts, and pay reasons (such as INPA, PAADJ, or ROEED) before transfer, though corrections after transfer to NAERSA must be made through the Employer Portal. Once submission data is prepared, users transfer files to NAERSA through the Transfer Submission File option, selecting their company reference and toggling the Transfer File toggle for each file, with the ability to check pending transfer statuses. The document concludes with reconciliation options through NAERSA, offering both Contribution Reconciliation Details for employee-level results by payroll run and Contribution Reconciliation Summary for employer-level totals by tax month, with NAERSA designated as the single source of truth for all pension contribution data.

t: Opt an employee out of a pension scheme when contractually enrolled
s: The auto enrolment assessment validates each employee's eligibility for auto-enrolment. This assessment checks whether the employee is already enrolled in a qualifying pension scheme. If the employee is enrolled, they are considered contractually enrolled and will not be auto-enrolled. Additionally,...
ss: Removing a contractually enrolled employee from a pension scheme requires end-dating their pension record in the system, which triggers a reassessment during the next auto-enrolment validation. Unlike auto-enrolled employees, contractually enrolled workers don't have a standard opt-out right under Pension Regulator rules—they must follow the scheme's membership cessation procedures. Open this article when you need to process a pension exit for an employee who was enrolled through their employment contract rather than through auto-enrolment, and when you may also need to process a payroll adjustment to stop pension deductions in the current period.
sl: This document explains the process for ending a contractually enrolled employee's pension scheme membership, which is necessary because employees who are contractually enrolled do not have the standard right to opt out of their pension scheme. The document describes how the auto enrolment assessment validates employee eligibility and records contractually enrolled status in the Auto Enrolment History table with either Event 6 (Contractual Enrolment Eligible) or Event 7 (Contractual Enrolment Non-Eligible). It clarifies that unlike employees who are auto-enrolled or opted in as non-eligible job holders, contractually enrolled employees cannot simply opt out but must instead have their pension end-dated to exit the scheme. When a pension end date is entered for a contractually enrolled or entitled worker employee, the subsequent validation and assessment process will reassess the employee and potentially auto-enrol them if they meet eligibility criteria. The document notes that users may need to process an adjustment if they do not want pension deductions to continue in the current payroll period. This guidance applies to payroll and HR administrators managing pension scheme memberships who encounter contractually enrolled employees wishing to leave their pension scheme, and it references The Pension Regulator's guidance confirming that workers enrolled under contractual enrolment have no right to choose to opt out and must follow the scheme's rules for ceasing membership.

t: Employee hasn't auto-enrolled in portal
s:
Auto-enrolment pension schemes are mandatory workplace pension arrangements that require employers to automatically enrol eligible employees in a qualifying pension scheme. 

 

This ensures that workers build retirement savings throughout their careers. The purpose of this legislation is to increas...
ss: When an employee fails to auto-enrol in a pension scheme through your portal, this document walks through the most common causes and how to fix them in the People Management system. It covers six key scenarios: the employee being marked as Exempt, auto-enrolment not being enabled for the company, the employee not meeting the minimum age requirement, defaults not being saved correctly, the staging period being set in the future, or qualifying earnings falling below the threshold. Use this guide when you need to troubleshoot why an eligible employee hasn't been automatically enrolled, or when you need to adjust settings like pay codes and company parameters to enable proper auto-enrolment.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving situations where employees have not been automatically enrolled in a qualifying pension scheme within an employer portal system. It outlines six primary causes and their corresponding solutions: an employee being marked as 'Exempt' in their Personal Profile under Payroll > Legislative Options > Auto Enrolment Details dropdown, auto-enrolment not being enabled at the company level via Settings > UK Tax Rates > General > Auto Enrolment (requiring the Apply Auto Enrol toggle to be activated), an employee not meeting the minimum age threshold configured in the Company Parameters section, defaults not being saved correctly in the Pensions Rules reference item field, the staging period being set in the future, and qualifying earnings falling below regulatory thresholds. The document includes step-by-step navigation instructions for accessing each configuration area through the dashboard's People Management section and the Settings menu, as well as guidance on reviewing and modifying pay codes that may be incorrectly classified as Non Qualifying earnings. This resource is designed for payroll administrators and HR personnel who need to diagnose and correct auto-enrolment failures within their pension administration system, particularly in the context of UK workplace pension legislation compliance.

t: Exclude pay code from pension calculation
s:
Incorrect pension contributions can occur when certain pay codes are unintentionally included in pensionable calculations. This issue typically occurs due to incorrect pay code configuration. 

 

To resolve this, you'll need to exclude the pay code from pension calculations either globally or for s...
ss: Excluding pay codes from pension calculations prevents incorrect pension contributions that result from improper pay code configuration. You can remove a pay code from pensionable calculations either globally across all schemes or selectively for specific pension schemes using the portal settings. Open this document when you need to adjust which pay codes should or shouldn't contribute to employee or employer pension calculations, or when correcting pension contribution errors caused by misconfigured pay codes.
sl: This document provides guidance on resolving incorrect pension contributions by excluding specific pay codes from pensionable calculations within the Access Group payroll system. The document describes two distinct processes depending on exclusion scope: a global exclusion method applicable when a pay code should never be pensionable under any circumstances, and a scheme-specific exclusion method for when a pay code should only be excluded from a particular pension scheme type. For global exclusions, users navigate to Settings > Codes > Pay Codes (Classic), select the relevant pay code from the dropdown menu, and toggle off the Pensionable ER field (with an optional Pensionable EE toggle for employee pension exclusions), then save changes. For scheme-specific exclusions, users access Settings > Codes > Pension Scheme, select the relevant pension scheme code, enable the Pay Code Exclusions toggle on the Next Page, add the pay code through a List interface, and configure the Pensionable ER and Pensionable EE toggles as needed. The document targets payroll administrators and HR professionals who manage pension scheme configurations and need to correct pay code misclassifications that have resulted in unintended pension contributions. This resource is particularly useful for organisations that have discovered configuration errors causing incorrect pension deductions or contributions and need to implement corrective measures quickly.

t: Employee 'Assessed But Postponed' on auto enrolment but wants to start pension at an earlier date
s:
Pension auto-enrollment is designed to enroll employees after 'X' months. However, if an employee requests to opt into the pension scheme earlier, you need to adjust their joining date to reflect this request.

 

Since the employee is already associated with a scheme and an auto-enrollment validati...
ss: When an employee with "Assessed But Postponed" auto-enrollment status requests to join their pension scheme earlier than the scheduled date, you'll need to manually adjust their pension record in the system. This involves ending their current postponed pension scheme (using the same date as the start date) and then adding a new pension scheme entry with the "Voluntary Opt in Auto Enrolment" event selected. Open this document if you need step-by-step instructions for modifying an employee's pension joining date before their auto-enrollment trigger date in PeopleXD.
sl: This document provides step-by-step guidance for HR administrators who need to manually adjust an employee's pension enrollment when that employee requests to join a pension scheme earlier than the standard auto-enrollment date. The document explains that employees marked with "Assessed But Postponed" status cannot join before their scheduled auto-enrollment date, even if they request early entry, and describes how to resolve this by ending the current pension scheme and creating a new one with an earlier start date. The process involves navigating to the Employee section, searching for the relevant employee, and clicking VIEW to access their record. Under the Pension menu, administrators must first end the current scheme by editing it and setting the end date to match the start date, then submit the changes. Next, they add a new pension scheme by returning to the Employee > Pension section, clicking Add, and filling in the required details while ensuring the "Auto Enrolment Opt In Event" dropdown is set to "Voluntary Opt in Auto Enrolment" before submitting. This document is typically used by payroll specialists, HR administrators, or pension managers within organizations using the Access Group system who encounter employees wanting earlier pension scheme participation than their auto-enrollment postponement date allows.

t: Enter or change re-enrolment period
s:
Updating the re-enrolment period in portal involves specifying the timeframe during which eligible employees are automatically re-enrolled in a pension scheme. 

 

This process plays a crucial role in ensuring compliance with legal requirements for pension auto-enrolment, while also preserving the ...
ss: Use this guide to set up or update your pension re-enrolment period in portal, which determines when eligible employees are automatically re-enrolled in the pension scheme. The re-enrolment period is a compliance requirement that helps you manage pension contributions and avoid penalties for non-compliance with auto-enrolment legislation. Open this document if you need to configure re-enrolment dates per pay group under Auto Enrolment parameters, or if you're managing the three-year reassessment cycle for employees who have opted out. The process involves navigating to Settings > Tax Rates > General > Auto Enrolment and entering the re-enrolment period in YYYYWW format for each pay group.
sl: This document provides guidance on updating the re-enrolment period in a payroll portal to ensure eligible employees are automatically re-enrolled in pension schemes in compliance with auto-enrolment legislation. The document explains that re-enrolment is a critical compliance requirement that helps manage employee pension contributions, support retirement planning, and avoid penalties for non-compliance. Key legal parameters are outlined, including that employees who opt out are reassessed every three years, employees who opted out within the past 12 months cannot be re-enrolled, and employees cannot be postponed during the re-enrolment process. The document provides step-by-step instructions for updating the re-enrolment period by navigating to Settings > General > Auto Enrolment, selecting Pay Groups from the Options dropdown menu, highlighting the relevant pay group, and entering the new re-enrolment period in YYYYWW date format before saving. The re-enrolment period can be configured per pay group under Auto Enrolment parameters in the pay group section of the portal. According to best practice noted in the document, a company's re-enrolment period should be set for 3 years after the staging date and then in 3-year cycles thereafter. This document is intended for payroll administrators and HR professionals responsible for configuring pension auto-enrolment settings and managing employee re-enrolment cycles within their organization's payroll system.

t: Back Office: Set up pension scheme
s:
Setting up a pension scheme in the back office is essential for ensuring that employees have access to retirement savings options that comply with regulatory requirements.

 

Establishing this scheme within payroll allows automatic deductions from employee wages and facilitates employer contributio...
ss: Setting up a pension scheme in CorePay involves configuring retirement savings options that comply with regulatory requirements and integrate with payroll for automatic employee and employer contributions. Use this document when you need to create a new pension scheme in the back office, define contribution percentages, select scheme types (such as Group Defined Benefit or Group Defined Contribution), and establish deduction rules for both employees and employers. You'll follow step-by-step instructions to enter pension scheme codes, descriptions, company details, and configure renewal periods and social welfare deductions. Open this guide if you're establishing pension schemes for the first time, setting up Additional Voluntary Contributions (AVCs), or need to configure how pension deductions are calculated from employee wages.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on establishing a pension scheme within the Access Group back office system to ensure employees have compliant retirement savings options with automatic wage deductions and employer contributions. The setup process begins in CorePay by navigating to Reference and selecting Pension Scheme, where users enter a unique numeric pension scheme code and descriptive name. Key configuration fields include specifying the pension company, selecting the scheme type (Group Defined Benefit Scheme, Group Defined Contribution Scheme, or Other Scheme), and setting the renewal period to determine whether renewals occur at the tax year start (period 1) or period 40. The document details how to configure employee deductions through Deduction Percent EE 1 to 3 fields, which can be broken into multiple percentage tiers or fixed values based on pensionable pay, with an optional social welfare deduction that applies the old age pension rate before calculating contributions. Additional configuration options include setting the Deduction Percent (ER) for employer contribution percentages, using the Override Scheme field to control whether percentages can be modified at the employee level, and ensuring employee pay codes are properly established with the Pensionable Employee Indicator set to Y before scheme setup. The document is designed for payroll administrators and back office staff responsible for implementing pension compliance and benefits infrastructure, helping them resolve setup requirements and configuration scenarios for both standard pension schemes and specialized arrangements like Additional Voluntary Contributions (AVCs).

t: Pension refund not processing for a UK employee
s:
A pension refund is the return of contributions made by an employee to their pension scheme. This typically occurs when an employee leaves a job or opts out of the pension plan before reaching retirement age.

 

For UK employees, processing a pension refund is crucial to ensure they receive any exc...
ss: Pension refunds for UK employees return contributions made to their pension scheme, typically when an employee leaves their job or opts out before retirement. This document troubleshoots why pension refunds fail to process in CorePay and Portal, covering issues like missing pensionable pay records, disabled refund generation settings, and closed pension schemes with end dates. Open this if a pension refund isn't processing for a UK employee and you need to identify the underlying cause and follow the step-by-step resolution for your system (Back Office or Portal). It provides specific navigation steps for accessing and updating employee pension details to enable refunds.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre explains pension refund processing for UK employees, covering what pension refunds are, why they are essential when employees leave or opt out of pension schemes, and most importantly, a troubleshooting guide for when refunds fail to process. The document identifies five specific scenarios that prevent pension refunds from processing: no pensionable pay recorded, no Year-to-Date (YTD) pension accumulated, the Generate Refund option not being enabled, and an end date being set on the pension record. For the no pensionable pay issue, users must enter a timesheet value of 0.01 pence on a pensionable pay code; for the Generate Refund not enabled issue, users must navigate to either the Maintain Employee Pension Details screen in Back Office or the Edit Pension screen in Portal and enable the Generate Refund toggle while ensuring an adjustment amount is entered. The document provides detailed step-by-step navigation instructions for both Back Office and Portal systems: in Portal, users click Employee, search for the employee, click VIEW then Pension, highlight the pension scheme, click the three-dot icon, and click Edit; in Back Office, users click CorePay, then Employee, then Maintain Employee Details, search for the employee, select Pension under Select details, and click Edit for the relevant pension scheme. To resolve the end date issue, users must ensure no end date is set on the Maintain Employee Pension Details screen, as a closed pension record will prevent refunds from processing. This document is primarily used by UK payroll administrators, HR professionals, and finance teams who manage employee pension schemes and need to troubleshoot failed pension refund transactions in Access Group's payroll systems.

t: Refund pension contributions
s:
Refunding pension contributions involves returning the amounts that employees have paid into their pension plans, typically when they leave the organization or opt out of the pension scheme.

 

It is important because it ensures financial accuracy and provides former employees access to funds they ...
ss: Refunding pension contributions involves returning amounts employees have paid into their pension plans when they leave the organization or opt out of the scheme. This process ensures financial accuracy and gives former employees access to their funds for other financial needs. Use the portal to process refunds by locating the employee record, navigating to their pension details, and adjusting the normal amount in the designated section. Open this document when you need to return pension funds to a departing employee or when processing an opt-out request.
sl: This document provides guidance on refunding pension contributions that employees have paid into their pension plans, particularly when they leave an organization or elect to exit the pension scheme, with the primary purpose of ensuring financial accuracy and restoring access to funds for former employees' financial needs. The document outlines a specific step-by-step process completed within a portal system that begins by navigating to the Employee section and using the search field to locate the relevant employee record, then clicking VIEW to access their details. Once in the employee record, users must click on the Pension section and locate the relevant pension code, where they click the three-dot icon to access additional options, followed by clicking Edit to modify the pension settings. A critical configuration requirement is that users must either enter a future date in the End Date field or leave it blank, as the refund will not process if the pension is marked as closed, which prevents the system from completing the refund transaction. Under the Adjust Normal Amount section, users initiate the actual pension refund processing, and after completing these adjustments, they save all changes by clicking the Save button. The document is primarily intended for HR personnel, payroll administrators, or pension scheme managers who regularly process employee departures or pension scheme changes and need to handle the financial reconciliation of returned contributions, and it includes references to related articles addressing common issues such as refunds not processing for UK employees or refunds applied with negative salary adjustments.

t: Delete or amend pension rate of pay
s:
Deleting an incorrect pension rate of pay for an employee is essential for ensuring accurate payroll processing and compliance with pension regulations. This action is necessary when errors occur, such as incorrect data entry, changes in employee circumstances, or updates to pension scheme rules.

 ...
ss: Pension rate of pay errors in payroll systems need to be corrected to ensure accurate pension contributions and regulatory compliance. Use this guide when you've discovered an incorrect pension rate has been entered for an employee and need to delete or amend it before payroll processing. If the error spans multiple tables or payroll has already run, you'll need to contact support with your employee number, incorrect rate, and effective date so they can run database scripts to fix it. After support resolves complex cases, you can re-enter the correct pension rate.
sl: This document explains the process for deleting or amending an incorrect pension rate of pay for an employee within a payroll system, emphasizing the importance of correcting such errors quickly to ensure accurate payroll processing and compliance with pension regulations. The document identifies common scenarios requiring this action, including incorrect data entry, changes in employee circumstances, and updates to pension scheme rules, and stresses the need to take prompt action before payroll calculations run for the relevant period to protect employees' financial planning and retirement savings. A critical limitation is noted: if the incorrect pension rate of pay has affected multiple database tables (specifically the personal_rate and position_history tables) or if the PAY290 payroll process has already executed, users cannot delete the entry themselves and must instead raise a support case online. When requesting support, users must provide specific details including the employee number, the incorrect rate of pay, and the date effective, after which the support team will run database scripts to delete or amend the incorrect entries. Once the support team completes the correction, users can then re-enter the correct pension rate of pay into the system. This document is typically used by payroll administrators or HR personnel who need to correct pension contribution errors in an Access Group payroll system before those errors propagate through payroll calculations and affect employee payments.

t: Add employee pension
s:
Adding an employee pension involves enrolling an eligible employee into a pension scheme, allowing them to save for retirement and benefit from contributions made by both the employee and the employer. 

 

This action should be completed when onboarding a new employee, after changes to an existing ...
ss: Enrolling an eligible employee into a pension scheme in PeopleXD allows them to save for retirement with contributions from both employee and employer. Open this guide when onboarding a new employee, after changes to an employee's status, or when setting up a new pension scheme. The process involves searching for the employee, navigating to the Pension tab, selecting a scheme from the dropdown, setting a start date, and configuring auto-enrolment settings. Use this guide if you need step-by-step instructions on how to add or manage pension records in the system.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide to adding employee pensions within the Access Group system, covering the enrollment process for eligible employees into pension schemes to enable retirement savings through combined employee and employer contributions. The process should be initiated during new employee onboarding, following changes to an existing employee's status, or when implementing a new pension scheme. Users navigate to the Employee section, use the Search Name field to locate the relevant employee, then access the Pension tab via the View menu to begin enrollment. From the Add option, users select the appropriate pension scheme from the Select Scheme dropdown menu, with the system automatically populating employee and employer contribution fields if the scheme defines both. Users must enter a Start Date, can update prepopulated data using override fields if needed, and select an Auto Enrolment Opt In Event from the corresponding dropdown menu in the Auto Enrolment area before completing any additional details and clicking Submit. The document addresses common scenarios such as employees assessed but postponed on auto-enrollment who wish to start earlier, pension refunds not processing for UK employees, and employee opt-out procedures, while also referencing related configuration guidance for auto-enrollment settings. This resource is designed for HR and payroll administrators responsible for employee onboarding and pension management within the Access Group platform.

t: Error: 'Pension already exists for the employee/Scheme Code'
s:
If you assign an employee a pension scheme or opt in an employee who previously had a pension and the following error appears, it is because you are attempting to add a new pension scheme to an employee that already has a record of the same scheme type. 

 

The correct process is to enter a new sta...
ss: When assigning or opting an employee into a pension scheme in PeopleXD, you may encounter an error stating the pension already exists for that employee and scheme code. This error occurs because the system detects a duplicate pension record rather than allowing a new enrollment. Instead of creating a new entry, update the existing pension record by entering new start and end dates and removing any opt-out reason. Open this document if you're trying to add a pension scheme to an employee and receive a duplicate pension error message.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre explains the error message that appears when attempting to assign a pension scheme to an employee who already has an existing record for that same scheme type. The error occurs specifically when users try to assign an employee a new pension scheme or opt in an employee who previously had a pension but already has a record of the matching scheme in the system. ss: Processing a pension refund with withholding tax in CorePay requires setting up two specific pay codes in the Reference section. First, you'll create a refund deduction pay code configured as non-taxable and non-PRSIable with a multiplier of -1, then set up a separate withholding tax deduction pay code using the same settings. Open this document when you need to process a pension refund that requires 20% withholding tax deduction, or when you're setting up the CorePay pay codes for the first time to handle pension refunds in your payroll system.
sl: This document provides comprehensive instructions for processing pension refunds that include withholding tax deductions within the Access Group's CorePay system. The process requires setting up two separate pay codes accessed through CorePay > Reference > Pay Codes: a refund deduction pay code and a withholding tax deduction pay code, each configured with specific field values including Description, Taxable (set to Non-Taxable), Hours/Values/Days/Units (set to Value), Deduction/Allowance/BIK (set to Deduction), Maximum Value (999999.99), PRSIable (set to Non-PRSIable), Multiplier (-1), Minimum Value (-999999.99), Analysis Code, Payslip Description Override, and Expense fields. The document clarifies that neither pay code is subject to PAYE, PRSI, USC, or PRD, and notes that withholding tax values are calculated outside of CorePay and must be entered as positive values on the timesheet. The actual CorePay refund process involves three steps: entering a negative value timesheet for the refund amount, refunding 100% of contributions using the refund pay code, and deducting 20% withholding tax using the withholding tax pay code. Back office payroll administrators and pension scheme managers use this document when they need to process pension refunds that comply with withholding tax requirements, particularly when standard PAYE and social security deductions do not apply.

t: Additional Superannuation Contributions (ASC) FAQs
s:
Additional Superannuation Contributions (ASC) are mandatory pension payments made by public sector employees in Ireland to fund their retirement benefits.

 

These contributions are calculated based on an employee's earnings and pensionable pay. Ensure accurate deductions and record keeping during ...
ss: Additional Superannuation Contributions (ASC) are mandatory pension deductions for Irish public sector employees that replaced the Pension Related Deduction (PRD) from January 2019 onwards. This document explains how ASC is calculated based on pensionable gross pay, how it integrates into CorePay and CorePension systems during payroll processing, and covers tax treatment including PRSI relief, USC exclusions, and payslip display requirements. Open this if you need to understand ASC eligibility rules across different pension schemes (Single Scheme, Standard Accrual, and Fast Accrual), handle employee transitions between schemes, or clarify how ASC differs from the previous PRD system.
sl: This FAQ document provides comprehensive guidance on Additional Superannuation Contributions (ASC), a mandatory pension contribution system introduced by the Irish government on January 1, 2019 to replace the temporary Pension Related Deduction (PRD) for public sector employees. The document explains that ASC is calculated based on pensionable gross pay (rather than total gross pay as with PRD) and details how ASC integrates with both the CorePay and CorePension systems following the Year End delivery for the 2018 tax year. It clarifies the tax and social welfare treatment of ASC, specifying that while ASC qualifies for tax relief and Employer PRSI relief, it does not qualify for USC relief or employee PRSI relief, and must be shown separately from other deductions on payslips. The document distinguishes between three pension scheme types for ASC purposes: Single Pension Scheme (applicable to those appointed after January 1, 2013), Standard Accrual Pension schemes (for those appointed before 2013), and Fast Accrual Pension schemes (such as the Garda Superannuation Scheme), noting that contribution-doubling requirements for fast accrual schemes do not apply to ASC. It addresses practical payroll scenarios including how to handle social welfare benefits and maternity leave in ASC calculations, clarifies that Benefit-in-Kind is excluded from ASC (differing from PRD treatment), and explains that ASC operates cumulatively like PRD but on a Week 1 basis when employees move between schemes and have not yet provided an ASC45 form. The document also references related reporting processes such as generating ASC35 and ASC60 annual reports and amending employee ASC cumulatives, making it essential reading for payroll administrators and HR professionals managing public sector employee pension contributions.

ss: The OAP (Occupational Absence Pay) element on pension liability may calculate incorrectly when an employee holds multiple appointments, as the system combines both positions instead of treating them separately. The issue typically stems from the multiplier setting on the salary record rather than the FTE value—you'll need to check and adjust the multiplier to reflect only the relevant appointment. If further adjustment is needed, the OAP Pay Multiplier field in the Sundry Profile can be used as an additional multiplier applied after the standard pay multiplier. Open this document if you're seeing combined FTE calculations across multiple appointments or incorrect pension liability amounts for employees with non-pensionable secondary roles.
sl: This document addresses a calculation error in the Access Group payroll system where an employee holding a second non-pensionable appointment incorrectly combines both positions when calculating the Full-Time Equivalent (FTE) for occupational assistance pension (OAP) liability. The root cause of the issue is an incorrect multiplier on the salary record associated with the appointment, not the FTE itself, since the system uses the multiplier rather than FTE for OAP calculations. To resolve this problem, users should navigate to the appointment record to check the FTE, then examine and modify the multiplier associated with the salary under that specific appointment, noting that the current multiplier may include both appointments combined but is capped at a maximum value of 1. The document explains that a secondary field called OAP Pay Multiplier is available in the Sundry Profile and can be configured if additional adjustment is needed, though this field functions as an additional multiplier applied after the employee's pay multiplier rather than as an override to it. This guidance is intended for payroll administrators and pension specialists who manage employee records with multiple appointments in the Access Group system and need to ensure accurate OAP calculations. The document also references related articles covering similar multi-appointment pension calculation issues, helping users identify related problems in their system configuration.

The document addresses a specific problem scenario where this timing restriction results in an underpayment of employer contributions, providing a resolution process: apply an override during an adjustment period in the next payroll cycle that includes both the correct amount and the underpayment amount, then make further adjustments in the following period to reflect the correct total and remaining adjustment amounts. This guidance is relevant to payroll administrators and pension scheme managers who handle auto-enrolment processes in the Access Group payroll system and need to ensure accurate contribution calculations despite the limitations on when overrides can be applied. sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving issues where AVC (Additional Voluntary Contribution) pension amounts are being incorrectly deducted from employee pay in the Access Group payroll system. The document outlines four primary areas to investigate: the accuracy of the AVC value stored in the employee's pension record (accessed via Employee > VIEW > Pension menu), whether timesheets have been added that might be adjusting the AVC amount (checked via Employee > VIEW > Timesheets Current Period), and the status of the Accumulate Unpaid indicator setting which determines whether the system carries forward unpaid AVC contributions from periods when employees had insufficient net pay. The Accumulate Unpaid indicator, when enabled, causes the system to accumulate AVC contributions that could not be deducted and attempt to recover them in subsequent payroll periods until the full amount is collected. Users can check and modify this indicator setting either through the Portal interface (Settings > Pay Codes, then searching for and editing the Accumulate Unpaid rule) or the Back Office system (CorePay > Reference > Pay Codes > Deductions tab), with an important caveat that pay code level changes impact all employees using that code and should be tested in UAT before applying to Live. For employee-specific overrides without changing pay code settings, users can access the Accumulated Unpaid Pension field through either the Portal (Employee > VIEW > Pension > Edit) or Back Office (CorePay > Employee > Employee Pension Details, Page 3), then clear or adjust the accumulated value and re-run the Payroll Validation job to prevent further deductions.

After submission, the document instructs users to run a single validation using a single payslip to verify the changes have been processed correctly. This document is primarily used by pension administrators, HR professionals, and payroll managers who need to handle early enrolment requests that deviate from standard auto-enrolment postponement dates, and it relates to broader auto-enrolment configuration and opt-out procedures referenced in the related articles section.

ss: Auto Enrolment pension pay codes must be configured correctly in your payroll system to ensure employee and employer contributions report accurately in Revenue PSR submissions. The two critical requirements are keeping the Pension Type field blank and using unique pay codes that aren't shared with other pension schemes—misconfiguration can result in contributions being incorrectly reported to Revenue and NAERSA stopping employees' Auto Enrolment Pension Numbers (AEPNs). Open this document if you need to check your current pay code setup in Portal or Back Office (CorePay), fix existing configuration errors, or resolve issues from previously submitted incorrect PSR returns. sl: This document provides guidance on configuring Auto Enrolment pension pay codes to ensure correct reporting in Revenue PSR (Pay and Service Request) submissions within the Access Group payroll system. The document outlines two critical configuration requirements: the Pension Type field must be left blank for Auto Enrolment pay codes, and these pay codes must be unique and not reused from other pension schemes. Users can check their configuration through either the Portal (by navigating Manage Payroll > Outputs tab > ROS > PAYE Modernisation > Pay Code Parameters) or the Back Office (CorePay > Update > PAYE Modernisation > Pay Code Parameters), where they verify the Pension Type dropdown is blank and confirm no other pension scheme uses the pay code. Incorrect configuration can result in Auto Enrolment contributions being incorrectly reported to Revenue, NAERSA stopping AEPNs (Auto Enrolment Pension Numbers) for affected employees, and requiring PSR correction submissions, with stopped AEPNs requiring direct contact with NAERSA for resolution as they do not reopen automatically. To fix misconfigured pay codes, users can either clear mapped pension types directly in the Pay Code Parameters screen or create new unique pay codes through Settings > Codes > Pay Codes > Create New Pay Code, with the option to remove pay codes from other schemes and create separate codes for those schemes. The document provides specific scenarios covering high-impact issues (such as pay codes with EE1, EE2, EE3, or ER pension types, or pay codes shared between multiple schemes) and lower-impact situations (such as adjustment or AVC codes), along with recommended actions for each. This resource is essential for payroll administrators and HR professionals using Access Group systems who need to ensure Auto Enrolment compliance and avoid Revenue reporting errors and AEPN suspension issues.

t: Clear stuck payroll job
s:

⚠️Important: If a job is stuck and it is not related to payroll validation or the generation of salaries and allowances, please chat with us in the Access Digital...
ss: Payroll jobs that become stuck or fail due to system interruptions and network timeouts can be resolved using the payroll job reset process in your portal. Before clearing a failed job, download and review the log file from Manage Payroll to check for ORA errors, which help identify the underlying cause. If no errors are found in the log, you can clear the failed job by clicking Reset Failed Job from the three-dot menu in Manage Payroll. Open this article when a payroll validation or salary and allowances generation job stops progressing and needs to be manually reset before rerunning.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide for resolving payroll jobs that become stuck due to system interruptions or processing errors, particularly those caused by network timeouts, though it explicitly advises users to contact support if the stuck job is unrelated to payroll validation or salary and allowance generation. The resolution process begins by checking the log file through the Manage Payroll menu's three-dot icon to download and review the file for ORA errors, using CTRL + F to search for specific error codes that may indicate the underlying cause. Once the log file has been reviewed, users proceed to clear the failed job by accessing the same Manage Payroll menu and clicking the Reset Failed Job option, which only appears when a job displays a failed status rather than while still running. If the Reset Failed Job option is not visible, administrators must enable this menu option by navigating to Security > Menu Profiles, searching for the Payroll profile, and setting the menu option "Update paygroup reset: WS_PAYROLL_MENU.PATCH_PAYGROUP_RESET" to Active. The document also covers user access configuration, requiring administrators to go to Security > User Management, select All Back Office Accounts, and either create new users or update existing ones with the appropriate Menu Profiles permissions. This document is primarily intended for payroll administrators and support users who need to diagnose and clear stuck payroll processing jobs before attempting to rerun them, and it references related failures such as PAY140 Validation Job and PAY290 Generate Salaries and Allowances job issues.

ss: The "Payroll Status Closed for processing" error occurs when the Generate Salaries and Allowances job is run with the Final Run option selected, which locks the payroll from further edits. sl: This document addresses a specific error message that users encounter in payroll processing systems when the "Payroll Status Closed for processing" error appears during salary and allowance generation. The error occurs when the Generate Salaries and Allowances job has been executed with the Final Run option enabled, which locks the payroll status and prevents further modifications. To resolve this issue, users must re-run the Salaries and Allowances job while ensuring the Final Run option is not selected, which will reverse the closed status and allow payroll processing to continue. The document references configuration settings related to the final run indicator and suggests consulting additional documentation to understand how enabling or disabling this indicator affects payroll operations. This guide is intended for payroll administrators and HR professionals who manage salary and allowance processing within their organization's payroll system. The document also provides cross-references to related error messages and articles, including guidance on running the payroll process itself and other common processing errors such as pay group availability issues and date validation problems.

ss: The Final Run Indicator is a safety feature in the Pay module that locks an employee's record once activated, preventing changes that could affect the next pay run. Use this when running the Generate Salaries & Allowances (PAY290) job in Portal under Manage Payroll > Process Payroll > Run/Rerun, toggling "Is this your Final Generate?" on or off depending on whether you're completing the final payroll run. Open this document when you need to understand how to activate the Final Run Indicator to protect your pay group's data before confirming timesheets and finalizing payroll processing.
sl: The Final Run Indicator is a safety mechanism within the Pay module that prevents modifications to employee records once activated, ensuring no changes interfere with the next pay run for a pay group. Users can run the Generate Salaries & Allowances process multiple times during initial checks without restriction, but the system will not permit timesheet confirmation until the Final Run Indicator has been turned on. The Final Run Indicator is accessed through the Generate Salaries and Allowances job (PAY290) within Portal by navigating to Manage Payroll, selecting the relevant pay group, clicking Process Payroll, and then clicking Run/Rerun next to Salaries and Allowances. During this process, users must toggle the "Is this your Final Generate?" field on if running the final salaries and allowances, or keep it off if it is not the final run, then click OK to confirm. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and finance teams who need to understand the workflow for finalizing pay runs and preventing accidental modifications to employee records that could affect payroll processing. The document also references related issues such as salary not generating, allowances not generating, and PRSI weeks not generating as expected, indicating it helps resolve common payroll generation problems.

t: Incorrect expense code on history after complete update
s:

ss: Expense codes in PeopleXD may be incorrect or fail to update before payroll processing, and if discovered after the Complete Update job runs and the payroll period closes, they cannot be amended within PeopleXD itself. Instead, corrections must be made directly in your finance system or general ledger file, then the PeopleXD record updated prospectively for future pay periods. Open this document if you need to correct an expense code (or cost centre) that has already been written to the general ledger history. It also explains how to review the General Ledger before it's finalized and how to reverse timesheets if corrections are needed before the Complete Update stage.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses the problem of incorrect expense codes appearing in the general ledger after payroll processing in PeopleXD, explaining both preventative measures and corrective actions depending on the stage at which the error is discovered. The document outlines that if an incorrect expense code is caught during the Payroll Update stage, users can reverse the payroll and make necessary changes, but once the Complete Update job has been run and the payroll period is closed, the expense codes cannot be amended within the system and retrospective corrections should not be attempted. Instead, users must correct the data directly in their external finance system or on the general ledger file itself, then update the record in PeopleXD going forward to prevent future occurrences. The document provides specific navigation steps for reviewing the general ledger before it is written to history, which involves navigating to Manage Payroll, selecting Outputs under the relevant pay group, clicking General Ledger, completing the required fields, and selecting Generate. For corrections that are needed, the document instructs users to reverse timesheets by clicking Manage Payroll, selecting Process Payroll under the relevant pay group, clicking the three-dot icon next to Payroll Update, and selecting Reverse Timesheet Confirm before making the relevant changes. The guidance also notes that the same principles apply to cost centre errors, and the document is intended for payroll administrators and finance professionals who manage payroll processing and general ledger reconciliation in the PeopleXD system.

Once duplicates are confirmed, the document provides two separate removal procedures depending on the system being used: Portal users should navigate to Manage Payroll > Inputs > General and then select either Maintain Employee Position/Point or Maintain Personal Rates to delete the duplicate records before saving and re-running the job, while Back Office users follow a similar process through CorePay > Pay Rates. ss: Salary arrears in CorePay may be generated for an employee even when none are actually due, caused by common configuration or data entry errors such as incorrectly backdated salary rows, unprocessed amendments, position rate changes, pay group transfers, or CorePersonnel amendment issues. This guide walks through eight different scenarios that trigger false arrears generation and provides specific troubleshooting steps for each—from reviewing Rate History in CorePay to rerunning the PAY290 (Generate Salaries and Allowances) job. sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving unwanted salary arrears generation in the Access Group's CorePay payroll system, addressing scenarios where arrears are incorrectly calculated despite no arrears actually being due for the period. The document identifies nine common causes of this issue and outlines resolution steps specific to each scenario, including navigating to CorePay > Employee > View Employee Details > Rate History to check for incorrectly entered salary rows with past effective dates, and using CorePay > Pay Rates > Maintain Employee Position/Point to delete erroneous entries. Additional causes covered include unprocessed salary amendments, incompatibility between the PAY290 (Generate Salaries and Allowances) program and newly entered position rates, employee pay group transfers causing timing issues, incorrect personal rate or position/point rate configurations, and data inconsistencies such as missing Pay355 (Complete Update) dates on the Employee Utility screen. ss: Salary amendments in PeopleXD let you correct or remove incorrect salary lines that have been added with future effective dates. When a salary line is added in error, you should create a new salary amendment with the same effective date to override the incorrect entry rather than deleting it. For past effective dates, amendments are the only way to ensure accurate pay records. For future effective dates, contact the support team via a new case if deletion is absolutely necessary, including a screenshot of the problematic salary line.
sl: This document provides guidance on correcting erroneous salary line entries that have been added with future effective dates in the payroll system. It explains that when an incorrect salary line has been created, users should complete a salary amendment using the same effective date as the incorrect entry, which causes the system to ignore the incorrect line and use the latest salary added for that date instead. For salary entries with past effective dates, only a salary amendment can be used to correct the information and ensure accurate pay processing. For future effective dates, while the support team can delete entries if necessary, this approach is not preferred due to potential complications with future salary increases. To request deletion of a future-dated salary line, users must raise a new case online and reference this article while attaching a screenshot of the problematic salary line. The document essentially distinguishes between two correction strategies based on whether the incorrect entry has a past or future effective date, with amendments being the standard approach and deletion reserved only for specific future-dated scenarios where complications might otherwise arise.

sl: This document provides guidance on moving a payroll period forward for inactive pay groups in the CorePay system to align them with the current payroll period. sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for payroll administrators who encounter failures when running the Generate Salaries and Allowances (PAY290) job in the CorePay system, specifically when the job fails without generating timesheets. For employee hours issues, users should check the log file for ORA-06502 errors related to retrieve_employee_details and verify that employee hours values and increment due dates are valid. Absence without pay problems include multiple error types: divisor errors (ORA-01476) when absence without pay rows conflict with pension rate salary rows or when adjusted allowances are incorrectly ended, and calculate_absence_allowance errors when multiple open-ended absence records exist for one employee. Data conflicts on position_history tables produce ORA-01403 errors when scale points are missing, requiring payroll users to record the correct scale point and analysts to update the date_input field to prevent arrears. Additional failure causes include date effective errors on position history (resolved through CorePay Enquiry and View Position History screens), space allocation issues requiring database administration team intervention on the SHARED_POOL table, and various PAY290 trace file errors (ORA-04063 and ORA-01403) in calculating absence allowance and fetching employee details. The standard resolution approach across all scenarios involves retrieving the PAY290 log file, searching for ERROR entries to identify affected employee numbers, and either making configuration corrections or raising a support case with the log file and article reference included.

t: Salary not generating

ss: Salary not generating covers payroll processing issues in PeopleXD when employee pay amounts fail to calculate during payslip generation. It walks through four common causes—timesheet-based compensation settings, overlapping appointments, zero pay rates, and ended salary lines—with step-by-step fixes for each scenario. Open this article when employees show no pay on their payslips or you need to troubleshoot missing salary amounts before running payroll jobs. sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving issues when employee salaries fail to generate during payroll processing in the Access Group payroll system. It identifies and explains four primary causes of salary generation failures: employee setup indicating compensation based on timesheet input (which must be disabled via Employee > Tax Details), timing conflicts when employees have multiple primary appointments with misaligned end dates and salary effective dates, personal salary rates set to zero, and salary lines marked as ended on active appointments. For most scenarios involving incorrect or zero rates and ended salary lines, the document instructs users to navigate through People Management > Dashboard > Employees, search for the affected employee, access Current Salary, and add a salary amendment with correct details and effective dates, followed by running a single validation to confirm the correction. The document is designed for payroll administrators and HR personnel who process payslips and manage employee compensation data, helping them quickly identify root causes and apply targeted fixes to resume accurate salary generation. Related articles referenced suggest this is part of a broader knowledge base addressing payroll configuration issues, including allowances generation, position history errors, and salary problems following appointment changes.

t: Process payroll for a single employee

ss: The single processing task in the payroll portal lets you recalculate payroll for one employee without rerunning validation for the entire pay group. Use this when you need to fix or update an individual employee's payroll details while keeping other employees' processed data intact. Open this guide when you've made changes to an employee record and need to reprocess their payroll in isolation. You'll access it through Employee > Actions > Single Processing.
sl: This document provides guidance on using the single processing task feature in the payroll portal to calculate payroll for an individual employee rather than processing an entire pay group. The primary advantage of this functionality is efficiency—it eliminates the need to rerun the full payroll validation task for all employees in the pay group when only one employee requires recalculation. Additionally, the single processing task preserves previously calculated gross to nett details for other employees in the pay group, updating only the relevant employee's payroll tables rather than clearing down all calculated data. To use this feature, users navigate to the Employee section, search for the specific employee by name using the Search Name field, access the View menu, click Actions, and then select Single Processing. The document emphasizes an important caveat that after making updates to employee records, users must re-run the payroll process to ensure all changes take effect properly. This document is designed for payroll administrators and HR professionals who need to make corrections or adjustments for individual employees without disrupting the payroll calculations for their entire pay group.

t: Retrieve an FPS response file after RTI is rejected from HMRC
s:
Retrieving an FPS (Full Payment Submission) response file after receiving a Real Time Information (RTI) rejection from HMRC is essential for accurate payroll processing. 

 

When HMRC rejects an RTI submission, it signals discrepancies or issues that need addressing. Accessing the FPS response file...
ss: When HMRC rejects your Real Time Information (RTI) submission, you need to retrieve the FPS (Full Payment Submission) response file to identify the specific errors causing the rejection. This document covers how to access and review the FPS response file using either the Portal or Back Office system, helping you understand what discrepancies need correcting before resubmitting to HMRC. Open this guide when you've received an RTI rejection and need to diagnose the issues, correct your payroll data, and ensure accurate tax reporting for your employees. The step-by-step instructions walk you through generating the RTI file, locating the HMRC response file, and transferring corrected submissions to maintain tax compliance.
sl: This document provides guidance on retrieving FPS (Full Payment Submission) response files when HMRC has rejected an RTI (Real Time Information) submission, which is a critical step in resolving payroll reporting discrepancies and ensuring tax compliance. The document explains that HMRC rejections indicate errors or issues within the submitted data, and accessing the FPS response file allows employers to identify the specific reasons for rejection so they can correct errors and resubmit accurately. The document provides dual instruction paths for two different system interfaces: Portal and Back Office. For Portal users, the process involves navigating to Manage Payroll, then Outputs, selecting RTI and Generate RTI, choosing the relevant pay group from a drop-down menu, optionally selecting Test mode if the file should not be submitted to HMRC, and then clicking Generate followed by Transfer, with the response file (HMRCresponse.xml) available in Report Centre to indicate any errors. For Back Office users, the equivalent process requires navigating through CorePay and Update, accessing Real Time Information (RTI), Generate RTI, entering the pay group manually, optionally selecting Test mode, copying the file location, and then proceeding to Transfer RTI Files where company details are input and the copied location is pasted. Both pathways include an option to select Test mode to prevent files from being submitted to or loaded to the HMRC gateway, allowing users to validate their submissions before live transmission. This document is intended for payroll administrators and employers who need to troubleshoot failed RTI submissions and retrieve detailed rejection information to ensure accurate employee payroll reporting.

t: Complete Update (PAY355) job is stuck
s:
The Complete Update job (PAY355) is a critical process for finalising and updating payroll data. However, there may be instances where this job fails to complete due to various reasons. 

 

We have compiled a list of possible causes for the failure of the PAY355 job and how to resolve these.

 

 
...
ss: The Complete Update job (PAY355) is a critical payroll process in PeopleXD that finalizes and updates payroll data, but it can become stuck or fail to complete. Common causes include locked user sessions in Core screens, incorrectly configured PAY355.BAT files, upstream job failures (PAY300 or PAY290), data issues after rollbacks, and timing conflicts during system maintenance or minor version releases. Open this document when the PAY355 job is stuck or has failed to complete, and you need to troubleshoot the specific cause and follow resolution steps. You'll also need to retrieve log files (such as pay355.log) and raise a support case with Access Group to confirm the issue and clear the job for re-running.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving instances where the Complete Update job (PAY355), a critical payroll finalisation process, fails to complete or becomes stuck in the system. The document identifies and explains six primary failure scenarios: locked jobs caused by users remaining logged into Core screens, incorrect setup of the PAY355.BAT file, failure of the preceding Run Payroll Update (PAY300) job, execution of payroll jobs (PAY290 or PAY140) for individual employees with mismatched processing dates, update data issues that arise after database rollbacks requiring background table clearing, and timing conflicts occurring when jobs are run during system maintenance windows or PeopleXD minor version releases. For each scenario, the resolution process involves retrieving relevant log files such as pay355.log, pay300.log, and trace files, checking how to retrieve log files through the system documentation, and raising a support case online with the log file attached for investigation. The document emphasises that when PAY355 jobs fail during minor version releases, the database enters Restricted Mode, which prevents user connections and causes the job to fail after multiple retry attempts, making it appear stuck. Users should avoid scheduling job executions during maintenance windows and version releases, and jobs can only be safely cleared and re-run after support confirms the root cause by reviewing the log files. This resource is designed for payroll administrators and system users who manage the payroll update process and need to diagnose and resolve job execution failures within the Access Group payroll system.

t: Set up payroll calendar
s:
A payroll calendar outlines the specific periods for processing payroll, including pay and cut-off dates for timekeeping and payroll submissions.

 

Configuring the payroll calendar is essential to ensure timely and accurate employee payments while aligning with the company's financial processes an...
ss: Payroll calendars define the specific periods for processing payroll, including pay and cut-off dates for timekeeping and submissions in CorePay or via the Portal. Setting up a payroll calendar for each company ensures timely and accurate employee payments while aligning with your organization's financial processes and tax regulations. Open this document when configuring a new payroll calendar, adding week 53 or 54 entries, or amending period end dates—particularly during the year-end process for upcoming tax year periods. The document covers how to access payroll calendar settings, understand calendar fields like week numbers and financial periods, and use options to build or rebuild calendars.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on setting up and configuring a payroll calendar within the Access Group payroll system, which outlines specific periods for processing payroll including pay and cut-off dates for timekeeping and payroll submissions. The setup process differs depending on your interface: Portal users navigate to Settings > Company Parameters > Calendars and select the relevant company from the dropdown menu, while Back Office users access CorePay > Reference > Payroll Calendar and use the query icon to select the company number. Every payroll company must have its own calendar with a minimum of 52 weekly entries, with additional entries required if week 53 or 54 occurs during the year; the calendar automatically spans the current year plus the next year, with the year-end process generating calendars for two additional years ahead. The Payroll Calendar screen contains multiple configurable fields including Week Number (formatted as YYYYWW), Financial Period and 4/4/5 Period assignments, Weekend Date, and various indicators such as Fortnightly Indicator, 4 Weekly Indicator, Monthly Indicator, and Multi Run settings that determine payroll frequency and processing rules. The document also details two additional screen options: the Amend Dates feature allows users to adjust period end dates by adding or subtracting days across a selected range of periods, and a build/rebuild function for calendar creation. Critical warnings emphasize that payroll calendars should only be configured during the Year End process for upcoming tax year periods, with strict instructions not to modify calendars for current or closed periods without contacting support, as calendar changes directly impact payroll accuracy and employee payment timing.

sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for setting up a grossing up pay code feature that allows employees to receive a desired net payment amount by calculating the corresponding gross salary. The document first guides users through checking if a grossing up pay code already exists by navigating to Settings > General > System Configuration, then selecting Payroll Validation/Update and reviewing the Grossing Up Pay Code dropdown menu. If no pay code is configured, the document explains how to create two new pay codes in the portal via Settings > Codes > Pay Codes: a GRO (grossing up) code with a multiplier set to 1 for actual payment, and a NET code with a multiplier of 0 used solely for calculation purposes. For the NET pay code specifically, users must set the Grossing Up Method rule to Normal Nett and assign the Gross Adjustment Code rule to reference the GRO pay code. The document then describes finalizing the configuration by returning to System Configuration > Payroll Validation/Update, selecting the GRO code from the dropdown, and setting the tolerance value to 0 for exact amount matching. This guide is used by payroll administrators and HR professionals who need to configure net-to-gross payment calculations within their payroll system.

t: Error: 'Pay Group not available'
s:

ss: When generating salaries and allowances, validating payroll, or running payroll updates in CoreHR, you may encounter a "Pay Group not available" error caused by incomplete jobs (PAY290, PAY140, PAY300, or PAY355), invalid password characters, locked user sessions, or full tablespace. Open this document if payroll processing jobs are failing and you need to troubleshoot the root cause by reviewing job logs and trace files. The guide provides specific steps for each error scenario, including how to retrieve log files and when to escalate to support.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for the "Pay Group not available" error that occurs during payroll processing jobs in CoreHR, specifically when generating salaries and allowances, validating payroll, running payroll updates, or completing updates for newly hired employees. The document identifies six distinct root causes for this error: incomplete PAY290 (generate salaries and allowances) jobs, incomplete PAY140 (payroll validation) jobs, incomplete PAY300 (run payroll update) jobs, incomplete PAY355 (complete update) jobs, invalid characters in user passwords, locked user sessions preventing job execution, and full tablespace conditions. For each incomplete job scenario, users are instructed to retrieve specific log and trace files (such as pay290.log0000, pay290.trc0000, pay140.log0000, pay300.log0000, and pay355.log0000, where 0000 represents the Pay Group number) and submit them when raising a support case online. When invalid characters (/, %, -, or @) are found in a user's password, the resolution involves changing the password to contain only letters and numbers, logging out completely from CoreHR, clearing the job status, and then re-running the PAY290 job. The document is intended for payroll administrators and HR professionals who manage payroll processing in CoreHR and encounter job failures, providing them with systematic diagnostic steps and information needed to escalate issues to support when self-resolution through password changes or session management is insufficient.
