t: Negative arrears calculated for positive input retrospection
s:
Negative arrears calculated for positive input retrospection refers to the process of adjusting payroll records to correct past overpayments or discrepancies. 

 

The reason why negative arrears are calculated when processing PIR is because of the pay code type. PIR will always use scale point 1 wh...
ss: Negative arrears can be calculated when processing Positive Input Retrospection (PIR) in payroll if you're working with scaled allowance pay codes, since PIR defaults to scale point 1 which may not match the actual scaled values used. Use this document if you're investigating unexpected negative arrears in your payroll records after applying PIR adjustments. Follow the steps provided to check your pay codes in the portal's Settings > Pay Codes section to confirm whether a code is a scaled allowance, then manually calculate and correct any arrears through timesheet entry if needed.
sl: This document explains the process of handling negative arrears that arise during positive input retrospection (PIR) in payroll systems, specifically addressing how to identify and correct discrepancies in payroll records related to overpayments. The negative arrears issue occurs because PIR automatically defaults to scale point 1 when applied to scaled allowance pay codes, which can produce negative values depending on the specific scaled rates configured in the system. To diagnose whether a pay code is causing this problem, users must navigate to Settings, then Codes, and select Pay Codes within the portal interface. Users then search for the relevant pay code in the Search field and review the Pay Code formula screen, which displays the current scale rates and confirms whether the pay code is classified as a scaled rate allowance. When a pay code is identified as a scaled rate allowance, the document indicates that arrears cannot be automatically corrected through standard processing and must instead be manually calculated and adjusted through timesheet entry. This guidance is primarily used by payroll administrators and HR professionals who manage retrospective pay adjustments and need to resolve discrepancies between expected and actual payroll calculations when scaled allowances are involved. The document also references related issues including general arrears calculation errors, maternity pay (SMP) problems, negative pay errors following pre-tax deductions, National Insurance (NI) arrears following category changes, and pension scheme tiered date effective calculations.

sl: This document provides guidance on recording Additional Superannuation Contributions (ASC45) supplementary details for employees who have provided previous employment information through a P45 form. t: Error: 'The NI Letter cannot be B, E, I or T if Date of Birth [XX-XXX-XX] is after 5 April 1961'

ss: National Insurance (NI) letter validation errors on FPS exception reports occur when an employee's NI letter is incorrectly set to B, E, I, or T for those born after 5 April 1961, which violates HMRC guidelines. Open this article when you need to resolve this error by logging a support case, having the support team update the NI letter on locked tables, and regenerating your FPS file for resubmission. The document also covers whether pay adjustments are needed after correcting the NI letter classification and how to process any necessary manual payments or cancellations to reflect the change.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses a specific validation error that appears on FPS (Full Payment Submission) exception reports when an employee's National Insurance letter is incorrectly configured as B, E, I, or T for individuals born after 5 April 1961, which violates HMRC guidelines. The document outlines a multi-step resolution process that begins with logging a support case online and attaching the FPS exceptions report for the support team's review. The support team performs a background update to correct the NI letter classification on the locked tables, after which users must regenerate and resubmit the FPS file through the system. Additionally, the document addresses a secondary consideration: since NI letter changes do not automatically recalculate employee pay, users may need to process a cancel payment followed by a manual payment using the updated NI classification if pay adjustment is required. The corrected FPS should be submitted first, with any resulting pay differences then being reflected in the next FPS submission for the pay group. This guidance is primarily used by payroll administrators and support teams working with Access Group's payroll system who encounter this specific validation error during FPS submission workflows.

t: Cancel year end cleardown status on UAT or Live environments
s:
You may need to cancel the year-end cleardown status in your UAT or Live environment, but this action requires careful consideration. The year-end clear down is a critical payroll process, and reversing it is highly restricted due to its impact on payroll data. 

 

You cannot reverse the year end c...
ss: Canceling the year-end cleardown status in PeopleXD UAT or Live environments requires a full system database rollback, which reverses all work completed by every user since the cleardown was performed. This action should only be considered in extreme scenarios because it erases all payroll inputs and runs made after the cleardown and incurs a charge equivalent to half a day's work. Open this document if you need to understand the severe consequences of reversing year-end cleardown and the only method available to do so. Before proceeding, you must thoroughly assess the impact and explore alternative solutions, as this is a highly restricted process due to its critical effect on payroll data integrity.
sl: This document provides guidance on cancelling the year-end cleardown status in UAT or Live environments within the PeopleXD payroll system, a critical but heavily restricted process. The document explains that the year-end cleardown cannot be reversed through standard undo or cancel options; instead, the only method to cancel this status requires rolling back the entire system to a previous database state. Before proceeding with a rollback, users are advised to thoroughly assess the impact and explore all alternative solutions, as the process incurs a financial charge equivalent to half a day's work and results in permanent loss of all changes made since the cleardown. This document is designed for payroll administrators and system managers in organizations using the Access Group's PeopleXD platform who may need to address critical issues arising from year-end cleardown procedures.

ss: Overtime calculations in Back Office's CorePay system may produce incorrect hourly values when deriving pay from period gross salary. The most common cause is the FTE Hours field being set to 1 on the Employees Appointment Details screen, which forces the system to ignore employee-level or pay group-level hours and use incorrect calculations. You can resolve this by navigating to Personnel Profile > Post Profile > Amend Appointment Details and setting the FTE Hours field to null, then re-running the Validation job. Open this document if your overtime or hourly rates are calculating incorrectly in CorePay and you need to troubleshoot the FTE Hours configuration.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses a specific issue where overtime calculations in the Back Office system are producing incorrect hourly values derived from period gross pay for individual employees. The guide identifies and explains two primary causes of overtime calculation errors: an FTE Hours field configuration problem and an Indicator setting issue for second salary employees. For the FTE Hours problem, users must navigate to CorePay > Employee > Personnel Profile > Post Profile > View Appointment Details in Back Office to check whether the FTE Hours field is incorrectly set to 1, which causes the system to ignore employee-level or pay group-level hours and produce inflated hourly values. The document provides a concrete example showing how an FTE Hours value of 1 causes the system to calculate an hourly rate of 958.22 instead of the correct 24.72 when employee hours of 38.75 should override pay group hours of 39. To fix this configuration error, administrators must access Amend Appointment Details through the same menu path and set the FTE Hours field to null, then re-run the Validation job to recalculate overtime correctly. For the second issue involving the Indicator not being switched to look at FTE hours for second salary employees, the document directs users to raise a support case online and reference the article title along with specific employee examples rather than providing direct resolution steps. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and Back Office system users who encounter discrepancies in overtime calculations and need to troubleshoot configuration settings affecting hourly rate calculations.

t: When is the RPN applied to an employee's record
s:
The RPN is applied and validated to an employee's record during the Validation Stage (PAY140) of payroll.

 

For example, if one pay group is at the run payroll update stage (PAY300), the RPN details used for payroll validation will also be applied during the Payroll Update. Any revenue updates fro...
ss: The RPN (Revenue Protection Number) is applied and validated to employee records during the Validation Stage (PAY140) of your payroll process. If a pay group is already at the Payroll Update stage (PAY300), the existing RPN details will be used for that update, but any new revenue updates from a fresh RPN download won't take effect until the next validation runs. Open this document if you need to understand when RPN changes are processed, why recent RPN updates aren't showing in payroll yet, or how RPN validation timing affects your pay groups.
sl: This document explains when the RPN (Revenue Protection Number) is applied and validated within an employee's payroll record in the Access Group system. The RPN validation occurs specifically during the Validation Stage, which is identified as process PAY140 in the payroll workflow. When a pay group progresses to the Payroll Update stage (PAY300), the RPN details that were used during validation are also applied at that point in the process. Revenue updates from the most recent RPN download will not become active until the Validation Stage is executed for the relevant pay group. The document clarifies that if RPN details are not immediately applied, they are not deleted from the system but instead remain inactive until the validation job runs again. This document serves payroll administrators and HR professionals who need to understand the timing and stages at which RPNs take effect, and it references related troubleshooting articles covering common errors such as unavailable pay groups, RPN retrieval and upload procedures, job conflicts, and unavailable RPN scenarios.

To resolve this, users navigate through the People Management portal by selecting People Management from the dashboard menu, then locating the employee through the Employees view and accessing their Current Salary record. Within the Current Salary section, users click the Allowances tab, select the relevant allowance, and use the three-dot menu icon to click Edit, where they can update the payroll end date and save the changes. The document cautions that adding a past date may generate salary arrears that require processing. If the allowance cannot be located or edited in People Management, users are instructed to raise a support case online referencing the article title and providing a screenshot of the allowance, the allowance pay code, and the intended payroll end date. s:

sl: This document describes the manual process for handling Temporary Rehabilitation Remuneration (TRR) payments in CorePay when an employee has exhausted full and half pay, as this functionality is not currently automated in the system. After the complete update job PAY355 has run, users navigate to CorePay > Employee > Employee Pension Details > Maintain Pension Details and access Page 2 to manually update the Tax Year, Calendar Year, and To Date fields under the Cumulatives group to include the total value of timesheet adjustments, since these fields are not automatically updated based on manual adjustments. The document emphasizes that breaking down contributions across the three separate pay codes is critical for accurate payslip display and proper data reporting to the CorePension module for pension statement details, rather than consolidating the adjustment into a single Deduction Adjustment (EE) field which would obscure the breakdown needed for payroll history purposes.

Within the employee record, users access the Select Details window and click on Payment Method, where they can enter the Alternative Bank Details and specify the exact percentage of net pay to be allocated to the alternative bank account. This document is typically used by payroll administrators or HR personnel in Back Office who need to configure payment distribution settings for employees requesting salary splits, and it references related procedures such as setting up foreign bank accounts and managing employee payment details synchronization between Core Personnel and CorePay.

t: Warning: "Please ensure that the Apprentice Levy liability for the tax month selected has been paid to HMRC via Third Party EFT before generating the EPS file"
s:
If you see a warning message when generating the EPS, it indicates a new feature introduced in version 28.0.105.

 

Issues occur if the EPS is generated for a tax month before the Third Party EFT for the revenue, including the Apprentice Levy, has been paid. The EPS takes the most recent tax month ...
ss: The Apprentice Levy feature in version 28.0.105 requires that Third Party EFT payments for revenue (including the Apprentice Levy) be submitted to HMRC before generating the EPS file for that tax month. If you generate an EPS before the corresponding Third Party EFT payment is made, the system calculates incorrect Year-to-Date values, causing discrepancies in subsequent Apprentice Levy calculations. Open this document if you receive a warning message when generating an EPS, or if you need to understand the correct sequence for processing Third Party EFT payments and EPS files to avoid recalculation issues.
sl: This document explains a warning message that appears when generating an Electronic Payment Submission (EPS) file in version 28.0.105, which alerts users to a critical sequencing issue in payroll processing. The problem occurs when an EPS is generated for a tax month before the corresponding Third Party EFT (Electronic Funds Transfer) payment for revenue, including the Apprentice Levy, has been submitted to HMRC. The system uses the most recently generated tax month to calculate amounts, which causes incorrect Year-to-Date (YTD) calculations; for instance, if an EPS for May 2024 is generated before a Third Party EFT for May 2024 is paid, the subsequent EFT will incorrectly subtract May's EPS amount instead of April's when calculating what is owed. This sequencing error prevents users from accurately generating a Third Party EFT bank file to calculate the Apprentice Levy liability after the EPS has been created. To resolve this issue, users must delete the most recent EPS history record and regenerate the prior month's EPS file (such as April's), though they should not attempt to resubmit this file to HMRC since it has already been reported. The document ultimately advises users to ensure the Apprentice Levy liability for the selected tax month has been paid to HMRC via Third Party EFT before generating the EPS file to avoid these discrepancies and rework.

It then explains how to generate Shorter Working Year transactions by accessing CorePay > Employee > Advanced Employee Features > SWY > Generate Shorter Working Year Transactions, which will only create entries for unprocessed employees and should only be used after the rest of the pay group has already been processed. The document addresses the scenario where payroll processing timing differs across a pay group, allowing administrators to handle employees with term-time arrangements separately while preventing errors from premature or duplicate transaction generation. Important limitations noted include that this process will overwrite existing logs for the pay group and that the Shorter Working Year feature is incompatible with Positive Input Retrospection employees, making it essential to understand these constraints before implementation. The document is intended for payroll administrators and HR personnel using the Access Group Back Office system who need to manage flexible working arrangements for employees who work only during school term periods while receiving salary distributed annually.

ss: Grossing up normal nett calculations in CorePay may produce incorrect employee net pay values. If the difference doesn't match expected amounts, use this document to determine whether database scripts are needed and what details to include when raising a support case.
sl: This document provides a troubleshooting procedure for resolving incorrect nett value payments when employees receive grossed-up compensation in the Access Group Back Office payroll system. This document is relevant for payroll administrators and HR personnel who manage timesheet processes across Core Time and CorePay systems and need to troubleshoot discrepancies in hourly rate calculations. The document also references related issues such as occupational salary offsets for absences, hourly pay code errors, and overtime calculation problems, indicating it is part of a broader knowledge base addressing CorePay calculation errors.

sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses issues with AEO (Attachment of Earnings Order) protected earnings calculations that are producing incorrect results. From this dropdown, users select either Gross Pay or Nett Pay depending on their configuration requirements, then close the page by clicking X and save the changes. The document explicitly notes that any changes made to this setting will impact all currently configured AEOs in the system. This guide is intended for payroll administrators and compliance officers who need to verify and correct how AEO deductions are calculated to ensure statutory compliance. The document also references related issues such as DEA pay code setup, attachment of earnings deduction errors, and minimum wage reporting problems that users may encounter in similar payroll scenarios.

sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses a specific database constraint violation error that occurs when running the pay355 Complete Update job in the payroll system. sl: This document provides instructions for disabling obsolete pay codes in the Access Group Back Office system, specifically within the CorePay module. sl: This document addresses the Budget Regeneration Failed issue, which occurs when the system cannot successfully regenerate budgets, resulting in incomplete or inaccurate budget data within the Access Group system. sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses an error message that appears when reviewing the Key Observation report for employees who have left the company in the previous month. The error occurs because the departing employee has no remaining salary to process, meaning any configured salary offsets cannot be applied or deducted. The document clarifies that this situation does not negatively impact the employee since they have already left the organization and explains that the error message itself will not interfere with normal payroll processing operations. To avoid encountering this issue in subsequent payroll runs, users should proactively configure necessary salary offsets for the leaver during their final payroll periods before departure. The document is primarily intended for payroll administrators and HR professionals who manage employee leavers and process timesheets within the Access Group system, particularly those reviewing Key Observation reports. Related guidance is available for similar error scenarios involving unapproved rejoiner timesheets, negative pay calculations after pre-tax deductions, and employees with missing timesheet entries.

t: Unprocess Zero Gross indicator
s:
The Unprocess Zero Gross indicator is a system feature that allows payroll administrators to unprocess pay runs where employees have zero gross pay.

 

You need to use this feature to correct payroll errors, adjust employee records, or ensure accurate reporting when zero gross pay entries are mista...
ss: The Unprocess Zero Gross indicator is a payroll system feature that controls how zero gross pay entries are handled during pay runs. Use this feature when you need to correct payroll errors, adjust employee records, or ensure accurate reporting for employees with zero salary amounts. The feature offers three options—Yes (prevents processing and tax refunds), Partially Process (processes employees but blocks tax refunds for zero salary staff), and No (allows tax refunds)—each with different impacts on arrears and day history records. Open this document when troubleshooting zero gross pay processing issues or deciding which setting best fits your payroll correction needs.
sl: The Unprocess Zero Gross indicator is a payroll system feature designed to help administrators manage and correct pay runs where employees have zero gross pay, addressing common payroll errors and ensuring accurate reporting when such entries are processed mistakenly. This feature provides three configurable options to handle zero gross pay scenarios differently depending on business requirements and payroll outcomes. When set to "Yes," employees with zero salary are not processed at all and no tax refunds are issued for any employees, though this setting can impact arrears calculations since days paid do not flow to day history. The "Partially Process" option allows zero salary employees to be processed while preventing tax refunds specifically for those zero salary employees, while still maintaining accurate arrears by recording days paid in history. When set to "No," the system operates as if tax refunds are being issued normally. Payroll administrators and finance teams use this feature when correcting payroll errors, adjusting employee records, or reconciling reporting discrepancies related to zero gross pay entries. The document references related issues such as arrears calculation problems, negative pay errors after pre-tax deductions are applied, and considerations for grossing up pay codes, linking this feature to broader payroll processing workflows and system integrations.

t: Warning: You must run "calculate hours in WFM" if payroll left overnight
s:

The purpose of this message is to alert clients to avoid leaving the payroll period open overnight after compl...
ss: The WFM (Workforce Management) system displays a warning message when the Confirm Timesheets process runs overnight without payroll finalization, which can cause absences to incorrectly carry over into the next payroll period. This document explains how to resolve the issue by reversing timesheets through the Portal's Manage Payroll and Process Payroll functions. Open this if you see the warning message in your pay group or need to prevent payroll data errors caused by leaving the payroll period open overnight. Follow the step-by-step instructions to reverse timesheets and ensure your payroll period closes properly before end of day.
sl: This document provides guidance on a warning message that appears in Portal when users access pay groups, cautioning against allowing the Confirm Timesheets process to run overnight without finalizing payroll, as this creates a risk of absences incorrectly carrying over into the subsequent payroll period. The document explains that the warning serves as a reminder to close out the payroll period immediately after completing the Confirm Timesheets step rather than leaving it open overnight. To resolve issues that may arise from this situation, the document outlines a specific corrective procedure within Portal: users must first click Manage Payroll and highlight the relevant pay group, then navigate to Process Payroll where they can locate the corresponding payroll entry and click the three-dot menu icon beside it. From this menu, users select the Reverse Timesheets option to undo the timesheet confirmation and prevent absences from being incorrectly carried forward. This document is primarily intended for payroll administrators and users responsible for managing timesheets and payroll cycles in the Access Group WFM (Workforce Management) system who need to understand the implications of their processing workflow and how to correct situations where the Confirm Timesheets process was left running overnight.

t: Error: 'Pay Group not available for Supplementary Mode as records exist on Pay History for next payroll period'

sl: This document explains the warning message that appears when users attempt to enable the Supplementary Run toggle in the Access Group payroll system but encounter an error indicating that the pay group is unavailable for supplementary mode because pay history records already exist for the next payroll period. The document describes a preventative feature designed to help users execute supplementary payroll runs while avoiding complications that stem from existing pay history data. To prevent this warning from appearing, users must initiate the supplementary payroll run before performing any manual payment entries in the current payroll period and before executing the Payroll Update job for that same period. The document emphasizes a critical limitation: once pay history has been created for the next period, the warning cannot be removed and the supplementary payroll run cannot be enabled, making the timing of these operations essential. The document is intended for payroll administrators and finance professionals who work within the Access Group payroll system and need to understand the sequencing requirements for supplementary payroll processing. Related resources are provided to address other supplementary payroll-related issues, including problems with payslip release timing and submission file generation requirements for previous payroll periods.

t: Error: 'LGPS Data has not created'
s:

There is duplicate data in the tiered rates of the pension scheme.

An adjustment to an employee's pension contributions was made using the Adjust Normal...
ss: The "LGPS Data has not created" error occurs when generating Local Government Pension Scheme reports and stems from two main configuration issues: duplicate entries in pension scheme tiered rates, or mismatched pay codes between main pension contributions and adjustments made via the Adjust Normal Amount feature. Open this document when you encounter an ORA-01427 error during LGPS report generation and need step-by-step guidance to identify the affected pension scheme and resolve the duplicate data or pay code conflict. The guide walks you through checking employee pension schemes, deleting duplicate rate entries, and ensuring adjustment pay codes differ from main contribution pay codes in your Portal settings.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving the "LGPS Data has not created" error that occurs when generating Local Government Pension Scheme reports in the Portal system. The document identifies two primary causes of this error: duplicate data entries in the tiered rates of the pension scheme (such as multiple entries with identical effective dates and threshold amounts), and incorrect pay code configuration when using the Adjust Normal Amount feature for pension contribution adjustments. To resolve duplicate rate issues, users must navigate to Settings > Codes > Pension Scheme, select the relevant pension code, access the Rates section under Banded Scheme Type, and delete the duplicate line using the three-dot icon. For pay code configuration problems, users must ensure that the pre-tax adjustment pay code used in the Adjust Normal Amount feature differs from the deduction pay codes (Deduction 1, Deduction 2, and Deduction 3) used for main pension contributions, updating both Employee Pay Codes and Employer Pay Codes sections if necessary. The document emphasizes testing any configuration changes in the UAT environment before applying them to the Live system and advises users to contact support if employee deductions have already closed for the affected period, providing specific details such as payroll period, pension scheme, pay codes, and affected thresholds. This resource is intended for payroll administrators and pension scheme managers who encounter errors when running LGPS reports and need to identify and correct underlying configuration issues.

t: Check correct PRSI rates in payroll processing
s:
To apply the correct PRSI rates when a pay group’s week end date differs from its payment date during a rate change, you may need to make manual adjustments.

 

The PRSI rates for a payroll period are determined based on PRSI rates effective as of the transaction date or the week end date for the p...
ss: Payroll systems determine PRSI rates based on week end dates or transaction dates, but Irish revenue regulations require rates to match the actual payment date. When a pay group's week end date differs from its payment date—such as a September 30 week end with an October 1 payment date—you must manually adjust the PRSI Date Effective field in either Portal or CorePay Back Office to ensure correct rates are applied. Open this document when you need to reconcile misaligned payment and week end dates during PRSI rate changes, or when your payroll processing shows incorrect PRSI deductions. The steps walk you through updating the PRSI Date Effective field in your chosen system so the correct rates are used for that pay period.
sl: This document explains how to apply correct PRSI (Pay Related Social Insurance) rates in payroll processing when a pay group's week end date differs from its payment date, which commonly occurs during rate changes. The system determines PRSI rates based on either the transaction date or the week end date defined in the company payroll calendar, with transaction dates calculated differently depending on payroll frequency (monthly payrolls use the last day of the month, while weekly, fortnightly, or 4-weekly payrolls use the week end date plus or minus any offset days). However, revenue regulations require that PRSI rates match those effective on the actual payment date, necessitating manual adjustments when these dates do not align. The document provides a concrete example where a pay group's week end date of September 30, 2025 conflicts with a payment date of October 1, 2025, requiring correction. It then describes two parallel step-by-step procedures for making these adjustments: one for Portal users (navigating Settings > Codes > PayGroups and entering the date in the PRSI Date Effective field) and one for Back Office users (navigating CorePay > Reference > Pay Groups and performing the same field update). Once the PRSI Date Effective field is populated with the correct date, the system recalibrates the transaction date to ensure proper rates are applied, and automatically clears this field after the complete pay group update runs. This guidance is essential for payroll administrators and accountants who process regular payrolls and must ensure compliance with revenue regulations regarding PRSI rate applications.

t: Back Office: Final Run indicator
s:
The Final Run Indicator is a safety mechanism within the Pay module to ensure that once it has been ticked on, any changes to an employee's record cannot be made that will interfere with that pay groups next pay run.
​
You can run Generate Salaries & Allowances as many times as needed to carry out t...
ss: The Final Run Indicator is a safety feature in the Pay module that locks employee records once activated, preventing changes that could disrupt the next pay run. You can run Generate Salaries & Allowances multiple times for initial checks, but you must enable the Final Run Indicator before the system will allow you to confirm timesheets. Access this indicator in Back Office by navigating to CorePay > Input > Generate Salaries and Allowances (PAY290 job). Enable this when you're ready to finalize payroll processing and prevent accidental modifications to employee data.
sl: This document explains the Final Run Indicator, a safety feature within the Pay module of the system that prevents modifications to employee records once activated, ensuring no changes interfere with the pay group's next scheduled pay run. The Final Run Indicator is accessed through the Generate Salaries and Allowances job (PAY290), which can be run multiple times during initial payroll checks on employees without restriction. However, the system will not permit timesheet confirmation until the Final Run Indicator has been explicitly turned on, making it a critical control point in the payroll process. To locate and view the Final Run Indicator in Back Office, users must navigate through CorePay, then Input, and select Generate Salaries and Allowances, where the indicator becomes visible on the subsequent screen. The document notes that Portal users should refer to separate Portal-specific instructions for accessing the same functionality. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and HR professionals who need to understand when and how to activate the Final Run Indicator to lock down payroll data before processing pay runs, and it also references related issues such as allowances not generating, negative pay errors, unpaid leave calculation problems, and PRSI week generation issues that may accompany Final Run Indicator management.

t: Error: 'Update not yet completed'
s:
If you see the above error message when running the Generate Salaries and Allowances (PAY290) job, this occurs because the system has already run the Confirm Timesheets task.

 

The Confirm Timesheets task closes timesheet inputs for the current payroll period, preventing any additional timesheet e...
ss: When running the Generate Salaries and Allowances (PAY290) job in your payroll system, you may encounter an "Update not yet completed" error if the Confirm Timesheets task has already been executed for the current payroll period. This error occurs because Confirm Timesheets locks timesheet inputs, preventing you from re-running the salary generation without first reversing the timesheet confirmation. Open this article if you need to reverse the timesheet confirmation step and re-run your payroll jobs in either Portal or CorePay, depending on which system you use.
sl: This document addresses the "Update not yet completed" error that occurs when attempting to run the Generate Salaries and Allowances (PAY290) job in a payroll system, explaining that this error happens because the Confirm Timesheets task has already been executed for the current payroll period. The Confirm Timesheets task functions to close timesheet inputs, which prevents users from entering additional timesheet data, and once this task is run, the Generate Salaries and Allowances job cannot be re-executed without first reversing the timesheet confirmation step. The document provides two separate procedural paths depending on which interface the user accesses: the Portal route, which involves navigating to Manage Payroll, selecting the relevant pay group, clicking Process Payroll, locating the payroll validation job, and then clicking the three-dot icon to access the Reverse Timesheets option; and the Back Office route, which requires accessing CorePay, selecting Input, choosing Reverse Timesheet Confirm, entering the pay group in the designated field, and verifying the period fields before proceeding. The document includes a helpful tip noting that the pay group will automatically return to the last step of Salaries & Allowances after the reverse operation completes. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and finance professionals who need to troubleshoot and correct payroll processing errors when timesheet confirmations have prevented salary generation, and it references the broader Processing Payroll user guide for additional context on payroll jobs and related tasks.

t: The stat pre year end clear down report values are incorrect

t: Error: 'ERRMESS :ORA-01422: exact fetch returns more than requested number of rows'
s:

ss: The PAY140 payroll job fails with an ORA-01422 error when employees have multiple PRSI classes assigned, typically caused by issuing a manual payment without first canceling the original payment using a different PRSI class. This issue occurs in the payroll system when manual payments are processed for previous periods without properly clearing the prior payment records. Open this article if your PAY140 job is stuck and you need to understand why multiple PRSI classes are causing the error and how to prevent it going forward. The solution involves always processing a cancel payment before issuing any manual payment to ensure PRSI class consistency.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses the Oracle database error "ORA-01422: exact fetch returns more than requested number of rows" as it manifests in the payroll system. The error specifically occurs when the PAY140 job becomes stuck because employee records in the trace file contain multiple PRSI classes. The root cause is a procedural error where a manual payment was issued for a previous period without first canceling the original payment, and the manual payment used a different PRSI class than the original payment, creating duplicate PRSI class entries. To prevent this issue from recurring, users must process a cancel payment before processing any manual payment in the payroll workflow. To resolve an existing occurrence of this error, users should raise a new support case online through the Access Group Help Centre and reference this article title, providing specific details including the affected payroll period and pay group. The document also references related articles covering similar payroll errors such as negative pay issues after pre-tax deductions and other Oracle database errors, indicating this is part of a broader knowledge base for payroll processing troubleshooting.

sl: This document provides guidance for resolving disputes or discrepancies between an employee's PAYE and National Insurance calculations in the payroll system. t: Back Office: Load digital certificates for Enhanced Reporting Requirements
s:
Individuals, companies, agents and other entities need the ROS Digital Certificate to access online services for business taxes. 

 

Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) is an additional permission under the employer ROS certificate. Revenue is automatically applying these ERR permissions to the e...
ss: Loading digital certificates in PeopleXD Payroll and PeopleXD Expense enables your system to submit Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) filings to Revenue. The ERR certificate must be retrieved after mid-December 2023, as older certificates lack the necessary permissions for ERR submissions. Open this document if you need step-by-step instructions to upload your ROS digital certificate through CorePay, including how to handle dual databases and enter the certificate password. sl: This document provides instructions for loading ROS Digital Certificates in back office systems to enable Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) submissions for business tax services. ERR is an additional permission layer built on employer ROS certificates that Revenue automatically applies to primary certificates, though it must be manually assigned to sub-certificates through the ROS permissions screen. The document addresses a critical compatibility requirement: certificates must have been retrieved after mid-December 2023 when Revenue amended certificate permissions, as older certificates cannot process ERR submissions. Users of both PeopleXD Payroll and PeopleXD Expense need to follow different upload procedures depending on their system configuration—uploading the ERR digital certificate to both applications if they use separate databases, or only to PeopleXD Payroll if they share a single database. The upload process involves navigating to CorePay > Update > Paye Modernisation > Load Digital Certificate, selecting the company reference from a drop-down menu, entering the certificate password provided by Revenue, browsing to select the certificate file, and clicking Load Certificate to receive confirmation. This document serves back office administrators and payroll professionals who manage tax compliance and reporting integrations across Access Group systems, and it functions as part of a larger configuration workflow that requires additional parameter setup after certificate loading is complete.

s:

Open this document if your payroll includes employees with multiple pension schemes and you need to identify whether pension contributions are calculating correctly or require manual adjustment. The guide provides steps to review gross to nett validation reports, identify affected employees, and either manually correct deductions before closing payroll or wait for the system patch to be applied. Use this resource if you're closing payroll before the fix is deployed on 19 January 2026, or if you need to verify pension calculations are working properly after the patch is applied.
sl: This document describes a pension deduction bug in payroll processing that occurs when employees have multiple pension records active in the same payroll period, including scenarios with two or more active pensions, one active and one ended pension still calculating, or multiple ended pensions processing retrospectively. The issue was introduced in version 28.0.142 deployed on 14 January 2026 and affects only payrolls processed after this deployment, with a fix being deployed on 19 January 2026 to resolve the problem. The document guides users through identifying impacted employees by reviewing gross to nett validation reports to locate those with multiple pension records in a single payroll period, then checking whether pension deduction values are correct for each scheme and whether ended pensions are calculating when they should not be. For organizations that must close payroll before the patch is deployed, the document outlines manual correction steps: identify affected employees, review their pension deductions, determine correct amounts, record adjustments on each pension scheme for the impacted employee, and rerun payroll validation. t: Set the payroll cutoff date
s:
The payroll cutoff date lets you control the flow of salary, allowance, and pension changes transferring from PeopleXD People Management to PeopleXD Payroll. 

 

When you set a cutoff date for a pay group, any changes entered in PeopleXD People Management after that date are automatically staged. Y...
ss: Setting a payroll cutoff date in PeopleXD controls when salary, allowance, and pension changes from People Management automatically stage before transferring to Payroll. When you set a cutoff date for a pay group, any changes entered after that date are held for review, letting you decide which ones to process in the current payroll period. Use this feature to prevent accidental changes from flowing through to payroll mid-period while still allowing HR administrators to make updates (which get staged for approval). Open this document when you need to establish or view a cutoff date for a specific pay group, or when you want to understand how staged changes work in your payroll process.
sl: This document explains how to set and manage the payroll cutoff date feature in PeopleXD, which controls the flow of salary, allowance, and pension changes from PeopleXD People Management to PeopleXD Payroll. The payroll cutoff date automatically stages any changes entered in PeopleXD People Management after the specified date, allowing HR administrators to review and decide which changes to process in the current payroll period, though it does not prevent administrators from entering changes. To set the cutoff date, users navigate to the Manage Payroll screen, select a relevant pay group via the three-dot menu, click Payroll Cutoff, enter or select a date using the calendar icon, and click OK to receive a confirmation message. The document includes an important warning that once the payroll cutoff date is on or before the current calendar date, no changes can be made or the date removed, and clarifies that the cutoff applies to the input date of changes rather than their effective date. Users can view the current payroll cutoff date in the Cutoff Date column on the Manage Payroll screen, and the system automatically removes the cutoff date once the current payroll period closes and all payroll tasks are complete. To access the payroll cutoff date functionality, users must have specific menu options assigned to their profile, including INPUTS - STAGED CHANGES in CorePortal Pay, or alternatively can be assigned the preconfigured CUTOFF_USER menu profile that includes all required options.

t: EPS Apprenticeship Levy figures looks incorrect
s:
The apprenticeship levy is an amount calculated at a rate of 0.5% of an employer’s annual NIable pay bill. As an employer, you need to report the apprenticeship levy through the EPS. 

 

PeopleXD automatically calculates the year to date apprenticeship levy owed and reports this on the monthly EPS....
ss: The apprenticeship levy is a 0.5% tax on annual NIable pay that PeopleXD calculates and reports monthly through the EPS, but figures can appear incorrect for several common reasons. This document explains why apprenticeship levy amounts might look wrong in PeopleXD—such as missing company allowance adjustments, discrepancies between EPS and observation reports, or year-to-date calculations that don't match individual months. Open this if your EPS apprenticeship levy figures seem inaccurate or don't match your payroll records, and you need step-by-step guidance to verify settings and understand calculation differences.
sl: This document helps users understand why apprenticeship levy figures in PeopleXD may appear incorrect when reported through the EPS (Employer Payment Summary), a mandatory monthly reporting requirement for the levy calculated at 0.5% of an employer's annual National Insurance-able pay bill. The document addresses multiple specific scenarios causing discrepancies, including the company allowance of £15,000 annually (£1,250 monthly relief), which users can verify by navigating to Settings > UK Tax Rates > General > Other, selecting Apprenticeship Levy from the Select Detail dropdown, Company Parameters from the Select dropdown, the relevant year, and checking the Apprentice Levy Threshold column for the company. A key issue resolved is the difference between observation report figures and EPS figures, which occurs because the EPS calculates at company level while observation reports work at individual employee level—users can verify accuracy by calculating the levy percentage from year-to-date National Insurance-able pay. The document also explains that the EPS screen displays year-to-date cumulative data only (not individual monthly figures) and may include early-processed weekly payrolls from the following month, preventing accurate reporting of previously missed months. Additionally, the document clarifies that FPS (Full Payment Summary) excludes National Insurance-able pay below the Lower Earnings Limit, while the EPS reports total company National Insurance-able pay regardless of this threshold. This resource is essential for payroll administrators, HR professionals, and finance teams who process payroll in PeopleXD and need to troubleshoot and validate apprenticeship levy reporting accuracy for HMRC compliance.

t: Remove old RTI FPS files
s:
RTI FPI files are files that transmit the details of employee payments and deductions to HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) every time you process payroll. 

 

By submitting FPS files in real-time, you ensure accurate reporting of payroll information, including tax, National Insurance, and other deducti...
ss: RTI FPS files transmit employee payment and deduction details to HMRC during payroll processing, ensuring accurate real-time reporting of tax, National Insurance, and other statutory deductions. Old or unwanted FPS files can clutter the RTI Generate/Transfer File screen, and this document explains how to safely remove them without affecting other system areas. For current payroll periods, you can regenerate files in test mode to overwrite unwanted submissions before transfer to HMRC. For previous periods with duplicate FPS files, you'll need to contact Access Group support engineers to have duplicates marked as accepted and removed from the system.
sl: This document provides instructions for removing outdated RTI FPS (Full Payment Submission) files from the RTI Generate/Transfer File screen, which are used to transmit employee payment and deduction details to HMRC in real-time to ensure accurate payroll reporting and regulatory compliance. The document addresses two distinct scenarios: removing files from the current closed payroll period, and handling duplicate files from previous periods. For current period files that have not been transferred, users can generate a replacement file in test mode by navigating to Manage Payroll, selecting the relevant pay group, clicking Output then RTI, selecting FPS as the File Type, choosing Test mode, and clicking Generate, which overwrites the unwanted file. After generating the test file, users must transfer it to HMRC by highlighting the file with "Generated" status and clicking Transfer, then confirm the transfer by locating the file with "HMRC Accepted" status and enabling the Confirmed toggle. For duplicate FPS files from previous periods, users cannot delete them directly; instead, they must raise a support case with the Access Group support engineers, providing the pay group, payroll period, and the original HMRC response confirming the submitted and accepted file. This document is essential for payroll administrators and finance professionals who need to manage RTI file submissions and maintain clean records on the system while avoiding the serious consequence of submitting duplicate files to HMRC, which cannot be reversed or recalled once submitted.

t: RTI - No FPS reports or files generating to the reports centres

ss: FPS and EPS file generation is essential for submitting payroll information to HMRC, but files may fail to appear in the reports centre due to data issues or file conflicts. Common causes include special characters in employee addresses that prevent proper file conversion, old XML files blocking the generation process, or duplicate RTI numbers in the system. This document provides troubleshooting steps to resolve these issues, such as checking and editing employee address details, or guidance on when to escalate to support for investigation. Open this if FPS control reports, exceptions reports, or XML/CSV files aren't generating or appearing in your reports centre.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving issues when FPS (Full Payment Submission) or EPS (Employer Payment Summary) reports and files fail to generate or appear in the reports centre, which is critical for submitting payroll information to HMRC. The document identifies three primary causes of generation failures: special characters in employee address data that cannot be properly converted to the database character set, old XML files remaining in the background that block the generation process, and duplicate RTI (Real Time Information) numbers assigned to employees. For the special character issue, users navigate through the portal's People management dashboard to locate the affected employee, access their Contact Information via the ACTIONS menu, select Personnel Profile, and then use the three-dot icon to edit and save the address details before regenerating the FPS file. When an old XML file is blocking generation or when duplicate RTI numbers are detected, the document directs users to raise a new support case online and provide specific information including the relevant pay group code, payroll period, and the old XML file itself. t: Set up Director's NI
s:
Director National Insurance (NI) refers to the specific National Insurance contributions applicable to company directors in the UK. These contributions differ from those for regular employees due to the unique earning patterns of directors. 

 

To ensure compliance with tax regulations and maintain...
ss: Director National Insurance (NI) in the UK applies different contribution rates to company directors than regular employees, and must be properly configured in your payroll system to maintain tax compliance. This document walks you through activating the Director indicator in Portal by accessing an employee's Sundry Profile and Work Details to toggle on the Director setting. The system automatically calculates Director NI using either the standard method (based on cumulative annualized earnings) or an alternative method (based on pay for that period). Open this guide when you need to set up or modify Director NI for qualifying employees, ideally at the start of the tax year to avoid mid-year recalculations and potential compliance issues.
sl: This document explains how to configure Director National Insurance (NI) in the Access Group payroll system for UK company directors whose contributions differ from regular employees due to unique earning patterns. The guide describes a straightforward activation process requiring users to navigate through Portal by clicking Employee, searching for the relevant employee, clicking View to access the Sundry Profile, then clicking Work Details to turn on the Director toggle. Most Director NI calculations are handled automatically by the system once this indicator is activated, though users can request an alternative calculation method based on pay for that period by raising a support case. The document clarifies that the standard method calculates NI on year-to-date cumulative earnings on an annualised basis, while the alternative method calculates on pay for that specific period, in accordance with HMRC guidance. Proper configuration is essential to prevent underpayment or overpayment of National Insurance and to maintain compliance with tax regulations, protecting both employers and directors from future liabilities. The guide strongly recommends applying Director NI changes at the beginning of the tax year in April rather than mid-year, as mid-year changes require support to run a script to ensure correct calculations for both employee and employer NI, and users must provide specific information including employee reference, description of change, effective period, and expected versus actual calculations if errors occur. This document is intended for payroll administrators and HR professionals responsible for configuring employee records in the Access Group system to ensure accurate director compensation processing.

t: Uplift employee tax codes
s:

ss: Bulk update employee tax codes in your payroll system to apply correct tax rates across multiple employees at once. Use the Tax Code Employee Uplift feature under Year End > Manage to select which employees to update (all, Scottish, Welsh, or English only) and set the effective date. sl: This document explains how to uplift employee tax codes in bulk within a payroll system, enabling payroll administrators to update tax codes for multiple employees at once rather than individually. Before performing a bulk tax code uplift, users must first review whether to include dormant employees by navigating to Settings > System Configuration > General and toggling the Dormant Employee on Tax Certs option on or off, then saving the changes. Users can then select which employees to update using specific codes: A for all employees, S for Scottish employees only, C for Welsh employees only, or E for English employees only, and must enter an adjustment value and effective date before confirming with OK. A critical note highlighted in the document is that this uplift process must be completed before loading any new tax certificates from HMRC to avoid conflicts or errors. The document is designed for payroll and human resources personnel responsible for managing employee tax administration and ensuring compliance with changing tax regulations across different regions within the United Kingdom.

t: Create and transfer RTI Files
s: Creating and transferring Real Time Information (RTI) files is a crucial process for employers in the UK, ensuring that payroll information is reported accurately and promptly to HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC). sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on creating and transferring Real Time Information (RTI) files to HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC), a mandatory process for UK employers to report payroll information including employee earnings, tax deductions, and National Insurance contributions with each payroll run. t: Error: '7844: The PeriodEnd within the IRheader must be within the same tax year'
s: If the FPS file displays the following error, it indicates an incorrect value for the offset days. The offset days adjust the weekend date on the calendar for a pay group. For instance, when paying a week in arrears, the offset days might be set to -7, which can create issues when processing the fir...
ss: When submitting FPS (Full Payment Submission) files at the start of a new tax year, you may encounter an error related to the PeriodEnd date in the IR header falling outside the current tax year. This typically occurs due to incorrect offset days settings in your pay group configuration, which can cause issues when processing the first FPS submission with week-in-arrears pay arrangements. Open this document if you need to correct offset day values in your pay group settings or adjust calendar week end dates in Portal to ensure RTI compliance. The steps provided walk you through updating these settings in Portal and temporarily adjusting dates during the first week of the new tax year before reverting them to their original values.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses error 7844, which occurs when the PeriodEnd value in the IRheader of an FPS (Full Payment Submission) file falls outside the current tax year, typically caused by incorrect offset days settings. The error commonly arises during first FPS processing of a new tax year when offset days (which adjust weekend dates on the pay calendar) are set to values like -7 instead of -1, creating date misalignment issues. The document provides two separate correction procedures: first, users must navigate to Portal Settings > Codes > Pay Groups, select the relevant pay group, and update the Offset Days field to -1 before saving; second, for RTI (Real Time Information) compliance, users must access Portal Settings > Company Parameters > Calendars, select the company, and temporarily adjust the Week End Date field to align with the new tax year before generating and transferring the FPS. The temporary calendar date adjustment must be performed only once during the first week of the new tax year, and once the FPS file is successfully transferred and accepted by HMRC, the Week End Date must be reverted to its original value. This document is used by payroll administrators and finance teams who process monthly or weekly FPS submissions and need to ensure their systems remain compliant with HMRC's RTI requirements when transitioning between tax years.

ss: When generating a previous year FPS file in your payroll system, the file may show no data if you haven't completed the year-end cleardown and moved into the new tax year first. You must run the previous year's FPS job only after you've processed any cancellations or manual payments and transitioned to the following tax year, otherwise the system won't recognize the data. Open this article if you're encountering a blank previous year FPS file after attempting to generate it. Contact support to run a system update if you've followed the correct sequence and still see no data.
sl: This document explains a specific data issue that occurs when generating the previous year's Full Payment Submission (FPS) file within the Access Group payroll system, where the file displays no data despite the user expecting information to be present. The problem arises when users attempt to cancel or process manual payments and then generate the previous year's FPS without properly sequencing their tax year activities, as the system requires the year-end cleardown process to be completed and a move into the new tax year before the previous year's FPS job can be run successfully. The document provides a concrete example illustrating that if a user cancels and processes a manual payment in tax year 2021, they must first run the year-end cleardown procedure and transition into tax year 2022 before attempting to process the previous year's FPS job, otherwise the system will fail to recognize the data. When this issue occurs, resolution requires contacting Support to run a system update on the user's account, with the recommendation that users raise a new case online and reference the article title when submitting their request. The document is intended for payroll administrators or finance professionals who manage year-end payroll processes, tax year transitions, and FPS submissions within the Access Group platform, particularly those who need to handle corrections or adjustments during the year-end closing period.

sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses a validation error that occurs when EPS (Employer Payment Summary) response files are processed through the Reports Centre, specifically the "Invalid content found at element 'AccountHoldersName'" error. The issue stems from the company name field being either too long to pass HMRC's validation requirements or containing characters that HMRC's system does not accept. The document provides a step-by-step resolution process that involves navigating to the Settings menu, selecting Organisations from the submenu, and then locating the specific company through a Code dropdown list. Users must then access the Payroll Parameters option from the Select Details dropdown menu and review the Username field located within the Banking Details section, as this field is the source of the problematic company name data. The document is designed for payroll administrators or compliance personnel who encounter this error when submitting employer payment information to HMRC and need to correct the account holder name configuration. After reviewing and correcting the username field to ensure it meets HMRC's character and length requirements, users must click Save to apply the changes before resubmitting the EPS file.

t: Error: 'The Entry In Tax Month Of 7 Is Only Valid If The Submission Is Made Between 6 September And 19 November Inclusive Of The 2023 Tax Year. Please Check.'
s:
If you try to transfer the EPS file and encounter an error, it means your submission is late.

⚠️Important: There are no workarounds for late submissions of EPS files.

To resolve this issue, you should proceed with submitting for the next period. This will ensure that all cumulative Year-To-Date va...
ss: EPS file submissions to HMRC are subject to strict deadline windows—for tax month 7, submissions must occur between 6 September and 19 November of the tax year. If you receive an error when attempting to transfer your EPS file, it indicates your submission has missed the required deadline, and there are no workarounds available for late submissions. Open this document if you're experiencing submission errors or need to understand the specific cut-off dates for EPS filings and how to proceed with correcting missed deadline submissions.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses a specific timing error that occurs when attempting to transfer an EPS (Employer Payment Summary) file outside the permitted submission window for a given tax month. The error message indicates that submissions for tax month 7 are only valid if made between 6 September and 19 November inclusive of the 2023 tax year, and the document explains that encountering this error during file transfer means the submission has been made after the deadline. The document clarifies that there are no workarounds or alternative solutions available for late EPS file submissions, establishing a hard deadline policy. To resolve the issue, users are instructed to abandon the current submission attempt and instead proceed with submitting the EPS file for the next available period, which will ensure that all cumulative Year-To-Date values are accurately reported to HMRC (Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs). The document also references a related requirement to ensure that Apprentice Levy liability for the selected tax month has been paid to HMRC via Third Party Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) before generating the EPS file. This guidance is primarily intended for payroll administrators and HR professionals who manage PAYE submissions and must meet strict HMRC filing deadlines.

ss: When submitting an FPS file to HMRC, you may receive a rejection error stating "Invalid content found at element 'CO2'" or "Invalid value ''", which occurs because vehicle CO2 emissions data is missing or improperly configured in the system. Open this document when your HMRC FPS submission is rejected due to CO2 emissions errors or when you need step-by-step instructions for updating vehicle emission data in the payroll system.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses a specific validation error encountered when submitting FPS (Full Payment Submission) files to HMRC, where the system rejects the submission with an "Invalid content found at element 'CO2'" or "Invalid value ''" error message. To resolve the issue, users must navigate through Portal's Administrator Dashboard, access the Car Administration Centre, search for the relevant employee record, and locate the p11D/P46 Details section where the CO2 Emissions field is found. The document provides a specific workaround for cases where CO2 emissions are currently set to zero: users should temporarily change the value to any other number, save the changes, and then revert it back to zero before saving again. Once the CO2 emissions field has been updated through this process, users must regenerate the FPS file and resubmit it to HMRC to complete the submission successfully. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and HR personnel who manage vehicle-related tax reporting and P11D submissions within Access Group's payroll system.

sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre provides guidance on resolving a specific validation error that occurs when submitting an FPS (Full Payment Submission) file, where an employee record has an annual pension amount entered but lacks a completed occupational pension indicator. sl: This HMRC notice document explains why an employment allowance claim may have been rejected and provides step-by-step instructions to resolve the issue within the payroll portal. t: Pay codes included in Council Tax court order nett calculation
s:
When a Council Tax court order is applied to an employee, the nett calculation determines the portion of their pay subject to the deduction. If specific pay codes are not explicitly excluded from this calculation, they are included by default, which can result in inaccurate deduction amounts. 

 

C...
ss: Council Tax court orders in PeopleXD use a nett calculation to determine how much of an employee's pay is subject to deduction, and pay codes are included in this calculation by default unless explicitly excluded. Configuring pay code exclusions ensures only the correct earnings are considered, preventing over- or under-deductions that could affect employee net pay and create payroll compliance issues. Open this document when you need to exclude specific pay codes from Council Tax deduction calculations before running payroll for employees with active court orders. Follow the steps to access Pay Codes settings, select the code to exclude, and apply the "Excluded for Council Tax" rule.
sl: This document explains how to configure pay code exclusions for Council Tax court order calculations within a payroll system, specifically addressing the challenge that pay codes are included in nett calculations by default unless explicitly excluded. The document describes a specific step-by-step process accessed through Settings > Codes > Pay Codes, where users search for and select a pay code, click the three-dot menu icon to edit it, navigate to the Rules page, and add a new rule by selecting "Excluded for Council Tax" from the Rules dropdown menu. The configuration requires enabling a toggle switch and saving the changes through the subsequent screens. This process is critical because failing to exclude specific pay codes from the Council Tax court order nett calculation can result in over-deductions or under-deductions from employee pay, creating both financial inaccuracy and payroll compliance issues. The document is intended for payroll administrators and managers who need to apply these exclusions before processing any payroll run where both the relevant pay codes and active court orders are present. Related functionality mentioned includes setting up DEA pay codes, configuring Scottish arrestment order rates, and general pay code editing procedures, indicating this is part of a broader payroll deduction management system.

t: Pay date on the online payslip is incorrect
s:
If the pay date on an online payslip appears as the day before the actual payment date, it can be due to the following reasons below. 

 

Below, we outline two possible causes as to why the online payslip shows a pay date earlier than the actual payment date and how to update the pay date for the c...
ss: Online payslips may display a pay date that is one day earlier than the actual payment date, typically due to SEPA processing date requirements and ESS offset settings in your pay group configuration. This guide covers how to correct the discrepancy by adjusting the ESS offset value to 0 in either the Portal or CorePay Back Office settings. Open this document if you notice mismatched dates on employee payslips or need to understand why the pay date shown differs from when payments are actually processed. For payslips in closed periods, you'll need to contact support to have database scripts run to correct the dates retroactively.
sl: This document provides guidance on resolving a common issue where the pay date displayed on online payslips appears one day earlier than the actual payment date. The document outlines two distinct causes for this discrepancy: first, a SEPA requirement that changed how processing dates are handled in bank files, which previously required adding an extra day to payslip dates; and second, instances where incorrect payment dates were entered during the complete update job in the payroll system. To resolve the SEPA-related issue, users can adjust the ESS offset setting in their pay group configuration through either the Portal (Settings > Pay Groups > selecting the pay group code > Next Page > ESS offset checkbox) or the Back Office system (CorePay > Reference > Pay Group on the third page > ESS offset checkbox), changing the value from its default setting to 0 to prevent date adjustments. The document explains that if the ESS Date Paid Offset field is left blank, the system defaults to adding one day to the paypath processing date, and any changes made must occur before running the complete update job to take effect. For payslips in closed periods where the pay date has already been incorrectly recorded, users must contact support through the Access Digital Assistant with details of the affected pay groups and payroll periods, as support will need to run database scripts to correct historical data. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and HR professionals who manage payroll systems and need to ensure accurate payment date information is displayed to employees on their online payslips.

t: Error: 'Unapproved Rejoiner has timesheets this period which will not be paid
s:

ss: When running observation or gross to net reports in People Management, an "Unapproved Rejoiner" error prevents an employee's timesheets from being paid during the current period. This occurs when a rejoining employee hasn't been properly processed through the portal's approval workflow. Open this document if you need to resolve unpaid timesheet issues for rejoined employees by checking the Awaiting Approval screen, verifying rejoin dates, and ensuring all salary approvals are processed in the Salary Approvals section.
sl: This document provides guidance for resolving an error that occurs when running observation reports or gross to net observation reports in the payroll system, which prevents an unapproved rejoiner employee from being paid despite having submitted timesheets for the period. The document describes a two-part troubleshooting process within the portal system to identify and correct the underlying People Management configuration issue. The first step involves navigating to Manage Payroll, selecting the relevant pay group, accessing the Inputs tab, then clicking Approvals and Rejoiners to locate the employee and click Join, after which the user must review details and save the changes. If this does not resolve the issue, users must then check the Salary Approvals screen by accessing People Management from the dashboard menu, selecting Command Centre, and clicking Salary Approvals to verify that all pending salaries are either approved or rejected, as any outstanding salaries will prevent processing. The document also clarifies that the rejoin date must fall within the current period or a prior period, and that employees with rejoin dates in future periods will not appear in the Payroll Dashboard until their designated rejoin period is reached. This guidance is intended for payroll administrators or HR personnel using the Access Group portal who encounter payment processing failures for rejoining employees with active timesheets.

t: Error: 'No Payslips from your current pay group for the period being viewed. No payslip history to display'
s:

We’ve compiled a list of possible causes for the error message and how to resolve them.

 

 

Cause 1: Print payslip indicator 

The employee's Print Payslip indicator is enabled, allowing...
ss: When employees receive the error "No Payslips from your current pay group for the period being viewed," this troubleshooting guide helps diagnose and fix the issue in CorePay and the employee self-service portal. The document covers seven common causes, including incorrect Print Payslip settings, portal display issues, disabled View ESS Payslip indicators at the pay group level, mismatched employee numbers, and pay group supplementary run mode. Open this guide when an employee cannot access or view their payslips online, and follow the step-by-step instructions for both Portal and Back Office to resolve the problem.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre provides comprehensive troubleshooting guidance for employees who encounter the error message "No Payslips from your current pay group for the period being viewed. No payslip history to display" when attempting to access their payslips. The document identifies seven distinct causes and their corresponding resolutions, each with step-by-step instructions for both Portal and Back Office environments within the CorePay system. The first cause addresses the Print Payslip indicator, which when enabled prevents online viewing; users must navigate to Employee > Tax Details in the Portal or CorePay > Employee > View Employee Details in the Back Office to disable this toggle. The second cause relates to portal settings where the "My Pay History" section may be minimized, requiring users to click a white arrow to expand the portlet. The third cause involves enabling the View ESS Payslip indicator at the pay group level through Settings > Pay Group (Classic) in the Portal or CorePay > Reference > Pay Groups in the Back Office. Additional causes include incorrect employee number registration preventing synchronization with CorePay, pay groups operating in supplementary run mode which blocks period synchronization, specific pay methods like "FP" in older system versions requiring support intervention, and insufficient widget space when multiple widgets are expanded simultaneously. This document is typically used by payroll administrators, HR personnel, and employee support teams who assist employees experiencing payslip visibility issues within the Access Group portal and back office systems.

t: Employee's home address not appearing on payslips

ss: The payroll system requires employee home addresses to be designated as "Default" in the Address Type field within People Management to display correctly on payslips. This issue typically occurs when address details aren't properly linked or when the default setting hasn't been configured. Open this document if you need to troubleshoot missing address information on employee payslips or need step-by-step instructions for updating address settings in the portal.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre provides guidance for resolving the issue where an employee's home address fails to appear on their payslips due to improper system configuration. The root cause is typically that the Address Type field is not set to "Default" in the portal, which prevents the address from being included in payroll documents. The document outlines a step-by-step process beginning from the dashboard menu where users select "People management," then navigate to the employee list by clicking "Dashboard" and selecting "VIEW" beside the employees section. Users must then search for the specific employee using the Search field, access their record by clicking "VIEW," and navigate to the "Contact Information" section to locate the "My Address Details" area. The critical step involves checking the "Address Type" column to verify it displays "Default," and if not, updating it to "Default Address" as required. After making this configuration change, users must regenerate the payslip for the relevant pay group to ensure the home address now appears correctly. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators, HR personnel, or support staff who manage employee records in the Access Group payroll system and need to troubleshoot missing address information on payslips.

t: Payslips are printing when the Print Payslip Indicator is not ticked
s:
When payslips continue to print for employees despite you having disabled the Print Payslip indicator in both Maintain Employee Details and at Pay Group level, this typically indicates that the Pay Group settings require synchronisation.
