ss: Payslips in CorePay continue printing for employees even when you've disabled the Print Payslip indicator in both Maintain Employee Details and Pay Group settings, which means your Pay Group settings need to be refreshed and synchronised. This happens because the Print Payslip indicator at pay group level requires manual resynchronisation to properly align with employee-level settings. Open this document if payslips are unexpectedly generating despite having turned off the Print Payslip indicator, and follow the steps to toggle the indicator on then off at pay group level and re-run payslip generation. The solution involves accessing CorePay Reference, locating your pay groups, and refreshing the Print Payslip indicator settings across all relevant groups.
sl: This document explains a synchronisation issue in the CorePay system where payslips continue to print for employees even after the Print Payslip indicator has been disabled in both the Maintain Employee Details screen and at Pay Group level. The problem occurs because the Print Payslip indicator at pay group level requires manual refresh to properly synchronise with employee-level settings. To resolve this issue, users must navigate to CorePay > Reference > Pay Groups, locate the relevant pay group in the Pay Group field, navigate to Page 3, and toggle the Print Payslip indicator on and then off before saving, repeating this process for all affected pay groups, then re-run the payslips. The document is primarily intended for back office administrators and payroll managers who manage employee records and pay group configurations in the CorePay system. An important note clarifies that the system will generate payslips regardless of the Print Payslip indicator settings if both pay group and employee parameters are populated during payslip generation, which helps explain why the indicator alone may not prevent payslip output. The document provides a specific step-by-step troubleshooting procedure that requires users to toggle settings to force synchronisation between the employee and pay group levels of the system.

t: Payslips and PDFs not opening
s:
When payslips fail to load across all companies (displaying only a loading circle) and PDF reports do not open in specific browsers, including IE11, Chrome for Mobile, and Safari for mobile, this typically indicates a javaScript library compatibility issue.

 

This issue occurs when the system upgr...
ss: Payslips and PDF reports may fail to load due to JavaScript library compatibility issues, particularly affecting IE11, Chrome Mobile, and Safari Mobile browsers. This typically occurs after system upgrades and prevents payslips from displaying and PDF reports from opening entirely. Open this document if you're experiencing stuck loading screens on payslips or PDFs won't open in your browser. The solution involves clearing your browser cache to ensure the system changes take effect properly.
sl: This document addresses a technical issue affecting payslip and PDF report functionality across the Access Group system, specifically when payslips fail to load and display only a loading circle while PDF reports refuse to open in certain browsers including Internet Explorer 11, Chrome for Mobile, and Safari for mobile. The root cause is identified as a JavaScript library compatibility issue that emerges when the system upgrades its JavaScript libraries, creating barriers to PDF functionality in older browsers like IE11 and incompatibilities with mobile browser versions. The document explains that the system resolved this problem by reverting to the previous version of the JavaScript library on Monday, 13 June 2022, as no alternative fix was available to restore IE11 compatibility at that time. The document is intended for users experiencing cross-company payslip loading failures or PDF opening problems across multiple browsers, whether on desktop or mobile devices. A critical procedural note emphasizes that users must clear their browser cache following the JavaScript library reversion to ensure the system changes take effect properly and restore normal functionality.

t: Configure and upload payslip logo
s:
A payslip logo is a visual representation, often your company's logo, that appears on employee payslips, enhancing brand identity. 

 

Including a logo on payslips not only reinforces your brand but also provides a consistent and recognizable format for employees. 

 

To upload and configure a pay...
ss: Payslip logos are company branding elements that appear on employee payslips in Access Group's payroll system, reinforcing brand identity and providing a consistent format. This document covers the complete process of uploading and configuring a logo across multiple payslip locations—including Back Office Payslips, Portal Payslips, and Portal Login—through the Administrator Dashboard. You'll need to enable the Upload Logo widget in Dashboard Configuration, grant user access via menu profiles, and upload PNG-formatted logos (200 x 100 pixels) with unique names to specific companies and pay groups. Open this guide when you need to add or update your company logo on employee payslips or manage logo visibility across different payslip types and user groups.
sl: This document provides comprehensive instructions for uploading and configuring a company logo to appear on employee payslips within the Access Group payroll system, enhancing brand identity and creating a consistent employee experience. The process involves two main stages: first, enabling the Upload Logo widget through the Administrator Dashboard by navigating to Site Manager, selecting Dashboard Configuration, searching for "Upload Logos/Templates" in the Search Widgets field, and toggling on the widget with a specified position. Second, users must grant access to the upload logo functionality by navigating to the Security Dashboard, selecting Menu Profiles, filtering by CorePortal and CorePortal Pay systems, and activating the "Upload of Template/Logo" menu option for relevant user profiles. The Upload Logo widget itself allows users to upload PNG-formatted images (200 x 100 pixels) to multiple payslip locations including Back Office Payslip, Copy Payslip, Portal Login, Quick Jump Toolbar, and Portal Payslip, with each logo requiring a unique name to avoid conflicts with existing logos or templates. The document also requires users to specify the company and pay group for payslip locations, noting that logos without company and pay group assignments will apply to those cases by default. This guide is primarily used by system administrators configuring payroll functionality and by portal administrators managing user access to logo upload features.

t: Portal: P45 retrieve details for manual completion
s:
A P45 is a tax document that an employer issues when an employee leaves their job. It details the employee's pay and tax deductions for the tax year up to the departure date.

ss: Use this document when you need to manually complete a P45 tax form in the portal for an employee who is leaving their job. The P45 records the employee's pay and tax deductions up to their departure date, which they'll need to report income accurately with a new employer or when claiming benefits. The process involves searching for the employee in the portal, accessing their Legislative section, and retrieving Year to Date Cumulatives data to complete the form. Open this guide if you're responsible for issuing P45s and need step-by-step instructions for the portal process, or if you need to troubleshoot access issues to the required screens.
sl: This document provides guidance on retrieving employee information within a portal system to enable manual completion of P45 tax forms, which employers issue when employees leave their employment to document pay and tax deductions up to the departure date. The P45 form is essential for employees to accurately report their income and tax when starting a new job or claiming benefits, as it helps prevent issues related to tax overpayment or underpayment. The document outlines a specific step-by-step process: users must navigate to the Employee section, search for the relevant employee by name, click the VIEW option beside their record, then access the Legislative menu followed by Year to Date Cumulatives to retrieve the necessary cumulative tax and pay information for form completion. The document also directs users to the HMRC website if they need to download blank P45 forms. For users who encounter access restrictions on the Cumulatives screen, the document provides two escalation pathways: contacting a superuser to request access permissions or raising a case online where support staff will guide the superuser through the access grant process. This document is primarily used by HR professionals, payroll administrators, or designated portal users who are responsible for preparing P45 documentation for employees leaving the organization.

t: Incorrect rate of pay on portal payslip
s:
An incorrect pay rate on a portal payslip can result from several factors, which are explained below.

 

The calculation for the hourly rate shown in the details tab of the payslip is as follows: Annual Salary / Days in Year x Pay Period Days / Pay Period Hours (using either full-time equivalent or...
ss: When an employee's portal payslip shows an incorrect hourly rate, this document explains the common causes and how to fix them. The hourly rate is calculated using annual salary, days in the year, pay period days, and pay period hours, and discrepancies often occur when a pay rate change timing doesn't align with the payroll processing cycle or when the wrong print rate is set at the pay code level. Open this guide if you need to troubleshoot rate calculation errors, update print rate settings in your pay codes, or understand why a recent rate change hasn't reflected on an employee's payslip yet.
sl: This document explains how to diagnose and resolve issues where an incorrect pay rate appears on an employee's portal payslip. The hourly rate displayed in the payslip details tab is calculated using the formula: Annual Salary / Days in Year x Pay Period Days / Pay Period Hours, which uses either full-time equivalent or employee standard hours. The document addresses two primary scenarios: when an employee has been moved to a new rate of pay during the current payroll period but their portal payslip still shows the old rate (typically due to timing issues with when the Complete Update job was run), and when an employee has not transitioned to a new rate but multiple rates are displaying for the same pay code. For the latter scenario, users must navigate to Settings > Codes > Pay Codes, search for the relevant pay code, click the three-dot icon to Edit, proceed to Next, and then edit the Print Rate rule to ensure the correct rate is configured. The document advises testing different print rate types in a UAT environment before applying changes to production. This guide is primarily intended for payroll administrators or HR professionals who manage employee pay rates and need to troubleshoot discrepancies between expected and displayed rates on portal payslips.

t: Error: '*** Negative Pay After Processing Pre-Tax Deductions **'
s:
After running the Validation job, some employees may experience negative pay due to pre-tax deductions, resulting in them not receiving any payment. This issue is reflected in the View Gross to Nett exceptions with the above error message.

 

There are several reasons why this may occur. We have co...
ss: Payroll processing in CorePay generates negative pay for some employees after running the Validation job, appearing as exceptions in the View Gross to Nett report. This occurs when pre-tax deductions (like bicycle schemes or AVCs), retrospective employee changes (joiner/leaver status), terminated deductions with retroactive dates, or incorrect P2C tax file data reduce gross pay below zero. Open this document when employees show zero payment or negative pay balances during payroll validation, or when you need to diagnose why specific staff members aren't receiving salary. The guide provides step-by-step instructions to identify the root cause through CorePay timesheet analysis and offers resolution steps for each scenario.
sl: This document addresses a payroll system error where employees receive negative pay after the Validation job (PAY140) processes pre-tax deductions, which is reflected in the View Gross to Nett exceptions report. The guide identifies four primary causes of negative pay scenarios: pre-tax deductions such as bicycle scheme contributions, travel passes, or AVCs reducing gross pay before PAYE is applied; retrospective employee departures where the system claws back salary and allowances; retroactive termination of deductions where the system reclaims previously paid amounts; and incorrectly loaded P2C tax files with zero tax credit and cut-off points that tax all income at higher rates. For each scenario, the document provides diagnostic steps accessible through both the Portal (Employee search, then Timesheets Current Period) and Back Office (CorePay > Enquiry > View Timesheet Details), instructing users to analyze timesheets for negative values, review leave dates, compare pay across periods, and examine the Source and Reference fields to determine whether entries were system-generated (marked with 'PAY' codes like 'PAY290') or user-entered (marked with username). The document explains key configuration indicators including POSHIST (position changes), LEAVER (retrospective departures), JOINER (retrospective hires), and POSRATE (scale rate changes) that flag why negative pay occurs. Resolution steps vary by cause, ranging from reviewing pre-tax deduction totals, to switching employees to week 1 tax basis, to toggling the Allow Negative setting in Pay Group configuration (accessible via Settings > Pay Groups in Portal or CorePay > Reference > Pay Group in Back Office) and contacting Revenue to verify tax certificates. This resource is primarily used by payroll administrators and HR teams who need to investigate and resolve negative pay situations during payroll processing cycles.

t: Retrieving payroll reports after Complete Update has been run
s:
In some cases, you may have limited access to payroll reports if they weren’t downloaded before running the Complete Update job and finalising payroll. These reports are only temporarily available immediately after payroll is closed.

 

For example, a payroll report from six months ago cannot be re...
ss: Payroll reports become inaccessible after running the Complete Update job and finalising payroll, as they are only temporarily available immediately after closure. Open this document if you need to retrieve specific payroll reports (such as payroll complete update controls totals, employee pre-final update pay listing, or employee gross high/low) that weren't downloaded before the update was run. Use the View Gross to Nett screen to check which reports are still available for generation, or contact support for help retrieving older reports. Keep this guidance in mind to avoid losing access to critical payroll documentation—download necessary reports before initiating the Complete Update process.
sl: This document addresses the challenge of retrieving payroll reports after the Complete Update job has been executed and payroll has been finalised, a situation where report availability becomes significantly limited. The document explains that payroll reports are only temporarily available immediately after payroll closure, meaning reports from previous periods (such as six months prior) cannot be retrieved once this window has passed. To determine which reports remain accessible, users should navigate to the View Gross to Nett screen to check for available reports. If no reports are available through this screen, users can raise a support case online and reference this article to request retrieval assistance from the Access Group support team, though the document emphasises that retrieval is not guaranteed. The document specifies three particular reports that may be retrievable from the background system: Payroll complete update controls totals, Employee pre-final update pay listing (second half only), and Employee gross high/low. The document strongly advises users to download necessary reports before running the Complete Update job to avoid losing access to critical payroll data. This guidance is primarily useful for payroll administrators and finance teams who need to access historical payroll reports or who may have overlooked downloading reports before system updates.

s:

It is currently set to display on line 12, and by design, it automatically extends to ...
ss: Payslips may display differently between the app and system versions due to how the miscellaneous pay code is configured to appear on line 12 and beyond. This layout discrepancy is a known issue scheduled to be fixed later this quarter, though the system payslip functions as designed. You'd open this article if employees are reporting visual differences in their payslips across platforms, or if you need a workaround to adjust the miscellaneous pay code name in System Configuration to improve clarity in the app view.
sl: This document explains a known display discrepancy where payslips appear differently between the app version and the system version, caused by how the miscellaneous pay code is configured to appear on line 12 of the payslip and automatically extend beyond that point. While the system (copy/printed) payslip displays correctly with this configuration, the app version handles the layout differently, creating an alignment issue between platforms that Access Group has scheduled to fix later in the quarter. The document provides a workaround for users who want to adjust the display before the fix is released, though users should understand that renaming the miscellaneous pay code will affect how all items grouped under that code appear on the payslip. To implement the workaround, users navigate to Settings > General > System Configuration > Payslip in the portal, then select the relevant pay code from the Allowances Miscellaneous Pay Code drop-down list and adjust the name as needed (such as moving pension to appear at the bottom), before clicking Save. This manual adjustment will improve clarity on the payslip in the app view until the permanent fix is deployed. The document is primarily intended for payroll administrators, HR personnel, or system configuration managers who need to resolve payslip display issues for employees and manage how allowances and miscellaneous pay codes appear across different platforms.

t: Set up a salary sacrifice pension
s:
Setting up a salary sacrifice pension allows employees to enhance their retirement savings while benefiting from potential tax savings.

 

A salary sacrifice pension plan involves employees agreeing to reduce their gross salary in exchange for employer contributions to their pension scheme. This ar...
ss: Salary sacrifice pensions allow employees to reduce their gross salary in exchange for employer pension contributions, resulting in tax and National Insurance savings for both parties. Open this guide when you're configuring pension deductions for the first time or need to ensure your payslip displays salary sacrifice pension contributions correctly.
sl: This document explains how to set up a salary sacrifice pension arrangement, which allows employees to reduce their gross salary in exchange for employer pension contributions, resulting in lower National Insurance contributions for both parties and increased retirement savings. The guide is designed for payroll administrators and HR professionals who need to configure salary sacrifice pensions within the Access Group payroll system portal. The core task described involves enabling the Pre-Taxable Deduction Print Side toggle to ensure salary sacrifice pension deductions appear correctly on payslips. The document provides two alternative procedural paths: the first route navigates through Settings > Pay Codes (Classic), selecting the relevant pay code, accessing the Deductions tab, and toggling on Pre-Taxable Deduction Print Side before saving; the second route follows Settings > Pay Codes (Classic), searches for the pay code in the Search field, selects the three-dot icon to Edit, then adds a Rule by searching for "pre taxable" and enabling Pre-Taxable Deduction Print Side. The document addresses the practical requirement of correctly displaying salary sacrifice pension deductions on employee payslips while managing the associated tax and National Insurance implications. Related configuration tasks referenced include configuring payslip parameters, setting up pension schemes in Back Office, processing pension refunds with withholding tax, and configuring auto-enrolment, indicating this is part of a broader pension administration workflow.

sl: This document addresses the ORA-01403 "no data found" error that occurs when attempting to run the P32 report in the back office system. Users experiencing this error should first verify that they have been granted access to the appropriate pay group in their system configuration. t: Minimum wage report rounding issue
s:
If the minimum wage report displays that an employee earning minimum wage is being paid less than expected, rounding differences during calculation may have slightly reduced the actual payment. This reduction then flags the employee in the report. 

 

For example: 

If an employee is paid £12.21 pe...
ss: The minimum wage report may incorrectly flag employees as underpaid due to rounding differences that occur during pay and hourly rate calculations. When an employee's total pay is rounded down (for example, £64.1025 becomes £64.10), recalculating their hourly rate can result in a figure below the legal minimum wage threshold, even though they were paid correctly. To resolve this issue and remove the false flag from the report, add a manual timesheet entry of £0.01 for the affected employee in that pay period, then re-run the minimum wage report. This rounding workaround ensures the employee is no longer incorrectly identified as earning below minimum wage.
sl: This document explains a rounding issue that can cause the minimum wage report to incorrectly flag employees as being paid below minimum wage when they are actually being paid correctly. The problem occurs because rounding differences during pay calculations slightly reduce the actual payment amount, which then triggers a false alert in the report. The document provides a concrete example showing how an employee paid £12.21 per hour for 5.25 hours of work generates an expected gross pay of £64.1025, which rounds down to £64.10, and when the report recalculates the hourly rate by dividing this rounded figure back by hours worked, it produces £12.2095 that rounds down further to £12.20, incorrectly identifying the employee as underpaid. To resolve this false flagging issue, users need to add a manual timesheet entry of £0.01 for the affected employee during the relevant pay period, then re-run the minimum wage report to update the calculations and remove the incorrect minimum wage alert. This document is primarily useful for payroll administrators and HR professionals who run the minimum wage report (NMW) and need to understand why certain employees are being flagged despite correct payment, and how to correct these false positives through the timesheet adjustment process.

t: Payslips not released after completing a supplementary payroll run
s:
Supplementary payroll runs allow you to process additional payments after the payroll for a current pay period has been completed. 

 

You can apply a supplementary run in the following cases:

Processing late starters or rejoiners

Handling late leavers

Correcting underpayments or payroll errors
...
ss: Supplementary payroll runs let you process additional payments after the main payroll is complete—for late starters, leavers, corrections, bonuses, LTIPs, share dividends, or compromise agreements. Payslips from supplementary runs won't release automatically; they're dependent on the main payroll run's release status for that period. Open this document if supplementary payslips aren't appearing after you've completed the run, or if you need to understand the correct sequence for releasing both main and supplementary payslips together. It covers two release options: releasing main payslips first (which auto-publishes supplementary ones), or finalizing both runs then releasing payslips together.
sl: This document explains how to handle a common issue where payslips generated from supplementary payroll runs fail to be released after completion. It describes supplementary payroll runs as a feature that allows processing of additional payments after the main payroll for a period has been finalized, covering scenarios such as late starters, rejoiners, late leavers, underpayment corrections, bonuses, long-term incentive payments (LTIPs), share dividends, Restricted Share Unit (RSU) exercises, and compromise agreements. The core problem addressed is that payslips from supplementary runs are dependent on the main payroll run's status—if main payroll payslips remain unreleased, supplementary payslips will not be released even after running the Complete Update job. The document provides two alternative workflows to resolve this issue: Option 1 involves finalizing the main run, releasing its payslips, then processing and finalizing the supplementary run (which automatically publishes supplementary payslips during Complete Update), while Option 2involves finalizing both runs first before releasing payslips together. This guide is intended for payroll administrators and HR professionals who manage supplementary payroll processing and need to ensure timely payslip distribution to employees. The document also references related troubleshooting articles addressing other errors, such as missing payslips from pay groups and pay history conflicts with supplementary mode processing.

t: Are there any reports I need to run before starting a supplementary run
s: Before you start a supplementary payroll run, it’s essential to ensure that all key tasks from the main payroll run are completed and that required submissions (RTI or PMOD) have been accepted. Failing to complete these steps may prevent you from processing a supplementary run, especially after the ...
ss: Supplementary payroll runs require completing several prerequisite tasks from the main payroll, including printing payslips, generating bank files, and successfully submitting RTI or PMOD files. You must verify that all FPS (Full Payment Submission) or PMOD submissions from the previous month have been accepted before processing a supplementary run. After confirming these steps are complete, you'll need to enable supplementary payroll mode for your pay group through the Settings menu. Open this document when you're preparing to run a supplementary payroll and need to understand what tasks must be finished first or when troubleshooting why your supplementary run isn't processing.
sl: This document outlines the essential prerequisites and procedures for executing a supplementary payroll run within the Access Group payroll system. It establishes that supplementary payroll runs are restricted to the latest closed period of the same tax year and cannot be processed after year-end cleardown (December for Ireland, March for the UK) until the first payroll of the new tax year has been completed. Before initiating a supplementary run, users must verify that all tasks from the corresponding main payroll run are fully completed, including printing payslips, generating bank files, and completing RTI (Real Time Information) or PMOD submissions, with confirmation that these submissions have been successfully accepted by the relevant authorities. The document provides specific step-by-step instructions for enabling supplementary payroll mode: users must navigate to Settings > Codes > Pay Groups in the portal, select the relevant pay group from the Pay Group Code drop-down menu, toggle the Supplementary Mode option, confirm the action, and save the changes. Once supplementary mode is enabled, the system returns the pay group to the previous payroll period and displays an orange "Supplementary" indicator in the Mode column on the Manage Payroll screen to signal the active status. This guide is primarily used by payroll administrators and finance teams who need to process corrective or additional payroll runs within the same tax year and must understand both the regulatory submission requirements and the system configuration steps necessary to avoid processing errors.

sl: This document explains how to handle payroll situations where employees receive payslips with zero or negative net pay, which can occur due to adjustments, deductions, or corrections. Within Admin Settings, users search for the specific parameter cp_show_ng_pay_period, click Edit, and change its value to Y before clicking OK to apply the change. For cases where administrators prefer not to enable this setting globally, the document provides an alternative approach: raising a new case online while referencing the article title and providing specific details including employee details and the relevant payroll period. The document is designed for payroll administrators and HR professionals who need to manage portal visibility of zero or negative net pay payslips within the Access Group payroll system. Related functionality includes negative net pay recovery setup, payslip display troubleshooting following manual payment cancellations, and Intelligent Payslips configuration, indicating this is part of a broader payslip management feature set.

Follow the step-by-step instructions provided to update the relevant fields in Maintain Timesheets and re-run the payroll job to resolve the issue.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre provides a troubleshooting guide for resolving the "Pay Code: [XXX] Zero Rate of Pay Used to Value This Timesheet" error that users may encounter when running the observation report in the CorePay payroll system. The guide addresses three primary causes of this error and supplies step-by-step resolution procedures for each scenario. The third scenario occurs when the transaction date on the timesheet falls outside the employee's appointment start and end dates, which users can resolve by accessing the same Maintain Timesheets screen, verifying the transaction date falls within the appointment period (with particular attention to mid-period departures), making necessary corrections, and re-running the salary job. t: Cumulative PRSI weeks do not match history PRSI weeks on pre year end data check report
s: If the cumulative PRSI weeks do not align with the history PRSI weeks, even though the employee’s PRSI weeks are correctly allocated throughout the year, it is because of a mismatch between the cumulative and history weeks on the Amend PRSI Class/Weeks screen which results to an incorrect exception ...
ss: The CorePay payroll system tracks PRSI (Pay Related Social Insurance) weeks cumulatively and historically, and mismatches between these two values can trigger exceptions on the pre year end data check report even when weeks are correctly allocated throughout the year. This issue occurs due to a discrepancy on the Amend PRSI Class/Weeks screen in back office, which prevents the cumulative and history totals from aligning. Open this document when you need to resolve PRSI week mismatches by recalculating totals through the CorePay employee maintenance screens. The fix involves re-entering PRSI week values for the relevant periods, which triggers a recalculation and reconciles the cumulative and history figures once the report regenerates.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses a specific data validation issue in payroll software where cumulative PRSI weeks do not match history PRSI weeks on the pre year end data check report, even when the employee's PRSI weeks have been correctly allocated throughout the year. The mismatch occurs due to a discrepancy between cumulative and history weeks recorded on the Amend PRSI Class/Weeks screen, which triggers an incorrect exception in the reporting process. To resolve this issue, users navigate through the back office system by accessing CorePay, then Employee, followed by PAYE/PRSI/TFA/Cumulatives, and clicking on Amend PRSI/NI Class/Weeks to locate the affected employee using the query icon. The resolution involves re-entering the weeks value for the required periods in the lower section of the screen, with the practical suggestion to temporarily set the value to 0 and then back to the correct amount (for example, changing 2 to 0 then back to 2). Once these steps are completed and the changes are saved, the system will automatically recalculate the PRSI totals, and the cumulative and history weeks will align when the report is regenerated. This document is relevant for payroll administrators and HR professionals who use Access Group's CorePay system and encounter discrepancies during pre-year-end data validation processes.

sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses a validation exception error that occurs when processing observation reports or viewing gross to nett calculations for new starters in a payroll system. sl: This document addresses a common accounting reconciliation issue in payroll systems where control totals fail to balance specifically because an employee has been moved to a different pay group. The document takes a pragmatic approach by advising that proceeding without manual intervention is acceptable, as simply noting the pay group change is sufficient from an audit perspective, meaning that formal corrective action or system adjustments are not necessary. t: Approved salary not pulling through to payslip

ss: When an appointment end date is set in the payroll system, the salary automatically zeroes out by design to prevent payments against ended roles. If you accidentally ended an appointment and need to reactivate it, removing the end date alone won't restore pay—you must create a new salary amendment and re-run the payroll jobs. Use this article if an employee's approved salary isn't appearing on their payslip after you've corrected or updated their appointment details. If the salary still doesn't generate after these steps, follow the troubleshooting guidance to raise a support case with the required employee information.
sl: This document explains why approved salaries sometimes fail to appear on payslips when an appointment record has been assigned an end date. The system automatically sets the salary to zero for any appointment with an end date to prevent payroll errors against terminated positions, which is intentional behavior rather than a malfunction. If an appointment end date was added by mistake and subsequently removed, simply deleting the end date does not restore the salary to the payroll process; instead, users must create a new salary amendment for that appointment to reinstate it. After recording the new salary amendment, users need to re-run the payroll jobs to ensure the corrected salary generates on the next payslip. The document is intended for payroll administrators and HR personnel who manage employee appointments and salary records in the Access Group system and encounter situations where ended appointments need to be reinstated. If the salary still does not appear on the payslip after following these steps, users should raise a support case and reference this article's title while providing the employee name and employee number for investigation.

t: Employee cannot view payslips

The issue typically stems from either an incorrect personnel number linked to their portal account or a pay method (such as CH) that prevents payslip output to the portal. You'll use the Security Dashboard to run an integrity test, or navigate to People Management or CorePersonnel to update the employee's pay method settings. Open this document when an employee reports they cannot access their payslips through the portal and you need step-by-step guidance to diagnose and resolve the problem.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving issues when employees cannot view their payslips in the portal, specifically when encountering "Error - No Tax Details Available" under the Tax Detail screen or "Error - No Payslips to display" under the My Payslips screen. The document identifies two primary causes: an incorrect personnel number linked to the employee's portal username, or an incompatible pay method (specifically pay method CH) that prevents payslip output to the portal. To diagnose an incorrect personnel number, administrators should navigate to Security Dashboard > User Management, search for the employee, click the three-dot icon, and run an Integrity Test; if no errors are found, a support case should be raised. To resolve pay method issues, the document provides two alternative processes: through the Portal by accessing People management > Dashboard > VIEW > the employee record > Actions > Personnel Profile > Bank Details > UPDATE, or through the Back office via CorePersonnel > Maintenance > Personal Profile, then selecting Payment Method from the Select Detail list and updating it accordingly. Both pay method update procedures ensure future payslips output to the portal, though historical payslips require contacting the support team to raise a new case referencing the article title and affected employee details. This document is typically used by HR administrators, payroll managers, and IT support staff assisting employees who report missing payslips or tax information in the portal system.

ss: Payroll payslips in PeopleXD may display blank when generated for an employee due to configuration or system issues. sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving blank payslips generated for individual employees within the Access Group payroll system. For the zero rate of pay scenario, the resolution process involves checking with HR to determine whether the employee should have an active or dormant status, and understanding that employees with a secondary status of "S," an enabled Print Payslip toggle, and an actual rate of pay (including amounts as minimal as $0.01) will generate printed payslips. For Complete Update job failures, the document directs users to raise a support case online while referencing the article title and providing specific details about the affected employee, as the support team will need to investigate the database directly. This document is designed for payroll administrators, HR personnel, and support staff who encounter situations where employee payslips appear blank and need systematic steps to identify and resolve the underlying configuration or technical issues causing the problem.

t: Reconciliation report
s:
The reconciliation report brings data together in one place, allowing you to see payroll values that would otherwise only be available in a limited format on a P32 report. This facilitates a more efficient end-of-period reconciliation process.

📌Note: This is only available for UK Payroll.

 

 

Co...
ss: The reconciliation report consolidates UK payroll data in one place, displaying income tax, national insurance contributions, apprenticeship levy, and amounts due to HMRC that would otherwise be scattered across limited P32 reports. Use this report during month-end or year-end close to efficiently verify and reconcile your payroll values against your employer payment submissions. You'll need to enable the FINALREPORTS_MENU.RECONCILIATION menu option in your Security Dashboard first, then access the report through Manage Payroll > Outputs > Reports and select your company, pay group, year, and tax month.
sl: The reconciliation report is a UK Payroll-specific tool that consolidates payroll data in a single location, providing comprehensive visibility into payroll values that are otherwise fragmented across limited P32 report formats, thereby streamlining the end-of-period reconciliation process. To access this report, administrators must first enable the FINALREPORTS_MENU.RECONCILIATION menu option through the Security Dashboard by navigating to Menu Profiles, locating the relevant user's menu profile (such as COREPORTAL_EMPLOYEE), selecting Manage Menu Options, filtering by CorePortal Pay system, and toggling on the required menu option. Once enabled, users run the report by accessing Manage Payroll, selecting the appropriate pay group, navigating to the Outputs tab, clicking Reports, then selecting Reconciliation and populating required fields including Company, Pay Group, Year, and Tax Month before printing and opening the resulting .csv file from the Report Centre. The report output is structured across four main sections: Income Tax (boxes 1–5, covering PAYE, student loans, postgraduate loans, and payment dates to HMRC), National Insurance Contributions (boxes 6–20, detailing gross contributions, statutory pay recoveries such as SSP, SMP, SPP, SAP, and SPBP, and net NICs due), Apprenticeship Levy split into period and year-to-date views (boxes 21–34, tracking leviable earnings, levy rates, and allowances), and Amount Due to HMRC per Employer Payment Submission (boxes 35–39, summarizing total amounts owed). The document also references related configuration tasks and error resolution scenarios, such as addressing invalid negative values in statutory pay recovery fields and configuring manual rate changes for year-end adjustments. This document is primarily used by UK payroll administrators and finance teams responsible for regulatory compliance reporting and month-end or year-end payroll reconciliation activities.

sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre provides guidance on resolving the error message "UNABLE TO DETERMINE PAYSLIP RATE OF PAY (RATE SEQUENCE NUMBER 1)" that occurs when running the observation report or the View Gross to Nett report in Back Office. The error occurs when specified position rates and scale points for an employee's salary are missing or not properly configured in the system. The document walks users through three main diagnostic and corrective steps performed within Back Office: first, reviewing the employee's salary history by navigating to CorePersonnel > Maintenance > Salary Administration > Maintain HR Salary Amendments; second, verifying that all position rates and scale points exist by checking both the HR Salary Amendments section and CorePay > Pay Rates > View Position Rates; and third, if rates are missing, adding them through CorePay > Pay Rates > Maintain Position Rates where users must record the position and scale point rate. A critical configuration note specifies that salaries cannot use scale 0 and must use scale points of 1 or above. This document is intended for payroll administrators and HR professionals who encounter reporting errors related to employee compensation setup and need to audit and correct position rate configurations in the system.

ss: REP-52251 and REP-56093 errors occur when you're unable to retrieve RPN output or cached job results in your system. Open this document if you're blocked from retrieving RPNs for a company and need quick troubleshooting steps—the resolution usually involves retrying the retrieval, waiting briefly, or having another user attempt the same task.
sl: This document provides guidance on resolving two specific error messages—REP-52251 and REP-56093—that users encounter when attempting to retrieve RPNs (Revenue Personnel Numbers) for a company, particularly when no RPN Exceptions report has been generated. Error REP-52251 indicates that output from a specific Job ID requested at a particular date and time cannot be retrieved, while error REP-56093 signals that cached output for a job is no longer valid. The document explains that these errors typically result from intermittent local issues such as network outages or problems with the user's laptop or browser rather than systemic failures. The recommended resolution involves attempting to retrieve the RPNs again or running the report after a brief waiting period to allow temporary issues to resolve. If the error persists after a retry, the document advises users to have another user attempt the same retrieval to determine whether the issue is specific to one user or account. The document also references related error articles covering connection timeouts, invalid PPSN and Employment ID combinations, job running conflicts in Pay Groups, and RPN response file retrieval failures with validation errors, providing a broader context for RPN retrieval troubleshooting. ss: Employee PRSI week overrides entered in the payroll system may not appear on the payslip or Cumulative screen due to several common configuration or data issues. This document covers the troubleshooting process for the PAY300 PRSI package, identifying why overrides fail to process and providing step-by-step resolutions for each cause—including missing PRSIable pay codes, quarterly pay periods, negative PRSIable pay, and incorrect override pay codes. Open this document when an employee's PRSI week override has been recorded but isn't displaying on their payslip or when you need to diagnose why the Payroll Validation Exception report is flagging unexpected PRSI behavior.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses a specific payroll issue where employees who have entered PRSI (Pay Related Social Insurance) weeks overrides find that these overrides do not display on their payslip or the Cumulative screen. The document provides a troubleshooting guide that identifies five possible causes and their corresponding resolutions for this problem. The first cause relates to PRSIable pay, where the absence of at least one PRSIable pay code during the pay period prevents the PAY300 package from processing the override; the resolution is to record a 0.00 value timesheet using the system-level Employee PRSI Override pay code. A second scenario involves quarterly-paid employees where recording a zero override may trigger a "PRSI WEEKS OVERRIDE OF 13 USED FOR THIS EMPLOYEE" message in the Payroll Validation Exception report, which is expected system behavior. The document also addresses situations where negative PRSIable pay prevents the system from applying the override or generating employee and employer PRSI, with a suggested mitigation of reducing illness benefit payments and distributing them across multiple pay periods. Additionally, the document warns that using an incorrect pay code when entering the override will prevent it from appearing, emphasizing the importance of using the correct employee PRSI override or employer PRSI override pay code as specified in the system. This guide is intended for payroll administrators and HR professionals who manage employee compensation and benefits within Access Group's payroll system and encounter issues with PRSI week overrides not reflecting in payroll documentation.

ss: The Observation report in CorePay may display a "Pension To Date Exceeds Pension Tax Limit Percentage of Gross to Date" error when processing salary adjustments for employees. This error occurs in two scenarios: when an employee on a Week 1 tax basis has pension and AVC contributions that exceed their allowed relief limit (calculated as a percentage of gross pay based on their age), or when an employee's date of birth is missing from the system. Open this document if you're running payroll validation and need to resolve pension contribution warnings, or if you need to check Old Age Pension rates and pension tax limits in the CorePay Reference section.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses the error message "Pension To Date Exceeds Pension Tax Limit Percentage of Gross to Date" and provides solutions for two distinct scenarios that arise when running the Observation report for employees receiving salary adjustments. The first scenario occurs when an employee is on a Week 1 tax basis and their total pension-related contributions (including AVC contributions and pension payments) exceed the allowed relief limit calculated as a percentage of their gross pay. To resolve this issue, users must navigate to the Back Office by clicking CorePay, then Reference, then Advanced Reference Features, then Reference K-P, and finally Old Age Pension Rates to access the Pension Tax Limits settings where OAP rates can be reviewed. The document illustrates the problem with a specific example showing how an employee aged 56 with a gross pay of €4,200.00 and a 35% OAP rate has an allowed limit of €1,470.00, but their combined AVC contributions (€2,648.17) and pension (€32.94) total €2,681.11, which exceeds this threshold. The second scenario that triggers this error involves an employee with no recorded date of birth in the system, which can be remedied by entering the missing date of birth and re-running the validation job. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and HR professionals working with the Access Group's payroll system who need to troubleshoot pension contribution calculation errors during the salary processing workflow.

sl: This document provides instructions for generating final control reports within a payroll management system to verify payroll accuracy at the conclusion of a payroll period. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and finance teams who need to validate payroll data integrity before finalizing payroll periods and submitting data to accounting systems. The final control reports serve as a critical reconciliation tool that helps identify discrepancies between different payroll calculation stages, preventing errors from flowing into downstream financial records and auto enrolment contributions.

t: The YTD values are incorrect in the Detailed Observation report (PAYB300DET)
s:

 ...
ss: The Detailed Payroll Observation Report (PAYB300DET) displays incorrect year-to-date values when it doubles the current period column and adds it to the year-to-date column due to payroll update timing. To get accurate results, run this report after completing the Run Payroll Update job (PAY300) but before running the Complete Update job (PAY355). If the complete update period has already been processed, the report will include that period's totals twice. Open this document when you notice discrepancies in year-to-date totals on your payroll observation reports and need to understand the correct timing and calculation method.
sl: The document addresses a specific data accuracy issue in the Detailed Payroll Observation Report (PAYB300det) where year-to-date values display incorrectly due to the report doubling the current period column values and adding them to the year-to-date column totals. This problem stems from the timing and sequencing of payroll update processes within the system. To resolve the issue, users must run the report after completing the Run Payroll Update job (PAY300) but before executing the Complete Update job (PAY355), ensuring the report captures accurate period data at the correct processing stage. The document explains that if the complete update period has already been processed, the report will incorrectly include that period's totals twice in the year-to-date calculation. The underlying calculation method sums all totals from the beginning of the year through the completed update period for the applicable pay group, then adds current period totals to this figure to generate year-to-date values. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and finance professionals who rely on the PAYB300det report for accurate payroll observation and reconciliation tasks, particularly when investigating discrepancies between reported year-to-date figures and expected values.

t: Error: 'Unable to Run Report'
s:
If you run a report within a CoreHR module and the following error appears, it is because of the Reports Server. 

 

All reports within CoreHR run from the same reports server. If a specific report fails to run and displays an error message, there is an issue with the Reports Server.

 

To resolve...
ss: When you encounter an error message while running a report in CoreHR (such as CoreTime or CorePersonnel modules), it's usually caused by an issue with the Reports Server. This document walks you through diagnostic steps to determine whether the problem is server-related, user-specific, or report-specific—including retesting with smaller data sets, different reports, different modules, and different browsers. You'll also find troubleshooting for user-specific issues like expired passwords and session problems. Open this document when a report fails to run in CoreHR and you need to isolate the cause before contacting IT support.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for users encountering an "Unable to Run Report" error when executing reports within CoreHR modules, explaining that all CoreHR reports run from a centralized Reports Server and that failures typically stem from issues with this server. The document outlines a systematic diagnostic process to determine whether the error originates from the Reports Server itself or from user-specific or report-specific issues, beginning with steps such as running the report again for a smaller data subset (e.g., a single employee rather than the entire company), attempting to run a different report within the same module like CoreTime or CorePersonnel, running a report from an entirely different module, having another user attempt the same report from their PC, and switching to a different browser such as Google Chrome or Mozilla Firefox. If the report runs successfully following any of these troubleshooting steps, the issue is determined to be user-specific or report-specific rather than a server problem. To resolve user-specific or report-specific issues, the document directs users to check whether their password has expired or changed, reset the password if it has zero days remaining (with a reference to a separate article on changing back office passwords), log out of CoreHR and log back in, and then attempt to run the report again. If the report continues to fail after completing all these steps, the document indicates that the Reports Server may be down and recommends contacting the local IT department to confirm whether network issues exist. This document is intended for CoreHR end-users and system administrators who need to diagnose and resolve report execution failures within the CoreHR system.

t: Upload payslip message
s:
The feature for uploading payslip messages allows you to add personalized or general messages to employees' payslips.

 

This process is crucial for communicating important updates, announcements, or reminders directly to employees in a clear and accessible manner. 

 

Use this feature whenever yo...
ss: The payslip message upload feature in Portal lets you add personalized or general messages directly to employee payslips without manually editing each one. You upload a specially formatted CSV file containing employee references and up to six lines of messages (45 characters each) through Uploads > Load Payslip Messages. Use this when you need to communicate important updates, announcements, or reminders to employees efficiently across your workforce. The CSV file must contain six commas and include at least the employee reference and Message1 field; you can also remove messages by marking fields with a dot (.) or delete all messages by leaving non-mandatory fields blank.
sl: This document explains how to use the payslip message upload feature in Portal to add personalized or general messages to employee payslips efficiently without manual editing of individual documents. The feature serves as a communication tool for sharing important updates, announcements, or reminders directly to employees in a clear and accessible manner. To upload payslip messages, users navigate to Uploads in Portal, select Load Payslip Messages under Employee Uploads, browse to select their file, and click OK, after which a confirmation message displays the number of records loaded before clicking Update Employee Message Details. The system requires CSV file format with a specific structure containing Employee Ref followed by six message fields (Message1 through Message6), with each line requiring exactly six commas to be recognized properly by the system. Each message field can contain up to 45 characters, though only Employee Ref and Message1 are mandatory; the remaining Message2-Message6 fields are optional. To remove messages for individual employees, users can amend the payslip message by uploading a file with only the Employee Ref and a dot (.) in Message1, leaving all other fields blank. This document is typically used by payroll administrators or HR personnel who need to communicate batch information to multiple employees through their payslips and manage message updates or deletions across the employee population.

t: Error: 'Could not find a minimum/living or apprentice hourly rate set up'
s:
If the error message appears while generating the minimum or living wage exception report, even after the rates and warning wage have been properly configured, it is likely due to incorrect company reference data. 
​
You’ll need to verify the country code entered for the company associated with the ...
ss: The minimum or living wage exception report in the Payroll Dashboard throws an error even when wage rates are correctly configured, usually due to missing or incorrect country code settings in company reference data. To fix this, navigate to Payroll Dashboard > Settings > Company Parameters > Organisations, select your company from the Code dropdown, and verify the Country Code field is populated with the correct value. Save any changes and regenerate the report to resolve the issue. If the error persists after updating the country code, contact the support team with reference to this article.
sl: This document addresses a specific error message—"Could not find a minimum/living or apprentice hourly rate set up"—that appears when users attempt to generate a minimum or living wage exception report within the Access Group payroll system, even when wage rates and warning thresholds have been correctly configured. The error typically stems from incorrect company reference data rather than missing rate configuration, making it a troubleshooting guide for payroll administrators and compliance personnel. The document provides step-by-step instructions to resolve the issue by navigating through the portal's Payroll Dashboard to Settings, then to Company Parameters and Organisations, where users must select their company from the Code dropdown menu and verify the Country Code field contains the correct value. If the Country Code field is empty, users must select the appropriate country code from the dropdown menu and save the changes. After completing this verification and saving the country code, users should attempt to generate the minimum wage exception report again to confirm the error has been resolved. The document notes that if the problem persists after following these steps, users should contact the support team and reference this article, indicating that more complex underlying issues may require professional assistance. This guidance is essential for payroll teams managing compliance reporting in multi-country or multi-company environments where country-specific wage regulations apply.

t: What is an iCue?
s:
iCues are intelligent trigger-based Insight reports, designed to proactively send alerts to stakeholders, when certain thresholds are breached/events are occurring.
​
Examples of how iCues could be used include:

Alert an employee when they have a large annual leave balance remaining.

Alert an empl...
ss: iCues are intelligent alert systems that automatically send notifications to employees, managers, and finance teams when specific thresholds or events occur in your HR data. They help monitor key metrics like leave balances, sick leave usage, attrition rates, and cost increases, enabling proactive management before issues escalate. Open this document when you need to understand what iCues are, how they work, or want to see examples of how they can be configured to track important HR events and thresholds across your organization.
sl: This document explains iCues, which are intelligent trigger-based Insight reports that automatically send proactive alerts to stakeholders when predefined thresholds are breached or specific events occur within the system. The document illustrates the versatility of iCues through multiple real-world use case examples across different user roles and organizational functions. These alerts can notify employees about significant annual leave balances, inform both employees and managers of important dates such as anniversaries or birthdays, and alert managers when their direct reports approach sick leave thresholds or when leave periods overlap. The system also enables higher-level alerts, such as notifying Human Resources Directors when attrition rates spike or alerting Finance Directors when costs are increasing. While the extracted text does not provide detailed configuration steps or menu paths for setting up iCues, it indicates that this functionality integrates with the Insight reporting system and relates to absence and leave management processes. The document serves HR professionals, managers, finance leaders, and HR directors who need to monitor workforce metrics and trigger timely communications based on organizational thresholds and events.

You would open this document if you've discovered that your payroll controls aren't reconciling properly and need to contact support to resolve the underlying issue. sl: This document addresses a technical troubleshooting issue where the Control Report PAYB141 fails to balance against the Detailed Amendments Report PAYB143. s:

This occurs because the Print Payslip Rate toggle is disabled. To enable this, follow the steps below in Portal.

ss: When employee payslips display without hours worked and pay rate information, the issue is typically caused by a disabled Print Payslip Rate toggle in your payroll system. You can resolve this by navigating to Settings > System Configuration > Payslip and enabling the Print Payslip Rate toggle. Open this document if your payslips are missing critical time and compensation details that employees need to see on their pay statements.
sl: This document addresses a payroll display issue where hours worked and pay rates fail to appear on employee payslips in the Portal system. The problem occurs specifically because the Print Payslip Rate toggle is disabled in the system configuration. To resolve this, users must navigate to Settings, then access General and System Configuration from the Portal menu. Once in System Configuration, users should click on the Payslip section and enable the Print Payslip Rate toggle to restore the display of hours and rates on payslips. After making this change, users must close the page by clicking the X button and then click Save to apply the configuration. This document is typically used by payroll administrators or system managers who manage Portal payroll settings and need to ensure that complete pay information is visible to employees on their pay statements. The document also references related articles covering other payslip display issues, such as missing payslip history, incorrect pay rates, negative payslips, and payslip problems following manual payment cancellations.

t: Payslip display issue in Portal following manual payment cancellation
s:
The employee's payslip in the Portal pulls data from the View Payment Details screen for each pay period to determine what appears online. 

 

If older payment details remain on that screen and the pay method is set to PP or CH, the system will display the original payslip to the employee.

 

To v...
ss: When a payment is manually canceled in your payroll system, the Portal may continue displaying the original payslip instead of reflecting the cancellation, because older payment details remain on the View Payment Details screen. This document covers how to access and display the correct canceled payment payslip in Portal by navigating to Manage Payroll, selecting Outputs, and using the Print Payslips function with the Copy Payslip Period option. Open this guide if you've canceled a payment and need to retrieve or view the updated payslip for an employee, or if employees are seeing outdated payslip information after a manual payment cancellation.
sl: This document explains how to resolve a specific issue where employee payslips display incorrectly in the Portal after a manual payment cancellation, occurring when the View Payment Details screen retains older payment data for pay methods set to PP (standing order) or CH (CHAPS). The document provides a step-by-step procedure for Portal users to locate and display the correct canceled payment payslip, beginning with navigating to Manage Payroll, selecting a pay group, and accessing Outputs. Users must then navigate to Print Payslips, enable the Select Specific Employee toggle, and search for the employee number using the Search Name field, adding each relevant employee to the selection. The process requires enabling the Copy Payslip option and selecting the appropriate Copy Payslip Period, with the important caveat that while users can search by actual payroll period (such as 202417), the system displays these as Financial or Tax Periods (shown as 202404). When a payment has been canceled during the selected period, the Cancel Payment toggle becomes available and should be enabled. After completing all additional configuration details, users send the corrected payslip to the Report Centre by clicking Print Payslip. This document is intended for Portal administrators or payroll personnel who need to verify or reissue payslips following manual payment cancellations and serves as a troubleshooting guide for the specific display issue that occurs when canceled payment records remain cached in the system.

t: The minimum wage report (NMW) is not looking at the substantial posts actual hours
s: If the minimum wage report is calculating an incorrect hourly rate for a substantial number of employees or if it has difficulty interpreting the substantial hours recorded, the issue may stem from data synchronization problems, configuration errors, or missing entries in the substantial hours recor...
ss: The Minimum Wage Exception report may show incorrect hourly rates or fail to account for substantial hours due to data synchronization issues, configuration errors, or missing records. Use this document when employees' calculated hourly rates appear below statutory minimums or when contracted hours don't match actual weekly hours worked. You'll learn how to access the Minimum Wage tab in Payroll Checking, review the exception report, and enable the Periodic Employee Hours toggle in Pay Group settings to resolve discrepancies. Open this if you're troubleshooting payroll compliance problems related to minimum wage calculations in your pay group.
sl: This document addresses issues with the minimum wage report in an Access Group payroll system that fails to accurately calculate hourly rates for substantial numbers of employees or misinterprets recorded substantial hours. The document identifies root causes including data synchronization problems, configuration errors, and missing entries in substantial hours records. To resolve these issues, users are directed to check the Minimum Wage Exception report by navigating to Manage Payroll, selecting a pay group, accessing the Payroll Checking tab, clicking View Gross to Nett, and then selecting the Minimum Wage tab, which displays employees whose calculated hourly rate falls below the statutory minimum. A common scenario addressed is when contracted hours do not match actual weekly hours, which is resolved by enabling the Periodic Employee Hours toggle in the pay group settings—accessed through Settings > Codes > Pay Groups, selecting the relevant pay group code, clicking Next Page, and toggling on the Periodic Employee Hours option before saving. This document is intended for payroll administrators and HR professionals who manage employee compensation and need to troubleshoot minimum wage compliance reporting issues within the Access Group payroll system. The document also references related articles covering minimum wage rounding issues, occupational salary offsets, minimum wage warning rates, and errors related to missing hourly rate configuration, indicating it is part of a broader help system addressing minimum wage calculation challenges.

ss: When a payslip (PAY375H) shows an outdated address even though the employee's current address is stored in the system, the issue is typically caused by the Payslip Options setting being configured to "Work" instead of "Home." You can fix this in CorePay by navigating to Employee > Maintain Employee Details, locating the Payslip Options section, and changing the setting to Home before regenerating the payslip. Open this document if payslips are displaying incorrect or old address information that doesn't match the employee records in your back office system.
sl: This document addresses a specific issue where employee payslips, identified as form PAY375H, display outdated address information even though current address details have been updated in the system. The problem occurs because the payslip option is configured to display the Work address rather than the Home address. To resolve this issue, users must access the back office system and navigate to CorePay, then select the Employee option. From there, they click Maintain Employee Details and enter the employee's personnel number in the Personnel No field. The core fix involves locating the Payslip Options section and changing the setting from Work to Home. After making this configuration change, users must save it using the save icon, then regenerate a copy of the payslip to display the correct address. This document is typically used by payroll administrators or HR personnel in the Access Group system who manage employee records and need to ensure payslips reflect accurate contact information.

Check that each employee has a valid Personnel Type assigned in Pers Data, and confirm their Portal username and menu group are correctly configured in PIN Maintenance. Open this document if users report missing payslips in Portal or if you need to troubleshoot employee access issues related to payroll information visibility. sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving situations where employees cannot access their payslips through Portal, focusing on employee configuration verification that should be maintained by customers or Superusers. The document outlines a systematic approach to diagnosing the issue by checking employee setup in Back Office through two main configuration areas: first, navigating to CoreTime > Pers Data > Person Maintenance to verify that each employee has a valid Pers Type assigned (such as Active - A or Permanent - P), and second, accessing Pers Data > PIN Maintenance to confirm the correct Portal username and menu group are configured for the employee. The troubleshooting process includes specific steps such as using the list icon in the Person field to select an employee, double-clicking records to review menu group assignments, and entering correct Portal usernames and menu groups if they are missing or incorrect. This document addresses the underlying configuration causes of Portal payslip visibility problems and helps users understand that access issues typically stem from incomplete employee setup rather than system errors. The related articles referenced at the end point to additional payslip-related issues including error messages about missing payslips for the current pay group, alternative display problems with allowances, and payslip release procedures.

t: Display a PPS number on a payslip
s:
Displaying a PPS (Personal Public Service) number on a payslip involves configuring the payslip template to include this unique identifier for Irish employees. 

 

Apply this to comply with Irish payroll regulations to provide employees with complete payroll information, and ensure proper identific...
ss: Configuring PPS (Personal Public Service) numbers on payslips in your payroll system ensures Irish employees receive complete tax and social welfare identification on their payroll documents. You'll enable this by accessing Administrator Dashboard > Site Manager > Admin Settings and setting the py_payslip_pps_no parameter to "Y". Open this document if you need to add PPS numbers to employee payslips to comply with Irish payroll regulations, or if you're customizing payslip templates to display additional employee and company information. Note that the PPS number will only appear on payslips generated after you make this change.
sl: This document provides instructions for configuring an Access Group payroll system to display PPS (Personal Public Service) numbers on employee payslips in compliance with Irish payroll regulations. The process involves enabling the py_payslip_pps_no parameter through the Portal interface to ensure employees receive complete payroll information with proper identification for tax and social welfare purposes. Users must navigate to the Administrator Dashboard via the dashboard menu, then access Site Manager and Admin Settings to locate the configuration options. In the Search field within Admin Settings, users can enter the py_payslip_pps_no parameter along with related parameters such as py_payslip_coname_ind (for company name display), py_payslip_company_no (for company registration number), or py_payslip_personnel_no (also for company registration number), then click Edit and enter Y to enable the setting before clicking OK. This configuration is typically used by payroll administrators or system managers who need to ensure payslips comply with Irish regulatory requirements. An important limitation is that the PPS number will only appear on payslips generated after the parameter change is applied, and this modification does not retroactively affect previously issued payslips. The document also references related articles covering payslip error messages, additional payslip parameter configuration, negative payslip creation, and Intelligent Payslip functionality for users seeking broader payslip management guidance.

t: Gross to nett report blank after generating the validation job
s:
If the report for the gross to nett pay is blank after generating the validation job, you need to adjust the gross high and gross low fields in the Pay Group screen. 

 

To do this, follow the steps below in Back Office. 

Click CorePay then click Reference.

Click Pay Group.

In the Pay Group Code...
ss: When your gross to nett pay report appears blank after running a validation job in CorePay, the issue is typically caused by overly restrictive Gross High and Gross Low field settings in the Pay Group screen. These fields filter which employees display on the report, and if set incorrectly (for example, gross high at 5000 and gross low at 50), no employees may meet the criteria. You can resolve this by adjusting both fields to zero in Back Office under CorePay > Reference > Pay Group, which ensures all employees appear on the report. After making these changes, re-run the validation to generate the complete gross to nett report.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving blank gross to nett pay reports that appear after running a validation job in the Access Group payroll system. The issue occurs when the Gross High and Gross Low fields in the Pay Group screen are configured with values that inadvertently filter out employee records from the report. Users access this configuration through the Back Office system by navigating to CorePay > Reference > Pay Group, where they can select a specific pay group using the list icon and navigate to page 2 using the arrow navigation icons. The document explains that the current field settings create an unintended filter—for example, if Gross High is set to 5000 and Gross Low to 50, the report will only display employees whose gross pay falls outside this range (less than 50 or greater than 5000), effectively excluding most employees. To resolve the blank report issue, users must amend both the Gross High and Gross Low fields to zero, which removes the restrictive filtering and ensures all employees are included in the report output. After making these adjustments in the Pay Group screen, users must re-run the validation job to generate a complete gross to nett report. This document is primarily intended for payroll administrators and Back Office users who manage pay group configurations and need to troubleshoot validation report discrepancies in the Access Group system.

t: Re-joiner not listed on the Payroll Exceptions report
s:
If a re-joiner is missing from the Payroll Exceptions report, it’s because they only appear on the report for the payroll period when their status was updated to active.

 

If an employee is marked as active with a future re-join date, they will appear on the Payroll Exceptions report for the perio...
ss: Re-joiners only appear on the Payroll Exceptions report during the payroll period when their status was changed to active, not necessarily when they actually rejoin. If an employee has a future re-join date but is already marked as active in the system, they'll show on the report for the period their status was updated rather than their scheduled re-join period. Use this article if you're trying to locate a returning employee on the Payroll Exceptions report and can't find them in the expected payroll cycle.
sl: This document explains why a re-joiner employee may not appear on the Payroll Exceptions report and clarifies the specific timing logic governing their visibility on that report. The document addresses a common configuration scenario where an employee is marked with an active status but has a future re-join date assigned to their record. The key issue resolved is that re-joiners only appear on the Payroll Exceptions report during the payroll period when their status was actually updated to active, not during the period when their scheduled re-join date occurs. This distinction is important because employees with future re-join dates will generate a report entry based on when the status change was processed in the system, which may be different from when they physically return to work. The document is targeted at payroll administrators and HR professionals who manage employee status changes and monitor the Payroll Exceptions report as part of their regular payroll processing workflows. Understanding this behavior helps users correctly interpret report results and distinguish between when status updates occur versus when employee re-join dates are scheduled to take effect.
