ss: The Net Pay and Deduction Orders report (Pay395) breaks down nett pay payments and deduction orders for a specific payroll period in your portal payroll system. Use this report when you need to verify deduction details or review nett pay calculations for a particular pay group and payroll run. Access it through Manage Payroll > Outputs > Reports, then select your pay group, period, and run number (Main Run or Supplementary Run) to generate the report. This is essential for payroll reconciliation and confirming that deductions have been correctly applied before finalizing payments.
sl: The Net Pay and Deduction Orders report (Pay395) provides a detailed breakdown of nett pay payments and deduction orders for a specified payroll period within the Access Group payroll system. Users access this report through the portal by navigating to Manage Payroll, selecting a pay group, then clicking through the Outputs and Reports sections to locate the Net Pay and Deduction Orders option. The report generation process requires users to make three selections from dropdown menus: the relevant pay group, the payroll period, and the run number (where 0 represents the Main Run and numbered values 1, 2, etc. represent successive Supplementary Runs). After configuring these parameters and clicking Generate Report, users are directed to the Report Centre where they can open the completed report. This document is essential for payroll administrators and finance teams who need to verify nett pay calculations and review deduction order details for specific payroll cycles, helping them reconcile pay information and investigate discrepancies between different payroll reports. The related articles reference common issues such as mismatches between nett pay figures in different reports, negative net pay recovery scenarios, and validation problems with employee pay generation.

t: Review payroll messages
s:
Payroll messages provide you with detailed information to help identify and resolve potential errors before the period is closed. Messages will automatically generate a different stages of the payroll process with most generating after the Payroll Validation task has been run.
​
To learn how to revi...
ss: Payroll messages in PeopleXD flag potential errors at different stages of the payroll process, particularly after the Payroll Validation task runs. This guide walks you through reviewing messages in the Payroll Checking tab, determining whether action is needed for affected employees, and using the OneView tool to make corrections before closing the payroll period. Open this document when you need to identify errors, understand what actions specific messages require, and reprocess payroll to resolve flagged issues.
sl: This document explains how to review and action payroll messages in the Access Group payroll system, which automatically generate at various stages of the payroll process to help identify and resolve potential errors before the period closes. The primary workflow involves navigating to Manage Payroll, selecting a relevant pay group, clicking the Payroll Checking tab, and then selecting Payroll Messages to view affected employees. For messages that require no action, users can dismiss them by clicking the three-dot icon and selecting Dismiss All, while messages requiring corrections involve clicking View to open OneView for the affected employee and making the necessary changes. After taking corrective action, users return to the Payroll Messages screen via the breadcrumb, click the three-dot icon, and select Reprocess to update the message status and flag employees as having unprocessed changes. The document then directs users to re-run the relevant payroll task and review the updated message status, which will display as either Resolved (indicating the action worked) or Unresolved (indicating further action is needed). This process is typically used by payroll administrators and processors who need to validate and correct payroll data, and the document references the Enhanced Payroll Messaging and Unprocessed Employees user guide for further detailed guidance on specific message types and configurations.

sl: This document provides guidance on correctly reporting taxable payrolled benefits within FPS (Full Payment Submission) files to ensure compliance with HMRC reporting requirements. The document directs users to contact HMRC directly or consult their official website for comprehensive and detailed guidance on payroll reporting requirements if they need further clarification. Related resources mentioned include articles on removing old RTI FPS files, troubleshooting issues with FPS reports not generating to reporting centres, handling payroll car benefits, generating third-party EFT files, and resolving situations where a full payment submission file has been generated in error for an already-submitted payroll period.

t: Configure Intelligent Payslips
s:
Intelligent Payslips let employees view their upcoming payslip details through Employee Self-Service (ESS) before you process payment. This helps employees check their payment information early and raise any discrepancies with payroll before payday.

📌 Note: Payslip previews update when the Payroll ...
ss: Intelligent Payslips is a payroll feature in Employee Self-Service (ESS) that allows employees to preview their upcoming payslip details before payment is processed, helping them verify earnings, deductions, and net pay early. You enable this feature per pay group through the Payroll Dashboard, and once activated, employees can view their payslip preview on both the mobile app and employee dashboard. Open this document if you need to set up payslip previews for your organization, configure which pay groups should have this capability, or understand how employees access their preview payslips.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on configuring and using Intelligent Payslips, a feature within Employee Self-Service (ESS) that allows employees to preview their upcoming payslip details before payment processing occurs. The configuration process requires administrators to navigate to the Payroll Dashboard, access the Manage Payroll tab, locate the relevant pay group using the three-dot menu, and click Enable Preview Payslips to activate the feature for that pay group. Once enabled, employees can access their payslip previews through both the mobile app and employee dashboard by searching for and selecting My Payslips, then clicking Preview Payslip to review total earnings, total deductions, and net pay for the upcoming period. The document addresses specific scenarios such as blank payslip previews when employees have no payments for a period and the display of allowances and deductions as continuous lists rather than grouped items. To implement this feature, users must have appropriate menu options assigned: administrators require the "Update paygroup parameter" option in Web Services, while employees need access to "Get paygroup parameter," "Get payments periods," and "Get periods" options in Web Services and the Native App Payslips Preview module. This document is primarily intended for payroll administrators who configure pay group settings and support employees in managing their payment information, helping to reduce payroll discrepancies by allowing employees to identify and report issues before payday. The document also notes that payslip previews update when the Payroll Validation job runs, and it references related articles covering issues like incorrect pay rates and payslip display problems following manual payment cancellations.

Open this guide when you need to print or distribute payslips to specific employees or entire pay groups as part of your regular payroll process.
sl: This document provides a guide for retrieving payslips in bulk within a payroll system, designed to help users save time and reduce manual administrative work while ensuring employees receive their payroll documents efficiently. The process involves enabling the "Select specific Employees" toggle to choose which employees' payslips to retrieve, then activating both the "Copy payslip" and "Print Payslip Range" toggles before selecting the desired payroll periods and clicking Print. An important limitation is noted: users can retrieve yellow payslips in bulk for multiple periods, but blue payslips can only be retrieved for the most recent period, which affects how this feature can be used across different pay cycles. The document also references related troubleshooting resources, including an error message that appears when "No Payslips from your current pay group for the period being viewed," plus configuration guidance for payslip parameters, Portal release settings, and known display issues following manual payment cancellations. ss: Changing or removing an employee's leaving date in Portal allows you to correct exit information pulled from People Management before final payroll processing. You can amend or delete the end date directly from an employee's contract record using the Command Centre, as long as you haven't yet run Final Generate Salaries and Allowances. Open this document if an employee's departure date was entered incorrectly, their exit has been delayed, or you need to update their leaving information before payroll is finalized. Note that certain changes—like reporting an earlier date than originally submitted to HMRC—may not be possible depending on your payroll processing status.
sl: This document provides instructions for correcting or removing an employee's leaving date in Portal when the date has been entered incorrectly or the employee's exit has been delayed. The employee's leave date is imported from the People Management system, and amendments can be made at any time before the Final Generate Salaries and Allowances process is run. To amend the date, users navigate from the dashboard to People Management, then Dashboard, then use the Command Centre to View Employees, search for the specific employee by name, access their Contracts section, click Summary, and select either "Amend End Date" or "Delete End Date" from the three-dot icon menu. The document addresses specific scenarios where complications arise: if an employee has already been set to dormant status in payroll and a later leaving date needs to be reported, the employee must be rejoined and processed as a Leaver with the correct date; however, if an earlier leaving date needs to be reported, this is not possible because the original date has already been reported to Revenue/HMRC. The document also notes that if a "Payroll Closed for Processing" error appears, indicating that Final Generate Salaries has already been run, users must re-run the salaries and allowances process without selecting the final run option. This guide is primarily intended for payroll administrators or HR personnel in Portal who need to correct employee leaving dates before payroll finalisation.

t: Error: 'Cannot leave and rejoin in the same period'
s:
The above error occurs because you have attempted to process an employee as both a leaver and a rejoiner within the same payroll period, i.e. the employee is marked as a leaver, and before this process is completed fully, they are then marked as a rejoiner.

 

This action will cause the real-time i...
ss: The "Cannot leave and rejoin in the same period" error occurs when you attempt to process an employee as both a leaver and rejoiner within a single payroll period in PeopleXD, which causes RTI failures and incorrect reporting to HMRC or Revenue. Open this document if you're trying to rehire an employee who was recently marked as a leaver and need to understand why the system is blocking the rejoin action. The document explains that employees must become fully dormant by completing the current period before they can rejoin in the next payroll period, and provides step-by-step instructions for processing leavers and rejoiners correctly.
sl: This document explains the error message "Cannot leave and rejoin in the same period" that occurs in PeopleXD payroll software when an employee is marked as both a leaver and rejoiner within a single payroll period. The error arises because the system processes leave dates from previous periods during the period in which they are entered, which prevents rejoining an employee until the next payroll period begins. The primary consequence of attempting this action is that real-time information (RTI) submissions to HMRC in the UK or PAYE Mod file submissions to Revenue in Ireland will fail, resulting in incorrect reporting of the employee's leave date to tax authorities. To resolve this issue, users must first process the employee as a leaver and then run payroll through to the Complete Update job, which marks the employee as fully dormant on PeopleXD and generates a P45 document. Only after closing the current period and waiting for the next payroll period to begin can the employee be rejoined in the system. The document outlines the specific step-by-step process for leavers and rejoiners, and notes that as a workaround, users can treat the situation as continuous employment if an employee would otherwise experience a gap in payment. This guidance is relevant for payroll administrators and HR professionals who manage employee lifecycle changes in PeopleXD and need to ensure compliance with UK and Irish tax reporting requirements.

ss: When an employee's leave date has passed, they appear dormant in Personnel but may still show as active in the Payroll Dashboard until the system processes the change. Running a complete update in PeopleXD Payroll will sync the dormant status across both systems. Open this article if you need to understand why a leaver still appears active in Payroll, or if you need to manually update an employee's leaving date to trigger the status change. If the dormant status doesn't update after running the complete process, use this article to help you raise a support case with the correct reference information.
sl: This document addresses the discrepancy that occurs when an employee appears dormant in the Personnel system but still shows as active in the Payroll Dashboard. The issue arises because the employee's leave date is in the past, which triggers a dormant status change in Personnel, but this change has not yet been synchronized to PeopleXD Payroll. To resolve this synchronization issue, users should run the complete update process, after which the status in the Payroll Dashboard should automatically change to dormant to match the Personnel system. If the employee's leaving date needs adjustment, users can update it in the Back Office system and then run the complete update again. If the status still does not change to dormant after running the complete update, the document advises users to raise a new case online, referencing both the article title and the leaver's name to facilitate support investigation. The document is intended for payroll administrators and personnel staff who manage employee records across both the Personnel and PeopleXD Payroll systems and encounter situations where system statuses become inconsistent during the employee departure process.

t: Back Office: Make a payment to a leaver
s:
Sometimes, an employee who has left the organization and is marked as dormant in both CorePay and CorePersonnel may require an additional payment.

 

Since dormant employees cannot be paid directly, a temporary rejoin is necessary to process the payment.

 

Temporary rejoin

To rejoin the employee...
ss: Making a one-off payment to a former employee marked as dormant in CorePay and CorePersonnel requires a temporary rejoin process, since the system cannot process payments to dormant staff. Use the CorePay Employee portal to access Advanced Reference Features and set the employee's status to temporary rejoin by entering "Y" in the Temp Rejoin field. Open this document when you need to pay a leaver an additional amount after they've left the organization, or if you're processing backdated payments for former staff. Note that for migrated leavers, you'll need to verify that deductions and allowances have proper end dates to avoid unintended payments during the temporary rejoin period.
sl: This document provides guidance for processing additional payments to former employees who have left an organization and are marked as dormant in both CorePay and CorePersonnel systems. Since dormant employees cannot be paid directly through normal processes, the document explains the temporary rejoin procedure as the solution to enable payment processing. The process involves navigating to CorePay, selecting Employee, then accessing Advanced Reference Features and the Set Employee Status for an Employee screen, where users enter the employee's reference number, set the Temp Rejoin field to "Y", and save the changes without entering a rejoin date or clearing the leaving date. The document notes an important consideration for migrated leavers: while the system automatically terminates deductions, allowances, pensions, and benefits in kind for employees marked as leavers in CoreHR, manual verification is required for migrated leavers to ensure all deduction and allowance records have appropriate end dates, preventing unintended payments or deductions during the temporary rejoin. Users should be aware that during a temporary rejoin, the employee's cumulative values will not be reset because the process omits a rejoin date, which is the mechanism that triggers such resets—cumulative values only reset when an employee is fully rejoined and multiple periods of employment are enabled. This document is typically used by back office payroll or HR administrators who need to process one-off payments to former employees while maintaining the integrity of their dormant status in the system.

t: Portal access to the online P45 after an employee has left
s:

ss: Portal access to online P45 documents for departing employees is controlled through a leaver profile setup in the People Management and Security Dashboard sections. This process involves creating a dedicated leaver menu profile, configuring an access profile with the P45 widget enabled, and then assigning leaver access to individual employees so they can retrieve their tax documents after leaving the organisation. Open this document when you need to grant a former employee access to their P45 or P60, or if you need to prevent specific leavers from accessing these documents.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on setting up portal access for employees who have left an organisation to retrieve important tax documents, specifically their P45 form. The process requires creating a dedicated leaver menu profile by navigating to Security Dashboard, selecting Menu Profiles, and creating a new profile while removing access to features that leavers should not use. Configuration occurs through People Management > Data Centre > HR Admin Setup Settings > Access Profile Configuration, where administrators must create a new access profile, enter required details, check the Leaver Profile option, and assign the previously created leaver menu profile. The document also explains how to verify that the P45 widget is enabled by accessing Admin Dashboard > Site Manager > Dashboard Configuration and confirming the P45 widget is turned on and configured for the leaver menu profile. To assign leaver access to an employee, administrators navigate to People Management > Dashboard > Employees, search for the employee, and either click Task List-Leaver to assign access, or alternatively access the HR Tasks Lists through People Management > Data Centre > View All, select the Leaver tab, and use the Add function to select Assign Leaver Access from the Task drop-down menu. The document resolves a specific limitation by noting that the system does not support excluding individual employees from P45 access through standard release functionality, recommending instead that administrators remove or assign a different menu profile that excludes the P45 widget enabled to prevent access. This guidance is essential for HR administrators and payroll professionals who manage offboarding processes and need to provide appropriate document access to departing employees while maintaining security controls.

ss: Resolve FPS generation errors in PeopleXD by entering starter declarations for new or rejoined employees. Open this document if you're receiving an error message stating that starter declaration information is missing, or when onboarding new employees to ensure all required tax setup steps are completed.
sl: This document provides guidance on resolving a validation error that occurs when generating Full Payment Submission (FPS) reports in an Access Group payroll system, specifically when starter declaration information is missing for new or rejoined employees. In the Payroll Dashboard, users navigate to Employee, search for the relevant employee, click VIEW, then access Tax Details to enter the starter declaration before saving. Alternatively, in People Management, users select the People Management option from the dashboard menu, navigate to Dashboard, find the employee in the list, access their record, and complete the same Tax Details section with the starter declaration information. The document emphasizes that entering starter declarations is a critical step when setting up or processing rejoined employees within PeopleXD, and failure to complete this step will prevent FPS reports from generating successfully. This guidance is essential for payroll administrators and HR personnel responsible for employee onboarding and RTI (Real Time Information) compliance with HMRC requirements.

t: Process a deceased employee
s:

In the Portal, users navigate to People Management, locate the employee through the Employee search function, access the Sundry Profile, and toggle on the Deceased indicator under the Work Details tab before saving changes. The Back Office method involves accessing CorePay, selecting Employee followed by Advanced Employee Features, then using the Set Employment Status for an Employee function to enter the employee number, date of death, leaving date, and check the Deceased checkbox. For UK employees specifically, there may be an additional requirement to update the NI letter with HMRC as part of the termination process, with instructions provided to access Tax Details in the employee record. The document is designed for HR, payroll, and personnel administrators who need to properly close out an employee's record following their death, ensuring compliance with both internal systems and external regulatory requirements such as those from HMRC.

The rejoiner process follows a similar path through Manage Payroll > Inputs tab > Rejoiners, but includes an additional step allowing users to change an employee's pay group before rejoining by clicking the three dot icon and selecting Amend Pay Group, before applying default values, making amendments, and clicking Rejoin Selected Employees. The document notes that if the Joiners or Rejoiners options are unavailable, users should follow an awaiting approval process, indicating this is an enhanced feature that may not be enabled in all system configurations. Open this document when you're onboarding a new starter and need to bring them into Payroll so they can receive their first payment. sl: This document provides instructions for onboarding new employees into the payroll system by joining them to an appropriate pay group, which is a prerequisite for processing their pay and managing their information within the Payroll Dashboard. The process requires that any outstanding salary approvals be processed first, as employees with pending approvals will not appear in the joiner list and cannot be successfully added. The core task involves navigating to Manage Payroll, selecting the relevant pay group, accessing the Inputs tab, clicking Approvals, then using the Join tab to add the employee by clicking the Join button next to their name. Users must review and update employee details in the displayed fields before saving the changes to complete the joining process. The document notes that if the Approvals option is unavailable, users should follow an alternative enhanced joiners process instead. Once an employee is successfully joined to a pay group, their details become accessible and manageable through the Payroll Dashboard. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and HR personnel who need to onboard new starters and manage employee payroll records, and it references related processes including the joiners, leavers, and re-joiners user guide for additional context.

t: Second salary

ss: Second salary is automatically triggered in your payroll system when an employee changes post or appointment, moving them from their primary salary to a salary paid as an allowance with a PAY290_ALLOW source code. The system simultaneously maintains a zero-value PAY290 timesheet for retroactive calculation purposes and recalculates any arrears from the new appointment's effective date. Open this document if you need to understand how appointment changes affect salary processing, verify whether an employee is being paid as second salary in CorePay Enquiry, or troubleshoot salary and arrears issues following a post change.
sl: This document explains how the system handles salary processing when an employee undergoes a post or appointment change, automatically transitioning them from their Primary Salary to a second salary structure. When such a change occurs, the system generates two timesheet entries: a zero-value entry with source PAY290 (used for retroactive calculations against the old appointment) and an actual salary value with source PAY290_ALLOW (the new second salary paid based on the new appointment). The second salary pay code operates at the system level and second salary details do not appear on the Maintain Employee Position/Point or Maintain Personal Rates screens since they are held as allowances rather than standard salary records. To verify whether an employee is receiving a second salary, users access CorePay, select Enquiry, then View Timesheet Details to identify the two salary timesheets for the relevant period. The document distinguishes between primary appointments (created only when employees first join or rejoin the company) and secondary appointments (all subsequent appointments), with primary appointments having no end date but being automatically concluded by the effective date of the next salary line. The system automatically triggers retroactive adjustments from the new appointment's effective date, which may result in positive or negative arrears, and when an employee rejoins, their first appointment after rejoin restarts the entire process. This document is essential for payroll administrators and HR professionals who need to understand and verify second salary calculations and troubleshoot related salary processing issues.

t: Pro-rata salary and allowance calculations
s:
This provides an overview of PeopleXD’s standardized approach to calculating salaries and allowances for salaried employees, including how partial pay periods are managed.

 

Standard salary calculations
Monthly salary calculation

For salaried employees, PeopleXD calculates monthly salary by divid...
ss: PeopleXD calculates salaries and allowances for salaried employees using standardized methods based on annual salary divided by pay periods (12 months or 52 weeks), with special handling for partial pay periods when employees join mid-period, leave, or receive salary changes. When partial periods occur, the system pro-rates pay based on either working days or calendar days depending on your Pay Group's "Pay Salaries and Allowances on Days Worked" setting, and for weekly payrolls it factors in your Payroll Calendar Week End Date and any configured offset days. Open this document if you need to understand how PeopleXD calculates partial month or week payments, verify the exact formulas used for mid-period changes, or check which Pay Group settings affect your pro-rata calculations.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide to how PeopleXD calculates salaries and allowances for salaried employees, with particular focus on pro-rata calculations when partial pay periods occur. The system uses standardized formulas for standard salary calculations, dividing annual salaries by 12 for monthly pay or by 52 for weekly pay, but the pro-rata methodology depends entirely on the Pay Group configuration settings accessed via Settings › Pay Groups. When mid-period changes occur—such as employee joiners, leavers, or salary adjustments—PeopleXD automatically pro-rates compensation based on either working days or calendar days depending on whether the "Pay Salaries and Allowances on Days Worked" setting is enabled in the Pay Group. If enabled, the system calculates pro-rata pay using the formula Annual Salary ÷ Working Days in Year × Days Worked in Period, where working days are configured at the pay group level and viewable in Payroll Dashboard › Settings › Pay Groups › Days In Year; if disabled, it uses a calendar-day basis with the formula Period Salary ÷ Calendar Days in Period × Calendar Days at Each Rate. For weekly and fortnightly payrolls, the Payroll Calendar (found in Settings › Company Parameters › Calendar) determines the Week End Date, and any Offset Days configured in the Pay Group settings are added to or subtracted from this date to establish the actual pay period end. Percentage-based allowances operate as an exception to standard pro-rata rules, applying their percentage to relevant calculation elements whenever they are active within a period regardless of the number of days worked. The document warns that Pay Group settings are highly customizable and implemented specifically for each organization, making it essential to consult before modifying pro-rata settings to avoid unintended consequences on payroll calculations.

ss: The Temporary Reinstate process in PeopleXD allows you to make final payments to employees who have left the organisation or temporarily rejoined after a period away. Open this document if you need to process a payment to a former employee, add timesheets for their final settlement, or manage allowances and deductions before their record returns to dormant status.
sl: This document explains the Temporary Reinstate process in PeopleXD, which allows payroll administrators to issue final payments to employees who have left the organisation or temporarily rejoined after an absence. The process works by making a departed employee active for a single payroll period only, enabling settlement of outstanding wages, holiday pay, and contractual benefits without permanently reinstating them to the system. To use this feature, administrators first locate the employee record by navigating to Manage Payroll, selecting the relevant pay group, accessing the Inputs tab, clicking Manage Payroll Employees, and filtering the Status field from Active to Dormant, optionally using the Leave Date field to refine results. Once the employee record is found and displayed via the View option, administrators click Temporary Reinstate and review the employee's allowances, deductions, pensions, and benefits in kind (BIK), adding or amending these records as needed by clicking the corresponding tiles and completing the required fields. After temporarily reinstating the employee—whose status then changes to Active—administrators add timesheets through the Timesheets Current Period tab by clicking ADD, entering regular payments such as final wages as usual, and applying the NI Band Override field with a value of one only for irregular payments like bonuses or arrears to ensure correct National Insurance calculations. The document emphasises important considerations such as verifying that migrated leaver records have end dates on all deductions and allowances to prevent unintended payments, and noting that cumulative values are not reset for temporary rejoiners unless the employee is fully rejoined with multiple employment periods enabled. Once the timesheets are saved and the payroll process completes normally for the pay group, PeopleXD automatically returns the employee to dormant status when the new payroll period begins.

t: Incorrect AWE calculation for maternity pay (SMP)
s:

The incorrect calculation of SMP or SPP often arises from improperly configured pay days ...
ss: Statutory Maternity Pay (SMP) and Statutory Paternity Pay (SPP) calculations in CorePay may produce incorrect results when SSP/SMP pay days are not properly configured to match actual monthly pay dates. The system needs to accurately reference the 8-week period before the qualifying week, which requires correcting the monthly pay day settings in either the Portal (Settings > UK Tax Rates > Average Pay / Pay Days) or Back Office (CorePay > Reference > Maintain Statutory Pay Parameters). Open this document if SMP or SPP amounts appear incorrect, or if you need to configure pay day settings to ensure employees receive the right statutory entitlements. Note that configuration changes apply to new maternity leave instances going forward and won't retroactively correct existing maternity records.
sl: This document provides guidance for resolving incorrect Statutory Maternity Pay (SMP) and Statutory Paternity Pay (SPP) calculations in the Access Group payroll system, which is essential for maintaining compliance with UK statutory regulations and ensuring employees receive accurate entitlements. The core problem addressed is that SMP and SPP calculations often fail because pay days are improperly configured, causing the system to calculate earnings from incorrect payroll periods instead of the required 8 weeks before the qualifying week (defined as Sunday through Saturday). The document instructs users to correct SSP/SMP pay days through either the Portal interface (Settings > UK Tax Rates > General > Average Pay/Pay Days) or the Back Office system (CorePay > Reference > Maintain Statutory Pay Parameters > Average Pay/Pay Days > Maintain SSP/SMP Pay Days for Pay Group), ensuring the monthly pay day is set to the actual pay day rather than the last day of the month. Users are advised to test all changes in the UAT environment before applying them to the live system and to note that amendments will only affect new maternity leave instances, not existing retrospective records. After making these configuration changes, users should verify the corrected Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) calculation on the Maintain SMP Details screen to confirm the system now references the correct months. This document is primarily used by UK payroll administrators and HR professionals managing maternity and paternity pay in Access Group systems who encounter calculation discrepancies.

sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre provides troubleshooting guidance for payroll administrators and HR personnel who need to resolve issues where Statutory Maternity Pay (SMP) is not being generated for UK employees in the system. The document explains that SMP eligibility requires an employee to have been continuously employed for at least 26 weeks before the 15th week before the expected week of childbirth, and outlines several specific investigation steps to diagnose why SMP may not be generating. It describes how to verify and correct the 15th week date through two system interfaces: the Portal (accessed via Employee > View > Maintain Statutory > three-dot menu > Edit) and the Back Office (accessed via CorePay > Input > Statutory Pay > Maintain SMP Details). It also explains a key system limitation: when a maternity start date is changed to fall within an already-closed payroll period, the system will not generate retrospective payments or recalculate affected days, requiring manual adjustment instead. The document is designed for payroll and HR professionals managing maternity pay in Access Group's CorePay system who need to diagnose common reasons for SMP generation failures and apply appropriate system-level or manual corrections.

t: Sick pay calculating incorrectly or not transferring properly to payroll
s:
If sick pay is not calculating correctly or is sent to payroll in error; for example, when sick pay is unexpectedly paid after the entitlement has elapsed, or when sick pay is not being calculated, it is due to the employee no longer having their hours calculated on the Maintain Hours screen. 

 

T...
ss: Sick pay calculations in CoreTime can fail or transfer incorrectly to payroll when employees are assigned to work groups with Calculate Clockings disabled, preventing hours from being properly recorded on the Maintain Hours screen. This article helps you identify and fix the root cause using Back Office, with two resolution options: moving the employee to a work group with Calculate Clockings enabled, or enabling this setting on their existing work group. Open this document when sick pay is unexpectedly paid after entitlement has elapsed, isn't calculating at all, or appears to be sending to payroll in error. The fix involves accessing CoreTime System Params to adjust Work Group Parameters and recalculate hours for the affected calendar periods.
sl: This document addresses troubleshooting issues when sick pay calculates incorrectly or fails to transfer properly to payroll in Access Group's Back Office system, such as when sick pay is unexpectedly paid after entitlement has elapsed or when sick pay is not calculated at all. The root cause of these problems is typically that employees no longer have their hours calculated on the Maintain Hours screen, which occurs when an employee has been moved to a work group with Calculate Clockings disabled. The document provides two resolution options, both accessed through the Back Office menu path CoreTime > System Params > Work Groups > General Parameters - 2. The first solution involves moving the affected employee to a different work group that has Calculate Clockings enabled on the Work Group Parameters screen, while the second option involves enabling the Calculate Clockings setting on the employee's existing work group. Both approaches require recalculating hours for the relevant calendar periods after making the configuration change. The document notes that configuring the existing work group will affect all employees within that work group, making it important to consider the broader impact of this change. This guidance is essential for payroll administrators and HR professionals who manage time and attendance in Access Group systems and need to ensure accurate sick pay processing and payroll integration.

t: Ireland: Illness benefit and statutory sick leave 2024 changes
s:
The Department of Social Protection have published clarification, regarding waiting days treatment and aligning the treatment of social welfare waiting days with the statutory sick paid days.

What this means

For the first sickness of the year, there will be 5 waiting days applied.

For subsequent ...
ss: Ireland's Department of Social Protection has updated waiting day rules for illness benefit and statutory sick leave, now applying 5 waiting days for the first sickness of the year and 3 waiting days for subsequent illnesses. If you use PeopleXD's Social Welfare module, Access Group will automatically update your system to comply with these changes (non-production release April 3, 2024; production April 10, 2024). Sites managing social welfare manually or using custom software need to review their current processes and submit change requests to align with the new waiting day requirements. Open this document to understand the changes, confirm your release dates, and identify what actions your organization needs to take.
sl: This document explains Ireland's 2024 changes to illness benefit and statutory sick leave regulations published by the Department of Social Protection, specifically clarifying how waiting days are now treated and aligned between social welfare and statutory sick paid days. The key regulatory change implements 5 waiting days for the first sickness occurrence in a calendar year, with subsequent illnesses in the same year subject to only 3 waiting days. For organizations using the People XD Social Welfare module, Access Group will release software updates to automatically incorporate these changes, with non-production deployment scheduled for 3rd April 2024 and production deployment for 10th April 2024 to ensure regulatory compliance. Organizations managing social welfare processes manually are directed to review the Department of Social Protection's formal announcement and assess how these waiting day changes impact their existing manual procedures. For clients operating custom software solutions to manage social welfare and waiting days, any necessary adjustments should be submitted as formal change requests to their software provider. The document serves payroll administrators, HR teams, and finance professionals responsible for processing sick leave, managing social welfare claims, and ensuring compliance with Irish employment regulations in their respective organizations.

s:

ss: SMP (Statutory Maternity Pay) in PeopleXD Payroll does not automatically recalculate when an employee receives a pay increase during maternity leave. To comply with the Alabaster ruling, you can manually override the Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) figure in the Maintain Statutory section to reflect the employee's revised pay rate. Open this document when you need to update SMP calculations after a pay rise, or when you need to ensure correct maternity pay compliance in Portal. The new AWE figure will be used for SMP calculation once payroll is next run or validation is performed.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre explains how to manually adjust Statutory Maternity Pay (SMP) in PeopleXD Payroll when an employee receives a pay increase during maternity leave, as PeopleXD does not automatically update SMP calculations in these circumstances. The document addresses compliance with the Alabaster ruling by providing a step-by-step process to override the Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) figure, which is the key metric used to calculate SMP entitlements. Users navigate through the Portal interface by accessing the Employee section, searching for the relevant employee, and then clicking View followed by Maintain Statutory to locate the maternity leave record. Once the correct maternity leave record is identified and highlighted, users click the three-dot icon, select Edit, and manually enter the new AWE figure in the Average Weekly Earnings field before submitting the changes. The newly overridden AWE figure takes effect once payroll is processed or a single validation is performed against the employee's record, ensuring that future SMP calculations reflect the revised earnings rate. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and HR professionals who manage maternity leave cases in organisations using PeopleXD Payroll and need to ensure accurate SMP payments following employee pay increases during leave periods.

sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on the external timesheet take-on process, which allows users to import employee timesheets from external sources into the CorePay payroll system using either CSV or fixed file formats. The document specifies exact field requirements and ordering for timesheet data uploads, including 15 possible fields ranging from mandatory entries (Pay Group, Employee Number, Transaction Date, Pay Code, Hours/Days/Value, and Status) to optional fields like Project, Expense Code, Sub-Category, Appointment ID, and Hourly Rate of Pay, with detailed format specifications (character length, data type, and decimal place handling) for each. Upon completion, the system automatically generates a report viewable in the Report Centre that details all generated timesheets, validation errors, duplicate entries (defined as identical pay code, value, and transaction date combinations), and warning messages for missing or incorrect reference data like Cost Centre or Pay Code, with a specific note that file names cannot contain apostrophes to avoid system errors.

t: Input period is not correct for the current monthly payroll period
s:

ss: When your payroll calendar shows the wrong input period for a monthly payroll cycle, it causes timesheets and payroll periods to display incorrectly in CorePay. You can fix this by adjusting the Monthly Indicator setting in either Portal (via Settings > Company Parameters > Calendars) or Back Office (via CorePay > Reference > Payroll Calendar), but only for future or next payroll periods—current periods require you to raise a support case instead. Open this document if you need to correct a misaligned payroll calendar and want step-by-step instructions for updating the Monthly Indicator setting.
sl: This document explains how to resolve the issue where an incorrect input period for a pay group causes timesheets and the payroll calendar to display the wrong payroll period, a problem that stems from misconfiguration of the Monthly Indicator on the payroll calendar. The document provides step-by-step instructions for correcting the Monthly Indicator through two different system interfaces: the Portal (accessed via Settings > Company Parameters > Calendars) and Back Office (accessed via CorePay > Reference > Payroll Calendar). Users must first locate the current week number in the calendar and review the Monthly Indicator field to identify any errors, then update it as needed before saving. The document emphasizes critical restrictions based on which payroll period is being modified: changes cannot be made to past periods, the current payroll period requires raising a support case rather than making direct changes, the next payroll period can be updated but requires rerunning payroll jobs to ensure accuracy, and future payroll periods can be freely modified. Users are advised that they can only adjust the calendar to bring it forward; if rolling the period back is necessary, they must raise a new case online and reference this article's title. For situations where the input period or payroll period remains incorrect after these steps, users should submit a new support case providing specific details including the affected pay group(s) and the required input or payroll period.

ss: When running a payroll validation job in CorePay, you may encounter an error stating "Employee Has No Associated Timesheet Entries" if hours weren't generated despite the job previously succeeding. sl: This document addresses a specific error that occurs when running a validation job for a pay group in the payroll system that has previously worked correctly but fails to generate employee hours, and it provides troubleshooting guidance for multiple root causes. The document outlines five primary scenarios that can trigger this error: a change in the employee's pay frequency (such as from fortnightly to monthly), the absence of a recorded rate of pay for the employee, the employee being placed on positive input status, hours not being signed off in CoreTime for employees on positive input, and employment status being out of sync (such as a rejoin date remaining populated when the employee should be fully active). For configuration-related issues such as pay frequency changes or employment status mismatches, users are directed to raise a support case online while providing specific details including the affected employee's information, pay group, and pay period. For the missing rate of pay scenario, users can self-resolve by reviewing and confirming the employee's rate of pay setup, then re-running the Generate Salaries and Allowances (PAY290) job from the back office. To resolve positive input issues, users must navigate to CorePay > Employee > Maintain Employee Details to ensure employees designated to receive salary generation are not flagged on positive input status. For employees paid via CoreTime timesheets, hours must be confirmed and sent from CoreTime to ensure proper salary generation. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and support teams who manage employee compensation, timesheet processing, and payroll validation within the Access Group's payroll system, particularly when troubleshooting unexpected validation failures.

t: Hourly pay code not paying correct hourly rate
s:

ss: Hourly pay codes in CorePay can display incorrect rates due to system misconfigurations, outdated pay rate changes, or improper pay code assignments to employees. This article walks you through troubleshooting steps in both the Portal and Back Office, including checking the pay code source (PAY290_ALLOW or PAY290) and verifying whether the Composite Overtime indicator is incorrectly enabled. Open this guide when employees are receiving inaccurate hourly compensation and you need to identify whether the issue stems from pay code setup or timesheet source configuration.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving issues where hourly pay codes in a payroll system are not calculating or displaying the correct hourly rates for employees, which can result in inaccurate compensation. The document explains that such issues typically stem from payroll system misconfigurations, pay rate updates that were not properly applied, or incorrect assignment of pay codes to employee records. To diagnose the problem, users must first check the source of an employee's salary through either the Portal (by navigating to Employee, searching for the employee, clicking VIEW, then selecting Timesheet Current Period) or the Back Office (by clicking CorePay, then View Timesheet Details, and using the right arrow icon to view the source). The document specifically addresses whether the salary source is 'PAY290_ALLOW' or 'PAY290', as this determination affects the next troubleshooting steps. A key resolution involves checking the Composite Overtime indicator setting at the pay code level by accessing the Employee record, clicking VIEW, and navigating to the Allowance Tab to verify whether the indicator is selected. If the salary source is identified as PAY290_ALLOW, the document recommends switching to an hourly pay code that does not have the Composite Overtime Indicator enabled. The document further explains that the Composite Overtime Indicator and Overtime Element settings should only be selected when processing composite overtime (overtime calculated on basic pay plus additional elements like shift differentials or allowances) rather than overtime based solely on basic pay. Payroll administrators and HR personnel responsible for managing employee compensation and timesheet processing in the CorePay system would typically use this document to diagnose and correct pay code configuration errors.

The problem occurs when a PIR run takes an extended time to process, which subsequently causes the Payroll Validation process to fail, and this delay is attributed to a large accumulation of timesheets linked to that particular employee through the PIR system. The timesheets causing the issue are identified by their source codes Pay291 and Pay921NEG, which are specific timesheet source labels generated during the PIR process. The document is designed for payroll administrators and system users who encounter the PAY140 job stalling or validation failures and need to understand the root cause related to PIR timesheet volume. To resolve this issue, users are instructed to raise a new support case online, referencing the article title and providing specific details about which employee is affected, allowing the support team to investigate and address the underlying timesheet accumulation. t: Timesheets negated and re-created with PAY1721 reference
s:
Manually input timesheets will be negated and recreated when Pay Codes have the rule Allocate over Employee Cost Allocation enabled. This configuration allows an employee's manually input timesheets to be allocated over an employee's cost allocation record.
​
Timesheets excluded from this are system...
ss: PAY1721 automatically negates and recreates manually input timesheets when a Pay Code has the "Allocate over Employee Cost Allocation" rule enabled, distributing the timesheet across the employee's cost allocation records. This process applies only to manually entered timesheets and excludes system-generated entries from WFM, Positive Input Retrospection, and Salaries and Allowances tasks. Open this document if you need to understand how timesheet allocation works across cost centres or troubleshoot why your manually input timesheets are being recreated with PAY1721 references.
sl: This document explains the automatic negation and recreation of manually input timesheets in the payroll system when specific configuration rules are enabled. The process is triggered when Pay Codes have the "Allocate over Employee Cost Allocation" rule enabled, which allows manual timesheets to be distributed across an employee's cost allocation records. The PAY1721 program executes this process by negating the original timesheet entry and recreating it with a PAY1721 reference across the range of cost centres specified in the employee's cost allocation record. System-generated timesheets from WFM (Workforce Management), Positive Input Retrospection, and the Salaries and Allowances task are excluded from this automatic negation and recreation process. The PAY1721 program will perform this negation and recreation even if the employee does not have an active cost allocation record assigned. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and HR professionals who manage timesheet allocations and need to understand how the system handles cost centre distribution for manually entered timesheets. The content serves as a reference for understanding the technical behavior and configuration settings that affect timesheet processing in the Access Group payroll system.

sl: This document explains how pay code types affect timesheet payment calculations within the Access Group system, specifically addressing a critical distinction in how allowance-type pay codes are processed. The document describes a counterintuitive calculation behavior where pay codes configured with type 'Allowance' and subset type 'Days' or 'Hours' calculate payments based on full-time equivalents rather than using the employee's individual multiplier, which can lead to incorrect payment amounts if not properly understood. To investigate or verify pay code configurations, users can navigate to Settings then Pay Codes in Portal to view both the pay code type and subset type for any codes in the system. ss: Updating an employee's appointment end date in PeopleXD People Management helps you correct or remove leave dates that have changed or were added in error. sl: This document provides instructions for amending or removing an employee's appointment end date within the PeopleXD People Management system, addressing situations where leave dates have changed or were entered incorrectly. The process involves navigating from the dashboard menu to People Management, then accessing the Command Centre to locate and view the specific employee's record. Users must then access the Contracts section, select the relevant contract from the three-dot menu (particularly important if the employee has multiple contracts), and choose the "Amend End Date" option. The amendment allows users to either enter a new end date or use the "Delete End Date" toggle to remove the date entirely, followed by clicking OK and Save to confirm changes. A critical prerequisite is that this process only works if the employee has not yet been processed as a leaver in PeopleXD Payroll; if they have already been processed, the employee must be rehired with a start date immediately following the incorrect end date instead. This document is primarily used by HR and payroll administrators who need to correct employee contract dates before final payroll processing occurs, and it references related guidance on contract start date corrections and constraints that apply once salary generation has been run in final mode.

ss: Switching an incorrectly assigned post in PeopleXD People Management allows you to reassign an employee to a different post while keeping their appointment ID intact. Use this process when an employee has only one post and needs to be moved to a new one—the post number and sequence will automatically update to reflect the change. Open this document if you need step-by-step instructions for deleting the current contract and creating a new one in PeopleXD, or if you're unsure whether salary updates will be required after the switch.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre provides instructions for reassigning an employee to a different post within the PeopleXD People Management system when they currently hold only one position. The process involves navigating to Command Centre, selecting View next to Employees, and searching for the specific employee before accessing their contract details. Users must locate the Contracts section, access the Summary area via the three-dot menu, and delete the current contract by confirming the deletion. After removing the old contract, users select the new post they wish to assign, proceed through the next steps, make any necessary adjustments to the employee's details, and verify that all contract information is accurate before saving. The system automatically retains the employee's existing appointment ID while updating the post number and post sequence to reflect the new assignment. Users should be aware that depending on the modifications made during the switching process, the system may require them to update the employee's salary information as a final step. This document is designed for HR administrators and people management professionals who need to reassign employees between posts while maintaining continuity in their employment records.

Open this guide when you need to correct or update when an employee's contract began, keeping in mind that earlier start dates require checking the underlying post's effective date to avoid system errors. The process includes built-in review steps to ensure all affected contract details are properly updated before saving.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for amending an employee's contract start date within the Portal system, specifically through the Command Centre interface. Users access the functionality by navigating to Command Centre, selecting an employee via the Employees VIEW option, accessing the Contracts section, and clicking the three-dot menu next to Summary to select Amend Contract Start Date. When a start date is changed, the system automatically reviews and may update multiple associated contract elements including Salary, Allowance, Cost allocations, Pension, BIK, Deductions, Substantive date, and Organisational roles, with each flagged for user review and the system indicating which details will be updated. A critical warning advises that if the new start date is earlier than the current date, users must check the underlying post's effective date to avoid receiving an error message stating the start date cannot be amended due to the post's effective date restriction. This document is essential for HR administrators and Portal users who need to correct employee contract start dates while understanding system limitations and the cascading updates that occur.

sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for removing contracts or contract amendments from an employee's record in the Portal system, typically when they have been added in error. The document includes important restrictions, such as the inability to remove a contract if it is the only or substantive contract on file—in which case users must switch the post instead—and notes that deleted contracts cannot be restored. t: Rules for deleting appointments
s:
Whilst the system includes functionality to delete appointments, it will prevent their removal if it has a detrimental impact elsewhere.

 

Posts that can be deleted

A primary ended post where the appointment isn't the first sequence in the post. I.e., the appointment ID varies from post number, h...
ss: Deleting appointments in PeopleXD requires understanding which post types the system allows you to remove. You can delete primary ended posts (where the appointment isn't the first in sequence), primary confirmed future posts, and secondary appointed or ended posts—but you cannot delete commenced posts, primary appointed posts, or ended posts that are the first sequence in their post. Open this document when you need to remove an appointment and want to know whether the system will allow it based on the post status and sequence rules, or when you're troubleshooting a deletion error.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre explains the rules governing when appointments can and cannot be deleted within the system, detailing the constraints that prevent removal of appointments when doing so would negatively impact other system functions. The document specifies which types of posts are eligible for deletion, including primary ended posts where the appointment is not the first sequence in the post (identified by a varying appointment ID such as 001234-1 when the post sequence is 2), primary confirmed future posts, secondary appointed posts, secondary ended posts meeting the primary ended appointment conditions, and secondary confirmed future posts. Conversely, it identifies posts that cannot be deleted under any circumstances: any commenced post, primary appointed posts, and primary or secondary ended posts where the appointment represents the first or only sequence within the post (such as post 000123 with sequence 1 and appointment ID 000123-1 with ended status). The system uses specific identifiers including post numbers, post sequences, appointment IDs, and appointment statuses to determine deletion eligibility, with the status field (such as "EN" for ended) playing a key role in these rules. This document is intended for users of Access Group's substantive appointment software who need to manage posts and appointments in the Back Office environment and encounter situations where they need to remove or modify appointment records. The document references related functionality such as removing vacant posts from the Org Chart, generating employee status reports, and creating historic appointment amendments, indicating it serves users managing organizational structures and employee records.

ss: Deleting an employee set up in error involves marking them for deletion in People Management's Command Centre, a process that completes overnight through an automated job. Before deletion, you should know that employees cannot be removed if their salary has already been paid or if WFM transactions exist on their record, and you'll need update webservice access to perform this action. Open this document if you need step-by-step instructions for marking an employee for deletion, or if you need to undo a deletion before the nightly processing job runs.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on deleting employee records in the People Management system, including the deletion process, important restrictions, and how to reverse a deletion if needed. Users must have access to update records, controlled through the update webservice menu option, in order to perform employee deletions. The document outlines the specific steps to delete an employee: navigate to the People Management dashboard, click the Command Centre tab, select View next to Employee, search for the employee, expand the Actions menu, and click Delete Person, then confirm with Yes to mark the employee for deletion and assign them a "deleting" status. Critical restrictions prevent deletion if the employee's salary has already been paid or if WFM transactions exist on their record, and deletion is also blocked if an appointment has only one sequence remaining after the proposed deletion. The document also covers how to undo an employee deletion before the nightly job executes by accessing the employee's record, expanding the Actions menu, clicking Undo Delete Person, and confirming the action. This resource is intended for People Management administrators and HR personnel responsible for managing employee records who need to remove employees set up in error or no longer required in the system.

ss: The Data Migration Update Facility lets you make bulk updates to employee records, contract records, and reference data in your system. For employees, you can update bank details, contacts, expense codes, probation details, shift assignments, and sickness categories; for contracts, you can update fields like job title, location, cost centre, employee status, and reporting manager; you can also update descriptions and settings for reference items like cost centres, pay codes, shift types, and work groups. Open this document when you need to make widespread changes across multiple employee or contract records at once, or when updating standard reference data fields in bulk rather than one record at a time.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on using the Data Migration Update Facility to perform bulk updates across three categories of data: employee records, contract records, and reference data items. For employee updates, the facility allows bulk modification of fields prefixed with 'Person -', including bank details (sort code, BIC, IBAN, account number, and Credit Union reference), contacts (mobile, email, and other assigned contact types), expense codes, home phone numbers, input locations for Payroll, pay code group assignments, probation details (expiry date, extension date, completion date, reason codes, and review dates), shift details (shift type and effective date), and sickness category codes. Contract record updates, identified by the 'Contract -' prefix in the widget, enable bulk changes to critical employment data such as Category, Cost Centre, Employee Status and Sub Status, FTE, Job Category, Job Title, Location, Project, Reports To (manager assignment), Sub Category, and Work Group. Reference data updates with the 'Reference -' prefix allow administrators to modify descriptions and configuration settings for Cost Centre Codes, Pay Codes, Shift Type Codes (including description, sequence, up to seven pattern codes, and dormant status), and Work Groups (description, shift, and holiday scheme assignments). This facility is designed for HR and payroll administrators who need to make systematic changes across multiple employee or contract records simultaneously, avoiding manual individual record updates and reducing the risk of inconsistencies. The document serves as a reference guide that specifies exactly which fields within each category can be bulk updated and what data elements are modifiable for each update type.

ss: Overriding system-generated continuous service values in the Portal allows you to manually adjust an employee's continuous service start and end dates when the system calculation doesn't reflect the correct service period. You would use this process when an employee has breaks in service, transfers between eligible and ineligible posts, or other circumstances that require the continuous service dates to be corrected in the Override Start Date and Override End Date fields. Access the employee's Service Details through Command Centre to review the current system-calculated dates and make manual adjustments as needed. This is essential for ensuring accurate service entitlements are maintained during complex employment scenarios involving career breaks or post transfers.
sl: This document explains how to override system-generated continuous service values in the Portal, specifically addressing how eligibility rules affect an employee's continuous service start date when breaks in service occur. The document details the system's automatic behavior: if a break in service is shorter than the number of days defined in eligible service rules, the continuous service start date remains unchanged, but if the break exceeds the defined threshold, the start date resets to the new post appointment's commencement date. It also covers scenarios where employees transfer into ineligible posts (which sets continuous service entitlements to zero) and then transfer back into eligible posts (which resets the service start date according to service rules). The document provides step-by-step instructions for manually updating continuous service dates through the Portal interface: users navigate to Command Centre, select View next to Employees, search for and view the relevant employee, access Key Information to review Service Details, and then update the Override Start Date and/or Override End Date fields before saving. This document is primarily used by HR administrators and payroll professionals who need to correct or adjust continuous service calculations when system-generated dates don't reflect an employee's actual service history due to breaks, transfers between eligible and ineligible posts, or other service interruptions. The related articles referenced suggest this functionality is part of a broader continuous service management system that integrates with employee records and career break management features.

t: Using continuous service
s:
A nightly database job calculates continuous service for employees, based on the eligible service rules defined in the system. When an employee meets the rule criteria, the system stores a continuous service start date for them. Service rules can be managed via either the portal or the back office.

ss: Continuous service in CorePersonnel is automatically calculated nightly based on eligible service rules you define, which determine when an employee's continuous service period starts and ends. You can configure these rules through either the portal (Data Centre > Eligible Service Rules) or back office (CorePersonnel > Reference > Service Rules), setting up to 3 reference criteria and defining whether break days between appointments should be included or excluded. The system recalculates continuous service dates whenever a post appointment is commenced, updated, or ended, and you can manually override these dates or enter TUPE dates if needed. Open this document when you need to set up or modify how continuous service is tracked for your employees, or when you need to understand what triggers a recalculation of these dates.
sl: This document describes how continuous service is calculated and configured in an HR system through an automated nightly database job that applies eligible service rules to determine when employees have met continuous service criteria. Users can configure these service rules through two pathways: the portal by navigating to Data Centre > View All > Eligible Service Rules and selecting Continuous Service, or the back office by going to CorePersonnel > Reference > Reference Q - Z > Service Rules > Eligible Service Rules and selecting Continuous Service. The configuration matrix allows administrators to set up to three references linked to organizational hierarchy, with dropdown selections that dynamically populate relevant reference data codes, and includes critical parameters such as Break in Service (which defines days between appointments that don't interrupt service), Length of Service options to include or exclude break days, and both Eligible and Active indicators to control whether rules count toward continuous service. The system automatically triggers continuous service recalculations when post appointments are commenced, updated, or ended, though confirmed future appointments do not affect calculations until they actually commence. The document also explains that continuous service dates can be manually overridden and influenced by TUPE dates, with displayed start dates following a specific precedence order of rule-calculated dates, TUPE dates, or override dates, and end dates similarly determined by rule calculations or override entries. This configuration document is intended for HR administrators and system managers who need to set up and maintain continuous service rules to ensure accurate calculation of employee service duration for compliance and benefits administration purposes.

t: Target end date and planned end date differences
s:
Target end date

This is the end date that can be entered against an employee's record. This is an estimated date that can be revised as the time approaches. EMS Notifications can be set up against this field, however, this is not an actual end date and the employee will not finish automatically on ...
ss: Target end date and planned end date are two distinct fields in employee records that serve different purposes in your HR and payroll system. The target end date is an estimated, revisable date used for notifications and reporting, while the planned end date marks when an appointment or role is expected to end based on project or job completion. Open this document if you need to understand the difference between these fields, set up leaver notifications, or troubleshoot end date amendments in your payroll process. This is essential reading if you're managing employee departures or trying to resolve issues with end date changes after payroll processing.
sl: This document explains the distinction between two different end date fields in the HR system: the target end date and the planned end date, clarifying their purposes, functionality, and how they interact with other system processes. The target end date is a flexible, estimated date that can be entered and revised on an employee's record and can trigger EMS Notifications for reminder purposes, but it does not automatically terminate employment or represent an actual end date. The planned end date, by contrast, is the expected conclusion date for an appointment, post, job, role, or project and is consistently applied across all instances of that appointment regardless of the actual end date that may occur. The document serves administrators, HR personnel, and payroll staff who manage employee lifecycle events and need to understand why these two distinct date fields exist and how they function independently. Related guidance covers the practical process of updating appointment end dates through both the Portal and Back Office systems, as well as addressing complications that arise when end dates cannot be removed after payroll processing or amended after salary generation has run in final mode. This document is most relevant when managing leavers, setting up employment notifications, or troubleshooting scenarios where end date modifications fail due to payroll or salary processing constraints.

t: Overview of substantive appointment software
s:
Introducing substantive appointments to the system also introduces several advantages and new terminology. These are outlined below.

 

Appointment IDs

It's important to clarify what an Appointment ID is. 

An appointment represents a contract an employee has with an organisation.

Each Appointmen...
ss: Substantive appointment software manages employee contracts and appointment IDs within your HR system, replacing the older primary and secondary appointment terminology with "substantive" and "non-substantive" designations. It ensures appointment IDs remain stable throughout an employee's tenure even when contracts are updated, while preserving holiday balances in Workforce Management and maintaining accurate HESA reporting. Open this document if you need to understand how appointment IDs work, how the system handles multiple contracts for a single employee, or what happens to appointments when employees are promoted, rehired, or leave the organization.
sl: This document provides an overview of substantive appointment software, explaining the fundamental concepts, terminology changes, and operational advantages introduced by this system within an HR management platform. The document clarifies that an Appointment ID is a unique identifier combining a post number and post sequence (for example, post no. 000123 with post seq. 1 creates appointment ID 000123-1) and that this ID remains constant throughout the lifetime of a single contract, even when the sequence increments due to contract updates. Key advantages of substantive appointments include preventing appointment ID changes during promotion scenarios, retaining employee holiday balances in Workforce Management, automatically assigning a new substantive appointment based on the next highest FTE when the current one ends, and ensuring correct HESA reporting. The software introduces new terminology where "Primary appointments" are now called "Substantive" and "Secondary appointments" are called "Non-Substantive," while allowing the substantive indicator to be overwritten when required. The document covers multiple employee scenarios including new starters (whose first appointment is substantive), ending or leaving employees, ending individual appointments (which also terminates associated elements like allowances, pensions, and cost allocation records), and re-hired employees (whose first new appointment becomes substantive). System administrators and HR personnel use this document when implementing substantive appointments, managing appointment lifecycles through Back Office functions like making substantive posts or replacing existing appointments, and resolving issues where appointment IDs previously changed during promotion or contract modifications.

Each field amendment must be saved individually by clicking the Save icon, as the system does not allow multiple fields to be changed and saved simultaneously. t: Recommended procedure for setting up an unpaid career break post
s:
