ss: Setting up an unpaid career break in CorePersonnel requires ending an employee's current appointment and creating a new planned appointment with "Career Break Unpaid" as the post title, while ensuring the employee is appointed but not commenced on payroll. This process allows the employee to receive a P45 and remain dormant in payroll while still appearing in the system as an appointed employee for reporting purposes. Use Post Management in CorePersonnel to create the new appointment, set the Sub Status to "Career Break," enter the target return date, and leave the appointment in "Appointed" status rather than "Commenced." Open this document when you need to process an employee going on unpaid leave and need to manage both their payroll cessation and their continued appointment record.
sl: This document provides a detailed procedure for setting up an unpaid career break post within the Access Group HR and payroll system, enabling employees to take career breaks while maintaining their appointment records for reporting purposes. The objective is to create a situation where an employee receives a P45 and becomes dormant on payroll (by ending their current appointment) while simultaneously being appointed to a new "Career Break Unpaid" post that remains active but uncommenced in the system. The procedure begins by navigating to CorePersonnel, Maintenance, Post Management, Post Profile Maintenance, where users select a valid post title from the list of values and click the red tick icon to populate post details. Key steps include selecting the relevant appointment, using the Appoint Person option to establish a Target End Date for when the employee will return, and configuring the Hierarchy screen with appropriate job titles, employee status, and critically, entering "Career Break" in the Sub Status field. The appointment must be left in "Appointed" status rather than "Commenced" to ensure the person does not appear as live on payroll, and the Pension Indicator should remain unticked. Critical success factors emphasize that HR must communicate with payroll to confirm the employee's payroll termination and P45 requirement, while the new appointment serves purely for administrative and reporting visibility of the employee's continued connection to the organization.

ss: Amending the Post FTE value in CorePersonnel allows you to update the sanctioned headcount allocated to a specific position in your organisation. You can increase or decrease FTE using the Maintain FTE option in Post Profile Maintenance, either by transferring FTE from another post or by adding/subtracting from the current value. Open this document when you need to adjust budgeted headcount for a role, record the change with an effective date and approval details, and maintain a system history of all FTE amendments. Note that the maximum FTE per post is 999; if you're approaching this limit, you'll need to create a new post instead.
sl: This document provides guidance for amending the Full-Time Equivalent (FTE) headcount value assigned to a post profile record in both the portal and back office environments within the CorePersonnel system. The Post FTE field captures the sanctioned or budgeted headcount for a specific position in the organisation, and because audit trails are maintained to record when updates were made and by whom, the field cannot be directly overwritten but must be amended through designated processes. Two FTE update methods are available: Transfer FTE allows users to reallocate FTE from one Post Profile to another, while Update FTE provides a straightforward addition or subtraction from the current value without affecting other posts. To update the Post FTE in the portal, users must navigate to the Post Profile Maintenance screen, select option 09 - Maintain FTE, choose the Update option, enter an Effective Date (which cannot be earlier than the Post Profile Effective Date), input the amendment amount as a positive value to increase or negative value to decrease the FTE, enter an Approved By name and role, and click Save. The back office process follows a similar path by clicking CorePersonnel, Maintenance, Post Management, Post Profile Maintenance, then selecting Maintain FTE and Update FTE option, with the same mandatory fields for Effective Date and Approved By information. The document notes that the maximum FTE applicable to a single post is 999, and if this limit is approached, a new post must be created in the portal or back office rather than continuing to amend the existing post.

ss: Creating a new post profile record in Back Office involves navigating CorePersonnel's Post Management module and entering key organizational details such as post title, effective date, post type, structure code, company, management unit, and department. The process also allows you to populate optional fields like pay scale, job description, reporting structure, FTE (full-time equivalence), and estimated annual cost, with the system automatically generating a unique Post Number upon save. Open this document when you need to set up a new position in your organization's structure, whether for recruitment purposes, organizational planning, or payroll setup. This is essential for HR administrators and recruiters who manage organizational hierarchies and job openings in the CorePersonnel system.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for creating a new post profile record in the Back Office system, specifically through the CorePersonnel module accessed via Maintenance > Post Management > Post Profile Maintenance > New. The process requires users to populate multiple required and optional fields, beginning with selecting a Post Title from the List of Values (LOV), entering an Effective Date, and choosing a Post Type and Structure Code from their respective LOVs. Users must then navigate through additional mandatory fields including Company, Management Unit, and Department by using the Tab key and selecting values from the available LOVs for each. The document describes numerous optional fields that can be completed depending on implementation requirements, including Category, Sub Category, Pay Scale, Requisition Number, Post Analysis Code, Report to Post (for establishing reporting hierarchies), Estimated Annual Cost, Job Description (which can integrate with E-recruitment systems), and Comments (with guidance to include user initials, date, and description). A critical field is FTE (Full-Time Equivalence), where users enter values such as 1.0 to indicate a full-time post. Upon clicking Save, the system automatically generates a unique Post Number that identifies the post record. This document is used by Back Office administrators and personnel management staff who need to establish new posts within the CorePersonnel system during implementation or ongoing organizational changes.

Open this document if you're creating or updating a substantive post assignment and need to resolve the appointment date mismatch by checking the Appointment History and Substantive Maintenance screens. Follow the steps to verify appointment records exist and enter the correct substantive dates to complete your setup.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses a specific error that occurs when a Primary Appointment cannot be set up with an active status on a specified date. To resolve the issue, users must enter a new Substantive Post by inputting the appropriate Substantive Date, typically corresponding to either when the post commenced or when it became the employee's substantive post. The process then requires selecting the relevant Appointment ID from the system's List of Values (LOV) and tabbing across to link the records before saving the changes. This document is primarily used by HR and payroll administrators who manage employee appointments and post assignments within the Access Group back office system, particularly when encountering appointment setup failures related to missing or conflicting substantive post dates. t: Back Office: Manager unable to access all employees
s:
The manager requires their work group to be appointed correctly via the Person Maintenance screen. To update the employee's work group so the employee will appear in the portal, follow the below steps.

Click CorePersonnel, then click Maintenance.

ss: When a manager cannot see employees in the Back Office portal, the issue is often that work groups haven't been correctly assigned in CorePersonnel. Open the Person Maintenance screen, navigate to the employee's Appointment History, and update their Work Group assignment through the Drill Down function—this ensures the employee appears in the manager's view. Use this guide when employees are missing from a manager's team or portal display despite being active in the system.
sl: This document provides guidance on resolving access issues where a manager cannot view all employees in the system due to improper work group configuration. The issue stems from the manager's work group not being correctly appointed through the Person Maintenance screen in CorePersonnel, which prevents employees from appearing in the portal. The solution involves navigating to CorePersonnel > Maintenance > Appointment History, entering the relevant Personnel No., and accessing the commenced appointment via the Drill Down function. Users must then locate and double-click the commenced sequence to update the Work Group field with the correct assignment. The process requires clicking OK multiple times—a minimum of two times and possibly three—to ensure the changes are saved and take effect. This document is typically used by system administrators or back office personnel who manage employee records and need to troubleshoot visibility issues when managers report missing employees in portal views or team scheduler functions.

t: Back Office: Bulk ending appointments and processing leavers
s:
The functionality to bulk end appointments and process employees as leavers exists in Back Office on the Bulk Update Leaver screen. To use this functionality, follow the steps below.

📌Note: The above screen remains open for customers in the back office until the equivalent functionality is created ...
ss: Bulk ending appointments and processing employees as leavers is handled through the Bulk Update Leaver screen in Back Office, accessed via CorePersonnel > Maintenance > Bulk Update Processing. Use this tool when you need to efficiently process multiple employee departures at once by searching for employees by filters, selecting their appointments, and entering leaving details. The system automatically determines whether to process an employee as a leaver based on whether all their commenced appointments are selected—if an employee has multiple appointments but only some are selected, only those appointments end and the employee remains active. Open this document when you're managing multiple staff departures and need to understand how the bulk processing logic handles single versus multiple appointments.
sl: This document provides instructions for using the Bulk Update Leaver functionality in Access Group's Back Office system, which allows users to end multiple employee appointments and process them as leavers simultaneously. The process begins by navigating to CorePersonnel, selecting Maintenance, then choosing Bulk Update Processing - Main Screen and selecting "Leaver" from the Select Action dropdown menu. Users then access the Bulk Update Leaver screen where they can search for employees using filters and select relevant employees and their appointments by ticking the Select checkbox or using the Select All button. Once employees are selected, users click Update Selected, enter the leaving details, and confirm the update. The tool's processing logic differs depending on the number of appointments: if an employee has only one commenced appointment, they are automatically processed as a leaver; however, if an employee has multiple commenced appointments, they are only processed as a leaver if all their appointments are selected—if some appointments remain unselected, only those selected appointments are ended while the employee retains open appointments and is not processed as a leaver. This functionality is currently available in Back Office pending the creation of equivalent functionality in the portal. The document is designed for back office administrators and HR personnel who need to efficiently manage bulk employee departures and appointment terminations rather than processing them individually.

t: Back Office: Creating a historic appointment / contract amendment for an employee
s:
A historic appointment is used to reflect an employee's movements in an organisation and to offer a complete history. It is entered retrospectively via the Appointment History screen in Personnel.

 

Why create an historic appointment?

One can be created for an employee whose appointment history s...
ss: Creating a historic appointment in Back Office's Appointment History screen lets you record an employee's past role changes and ensure their appointment history accurately reflects their employment journey. Use this process when an employee's record needs to show previous positions they held (for example, working part-time before transitioning to full-time in a different role). You'll need to adjust existing appointment dates to create a gap, then use the Create Historic Sequence button to add the retrospective appointment with the correct post, start date, end date, and salary details. Open this document when you're correcting incomplete appointment records or documenting historical role movements that didn't get recorded when they originally occurred.
sl: This document provides guidance on creating historic appointments in the Access Group back office system, which allows HR professionals to retrospectively record an employee's past job movements and build a complete appointment history within Personnel records. The process is accessed through Back Office > Core Personnel > Maintenance > Appointment History, where users query a personnel number and navigate the Appointment History screen to view and modify existing employment records. To create a historic appointment, users must first establish a gap in the employee's current appointment history by adjusting end dates on existing posts, then use the Create Historic Sequence button to input the historic post details including the Post Number, mandatory start and end dates, and any applicable salary information. The system includes validation checks that will confirm successful creation with a Generated Sequence number message, and automatically populates salary details if existing records match the post's date range, though entered salary details do not flow through to the Pay system unless specifically configured. The document addresses common errors including "Start Date must be within the Start and End Dates for this Appointment ID" (which occurs when no employment gap has been created) and "Appointment Record Cannot Exist Before Person Started" (which occurs when attempting to backdate beyond an employee's original start date), recommending users employ the standard Amend Appointment functionality instead when these errors occur. This functionality is primarily used by back office HR administrators who need to correct incomplete appointment histories or record employees' past role transitions, such as documenting a period of part-time work followed by a full-time promotion.

ss: The "Query caused no records to be retrieved" error in CorePersonnel occurs when users cannot find or access employee records in the Personnel Profile screen or Search function. This can happen for multiple reasons, including insufficient user access permissions to the employee, the employee being dormant or marked as a temporary rejoiner in CorePay, missing or corrupted employee data, or system parameter settings that restrict visibility. Open this document when an employee record fails to appear in search results or when you need to troubleshoot why a user cannot view a specific employee's details in CorePersonnel, even though the employee exists in the system.
sl: This Access Group Help Centre document provides comprehensive troubleshooting guidance for the "Query caused no records to be retrieved" error that users encounter in CorePersonnel when searching for or accessing employee records. The document addresses multiple root causes of this error and outlines specific resolution steps for each scenario, including issues related to user access permissions controlled via the CorePersonnel System User screen, dormant employee status (which requires selecting Dormant or All employees search options), missing or corrupt employee data on CorePersonnel tables, and employees set as temporary rejoinders in CorePay using the Set Employee Status screen. Additional causes covered include incorrect date entries in employee records (such as year 2105 instead of 2015), inactive home addresses, cancelled substantive records on the Substantive Maintenance screen, and employees assigned to sensitive departments that the user lacks access to. The document also explains how a Client Parameters setting in CorePersonnel Reference Q-Z System Parameters Advanced can restrict access to employees when the "Hide all information when viewing employees you no longer have access to" parameter is enabled, and provides navigation paths for disabling this setting in both Back Office and the Data Centre portal. For complex data issues that cannot be resolved through these standard troubleshooting steps, the document instructs users to raise a new support case while referencing the article title and providing relevant details such as the username and employee personnel number.

Open this guide when you need to move an employee to a different post or position without creating a new hire record, and follow the 2-step wizard to complete appointment and salary details.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for replacing an existing appointment for an employee within the CorePersonnel system's Back Office module. The process begins by navigating to CorePersonnel, Maintenance, Personal Profile, then New Appointments, and selecting the Posts tab to query for an Authorised Post Appointment and search for the existing employee. The document clarifies that no Transfer Details are required when replacing an appointment in this scenario, distinguishing this process from other appointment-related tasks. Users must complete a two-step wizard to enter the employee's Appointment and Salary Details, including typing the Commenced Date on the Appointment Details page, after which the new Post Appointment will display on the Appointments list. The document notes that the Substantive Date should remain unpopulated for the new Post Appointment but will be automatically populated for the earlier existing Post Appointment with the Start Date of the replacement Post Appointment. This guide is intended for back office administrators managing employee appointments and may be followed by the Salary Approval process if applicable to the organization's configuration.

sl: This document provides guidance for resolving an "Invalid Payroll Status, Cannot Process Employee" error that users encounter when an employee record contains a payroll status that the system cannot process. The error occurs when the payroll status associated with an employee is not recognized or accepted by the system's validation rules. To troubleshoot this issue, users must retrieve the employee's status report and carefully document the Payroll Status field shown in that report, then compare it against the list of Valid Payroll Statuses that are accepted from CorePay into CorePersonnel Post Management. The document indicates that this involves integration between two key systems—CorePay and CorePersonnel—and their data synchronization process for payroll status values. If the comparison reveals a mismatch or invalid status, users are instructed to raise a new support case, reference this article's title in their request, and attach a copy of the employee's status report to provide context for the support team. The document assumes users know how to generate an employee status report and references a related article for assistance with that task. This guidance is typically used by payroll administrators, human resources staff, or support personnel who manage employee records and encounter processing errors related to payroll status validation during routine system operations.

Use this document when you need to end an employee's current appointment and transition them to a Career Break post, or conversely, when bringing them back by setting up a new appointment with updated pay and employment details. The process ensures employees on career breaks remain in the system without active payroll while maintaining a clear pathway for their eventual return. Open this if you're handling the administrative setup for an employee entering or exiting a career break period.
sl: This document provides step-by-step guidance for managing employee career breaks within a post management environment, covering both the process of placing an employee on a career break and the procedure for bringing them back to active employment. When an employee begins a career break, the document instructs users to end the current appointment, plan a new appointment against a Career Break bucket post with the "Planned Pay Details Not Required" checkbox enabled, and ensure the appointment is not commenced. For employees returning from a career break, the process involves ending the career break appointment and planning a new appointment against either a new or existing post, after which users must access CorePersonnel via Personal Profile to initiate the New Appointments rehire workflow. During the rehire process, users search for the employee with rehire status selected, update personal details as needed, populate appointment details including hours and FTE, and verify that pay details are accurate before submitting for approval. The document addresses the common scenario of managing employment gaps without disrupting the payroll and personnel management systems, and it is designed for HR and payroll administrators who need to process career break placements and returns within the Access Group's post management system. A related article on setting up an unpaid career break post is referenced for additional configuration details.

sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for modifying the Full-Time Equivalent (FTE) hours assigned to an existing employee post within the CorePersonnel system. sl: This document provides guidance for resolving the PER621-002 error that occurs when a leave date or resignation effective date is set before the appointment sequence start date in an HR management system. sl: This document provides instructions for removing employee contracts and contract amendments from the Access Group People Management portal, addressing situations where contracts have been added in error. t: Amend an employee's contract
s:

Contract amendments fall into two categories depending on whether they affect the employee's sala...
ss: Use PeopleXD to update an existing employee's contract when details change, such as job title, location, hours, FTE, or employment status. The system distinguishes between amendments with no salary impact (like location or job title changes) and those requiring salary recalculation (like FTE or contracted hours adjustments), automatically calculating new pay multipliers where needed. Open this document when you need to record contract changes and want to understand the step-by-step process in Command Centre, including how to set effective dates and select appropriate reason codes. PeopleXD maintains a complete timeline of all amendments, so you can also use this guide to view the full history of contract changes for any employee.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on updating existing employee contracts in the PeopleXD system to record changes such as hours, FTE, job title, location, or other contract details, with the system automatically tracking all amendments in a complete timeline. The document distinguishes between two types of amendments: those with no salary impact (such as location or job title changes) and those with salary impact (such as changes to hours, weeks, or FTE that require recalculation of the employee's pay multiplier). For amendments with no salary impact, users navigate from the dashboard menu to Command Centre, select the employee and relevant contract via the Contracts tab, click Update in the Amendments section, update organisational structure fields if needed, select an effective date that must be on or after the current contract effective date, choose a reason code that does not impact salary, update other contract fields as needed, and click Save. For amendments with salary impact, users follow a similar process through Command Centre and the Contracts tab but must select a reason code (such as promotion) and update fields like contracted hours or FTE, after which the Amend Salary screen opens automatically to allow review and update of pre-populated salary information before saving. The document also explains how to view the complete contract timeline by accessing the three-dot menu next to the contract summary and selecting Timeline, allowing users to review key information and all historical amendments. This document is typically used by HR administrators or payroll personnel who need to maintain accurate employee contract records and ensure that salary calculations remain current when contract terms change.

t: Length of Service versus Total Length of Service
s:
Total Length of Service

(HR0120 - Personal profile, HR Data/Appointment Details)
​
This is a standard CorePersonnel field used to show the Total Length of Service of employees main appointment history.
​
It is calculated as the length of each post from the Date Started until now. If the Date Starte...
ss: CorePersonnel tracks two related but distinct service calculations in employee personal profiles: Total Length of Service and Length of Service. Total Length of Service sums the duration of each post from its start date to present day, while Length of Service uses a simpler calculation counting only from the most recent start date. Open this document if you need to understand how these fields are calculated, troubleshoot discrepancies between them, or determine which metric to use for reporting, payroll, or HR purposes.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre explains two related but distinct CorePersonnel fields used for calculating employee service duration, both found in the HR0120 Personal profile under HR Data/Appointment Details. The Total Length of Service field calculates service by summing the length of each post from its Date Started until the present day, based on the employee's main appointment history, and only begins counting from when posts actually commenced rather than from an earlier date set in the system. The Length of Service field offers a simpler alternative calculation that counts only from the Latest Start Date to the present without considering which specific posts an employee has held during that time. The document clarifies a key difference between these fields: Total Length of Service accounts for multiple posts and their individual durations, while Length of Service provides a straightforward tenure measurement from the most recent start date. The document also identifies a potential issue where overlapping posts can create date duplication in the Total Length of Service calculation, which should not occur in normal circumstances. This guidance is relevant for HR professionals and system administrators using CorePersonnel who need to understand how service calculations work, differentiate between the two fields, and troubleshoot scenarios where service duration reporting appears inaccurate.

sl: This document provides instructions for updating appointment details within an existing contract without initiating a new sequence in the Portal system. Once the employee record is opened, users click the Contracts section and select UPDATE to begin modifying contract details. The document includes a helpful tip that employees with multiple contracts require manual selection from a dropdown menu to ensure the correct contract is being amended. This guidance is intended for Portal users, typically HR or people management professionals, who need to modify existing employee contract details such as organizational assignments and contract information while maintaining the continuity of the current appointment sequence. Related articles on contract deletion, cost centre amendments, and contract start date corrections are referenced for users requiring additional assistance with related tasks.

Open this guide when you need to make straightforward changes to hours or weeks while keeping the existing contract structure in place.
sl: This document provides a step-by-step guide for updating an employee's contracted hours or weeks within the Access Group system without requiring a full contract amendment process. A key feature is that the Amend Salary screen opens automatically if the reason code is configured correctly, enabling users to review and update pre-populated salary information in the same workflow. sl: This document provides guidance on updating an employee's substantive appointment in the Access Group's back office system, which is the employee's primary, ongoing position within the organisation. t: Portal: Overview of document and email generation
s:
The Document and Email Generation feature on PeopleXD allows a user to automatically generate documents, letters or emails based on employee data, e.g. employee contracts, letters of offer, HR forms etc.

 

Documents

A document refers to a file (MS Word or PDF) that can be generated from PeopleXD ...
ss: PeopleXD's Document and Email Generation feature lets you automatically create employee contracts, offer letters, HR forms, and recruitment emails by merging employee data into pre-built templates. You can generate documents in Word or PDF format, download them for further editing, and store them directly on an employee's profile, or send system-generated emails to candidates and staff. Templates are created using mail merge functionality and can be organized into groups like Contracts or Recruitment, with document types controlling access permissions for HR admins, recruiters, employees, and managers. Open this guide when you need to understand how to set up or use automated document and email generation in PeopleXD for HR and recruitment processes.
sl: The Document and Email Generation feature on PeopleXD enables users to automatically generate documents, letters, and emails by merging employee data into pre-configured templates, supporting use cases such as employee contracts, offer letters, HR forms, and recruitment correspondence. Documents are MS Word or PDF files created by merging employee data from the system into stored templates, which users can then download for further editing and printing, or automatically store against an employee's record on the Employee Profile screen; users can also independently upload documents like passport copies to employee profiles outside the generation process. System-generated emails are produced automatically from PeopleXD and sent to employees or applicants, with typical applications in the recruitment process such as interview invitations, though they can also be generated for HR administration purposes. Templates are the foundational component, with document templates created using MS Word mail merge functionality and uploaded to PeopleXD, while email templates are created and maintained directly within the system; templates can optionally be organized into Template Groups by category such as Contracts, Recruitment, or Salary. The system uses Data Sources—temporary files pre-populated with record data—to enable standard mail merge functionality, with each HR or recruitment admin screen from which documents or emails can be generated linked to specified data sources containing employee, applicant, contract, or other record fields mapped to templates. Document Type is a critical configuration setting that groups generated or uploaded documents on employee and applicant records, controlling visibility and access permissions for HR Admins, Recruitment Admins, Employees, and Managers. This document serves HR professionals, recruitment administrators, and system users who need to understand how to leverage template-based automation for document and email generation workflows within the PeopleXD platform.

An MSS user with document upload permissions enables the ESSG document type in the Data Centre, then uploads documents through their employee profile in either standalone PeopleXD or PeopleXD within Access Evo. After uploading, disable the general document upload feature to prevent accidental posting of confidential information.
sl: This document provides instructions for enabling and uploading public documents accessible to all employees using the ESSG document type, typically labeled as General Documents, within the Access Group portal system. The process begins in the Data Centre by navigating to Reference Data, opening Document Type, and locating the ESSG document type to configure access permissions through the Options menu, where ESS users are granted view-only access (first slider on, second slider off) and MSS users receive both view and add permissions (both sliders on). The document emphasizes critical security considerations, including testing the configuration in UAT first, ensuring uploaded content is free of sensitive information and appropriate for all-employee visibility, and subsequently disabling the general document upload capability to prevent accidental uploads of restricted materials. The actual document upload process differs slightly depending on the system configuration: standalone PeopleXD users access uploads through User Profile > My Profile > EMPLOYEE DETAIL > Documents > UPLOAD, while users accessing PeopleXD within Access Evo follow the same path but initiate it from the top-left screen corner using their name or My Profile icon. MSS users with document upload access are responsible for completing the Upload Document template and selecting the correct Document Type before confirming the upload. This guidance is primarily intended for system administrators and MSS users managing company-wide document distribution through the portal, ensuring consistent and secure sharing of public organizational materials.

t: Editing employee and manager request forms
s:

ss: Employee and manager request forms in the Access Group system can be edited, but the level of changes available depends on whether the form has already been used. Unused forms are fully editable, while used forms have certain read-only restrictions—you can update descriptions, status, add new fields, and modify lookup items, but you cannot delete existing fields. This document walks you through accessing the Data Centre, navigating to Employee and Manager Requests, and making your edits before saving. Open this guide when you need to modify an existing request form or understand what changes are permitted after a form has been actively used.
sl: This document explains how to edit employee and manager request forms within the Access Group system, covering both what can and cannot be modified depending on whether a form has been used. The editing process involves navigating from the dashboard menu to Data Centre, selecting HR Admin Setup Settings, clicking OPEN, then accessing Employee and Manager Requests where users can locate the desired form via its three-dot menu and select Edit. For unused forms, all features are fully editable, but once a form has been used, certain restrictions apply to protect data integrity. On used forms, editable elements include the form description, form status (such as setting it inactive), addition of new fields, limited amendments to existing fields, the mandatory toggle, section field types for layout adjustments, and lookup items within list fields—though users will receive warnings if updating list items that are already referenced in existing requests. Notably, users cannot delete fields from forms that have been used; instead, fields can be set to inactive status to remove them from view. After making all necessary updates to the form fields, users must click OK to confirm changes and then SAVE to finalize all amendments. This document is intended for HR administrators and managers who need to maintain and refine their request forms while managing the constraints that come with form usage history.

The process begins by navigating to the Data Centre from the dashboard menu, then locating HR Admin Setup Settings and selecting the Employee and Manager Requests section. To clone a form, users must click the three-dot menu next to the form they wish to copy and select the Clone option from the dropdown. After initiating the clone, users are required to input both a Code and Description for the new form, then confirm by clicking OK. Once the cloned form has been created, it becomes fully editable, allowing users to modify any fields or settings to suit their specific requirements. The document is designed for HR administrators and system configuration users who need to efficiently create multiple similar request forms without manually recreating each one from the beginning. Related functionality documented elsewhere in the help centre includes editing these forms after creation, deleting or deactivating them, restricting user access to specific forms, and actioning requests once they have been submitted.

sl: This document provides instructions for managing employee and manager request forms in Access Group's system by either removing them entirely or disabling them from active use. To delete a form, users navigate from the dashboard menu to Data Centre, open HR Admin Setup Settings, select Employee and Manager Requests, choose either Employee Requests or Manager Requests, locate the form using its three-dot menu, and confirm the deletion. To deactivate a form instead, users follow the same initial navigation steps but click Edit from the three-dot menu and toggle the Active field to set the form as inactive before saving changes. This document is designed for administrators or users responsible for managing request form configurations within the system, particularly those who need to remove outdated or duplicate forms while maintaining audit trails for previously used forms. The guide distinguishes between these two scenarios because deleting is only possible for unused forms, while forms with existing submissions must be deactivated rather than deleted to preserve data integrity.

sl: This document provides instructions for restricting access to employee and manager request forms by assigning criteria groups that limit availability to specific staff subsets. For new group creation, users move available items to the Assigned column using the chevron icon, can add multiple criteria by clicking ADD, and must activate and save the configuration before it takes effect. This guide is essential for HR administrators and system configuration users who need to control which employees and managers can access specific request forms, and serves as a foundational reference that complements related documents covering form deletion, team member access, and general user access configuration.

t: Workflow process and EMS trigger for employee and manager requests
s:
The approval and notification process for employee and manager requests consists of two elements. These are a workflow process for the request and an EMS alert to trigger the workflow. To complete these, follow the steps below.

 

Workflow process

One or more workflow processes should be configure...
ss: The workflow process and EMS trigger feature in HR Admin Setup Settings enables you to route employee and manager requests to the correct approvers and automatically trigger workflows when requests are submitted. You'll configure workflow processes in HR Process Configuration to define approval steps, then create corresponding EMS alerts in HR Event Configuration to specify which workflow should trigger based on request type (such as Cycle to Work Scheme). Open this document if you need to set up or modify how employee and manager requests are approved and routed through your system, or if you're troubleshooting why requests aren't reaching the right approvers.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on setting up the approval and notification infrastructure for employee and manager requests within an HR system, consisting of two interconnected components: a workflow process and an EMS (Event Management System) alert trigger. The workflow configuration process begins in the dashboard by navigating to Data Centre, accessing HR Admin Setup Settings, selecting Hr Process Configuration, and then creating a new process through the Add New Process template, with the process category set to either Employee Requests or Manager Request Events. Once the workflow template is saved, users must configure the required workflow steps to determine how requests are routed to appropriate recipients or approvers. The EMS trigger setup is equally critical and involves creating alerts in HR Event Configuration that automatically launch the corresponding workflow when conditions are met, such as when REQUEST_TYPE matches a specific request type like Cycle to Work Scheme. Key configuration settings for the EMS trigger include setting the event type to "Submitted" to ensure the workflow triggers upon request submission, specifying "Process" as the notification type, and using the Conditions tab to define which workflow process activates based on request attributes. The document is designed for HR administrators and system configurators who need to establish request routing and approval mechanisms, and it emphasizes that multiple processes and corresponding EMS triggers should be configured to accommodate different request types within the organization.

sl: This document provides a reference guide for understanding the various statuses that employee and manager requests progress through within the PeopleXD system's approval workflow. It contains a status table that defines five distinct request states: Saved (created but not submitted), Submitted (awaiting approval), Approved (approval granted), Rejected (approval denied), and Complete (finished with an outcome that is neither approved nor rejected). t: Action an employee or manager request

ss: Employee and manager requests submitted through PeopleXD trigger notifications to designated approvers, who can review and approve or reject them using the Employee Request Approvals or My Approvals widgets on their dashboard. This document walks you through how to action these requests at each stage, including viewing multi-stage approval workflows and accessing requests via the PeopleXD Mobile App. Open this if you need to approve employee or manager requests, manage requests as an HR administrator, or understand how request notifications and approvals work in the system.
sl: This document provides a complete guide for handling employee and manager request submissions within the Access Group system, covering notification processes, approval workflows, and administrative oversight. When employees or managers submit request forms, the system automatically sends notifications to designated approvers through the Notification Centre, with the request creator receiving confirmation once the approver takes action; manager requests that don't require approval trigger email notifications instead. Approvers can review and action requests from two main areas: the Employee Request Approvals widget (accessed via dashboard menu search, where users select VIEW then APPROVE or REJECT) or the My Approvals widget (accessed similarly through the dashboard menu search for "My Approvals Notifications"). HR administrators with appropriate permissions can manage all employee and manager requests centrally through the HR Process Administration screen, which is accessed by searching for Data Centre in the dashboard menu, opening HR Admin Setup Settings, selecting Hr Process Administration, and filtering by Process Category to display either Employee Requests or Manager Request Events. The document acknowledges that approval workflows may include multiple approval stages before completion and notes that these processes are also available on the PeopleXD Mobile App. This guide is intended for approvers reviewing individual requests, HR administrators overseeing all requests through the administrative interface, and employees or managers submitting requests who need to understand the notification and approval workflow.

sl: This document provides administrators with instructions on how to monitor and track requests that have been submitted by employees or their managers within the Access Group system. sl: This document provides guidance on generating reports in PeopleXD Insight specifically for employee and manager requests within the Personnel business area. The document identifies two distinct request types that can be reported on: Employee Requests and Manager Requests, each accessible through dedicated views named "Hr Employee Request (Personnel)" and "Manager Request (Personnel)" respectively. Users access this reporting functionality by selecting data from these views within PeopleXD Insight, with the specific views available depending on whether the user needs to report on employee-initiated or manager-initiated requests. Access to request data is controlled through HR User Access permissions, meaning that a user's ability to view and report on request information depends on the same general employee data access settings applied to other reports within the Personnel business area. The document assumes users may encounter access restrictions and references related articles covering user access assignment, diversity data visibility issues, and configuration of request forms in HR Process Administration. This document is primarily used by HR administrators, managers, and reporting personnel who need to create reports on request activity and manage access permissions for different user roles within the PeopleXD system.

sl: This document provides a comprehensive reference guide for controlling user access to employee and manager request forms through menu option assignments in an HR management system. It covers three distinct categories of menu options: widgets accessible through CorePortal (including MAIN_MENU.PERS_USER_DEFINED_MANAGER, MAIN_MENU.EMPLOYEE_REQUEST_WIDGET, MAIN_MENU.EMPLOYEE_REQUEST_APPROVALS_WIDGET, MAIN_MENU.EMPLOYEE_REQUEST_HISTORY, and MAIN_MENU.APPROVALS_WIDGET_ACCESS), administrator-level request views available in People Management and Web Services (such as EMPLOYEE_DASHBOARD_MENU.HR_ADMIN_MANAGER_REQ_VIEW and EMPLOYEE_DASHBOARD_MENU.HR_ADMIN_EMPLOYEE_REQ_VIEW), and configuration screens for setting up and managing requests (including HR_CONFIGURATION_MENU.EMPLOYEE_MANAGER_REQUESTS and ORGANISATIONAL_CONFIGURATION_MENU.EMPREQUDF_ASSIGNMENT). The document extensively references Web Services menu options for configuration management, with operations to create, retrieve, update, and delete UDF (user-defined field) configurations such as combo lists, items, and UDF codes. This resource is primarily used by HR administrators and system configuration managers who need to assign appropriate access permissions to employees and managers for submitting and approving requests within the People Management and CorePortal systems. The document acknowledges that users uncertain about menu option assignment procedures can consult additional guidance resources, and it references related documentation on restricting access, enabling forms in HR Process Administration, and locking down personal information access.

t: Enabling access to employee and manager request forms in HR Process Administration
s:

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Data Centre.

Next to People Management, click OPEN, then click HR User Ac...
ss: HR administrators can enable employee and manager request forms in HR Process Administration by configuring user access permissions through the Data Centre. This process involves selecting an employee or manager in the Portal settings, granting Process Access rights, and toggling permissions for Employee Requests or Manager Request Events. Open this guide when you need to give specific users access to submit or manage requests within the HR Process Administration system, or when troubleshooting why certain request forms aren't appearing for employees or managers.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for HR administrators to enable access to employee and manager request forms within the HR Process Administration system. The process begins by navigating to the Data Centre from the dashboard menu, then accessing HR User Access through the People Management section's OPEN button. Once in the Portal area, administrators select a specific employee by username (searchable by name or personnel number), then configure their access permissions by selecting Process Access in the Security Type field and clicking Show Access. The core configuration involves choosing either Employee Requests or Manager Request Events under the Description field, then toggling the View, Add, Delete, and Edit sliders to grant or restrict the appropriate permissions for that user. After adjusting these settings, administrators must click SAVE and then OK to apply the changes. This document is intended for HR administrators who need to control which employees and managers can submit or access requests through the HR Process Administration portal, and it directly addresses scenarios where access permissions need to be granted or modified for specific users.

ss: The HR Process Administration screen in PeopleXD allows you to search for and manage staff requests that require approval or rejection. Use this document when you need to locate pending staff requests, edit task details, or update approval statuses either through the portal or CoreHR back office. Open this guide if you're an HR administrator handling multiple approval workflows and want to understand the proper process to avoid duplicate tasks in the system. This is essential reading if you're responsible for actioning staff requests and need step-by-step instructions for both portal and back office approval methods.
sl: This document provides instructions for administrators to search for, locate, and manage staff requests within the HR Process Administration screen, accessible through the Data Centre's HR Admin Setup Settings in the Access Group system. The document outlines two primary methods for handling staff request approvals: the portal-based approach, which involves navigating to HR Process Administration, selecting Staff Requests from the Process Category List of Values, and then using the three-dot ellipsis menu to edit task status details; and the back office approach via CoreHR's Event Management module, which follows a similar navigation path but offers an alternative workflow. A critical known issue is flagged: when multiple approval tasks exist within a single process, approving a second task through the portal can generate a duplicate task stuck in pending approval status, for which the Development and Product Teams are actively working on improvements. The document addresses this problem by recommending that administrators use the back office method to set multiple tasks to 'Approved' status rather than the portal interface. Both methods ultimately require the user to locate the relevant staff request, navigate to its Task Status Details, and update the task status to the required state before saving. This document is intended for HR administrators and process managers who need to review, approve, or reject staff requests within the organization's HR workflow system.

ss: Bulk upload corrections in HESA allows you to update multiple records at once through CoreHR by uploading a corrected CSV file. Use this process when you've identified errors in your initial HESA data load and need to fix them without manually editing individual records. Open this document when you're ready to re-upload a CSV file with corrections, preview the changes before final completion, and resolve any validation errors that appear during the upload preview step.
sl: This document provides instructions for performing bulk updates and corrections to HESA (Higher Education Statistics Agency) data within the CoreHR system. The process begins by navigating from Back Office to the CoreHR product, then accessing the CoreHESA menu and selecting option 13 "Load Data File" from the Select Option list. Users must then browse for and select a CSV file to upload, specify the Record Type, and click Upload Data to initiate the process, though this step can be skipped if the Record Type is HESA User Defined Load or HESA Contract Exemption Load. The system allows users to generate a preview of the load before finalizing it, which is critical for identifying and resolving any errors present in the CSV file. If errors are detected during preview, users must correct them in the source CSV and repeat the upload steps with the corrected file. Once all errors are resolved and the preview is satisfactory, users navigate to the HESA Load Details tab and click Complete Upload to finalize the bulk correction. This document is typically used by HESA administrators or data managers who need to perform large-scale data corrections or migrations within educational institutions using the Access Group's CoreHR system.

ss: Use the CorePortal Template Data Source Configuration to display an employee's Known As name on the Generate Document & Email screens. You'll need to update three specific data sources—HR_PERSON_MERGE, PERS_POST_PERSON_MERGE, and PERS_POST_APPOINTMENT_MERGE—by replacing standard fields like FORENAME with the KNOWN_AS field. Open this guide when you're setting up document and email templates and want employees' preferred names to appear instead of their formal first names. This configuration is done through HR Admin Setup Settings in the Data Centre widget.
sl: This document provides instructions for configuring an employee's "Known As" name to appear on the Generate Document & Email screens within the Access Group system. The process involves updating three specific data sources: HR_PERSON_MERGE, PERS_POST_PERSON_MERGE, and PERS_POST_APPOINTMENT_MERGE through the CorePortal - Template Data Source Configuration menu option. Users must navigate to the Data Centre widget, open HR Admin Setup Settings, search for Document and Email Templates, and access the Data Source Config tab to make the necessary modifications. For each data source selected, the existing column (such as FORENAME) must be deleted and replaced by clicking Add and selecting the KNOWN_AS field instead. The configuration is completed by enabling the Quick Search toggle, entering a description such as "Known As Name," and saving the changes. This document is typically used by system administrators or HR personnel who manage document and email template configurations and need to ensure that employee known as names are properly displayed when generating official documents and communications.

ss: Upload documents like pension statements directly to individual employee profiles in the portal's People Management section. This process is useful when you need to store important employee-specific files in a centralized location within the system. Open this guide when you need step-by-step instructions for attaching documents to an employee's record, including how to categorize the document type and add descriptions for easy reference.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for uploading documents, such as pension statements, directly to individual employee profiles within the portal system. The process begins from the dashboard by navigating to the People Management section, then selecting View beside Employees and using the search field to locate the relevant employee. Once the employee record is open, users click View followed by the Files tab to access the document upload interface. The upload workflow involves clicking Add, selecting the appropriate document type from the Document Type drop-down menu, entering a description in the Description field, and then clicking Upload to complete the process. This functionality is designed for portal users who need to attach supporting documentation to employee records for administrative purposes such as pension management or compliance documentation. The document also references related portal tasks including assigning menu profiles to users, rehiring employees, and uploading public documents, indicating this is part of a broader employee profile management system.

t: Menu Option to Delete an uploaded Document
s:
There is not single menu option that allows a person to delete a document only. The menu option that gives a user this access to delete will also give the user access to upload too. When it is removed, they will not have access to upload a document via the People Management dashboard:

EMPLOYEE_DASH...
ss: Deleting an uploaded document in the People Management dashboard requires removing the EMPLOYEE_DASHBOARD_MENU.FILE_UPLOAD menu option, though this will also prevent users from uploading documents through that interface. Users who need continued upload access can use the Manager dashboard instead by activating MAIN_MENU.DOCUMENT_UPLOAD_MGR and MAIN_MENU.DOCUMENTMANAGERVIEW menu options. Note that the Manager dashboard has no built-in delete functionality for documents. Use this guide when configuring user permissions around document management access across the People Management and Manager dashboards.
sl: This document explains the menu options required to grant users access to delete uploaded documents within the Access Group system, clarifying an important limitation that document deletion and upload permissions are bundled together rather than being separate functions. The primary menu option that enables document deletion is EMPLOYEE_DASHBOARD_MENU.FILE_UPLOAD, which simultaneously grants upload access through the People Management dashboard; removing this permission prevents users from uploading documents via that dashboard. As an alternative, users with manager-level access who have direct reports can upload documents through the Manager dashboard by activating two menu options: MAIN_MENU.DOCUMENT_UPLOAD_MGR and MAIN_MENU.DOCUMENTMANAGERVIEW. However, the document clarifies an important constraint that the Manager Dashboard contains no functionality to delete documents, meaning managers cannot remove documents they have uploaded through that interface. This document is intended for administrators or system configurators who manage user permissions and need to understand the relationship between menu options for document management across both employee and manager dashboards. The guide helps resolve confusion around permission structures by explicitly stating that deletion capability cannot be granted independently from upload capability within the People Management dashboard environment.

t: Download and Import Menu Profiles
s: You can download menu profiles to an external file. This can be useful for uploading into another environment, for example when moving custom menu profiles from UAT to a production environment. The menu profile should be downloaded in a .PROF file type extension as per the below instructions and the...
ss: Menu profiles control user access and navigation options in your system, and this document covers how to download them to external .PROF files and import them back into different environments. Use this guide when you need to move custom menu profiles between environments—such as transferring configurations from UAT to production—or when you want to back up and restore menu profile settings. The process involves accessing the Menu Profiles widget in the Security dashboard, then using the download and import functions to transfer or deploy profiles across your system.
sl: This document provides instructions for downloading and importing menu profiles in the Access Group system, enabling users to transfer custom menu configurations between environments such as moving from UAT to production. The download process involves accessing the Security dashboard, locating the Menu Profiles widget, finding the specific menu profile to be exported, and selecting the Download Menu Profile option from the three-dot menu, with the file saved in .PROF file format. The import process follows a similar navigation path through the Security dashboard and Menu Profiles widget, then requires users to either create a new blank menu profile or select an existing one before accessing the three-dot menu and selecting Import Menu Options. When importing, users must specify "From external file" as the source and then upload the previously downloaded .PROF file, confirming the action by clicking OK. This document is designed for system administrators and configuration managers who need to replicate menu profiles across different system environments or manage user access permissions consistently. Related tasks such as assigning menu profiles to users, setting default menu profiles, and creating new menu profiles are referenced but detailed in separate documentation articles.

t: Configure employee and manager request forms
s: You can create request forms using the employee and manager requests screen. These allow an employee, or a manager on behalf of an employee, to submit a request form within PeopleXD that's then routed to its intended recipient via a workflow process. To learn how to do this, watch the video or follo...
ss: Employee and manager request forms in PeopleXD allow employees or their managers to submit requests that route automatically through a workflow process. This document covers how to create these forms from scratch, add up to 40 customizable fields (including text, numeric, date, list, and reference fields), and configure form settings like help text and mandatory declarations. Open this guide when you need to build a new request form, customize its layout and fields, or adjust visibility and approval workflows in your PeopleXD system.
sl: This document provides comprehensive instructions for creating and configuring employee and manager request forms within PeopleXD, which allow employees or managers to submit requests that are routed through a workflow process to the intended recipient. The setup process begins by navigating to the People Management dashboard, accessing the Data Centre tab, opening HR Admin Setup Settings, and selecting Employee and Manager Requests before clicking ADD to create a new form with a unique code and description. Once created, administrators can add up to 40 fields to the form (with a section field automatically generated as the first field) by clicking the three-dot menu and selecting Edit, then choosing from field types including Text, Numeric, Date, List, Text Area, Reference, and Section, each with specific configuration options such as format masks for numeric fields and reference types for manager request forms. The document details how to configure list items by clicking LIST ITEMS and adding descriptions, and explains section type options (Grid, Top Down, or Full-Width) to control field layout and display. Additional form settings can be amended through the ACTIONS menu and Settings option, allowing administrators to show or hide specific fields, add help text and purpose messages, include declarative statements with mandatory checkboxes, and apply appointment-specific linking for manager requests. The document also explains how to preview forms from the Edit Request Form screen by clicking the Preview button to review the final appearance before deployment. This resource is essential for HR administrators and system configurators who need to customize request workflows in PeopleXD to meet their organization's specific employee and manager request handling procedures.

t: Certificate *.corehr.com is due to expire
s:
If a warning message appears stating that the '*.corehr.com' certificate is due to expire, you do not need to take any action. The Access Group maintains this domain, and the technical team will update the certificate automatically. This activity incurs no charge.

Related Articles

ss: The *.corehr.com SSL certificate expiration warning affects CoreHR users who may see alerts about the domain certificate reaching its end of life. You don't need to take any action when this warning appears, as The Access Group's technical team handles certificate renewal automatically at no cost to your organization. Open this document if you've received a certificate expiration notice for CoreHR and want to confirm whether you need to respond or if it's being managed by The Access Group.
sl: This document addresses a specific warning message that users may encounter regarding the expiration of the '*.corehr.com' certificate in their CoreHR system. The document clarifies that when users see this certificate expiration warning, they do not need to take any immediate or follow-up action on their part. The Access Group, which maintains the *.corehr.com domain, has responsibility for managing the certificate lifecycle and will automatically update the certificate when necessary to prevent service interruption. Users are assured that the automatic certificate renewal process incurs no additional charges to their organization. This document is relevant for CoreHR system administrators and end-users who may encounter the warning message and become concerned about the certificate status. The document distinguishes this scenario from related certificate expiration issues, as indicated by a cross-reference to an article titled "SSO certificate is due to expire - action required," which describes a different certificate situation that does require user intervention. The straightforward guidance provides reassurance that the certificate warning can be safely ignored while the backend maintenance is handled by Access Group's technical team.

t: SSO certificate is due to expire - action required

If your SSO certificate is due to expire, the technical team at Access must renew it. To begin this process, please raise a support case and include the following details.

The environments affected (e.g. Live or UAT).

The expiry date of the current certificate.

Support will raise an internal requ...
ss: SSO (Single Sign-On) certificate renewal is a process managed by Access Group's technical team that requires a support case to initiate. Open this document when you receive a notification that your SSO certificate is expiring and need to understand what information to provide—including affected environments (Live or UAT) and the expiry date—so that the Optimisation Services and DBA teams can process the renewal. This is essential reading if you want to know what to expect, including that the service typically involves a charge that requires your approval before work begins. Note that if the issue involves a *.corehr.com certificate specifically, Access handles that renewal automatically without action needed on your part.
sl: This document provides guidance on managing the renewal of Single Sign-On (SSO) certificates that are approaching their expiration date in Access systems. When an SSO certificate expiration is imminent, the technical team at Access Group must perform the renewal, which begins by raising a support case that includes specific information such as the affected environments (for example, Live or UAT) and the expiry date of the current certificate. Once the support case is submitted, Access Group's internal request process is activated, with the Optimisation Services and DBA teams collaborating jointly to handle the certificate renewal work. The document clarifies that SSO certificate renewal is a chargeable service, and Access Group will request your approval before proceeding with the work. An important distinction is noted: if a warning message specifically indicates that the *.corehr.com certificate is due to expire, this is handled separately and automatically by the Access Group technical team without requiring manual intervention or support case submission. This document is intended for Access Group users and administrators who manage system access and authentication infrastructure and need to understand the process for addressing expiring SSO certificates in their environments.

t: API details for setup
s:
There are two distinct groups of web service endpoints used to manage data interactions within client databases.

B2B endpoints - These provide non-user-based functionality, such as a machine pushing clockings to the database or a sync job updating employee contact details across multiple locations ...
ss: API endpoints in PeopleXD fall into two categories: B2B endpoints for system-to-system integrations (like clocking machines and employee data syncs), and User endpoints that require portal credentials for standard user tasks such as updating profiles or submitting leave requests. Open this document when you need to understand which endpoint type supports your specific integration or workflow, or when you're setting up automated data connections between systems and the PeopleXD database. This reference covers the foundational technical structure for managing data interactions within your organization's client databases.
sl: This document provides an overview of the web service endpoints available within the API for managing data interactions in client databases through the PeopleXD system. It describes two distinct categories of endpoints: B2B endpoints, which enable non-user-based functionality such as machines pushing clockings data to the database or automated sync jobs updating employee contact details across multiple organizational locations, and User endpoints, which require PeopleXD portal user credentials and support everyday user tasks including updating profile photos and submitting leave requests. The document serves as an introductory reference guide for developers and system administrators who need to understand which endpoint type to use for different integration scenarios and data management processes. It references related configuration tasks such as troubleshooting portal welcome registration emails for employees, configuring the PeopleXD Mobile App, and managing the Event Type Maintenance screen through the EMS module. The document indicates that more detailed technical specifications are available separately for both endpoint groups. This resource is typically consulted by API developers implementing integrations, system administrators setting up automated data processes, and technical staff managing the PeopleXD platform configuration.

t: PeopleXD SMTP server migration
s:
Access is migrating the SMTP server that processes emails sent from PeopleXD. The legacy SMTP server, hosted in a Magnet Plus (formerly BT) data centre, will be replaced with a new SMTP server hosted in a UK-based Access Group data centre.

 

For customers who do not use their own sending domain, t...
ss: PeopleXD is migrating its SMTP email server from a legacy Magnet Plus data centre to a new UK-based Access Group data centre that supports DKIM authentication. This change improves email delivery reliability and reduces the risk of PeopleXD emails being marked as spam by providers like Gmail and Hotmail. Most customers require no action—the default sending address will change to peoplexd@accessacloud.com, though custom sending domains can be maintained. Open this document if you use PeopleXD and want to understand changes to your email sending configuration, or if you're experiencing issues with emails being filtered as spam.
sl: This document describes PeopleXD's migration from a legacy SMTP server hosted in a Magnet Plus data centre to a new server hosted in an Access Group UK data centre, addressing email deliverability issues caused by the absence of DKIM authentication support on the current system. The migration will change the default sending address for customers not using a custom domain to peoplexd@accessacloud.com, which has DKIM authentication configured to improve email delivery reliability and reduce the likelihood of emails being incorrectly filtered as spam by providers such as Gmail and Hotmail. The document explains that most customers require no action, though those using custom "from" addresses may need to configure DKIM and/or Sender Policy Framework (SPF) settings, and Access Group will proactively contact any customers requiring changes before implementation. The sending address remains configurable within the PeopleXD application, and customers can continue using their own custom sending domains if preferred. Migration will be completed by 30 June 2026 with no downtime or service interruption, and the new infrastructure will store 30 days of SMTP server logs containing minimal sensitive data beyond the "from" email address. This document is intended for PeopleXD administrators and users who need to understand how the email migration affects their system configuration and to reassure them that the change improves deliverability without requiring immediate action for most implementations.

t: Oracle Forms 12.2.1.19 upgrade
s:
The Oracle Forms version used by the PeopleXD back office forms application is being upgraded from 12.2.1.4 to 12.2.1.19. This explains what is changing, when it is happening, and what to do if you experience any issues after the upgrade.

 

What is changing
