ss: Oracle Forms is being upgraded in the PeopleXD back office forms application from version 12.2.1.4 to 12.2.1.19 on 17 May 2026, with the jar files being re-signed to support a newer version that Oracle will continue to support. The upgrade requires no action from users as updated files download automatically in the background on first run. Open this document if you experience issues running the back office forms after the upgrade date, as it provides troubleshooting steps including checking your Java Runtime Environment version, clearing your Java cache, and ensuring administrator privileges. If problems persist after following these steps, the document directs you to contact support through the Access Digital Assistant.
sl: The Oracle Forms version used by the PeopleXD back office forms application is being upgraded from version 12.2.1.4 to 12.2.1.19, with the User Acceptance Testing (UAT) upgrade already completed and the Production upgrade scheduled for 17 May 2026 at 8pm. The primary change involves re-signing the associated jar files within the PeopleXD back office forms application with the higher version number, driven by the current version of Oracle Forms reaching end-of-life status and losing Oracle support. Users can expect minimal disruption as the updated jar files will download automatically in the background upon first run of the application, requiring no manual intervention. However, if users experience issues running the back office forms application after the upgrade, the document provides a troubleshooting process including verifying that Java Runtime Environment (JRE) version V8u211 or higher is installed, clearing the Java cache using steps available on the Java help website, and ensuring administrator privileges are enabled on the local machine for application execution. If these steps do not resolve the issues, users are directed to contact a human agent through the Access Digital Assistant for additional support. This document is intended for PeopleXD back office forms application users who may encounter technical difficulties following the upgrade and need guidance on resolution steps.

t: Migration to the new PeopleXD Ideas Portal
s:
As part of our continued efforts to improve the way we collect and action feedback from our PeopleXD clients, we are migrating to a new Ideas Portal hosted within the Access Aha! environment.

 

This new portal provides a more modern interface, enhanced tracking features, and a stronger foundation ...
ss: The PeopleXD Ideas Portal is moving to a new platform hosted in Access Aha!, with the legacy portal retiring permanently on 30th June 2025. Use this document if you need to access the new ideas portal, submit feedback, or vote on PeopleXD product improvements—either by accepting an email invitation or registering manually. Ideas submitted in the last 12 months or with 10+ votes will automatically transfer, though older ideas won't appear but remain internally for roadmap planning. Open this if you're having trouble locating old ideas, registering for the new portal, or understanding how the migration affects your account.
sl: This document guides PeopleXD clients through the migration from the legacy Ideas Portal to a new Ideas Portal hosted within the Access Aha! environment, which takes effect on 30th June 2025 when the old portal is permanently retired. The new portal offers a modern interface, enhanced tracking features, better two-way communication, and AI-assisted idea prioritisation. Ideas submitted in the last 12 months or with 10 or more votes will be automatically transferred to the new portal, while older ideas meeting neither criterion will be retained internally by the product team but won't appear in the portal. Users can access the new portal either through an email invitation sent to those who previously submitted or voted on ideas in the legacy portal within the last 12 months (where accounts are automatically created), or by manually registering at the PeopleXD Ideas Portal by clicking Sign up and entering their work email address and name in the designated fields. Once registered, users can browse and vote on existing ideas, submit new ideas, and follow ideas to track progress and status changes. The document addresses the issue of missing ideas by recommending users search with alternative titles or categories, or resubmit ideas as new entries if they cannot be located. Support is available for registration, login, or other issues through the online case submission system or by contacting a customer success manager.

t: XD Hub
s:
XD Hub is the PeopleXD Customer Release Portal and is accessible to authorised users from PeopleXD. 
​
It includes information relating to upcoming features and Feature Packs releases. From XD Hub, you can download feature setup guides to help you self serve the new features.
​
The following menu se...
ss: XD Hub is the PeopleXD Customer Release Portal where you can access information about upcoming features and Feature Pack releases. The portal allows you to download feature setup guides that help you self-serve the implementation of new features in PeopleXD. Open this document when you need to understand how to access XD Hub, what security permissions are required, or where to find setup guidance for newly released features in your PeopleXD system.
sl: XD Hub is the PeopleXD Customer Release Portal that provides authorized users with access to information about upcoming features and Feature Pack releases within the PeopleXD system. The portal enables users to download feature setup guides that support self-service implementation of new features, allowing customers to independently configure and deploy releases without requiring extensive external support. To access XD Hub, users must have specific menu security items configured in their system, including the "XDHub" Web Services permission, the "Xdhub – Get Token" Web Services permission, the "XD - Feature Set Up Guides" CorePortal permission, and the "XD - Acknowledge Feature Launch" CorePortal permission. The document serves as a reference guide for system administrators or portal managers who need to configure user access rights and for end users who need to understand what permissions are required before they can view and utilize the portal's resources. The primary use case is enabling customers to stay informed about upcoming releases and to independently access the documentation and guidance needed to implement new features within their PeopleXD environment. This documentation is particularly relevant for organizations using PeopleXD who want to manage their own feature deployments and understand the access control requirements for the release portal.

t: Feature Pack releases
s:
New PeopleXD features are delivered via Feature Pack releases. A Feature Pack is simply a bundle of features which are released together.
​
The XD HUB is your starting point for new features. 
​
As a PeopleXD administrator for your business, you should:

Monitor the XD Hub Release Management space. ...
ss: Feature Pack releases deliver new PeopleXD functionality in bundled updates, which administrators need to monitor, review, and implement. As a PeopleXD administrator, you'll use the XD Hub Release Management space to track upcoming Non-Production and Production release dates, then consult Feature Guides to understand new capabilities before configuring them with the XD Assistant. Open this document when you need to understand how new features are rolled out to your PeopleXD system, what your responsibilities are as an administrator, or where to find release schedules and feature documentation.
sl: This document provides an overview of how new PeopleXD features are delivered to users through Feature Pack releases, which are bundled collections of features released together on scheduled dates. The XD HUB serves as the primary access point where PeopleXD administrators can locate and monitor all available Feature Pack releases, including both Non-Production (UAT) and Production environment release schedules. When a new Feature Pack becomes available, administrators receive notification through a banner that displays across the PeopleXD interface, prompting them to take action. As a PeopleXD administrator, users are responsible for regularly monitoring the XD Hub Release Management space to stay informed about upcoming and current Feature Pack deployments. The document directs administrators to consult Feature Guides to understand the new functionality being introduced in each Feature Pack release, and to acknowledge new Feature Packs within the system. Configuration of the newly released functionality is accomplished through the XD Assistant, which provides guided setup options for administrators implementing these features in their business environment. This document is intended for PeopleXD administrators who need to understand the feature release cycle, stay informed about available updates, and manage the implementation and acknowledgment of new Feature Packs in their organization.

t: Configure the PeopleXD Mobile App
s:

​

Go to the Administrator Dashboard

Select the menu profile you want to configure from the dropdown

Expand the modules you want to grant a...
ss: The PeopleXD mobile app configuration allows administrators to control which modules and features are available to users on their mobile devices. Through the Administrator Dashboard's Site Manager widget, you can select a menu profile, enable specific modules, and customize the sidebar navigation by dragging modules into your preferred order. Open this document when you need to set up or modify mobile app access for your workforce, restrict certain features to specific user groups, or reorganize how modules appear in the mobile interface. You'll also need to ensure the appropriate Web Services menu permissions are enabled on user profiles to support these mobile configurations.
sl: This document provides a complete guide to configuring the PeopleXD mobile app, including both a video reference and step-by-step written instructions for administrators. The configuration process begins by navigating to the Administrator Dashboard and accessing the Site Manager widget, where users click Open on the Mobile Configuration option to begin customizing the app experience. Administrators select their desired menu profile from a dropdown menu, then expand the modules they wish to manage and enable the relevant toggles to grant access to specific features and functionality. The document also covers sidebar navigation configuration through a dedicated tab, where administrators can use a Position column to drag and drop modules into their preferred order within the mobile app interface. To access the Mobile Configuration screen, three specific menu options must be enabled on the user's menu profile: Get config navigation (WS_NATIVE_MENU.GET_CONFIG_NAVIGATION), Update config navigation (WS_NATIVE_MENU.PATCH_CONFIG_NAVIGATION_ID), and Get config menuoptions (WS_NATIVE_MENU.GET_CONFIG_MENUOPTIONS), all of which are Web Services-based permissions. This document is primarily intended for system administrators and IT configuration specialists who are responsible for setting up and customizing the PeopleXD mobile application for their organization's users.

t: Portal: Creating an event notification (EMS)
s:
The system allows you to generate alerts and notifications based on data changes or dated events. To configure this, follow the steps below.

 

Create new notification

From the dashboard menu, enter Data Centre in the search bar and select it.

Next to HR Admin Setup Settings, click OPEN, then cli...
ss: Event notifications in the Portal alert users about HR data changes or scheduled events by sending automated reminders to specific recipients. This document walks through setting up a new notification in HR Event Configuration, including defining when alerts trigger (number of days before or after an event), selecting who receives them (via email or organizational role), and customizing the notification message with subject lines and body content. Use this guide when you need to configure automated alerts for HR events like probation dates, anniversaries, or other milestone events that require advance notice to managers or employees. You can also set up conditional logic to ensure notifications only send when specific criteria are met.
sl: This document provides comprehensive instructions for configuring event notifications in a Portal system that generates alerts based on data changes or dated events. The process begins in the Data Centre section accessed through the dashboard menu, where users navigate to HR Admin Setup Settings and select HR Event Configuration to create a new notification under a specific Event Category and Event Type. Users must define event timing by entering the number of days in the Generate Notification field and selecting whether the notification triggers Before or After that interval, then activate the notification and optionally enable Test Mode Indicator to restrict email reminders to administrators only. The notification recipients are configured by selecting a Notification Type such as Email, Organisation Role, or other options, with Email requiring an email address and optional CC field, while Organisation Role requires Structure, Organisational Group, and Organisational Role fields, with a special configuration for manager notifications using Reports To Manager. Users can add up to three conditions using the Conditions section by selecting fields, operators, and comparison values from a chosen table view, combining multiple conditions with AND or OR logic to control when notifications are triggered. The final step involves configuring the notification subject and message body through separate Configure Subject and Configure Message screens, where users select a data source view and insert system variables and custom text to personalize the alert content. This document is intended for HR administrators and system configuration specialists who need to set up automated event notifications to trigger alerts for specific business scenarios such as probation period alerts or other HR-related events.

t: New starter notification sent to the role's prior manager
s:
EMS notifications are generated based on the reminder date rather than the event date. The manager notified will be the one in place on the reminder date. Review the event configuration to identify and update when the reminder falls.

From the dashboard menu, in the search bar, enter and select Data...
ss: When a new starter notification is sent to a manager in PeopleXD, the notification timing is based on the reminder date rather than the actual event date, which means the manager notified will be whoever holds the role on that reminder date. To control when these notifications are triggered, you need to configure the reminder settings in HR Event Configuration under the New Starter Notification event type. Open Data Centre from the dashboard, navigate to HR Admin Setup Settings, and edit the event to adjust the "No Of Days" and "Before/After" values for when the notification should generate. Use this guide if you need to change when new starter notifications are sent to managers or if you want to understand why a notification went to a specific manager.
sl: This document explains how to manage Email Management System (EMS) notifications for new starter events, specifically addressing the critical issue that notifications are triggered based on reminder dates rather than event dates, which determines which manager receives the notification. The document provides step-by-step instructions for accessing and configuring these settings, starting from the dashboard menu by searching for and selecting Data Centre, then navigating to HR Admin Setup Settings, clicking OPEN, and accessing HR Event Configuration. Users must select the Event Category and locate the required Event Type (typically categorized under HR Event with type New Starter Notification), then click Edit from the three-dot menu to modify notification settings. The configuration process involves reviewing the No Of Days and Before/After values under Event Notifications to understand when reminders are generated, with the key principle that when days and Before are specified together, the reminder date falls that number of days prior to the event date. To adjust notification timing, users click Edit on the specific notification, enter a number of days in the Generate Notification field, select either Before or After from the Days dropdown menu, and save their changes by clicking Save followed by OK. This document is essential for HR administrators and system managers who need to ensure that new starter notifications reach the correct manager at the appropriate time, particularly when organizational changes or staffing transitions affect who should be notified on specific reminder dates.

ss: HR Event Configuration lets you set up automated notifications when employee data changes, such as address or bank details updates. Access this feature through People Management > HR Admin > Data Centre, then search for and configure HR Events with customizable recipient lists, message formats, and company-specific conditions. Use this when you need to alert relevant staff members whenever critical HR events occur in your system. You can also duplicate existing event configurations as templates to speed up setup for similar notifications.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for configuring notifications that trigger when HR events occur, such as employee address changes or bank details updates. Users access the configuration interface by navigating to People Management / HR Admin, then selecting Data Centre and View all, followed by searching for and selecting "HR Event Configuration" with "HR Events" chosen from the Event Category dropdown. Once an HR event is located in the list, users click the three-dot ellipsis menu and select Edit to either modify existing notification settings or add new ones. The configuration process requires filling out three key areas: the Recipient area where notification delivery method is specified, the Message area for customizing the notification format or note content, and the Conditions area for restricting notifications to specific company areas or departments. After completing all required information across these sections, users save the configuration by clicking the Save button. The document also includes a helpful tip for users who want to replicate an existing event's settings, explaining that they can click the three-dot ellipsis on the source event, select Edit, and then click Copy Event to use it as a template. This guide is intended for HR administrators and HR system users who need to ensure that appropriate stakeholders are automatically notified when significant employee data changes occur in the system.

t: Staff request not showing in Process Administration screen
s:

ss: Staff Request events aren't appearing in the Process Administration screen because the process attachment or event notification activation is missing in Hr Event Configuration. Use this guide when staff requests fail to show up in your HR workflows, whether you're accessing the system through the People Management portal or CoreHR back office. Follow the steps to verify that a process is attached to the Staff Request event and that the Active Indicator is enabled in Event Notifications. This resolves visibility issues that prevent staff requests from being searchable and actionable in Process Administration.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving an issue where staff requests do not appear in the Process Administration screen, addressing a common configuration problem in HR systems. The document covers two parallel navigation paths depending on whether users are accessing the system through the Portal or Back Office interface. For Portal users, the resolution involves navigating to the People Management dashboard, selecting Data Centre and View all, then searching for Hr Event Configuration, where users must locate Staff Requests in the Event Category and edit the Staff Request Status event. Back Office users follow a similar process by selecting the CoreHR product, navigating through the top menu to CoreHR, then Event Management, and finally HR Event Configuration to access the same Staff Request Status settings. The core issue this document resolves is ensuring that two critical configuration settings are properly enabled: the Process field must be populated with an assigned process, and the Active Indicator must be enabled or ticked to activate event notifications. This configuration must be completed for the relevant event notification within the Event Notifications section for staff requests to display correctly in the HR Process Administration screen. The document is designed for system administrators and HR personnel responsible for configuring HR workflow processes and event management in CoreHR systems, particularly those troubleshooting visibility issues with staff requests in administrative screens.

t: EMS alerts are triggering from a test environment
s: As a test environment is for testing, it is not ideal for EMS alerts to be triggering to employees as they may be confused with alerts from a live environment. You can disable EMS alerts completely, or leave them enabled and direct them to an administrator email account for test purposes. To complet...
ss: EMS alerts in test environments can be disabled or redirected to prevent confusion with live production alerts. This document covers how to configure EMS (Event Management System) parameters in both the Portal and Back Office, allowing you to turn alerts on/off or direct them to an administrator email address for testing purposes. Open this guide when you're setting up a test environment and need to manage alert behavior to avoid sending notifications to employees during testing cycles.
sl: This document provides guidance on preventing EMS (Event Management System) alerts from reaching employees in test environments, which could cause confusion by appearing as live system notifications. The document addresses the problem that test environment alerts should either be completely disabled or redirected away from regular staff to avoid mistaking them for production alerts. It offers two separate configuration paths depending on the system being used: the Portal approach requires navigating to the Data Centre via the dashboard menu, then accessing EMS Parameter Maintenance; the Back Office approach requires selecting Event Management from the main CoreHR menu and then accessing EMS Parameter Maintenance. Both methods involve configuring three key controls on the EMS Parameter Maintenance screen: the EMS On/Off toggle to enable or disable alerts entirely, the Administrator Email field to specify a testing email address, and the Test Run toggle which, when enabled, directs all emails to the administrator email account instead of regular users. The document is intended for administrators and testing teams who need to manage EMS alert behavior in non-production environments to ensure test notifications do not inadvertently reach end users. Related articles are referenced for broader topics including welcome registration emails, general EMS troubleshooting, EMS parameter maintenance management, event notification creation, and test email functionality in non-production environments.

t: HR event notification emails not creating and / or sending as expected
s:
Possible causes of this issue:

Cause 1: The EMS On/Off indicator is unticked or the Test Run is ticked.

Cause 2: The Event Type or/and Event Notification is disabled or the Event Notification runs in the Test Mode.

Cause 3: The DBA job related to processing these Event Notifications has not been ...
ss: HR event notification emails in CoreHR may fail to send due to disabled Event Management System (EMS) settings, inactive Event Types or Notifications, or misconfigured database jobs. Use this document to troubleshoot why HR Event Notifications aren't creating or sending by checking EMS On/Off indicators, Test Run settings, and Active Indicator switches in both the Portal and Back Office. Follow the step-by-step resolutions to re-enable email processing in CoreHR's Event Management section or check the Email Queue for created messages. Open this guide when HR event notification emails stop working unexpectedly or aren't being generated for configured events.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving issues where HR event notification emails fail to create or send properly within the CoreHR system. The document identifies three primary causes: the EMS (Event Management System) On/Off indicator being disabled or Test Run being enabled, the Event Type or Event Notification being disabled or running in Test Mode, or the DBA job responsible for processing Event Notifications being improperly configured or broken. Resolution 1 requires users to access the Back Office in CoreHR, navigate to Event Management > EMS Parameter Maintenance, ensure the EMS On/Off indicator checkbox is selected and the Test Run checkbox is unchecked, then save these changes. Resolution 2 addresses configuration at both the Portal and Back Office levels, requiring users to access Hr Event Configuration, verify that the Active Indicator switch is enabled for the relevant Event Type, edit the specific Notification ID, and confirm that the Active Indicator is on while the Test Mode Indicator is off. Resolution 3 advises users to check the Email Queue to determine whether emails have been generated for the events in question, and if not, to raise a support case with details about when the issue was first observed. This document is typically used by HR administrators and system configuration specialists who need to diagnose and resolve email delivery problems related to HR event notifications in the CoreHR platform.

ss: System reminders in CoreHR automatically notify users—via diary entries or emails—about important HR events such as new employee start dates, department changes, or contract expiry dates. You can set up reminders for individual users, groups, managers, or IT teams, and they'll receive alerts a specified number of days before the event occurs. Access the Event Management System through CoreHR to configure reminder parameters, manage user assignments, query existing reminders, or clear down old events. Open this document when you need to understand how to create, manage, or troubleshoot system-generated HR reminders and notifications in CoreHR.
sl: This document explains how to create and manage system alerts, events, and reminders in the CoreHR system for any user with a Personnel number, role assignment, individual or group email address, or Oracle login. System reminders can be generated for various HR scenarios, such as notifying IT of new employee start dates or alerting managers and HR to department changes or upcoming employee expiry dates. When reminders are created, a diary entry is generated in the system and users are automatically prompted to view their reminders upon login, or they can access reminders at any time; alternatively, recipients can receive email notifications to take action on events. The Event Management System is accessed through the CoreHR Menu by selecting CoreHR, Event Management, which provides five main configuration options: EMS Parameter Maintenance for setting up reminder system parameters, EMS User Maintenance for storing usernames, EMS Event Clear Down for removing existing reminders, EMS Enquiry for querying reminders, and HR Event Configuration as the main setup screen where reminders are configured. This document is intended for HR professionals, IT personnel, and system administrators who need to set up automated notifications and manage event-driven workflows to track employee lifecycle events and organizational changes. The document references related troubleshooting articles addressing issues such as EMS alerts triggering from test environments and HR event notification emails failing to create or send as expected.

t: Manage the EMS Parameter Maintenance screen
s:
📌Note: This article is based on users who are Superusers within an Organisation and any changes within EMS should only be carried out by a Superuser. Certain System Parameters need to be set up prior to using the EMS. These parameters are of a Technical nature. 

This screen can be accessed as follo...
ss: The EMS Parameter Maintenance screen in CoreHR (Back Office) or People Management (Portal) allows Superusers to configure technical settings that control how the Event Management System operates. Key parameters include enabling/disabling EMS globally, selecting event notification software (CoreHR or MS Outlook '97), configuring mail server details, and setting up SQL file storage paths and locations. Use this screen when you need to set up or adjust how event reminders and notifications are sent across your organization, including email delivery, test mode functionality, and mail history retention. Only Superusers should access this screen, as changes to parameters like SQL Plus location affect all system users.
sl: This document provides Superusers with guidance on accessing and configuring the EMS Parameter Maintenance screen, which contains technical system parameters that must be established before using the Event Management System. The screen can be accessed through two pathways: Portal > People Management, Data Centre, EMS Parameter Maintenance, or Back Office > CoreHR, Event Management, EMS Parameter Maintenance. The document explains numerous configuration settings including the EMS On/Off toggle that globally enables or disables the system, the Email Separator field used to parse usernames on the EMS Maintenance screen, and the EMS Event Software parameter which determines whether reminders are sent through CoreHR, MS Outlook '97 (if installed), or no software at all. Critical technical settings include the SQL Dir.Path (which requires a backslash at the end to avoid errors), SQL Plus Location (typically on a server at client sites, with changes affecting all users), Mail Server (storing DNS Name or IP address), and the Create Script File and Drop Script File parameters for managing generated SQL files. Additional configuration options address email functionality through the Mail Server parameter, EMS Mail History (which clears processed emails after a specified number of days), EMS Username (identifying the sender of reminders), Administrator Email address, and a Test Run mode that redirects all reminder emails to the administrator only rather than intended recipients. This document is essential for Superusers who need to set up or troubleshoot the Event Management System's core email notification and event reminder functionality.

ss: Event Management System (EMS) notifications in CoreHR alert users automatically when specific HR data changes or dated events occur. This back office guide walks you through setting up new notifications from scratch—including selecting notification types (email, manager alerts, etc.), configuring recipients, setting timing rules, and customizing subject lines and message content. Open this document when you need to create an alert that triggers on a particular condition, such as notifying a manager before an employee's review date or sending an email when an employee status changes. The instructions also cover how to use test mode to safely validate notifications before sending them to real users.
sl: This document provides comprehensive back office instructions for creating event notifications in CoreHR through the Event Management system, enabling automated alerts based on data changes or scheduled dates. The process begins by navigating from Available Products to CoreHR, then to Event Management and Hr Event Configuration, where users select an Event Category, choose an Event Type to edit, and add a new notification with the appropriate Notification Type such as Email or Organisation Role. Users must complete type-specific fields, including Email Address and optional CC Email for email notifications, or Structure, Organisational Group, and Organisational Role for manager notifications designated with "Reports To Manager." Event timing is configured by specifying the number of days in the Generate Notification field and selecting Before or After, with an Active Indicator and optional Test Mode Indicator to limit test emails to administrators only. The notification subject and message body are built separately using plain text only (no formatting options) by selecting data sources and entering text, with the ability to insert system variables from the data source lists. Up to three conditions can be configured to control when notifications trigger, requiring users to specify a Table Name, field to compare, an operator such as equals, and a comparison value in single quotes, with multiple conditions joined by AND or OR logic. This document is intended for back office administrators responsible for configuring automated HR event notifications and managing when and to whom alerts are sent.

ss: The Event Type Maintenance screen in CoreHR allows you to configure and manage automated reminders and notifications triggered by specific HR events, such as Probation Expiry or Change of Cost Centre. Use this screen to create new reminders, edit or delete existing ones, and control key settings like when reminders fire (daily or on specific days), who receives them (email, employee role, manager, etc.), and how many days before or after an event the notification should be sent. You'll open this screen when you need to adjust how HR event notifications work in your system—for example, to change a reminder's recipient, modify the timing of alerts, or troubleshoot why notifications aren't being sent as expected. The screen displays event type details in the top half and notification settings in the bottom half, with read-only notification rows that require editing through the individual edit buttons.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on accessing and managing the Event Type Maintenance screen within CoreHR's EMS system, which is navigated through the Hr Event Configuration screen via the Data Centre in CorePortal's HR Admin Setup Settings. The Event Type Maintenance screen allows users to view and configure event types (such as Probation Expiry or Change of Cost Centre) and create, edit, or delete associated reminders and notifications triggered when database changes occur. The upper section of the screen displays event type details including the Event Type field, an editable Description field, Last Run Date, Database Trigger settings, Active Indicator toggle, Ignore Event Days threshold (60+ days), and day-of-week scheduling options (Run on Monday–Sunday), all of which can be saved via the Save button. The lower Event Notification section presents read-only notification records that can only be modified through the Edit button, with columns displaying Notification ID, Subject, Active status, Test Mode toggle, Notification Type (Email, Employee, Organisation Role, Person, Process, Reports To Manager, or Username), Recipient details, and timing controls including No of Days and Before/After fields. This document is intended for HR administrators and system configuration specialists who need to set up automated HR reminders and event-driven communications within the CoreHR system, such as sending probation expiry alerts to managers or new starter notifications to HR teams at specified intervals relative to key HR events.

ss: Event Notifications in the Access Group Portal can be configured to trigger when a new starter is entered into the system, rather than waiting until their actual start date. You can achieve this through two methods: setting up a 'Post Person' event type notification or adjusting the 'Days Before' setting to a larger number (such as 300 days) alongside the 'Ignore Event Days' configuration. Open this document if you need to ensure HR notifications are generated immediately upon creating a new employee record in People Management, Data Centre, rather than on their future start date.
sl: This document provides instructions for configuring an Event Notification within the Access Group portal system to trigger when a new starter is entered into the system. The document presents two alternative resolution methods for achieving this notification setup, both involving navigation to People Management, Data Centre, View All, and accessing the HR Event Configuration through the search function. Resolution 1 involves selecting the 'Post Person' event type from the Event Category dropdown, locating the 'Start Date' field, and editing the configuration directly at that point. Resolution 2 offers an alternative approach by setting the 'Days Before' parameter to a large number such as 300 days, which ensures that any new starter created up to 300 days before their actual start date will generate a notification upon entry. Both methods require understanding and potentially modifying the 'Ignore Event Days' setting, which by default prevents events from triggering if the trigger date falls more than 60 days in the past; this threshold must be adjusted to match your chosen 'Days Before' value to ensure proper notification behavior. The document is intended for HR administrators and portal users responsible for managing new starter workflows who need to ensure timely notifications are generated when employee records are created. Related resources referenced include guidance on creating event notifications through the EMS (Event Management System), managing event type maintenance, and troubleshooting scenarios where HR event notification emails fail to create or send as expected.

t: Send test emails to users in a non-production environment
s:
Your non-production environments, for example User Acceptance Testing (UAT), are typically configured to send emails to a test queue based on the Test Run setting being enabled. You can temporarily disable this setting, whilst testing, to validate email-based processes against real recipients.

⚠️ I...
ss: Testing email-based processes in your non-production environment (such as UAT) requires temporarily disabling the Test Run setting in EMS Parameter Maintenance so emails reach real recipients instead of a test queue. This document walks you through turning off Test Run mode, monitoring emails in the queue, triggering test emails to validate they process correctly, and critically, re-enabling Test Run afterwards to prevent accidental email delivery to users. Open this guide when you need to verify that email notifications, alerts, or automated messages work as expected before deploying changes to production.
sl: This document provides instructions for temporarily disabling test mode in non-production environments, such as User Acceptance Testing (UAT), to send emails to real recipients instead of a test queue. The process involves navigating to the Data Centre via the dashboard menu, selecting View All, then accessing EMS Parameter Maintenance to toggle the Test Run setting off, which allows emails to reach configured recipients rather than being diverted to the test queue. Once Test Run is disabled, users can check the email queue by going to Data Centre > View All > View Email Queue to monitor which emails are waiting, processing, or have been sent, with the system prioritizing the most recent emails first based on client configuration. To validate that email-based processes work correctly, users can trigger a test email by performing an action such as uploading an employee document, then verify that it appears in the queue, processes successfully, and arrives in the correct inbox. The document emphasizes the critical importance of re-enabling Test Run mode after testing is complete by returning to EMS Parameter Maintenance and toggling the setting back on, preventing unintended email delivery to real recipients in the non-production environment. This guide is typically used by system administrators, quality assurance teams, and UAT coordinators who need to validate email functionality and user workflows before deploying changes to production systems.

This document walks you through creating and managing these task lists in the Data Centre via HR Admin Setup Settings, including how to add tasks, enter optional information, and reorder steps. Open this guide when you need to set up automated task workflows for any of these HR lifecycle events or want to customize the task sequence for your organization.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on creating HR task lists within the Access Group system, which are essential sequential workflows that outline mandatory steps for key HR processes including new starters, new contracts, additional contracts, rehires, and leavers. The document offers both video and written instruction formats to help users understand and implement task list creation. ss: Marking onboarding checklist items as complete in PeopleXD's People Management module allows you to quickly finalize all outstanding onboarding tasks for an employee before processing them as a leaver. You can access an employee's incomplete checklist items through either the Employee Search or Onboarding Progress screens in the Command Centre widget, then use the "Complete All" button to mark everything at once. Open this document when you need to close out an employee's onboarding record before their exit or when you want to bulk-complete multiple outstanding tasks rather than doing them individually.
sl: This document provides instructions for completing all remaining onboarding checklist items for an employee within the Access Group system before processing them as a leaver. Users begin by navigating to People Management on the Portal and then locating the target employee through either the Employees or Onboarding option in the Command Centre widget. If accessing via the Employee Search screen, users find the employee, click View next to their record, and then select the Onboarding tab to proceed. Alternatively, users can access the Onboarding Progress screen directly, locate the employee, and click View next to their record. Once the employee record is open, incomplete checklist items are displayed under a Tasks Outstanding section, where users can click a Complete All button to mark all remaining items as complete in a single action. This process is designed to streamline offboarding workflows by ensuring all onboarding tasks are formally closed before an employee's leaver status is processed.

t: Cancelling out of an onboarding step removes system accesses
s:
Menu COREPORTAL_EMPLOYEE, or a similar profile, has been set as the menu profile to be added to an employee's account once onboarding is completed. If onboarding is left incomplete or cancelled, the system will remove this menu profile.

 

To prevent this, in Admin Settings you will need to set par...
ss: Cancelling or incompletely finishing employee onboarding in CorePortal automatically removes the menu profile (such as COREPORTAL_EMPLOYEE) from the employee's account. If you want to retain menu access even when onboarding is cancelled, you need to set the cp_onboardingmenuprofile parameter to blank in Admin Settings. Open this document if an employee has lost system menu access after their onboarding was interrupted or cancelled, or if you need to prevent menu profile removal during incomplete onboarding processes.
sl: This document explains a specific issue that occurs when employee onboarding processes are not completed in full within an Access Group system. The document describes how the COREPORTAL_EMPLOYEE menu profile (or similar profiles) is configured to be automatically added to employee accounts upon successful onboarding completion. If an employee's onboarding is left incomplete or cancelled at any point, the system automatically removes the menu profile that was intended to be assigned, which can result in unexpected loss of system access. To prevent this automatic removal behavior, administrators can navigate to Admin Settings and set the parameter cp_onboardingmenuprofile to a blank entry, which disables the automatic profile removal upon onboarding cancellation. This document is primarily useful for system administrators and onboarding managers who need to maintain consistent access permissions for employees whose onboarding processes may be interrupted, paused, or cancelled. The guidance provided helps resolve scenarios where employees experience unexplained removal of menu profiles and associated system access due to incomplete onboarding workflows.

t: Portal: Create probation alerts
s:
To create probation alerts:

From the dashboard menu, search and select Data Centre.

Scroll to Event Management.

To configure an HR Event, click HR Event Configuration.

With Event Category set to HR Events, scroll to Probation Expiry.

On the three-dot ellipses, click Edit to open Event Maintenan...
ss: Probation alerts notify relevant staff when employee probation periods are about to expire in your HR system. Set up these automated alerts through the Data Centre's Event Management section by configuring the HR Event for Probation Expiry, specifying when notifications should trigger (typically days before expiry), and defining who receives them and what the message contains. Open this guide when you need to ensure managers or HR staff are automatically reminded about upcoming probation reviews, or when setting up notification rules for the first time in your organization.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for setting up probation alerts within a portal system's Event Management feature, specifically guiding users through the HR Event Configuration process. The process begins by navigating from the dashboard menu to Data Centre, then to Event Management, where users select HR Event Configuration and locate the Probation Expiry option within the HR Events category. Users access the Event Maintenance screen via the edit function (three-dot ellipses menu) and create a new notification by specifying when the alert should trigger, typically a designated number of days before the probation expiry date. The configuration requires users to define notification recipients by selecting a Notification Type and Email Address, with a specific note that alerts intended for managers should use Organisation Role set to "Reports To." The alert content is then customized through the Message section, where users configure both the Subject and Message text by selecting an appropriate Data Source and entering custom text for each field. Once all settings are configured on the Event Maintenance screen, the probation alert can be activated using the Active indicator, though the document recommends testing the configuration in a test environment before full deployment. The document also references related resources including general event notification creation procedures, troubleshooting guidance for notification delivery issues, and back-office EMS (Event Management System) instructions.

ss: Social Hub's Policy Documents & Handbooks feature lets you upload onboarding materials that new starters can access during their first days. Follow the steps in Portal under People Management > Social Hub Configuration to add and upload files for your new employee onboarding process. Open this document if you need to make company policies, handbooks, or other reference materials available to incoming staff, or if you encounter a file permission error when trying to upload documents. You'll need the "CorePortal - Employee Document Upload" menu option enabled in your Portal account to complete uploads successfully.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for uploading policy documents and handbooks to Social Hub so that new employees can access them during the onboarding process. The process begins by navigating to the Portal, then selecting People Management and locating Social Hub Configuration to access the Policy Documents & Handbooks section. Users must click Add to create a new document entry by typing in a document name and confirming with OK, then use the Upload button to select and upload the actual document file before saving the changes. The document addresses a common permission error that may occur—specifically the "Permission to upload this file type denied" message—which can be resolved by ensuring that the CorePortal - Employee Document Upload menu option (System and reference 766324045) is enabled within one of the menu profiles assigned to the user's Portal account. This guide is intended for Portal administrators or users responsible for managing employee onboarding materials who need to make policy documents and handbooks available to new starters through the Social Hub platform. The document also references related procedures for uploading public documents for all employees and uploading documents under individual employee profiles as alternative or complementary tasks.

Open this document when you need to record why an employee is leaving the organization or update their associated leaving code in the system. sl: This document provides instructions for updating an employee's leaving reason and leaving code within the Portal application's Personal Profile screen. Once in the amendment interface, users update the reason code field and save the changes to complete the process. This document is typically used by HR administrators, managers, or personnel specialists who need to record or modify employee departure information in the system. The guide references related administrative tasks such as cost centre amendments, contract modifications, and contract hour changes, indicating it is part of a broader suite of employee record management documentation. The document addresses the need to maintain accurate leaving information in the Portal system, which is essential for employment records, compliance, and reporting purposes.

t: Display known as name on HR Admin screens
s:
You can display and search an employee's Known As/Preferred Name within HR Admin instead of their legal forename. This takes effect across the screens accessible within the Command Centre, Employee Record and Post Management.

 

Note: This doesn't impact the generate document and letter screens. To...
ss: HR Admin allows you to display and search employees by their Known As or Preferred Name instead of their legal forename across the Command Centre, Employee Record, and Post Management screens. You enable this feature by navigating to Site Settings, opening Admin Settings, finding the 'cp_hradmin_knownas' setting, and changing its value to Y. Open this document if you need employees' preferred names to show in HR Admin searches and screens, or if your organization wants to use known as names as the primary identifier in these areas. Note that this setting only affects HR Admin screens—document and letter generation screens require a separate configuration.
sl: This document provides instructions for enabling the display of an employee's Known As or Preferred Name throughout HR Admin screens as an alternative to their legal forename. The feature applies across multiple areas of the system including the Command Centre, Employee Record, and Post Management sections, though it does not affect document and letter generation screens which are covered separately. To implement this functionality, users must navigate to the Site Settings widget, access Admin Settings, and locate the configuration setting 'cp_hradmin_knownas' which they can then edit to change its value to Y. Once this setting is enabled, any employee who has a known as name recorded in the system will automatically have that name display across the relevant HR Admin screens instead of their legal forename, and this name will also be searchable within these areas. The document is primarily intended for HR administrators and system configuration staff who have access to Site Settings and Admin Settings to manage organizational preferences. Additional related resources are referenced for related tasks such as granting HR access to users, preventing name updates, and enabling Known As names in document generation processes.

t: How to report on surveys
s:
Reporting on surveys using Insight
To facilitate reporting on surveys, special survey views exist in Insight only.
When a survey is created, a dynamic view is created for Insight with the same name as the survey.
If the name of the survey is 'New Job Survey', then the view in Insight will be 'New Jo...
ss: Survey reporting is handled differently depending on whether you're using Insight or an external reporting tool connected to PeopleXD. In Insight, dynamic survey views are automatically created with the same name as your survey (for example, "New Job Survey (Personnel)"), and you can combine these with the HR PERSON MASTER view to see which employees answered each survey. If you're using an external reporting tool, survey data is stored in the cp_custom_forms table, but the specialized Insight survey views aren't available in external tools. Open this document when you need to set up survey reporting and want to understand which tool and approach will work best for your reporting needs.
sl: This document explains how to generate reports on surveys within the Access Group system, covering both the native Insight platform and external reporting tools. In Insight, special survey views are automatically created whenever a survey is established, with the view name derived from the survey name followed by "(Personnel)"—for example, a survey titled "New Job Survey" generates a corresponding Insight view called "New Job Survey (Personnel)". To produce meaningful reports in Insight that link survey responses to specific employees, users must include the HR PERSON MASTER view and incorporate its fields for person reference, forename, and surname. When using external reporting tools connected to the PeopleXD database, users have access to most views and tables, but the specialized survey views created in Insight are not available in external tools since they exist exclusively within Insight. However, external reporting tools can access the underlying survey data stored in the cp_custom_forms table, providing an alternative reporting pathway. The document recommends using Insight for survey reporting purposes because of its specially configured views that are optimized for this function, making it the preferred solution over external tools for this specific reporting need. This guidance is intended for users who need to analyze survey data and track responses at the employee level, whether they are working within Insight or attempting to access survey information through connected external reporting platforms.

t: Portal: Amend a cost centre for an employee
s:
The cost centre assigned to an employee's contract can be updated. Follow the below steps.

From the dashboard menu, in the search bar, select People Management.

Search the employee, click VIEW, then click Contracts.

🤓Tip: If the employee has...
ss: Amending a cost centre for an employee in PeopleXD Portal involves navigating to the employee's contract record through People Management and Command Centre, then updating the cost centre assignment through the Amendments section. You'll specify an effective date for the change, select a reason, and save the update—with the system creating a new sequence if the date differs from the current one. Open this guide when you need to reassign an employee to a different cost centre, such as during internal transfers or organizational restructuring. Note that if the reason for the change is linked to salary adjustments, you'll need to reapply salary details afterward.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for updating the cost centre assigned to an employee's contract within the Portal system, accessed through the Access Group Help Centre. Users navigate from the dashboard menu by selecting People Management in the search bar, then accessing Command Centre and choosing View under Employees to locate the specific employee. Once the employee is found and selected, users click VIEW and then Contracts, with an option to select from multiple contracts using a drop-down menu if applicable. The amendment process involves clicking UPDATE under the Amendments section, selecting a new Cost Centre, and proceeding to the next screen where an Effective Date must be entered. The system creates a new sequence if the effective date is later than the current sequence date, or updates the existing sequence if the date matches. Users must select a Reason for the amendment and click SAVE to confirm the changes, with an important caveat that if the reason is linked to salary changes, salary details must be reapplied afterward. This document is typically used by payroll administrators, HR professionals, or portal users responsible for maintaining accurate employee cost centre allocations in response to organisational changes or employee transfers.

t: Portal: Language pack overview
s: The language pack contains a library of all labels and phrases used within PeopleXD. Authorised users can update the labels and phrases displayed on screen, either through the Site Manager widget or by selecting the Enable Language Pack option from their user profile menu. Watch the video or follow ...
ss: The language pack in PeopleXD lets authorized users customize all on-screen labels and phrases used throughout the system. You can update default labels using either the Site Manager widget or by enabling Language Pack mode from your user profile menu, then search for and modify specific text. Open this document when you need to change system terminology, translate labels into different languages, or adjust default wording to match your organization's preferences. Note that changes can take up to 72 hours to appear across all instances in the system.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide to managing and customizing labels and phrases within PeopleXD using the language pack feature, which is a library of all text labels displayed throughout the system. Authorized users can update these labels through two methods: the Site Manager widget accessible from the dashboard menu, or the Enable Language Pack option located in their user profile menu (represented by a circle icon in the top right corner). Using the Site Manager widget, users enter the Site Manager in the dashboard search bar, open the Language Pack section, search for specific labels using the search field, and then click into the Label field to replace text directly, with changes saving automatically across all instances in the system. The Enable Language Pack mode offers an alternative approach where users navigate to the specific screen containing the label to be updated, enable the mode from their user profile, hover over highlighted green fields, enter new phrase text in a pop-up window, and save changes before disabling the mode through the user profile menu. The document notes that while multiple languages are available within PeopleXD and are managed by Access, users can modify the default labels supplied for any language, though it may take up to 72 hours for changes to become effective. For users experiencing issues where amendments are not visible after 72 hours, the document recommends clearing the browser cache or switching to private or incognito mode to resolve potential display problems.

t: Portal: Create a new User Defined Field
s:
User Defined Fields (UDFs) are used to hold data on the system that are specific to an individual organisation and are not available as standard. To find out how to configure your user defined data, watch the video or follow the below steps.

ss: User Defined Fields (UDFs) let you store custom data in the People Management system that isn't available as a standard field, tailored to your organisation's specific needs. This document walks you through creating a new UDF in the Data Centre, setting up data labels, and configuring CorePortal display and update permissions for employees and managers. Open this guide when you need to add custom data fields to track organisation-specific information, or when you want to control how employees and managers view and edit these fields through CorePortal. It's recommended to test your UDF configuration in a test environment before applying changes to your live system.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for creating User Defined Fields (UDFs) in the Portal, which are custom data fields that hold organization-specific information not available as standard system fields. The process begins by navigating to the People Management Dashboard, accessing the Data Centre tab, and opening the HR Admin Setup Settings option to reach the User Defined Objects section. Users must create a new UDF by clicking Add and entering a Reference Code and Description, then proceed to configure data labels through the three-dot menu to ensure the Active toggle is enabled. The Advanced settings menu allows administrators to specify whether the UDF applies to Employees or Post Appointments, and to configure three key Portal visibility toggles: Display on CorePortal (controls whether employees and managers can view the field), Allow Update on CorePortal (controls editing permissions), and Hide Dates on CorePortal (removes From Date and To Date fields from all Portal screens affecting employee, manager, and HR administrator views). The document emphasizes best practice by recommending that all configuration changes be tested in a test environment before deployment to live systems. This resource is intended for HR administrators and system configurators who need to extend the Portal's data capture capabilities for their specific organizational requirements, with related guidance available for granting HR Portal access, updating employee information, and troubleshooting UDF reporting issues.

t: ModSecurity checking and issues
s: ModSecurity is an Application Firewall that filters, monitors, and blocks HTTP traffic to and from a web application. By inspecting HTTP traffic, it can prevent attacks stemming from web application security flaws, such as SQL injection, cross-site scripting (XSS), file inclusion, and security misco...
ss: ModSecurity is an application firewall that protects web applications by filtering and blocking potentially harmful HTTP traffic, including threats like SQL injection, cross-site scripting, and file inclusion attacks. Certain characters and syntax—such as parentheses, exclamation marks, equals signs, HTML formatting tags, and URL parameters with ?ref= —can trigger ModSecurity blocks and cause 403 errors when entered in text or comment fields. If you encounter a 403 Forbidden error while using Access Group systems, check whether you've included any of these flagged items in your input and remove them before saving. This document helps you identify and resolve ModSecurity-related blocks that prevent you from submitting forms or saving data in your application.
sl: This document explains ModSecurity, an Application Firewall that filters, monitors, and blocks HTTP traffic to and from web applications by inspecting requests to prevent attacks such as SQL injection, cross-site scripting (XSS), file inclusion, and security misconfigurations. The document identifies specific items and syntax that are likely to be blocked or trigger errors when used in the system, including HTML elements like SRC and Style tags, special characters such as parentheses, exclamation marks, equals signs, and angle brackets, formatting syntax like /bold, and URL patterns containing query parameters like ?ref=Link, as well as references to images and logos. When users encounter a 403 Forbidden error while working with text or comment fields, the document advises them to remove any of these problematic items from their input and save again to resolve the issue. The document references a related article on the "Error - '403: Forbidden'" topic for additional troubleshooting information. This resource is primarily used by system administrators, content editors, and end users who need to understand why certain content is being blocked and how to modify their submissions to comply with the firewall's security rules. The document explicitly notes that the list of blocked items provided is not exhaustive, meaning other syntax or content may also trigger ModSecurity filters.

t: System emails not being delivered
s:
Emails may not be reaching their intended recipient as they are being treated as spam by their email provider or an error occurred whilst being processed by the system. To check this, follow the below steps.

 

Review the email queue

You'll need to view the email queue to determine if the email ha...
ss: System emails generated in PeopleXD may fail to reach recipients if they're blocked as spam by the recipient's email provider or if an error occurs during processing. Use the Email Queue viewer in either the People Management portal or CorePersonnel back office to check whether emails were successfully processed and left the PeopleXD server. If emails show as processed with no errors, contact your IT department or email provider as the issue lies outside the system. If emails aren't processing correctly, verify that the EMS Username setting matches the Administrator Email field (typically peoplexd@accessacloud.com), as misconfigurations commonly cause emails to be flagged as junk, especially with Gmail and Hotmail accounts.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving issues where system emails fail to reach intended recipients in PeopleXD, a situation that typically occurs either because emails are being filtered as spam by the recipient's email provider or because an error occurred during system processing. The document describes two primary diagnostic and resolution procedures: first, reviewing the email queue to determine whether emails have been successfully generated and processed by the system, which can be accessed via the People Management dashboard by clicking View All on the Data Centre widget and searching for View Email Queue, or alternatively through CorePersonnel by selecting Reference > Utilities > View Email Queue in the back office interface. If emails show a Processed status in the Email Queue with no errors displayed, this indicates the system is functioning correctly and the user should contact their local IT department or email provider, as the emails are likely being treated as spam or junk by the recipient's email system. The document also addresses a specific configuration issue where an incorrectly configured EMS Username setting can cause emails to be flagged as junk mail, a problem that frequently affects Gmail and Hotmail accounts. To resolve this configuration problem, users can access EMS Parameter Maintenance through the People Management dashboard (Data Centre widget > View All) or through CorePersonnel (Reference > Utilities), and must ensure that the EMS Username field matches the Administrator Email field, with both typically containing peoplexd@accessacloud.com. This document is designed for system administrators and support staff responsible for managing email delivery and system configuration within PeopleXD environments.

t: Create a HAR file in Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge
s: There will be very rare occasions that the support team are not able to replicate an issue that has been raised to us. In these cases our Developers will require some information from the browser you are using when you experience the issue. This can be recorded and sent to us via HAR file, which you...
ss: When the Access Group support team cannot reproduce a reported issue, they may ask you to provide a HAR file—a browser recording that captures your interaction with the system and helps developers identify the problem. A HAR (HTTP Archive) file is a JSON-formatted log that records all network activity and code interactions without requiring third-party software. Open this document if support has requested a HAR file and you need step-by-step instructions to create one in Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge using the built-in Developer Tools. You'll learn how to record the issue, download the file, and securely send it to the development team.
sl: This document provides instructions for creating and submitting a HAR (HTTP Archive) file to the Access Group support team when they cannot replicate a reported technical issue. A HAR file is a JSON-formatted archive that records browser interactions with a website and allows developers to analyze code-level details to identify problems. The document covers the step-by-step process for both Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge: navigating to a point before the issue occurs, opening Developer Tools using the F12 key, accessing the Network tab (expanding the view with the >> icon if necessary), enabling the Preserve log checkbox to maintain data across tab changes, and then recreating the reported issue while the tools automatically capture relevant data. Once the issue is fully replicated, users download the HAR file using the download icon and save it locally, with a recommendation to zip and password-protect it for security. The final step involves attaching the file to an email reply to the support request and providing the password in a separate message. This document is essential for end users experiencing technical problems with Access Group applications who need to provide developers with detailed browser interaction data that cannot be easily captured through standard support channels.

t: Email notification 'Notification - Bank Details have been Updated.' received
s:

ss: When an employee updates their bank details in PeopleXD, an automated notification email is sent that cannot be disabled, but you can customize its content. Use the Administrator Dashboard to navigate to Site Admin > Admin Settings and modify the email body parameters (cp_email_pay_prefix and cp_ext_bank_mail_body) to change the notification message. Open this document if you need to configure or customize the wording of the "Bank Details have been Updated" notification that employees receive, or if you want to understand how the email text is generated and which settings control different sections of the message.
sl: This document explains how to manage the email notification that is automatically sent whenever an employee updates their bank details through the portal. The notification email is mandatory and cannot be disabled entirely, but system administrators can customize the message content across multiple components. To configure the notification, administrators must navigate to the Administrator Dashboard, access Site Admin, then Admin Settings, where they can search for and modify the parameter cp_email_pay_prefix to update the email body. The email message is constructed from three distinct parts: the opening text uses the parameter cp_ext_bank_mail_bod (for example, "Your bank details have been updated via PeopleXD"), which can be edited in Admin Settings; the middle section containing timestamp and URL information ("Updated on date @ time You can view full details @ the following Web address") is managed through the Language Pack; and the closing text uses the cp_email_pay_prefix parameter. After making any configuration changes to these parameters, administrators must save the updates for them to take effect. This document is primarily used by system administrators and portal managers who need to customize employee communications regarding bank detail updates in the PeopleXD system.

t: Label not changed via the language pack
s:

ss: When you update a system label through the language pack, changes can take up to 72 hours to appear in your interface. If you need to see the updated label immediately, try clearing your browser cache or viewing the page in private or incognito mode to bypass cached versions. Open this document if label changes aren't displaying right away and you want to troubleshoot the delay without waiting the full 72 hours. It also helps you verify that your language pack update was actually saved correctly.
sl: This document addresses the issue of system label changes made through the language pack not appearing immediately in the user interface, explaining that such amendments can require up to 72 hours to take effect across the system. The document provides users with troubleshooting steps to work around the standard processing delay without waiting for the full 72-hour period to elapse. The first recommended action is to clear the cache from the user's browser, which can help remove outdated cached versions of the labels preventing the new text from displaying. If clearing the browser cache does not resolve the visibility issue, users are instructed to check the relevant page using private or incognito mode browsing, which bypasses locally stored cache files that might be causing the problem. The document also suggests that if neither of these initial troubleshooting steps rectifies the issue, users should verify that the update was actually applied to the system by checking the amendment through available verification methods. This guidance is particularly useful for administrators and users managing language pack configurations who need to confirm label changes are working correctly or require faster confirmation than the standard 72-hour processing window allows.

ss: The org chart employee card in PeopleXD displays employee contact and organizational information including name, job title, department, email, and phone number. This document explains how to customize which details appear on the card by configuring administrator settings—such as changing the organizational level from department to location, switching the displayed contact type from home phone to mobile, or toggling the home phone number visibility. Open this if you need to modify what employee information is visible when users view the org chart, or if you're setting up the org chart display for the first time and want to control which contact details appear.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre provides a comprehensive guide to configuring which employee details appear on individual employee cards within an organizational chart display system. The employee card can display default information including job title, name, initials or employee photo, department, email address, and phone number, with certain fields marked as configurable. The document describes three main configuration processes, all accessed through the Administrator Dashboard > Site Manager > Admin Settings path: adjusting the organizational level displayed (using the cp_org_structure_element parameter, with examples like LOC for Location), changing the contact type shown on cards (via the cp_org_contact_type parameter, such as MOBILE for work mobile phone), and enabling the home phone number display (through the cp_org_show_home_no parameter set to Y). A critical prerequisite is noted: the home phone number must be enabled before alternative contact types can be displayed on the card, otherwise the system will show the employee's extension by default. This configuration guide is primarily used by system administrators who need to customize how employee information is presented in organizational charts across their portal systems. The document also references related functionality such as assigning organizational roles to employees, enabling org chart access, and managing menu profile assignments.

t: Error - 'Invalid File Template. Please download the latest template... '
s:
If you try to upload a file using the data migration functionality with the latest template and receive the message, 'Invalid File Template. Please download the latest template...', check that the file is correctly delimited. Use a pipe delimiter ( | ) to separate the data. 

For example, '00112200|...
ss: When uploading files through the data migration functionality, you may encounter an "Invalid File Template" error message even when using the current template. This error typically occurs when your file isn't properly delimited—the system requires pipe characters ( | ) to separate data fields in your migration file. Check that each data field is separated by a pipe delimiter, following the format: '00112200|1234567|YYY|XXXXX||ABCDEF'. Open this article if your data migration uploads are being rejected and you need to verify your file formatting.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses a specific error message that users encounter when attempting to upload files through the data migration functionality. The error message reads 'Invalid File Template. Please download the latest template...' and indicates that there is a formatting issue with the file being uploaded. The primary cause of this error is incorrect file delimitation, meaning the data fields are not properly separated according to the system's requirements. The document specifies that users must use a pipe delimiter (|) to separate data fields within the migration file, and provides a concrete example of correctly formatted data: '00112200|1234567|YYY|XXXXX||ABCDEF'. This guide is intended for users working with Access Group's data migration tools who need to troubleshoot file upload failures and understand the proper technical formatting standards. By following the delimitation instructions outlined here, users can resolve the template validation error and successfully upload their migration files to the system.

ss: When your organisation adds new roles or changes job structures, you'll need to set up new job title codes in the Portal system. Open this guide if you're adding job titles for the first time or need step-by-step instructions for entering them into the system. sl: This document provides instructions for adding new job title codes to the system when organisational changes require updates to job title descriptions. The process involves navigating from the dashboard menu by searching for and selecting Data Centre, then accessing Reference Data and clicking on Job title Codes to reach the configuration area. Users must click the Add button, complete all required fields in the form, and save the entry to create the new job title code. A critical warning emphasises that job title codes must contain only alphanumeric characters, and users should avoid using special characters such as ampersands or other symbols, as these can negatively impact other parts of the system. This document is typically used by administrators or human resources personnel who manage organisational structure and employee records and need to maintain accurate job classification systems. The document also references related tasks such as creating post profile records, setting up terms and conditions profiles, and amending job titles for existing employees, as well as alternative methods for performing this task in the back office system.

t: Data Migration tool - explained and access
