ss: The Data Migration tool enables bulk uploading of data during initial system setup by reading delimited files, validating content in temporary tables, and then migrating verified data into the software for active use. You'll open this document to understand how the tool works, learn which menu profile (COREPORTAL_DATAMIGRATION_USER) grants the necessary permissions, and find guidance on completing uploads and processing updates. Use this when you're setting up your system and need to load large volumes of data efficiently rather than entering records manually.
sl: This document explains the Data Migration tool, which enables bulk uploading of specific data during initial system setup and configuration. The tool operates through a three-stage process: it reads delimited files and parses each field into temporary tables, performs validation on the contents, and then allows users to migrate the validated data into the software for full operational use. The document provides guidance on navigating key screens throughout this workflow, with additional help available on the dashboard, upload screens, migrate screens, and completed screens. To enable users to perform data migration tasks, administrators can assign the pre-configured menu profile COREPORTAL_DATAMIGRATION_USER, which includes all necessary menu options for completing data migration uploads and processing updates. The document addresses common issues users may encounter, such as the "Invalid File Template" error, and references related functionality including bulk data updates via the Data Migration Update Facility and employee deletion procedures. This resource is primarily used by system administrators and data migration specialists during the implementation phase of Access Group software, as well as by authorized users who need to perform regular bulk data uploads and maintenance tasks.

t: Portal: Upload data migration files
s:
To upload a data migration file, download the required template, open it to enter the necessary data, then save and upload it. Follow the steps below.

Download the template files from the Data Migration Templates widget.

You might need to rename the file with a .csv file extension.

Open Microsoft...
ss: Data migration file uploads in PeopleXD require downloading a template, formatting it correctly in Excel, and saving it as a CSV file before uploading through the portal. The process involves opening the template with the text import wizard, selecting the pipe character as the delimiter, and entering your data below the header rows without modification. Open this document when you need step-by-step instructions for preparing and uploading employee or system data files to PeopleXD. You'll also find guidance on using helper files and avoiding common formatting errors that prevent successful uploads.
sl: This document provides instructions for uploading data migration files into the PeopleXD system, guiding users through the complete process from template download to final upload. Users must first download the required template files from the Data Migration Templates widget, then open the template in Microsoft Excel using File > Open rather than opening it directly, which triggers the text import wizard where users must select the pipe character (|) as the delimiter and choose Text as the data format. After completing the import wizard, users enter their data starting from the row beneath the column headings, which PeopleXD uses to identify the template file type during upload. The document emphasizes critical requirements that the top two rows of the file must match the blank template exactly without any additional data such as pipe characters, and users must not rename or modify these rows. When saving the completed file, users must select Save as and choose the .csv (comma delimited) format, though they may need to rename files with a .csv file extension initially. This document helps resolve the error message "Invalid File Template. Please download the latest template..." and is typically used by administrators or data managers performing bulk employee record updates or data migrations into the PeopleXD system through the Data Migration tool.

t: Amending contact types
s:
To add a new contact type or to review existing contacts, follow the steps below.

 

Portal

Navigate to the People Management dashboard.

Click Data Centre, then click Open next to Reference Data.

Select Contact Type.

Press Add.

Enter a unique code and description for the new contact.

Enable t...
ss: Contact types are custom categories for employee contact information managed in PeopleXD's Portal or CorePersonnel back office. This document walks you through adding new contact types and configuring whether employees can view or update them via the Employee Self-Service (ESS) portal. Open this guide when you need to create a new contact type, enable self-service access for specific contact fields, or restrict which contact details employees can modify. You'll also need to ensure users have the Contact Information Update menu option enabled to make changes to their contact details.
sl: This document provides instructions for adding new contact types or reviewing existing contact types within an organisation's personnel management system, accessible through two different interfaces: the Portal and the Back Office (CorePersonnel). In the Portal, users navigate to the People Management dashboard, access the Data Centre, select Contact Type, and use the Add function to enter a unique code and description while enabling the ESS Display and Update fields before saving. In the Back Office, users access CorePersonnel, navigate to Reference > Reference A-C > Contact Types, click the green plus button to add a new record, and toggle the ESS display and ESS update options as needed before saving. The document explains that ESS Display controls visibility of contact types in the My Contact Details section, while ESS Update determines whether employees can modify those contact details, and administrators can selectively disable update access for specific email or contact types to restrict user permissions. Users must also have the menu option "Contact Information Update" enabled within their assigned menu profiles in order to update any contact details in the system. This guidance is typically used by system administrators, HR configuration specialists, or personnel managers who need to establish or modify the types of contact information employees can view and maintain within their organisation's personnel system.

t: Portal: Maintaining employee addresses
s:
The system is designed so that only HR admins have the effective date option when changing the address, employees just overwrite the current value.

 

To update an employee address as an administrator, follow the steps below.

In the portal, go to People Management dashboard.

Go to the Command Cen...
ss: Updating employee addresses in the Portal requires HR admins to navigate the People Management dashboard, locate the employee, and edit their contact information with an effective date. HR administrators can maintain a complete address history by adding new address records with future effective dates rather than overwriting existing entries. Use this guide when you need to update an employee's address in the system while preserving historical records, or when you want to set a future address change that will take effect on a specific date.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for HR administrators to maintain and update employee address information within the Portal system, specifically through the People Management dashboard. The process involves navigating to the Command Centre widget, selecting VIEW next to Employees, searching for the target employee, accessing the Contact Information tab, and then selecting the three dot ellipsis next to Default Address to edit address details, where administrators have access to an Effective Date field that regular employees do not possess. The document explains how to preserve address history by using the Add Address function in the Address Maintenance screen, with the capability to set different address types (Home or Default) and future effective dates to create multiple address records. It clarifies the distinction between different update methods: editing addresses through the Address Maintenance screen with a Home address type and future effective date will update both the Personal Profile screen and create a new record, while using a Default address type will only add a record to the Address Maintenance screen without updating the Personal Profile. The document notes that direct edits to the Personal Profile screen or updates via the Portal interface will only modify existing address entries rather than creating new historical records. This guidance is essential for HR administrators who need to maintain accurate employee contact information while preserving a complete audit trail of address changes over time.

t: Back Office: Create a new User Defined Field
s:
User Defined Fields (UDFs) are used to hold data on the system that are specific to an individual organisation and are not available as standard. To configure these, follow the steps below.

🤓Tip: User defined fields can also be configured in the portal.

Select CorePersonnel.

Select Reference and ...
ss: User Defined Fields (UDFs) in CorePersonnel allow you to create custom data fields specific to your organization that aren't available as standard fields. This document walks you through creating a new UDF in the Back Office, including how to set the code, description, security permissions, and advanced parameters like where the field should appear (Employee Personal Profile or Appointment Details). You'll also learn how to configure data types for your UDF such as List Item, Numeric, Date, or Text Area. Open this document when you need to add custom data fields to capture organization-specific information in your CorePersonnel system.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for creating User Defined Fields (UDFs) in the Back Office system, which are custom data fields tailored to an individual organisation's specific requirements that are not available as standard features. The basic creation process involves navigating to CorePersonnel, then Reference and Reference Q-Z, clicking User Defined Field Codes, inserting a new row using the green plus icon, and entering a code and description before saving. Beyond the basic setup, administrators can configure additional settings through the Security Required option to set per-user access permissions and the Advanced settings to define where the UDF data will appear, such as on the User Data screen in the Employees Personal Profile or in the User Data section of the Appointment Details screen. For UDFs that require more detailed information, up to 12 additional fields can be created as pop-ups with Data Labels and User Data entries. The document outlines five Data Type options available for these fields: List Item (for pick lists created via the Defined List Items button), Numeric (for numeric-only input), Date (for date function recording), Text Area (for free-form text entry), and Reference (for Manager Request configuration), with a specific note that start dates cannot be restricted. This guide is intended for back office administrators and system configuration users who need to customize the system to capture organisation-specific data, and the document also notes that UDFs can alternatively be configured in the portal.

t: Update gender identity reference data
s:
Gender identities can be updated or maintained in either the portal or back office. In both instances, the following applies.

The code can be a maximum of six alphanumeric characters.

The description can contain up to 40 alphanumeric characters.

There is no active indicator. Once created, all ite...
ss: Gender identities are reference data that can be created and updated in either the People Management portal or the CorePersonnel back office. Each gender identity entry requires a code (up to six alphanumeric characters) and a description (up to 40 characters), and all created items are immediately available for selection without needing to activate them. Use this document if you need to add new gender identity options to your system or modify existing ones in either the portal's Data Centre or the back office's Reference section.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for updating and maintaining gender identity reference data in either the portal or back office of an Access Group system. The document specifies technical constraints for the data being created: codes can be a maximum of six alphanumeric characters, descriptions can contain up to 40 alphanumeric characters, and there is no active indicator, meaning all created items are automatically available for selection once established. For portal users, the process involves navigating to People Management > Data centre > View all > Other References, selecting Gender Identity from the Reference Type field, and then clicking Add to enter the code and description before saving. For back office users, the equivalent process requires navigating to CorePersonnel > Reference > Reference Q - Z > Other References, updating the Reference Type field to GNDRID (Gender Identity), using the green tick button to search, and either clicking into a blank row or using the green plus button to create a new entry before entering the code and description and saving. This document serves administrators and system managers responsible for configuring and maintaining organizational reference data within the Access Group HR management system, ensuring consistent gender identity options are available across employee records and forms.

t: Back Office: Generating an Employee Status report
s:
An Employee Status report can be generated through the personal profile of an employee. This will highlight the main details for an employee on CorePay and CorePersonnel, including certain audit aspects of the software.

 

Generating the status report

Click CorePersonnel, Maintenance, Personal Pro...
ss: The Employee Status report is generated through CorePersonnel and CorePay to display key employee details and audit information for a specific worker. Use this report to verify an employee's current payroll status—whether they're Fully Active, Fully Dormant, Leaving, Rejoining, or in a transition state—and to confirm their appointment history matches their payroll records. Open this document when you need to troubleshoot employee status issues, validate payroll setup, or provide documentation for cases involving employee appointments or payroll changes. The report also helps identify when employees have been correctly processed as leavers, rejoiners, or when status updates are pending after payroll runs.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide for generating and interpreting Employee Status reports within the CorePersonnel and CorePay systems, serving HR and payroll administrators who need to verify employee records during onboarding, termination, or status change scenarios. The report is generated by navigating to CorePersonnel > Maintenance > Personal Profile, querying the employee, selecting "View Employee History" from the Select Detail list, and clicking "Status Report," which outputs a PDF file through the Report Destination drop-down menu. The document explains that employees must appear as "Fully Active" (with Secondary Status = 'S') once created in CorePersonnel and added to CorePay, and as "Fully Dormant" (Secondary Status = 'Z') once ended and processed as a leaver by Payroll. It details multiple status transitions including employees marked as "Leaving" (with New Secondary Status = 'Z'), "Leaver-Rejoiner" (New Secondary Status = 'Y'), and "Rejoiner-Leaver" (New Secondary Status = 'T'), each with specific field requirements in the Appointment History section that must align with corresponding CorePay records. The document emphasizes critical constraints such as the limitation that Payroll cannot process more than two status changes in a single period and that Continuous Employment thresholds determine whether an employee can rejoin within the same payroll period. Users should attach generated Status Reports to cases involving Employee Appointments or Payroll Status issues and ensure that all Payroll Status values match the Appointment History to resolve discrepancies or configuration problems.

t: Portal: Incorrect post title, job title, or department
s:
This can be due to the record not being updated on Substantive Maintenance screen. This update can be only done in Backoffice in:

In CorePersonnel navigate to:​​​​​​

Maintenance, Post management, Substantive maintenance.

Add record with current commenced appointment.

If record is already there t...
ss: When an employee's post title, job title, or department displays incorrectly in the Portal, the issue often stems from outdated records in CorePersonnel's Substantive Maintenance screen. You can fix this in Backoffice by navigating to CorePersonnel > Maintenance > Post management > Substantive maintenance, then either adding a new record with the current appointment or refreshing an existing record by temporarily changing the substantive date forward one day and back again. This process updates the HR record and forces the Portal to refresh the employee's job title information. If these steps don't resolve the problem, contact support with a reference to this article for further data refresh assistance.
sl: This document provides guidance for resolving issues where an employee's post title, job title, or department displays incorrectly in the Portal system, which typically occurs when the corresponding record has not been updated on the Substantive Maintenance screen. The fix requires accessing CorePersonnel's Backoffice system and navigating to Maintenance > Post management > Substantive maintenance, where users must either add a new record with the current commenced appointment if no record exists, or modify an existing record by temporarily changing the substantive date forward by one day and then reverting it back to the original date (for example, changing a date of 01-NOV-2018 to 02-NOV-2018 and then back again). This date manipulation process forces a refresh of the HR record and Portal data, which resolves the display discrepancy and ensures the correct job title appears in the Portal. The document is intended for HR and personnel administrators or support staff who manage employee records in CorePersonnel and need to troubleshoot Portal display errors related to job titles and departments. If the prescribed steps do not resolve the issue, users are advised to contact support with a reference to this article, as support staff may need to perform additional data refresh operations on their end.

t: Back Office: Amend a cost centre for an employee
s:
To amend a cost centre for an employee, follow the steps below.

Click Personnel, Maintenance, Personal Profile.

Query the employee.

Select Post Profile.

Select Amend Appointment. 

Type the New Effective Date for this change.

📌Note: A new sequence will be created if the date's later than the cu...
ss: Updating an employee's cost centre assignment in the Back Office Personnel module involves navigating to their Personal Profile and Amend Appointment section, then selecting a new cost centre with an effective date. Use this guide when you need to reassign an employee to a different cost centre for budgeting or departmental tracking purposes, or when an employee transfers between cost centres. The process creates a new sequence record if the effective date is later than the current sequence, or updates the existing sequence if using the same date.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for updating an employee's cost centre assignment within the Back Office system. Users navigate through the Personnel menu, then Maintenance, and finally Personal Profile to access the employee record, after which they query the specific employee and select their Post Profile followed by Amend Appointment. The process requires entering a New Effective Date for when the cost centre change should take effect, with an important system behavior note that a new sequence will be created if the date is later than the current sequence date, while the same date will update the existing sequence. The user then selects the List of Values (LOV) beside the Cost Centre field to choose the new cost centre from available options. This document is typically used by HR or payroll administrators in the Back Office system who need to reassign employees to different cost centres for budgeting or organisational purposes, whether due to departmental moves, project transfers, or cost allocation changes. The final step is clicking Save to confirm the amendment, which completes the cost centre update for the employee's record.

t: What is the Reference Type TEXT AREA used for in User Defined Objects
s:
When a user clicks on ... and selects Advanced option, they will see different User Defined Types e.g Employee, Manager Requests, Post Appointment, eRecruitment.
​
The Text Area reference type is reserved for User Defined Codes linked to eRecruitment only.
Text Area reference types cannot be used wi...
ss: The Text Area reference type is a specific field option used exclusively within eRecruitment User Defined Objects. This reference type allows you to create text input fields for recruitment-related custom codes and cannot be applied to other User Defined Code types like Employee, Manager Requests, or Post Appointment. Open this document when you're setting up custom recruitment forms or fields in your eRecruitment module and need to understand which reference types are available for your specific use case.
sl: This document explains the purpose and constraints of the Text Area reference type within User Defined Objects in the Access Group system. When users navigate to the Advanced option in the system, they can select from various User Defined Types including Employee, Manager Requests, Post Appointment, and eRecruitment. The Text Area reference type is specifically reserved for use only with User Defined Codes that are linked to eRecruitment functionality, making it a specialized field type with limited application scope. A critical constraint detailed in the document is that Text Area reference types cannot be applied to any other types of User Defined Codes beyond eRecruitment, preventing their use in Employee, Manager Requests, or Post Appointment categories. This document would be most useful for system administrators, HR personnel, and eRecruitment specialists who are configuring User Defined Fields and need to understand which reference types are appropriate for their specific implementation context. The document references related configuration tasks including creating new User Defined Fields in the Portal and Back Office environments, configuring CorePersonnel users, and troubleshooting issues with User Defined Field reports in Insight.

The process also notes that corresponding updates may be needed in PeopleXD People Management depending on how your organisation captures this information. sl: This document provides instructions for updating reference data descriptions for HESA fields within the Access Group's Back Office system, specifically targeting users who need to modify existing reference data rather than create new entries. The process begins in Back Office by navigating to CoreHR from the Available Products list, then accessing the CoreHESA menu and selecting "HESA Reference Data" from the Select Option list. This guidance is primarily intended for HR administrators and Back Office users responsible for maintaining HESA (Higher Education Statistics Agency) compliance and reference data accuracy within their organization's CoreHR configuration.

t: Continuous Service Date not Populating
s:
There is a rule set up that dictates when a continuous Service Date is calculated on the Eligible Service Rules screen:

Go to People Management Dashboard

Go to Data Centre, View All, Eligible Service Rules

Select 'Continuous Service' from the dropdown list and you will see the current rules set u...
ss: The Continuous Service Date calculation in PeopleXD is controlled by rules configured on the Eligible Service Rules screen within the People Management Dashboard. If your continuous service dates aren't populating correctly, you may need to add new lines to capture additional employee types or enable the rule using the toggle switch. Open this document when you're troubleshooting missing or incorrect continuous service date values in your employee records, or when setting up rules for a new employee type that isn't being recognized by the system.
sl: This document explains how to configure the Continuous Service Date calculation in the Access Group system by navigating to and adjusting rules on the Eligible Service Rules screen. Users access this configuration by starting from the People Management Dashboard, then proceeding to Data Centre, selecting View All, and opening the Eligible Service Rules section. The document addresses the specific problem of the Continuous Service Date not populating by identifying that a rule set governs when this date is calculated, and users can view the current rules by selecting 'Continuous Service' from a dropdown list to see which rules are activated. The primary resolution involves adding new lines to the existing rule to ensure all outstanding employee types are captured within the system's calculations. Users must also enable the rule by toggling it to the 'on' position to activate it and ensure that the Continuous Service Date populates correctly for future records. This document is designed for system administrators or People Management personnel who manage employee data configuration and need to troubleshoot why continuous service dates are not automatically generating as expected.

ss: Cost centre assignments in PeopleXD are controlled by the post structure setup, and some fields may be hardcoded and unable to be modified. If you're unable to update a cost centre for an employee, you'll need to check the Post Profile Maintenance settings in People Management to determine whether the cost centre field is amendable or locked. When fields are hardcoded, creating a new post with the required structure is the recommended solution. Open this document when you encounter restrictions while trying to change an employee's cost centre assignment.
sl: This document provides guidance for reviewing how a post is configured within the People Management system, specifically when users encounter issues updating a cost centre. The document directs users to navigate through People Management > Data Centre > View All > Post Profile Maintenance, where they can select a specific post and click View to examine its original structure and configuration details. The Post Profile Maintenance screen displays whether certain fields are amendable or hardcoded, which is critical information for understanding why cost centre updates may not be possible. When a field is hardcoded, it cannot be changed through standard amendment procedures, in which case the document advises creating a new post with the required structure instead. This document serves system administrators and HR professionals who manage employee records and organizational structures and need to troubleshoot cost centre update failures by identifying underlying post configuration constraints. The related articles section references complementary procedures for amending cost centres for employees through both the Portal and Back Office interfaces, as well as related tasks like adding units to the business structure and amending appointment details.

ss: EMS notifications in CoreHR can be customized by accessing Event Management through the CoreHR back office menu and navigating to Hr Event Configuration. Open this document when you need to modify the text, content, or settings of an existing EMS notification that's already set up in your system. Make sure to activate the notification and save your changes once you've completed your edits.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for editing the content, message, and subject line of existing EMS (Event Management System) notifications within the Back Office environment. The process begins by navigating to CoreHR, accessing the CoreHR menu, and locating the Event Management section to open the Hr Event Configuration screen. Users must then select their desired Event Category and click Edit next to the specific Event Type they wish to modify. The document explains how to use the Configure Subject and Configure Message buttons to customize both the notification subject and body text, which involves selecting a data source from the Select Data Source dropdown menu, entering custom Subject Text and Message Text, and incorporating Available Items as needed. To finalize the changes, users must ensure the Active Indicator is selected and click Save Changes to apply the modifications. This guide is intended for Back Office administrators or HR personnel responsible for managing and maintaining EMS notifications within their CoreHR system, particularly when existing notification templates require content updates or corrections.

This document is primarily used by Back Office administrators and personnel managers who need to configure custom user-defined fields and establish standardized reference codes for organizational use. The guide addresses the practical task of extending the system's flexibility by allowing administrators to define custom reference values that align with their organization's specific requirements for post creation and management.

sl: This document provides instructions for adding new job title codes to the Access Group back office system when organizational changes require new job title descriptions. Users create a new job title code by clicking the green plus icon to insert a fresh record, completing all required fields, and saving the entry using the yellow save icon. The document emphasizes a critical constraint: job title codes must contain only alphanumeric characters, and users must avoid special characters such as ampersands or other symbols, as these can negatively impact other areas of the system. This task is typically performed by HR administrators or system configurators who need to establish new job classification structures in response to staffing reorganizations or role structure changes. The document also references related functionality including amending job titles for existing employees, setting up job title codes via the employee portal, creating post profile records, and managing job categories, indicating this is part of a broader job and post management configuration process.

t: Data Migration Tool - Migrate and completed screens
s:
The Errors screen lists all files that have completed validation and have encountered file or line errors.
​
The errors can be viewed per file or all at once and each list is paginated to 50 results per page.
​
The errors page should be displayed by line number when viewed by file and by file and li...
ss: The Data Migration Tool's Errors and Completed screens help you identify and resolve validation issues when migrating files into CoreHR. After uploading files, the Errors screen displays any validation failures organized by file and line number, with options to re-upload the file, re-validate without uploading, or delete and start over. Once all errors are corrected and files pass validation, you trigger the migration process to move the data into the CoreHR main database, where completed files appear in the Completed Files section. Open this document when you need to troubleshoot validation errors during a data migration, understand what actions are available per file, or track the status of files moving through the upload and migration workflow.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide to the Errors screen and completion workflow within the Data Migration Tool, which processes and validates files being migrated into the CoreHR main database. The document describes how validation errors are displayed and organized—either per file or all at once with pagination set to 50 results per page, with errors sorted by line number when viewing individual files and by file and line number when viewing all errors together. Users have four primary options when errors are encountered: Re-upload File to replace it with a corrected version, Re-validate File to clear errors without re-uploading when only system configuration changes are needed (such as adding missing reference data or setting up a Department), View Errors for File to focus on a specific file's issues, or Delete File to start the process again. The Observations page groups error messages by their codes to identify common or recurring issues, and for files with fewer than 100 errors, the detailed error view by line is recommended for pinpointing validation issues with specific records. Once all reference-based errors are resolved and files show "Validation Complete. No Errors" status on the Upload tab, they appear in the Valid Files section of the Migrate tab, at which point users should wait until all files are validated before proceeding. The final step involves pressing the Migrate button (which is menu-controlled and requires appropriate access permissions) to queue files for migration into the CoreHR database; a DBA job then processes the migration (running every 5 minutes in versions prior to V23, or on demand in V24+), after which completed files appear in the Completed Files section and are removed from the File Upload screen to allow additional files of the same type to be uploaded.

t: Changing the default donotreply@corehr.com email
s:
It is NOT suggested that this email address be changed in most cases due to the increase chances of a bounce back. This will in turn cause problems notifying the employees or staff that need those notifications for approvals etc.

For event notifications you can use Admin@corehr.com but this can sti...
ss: The donotreply@corehr.com email address is the default notification sender in CoreHR for approval alerts and employee notifications. Changing this email address is not recommended in most cases because it increases the risk of bounce-back errors that can prevent staff from receiving critical approval notifications. If you need to use a different email address like Admin@corehr.com, test the change in UAT first, or alternatively configure SPF records for the BT mail relay IPs to avoid delivery issues. Open this document if you're considering changing your CoreHR notification email address or troubleshooting delivery problems with system notifications.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre provides guidance on changing the default donotreply@corehr.com email address in the CoreHR system and outlines the associated risks and alternatives. The primary process it describes is modifying the notification email address used by CoreHR, with specific mention of the alternative Admin@corehr.com address that can be used for event notifications. The document addresses the problem of email bounce backs, which occur when the default email is changed and can prevent critical notifications from reaching employees and staff who require them for approvals and other operational processes. It strongly recommends testing any email address changes in the UAT (User Acceptance Testing) environment first before implementing them in production, and advises reverting to the original address immediately if any bounce backs occur. For users who want to use a custom email address instead of donotreply@corehr.com, the document provides a technical solution: adding SPF records for the BT mail relay IP addresses that support PeopleXD's mail relay system, including four specific mail server addresses (mail.esat-x.com, mail01.mail.esat-x.com, mail02.mail.esat-x.com, and mail03.mail.esat-x.com) with their corresponding IP addresses. This document is primarily intended for CoreHR system administrators and IT personnel responsible for email configuration who are considering changing the default notification email address or troubleshooting email delivery issues within their organization.

Admin Tools

ss: The Portal Parameter cp_knownas_description controls whether the 'Known As' field appears instead of the standard Forename column in employee records. Use this feature when you need staff to be searchable and identifiable by their preferred name rather than their legal first name. Enable it by navigating to Administrator Dashboard > Site Manager > Admin Settings, searching for the parameter, and setting it to Y. This functionality is available as of patch 28.0.122 and should be tested in UAT before deploying to your live environment.
sl: This document provides instructions for enabling the "Known As" feature to replace the standard Forename field in an Access Group portal system, specifically applicable from patch version 28.0.122 onwards. The document describes a configuration process that allows employees to be searched for and identified using their "Known As" name instead of their formal forename. The primary task involves accessing the Administrator Dashboard, navigating to Site Manager, and locating the Admin Settings section where administrators must search for the parameter "cp_knownas_description" (or alternatively "cp_hradmin_knownas" depending on the implementation). Once located, administrators need to edit this parameter and set its value to "Y" to activate the feature, then save the changes. The document recommends testing this configuration in a UAT (User Acceptance Testing) environment before implementing it in a production system. This functionality is particularly useful for organizations where employees commonly go by names other than their formal forenames, improving user search and identification processes across employee-facing screens and HR administration interfaces. The document also references related articles covering how Known As names can be displayed on org charts, employee cards, document generation screens, and HR Admin screens.

ss: UDF event notifications enable you to set up automated alerts based on User Defined Fields in your HR system. Unlike standard HR Events notifications, User Defined Fields must be configured through the HR User Data Events category in the Data Centre's HR Event Configuration. Open this document when you need to create an event notification that triggers on custom or user-defined HR data fields, and follow the step-by-step instructions to configure the notification type, recipients, and message content.
sl: This document provides guidance on creating event notifications specifically for User Defined Fields (UDFs) in an HR system, addressing a common configuration issue where UDFs cannot be added through the standard HR Events notifications category. It explains that while UDFs are not available in the HR Events notification view, they are accessible through the HR User Data Events event category, which is the correct location for this configuration task. The document outlines a step-by-step process beginning in the Data Centre, navigating to HR Event Configuration, and selecting HR User Data Events from the Event Category dropdown list before editing an event type and clicking Add New Notification. The instructions detail how to configure the notification generation timing, set up recipient preferences on the Recipient tab by selecting the appropriate Notification Type, and then move to the Message tab where users must configure both the Subject and Message fields by selecting HR_USER_DATA_EMS_VIEW as the Data Source. The process concludes with ensuring the Active toggle is enabled and saving the configuration. This document is primarily used by HR system administrators or power users who need to set up automated notifications triggered by changes to user-defined data fields, helping them avoid the common mistake of attempting configuration in the wrong event category.

t: Creating a basic audit report
s:
To identify updates made to an employee's data, follow these steps to create an audit report in Insight.

From the dashboard menu, select Insight.

Click ACTIONS, then select Create Report.

Enter a report title, then click OK.

Under Select a setting, select Columns.

Click ADD, then select Column....
ss: Creating an audit report in Insight allows you to track and identify updates made to employee data across Pay, Personnel, Time, and other functional areas. Use this process when you need to investigate what changes were made to specific employee records, who made them, and when they occurred. Open this document if you're setting up a report to monitor data modifications in your HR system—you'll learn how to select audit views, add relevant data columns, apply filters to narrow results, and run the report. This is essential for compliance, data governance, or investigating discrepancies in employee information.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for creating an audit report in Insight to track and identify updates made to employee data across various functional areas. The process begins by navigating to the Insight option from the dashboard menu, then selecting Create Report from the ACTIONS menu, where users enter a report title and proceed to configure the report structure. Users must access the Columns settings to filter available audit views, with options specifically including Audit Details (Pay), Audit Details (Personnel), Audit Details (Time), and other functional areas depending on system configuration. The document recommends selecting relevant data fields such as Person Reference, Table Name, Field Name, New Value, Old Value, and Username to capture meaningful audit information in the report output. Additional filtering capabilities are available through the Filters option under Select a setting, allowing users to restrict returned data by selecting data items, comparison operators, and filter values to refine results. The document is designed for users who need to monitor employee data changes within the Insight reporting system, particularly those responsible for compliance, HR administration, or system auditing across payroll, personnel, and time management modules. Once filters are configured as needed, users execute the report by clicking REFRESH DATA followed by OK to generate the final audit report output.

t: Portal: Enable access to Insight
s:
To grant a user access to Insight and ensure they can view the correct employee records, follow the steps below.

 

Assign Insight access

ss: Enabling Insight portal access involves two key steps: assigning the COREPORTAL_INSIGHT menu profile to a user in Security > User Management, then configuring their employee record visibility in People Management > Data Centre. You can restrict what employees they see by setting access at the company or department level, controlling whether they view all company employees or only those in specific departments. Open this document when you need to grant a new user permission to access Insight and determine which employee records they're allowed to view based on their role and department.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for granting users access to the Insight system and configuring their permissions to view employee records at appropriate levels within an organization. The first process involves assigning Insight access through the Security menu by navigating to User Management, locating the employee using the search function, accessing the 3-dot menu to select 'Manage Account', then selecting Menu Profile and activating the COREPORTAL_INSIGHT menu profile. The second process requires configuring employee record access by going to People Management, Data Centre, View All, searching for HR User Access, and entering the employee's username or reference number to assign personnel access permissions. Users can control the scope of employee visibility through the 'Security Type' field dropdown, which allows them to assign access by company, department, or other organizational levels, with company-level assignments granting visibility to all employees in that company and department-level assignments limiting visibility to those specific departments. The document addresses the common scenario of ensuring users can view the correct employee records based on their role and organizational position, which is essential for HR professionals and system administrators managing data access. Changes to access settings are automatically saved when toggles are switched on, eliminating the need for manual confirmation steps. This guide is typically used by HR administrators, system administrators, or access managers who need to onboard new users to the Insight portal or modify existing user permissions within the system.

t: Insight: Access to view, create and edit reports

ss: Access to CorePortal Insight reporting is controlled through specific menu options that determine which functions users can perform and which business areas they can report on. Standard functions include viewing, creating, editing, deleting, and cloning reports, each requiring its own corresponding menu option. Business area menu options (such as CorePersonnel, CorePay, CoreTime, CoreHourly Timesheets, and others) control which data sources appear in the Current Data Views filter when users create or edit reports. Open this document when setting up user permissions for reporting in CorePortal or when you need to understand which menu options grant access to specific reporting functions and business data areas.
sl: This document explains the menu options and access controls required within the CorePortal system to perform reporting functions in the Insight tool, serving as a configuration guide for system administrators setting up user permissions. The document outlines five standard menu options needed for basic report management: CorePortal - Insight View Reports (for viewing), CorePortal - Insight Create Reports (for creating), CorePortal - Insight Edit Reports (for editing), CorePortal - Insight Delete Reports (for deletion), and CorePortal - Insight Clone Reports (for cloning reports). Beyond standard functions, the document details 17 business area menu options that control which data sources appear in the Current Data Views filter when creating or editing reports, including areas such as CorePersonnel, CorePay, CoreBudget, CoreTime, CoreRecruitment, CoreAMS, CoreHESA, and CoreTalent, among others. Users who gain access to a business area automatically receive access to all views within that business area without requiring additional permissions, with the exception of LOV (List of Values) views, which require the separate CorePortal - Insight Area LOV Selection Allowed menu option to be enabled for creating reference data reports. The document is designed for system administrators and access managers who need to configure menu profiles in CorePortal to grant users appropriate reporting permissions based on their organizational role and responsibilities.

t: Insight: Reporting on UDFs

Open this article when you're setting up UDF reports, troubleshooting missing data in your reports, or need to understand which access rights users require to view UDF information.
sl: This document provides guidance on reporting on user-defined field (UDF) data within an employee management system, specifically focusing on how to access and utilize the Person User Data folder for this reporting purpose. The document emphasizes a critical prerequisite: users must have appropriate access permissions to the UDFs they intend to report on, which is essential for successful data retrieval and report generation. The content addresses common reporting scenarios and troubleshooting situations, including cases where employees may be missing from reports that include diversity or UDF fields, and instances where no data displays in UDF user-defined reports despite configuration attempts. The document references related functionality across multiple system areas, including Portal and Back Office environments where new User Defined Fields can be created, indicating this is part of a broader UDF management ecosystem. Additional coverage includes UDF event notifications, suggesting the document touches on how system alerts or triggers work in relation to user-defined field activities. This resource is primarily intended for system administrators, HR professionals, and report developers who need to configure and troubleshoot employee data reporting that incorporates custom user-defined fields beyond standard system fields.

t: Insight: Employees missing from a report with diversity or UDF fields
s:
Insight reports that source data from multiple views include only employees who have data present in both views, as demonstrated below.

If a person has no diversity entries in their record, they will not appear in a report built from a personnel view (e.g. HR Person Master) and the Person Diversity...
ss: When building Insight reports that combine personnel views with diversity or user-defined field (UDF) data, employees missing either type of information won't appear in results because they lack entries in those specific tables. This becomes a problem when you need a complete employee list regardless of whether individual records contain diversity data or UDFs. Enabling an outer join on the report can resolve this by including all employees from the base view, though you'll need to contact your support team or CSM to implement this change. Be aware that outer joins may not be available if your report includes columns from transactional tables like Appointment or Salary History, as this could impact system performance.
sl: This document explains a data filtering issue in Insight reports that occurs when combining personnel views with diversity or user-defined field (UDF) data sources. The problem arises because Insight reports using multiple views (such as HR Person Master combined with either the Person Diversity (Personnel) view or Person User Data (Personnel) view) only display employees who have data present in both views simultaneously. Specifically, employees without diversity entries will not appear in reports linking personnel and diversity views, and employees without UDF entries will not appear in reports linking personnel and UDF views, as these individuals do not exist in the respective database tables. To resolve this issue and return all employees or applicants regardless of whether their records contain diversity or UDF data, an outer join must be enabled on the report, which requires contacting the support team or Customer Success Manager to determine feasibility and implement the change. The document includes an important warning that enabling outer joins may negatively impact system performance if the report includes columns from transactional or large tables such as Appointment History or Salary History, in which cases Access may decline to add the outer join. This guidance is essential for HR administrators and reporting users who need comprehensive employee lists in Insight and are experiencing unexpectedly incomplete report results when incorporating diversity or UDF fields.

t: Insight: Exported file cannot be opened in Microsoft Excel
s:
If Microsoft Excel displays an error when attempting to open the exported file, or if the file appears empty, there are several possible causes. Please review the following.

 

Firefox web browser

Mozilla Firefox may not automatically generate the file in a valid format for Excel. The simplest sol...
ss: Exported files from Insight reports won't open in Microsoft Excel or appear empty due to browser or data formatting issues. If you're using Firefox, the browser may not generate files in a valid Excel format—you'll need to change Firefox's default program setting to open .xlsx files directly in Excel, or switch to Chrome or Edge. If the report contains irregular characters, symbols, or emojis, remove them from the data fields before exporting. Alternatively, export the report as a CSV file and then save it as .xlsx format in Excel.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving errors when attempting to open exported files from Insight in Microsoft Excel, addressing scenarios where the file either fails to open or appears empty upon export. The document outlines specific procedures for Firefox web browser users, beginning with navigating to the relevant report, clicking Actions, then selecting Export Data and choosing Excel format before clicking OK. When Firefox displays the download pop-up box under "What Should Firefox do with this file?", users must ensure Microsoft Excel is selected as the default program; if Excel is not available in the dropdown menu, users must click Other and then Browse to manually locate the EXCEL.EXE file, typically found at C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\EXCEL.EXE, though the location may vary by system configuration. After selecting EXCEL.EXE as the default program, users should tick the option "Do this automatically for files like this from now on" and click OK to prevent future issues. The document also addresses invalid data format problems, advising users to review report data for irregular characters, symbols, or emojis that may cause export failures, and to remove such data from individual fields before re-attempting the export. As an alternative solution, the document recommends exporting the report as a CSV file through Insight and then opening and saving it in .xlsx format within Excel. This resource is designed for Insight users who encounter export compatibility issues, particularly those using Firefox as their default browser or encountering data formatting problems during the export process.

t: Insight: Unable to access scheduled report from a link
s:
When using a scheduled Insight report, the email now includes a link to access the report rather than emailing as an attachment.

 

To make sure this link works.

In the PeopleXD portal, go to Administrator Dashboard. 

Click Site Manager and open Admin Settings.

ss: Scheduled Insight reports in PeopleXD now deliver links via email instead of file attachments, but these links may not work without proper configuration. To fix broken report links, you need to update two parameters in the PeopleXD Administrator Dashboard: saashostserver and cp_insight_email_url, entering your portal URL with the correct client code and environment designation (production or UAT). If you're using Access Evo, there's an additional configuration step with a different URL format. Open this document when you can't access a scheduled Insight report from an email link, or when setting up scheduled reports for the first time.
sl: This document explains how to troubleshoot issues with accessing scheduled Insight reports via email links in the PeopleXD portal. When Insight reports are scheduled, they are now delivered as email messages containing a link to access the report rather than as file attachments, and this document provides the configuration steps necessary to ensure these links function properly. To resolve access issues, administrators must navigate to the Administrator Dashboard in the PeopleXD portal, then proceed to Site Manager and open Admin Settings. Within Admin Settings, administrators need to locate and configure two specific parameters: saashostserver and cp_insight_email_url, both of which must be populated with the appropriate portal URL. The standard portal URL format required is https://my.corehr.com/pls/coreportal_xxxp/, where xxxp represents the client code followed by either "p" for production environments or "u" for UAT environments. For organizations using Access Evo, the cp_insight_email_url parameter requires a different URL format that includes the Access Evo cloud infrastructure path and workspace identifiers. This document is primarily used by system administrators and IT support staff who manage PeopleXD portal configuration and need to ensure scheduled report delivery functionality works correctly for end users across their organization.

t: Insight: Organisational roles audit
s: The system does not create values for a specific employee in the audit table against entries that were done in the HR_ORGANISATIONAL_PERSON table which stores the organisational roles data, thus it cannot be precisely established which user actioned the change/update to the org role of an employee. ...
ss: Organisational roles in the HR_ORGANISATIONAL_PERSON table don't automatically populate audit values, making it difficult to track who changed an employee's role. You can create an Insight audit report to identify which user updated or ended an organisational role on a specific date by filtering on the DATE_TO field and the HR_ORGANISATIONAL_PERSON table. Open this document when you need to investigate who made recent changes to employee organisational roles or end dates, or when you require an audit trail for role modifications. Note that the report shows the user who entered the change but may not specify which exact organisational role was affected if multiple changes occurred on the same date.
sl: This document explains a limitation in the Access Group system where audit values are not automatically created for specific employees in the audit table when organisational roles data is updated in the HR_ORGANISATIONAL_PERSON table, making it difficult to determine which user made changes to an employee's organisational role. To work around this issue, the document provides a detailed procedure for creating an Insight report that captures related audit information about who updated and ended organisational roles with specific end dates. The process begins by navigating to Insight from the dashboard menu, selecting Create Report from the Actions menu, and naming the report. Users must then configure the report by adding specific columns from the Audit Details (Personnel) view, including Audit Type, Table Name, Date And Time, Date And Time 24hour Format, Field Name, Old Value, New Value, and Username. The report requires three critical filters: Table Name set to equal HR_ORGANISATIONAL_PERSON, Field Name set to equal DATE_TO, and New Value containing the specific end date in the DD-MMM-YY format being investigated. After sorting results by the Date And Time column in descending order, the resulting report displays the username of who entered the end date, when the change occurred, and the exact time in 24-hour format. However, the document notes an important limitation: if multiple users have entered the same end date for organisational roles, the report cannot distinguish which specific user made changes for which particular organisational role, requiring additional internal verification. This document is typically used by HR administrators, system auditors, or Access Group support staff who need to investigate historical changes to employee organisational role assignments.

t: Insight: No data displaying in a UDF user defined report
s:
Reason 1

A UDF(User Defined) report with Person User Data, HR Person Master and Appointment History views generates no data. When the Appointment History view fields are removed, data displays.

UDF Codes can be linked to either personnel number or appointment ID. When linked to personnel number, t...
ss: UDF (User Defined Field) reports in Insight may display no data when they combine Person User Data, HR Person Master, and Appointment History views, or when Manager-level access hasn't been configured properly in the System User security settings. This document walks through three common reasons why data fails to appear and provides step-by-step instructions to resolve the issue using the PRBI_GET_USER_DATA_FIELD function. Open this if your UDF report is returning blank results despite having the correct views and data sources configured, or if you need to restructure a report to display User Defined Fields correctly.
sl: This document troubleshoots the common problem of User Defined (UDF) reports displaying no data when configured with specific view combinations in the Access Group system. It identifies three distinct reasons why data fails to appear: Reason 1 occurs when a UDF linked to personnel number is combined with the Appointment History view, which causes no data to display because the appointment ID remains blank for employees; Reason 2 happens when a report uses Person User Data and HR Person Master views with Manager access type, as the Person User Data view requires explicit security access granted via Security Dashboard > Setup > System User > Personnel Access rather than relying on manager permissions; and Reason 3 applies when a UDF is created in Data Centre with the Security field enabled, requiring the logged-in user to have access configured in the Security dashboard under System Users for the User Defined security type. For Reasons 1 and 2, the document provides detailed step-by-step instructions to resolve the issue by creating an Insight report using HR Person Master view instead, implementing the PRBI_GET_USER_DATA_FIELD function, and adding calculations through the Calculation feature with the XD Functions tab. The resolution process requires entering three mandatory parameters—P_EMPNO (Person Reference), P_REFERENCE_CODE (the UDF Code), and P_TEXT (field identifier such as DATE1, TEXT1, or TEXT2)—to retrieve the specific UDF field data, with the example demonstrating how the function call should appear in the system. This document is used by report administrators and managers who need to troubleshoot why their UDF reports return blank results despite proper configuration and access rights.

Open this document when you need to investigate who revoked employee access or generate a report of access removal events for compliance or troubleshooting purposes.
sl: This document provides guidance on creating an Insight Report to audit and track when user access to personnel data has been removed from the system. The report is built using the Audit Details (Personnel) view and includes key fields such as Audit Type, Date Audited, Username, Old Value, New Value, Table Name, and Field Name to capture comprehensive access removal information. The primary table referenced is PERS_USER, which stores access permissions to personnel data, and the PERSONNEL_NO field is recommended as the filter criterion to identify which employee's access was revoked. The document specifies exact filter configurations: Table Name set to PERS_USER, Field Name set to PERSONNEL_NO, Audit Type set to Delete, and Date Audited set to a specific date range, which together reveal the identity of the user who removed access from an employee. While other Audit Types such as Insert and Update exist in the system, Delete is the specific audit type relevant for identifying access removal events. This document is typically used by HR administrators, access managers, or audit personnel who need to investigate when and by whom employee access permissions have been terminated in the system.

sl: This document provides guidance on creating reports for Social Onboarding Checklists within the Access Group system, specifically using the Insight reporting tool. It addresses a common user question about consolidating all onboarding data into a single report, explaining that this is not possible because checklist data is stored across multiple database tables depending on the checklist type. For specialized reporting needs, the document directs users to alternative approaches: the Hr Person Master view should be used when reporting on Next of Kin details, while the Person User Data view should be used for User Defined Checklists, with the specific view selected based on the relevant User Defined Item. This document helps resolve access provisioning scenarios where users need differentiated visibility into personnel data based on their organizational role and responsibilities, and it assumes readers are already familiar with back office administration and system configuration concepts.

Open this document when you need to audit salary modifications, verify approval workflows, or investigate why a salary isn't appearing on the approval screen.
sl: This document explains how to track and review salary changes within a system by generating reports through the Insight reporting tool. Users can create an Insight report based on the Salary Approval History (Personnel) view to monitor all salary-related transactions and their approval statuses. The report allows administrators and HR personnel to add multiple informational columns including Person Reference, Salary, Effective Date, Approval Date, Approval Id, Transaction Type, Username, and Reference and Description fields to customize their analysis. The Transaction Type column is particularly useful as it displays one of three values—A for Approved, R for Rejected, or C for Created—enabling quick identification of the status of each salary change request. The Username column identifies which user actioned or processed each transaction, providing accountability and audit trail information. This document is typically used by HR administrators, payroll managers, and system auditors who need to investigate salary approval workflows, verify approval statuses, or troubleshoot issues where employee salaries are not displaying correctly in approval screens. Open this document when you need to understand why you're receiving bank detail update notifications that don't reflect real changes, or when you need guidance on using audit reports to track authentic updates to employee banking information.
sl: This document describes an issue within the Access Group system where bank details update notifications are sent to users even when no actual changes have been made to the underlying data. The document explains that while these notifications are triggered by the save action, the system's audit report functions differently and only records notifications as actual changes when new values are entered and saved, creating a discrepancy between what notifications report and what the audit log reflects. To obtain accurate information about genuine bank details modifications, the documentation recommends consulting the audit report instead of relying solely on notifications, since the audit report excludes cases where identical values are re-saved. The document is primarily useful for system administrators, compliance officers, or financial teams who need to distinguish between false-positive notifications and actual bank details updates, and who may need to validate changes through proper audit trails. ss: When you add an end date to an employee's allowance in your payroll system, it may continue showing as approved while payroll processing is still running for the current period. This is expected behavior—the allowance remains active until the payroll cycle completes for that employee's pay group. Once payroll processing finishes, the system automatically updates the allowance status to Ended. Open this article if you've set an allowance end date but are seeing it still marked as approved and need to understand why.
sl: This document explains the behavior of allowances in a payroll system when an end date is assigned to an employee's allowance record. It addresses the specific issue where an allowance continues to display as approved status even after an end date has been added, rather than immediately changing to an ended or inactive status. The document clarifies that this occurs because the system maintains the allowance in its active, approved state while payroll processing for the current pay period is actively running. Once the payroll processing cycle has been completed for the employee's pay group, the system automatically updates the allowance status from approved to Ended, resolving the apparent discrepancy. This document is relevant for payroll administrators and HR personnel who manage employee allowances and need to understand the timing and mechanics of how allowance status changes are processed in relation to payroll cycles. The document also references related processes including updating appointment end dates, generating salaries and allowances in final mode, and troubleshooting scenarios where ended allowances continue to make payments, indicating it is part of a broader help resource for allowance and payroll management.

ss: Updating an employee's salary in PeopleXD or CorePersonnel involves submitting a new salary amendment rather than deleting an incorrect one, since approved or rejected amendments cannot be removed from the system. You can correct salary errors by creating a new amendment with the same effective date as the original, with both entries appearing in the salary history but the latest one taking precedence. For ended appointments, submit an amendment with an effective date before the appointment end date to ensure the system generates the correct salary. Access this process through either the People Management dashboard (portal) or CorePersonnel back office, depending on your role.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on correcting and updating employee salary information within an Access Group system, covering both scenarios where corrections are needed and standard amendment procedures. The key constraint explained is that approved or rejected salary amendments cannot be deleted; instead, users must submit a new salary amendment with the same effective date and the correct salary amount, with the system distinguishing between amendments using the input date and allowing the latest entry to override previous incorrect versions. For ended appointments, users should submit a new salary amendment with an effective date earlier than the appointment's end date to ensure the system generates the salary as expected. The document provides two separate procedural paths: the Portal instructions guide users through the People Management dashboard, Command Centre widget, and Employee view to access the Current Salary tab, select the correct contract, and add new salary details through the New Salary section; the Back Office instructions direct users through CorePersonnel's Maintenance menu to Salary Administration and the Maintain HR salary amendments function where they search for the employee and use the Add button to enter and save salary details. This document is used by HR administrators, payroll personnel, or managers who need to correct salary entry errors, apply salary amendments, or adjust compensation for employees with ended contracts, and it references related processes such as amending job titles, contract amendments, and troubleshooting increment issues.

sl: This document provides HR and payroll personnel with instructions on how to cancel employee allowances in the Access Group system, a process that prevents future payments for a specific allowance and is typically used to correct allowances set up in error. An allowance can only be cancelled if it meets two specific conditions: it must be fully approved (not in "Outstanding" status if Salary Approvals are being used) and it must be visible in Payroll, meaning employee payroll setup has already been completed; conversely, allowances cannot be cancelled if they are Outstanding or not yet visible to Payroll. The document provides step-by-step instructions beginning from the People Management dashboard, directing users to the Command Centre widget, selecting the Employees option, searching for and viewing the specific employee, and then navigating to the Current Salary tab where the Allowances section contains a three-dot menu to access the Cancel function. If an allowance does not meet the required conditions for cancellation, the system prevents the user from proceeding, though the document notes that fully approved allowances not yet visible to Payroll can be deleted directly instead of cancelled. A critical warning explains that money is only clawed back for cancelled allowances if they are still open at the time of cancellation; if an allowance was already ended before cancellation is attempted, manual arrears calculation and timesheet entry adjustment are required to recover overpaid amounts.

t: Planned salary is not showing for approval
s:

ss: When you create a post in PeopleXD, you can set a planned (indicative) salary for that position, but this isn't an actual employee salary—it's just a placeholder. If you appoint a new starter to that post without entering their own salary record, the system displays the planned salary instead, which won't appear for approval. Open this article if a salary isn't showing up in the approval workflow and you need to understand why the employee only has a planned salary rather than an active salary record. You'll learn the valid salary statuses (Pending, In Approval, Approved, Future, or Rejected) and how to properly set up an employee's actual salary so it can be processed for approval.
sl: This document explains the distinction between planned salaries and true employee salaries in the Access Group HR system, clarifying why a planned salary might appear on an employee record when it shouldn't. When creating a post, HR can enter an indicative planned salary that applies to that post position; however, when a new starter is appointed to the post, a separate true salary must be entered specifically for the employee. If no true salary is entered for the employee, the system defaults to displaying the planned salary instead, which can cause confusion during salary approval processes. The document outlines the valid statuses that a true salary line can have: Pending (not yet approved at any level), In Approval (partially approved by some but not all approvers), Approved (fully approved by all required approvers), Future (approved with an effective date greater than today), and Rejected (rejected salaries that won't be paid). This troubleshooting guide helps HR administrators and payroll personnel understand why expected salaries may not be showing for approval and identifies the core issue of missing or incomplete employee salary entries. The document references related tasks such as amending salary details for employees, investigating salary visibility issues on the salary approval screen, deleting pending salary approvals, and managing career breaks in post management environments.
