t: Control a Manager's visibility of employee salary details
s:
This is controlled by a menu option - CorePortal - Manager Appointment Salary - which can be enabled/disabled via Security.

Menu option name: CorePortal - Manager Appointment Salary
​Menu ID: MAIN_MENU.Man_App_Sal
​System: CorePortal
​Unique menu option reference: 337360

 

In Security Dashboard, ...
ss: Controlling manager access to employee salary information in CorePortal is managed through the Security Dashboard menu profiles. To hide salary details from a manager's view, you'll disable the "CorePortal - Manager Appointment Salary" menu option (Menu ID: MAIN_MENU.Man_App_Sal) by switching off its Active toggle in the relevant manager's menu profile. You should also ensure the "CorePortal - Administrator Appointment Salary" option is disabled for that manager. Use this process when you need to restrict which managers can see salary data for their team members or across the organization.
sl: This document provides instructions for controlling manager access to employee salary information within the CorePortal system by enabling or disabling a specific menu option. The core process involves navigating to the Security Dashboard, locating the Menu Profiles tab, and searching for the relevant menu profile (such as COREPORTAL_MANAGER). Once the appropriate menu profile is found, users click the three-dot ellipsis and select "Manage Menu Options" to access the configuration settings. Within this interface, managers can search for and locate two critical menu options: "CorePortal - Manager Appointment Salary" (Menu ID: MAIN_MENU.Man_App_Sal, reference 337360) and "CorePortal - Administrator Appointment Salary," which control visibility of salary details. To hide employee salary information from a manager's view, the Active toggle for the "CorePortal - Manager Appointment Salary" menu option must be switched off, and the document emphasizes that the "CorePortal - Administrator Appointment Salary" option should also be disabled for the manager. This document is primarily used by system administrators or security personnel who manage user access permissions and need to restrict or grant managers' visibility of sensitive employee compensation data within the CorePortal system.

t: Salary has not incremented but the increment due date has passed
s:
This issue can be caused by the following.

New salary exists with date effective the same or greater than the increment due date.

Increments are not maintained via CorePersonnel yet auto_increment on pay_group is N.

To resolve this, follow the steps below. 

Click CorePersonnel, then click Mainte...
ss: Salary increments in CorePersonnel may fail to process when a new salary record exists with an effective date that matches or exceeds the increment due date. This document covers the salary administration process in CorePersonnel's Maintain HR Salary Amendments function and explains why the increment job won't create or roll forward to the scheduled increment due date. Open this guide if an employee's salary has not incremented despite the increment due date passing, and you need to diagnose whether a conflicting salary record is blocking the increment from applying.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses a specific payroll issue where an employee's salary increment fails to process even though the increment due date has already passed. The problem occurs in two primary scenarios: when a new salary record exists with an effective date that is the same as or later than the increment due date, or when increments are not being maintained through CorePersonnel while the auto_increment setting on the pay_group is configured as "N". To diagnose and resolve this issue, users must navigate to CorePersonnel, select Maintenance, then access Salary Administration and the "Maintain HR Salary Amendments" function. The troubleshooting process requires querying the employee record, selecting the relevant appointment, and comparing two critical dates on the Salary Details tab: the effective date of the latest salary row at the bottom of the screen and the increment due date displayed at the top. The document explains that when a salary entry exists with an effective date on or after the increment due date, the system's increment job cannot generate a new increment or advance to the increment due date as expected. This guide is typically used by HR administrators, payroll managers, and back-office personnel who manage salary amendments and need to understand the interaction between salary effective dates and increment scheduling rules in the CorePersonnel system.

t: Access to delete contracts and contract amendments, or to switch posts
s:
If plans change or an error occurs, administrators may need to delete contract details or to reassign an employee to a different post. Ensure that the following menu options are added to their profile to enable these actions. 

📌Note: We've further guidance if you're unsure how to enable or assign a...
ss: Configure administrator access permissions to delete employee contracts, contract amendments, and reassign staff to different posts in your system. This document specifies the exact menu options and IDs required in Web Services and People Management to enable these critical administrative functions. Open this guide when you need to grant permissions to administrators who handle contract changes, correct post assignments, or remove contracts due to plan changes or data errors. It also covers the post-switching process that occurs when deleting a contract for employees with multiple active positions.
sl: This document provides administrators with the specific menu options and system configuration settings required to perform three key tasks: deleting contracts, deleting contract amendments, and switching employee posts in the Access Group system. For deleting contracts, administrators must enable six Web Services menu options including Delete appointments (WS_PROFILE_MENU.DELETE_APPOINTMENTS_ID), Delete appointments Proxy for Personal Post Access (WS_PROFILE_MENU.DELETE_APPOINTMENTS_ID_PROXY), and four variations of Get appointments linked items menu options that retrieve linked item data in the Web Services system. To delete contract amendments, a single menu option from the People Management system (EMPLOYEE_DASHBOARD_MENU.DELETE_CONTRACT_AMENDMENT) must be assigned to the administrator's profile. When an employee has multiple active posts and an administrator attempts to delete a contract, the system automatically prompts for a post switch, requiring two additional Web Services menu options: Update appointments (WS_PROFILE_MENU.PATCH_APPOINTMENTS_ID) and Update appointments Proxy for Personal Post Access (WS_PROFILE_MENU.PATCH_APPOINTMENTS_ID_PROXY). The document is designed for system administrators who manage employee contracts and post assignments and need to configure appropriate access levels when plans change or errors occur during contract administration. The document also references related guidance articles on deleting appointments in the portal, switching incorrectly assigned posts, and granting access to delete employee records.

t: Portal: Assign a menu profile to a user
s:
Menu profiles can be assigned to individual employees in the PeopleXD portal by following one of the processes outlined below.

 

Assign to an employee via People Management

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Command Centre.

Click View next to Employees, then search for the employee.
...
ss: Menu profiles control what sections and features individual users can access in the PeopleXD portal. You can assign menu profiles to employees through two methods: via People Management in the Command Centre, or via Security through User Management. Open this document when you need to grant specific portal access permissions to an employee or user, or when setting up a new user's interface customization. This is essential if you're configuring user permissions in PeopleXD or troubleshooting access issues for portal users.
sl: This document provides instructions for assigning menu profiles to users in the PeopleXD portal and covers two distinct administrative pathways to accomplish this task. The first method uses the People Management route, which requires navigating to the Command Centre from the dashboard menu, locating the specific employee through the View option next to Employees, and then accessing the ACTIONS menu to select Assign Access followed by Menu Profiles, where available profiles can be dragged from the Available section to the Assigned section. The second method operates through the Security section via User Management, where administrators select the appropriate account type—either All Active Portal Accounts for stand-alone PeopleXD sites or All Active Evo Accounts when launching from Access Evo—then locate the user and access their three-dot menu to select Manage Account and Menu Profiles. Both processes allow searching for employees or users by multiple identifiers including name, personnel number, username, or personnel number, providing flexibility in locating the correct individual. This document serves administrators and portal managers who need to configure user access and permissions within PeopleXD by controlling which menu options are available to specific employees or users. The document also references related articles covering user account creation, access assignment for employee viewing, default menu profile configuration, automatic assignment issues, and menu profile creation, suggesting this is part of a broader user and access management system within PeopleXD.

t: Grant access to view applicants in the Command Centre
s:
If admin users are unable to view successful recruitment applicants in the Command Centre, this feature can be enabled by adding a menu option to one of their assigned menu profiles. Follow the steps below.

📌Note: We recommend testing any changes to security access in UAT before applying them to th...
ss: Enabling the Successful Applicants menu option in the Command Centre requires admin users to update their assigned menu profiles in the Security settings. This process involves searching for the relevant profile, locating menu option 898328720, and activating it to grant visibility of recruitment applicants. Open this document when admin users report they cannot view successful applicants in the Command Centre, or when you need to configure recruitment visibility permissions for your team. The guide recommends testing any security access changes in UAT before applying them to your live system.
sl: This document explains how to resolve issues where admin users cannot view successful recruitment applicants in the Command Centre by enabling a specific menu option within their assigned menu profiles. The process begins by navigating from the dashboard menu to Security, then to Menu Profiles, where administrators search for the profile name that needs updating, ensuring it includes the People Management system. Once the correct profile is located by clicking its three-dot menu and selecting Manage Menu Options, administrators search for "Successful Applicants" in the search bar to locate the relevant menu option. The final step involves activating the menu option identified by the system number 898328720 by clicking the Active button next to it. This document is primarily used by system administrators or access managers who need to grant or restore viewing permissions for recruitment applicants to other admin users within their organization. The guide emphasizes testing any security access changes in UAT before implementing them in the live system to prevent unintended consequences.

t: Reset an account password
s:
If a user has forgotten their password credentials for their portal or back office account, or they've expired, they can be reset in PeopleXD Security. To do this, follow the steps below.

📌Note: A different password reset process is followed if users connect to PeopleXD via Access Evo.

From the da...
ss: Resetting forgotten or expired passwords for PeopleXD portal and back office accounts is managed through PeopleXD Security using the User Management function. A super user can search for the account by username, name, or personnel number, then reset the password through the Manage Account menu. Open this document when a user needs their password reset or when you're responsible for resetting passwords for other team members in your organization. Note that a different process applies for users connecting via Access Evo, and the Access support team cannot perform password resets directly.
sl: This document provides instructions for resetting user account passwords in PeopleXD Security when credentials have been forgotten or have expired. The process involves accessing the Security section from the dashboard menu, navigating to User Management, and selecting either All Active Portal Accounts or All Back Office Accounts from a drop-down menu. Users can search for the target account by entering the username in the Search users field, or alternatively by the user's name or personnel number if the username is unknown. Once the account is located, administrators click the three-dot menu next to the user record, select Manage Account, then navigate to ACTIONS and choose Reset Password. A new password complying with the organization's password policy must then be entered and confirmed with OK. The document notes that a different password reset process applies for users connecting via Access Evo, and importantly, it clarifies that only super users can reset passwords—the Access support team cannot perform this function, and users should contact their super user, Access Account Manager, or Customer Success Manager for assistance if needed. Related resources include articles on creating portal and back office accounts, configuring back office accounts, password policy requirements, and troubleshooting the "Active Directory Synched accounts cannot change password" error.

t: Changing a portal account username
s:
If you need to amend the portal account username for an employee, follow the steps below.

📌Note: You will not be able to delete the old username.

Log into Portal.

Go to the Security area, then click User Management.

Create a new Portal account by clicking on the Create New User button on the Sys...
ss: Changing a Portal account username involves creating a new user account in the Security > User Management area and linking it to the correct employee record. This process allows you to update an employee's Portal login credentials while automatically revoking access to the old account and transferring associated data like Payslips and Annual Leave. Open this document when you need to correct or amend an existing Portal username, keeping in mind that the old username cannot be deleted. You'll need to set a temporary password for the new account and have the user log in with their updated credentials.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for administrators who need to change a portal account username for an employee within an organization's Access Group system. The process begins by logging into Portal and navigating to the Security area, then selecting User Management to access the System Users widget. A new Portal account must be created using the Create New User button, where the administrator selects Portal as the User Type and enters a new username along with a temporary password. Once the account is created, the administrator must link this new Portal account to the correct employee by locating the username in the System Users widget, clicking the ellipsis icon, selecting Manage Account, and then clicking Link to HR Person to find and confirm the employee. This linking process automatically removes the employee's access to the old account and transfers all associated data including Payslips and Annual Leave to the new account. The document notes an important limitation: the old username cannot be deleted from the system. Finally, the administrator should instruct the user to test their access by logging into Portal using the new username and the temporary password that was set during account creation. This document is typically used by portal administrators or IT support staff who manage user accounts and need to correct username errors or update employee account information while preserving their historical data and permissions.

t: Assigning default menu profiles
s: The Security Access screen include a list of roles and indicators. The purpose of these indicators is to provide a quick way for a user to identify the role that the employee has in the organisation and assign them to a default menu profile. These may be managed in a number of ways, some of them are...
ss: Default menu profiles in PeopleXD Security control which menus and options employees see based on their organizational role. You can assign these profiles three ways: manually through User Management, automatically via Self Registration with Menu Profile Matrix Account Provisioning, or through organisational role rules in the Menu Profile Matrix. Open this document when you need to set up or configure how employee portal access and menu visibility are assigned based on their job role. Use it if you're managing user accounts in PeopleXD Security and want to streamline profile assignments across your organization.
sl: This document explains how to assign default menu profiles to employees using the Security Access screen in PeopleXD, which displays roles and indicators to help users identify an employee's organizational position and determine appropriate access levels. The document covers three distinct methods for assigning menu profiles: manual assignment directly through the employee's portal user account in PeopleXD Security, automatic assignment via Self Registration with Menu Profile Matrix Account Provisioning, and assignment through organizational role rules defined in the Menu Profile Matrix. For manual assignment, users navigate to Security > User Management, search for the employee, click the three-dot ellipsis on their account, select Manage Account, click Menu Profiles, and activate the appropriate profiles. The automatic Self Registration method requires navigating to Security > Self-Registration, turning off the Status on Default within the Self Registration Profiles widget, editing the configuration, enabling Matrix Rules on step 5, and selecting the Default Menu Profile for newly created accounts before saving. The organizational role rules method involves going to People Management > Data Centre, clicking View All next to HR Admin Setup Settings, selecting Menu Profile Matrix, clicking Add, configuring settings via dropdown options, and saving the changes. This document is essential for system administrators and access managers who need to efficiently configure user permissions and ensure employees receive appropriate menu profiles based on their roles within the organization.

s:

In the dashboard menu, search for and select Security.

Click Save.

To check if the Back Office account was created...
ss: Creating a Back Office account involves accessing the Security menu in your dashboard, selecting User Management, and setting up a new user with Back Office credentials. After creating the account, you'll need to verify it was set up correctly by navigating to All Back Office Accounts and linking it to the relevant HR employee record. You'll then assign the appropriate menu profiles to complete the configuration. Open this document when you need to set up a new Back Office user account from scratch or need step-by-step guidance on the verification and profile assignment process.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for creating and configuring a Back Office account within a portal system's security management interface. The creation process begins by navigating to the dashboard menu, selecting Security, then accessing User Management to click Create New User, where users must specify "Back Office" as the User Type and enter both username and password before saving. To verify successful account creation, administrators follow a similar path through Security and User Management but select All Back Office Accounts, then locate the relevant user and access the three-dot menu to click Manage Account. The configuration process requires clicking Actions, selecting Link to HR Person, and associating the account with the relevant employee from the system. The final setup step involves assigning the appropriate menu profiles to complete the Back Office account configuration. This document is typically used by system administrators or account managers who need to establish new Back Office user access within the organization's portal system, and it addresses the foundational task of user provisioning and linking employee records to their corresponding system accounts.

t: Single sign-on with LDAP
s:
When you have delegated your SSO authentication to an LDAP (e.g. Microsoft Active Directory), users log into PeopleXD Portal using their LDAP Account. When you use LDAP:

Passwords are not stored.

Authentication is delegated to an LDAP (e.g. Microsoft Active Directory).

LDAP allows for a user to l...
ss: Single sign-on with LDAP enables users to log into PeopleXD Portal using their Microsoft Active Directory or other LDAP account credentials, with authentication managed by your external directory rather than storing passwords in PeopleXD. Open this document if you need to set up or configure LDAP authentication, understand how password management works with delegated authentication, or learn how to record LDAP usernames in employee records. You'll find step-by-step instructions for navigating to the Contact Information screen and entering each employee's unique LDAP username in PeopleXD. This is essential reading if your organization uses Active Directory for network authentication and wants to streamline portal access.
sl: This document explains how to implement single sign-on (SSO) authentication using LDAP, such as Microsoft Active Directory, within the PeopleXD Portal system. It describes the key operational characteristics of LDAP authentication, including that passwords are not stored in PeopleXD but are instead managed by the external LDAP directory, and that users log into the portal using their LDAP credentials rather than separate Portal credentials. The document provides step-by-step instructions for configuring LDAP usernames in PeopleXD, requiring administrators to navigate to the Command Centre, select the Employees option, locate the specific employee record, access the Contact Information tab, and populate the LDAP user field with the employee's unique LDAP username through an Edit function. It emphasizes that LDAP usernames must be unique within the system and that the LDAP directory itself manages password policies rather than PeopleXD. This configuration is typically performed by system administrators or HR personnel setting up SSO authentication for their organization and allows users to access shared network applications with a single username and password across multiple systems. The document also references related help articles addressing password changes for Active Directory-synced accounts and general portal account username modifications, which may be consulted when users encounter authentication or password management issues.

t: Reuse the employee number from a deleted personnel profile
s:
A personnel number previously assigned to a deleted employee record can be reused, subject to the configuration rules in place. Review our detailed guidance first, then follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Data Centre.

Next to HR Admin Setup Settings, click OPEN, ...
ss: Reusing employee numbers from deleted personnel profiles in your HR system requires enabling the Default Manual option in Personnel Numbering Maintenance within Data Centre settings. This process allows you to manually assign a previously used personnel number when creating a new employee through the new starter wizard. Open this document when you need to recycle employee numbers due to high-volume hiring, number management constraints, or system configuration requirements. Follow the steps to activate manual numbering in your UAT environment first before implementing changes in your live system.
sl: This document provides guidance on how to reuse employee identification numbers from deleted personnel records within an HR system, subject to existing configuration rules. The process begins by navigating to the Data Centre from the dashboard menu, then accessing HR Admin Setup Settings and selecting Personnel Numbering Maintenance. The core configuration task involves enabling the "Active" option next to "Default Manual," which allows manual entry of personnel numbers during employee creation; the document notes this setting is normally enabled by default but recommends testing any changes in a UAT environment first. After enabling this option and saving the changes, users can then specify a particular personnel number when adding a new employee through the new starter wizard, effectively allowing recycling of previously assigned numbers. This document is primarily intended for HR administrators and system configuration staff who manage personnel records and need to optimize the reuse of employee numbers in their organization. The guidance assumes users have access to the dashboard, Data Centre, and HR Admin Setup Settings, and should be followed in sequence to ensure the personnel numbering system is properly configured before attempting to reuse deleted employee numbers.

t: Set up the generation of personnel numbers
s:
To help you configure personnel number generation, watch the video or follow the steps below.

 

 

Define personnel number generation rules

From the dashboard menu, search for and select Data Centre.

Next to HR Admin Setup Settings, click OPEN.

Click Personnel Numbering Maintenance to review th...
ss: Personnel number generation in PeopleXD is configured through the Data Centre's HR Admin Setup Settings, where you define numbering rules and set system defaults for automatic or manual routines. Use this document when you need to establish how employee numbers are created and assigned, customize numbering patterns, or switch between manual and automatic number generation. Open it during initial system setup or when your organization's employee numbering requirements change. The process involves accessing Personnel Numbering Maintenance to review and update generation rules, then setting your preferred default routine in System Parameters.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for configuring how personnel numbers are generated within an HR management system, covering both the definition of generation rules and the system-wide default settings. The first process involves accessing the Data Centre from the dashboard menu, opening HR Admin Setup Settings, and navigating to Personnel Numbering Maintenance to review and modify the current numbering rules by clicking into relevant fields and updating details as needed. Users are explicitly warned not to amend three critical fields: Personnel No Type, Generation Type, and Generation Routine, as these should remain unchanged to maintain system integrity. The Active checkbox can be toggled to enable or disable specific numbering rules as required before saving changes. The second process allows administrators to set the system-wide default behavior for personnel number generation by accessing the Data Centre, opening HR Admin Setup Settings, then clicking System Parameters, and selecting either Default Manual or Default Automatic under the Default Generate Personnel No Routine option. This document is intended for HR administrators and system configuration managers who need to establish or modify personnel numbering protocols within their organization's HR system. The related articles suggest this configuration is part of a broader new starter setup process and connects to other HR administration tasks such as employee number reuse and user access management.

s:

ss: Processing an employee as a leaver in PeopleXD Portal involves navigating to the People Management dashboard, locating the employee record, and selecting the Process As Leaver action. This task guides you through entering the required information to formally mark an employee's departure in the system. Open this document when you need to initiate the leaver process for an employee who is leaving your organization, or when you're setting up the administrative steps needed before their final day.
sl: This document provides instructions for marking an employee as a leaver within the Access Group's People Management system, and it caters to HR administrators and managers responsible for employee lifecycle management. The process begins by navigating to the People Management dashboard and accessing the Command Centre widget, where users click View on the Employees option to locate and select the specific employee. Once an employee's record is open, users click the Actions button and then select Process As Leaver to initiate the leaver workflow. The system then requires users to enter required information in designated fields before saving the changes to finalize the employee's leaver status. The document acknowledges related processes such as updating appointment end dates, creating allowances, and assigning the Leaver Profile to an employee, which may be performed alongside or instead of the main process. This procedure is typically used when an employee is leaving the organization and needs to be transitioned out of active employment status in the system.

t: Cannot remove a leaver's end date once processed by payroll
s:
This error indicates the employee is fully dormant on payroll, so you can no longer remove the end date. To rectify this, you will need to rehire the employee.

Related Articles
Portal: Updating an appointment end date
Portal: Contract start date corrections
Unable to amend end date as generate sala...
ss: When an employee's end date has been processed by payroll and they become fully dormant in the system, you cannot remove or modify that end date through standard processes. This article explains why the end date removal fails and what you need to do instead—specifically, that you'll need to rehire the employee to make changes. Open this if you're trying to amend a leaver's end date after payroll has already processed it and you're encountering an error preventing removal.
sl: This document explains a specific limitation in the payroll system where an employee's end date cannot be removed after the employee has become fully dormant on payroll. The issue occurs after payroll processing has completed, at which point the system locks the end date field to prevent modifications. Users encountering this error will find that attempting to remove or alter the end date through standard processes will be blocked by the system. To resolve this situation and regain the ability to modify the employee's status, the document indicates that the only available solution is to rehire the employee through the appropriate rehire process. The document serves HR and payroll administrators who need to understand the constraints around modifying leaver information once payroll processing has finalized an employee's dormant status. Related guidance is available through several connected articles covering appointment end date updates in both the Portal and Back Office systems, as well as information about running final mode salary generation, which appears to trigger similar restrictions on end date amendments.

t: Portal: Rehire an employee
s: Rehiring employees efficiently ensures a smooth return to the workforce and maintains accurate records. Whether an employee returns after a temporary departure or renews a contract, following the correct rehiring process in the portal helps prevent errors and compliance issues. Watch the video or fo...
ss: The rehiring process in the portal Command Centre allows you to efficiently bring dormant employees back into your workforce while maintaining accurate records. Use this guide when an employee returns after a temporary departure or renews their contract, as following the correct steps prevents errors and compliance issues. The process involves locating the dormant employee record, launching the rehire wizard, and completing four stages of setup before saving the changes to the system.
sl: This document provides guidance on efficiently rehiring employees through the portal system while maintaining accurate workforce records and ensuring compliance. The process begins by accessing the Command Centre from the dashboard menu via the search bar, then navigating to the Employees section and selecting the Dormant filter from the dropdown to locate inactive staff members. Once the relevant employee is found and their record is opened by clicking VIEW, users access the rehiring functionality through the ACTIONS button, which launches the rehire wizard. The rehiring workflow is divided into four stages that must be completed sequentially: stages 1, 2, and 3 are progressed through using the NEXT button, followed by stage 4, which is finalized by clicking SAVE. This document is intended for HR personnel and administrators who handle employee returns, whether following temporary departures or contract renewals, and helps prevent common errors and compliance issues that can arise from improper rehiring procedures. The document also references related articles covering scenarios such as missing rehire options, dormant employee list issues, and alternative rehiring processes available in the back office system.

t: Unable to amend end date as generate salaries and allowances has been run in final mode
s: Once Final Generate (Final Mode) has been enabled during the Salaries & Allowances job for a pay group in PeopleXD Payroll, it is no longer possible to amend or delete the employee’s end date in PeopleXD People Management. To resolve this, liaise with your internal payroll team and follow the steps ...
ss: When Final Mode is enabled for the Salaries & Allowances job in PeopleXD Payroll, you cannot amend or delete an employee's end date in PeopleXD People Management. Open this article if you need to change an employee's end date but encounter this restriction during payroll processing. The document provides steps to resolve the issue by rolling back processes and temporarily disabling final generate mode, making your amendment, then re-enabling the mode to resume normal payroll processing.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre explains the restriction that prevents users from amending or deleting an employee's end date in PeopleXD People Management once the Final Generate function has been run in Final Mode during the Salaries & Allowances job for a specific pay group in PeopleXD Payroll. The document provides a resolution process that involves four main steps: rolling back processes and disabling final generate mode, amending the end date, re-enabling final generate mode, and resuming normal payroll processing. It includes a critical warning that if payroll processing has advanced too far, rolling back may not be possible, which means no amendments can be made during that pay period. This guidance is intended for payroll administrators and HR professionals who work with PeopleXD systems and need to update employee end dates but encounter this system restriction. The document references related help articles on updating appointment end dates and addresses a related error message about allowance amendments, indicating it is part of a broader knowledge base covering PeopleXD configuration and payroll management workflows.

t: Creating the Leaver Profile
s:
Creating the Leaver Profile allows leavers limited system access for a short period following their departure.

Go to Data Centre then to HR Admin Setup Settings (or click View All).

Find Access Profile Configuration and open this option.

Click on Add, enter the Profile Name, and set Expiry Days -...
ss: The Leaver Profile feature in PeopleXD allows you to configure limited system access for departing employees during their notice period or immediately after departure. You set this up in Data Centre by navigating to HR Admin Setup Settings, then Access Profile Configuration, where you define the profile name, expiry days, and assign the appropriate menu profile for leavers. Open this guide when you need to establish the rules for how long former employees can access the portal and what functions they can perform before their access is fully removed. Once configured, you'll use this leaver profile when processing employee departures through the HR Task List.
sl: This document provides instructions for creating a Leaver Profile within an HR management system, which enables departing employees to retain limited portal access for a defined period after their exit date. Users access the feature by navigating to Data Centre, then HR Admin Setup Settings (or using the View All option), and selecting Access Profile Configuration. The setup process involves clicking Add, entering a Profile Name, and specifying Expiry Days to determine how long leavers will retain system access following their departure date. The configuration requires ticking the Leaver Profile checkbox and selecting an appropriate menu profile from the available options using the right arrow assignment tool. Once created, this leaver profile becomes available for assignment to departing employees through the HR Task List workflow, streamlining the process of granting temporary, restricted access to leavers. ss: When a rehired employee continues appearing on the CorePersonnel dormant list after rejoining, this is typically expected behavior during payroll processing. The employee's status automatically updates to fully active ('S') once you run the Complete Update Payroll Job (Pay355) and subsequent payroll steps are completed. If an employee remains dormant, check whether they're assigned to a pay group that has active payroll runs—employees in unprocessed pay groups stay dormant until moved to an active pay group. Open this document if you're concerned about a rehire still showing as dormant in CorePersonnel or need to understand the timeline for their status to update.
sl: This document explains why rehired employees may continue appearing on the dormant employee list in CorePersonnel after being processed as rehires, and provides guidance on resolving or understanding this behavior. The primary recommendation is to ensure an employee is fully dormant before processing them as a rehire to prevent issues from occurring. In the most common scenario, the system is functioning correctly and no manual intervention is required; users should simply wait for the employee's status to update automatically when running the Complete Update Payroll Job (Pay355), which will transition the employee from dormant status to fully active ('S') as payroll processing steps are completed. The document clarifies that employees may temporarily show a date left and latest start/rejoin date in CorePersonnel while the payroll is still processing, though they are typically not actually dormant in CorePay (where dormant status is marked as 'Z'), meaning their approved salary remains unaffected. A second scenario addresses situations where an employee remains dormant because they are assigned to a pay group that is not processed or has no payroll runs completed for it; in this case, the employee will only become active once moved to a pay group that is actively processed. A third scenario mentions employees who are in a pay group, rejoin, and are moved to a different pay group before the rejoin is fully completed, requiring coordination of these actions. The document notes that the Customer Support team cannot manually intervene to activate employees earlier, as doing so could create knock-on effects in CorePay.

The document is designed for HR administrators and portal users who need to maintain accurate company information within their organisation's structure without affecting the underlying company code or system identifiers. This task is part of broader organisational data management functions, as indicated by related articles covering reference data additions, cost centre amendments, HR access grants, and employee role assignments. The straightforward four-step procedure ensures that company naming changes can be made efficiently while preserving the integrity of the company's unique identifier code in the system.

t: Remove a vacant post from the Org Chart
s:
To remove a vacant post from the Org Chart, you need to complete one of the following actions. 

unlink post's appointment from a vacancy in case of 'Recruiting' status.

end post's appointment in case of 'Authorised' status.

📌Note: Updates to the Org Chart will be visible the next day after the ov...
ss: Removing a vacant post from the Org Chart in PeopleXD requires different actions depending on the post's status: unlinking the post's appointment from a vacancy if it has 'Recruiting' status, or ending the appointment if it has 'Authorised' status. For recruiting posts, navigate to Recruitment, find the vacancy, and use the Remove button on the Linked Appointments tab. For authorised posts, access Post Profile Maintenance in the Data Centre, locate the post, and select End Appointment with an appropriate end date. Open this document when you need to clean up vacant positions from your organization chart after recruitment is cancelled or positions are no longer needed.
sl: This document provides instructions for removing a vacant post from the Org Chart within the Access Group system, covering two distinct processes depending on the post's status. For posts with 'Recruiting' status, users must unlink the post's appointment from its associated vacancy by navigating to Recruitment, locating the vacancy in the Vacancies widget, selecting Edit Vacancy from the Actions menu, accessing the Linked Appointments tab, and using the Remove button to unlink the appointment. For posts with 'Authorised' status, users must end the post's appointment by going to the Data Centre widget, selecting View All, opening Post Profile Maintenance, viewing the post, navigating to the View Appointments tab, filtering by Authorised status, and then selecting End Appointment from the Actions menu while specifying an end date. The document includes a helpful tip that users can create an Insight report using the Competition Appointment (Recruitment) view if they need to identify the vacancy ID associated with an appointment. A critical note indicates that changes to the Org Chart will not appear immediately but will be visible the following day after the overnight job completes. This document is essential for HR administrators, recruiters, and organizational managers who need to maintain accurate organizational structures by removing posts that are no longer required or have been filled.

t: Back Office: Configuring org roles and groups
s:
Organisation roles and groups - Terminology

The first step of understanding Organisation Roles and Groups is to have a clear understanding of the terminology involved:

Reporting to Type - This is either Employee ('E') or Organisational ('O') Role and Group. If this is set to 'E' then logic is simp...
ss: Organisational roles and groups in CorePersonnel define the hierarchical structure used to manage reporting lines, approvals, and access controls across your HR system. This document covers how to set up organisational roles (such as Line Manager or Timesheet Approver), assign them at specific organisational levels (Company, Department, Cost Centre, Work Group, etc.), and configure the "Reports To" functionality either by individual employee or by organisational group. Open this if you need to establish or maintain manager hierarchies, set up role-based access for different departments or business units, or configure how reporting relationships are defined in CorePersonnel.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide to configuring organisational roles and groups within the Back Office system, specifically addressing how to set up reporting hierarchies and manager assignments in CorePersonnel. The document begins by defining key terminology: "Reporting to Type" (either Employee or Organisational), "Organisational Role" (such as Line Manager or Timesheet Approver), and "Organisational Group" (such as Company, Department, or Cost Centre), which are essential concepts for understanding the configuration process. To set up organisational roles, users navigate to CorePersonnel through Personnel > Reference K-P > Organisational Role Types to create roles, then configure the "Reports To" functionality via CorePersonnel Main Menu > Reference Q-Z > System Parameters, where they can choose between individual employee-level assignment or organisational group-based setup. The document explains that managers can be assigned at various hierarchical levels including Company, Cost Centre, Department, Division, Location, Management Unit, Pay Group, Project Code, User Fields 1-5, and Work Group (the default level), each with Date From and Date To fields to define applicability periods. Users have two primary screens for maintaining organisational roles: "Maintain Organisational Roles" and "Maintain Organisational Roles by Person," with the latter allowing role assignment by selecting an employee, choosing the role and organisational group from dropdown lists, and specifying the date range and group item. This document is intended for Back Office administrators and CorePersonnel users who need to configure manager reporting structures and employee hierarchies, and it addresses scenarios where standard reporting chains need to be overridden or customized at different organisational levels to support various functional requirements.

ss: Adding a new location to your organisational hierarchy structure in CorePersonnel involves navigating to Post Management, editing your Organisational Hierarchy, and creating a new location entry with its code, name, and area code. Open this document when you need to expand your business structure by registering a new office, branch, or work site in the system. The step-by-step instructions walk you through the Back Office process from initial setup to saving the new location so it appears in your active locations list.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for adding a new location to an organisation's hierarchy structure within the Back Office system, specifically targeting users responsible for maintaining organisational data and structures. The process begins by navigating to CorePersonnel, then Maintenance, followed by selecting Post Management and clicking on Organisational Hierarchy. Users must locate their Structure and click Edit, then confirm a warning dialog that appears by clicking Yes. The next stage involves clicking the Reference button next to Location and using the Green tick icon in the top left to display all currently active Locations in the system. To add a new location, users click the Green Plus icon and enter three required pieces of information: the Code, name, and area code for the new location. After entering these details, users click Save to complete the addition to the organisational hierarchy. This document is primarily used by back office administrators, human resources personnel, or organisational structure managers who need to expand their company's location hierarchy and maintain accurate reference data within the CorePersonnel system.

ss: Creating new organisation units and adding them to your business structure in CorePersonnel involves two key processes: first setting up the unit itself (either through Reference menus or Organisational Hierarchy configuration), then positioning it within your hierarchy under the appropriate department or level. Open this document when you need to establish a new location, department, or other business unit and integrate it into your existing organisational structure. You'll use the CorePersonnel back office module, navigating through Reference or Post Management sections depending on your preferred method. This task is essential when your business expands, reorganises, or needs to reflect structural changes in the system.
sl: This document provides instructions for creating and adding new organisation units to a business structure within the Access Group back office system. It describes two alternative methods for creating new business units: the first involves navigating through CorePersonnel > Reference, selecting the appropriate alphabetic reference group (such as Reference K - P for Location Codes), using the query icon to refresh configured codes, and clicking the insert icon to create a new record with relevant details before saving. The second method uses CorePersonnel > Maintenance > Post Management > Organisational Hierarchy, where users can edit their structure and insert new records through the Reference section. Once a unit is created, users can add it to the organisational hierarchy by navigating to CorePersonnel > Maintenance > Post Management > Organisational Hierarchy, expanding the hierarchy data to the required level (such as expanding to a specific department), selecting the appropriate "Add" option for the unit type, and using the search function to locate and add the item to the hierarchy. The document emphasizes enabling the "Active" status before saving where this option is available and recommends checking the "Include Linked Items" option to display all available elements during the addition process. This guide is intended for back office administrators and organisational managers who need to expand their company's business structure and maintain accurate hierarchical relationships within the system.

s:

Access this process through CorePersonnel > Maintenance > Post Management > Organisational Hierarchy to review existing structures and verify that all required fields are populated and the hierarchy indicator is enabled at the top level. Open this guide when you need to audit your org structure setup, troubleshoot missing or blank date fields, or confirm that your hierarchy is correctly configured before ongoing operations.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for validating an organisational hierarchy structure in the CorePersonnel system's Back Office module. Users access the validation process by navigating to CorePersonnel > Maintenance > Post Management > Organisational Hierarchy, which opens the Maintain Hierarchy Structure screen displaying all existing structures. The document outlines critical validation checks to ensure that the organisational structure includes minimum required fields: Company (ORGZ), Management Unit (MGTU), Department (DEPT), Cost Centre (COST), Location (LOC), and Work Group (WRKGRP). It also requires verification that the Hierarchy Indicator is enabled at the top level of the structure. The document identifies specific error scenarios that warrant escalation to support, including missing structure codes, blank Date Applied fields, and blank Effective Date fields; users encountering these issues should click Edit on the structure code to access the Add New Hierarchy Structure screen for remediation. This document is primarily used by system administrators, HR professionals, or Back Office operators responsible for configuring and maintaining organisational data integrity within CorePersonnel.

t: Assign organisational roles to employees
s:
Organisational roles need to be linked to the actual employee record of the user that will be fulfilling the role on PeopleXD. Hence, organisational roles cannot be assigned to external users.

 

For example, in order for an employee to receive notifications as the Head of Department for the Techno...
ss: Organisational roles in PeopleXD must be assigned directly to employee records to enable system notifications and workflow processes—for example, flagging an employee as Head of Department or Payroll Salary Approver. You can assign roles using two methods: the Maintain Org Roles screen (organized by department, pay group, or work group) or the Maintain Organisational Roles by Person screen (organized by individual employee). Both methods require you to select the org structure, define the role type, specify effective dates, and save the assignment so the employee can participate in role-dependent processes. Open this document when you need to set up or modify an employee's organizational role permissions in PeopleXD.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on assigning organisational roles to employee records in PeopleXD, a personnel management system, explaining that organisational roles must be linked to actual employee records rather than external users to enable role-specific system functionality. The document describes two distinct methods for assigning roles: the first via the Maintain Org Roles screen (accessed through Back Office > CorePersonnel, Reference, Maintain Organisational Roles or Portal > People Management, Data Centre, View all, Maintain Organisation Roles), where users select an organisational structure, group type, and group item before adding role assignments to available rows; and the second via the Maintain Org Roles by Person screen (Back Office > CorePersonnel, Reference, Maintain Organisational Roles by Person or Portal > People Management, Data Centre, View all, Maintain Organisation Roles by Person), which begins with a keyword search to locate specific employees before assigning roles. Both methods require users to populate identical fields: the Role drop-down to select the specific organisational role, a Date From field (in DD-MON-YYYY format) indicating when the role becomes active, an optional Date To field marking role cessation, and identification of the organisational group and group item against which the role applies—such as Department for Head of Department, Pay Group for Payroll Salary Approver, or Work Group for Reports to Manager. The document is designed for PeopleXD administrators and HR personnel who need to configure role assignments that enable employees to receive notifications and participate in system processes tied to their designated positions within the organisation. Once saved, these assignments make employees visible in the system as having specific roles and allow them to engage in all corresponding system processes and workflows associated with those roles.

s:

ss: Use the Customer Success Portal to reopen a support case that has been marked as resolved when the provided solution hasn't worked for you. You have 72 hours from the time support closed the case to reply and reopen it by adding a comment—after this window closes, the case will be fully closed. Rather than creating a new case, replying to the original case ensures the analyst who handled your issue receives notification and can continue supporting you without delays.
sl: This document provides instructions for reopening a customer support case that has been marked as resolved when the provided solution has not worked. The process involves logging into the Customer Success Portal, navigating to View All Cases, selecting the specific case marked as Solved, and adding a comment to reopen it. The document emphasizes a critical time constraint: customers have only 72 hours from the time support marks a case as resolved to reply and reopen it, after which the case will be fully closed if no response is received. An important warning cautions users not to open a new case instead, as doing so will fail to notify the original analyst and may delay resolution of the issue. This guidance is intended for customers in the Access Group support system who need to escalate unresolved issues without losing continuity with their assigned support analyst. The document also references related articles covering topics such as creating HAR files for diagnostic purposes, understanding case priority levels, and handling duplicate cases in the support portal.

t: Identifying a case priority
s:
When raising a new case for the support team's attention, it’s important to assign the correct priority to ensure the issue is resolved within an appropriate timeframe. The available priority levels and the conditions under which they apply are outlined below.

 

Priority 1
Critical Impact

Service...
ss: Case priority assignment determines how quickly the support team will address your issue, ranging from Priority 1 (critical service outages affecting payroll, banking, or portal access) to Priority 4 (minor access or account issues). Use this guide when submitting a support case for payroll systems, CoreTime, banking functions, or other business-critical software to select the appropriate priority level based on the scope and impact of your problem. Priority levels reflect whether the issue affects all users or just some, whether core functions are completely down or still partially working, and whether business-critical processes like pay runs or bank file submissions are blocked. Open this document whenever you're unsure whether your case should be treated as urgent or routine.
sl: This document provides guidance for support team members or case managers on how to properly categorize and assign priority levels to incoming support cases within the Access Group system. It establishes four distinct priority tiers—Priority 1 (Critical Impact), Priority 2 (Significant Impact), Priority 3 (Minimal Impact), and Priority 4 (No Impact)—each with clear definitions and specific examples of issues that fall within that category. Priority 1 cases include the most severe situations such as complete service unavailability across platforms, portal unavailability for all users, bank file submission failures, and incomplete pay runs, all of which require immediate attention. Priority 2 addresses significant but partial service disruptions affecting business-critical functions, including module unavailability for all users, salary amendments, invalid IBAN codes, and payroll submission issues not appearing in ROS. Priority 3 encompasses minor system performance issues or problems in non-critical environments like UAT, such as individual amendments, payment cancellations, timesheet deletions, and cost allocation errors. Priority 4 is assigned to negligible-impact issues in non-critical processes, such as locked user accounts, access problems to specific screens, and inability to view staff qualifications in the personnel module. This document is typically used by support administrators, case managers, or anyone responsible for triaging incoming support requests to ensure issues are routed and resolved according to their actual business impact and urgency.

t: Duplicate cases in the support portal
s:
The support team may close a case without providing a solution if it is identified as a duplicate. A case is considered duplicate when an existing ticket already addresses the same issue. This can happen for several reasons.

A customer accidentally creates two cases for the same issue. In this scen...
ss: When you submit a support case, the support team may close it as a duplicate if an existing ticket already addresses the same issue. This typically happens when you accidentally create multiple cases for the same problem, submit a new case instead of using the escalation procedure, or open a new case rather than reopening a previously resolved ticket. In these situations, the support team closes the duplicate case and adds you as a collaborator on the original ticket, where you'll receive all future updates. Read this if you've had a case closed as a duplicate or want to understand how to properly escalate or reopen existing cases.
sl: This document explains how the support team manages duplicate cases in the support portal and the circumstances that lead to cases being closed without a solution. A duplicate case occurs when an existing ticket already addresses the same issue, and the support team will close the duplicate while continuing work on the original ticket. The document describes three specific scenarios that commonly result in duplicates: when a customer accidentally creates multiple cases for the same problem (in which case the original case owner is added as a collaborator to the second case), when a customer opens a new case to escalate an existing one (requiring use of the escalation procedure instead), and when a customer creates a new case to continue investigation rather than reopening a previously resolved case. In all duplicate situations, the support team closes the redundant case and directs all future updates and communication through the original ticket to maintain a single source of record. This document is relevant for support team members who triage and manage incoming cases, as well as for customers who need to understand why their case might be closed in favor of an existing ticket addressing the same issue.

ss: The Classic UI indicator parameter (cp_display_old_ui) controls whether users see the modern or classic interface in your system. sl: This document provides instructions for enabling or disabling the UI display option between modern and classic user interfaces within the system's administrator settings. The process requires access to the Administrator dashboard, where users must navigate to Admin settings to locate the configuration parameter. The specific setting that controls this functionality is identified as cp_display_old_ui, which serves as the toggle mechanism for switching between UI versions. t: Portal: Manager unable to access all employees
s:

ss: When a manager cannot see all their expected staff on the dashboard or isn't receiving leave requests for approval, the issue is often an incorrect work group assignment on an employee's contract. This document walks through accessing the People Management system, locating the employee's contract in the Command Centre, and updating the work group assignment with the correct effective date. Open this guide when you need to fix visibility or approval routing issues for specific employees under a manager's supervision.
sl: This document addresses a common access issue where managers cannot view all expected staff members on their dashboard or receive leave requests for approval, with the root cause typically being incorrect work group assignments on employee contracts. The document provides step-by-step instructions to resolve this issue, beginning with navigating to People Management from the dashboard menu and then accessing the Command Centre to locate and view the specific employee. Once the employee record is located, users must click VIEW to access the Contracts section, where they can select the relevant contract if the employee has multiple ones listed in a drop-down menu. The resolution process involves clicking UPDATE under the Amendments section, noting the latest start date, and then updating the Work Group field before clicking NEXT. Users must then update the Effective Date field with the previously noted start date and complete any blank mandatory fields such as Reason before saving the changes. This document is intended for managers or administrators who need to troubleshoot visibility issues in the portal and ensure employees have proper work group assignments so that staff appear correctly on manager dashboards and leave requests route appropriately for approval.

ss: Granting HR access to users in People Management determines what employee data they can view and manage in the system. This document covers three methods to configure HR user access: using the HR User Access (Basic) screen via the Data Centre widget, assigning access directly from an employee's record, or managing permissions through the System Users screen in the Security dashboard. Open this guide when you need to set up HR access for new team members, adjust existing user permissions by structure level, or enable specific menu profiles and data visibility. Each method offers different entry points depending on which dashboard or employee record you're already working in.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide for granting HR access to users within a People Management system, detailing how employee data visibility is controlled through user role configuration. The document outlines three distinct methods for assigning and managing HR user access depending on which system areas the administrator has permission to access. The second method involves using the Assign Access screen from an employee's individual record, accessed through the People Management Dashboard > Command Centre tab > Employees > View, where administrators can assign both HR access and menu profile access by selecting the HR User Access tab and moving items to an Assigned column. The third method operates through the Security dashboard's System Users screen, where administrators can select the Portal, locate the employee in the Username list, choose Personnel Access from the Security Type list, configure Structure Code and Access Level settings, and toggle the Access Granted switch for each item. This document serves administrators, HR managers, and system users who need to configure employee data access permissions based on organizational structure and role requirements.

sl: This document explains how to assign organisational roles to employees and managers within a portal system, detailing the processes administrators use to define managerial and approval responsibilities across the organisation. The second approach, Maintain Organisational Roles by Person, allows administrators to search for and select specific employees by name or personnel number through the same Data Centre interface, then assign roles to those individuals within their selected business unit structure. Both processes follow identical navigation paths starting from the dashboard menu, searching for and selecting Data Centre, clicking VIEW ALL, then accessing Maintain Organisation Roles, with final confirmation achieved by clicking Save and OK. This document is designed for system administrators responsible for managing approval workflows and managerial hierarchies, helping them resolve scenarios where specific employees need salary approval access or manager dashboard visibility based on their organisational position and responsibilities.

sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide for setting up user permissions and access controls so that employees can approve salaries in either the portal or back office system. The document helps resolve scenarios where salary approval functionality is unavailable or not visible for specific users, addressing permission gaps that prevent approvers from performing their duties. t: Portal: Release a system lock
s:
A network outage or an incorrect logout has caused a function to become locked and unavailable. To resolve this, follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, enter Security in the search bar and select it.

Click Back Office Sessions, then click VIEW ALL.

Click Status, then select Sort Ascendi...
ss: When a network outage or incorrect logout leaves a function locked and unavailable in your system, you can release the lock by accessing Security settings from the dashboard and terminating the affected sessions. This process involves navigating to Back Office Sessions, sorting by status to identify locked sessions, and using the KILL SESSION function to clear them. Open this document when you encounter a locked function that's preventing you from working in PeopleXD or need to resolve session-related access issues caused by connection problems or improper logouts.
sl: This document provides guidance on resolving system locks that occur when network outages or incorrect logouts prevent a function from becoming available in the portal. The process begins by navigating to the Security section through the dashboard menu search bar, then accessing Back Office Sessions and clicking VIEW ALL to display all active sessions. Users can then organize the sessions by clicking Status and selecting Sort Ascending, which groups sessions by their status type to simplify identification of the problematic session. Once the affected session is located, the resolution involves clicking KILL SESSION on the relevant session entry to terminate it and release the lock. This document is typically used by portal administrators or support personnel who need to restore functionality to locked systems and get users back to normal operation without waiting for automatic timeout. The guide also references a related article about unlocking locked records within PeopleXD modules from the back office, suggesting it is part of a broader collection of portal troubleshooting and administration documentation.

t: Access to salaries
s:
You can grant administrators access to salary information in an employee record record by ensuring they have the appropriate menu option enabled and are assigned the correct pay group access. To do this, follow the steps below.

 

Required menu option

The following menu option must be enabled on t...
ss: Grant administrators access to salary information in employee records through People Management or CorePortal by enabling the APPOINTMENT SALARY menu option on their user profile. You must also assign the correct pay group access in CorePay Pay Users, which allows administrators to view employee salary and allowance data. Use this document when setting up new HR admin users who need to access or approve salary information, or when troubleshooting why an administrator cannot see the Current Salary tab in an employee record.
sl: This document provides instructions for granting administrator access to salary information within employee records in an Access Group system. It covers two essential requirements: first, administrators must have the APPOINTMENT SALARY menu option enabled on their user menu profile, which can be configured in either the People Management system (Menu ID: EMPLOYEE_DASHBOARD_MENU.APPOINTMENT_SALARY, reference 409392) or alternatively through CorePortal (Menu ID: MAIN_MENU.HR_ADMIN_APPOINTMENT_SALARY, reference 409392), enabling the Current Salary tab to display on employee records. Second, users must be assigned access to the relevant pay groups by navigating to Portal's Security section, clicking the Set Up tab, opening the CorePay Pay Users widget, selecting Portal Account, and using the Filter icon to locate the user and verify existing pay group access. If a user cannot be found in this search, they have no pay group access and must be added by clicking Add, entering the pay group code, username, and input location, then saving the configuration. This document serves HR administrators and system configuration staff who need to manage which employees and administrators can view salary and allowance data within the system. The guidance also references related articles addressing scenarios where salary information is not visible for approval, where the Current Salary tab is missing entirely, or where access controls need to be adjusted for specific managers or employee privacy settings.

ss: Locking or unlocking user accounts in CorePortal controls whether employees can access portal and back office accounts. System administrators and super users follow the same process for both account types: navigate to User Management, query the employee, select the relevant account type, and toggle the Locked option on or off. Open this document when you need to disable an employee's system access immediately or reinstate access for a returning or transferred employee.
sl: This document provides instructions for locking or unlocking user accounts to disable or reinstate account access within the CorePortal system, a task typically performed by site system administrators or super users. The document covers two distinct processes: managing portal accounts and managing back office accounts, each following a similar procedural path. For both account types, users must first log into CorePortal and navigate to User Management using the keyword search or quick jump option at the top of the screen. The process requires querying the specific employee and selecting either "All Active Portal Accounts" for portal accounts or "All Back Office Accounts" for back office accounts from the dropdown menu. Once the employee is located, users click the three dots menu and select "Manage Account," where they can toggle the "Locked" option to either lock or unlock the account as needed. This document helps resolve access control scenarios where account activity needs to be suspended temporarily or restored after previous suspension, and it addresses the common administrative task of managing user permissions across both the portal and back office environments.

t: Portal: Assigning access to users to view employees
s:
Access to employee records in the PeopleXD People Management dashboard is controlled by the personnel access that has been granted to a user. To manage this, follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, in the search bar, enter and select Data Centre.

Click VIEW ALL, then click HR User Access....
ss: Controlling user access to employee records in the PeopleXD People Management dashboard requires assigning personnel access through the Data Centre's HR User Access settings. This process involves selecting an employee, choosing a Structure Code and Access Level, then enabling access to specific items or all records at once. Open this document when you need to grant a user permission to view employee data in the Portal, or when managing what employee information different team members can access. The steps also show how to use an employee's name or personnel number to quickly locate the right person in the system.
sl: This document provides instructions for controlling and granting user access to employee records within the PeopleXD People Management dashboard, specifically through the portal's access management features. The process begins by navigating to the Data Centre from the dashboard menu using the search bar, then selecting VIEW ALL followed by HR User Access to reach the configuration screen. Users must locate the target employee by entering either their name or personnel number in the Username field, then configure access permissions by selecting Personnel Access under Security Type and choosing an appropriate Structure Code. The document guides users through selecting an Access Level and using the Show Access function to view available permissions, after which they can either enable Access Granted for individual items or use the Select All option to grant broader permissions. This procedure is essential for administrators or HR personnel who need to manage which employees can view specific personnel records in the system, preventing unauthorized access while ensuring necessary visibility for legitimate business purposes. The document is designed for HR administrators and system managers responsible for configuring user permissions and controlling data visibility within the PeopleXD platform.

t: Learn account not creating
s:
If an employee’s Learn account has not yet been created and they are unable to log in to view their training requirements, please check the following details in PeopleXD.

Email Address - Ensure this is entered as the employee’s work email address.

⚠️Important: If the email address has previously b...
ss: When an employee cannot log in to Learn to access their training requirements, their account may not have been created yet. Check their PeopleXD record to ensure their work email address is entered correctly (and removed from any dormant employee records if it was previously used), a manager is assigned, and their job title has no extra spaces. Learn accounts are generated automatically overnight, so allow one business day after making any corrections before following up. Open this document if you're troubleshooting why an employee lacks Learn access despite being in the system.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for situations where an employee's Learn account has failed to be created, preventing them from accessing their training requirements and logging into the system. The document directs users to verify three specific employee record fields in PeopleXD: the Email Address (which must be the employee's work email), the Manager assignment, and the Job Title (which should not contain leading or trailing spaces). A critical consideration highlighted is that if the email address was previously associated with a dormant employee record, it must be removed from that old record by contacting support before a new Learn account can be provisioned. The document notes that Learn accounts are generated through an overnight automated process, so any corrections made to these three fields should be reviewed the following day to confirm successful account creation. This troubleshooting document is primarily used by HR administrators, support staff, or managers who need to diagnose why new employees cannot access their training records in the Learn system due to account provisioning failures.

ss: Updating employee bank details in PeopleXD requires administrators to have specific security permissions configured first. This document covers how to enable access through the Menu Profile in portal Security and then how to locate and update an employee's bank details via the People Management Dashboard. Open this guide when you need to add or modify an employee's banking information for payroll purposes, or when you're setting up administrator permissions to manage sensitive employee financial data.
sl: This document provides guidance on managing employee bank details within the Access Group system, covering both the permission setup required and the practical steps for updating this sensitive information. Administrators must first establish appropriate access permissions by navigating to portal Security, selecting the relevant HR Admin Menu Profile, clicking the three dots to access Manage menu options, and ensuring that both "CorePortal - Employee Bank Details Pay Update" and "CorePortal - Employee Bank Details Pay View" options are enabled. Once permissions are configured, bank details can be added or modified by accessing the People Management Dashboard, querying the specific employee record and clicking View, then selecting Actions followed by Personal Profile in the top right corner, where bank details can be updated and saved. The document emphasizes that employee bank details are classified as sensitive information, making proper access control essential before any administrator can make changes to these records. The guidance also references related articles on access management topics including salaries access, employee contract visibility, personal information lockdown, and bank details restriction—indicating this is part of a broader suite of security and access control documentation. This resource is primarily used by HR administrators and system administrators who need to configure security settings and by HR personnel who regularly update employee banking information in their operational workflow.
