The resolution process involves locating the specific role or group that grants HR Dashboard viewing permissions, then adjusting the From Date field by moving it back one day and saving, followed by changing it back to the original date and saving again—a process that must be repeated for each record if multiple entries exist with the same role or group. The document is designed for system administrators or HR personnel who manage user access and organizational role assignments, particularly when troubleshooting why managers cannot access employee HR Dashboard information despite having the role assigned. If the date adjustment procedure does not resolve the issue, the document directs users to escalate the problem by raising a support case.

t: Message 'Error: oops, something has gone wrong. no employee mapping found..'
s:
This error in PeopleXD or eRecruitment may result from various scenarios.

Cause 1 - No LDAP row for the employee in the Contact screen.

Cause 2 - No email address for the employee in the Contact screen.

Cause 3 - Portal username is not linked to the back-office account.

Cause 4 - Incorrect recru...
ss: When you see the "Error: oops, something has gone wrong. No employee mapping found" message in PeopleXD or eRecruitment, it typically means there's a missing or incomplete employee record in your system. The error can stem from four main causes: a missing LDAP network username in the Contact screen, a missing email address, a portal username that isn't linked to the back-office account, or an incorrect recruitment URL for Active Directory clients. Open this article if you need step-by-step instructions for updating employee contact details in People Management or CorePersonnel, linking portal accounts to HR records, or correcting your recruitment portal URL.
sl: This document explains the "Error: oops, something has gone wrong. no employee mapping found" message that occurs in PeopleXD or eRecruitment systems, providing users with four distinct causes and corresponding resolutions to troubleshoot and fix the issue. The error stems from missing or incomplete employee data configurations, specifically: the absence of an LDAP row in the Contact screen, missing email addresses in the Contact screen, unlinked portal usernames to back-office accounts, or incorrect recruitment URLs for Active Directory clients. Resolution 1 addresses the LDAP configuration gap by guiding users through People Management (Command Centre > Employees) or CorePersonnel (Maintenance > Personal Profile) to add the employee's network username under Contacts as an LDAP entry. Resolution 2 resolves missing email addresses through similar navigation paths in either the portal or back-office systems, requiring users to add a new Contact row with type EMAIL and the employee's email address. Resolution 3 tackles portal-to-back-office account linking by accessing Security > User Management in the portal, where users search for the employee, select "Manage account," and click "Link to HR Person" to connect the portal account to the correct personnel number. Resolution 4 addresses URL-related issues specific to AD (Active Directory) clients, directing users to replace the standard CorePortal URL with the alternative recruitment-specific URL containing "CLIENTCODErecruit" in the path. This document is essential for HR administrators, IT support staff, and portal users who encounter employee mapping errors during recruitment or personnel management processes.

t: Error - 'Could not reserve record'
s:

ss: The "Could not reserve record" error occurs when another user is actively accessing the same record in PeopleXD, locking it from your edits. Open this document when you encounter this error message and need to regain access to a locked record. The solution involves either waiting for the record to unlock automatically (which can take an hour or more) or contacting your security administrator to manually end the session holding the lock.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre explains the "Could not reserve record" error message that users encounter in their system. The error occurs when a database record is currently being accessed and locked by another user, which prevents the current user from editing that record. The document provides two primary resolution strategies: users can wait for the record to be automatically unlocked by either the other user or the database system itself, though this process may take an hour or more, or they can contact their security administrator to manually unlock the object by ending the holding session that is locking the record. The document is designed for end users who need to troubleshoot access issues when attempting to edit records in the system. It references related error messages and articles including invalid username/password errors, query retrieval failures, email registration validation issues, and instructions for unlocking locked records from the PeopleXD module back office interface. This documentation helps users understand the cause of the lock and provides actionable steps to regain access to the records they need to work with.

sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for users encountering an 'An unknown error has occurred' message when attempting to view the contracts tab on an employee record within the Access Group system. The document outlines two primary resolution steps: first, users should re-assign the employee's personnel access, and second, they should relink the portal account to the employee's personnel number. The guide includes a helpful tip recommending that even when personnel access settings appear to be configured correctly, users should disable and then re-enable the Active toggles associated with the user account to ensure the access permissions are properly reapplied to the system. This document is primarily used by system administrators, HR personnel, or support staff who manage employee records and user access within the Access Group platform and need to resolve contract visibility issues. The document also references related troubleshooting articles addressing similar errors, including the generic 'An unknown error has occurred' on the contracts screen and the 'Query caused no records to be retrieved' error, indicating that this is part of a broader support knowledge base for contract-related system issues.

t: Error - 'Sorry But Page Not Found' when logging into portal
s:

ss: When you encounter a "Sorry But Page Not Found" error while logging into CorePortal, this guide walks you through systematic troubleshooting steps and identifies five potential causes, including locked CorePortal accounts, LDAP configuration issues, incorrect post-login page settings, incomplete self-registration, or misaligned onboarding processes. Open this document if you're experiencing login failures that result in error pages rather than successful portal access. The guide provides specific resolutions for each cause, such as unlocking accounts through Core Back-Office or resending self-registration emails, and helps you determine whether the issue affects a single user or multiple users across your Live or UAT environments.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for users encountering a "Sorry But Page Not Found" error when logging into the Portal, and is designed to help both end users and IT support staff systematically diagnose and resolve the issue. The document begins with initial diagnostic steps, including contacting the local IT team to check for network problems, determining whether the error affects the Live and/or UAT environments, and identifying whether the issue is isolated to a single user or widespread across multiple users. For single-user issues, the document recommends having the affected user log off, clear their cache and browser history, and log back in. The guide outlines five potential causes of this error: a locked CorePortal account, changes to LDAP Core User configuration, an incorrect value assigned to the CP_POST_LOGIN_PAGE setting, an employee who has not completed the self-registration process, or employees being directed to an Onboarding Page when onboarding processes are not in use. Corresponding resolutions are provided for each cause, including a Super-User procedure to unlock accounts through the Core Back-Office by navigating to CoreSecurity, Tools, User Management, entering CorePortal in the user field, and clicking Unlock. Additional resolutions address LDAP Core User configuration verification, resending self-registration emails when necessary, and raising new support cases for issues requiring further investigation. The document references related error articles covering similar portal access issues with different error messages.

ss: The PeopleXD back office login fails with an ORA-12154 error when the system cannot resolve your database connection identifier. sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving the 'ORA-12154: TNS could not resolve the connect identifier specified' error that occurs when attempting to log in to the PeopleXD back office system. The document identifies five primary causes of this login failure: an incorrectly specified URL, an incorrect database identifier, the URL not being present on the user's trusted site list after a PC or browser update, the URL not being whitelisted by the customer's IT department, and special characters (@ or /) within the user's password. It serves users who need to access PeopleXD's back office environment for administrative purposes and encounter connectivity or authentication barriers. t: New year essentials
s:

ss: New Year Essentials covers common setup and troubleshooting issues across PeopleXD, Access Evo, Insight reporting, and related HR systems at the start of the calendar year. It addresses four main areas: system access problems (password resets, MFA, locked accounts), employee status changes (leavers, rehires, contract endings), contract and date management (start/end date corrections, amendments), and reporting accuracy (missing data in Insight reports, audit trails). sl: This document is a compilation of frequently asked questions and practical guidance designed to help users navigate common issues at the start of a new calendar year, organized into five main topic areas with direct links to detailed Help Centre articles. The system access and login issues section addresses password resets, locked accounts, MFA problems, login errors including "Invalid Username / Password combination" messages, self-registration email delivery failures, and management of Access Evo organisation member settings for users accessing PeopleXD through either the Access Button or an Access Evo tab. The employee status queries section covers issues such as employees remaining marked as active after contract termination, inability to remove leaver end dates post-payroll processing, missing rehire options for dormant employees, and the process for removing system access for departing staff. The contract and date management section provides guidance on creating, amending, and correcting contracts, including resolving conflicts between start dates and post effective dates, updating incorrect end dates, handling end date changes after salary runs, deleting contracts or amendments, and managing active posts and employee records. The reporting and data accuracy section supports troubleshooting within the Insight reporting system, including scenarios where reports return no data, specific employees are omitted, diversity or user-defined fields cause data gaps, and procedures for creating audit reports to track employee record changes or access removal via the System User screen. The onboarding and workflow errors section addresses issues such as completed onboarding showing as incomplete, exit interview completion problems for departing employees, HR event notification email failures, and errors related to invalid advanced condition statements.

t: Insight report output is blank
s:
If your Insight report returns blank when you attempt to include PeopleXD Workforce Management (WFM) data, it’s likely due to one of the following reasons:

The employee doesn't have the correct work group access.

The employee isn't set up with Manager Self Service (MSS) access in CoreTime and Peop...
ss: When your Insight report displays blank after trying to include PeopleXD Workforce Management (WFM) data, it's typically caused by missing work group access or Manager Self Service (MSS) access in CoreTime and PeopleXD WFM. Open this document if an employee cannot view WFM data in their Insight reports or if you need to configure user access in the WFM Admin Dashboard. The guide provides step-by-step instructions to add work group access, create new system users with portal access, and grant the necessary security permissions through PeopleXD Security. Use this resource whenever you're troubleshooting blank Insight reports or setting up WFM access for employees in your organisation.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving blank Insight reports when attempting to include PeopleXD Workforce Management (WFM) data. The document identifies two primary causes of the issue: employees lacking correct work group access, or employees not being set up with Manager Self Service (MSS) access in CoreTime and PeopleXD WFM. The resolution process involves three main procedures accessed through the WFM Admin Dashboard. The first procedure, "Add work group access," requires navigating to WFM Configuration > WFM System User Configuration, locating the employee, and adding the respective work groups and departments via the Access Details section. The second procedure, "Add system access," is necessary if the employee doesn't exist in the WFM System User Configuration screen; it involves creating a new user with Portal Access type, selecting the employee from the Person list (who must already exist in PeopleXD), assigning a Company, and then adding work groups and departments to the Access Details tab by moving criteria to the Assigned Departments column. The third procedure, "Grant security access," applies when users lack permission to access the WFM System User Configuration screen itself; this requires navigating to Security > User Management, selecting the employee's account, accessing Menu Profiles, locating WFM_SYSTEM_USERS_CONFIG, and enabling the toggle to grant the necessary permissions. Users must log out and log back in after completing the configuration steps for changes to take effect. This document is designed for system administrators, managers, or support personnel responsible for configuring user access and resolving reporting issues in PeopleXD WFM environments.

t: How to Unshare a Report
s:

ss: Unsharing Insight reports removes specific employees from receiving a shared report. Use this process when you need to stop report distribution to certain team members by moving them from the Selected Recipients list back to Available Recipients. Open this guide if you're managing report access in Insight and need to revoke sharing permissions for one or more employees.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for removing report access from specific employees within the Insight system. The process begins by navigating to Insight and opening the relevant report, then accessing the Share/Schedule option through the Actions button. To unshare a report, users must locate the employee in the Selected Recipients list, check the box next to their name, and use the back arrow positioned between two columns to transfer that employee back to the Available Recipients list. Once the recipient has been moved, users must click Save to finalize and confirm the changes. This document is typically used by report owners or administrators in Insight who need to revoke report sharing permissions from employees who no longer require access. The guide also references related articles covering topics such as blank report output, leave request reports, report ownership transfers, and access error troubleshooting, which may be helpful for users encountering related issues or needing broader report management guidance.

sl: This document explains how to create a report specifically tracking manually entered clock times for employees within an organization's time and attendance system. s:

ss: Timesheet Input allows you to capture and report on comments and narrative notes entered by employees during timesheet submission, such as notes about overtime, shift changes, or manual entries. To access this information, use the 'Person Calculated Hours' folder in reporting and select the 'Narrative' column, which will display any comments logged at the time of timesheet entry. Open this document if you need to audit or review additional context and notes attached to employee timesheets, or if you're setting up a report to track what information was documented alongside timesheet submissions.
sl: This document explains how to generate reports on comments and narrative information that employees enter during timesheet submission in the Timesheet Input process. To create this report, users navigate to the 'Person Calculated Hours' folder within the reporting module and select the 'Narrative' column, which will display any comments or narrative text that was entered at the time of timesheet submission. An important caveat is that the 'Narrative' field will only be populated if a comment was actually entered during the timesheet input process, meaning empty fields indicate no narrative was provided for that particular timesheet entry. This reporting capability is useful for managers and administrators who need to audit or review the supplementary information employees provide to explain their logged hours. The document also references related functionality for reporting on manually entered clock times, identifying who input or approved hours in Timesheet Input or Maintain Hours screens, and leveraging roster attributes in Workforce Management for enhanced reporting capabilities.

t: Portal: Transfer ownership of a report in Insight

ss: When a report owner leaves your organization or changes roles, you may need to reassign ownership of their Insight reports in Portal to ensure continuity. This guide walks through the process of transferring report ownership, which involves accessing the Admin Area, searching for the report, and selecting a new owner from the employee list. The new owner will gain full permissions to edit, share, and manage the report, while the previous owner's access level adjusts based on existing sharing settings. Use this guide whenever you need to hand over Insight report management responsibilities to a different team member.
sl: This document provides instructions for transferring ownership of Insight reports in Portal, a necessary process when a report owner leaves the business or changes roles to ensure continuity of report management. The guide walks users through a specific menu path: starting from the Portal home screen, navigating to Insight, selecting Admin Area, and then using the search bar to locate the report requiring ownership transfer. Once the target report is found, users access the three dots menu on the right-hand side of the report entry and select the "Manage Owner" option, which opens a pop-up window displaying an employee list from which the new owner can be selected. After choosing the new owner and clicking Save, the ownership transfer is completed, granting the new owner full permissions to edit, share, and manage the report. The document clarifies what occurs following the transfer: the previous owner loses owner-level permissions but may retain access to the report depending on its sharing settings, allowing for controlled access management. This guide is primarily used by Portal administrators or managers responsible for report governance when organizational changes necessitate reassigning report ownership to maintain operational efficiency.

t: Report on clockings
s:
You can report on employee clockings to review attendance, hours worked, and time in/out records from either the Portal or Back Office.

This article explains the different ways you can run clocking reports in Workforce Management. Choose the method that suits your reporting needs.

 

Run the Daily...
ss: Workforce Management (WFM) allows you to generate clocking reports from either the Portal or Back Office to review employee attendance, hours worked, and time in/out records. In the Portal, use the Daily Clocking Hours report to view clockings by department, work group, or individual employee; in Back Office, choose between the Daily Clockings/Hours report (for a single calendar period) or the Daily Attendance report (to track clockings across a date range). Open this document when you need to pull attendance data, verify employee hours, audit time records, or export clocking information to Excel for payroll or compliance purposes.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on reporting employee clockings within Workforce Management to review attendance, hours worked, and time in/out records using either the Portal or Back Office system. For Portal-based reporting, users can run the Daily Clocking Hours report from either the WFM Admin Dashboard or the Workforce Management Dashboard by navigating to Reports, selecting Daily Clocking Hours from the Report Type drop-down menu, and using the Period and Group By fields to specify the time period and grouping method (by department, work group, or individual employee), with optional additional fields available for further refinement before clicking Run Report. Back Office offers two distinct reporting options depending on user needs: the Daily Clockings / Hours report (accessed via CoreTime > Reports > Daily Clockings / Hours) for reporting on specific calendar periods with an optional Clockings Only checkbox to exclude hours data, and the Daily Attendance report (accessed via CoreTime > Reports > Daily Attendance) which allows reporting across date ranges but displays only First In and Last Out clockings for each day. Both Portal and Back Office reports can be printed or exported to Excel, though users may encounter a file format mismatch message when exporting to Excel, which requires clicking Yes to proceed. This document serves HR professionals, managers, and Workforce Management administrators who need to track employee attendance patterns, verify hours worked, investigate clocking discrepancies, and generate attendance reports for compliance or payroll purposes. The related articles referenced suggest this document complements troubleshooting guides for issues such as clocking method identification, balance detail reporting, hours calculation problems, and missed clocking scenarios.

Open the Insights tool

Add columns to the report

Click ADD, then select the relevant columns. Below are the recommended fields from the...
ss: Use the Insights tool in the Person Calculated Hours (Time) view to create a custom report tracking who input, approved, and signed off hours in your timesheet system. This is useful when you need to audit timesheet actions, verify approval workflows, or investigate the history of specific employees' hour entries and sign-offs. Build your report by selecting relevant columns like Username, Signed Off By, Approved By, and their corresponding dates, then apply filters by employee or date range to narrow down the data you need. Open this document when you're conducting timesheet audits, troubleshooting approval issues, or need to demonstrate compliance with your organization's hour entry and sign-off procedures.
sl: This document provides comprehensive instructions for creating audit reports within the Insights tool to track timesheet activity across input, approval, and sign-off stages. The process begins in the Insights section of the dashboard menu, where users create a new Table-type report and then populate it with relevant columns from the Person Calculated Hours (Time) view, including fields such as Username (who input hours), Signed Off By, Approved By, and their corresponding dates, along with status indicators showing whether hours were signed off or approved. The document specifies key data fields available for reporting, including Person Reference for employee identification, Calculated Date for when hours were saved, Calculated Hours for totals entered, and Date Input for when the information was originally submitted to the system. Users can refine reports using optional filters, such as filtering by specific employee (using Person Reference) or by date range (using Calculated Date), enabling them to view both current and historical timesheet records. The guidance also references the View Person Master (Time) option for adding supplementary columns beyond the standard Person Calculated Hours view when additional data points are required. This document is designed for managers, HR personnel, and timesheet administrators who need to audit, investigate, or verify timesheet processing workflows and accountability within the timekeeping system.

t: Enhanced pay code instance report
s:
The enhanced pay code instance report allows you to analyse absence patterns across multiple pay codes treated as a single absence category. This helps you identify trends and make data-driven decisions regarding absence management policies.

 

Previously, you could report on only one pay code at a...
ss: The enhanced pay code instance report in WFM allows you to analyse absence patterns by grouping multiple related pay codes together as a single absence category, rather than reporting on them individually. Use this report to identify absence trends, apply threshold filters, and make data-driven decisions about absence management policies with significantly less manual effort. Access the report from the WFM Admin Dashboard by selecting your pay codes, setting date ranges and threshold criteria, then running the report to see which employees meet your specified parameters. Open this document when you need to track absence patterns across multiple pay code types, compare absence trends over time, or generate insights to share with your management team.
sl: The Enhanced Pay Code Instance Report is a tool within the WFM Admin Dashboard that enables users to analyse absence patterns by grouping multiple related pay codes together and treating them as a single absence category, which represents a significant improvement over the previous capability of reporting on only one pay code at a time. To generate a report, users access the Reports section from the WFM Admin Dashboard menu, select "Pay Code Instance" from the Report Type dropdown, specify a date range, click the Pay Codes button to select relevant codes for analysis, enter threshold values in the Selection Criteria fields, optionally refine the report using Report Details options, and then click Run Report to display employees meeting the specified criteria. The system allows users to apply advanced filtering based on specific day or instance thresholds, which streamlines the reporting process and significantly reduces the time spent on manual analysis compared to generating separate reports for each pay code. After generating the report, users can access the integrated Insight view called "Pay Code Instances (Time)" to review detailed breakdowns of absences across the selected pay codes and apply additional filters by specific pay codes or date ranges. The document is primarily intended for payroll administrators, HR managers, and absence management professionals who need to identify absence trends, make data-driven decisions about absence policies, and share findings with their management teams. The report results can be exported for further analysis of absence trends over time, making this tool particularly valuable for organisations seeking to understand patterns across multiple related absence types while maintaining a unified analytical framework.

t: Error: "You do not have permission to create historical absences outside of the rollback period" on Portal
s:
To resolve this error, The rollback period can be increased to allow the absence to be recorded.

 

To rollback the period follow the steps below:

From the dashboard menu click WFM Admin Dashboard then click WFM Configuration.

Click Company and Calendar Config then next to the relevant company cl...
ss: This document covers the rollback period settings in the WFM Admin Dashboard, which controls how far back in time absences can be recorded in the Portal. When you encounter a "You do not have permission to create historical absences outside of the rollback period" error, you'll need to increase the rollback weeks for your company to allow past absences to be entered. Open this guide if managers or employees are unable to record absences for dates beyond the current rollback window and you need to adjust the WFM Configuration settings. The fix involves updating the "Rollback Weeks For Data Entry" parameter for either managers or employees in your company's calendar configuration.
sl: This document provides a solution for resolving the error message "You do not have permission to create historical absences outside of the rollback period" that occurs when users attempt to record absences in the system. The core issue is that the rollback period—which defines the time window during which historical absences can be entered—is too restrictive, preventing absence creation beyond its current boundaries. To fix this problem, administrators must access the WFM Admin Dashboard from the dashboard menu, then navigate to WFM Configuration to adjust the relevant settings. The actual configuration change is made by selecting Company and Calendar Config, locating the appropriate company via the three-dot menu, and clicking View/Edit to access the Summary tab. Within the Summary tab, administrators update the "Rollback Weeks For Data Entry" field, which can be configured separately for managers (MGR) or employees (EMP) depending on user role permissions. After adjusting the rollback weeks to allow a wider timeframe for historical absence entry, the changes must be saved to take effect. This document is typically used by WFM (Workforce Management) administrators or HR personnel who manage absence recording permissions and need to extend the period during which staff can retrospectively log absences in the Portal system.

t: Configure a return to work interview template
s:
You can use Return to Work Interview (RTWI) templates to standardise questionnaires and ensure consistent return to work conversations across your organisation, while giving you the flexibility to tailor templates to different absence types and workflows.

 

To set up and manage an RTWI template.

...
ss: Return to Work Interview (RTWI) templates in WFM Admin Dashboard let you standardise and customise absence questionnaires across your organisation, with the flexibility to tailor them by absence type and workflow. You can build structured templates by creating sections, adding configured questions (setting whether they're mandatory), and assigning them to specific pay codes. Use PeopleXD Insight reporting views to track RTWI completion and access interview responses across your workforce. Open this document when you need to create new RTWI templates, configure questionnaire sections and questions, or set up Insight reporting to monitor return to work conversations.
sl: This document provides comprehensive instructions for setting up and managing Return to Work Interview (RTWI) templates within the Access Group workforce management system, enabling organisations to standardise return to work conversations while maintaining flexibility across different absence types and workflows. Users access the RTWI configuration through the WFM Admin Dashboard by selecting WFM Configuration and navigating to Return to Work Interview, where they can create templates by entering a code and template name, assigning relevant pay codes, and toggling on required settings. The questionnaire structure is built using sections, created through the three-dot menu by selecting Add/Edit Section and specifying section headings and types, which can then be repeated to create multiple sections. Questions are added to each section via the Add/Edit Question option, where users enter question text and descriptions, select question types, and configure additional settings through the Configure menu—with configuration options varying based on the selected question type. The document explains how to enable insight reporting through PeopleXD Insight, which offers three reporting views: Rtwi Access (Time) to display a log of form viewers, Rtwi Answers (Time) to hold questions and responses for each template, and Person Absence Detail (Time) for general absence reporting that now includes RTWI data fields. To use the Rtwi Access (Time) view, users must enable the Record Return To Work Interview Viewing toggle in WFM Configuration's General Settings, while access to the Rtwi Answers (Time) view requires enabling a menu option on the relevant menu profile, with the WFM_RTWI_ADMIN profile already including this option by default. HR administrators and workforce management teams typically use this document to configure standardised return to work processes within their organisation's CorePortal system.

t: Assign managers access to a company for leave requests
s:
To assign managers access to a company for leave requests, follow the steps below in back office.

Click CoreTime then click System Params.

Click System Users.

From the Access drop-down down menu, select the Organisational Roles option.

In the Org Role field, enter the org role used for leave req...
ss: Manager access to leave requests in CoreTime is configured through the back office System Users section using Organisational Roles. This document walks you through assigning the correct org role (such as MGRESS) and linking it to a company so managers can view and process employee leave requests. Open this guide when you need to set up or troubleshoot manager permissions for leave request approvals, or when managers are unable to see pending leave requests on the portal.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for granting managers access to company leave requests within a back office system. The process begins by navigating to CoreTime and accessing System Params, followed by clicking System Users to reach the configuration area. Users must then access the Access drop-down menu and select the Organisational Roles option, which allows them to specify which organizational role should have leave request access by entering a value such as MGRESS in the Org Role field. After identifying the appropriate organizational role, the next step involves assigning the company to that organizational role through the interface. Once the configuration is complete, users must save the changes by clicking the save icon to apply the access permissions. This document is primarily intended for system administrators or back office personnel who need to configure manager access levels for processing employee leave requests, and it helps resolve scenarios where managers cannot view, receive notifications about, or approve leave requests in the system.

t: Start and End Times on Leave & Absence Screens
s:
Having employees accurately record their start and end times on part day leave enables managers to efficiently plan for periods of unavailability.
​
The Start & End Times on Leave & Absences Screens section within General Settings allows you to configure the options to display the Start/End Times on...
ss: Configure start and end times on leave and absence entry screens in WFM's General Settings to require employees and managers to specify exact times for part-day absences. This feature helps managers plan for periods of unavailability by capturing precise scheduling details beyond just full-day leave records. Open this document when you need to enable the Display Start & End Times toggle, select options for full and part days, configure the required Web Services menu options, or set up additional Team Scheduler parameters. The configured start and end times will then display across employee calendars, absence summaries, leave approval screens, and Team Scheduler throughout the system.
sl: This document explains how to configure and enable start and end time fields on leave and absence entry screens within an Access Group workforce management system, allowing employees and managers to accurately record partial day leave periods for better resource planning. The configuration process takes place in the WFM Admin Dashboard under WFM Configuration, specifically within the General Settings tile where administrators locate the Start & End Times on Leave & Absence Screens section and toggle on the Display Start & End Times parameter, then select options for how times should be captured on full days, part days, and whether they should be used to calculate duration. Two specific Web Services menu options must be enabled on the relevant Menu Profile to support this functionality: Get absences startendtimes (WS_LEAVE_MENU.GET_ABSENCES_STARTENDTIMES) and Get settings global (WS_ROSTER_MENU.GET_SETTINGS_GLOBAL). For Team Scheduler users, additional configuration is required by setting the Coreportal Parameter sch_show_from_to to "Yes" to enable the display of start and end times. When enabled, start and end times appear across multiple screens and interfaces including Employee and Team Calendar views, Absence & Leave Summary Screens, Leave Approval screens, Team Scheduler tooltips, the Employee Calendar Widget on the Portal, My Requests Widgets, Leave Request History in Person Maintenance, and several work-in-progress features like the Employee Work Schedule Widget and Bulk Leave Approval. This document is intended for system administrators and workforce managers who need to configure the system to enforce time tracking for partial day absences and for employees and managers who will use the leave and absence entry screens once the feature is enabled.

t: A leave type doesn't appear in the Absence drop-down
s:
If an absence type is missing from the Leave Type drop-down when recording an absence, it’s likely that the pay code isn’t assigned to the employee’s pay code group. To resolve this, follow the steps in each section below in order.

 

Mark the pay code as an absence

From the dashboard menu, Click ...
ss: When an absence type is missing from the Leave Type drop-down in WFM, it's usually because the pay code isn't assigned to the employee's pay code group. This document walks you through configuring pay codes as absence types, adding them to pay code groups, and verifying the employee has the correct access at the employee, system user, and work group levels. You'll also learn how to handle HR-only pay codes and grant necessary permissions in both the Portal and CoreTime Back Office. Open this if staff can't see specific leave types when recording absences in your WFM system.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive troubleshooting guide for resolving the issue when an absence type fails to appear in the Leave Type drop-down menu during absence recording in a workforce management system. The document walks through five sequential resolution processes, beginning with marking the pay code as an absence within WFM Admin Dashboard by navigating to WFM Configuration > Pay Codes, selecting the relevant pay code, and enabling the Absence indicator checkbox. It then explains how to add the pay code to a pay code group through WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Configuration > Pay Code Groups, followed by a three-part verification process to confirm the employee has correct pay code group assignments at the Employee Level (WFM Person Maintenance), System User Level (WFM System Users Configuration under Access Privileges), and Work Group Level (WFM Configuration > Work Group). The document addresses the specific scenario where a pay code may be marked as "HR Only," restricting access to only those system users with the HR User privilege, and provides detailed steps for granting HR User access on both the Portal and Back Office (CoreTime) systems. Finally, it covers how to enable WFM System Users Configuration access through the Security menu and User Management section for users who cannot see the necessary configuration screens. This guide is designed for WFM administrators, HR personnel, and system configuration staff who need to diagnose and resolve pay code visibility issues affecting employee absence recording functionality.

t: Managers not receiving email notifications in MSS when an employee logs a leave request
s:
This issue usually occurs because there is no leave request process code attached to the relevant pay code as, without the process code, no notifications will appear in the manager's dashboard, or the manager is not set up with Manager Role Access for the employee's Work Group on Core Personnel.
​
T...
ss: Managers not receiving email notifications when employees log leave requests in CoreTime or WFM typically occurs because no leave request process code is attached to the relevant pay code, or the manager lacks Manager Role Access for the employee's Work Group in Core Personnel. This document walks you through configuring leave request process codes in both Back Office (CoreTime) and Portal (WFM Dashboard), and verifying manager role setup in Core Personnel or People Management. You should open this guide if managers are missing notifications about new leave requests in their dashboard, or if you need to troubleshoot why leave request emails aren't being generated when employees submit time off.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving a specific issue where managers fail to receive email notifications when employees submit leave requests in the MSS (Manager Self-Service) system. The core problem is identified as one of three potential causes: a missing leave request process code attached to the relevant pay code, the manager lacking Manager Role Access for the employee's Work Group in Core Personnel, or an empty work email address field on the employee's personnel profile. To resolve the first issue, users must navigate to either CoreTime (Back Office) or WFM Dashboard (Portal), access the Pay Codes section, and configure the Leave Request Process Code and Leave Request Cancel Process Code dropdown fields with appropriate process codes such as LR100 or CA001. The document then instructs users to verify the fix by submitting a test leave request and checking the email generation status in Core Personnel's View Email Queue utility. For the second potential cause, managers must be set up with Manager Role Access through either the Maintain Organisational Roles function in Core Personnel (Back Office) or the People Management section (Portal), querying the employee's Work Group to confirm proper access configuration. Finally, if the manager's email address field is empty on the employee's personnel profile, users should navigate to People Management, locate the employee's Contact Information section, and populate the Work Email Address field before saving changes. This document is typically used by system administrators, HR personnel, or support staff who manage MSS configurations and troubleshoot notification issues affecting the leave request workflow.

t: Leavers in CorePersonnel still active in CoreTime
s:
There are a few reasons this could be happening. To resolve this, check each of the following in order.

Employee hasn't been ended in Personnel

The calendar used by the employee has yet to be advanced passed their end date

The LE (Leaver) code has been deleted from 'Employee Status' in CorePerson...
ss: When an employee marked as a leaver in CorePersonnel still appears active in CoreTime, this is usually because the employee hasn't been properly ended in Personnel, the calendar hasn't been advanced past their end date, or the Leaver (LE) status code is missing from Employee Status. This document walks through five troubleshooting steps to identify which scenario applies and how to resolve it, including ending the employee in Personnel, advancing the calendar period, or recreating the Employee Status code. Open this article if leavers are continuing to show as active in your CoreTime system or timesheets when they should have been removed.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving the issue where employees marked as leavers in CorePersonnel remain active in the CoreTime system. The document outlines five common root causes: the employee has not been ended in Personnel, the calendar used by the employee has not been advanced past their end date, the LE (Leaver) code has been deleted from the Employee Status field in CorePersonnel, an automatic period advancement through an Overnight Job is in progress, or the CoreTime calendar itself has not been advanced since the employee was marked as a leaver. Resolution steps include ending the employee directly in Personnel (where status updates when the period advances next), waiting for the calendar period to advance automatically past the employee's end date, or manually recreating the LE Employee Status code via CorePersonnel > Reference > Reference D-J > Employee Status. For User Defined Calendars assigned to work groups (identifiable by checking the Pay Frequency parameter in System Params, Work Groups), administrators can manually advance the period through Portal > WFM Admin Dashboard > Advance Period > Monthly User Defined Calendar > Advanced Period, though this should not be done if the calendar generates timesheets. The document notes this issue was resolved in specific software versions (20.0.23+, 21.0.20+, 22.0.5+), and users experiencing ongoing issues should raise a support case if they do not wish to wait for automatic calendar advancement.

t: Portal: Check pro-rata calculation for annual leave balance
s:
In order to check pro-rata calculation for annual leave balance follow the below steps:

Navigate to People Management, then select Employee.

Click View next to the relevant employee’s name.

Go to the Balances tab, then click the three-dot menu next to the desired balance.

Select Balance Adjustme...
ss: The PeopleXD Portal's pro-rata calculation feature lets you verify how an employee's annual leave balance has been adjusted based on their full-time equivalent (FTE) status. Use this process when you need to review the Balance Adjustment details for a specific employee and cross-check their FTE against the pro-rata calculations recorded in CoreTime Back Office. Navigate to People Management > Employee, view the employee record, then access the Balances tab to see the pro-rata calculation applied. This is essential when troubleshooting leave balance discrepancies, especially for new starters or employees whose FTE has changed mid-year.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for verifying how an employee's annual leave balance has been calculated on a pro-rata basis within the Access Group's People Management system. Users navigate to People Management and select Employee, then click View next to the relevant employee's name to access their record. The Balances tab contains a three-dot menu next to the desired balance, where selecting Balance Adjustment reveals the Pro-Rata Calculation that reflects the employee's Full-Time Equivalent (FTE) status. To further verify the calculation, users can navigate to the Employee section, select Contract, and view the latest contract under the Amendment section. The document emphasizes the importance of cross-verifying the FTE used in the pro-rata calculation with the information recorded on the 'Record Absence Details' screen within CoreTime (Back Office) to ensure accuracy. This process is typically used by HR administrators and payroll specialists who need to validate that annual leave entitlements have been correctly adjusted for employees with part-time contracts, mid-year starters, or those who have experienced FTE changes during their employment. The related articles reference common scenarios where pro-rata calculations may require review, including incorrect entitlements and leave balance reduction issues.

t: Extend non-cycle shifts
s:
You must extend the system calendar before you can extend non-cycle shifts. If you don't update the calendar, employees can't submit leave requests, managers can't record absences, and timesheet calculations become incorrect.

 

To extend the system calendar and ensure employees can submit leave re...
ss: Extending non-cycle shifts in WFM ensures your system can properly handle leave requests, absence recording, and timesheet calculations for shifts that don't follow standard cycles. You can complete this task through two paths: the WFM Year End Tasks tab or the WFM Admin Dashboard's WFM Configuration section, both using the same Generate Period workflow. Open this document when you're performing year-end maintenance or need to update shift patterns beyond the current period. Note that you must extend the system calendar first before extending any non-cycle shifts.
sl: This document provides instructions for extending non-cycle shifts within a workforce management system, a prerequisite task that must be completed after extending the system calendar to prevent errors in leave requests, absence recording, and timesheet calculations. The document explains that non-cycle shifts can be extended through two different locations: the WFM Year End Tasks screen or the WFM Admin Dashboard, both accessible from the WFM Admin Dashboard interface. For the WFM Year End Tasks method, users navigate to the WFM Year End Tasks tab, locate the Extend Non-Cycle Shifts task via the three-dot menu, search for the relevant Shift Code, and then access the Shift Patterns section to use the Generate Period function. The WFM Admin Dashboard method follows a similar process but requires users to navigate to the WFM Configuration tab and select Non-Cycle Shifts instead. Both methods require selecting a From Period and To Period from drop-down lists, specifying the destination periods in the Copy periods into section, and then saving the changes. Users must repeat the process for each non-cycle shift that requires extension, making this a task typically performed by WFM administrators during year-end calendar management activities. The document also references related articles for extending the system calendar, setting up cycle shift types, and extending standard shift types for users who need additional guidance on related configuration tasks.

t: Cannot approve leave in Bulk
s:
If you're unable to approve leave in bulk, it may be due to a system parameter that needs enabling in People XD Workforce Management.

 

To enable bulk leave approvals, follow the steps below.

Click Admin Dashboard and then click Site Manager.

Click Admin Settings

Search for cp_lv_req_process_ro...
ss: Bulk leave approvals in People XD Workforce Management require a specific system parameter to be enabled. If you're unable to approve multiple leave requests at once, you'll need to access the Admin Dashboard, navigate to Admin Settings, and enable the cp_lv_req_process_role parameter. Open this document when you encounter issues approving leave in bulk or need to set up bulk approval functionality for your team.
sl: This document addresses the issue of being unable to approve leave requests in bulk within the People XD Workforce Management system and provides the specific configuration steps needed to enable this functionality. The problem typically stems from a disabled system parameter that requires activation through the administrative interface. To resolve this issue, users must navigate to the Admin Dashboard, select Site Manager, then access Admin Settings where they search for the parameter cp_lv_req_process_role and set its value to Y. Once this configuration change is completed, the bulk leave approval feature becomes fully functional within the system. This document is primarily intended for system administrators or users with access to administrative settings who need to troubleshoot why managers or approvers cannot process multiple leave requests simultaneously. The document also references related help articles covering other common leave approval errors and the mechanics of how the bulk leave approval screen operates within PeopleXD, suggesting it is part of a broader support section addressing leave management workflows.

t: Remove rounding from taken leave
s:
How Rounding Works in Leave Balances

By default, rounding is applied to both taken and booked leave. The system rounds up to the nearest half hour, which can sometimes result in employees losing a small portion of their leave.

 

Example:

If an employee on an 8.5-hour day books half a day’s leave...
ss: Rounding in WFM leave balances is applied by default to both taken and booked leave, rounding up to the nearest half hour and potentially causing employees to lose small portions of their leave entitlement. You can control where rounding is applied by accessing the Balance Configuration screen in the WFM Admin Dashboard and adjusting the Apply Rounding To settings, with options to apply rounding to all balances, entitlement only, or taken leave only. Open this document if you need to modify how leave rounding works in your system to prevent unintended leave balance deductions or to align rounding with your organization's leave policies.
sl: This document explains how the Access Group's Workforce Management (WFM) system applies rounding to leave balances and provides instructions for adjusting where rounding is applied. By default, the system rounds both taken and booked leave up to the nearest half hour, which can disadvantage employees by reducing their available leave—for example, an employee on an 8.5-hour day booking half a day's leave would lose an additional 15 minutes due to rounding. To modify rounding settings, administrators navigate to the WFM Admin Dashboard, select WFM Configuration, and then access the Balance Configuration tile to locate and edit the relevant Balance record. Within the Balance Configuration screen's Summary tab, users locate the Rounding Rules section and use the Apply Rounding To dropdown field to specify where rounding should be performed. The dropdown offers three options: "All" (which applies rounding to both Taken and Entitlement balances and is the default setting), "Entitlement" (which applies rounding only to Reserved, Floating, Accrued, and Carried balances), and "Taken" (which applies rounding only to taken and booked leave). This document is intended for WFM administrators and HR professionals who need to configure leave balance settings to address fairness concerns around automatic rounding that may unfavorably impact employee leave entitlements.

t: Remove the display of cancelled Annual leave from Manager's team calendars
s:
Why Cancelled Leave Still Shows in the Team Calendar

It is not possible to remove notifications of cancelled annual leave from a manager’s team calendar.

 

Why?

The section being referred to in Team Scheduler is called Leave Request. This view will display all leave requests, regardless of their...
ss: The Team Scheduler's Leave Request view displays all leave requests regardless of status—including submitted, approved, rejected, and cancelled entries—and this filter cannot be customized to hide specific statuses. If cancelled annual leave notifications are cluttering your team calendar and you want to remove them, you'll need to disable the entire absence display feature rather than filter individual statuses. Open this document when you're managing your team's calendar in Team Scheduler and need to understand why cancelled leave still appears or want to turn off absence visibility completely using the SCH_SHOW_ABSENCES parameter.
sl: This document explains why cancelled annual leave entries continue to appear in managers' team calendars within the Team Scheduler module and provides guidance on addressing this visibility issue. The document clarifies that the Leave Request section in Team Scheduler displays all leave requests regardless of their status, including Submitted, Approved, Rejected, and Cancelled entries, as the Leave Request filter cannot be customized to exclude specific statuses and will always show the complete history of leave actions. While it is not possible to selectively remove notifications of cancelled annual leave from the team calendar view, the document offers an alternative solution for managers who prefer not to see any absence information at all. To implement this workaround, users can update the system parameter SCH_SHOW_ABSENCES and set it to 'N', which will disable the entire absence display feature in Team Scheduler. This parameter change will remove all absences from appearing in the Team Scheduler view, including cancelled, approved, and pending leave requests, providing a complete hide rather than selective filtering. The document is intended for managers and system administrators who use Team Scheduler to manage team calendars and need to understand the limitations of absence visibility customization, along with the available configuration options to control how leave information is displayed.

t: Book more than one absence type for the same day
s:
The system can be set up to allow employees to book more than one leave type on the same day (for example, Annual Leave and Medical Leave).

 

How to Enable This Setting

Go to CoreTime and select System Params.

Click on Ref A to C, then select Control Params.

Click on Advanced Options.

Tick the...
ss: CoreTime allows employees to request multiple leave types on the same day by enabling the overlapping leave requests feature. Use this guide if you need to set up your system to permit employees to book combinations like Annual Leave and Medical Leave simultaneously. Access System Params > Control Params > Advanced Options in CoreTime and toggle the ALLOW OVERLAPPING LEAVE REQUESTS checkbox to activate this setting. Test this configuration in your UAT environment before deploying to your Live system.
sl: This document provides guidance on enabling the functionality within CoreTime that allows employees to simultaneously book multiple absence or leave types on the same calendar day, such as combining Annual Leave with Medical Leave on a single date. ss: The WFM Admin Bulk Leave Approval screen uses an Admin Security Type setting that controls which filters and buttons appear for leave approval tasks. Open this document if you need to troubleshoot missing filters on the Bulk Leave Approval, Approve Hours, Employee Calendar, or Balance Re-Calculation screens, or if you need instructions on changing your Admin Security Type setting to regain access to these features.
sl: This document explains why the Department and Work Group filters along with the Team Calendar button may not display on the WFM Admin Bulk Leave Approval screen, and provides step-by-step instructions to resolve the issue. The visibility of these interface elements is controlled by the Admin Security Type setting, which is found by navigating to WFM Admin > Config > General Settings. The document describes three distinct Admin Security Types: Structure Code Access (which hides the filters and Team Calendar button and restricts access to Company/Division level), System User Access (which displays the filters and Team Calendar button based on Work Groups and Departments assigned to the user's WFM System User account), and Team Area Access (used only for clients with rostered Team Areas). If the Work Group and Department filters are missing, the user is likely operating under Structure Code Access and must change the Admin Security Type to System User Access to restore visibility of these elements. To make this change, users with appropriate system permissions must navigate to WFM Admin > Config > General Settings, modify the Admin Security Type setting, and save the changes. After changing the setting, users should verify their Work Group and Department access by going to WFM Admin > Config > WFM System Users and selecting their username to confirm assigned groups and departments. The document notes that this setting affects employee visibility across multiple screens including Approve Hours and Balance Re-Calculation, though the Sign Off Hours screen displays all employees regardless of the Admin Security Type setting. Once changes are saved and the user has logged out and back in, the Work Group and Department filters and Team Calendar button should appear on the Bulk Leave Approval screen.

s:

ss: A break in absence occurs when absence records don't calculate or transfer to payroll in the correct sequence, typically due to pay code calculation order issues, overlapping absence entries, or misconfigured system calendar periods. If an absence with an incorrect start date has already been sent to payroll after the period closes, you'll need to manually correct it through the Payroll Dashboard by accessing the employee's Absence Summary tab and editing the absence record directly. Use this guide when you discover gaps or sequencing problems in employee absences that have already reached PeopleXD Payroll, or when you need to fix absence start dates after payroll closure.
sl: This document explains how to identify and resolve breaks in employee absences that have been transferred to payroll, particularly when payroll periods are already closed. A break in absence occurs when pay codes fail to calculate on their intended dates in the timesheet (such as 14-AUG calculating before 13-AUG), when overlapping absences are entered on dates with existing absences, or when system calendar open periods are configured too far back in time. The document provides a step-by-step process for manually fixing absences with incorrect start dates after payroll closure, beginning with navigating to Payroll Dashboard > Employee, searching for and viewing the employee record, and then accessing the Absence Summary tab. Users must locate the problematic absence, click the 3-dot menu to select Occupational Detail, and then click the 3-dot menu again to select Edit Absence, where they can update the Absence Start Date field before saving changes. The document includes an important warning that users should not update absences in the current payroll period using this method; instead, after updating past absences, they must re-run Payroll Validation for the employee to update absences in the current payroll period. This guidance is intended for payroll administrators and HR personnel who manage employee absences and must correct data synchronization issues between absence management systems and the PeopleXD Payroll system.

s:

ss: Absence Triggers in your absence management system can be configured using either Days or Occurrences in the Sum Rule, each tracking absences differently. Days measures total time off (counting full days as 1 and half days as 0.5), while Occurrences counts the number of absence events regardless of their length. Use Days if you need to monitor cumulative time away, or use Occurrences if you want to track how many separate absence instances an employee has taken. Open this document when setting up or troubleshooting absence triggers to ensure you're using the right calculation method for your organization's policies.
sl: This document explains the critical distinction between Days and Occurrences when configuring Absence Triggers in the Sum Rule calculation within an absence management system. The document clarifies how the system counts different types of absences, establishing that full day absences equal 1 day and 1 occurrence, while half day absences equal 0.5 days but still count as 1 occurrence. The guide provides a practical example demonstrating the calculation method: an employee with 3 full day absences and 2 half day absences would be counted as 4 total days (3 + 2 × 0.5) but 5 total occurrences (3 + 2). Users configuring absence triggers should choose Days if they want to track total time off in a fractional format, or Occurrences if they want to count the number of absence events regardless of whether they are full or half days. This distinction is essential because different organizational policies and reporting requirements may call for measuring absence differently—some may prioritize the actual hours or days absent, while others prioritize the frequency of absence events. The document also references related error messages including "[Pay Code] must be entered in XXX days segments" and "Leave must be entered in full days segments when adding absence," which users may encounter when their configuration settings do not match their data entry method.

sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses the issue of managers being unable to view leave requests on their portal and outlines four distinct causes with corresponding resolutions. The first cause involves managers lacking the correct Organisational Role assignment in CorePersonnel, which requires navigating to Core Personnel > References > Maintain Organisational Roles, selecting the Work Group from the Organisation Group dropdown, and adding the ORG role with the manager's employee number and personnel reference number. The second cause occurs when a username exists in the system but is not linked to an employee in CoreTime, requiring staff to access CoreSecurity > Tools > User Management (or CoreTime) > System Params > System Users to establish this link. The third scenario addresses situations where the user exists and is linked to an employee but lacks the necessary Work Group or Department access, which can be remedied by selecting CoreTime > System Users, entering the username, adding the appropriate work group or department, and saving the changes. The final cause is when a manager has no corresponding CoreSecurity username at all, requiring creation of a new user account through CoreSecurity > Tools > User Management by entering a username, assigning a password, and saving. sl: This document addresses a specific bug in CoreTime where company holidays are incorrectly deducting twice from an employee's balance, and explains that this occurs when the Company Holiday Scheme uses the same Pay Code that is configured as the Affecting Code for the balance itself. t: Overlapping Absence
s:
What is Overlapping Absence?

Overlapping Absence occurs when an open-ended absence (such as long-term sickness) overlaps with planned leave (like annual leave or parental leave).

Without proper configuration, this can cause payroll calculation issues, potentially leading to overpayments or incorre...
ss: Overlapping Absence occurs when open-ended absences like long-term sickness overlap with planned leave, which can cause payroll calculation errors and overpayments if not properly configured. Enable the Overlapping Leave and Absence parameters in WFM Admin Dashboard to automatically detect overlaps, improve payroll accuracy, and have the system close open-ended absences when upcoming leave is booked. This feature reduces manual monitoring and admin workload by sending automatic notifications and managing absence closure without requiring staff intervention. Open this document when you need to configure overlap detection settings or troubleshoot payroll issues related to conflicting absence types.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre explains the concept of overlapping absence and provides configuration instructions for managing it within a workforce management system. Overlapping absence occurs when an open-ended absence such as long-term sickness overlaps with planned leave like annual leave or parental leave, and without proper configuration can cause payroll calculation errors, overpayments, or incorrect processing of occupational absence. The document outlines the benefits of enabling the Overlapping Leave and Absence parameters, which include automatic notifications when potential overlaps are detected, improved payroll accuracy for sickness and occupational absence, system-managed closure of open-ended absences when upcoming leave is booked, and reduced administrative workload. To enable this feature, users navigate from the WFM Admin Dashboard to WFM Configuration, locate and click the General Settings tile, scroll to the Overlapping Leave and Absence Parameters section, and switch on the Enable Overlapping Leave and Absence toggle, which automatically disables existing advance overlapping leave parameters with an expected warning message. The configuration also requires setting the Overlapping Absence Restriction period, which determines how far ahead the system checks for planned leave and defaults to 7 days but can be customized based on organizational needs. The process concludes by clicking Save to apply the configuration changes. This document is primarily used by workforce management administrators and payroll teams who need to configure absence management settings to prevent payroll processing errors and streamline leave administration.

t: Managing Overlapping Absences When One Is Open-Ended
s:
In PeopleXD, the system allows you to record overlapping absences, but this can cause calculation errors—especially when one of the absences is open-ended.

Best Practice

ss: Managing overlapping absences in PeopleXD requires careful handling when one absence is open-ended, as the system can produce calculation errors, reporting issues, and payroll problems if not managed correctly. This document covers the best practices for recording absences in PeopleXD, specifically addressing scenarios where an employee has an open-ended absence (like long-term sick leave) that overlaps with other scheduled time off. You should open this document if you need to understand how to properly delete future-dated absences, close open-ended absences, and re-add leave after resolving overlaps to maintain accurate absence calculations and entitlements. The guide includes a worked example of an employee on long-term sick leave with conflicting leave dates, plus key rules for preventing system errors in absence and payroll processing.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre explains how to properly manage overlapping absences in PeopleXD when one absence is open-ended, a scenario that can trigger calculation errors within the system. The guide establishes clear best practices: only permit overlapping absences if both have defined end dates, avoid overlapping an open-ended absence with any other absence, and delete any future-dated absences that fall after an open-ended absence begins. The document provides a concrete example in which an employee goes onto long-term sick leave (open-ended) starting 20-OCT-2022, then demonstrates the required actions for different situations—such as deleting a pre-booked leave on 10-DEC-2022, closing the open-ended absence by entering an end date when the employee returns on 01-DEC-2022, and re-adding the future leave only after the open-ended absence has been closed, which can be done by a Manager, HR/Admin, or via Leave Request where applicable. If overlapping open-ended absences are left unresolved, the system may produce incorrect absence calculations, reporting errors, and issues with entitlements and payroll integration. This document is typically used by HR administrators, managers, and payroll professionals in organizations using PeopleXD who need to maintain accurate absence records and prevent downstream errors in absence reporting and payroll processing. The guide emphasizes that keeping records clean by removing future absences before an open-ended absence starts, then re-adding them afterward, ensures data accuracy throughout the system.

ss: Running a future calculation in CoreTime allows you to selectively calculate specific pay codes while excluding others, such as preventing Annual Leave from calculating during the process. This involves configuring Global Parameters and individual pay code settings to enable Future Calculation only for the codes you want to process, then running the Calculate Hours function. Open this document when you need to control which pay codes are included in future calculations, or when certain pay codes are calculating when they shouldn't be. The process requires configuration changes in both System Params and the WFM Admin Dashboard, with settings that must be reversed immediately after the calculation completes.
sl: This document provides instructions for running a future calculation for specific pay codes in order to selectively prevent certain pay codes, such as Annual Leave, from calculating during the future calculation process. The document describes two separate procedures: one for the core system and one for the Portal interface. For the core system, users must first navigate to System Params > Ref D to J > Global Parameters and set the Future Calculation End Date to End Of Period while leaving Calculate All Pay Codes unticked, then access Core Time > System Params > Pay Codes to query the desired pay code and enable the Future Calculation checkbox in the General 4 screen. Users then execute the calculation by navigating to Core Time > Time Mgt > Calculate Hours, after which they must immediately reverse both configuration changes by clearing the Future Calculation End Date field and disabling the Future Calculation checkbox for the affected pay codes. For Portal users, the process involves accessing WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Configuration > Pay Codes, querying the specific pay code (such as 3700 for Annual Leave), enabling Future Calculations in the Input Validation section, and then proceeding to Calculate Hours where they enable Future Calculations again and specify the Start and End dates before clicking Calculate. This document addresses the common issue of preventing unwanted pay codes from calculating during future calculation runs and is intended for payroll and time and attendance administrators who need to control which pay codes are processed during batch calculations.

s:

ss: When a manager in CoreTime cannot select approve or reject options for a leave request, it's typically because they're trying to approve leave outside their permitted timeframe. This restriction is controlled by the MGR: Rollback weeks for Data Entry setting in System Parameters, which limits how far back (or forward) managers can process leave requests. Open this document if you need to adjust a manager's data entry permissions or resolve cases where the approve/reject buttons aren't appearing on the Portal. The fix involves accessing CoreTime's Control Parameters and updating the rollback weeks value to match your organization's requirements.
sl: This document addresses a specific issue in the Portal where managers are unable to approve or reject leave requests because they are attempting to process requests outside their authorized timeframe. The problem stems from the MGR: Rollback weeks for Data Entry configuration setting, which restricts the data entry permissions available to managers based on how many weeks back from the current date they are allowed to access. To resolve this issue, managers or administrators must navigate to CoreTime, then System Params, followed by Reference A-C and Control Parameters, where they select the relevant company and access General Parameters - 4. Within this configuration screen, the MGR: Rollback weeks for Data Entry setting can be adjusted, with the numeric value representing how many weeks back from the real-time calendar the manager is permitted to operate (for example, a value of 2 allows access to requests from two weeks prior). After making the necessary adjustment to accommodate the leave request date, users must click Save to apply the changes. This document is intended for system administrators or managers who need to understand why leave approval functionality is restricted and how to expand those permissions through backend configuration rather than through the Portal interface itself.

ss: Public holidays missing from timesheets or employees unable to book leave on those dates typically indicates a configuration issue in CoreTime. This document covers three common causes: missing company or public holiday dates in the holiday scheme, employees assigned to different holiday schemes via work group override, and inconsistent work patterns across employees. Use this guide when employees report they can't request leave on public holidays or when public holidays aren't showing on their timesheets, and follow the step-by-step instructions to check and configure holiday schemes and work patterns in CoreTime.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving issues where employees cannot request leave on public holidays or public holidays fail to appear on their timesheets, conditions that typically signal configuration problems within the CoreTime system. The document identifies three primary causes: missing company or public holiday dates in the holiday scheme configuration, employees assigned to alternative holiday schemes through work group overrides, and inconsistent work patterns across the workforce that affect public holiday visibility. To resolve missing holiday dates, users must navigate to CoreTime's System Params menu, access Holiday Schemes, select Company Holiday Details, query the relevant scheme, and add any missing company or public holidays before saving. The document also instructs users to check for holiday scheme overrides by accessing the employee's profile through CoreTime's Pers Data section, selecting Person Maintenance, and reviewing the Work Group Override to identify if the employee uses a different holiday scheme that may lack proper public holiday configuration. A third resolution path requires users to examine work patterns through CoreTime's Time Management module by clicking Maintain Hours, searching for the employee, and viewing their Roster to confirm whether they are scheduled to work on public holidays, as scheduling inconsistencies can cause visibility differences. Once these three areas—holiday scheme dates, work group overrides, and work pattern assignments—have been reviewed and corrected, employees should gain the ability to book leave on public holidays and see those holidays properly reflected in their timesheets. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators, HR professionals, and CoreTime system administrators who manage leave requests and timesheet configurations for their organizations.
