ss: When employees see no pay code options or incorrect options in the Annual Leave drop-down list on the WFM portal, it's usually because their Personalised Pay Code Group (PPCG) is either empty or missing the required Annual Leave pay code. Use this document to check and update an employee's Pay Code Group assignment in WFM Admin Dashboard, ensuring the correct Annual Leave pay code is present. Open this if an employee reports that the Annual Leave booking drop-down is blank or doesn't show the pay codes they need.
sl: This document provides guidance for resolving issues where employees see no options or incomplete options in the drop-down list when booking Annual Leave in the system. The problem typically stems from the employee being assigned to a Personalised Pay Code Group (PPCG) that either has no pay codes assigned at all or does not contain the correct pay code for Annual Leave. The document outlines a three-step diagnostic and resolution process, beginning with checking the employee's Pay Code Group assignment by navigating to the WFM Admin Dashboard, selecting WFM Person Maintenance, querying the employee, and reviewing the Personal Groups section. The second step involves reviewing the assigned Pay Code Group itself by going to WFM Admin Dashboard, selecting WFM Configuration, clicking Pay Code Groups, and verifying whether the required Annual Leave pay code is present in the group. The third step provides instructions for updating the Pay Code Group either by adding the missing pay code directly to the group and clicking Save, or by assigning a different Personalised Pay Code Group to the employee in WFM Person Maintenance under Personal Groups. The document emphasizes that if a PPCG is assigned but contains no pay codes, employees will see a completely empty drop-down list when attempting to book Annual Leave on the portal, making it essential to ensure the relevant Annual Leave pay code is always included in the assigned Pay Code Group. This document is typically used by HR administrators or WFM (Workforce Management) system administrators who need to troubleshoot employee access issues related to leave booking functionality.

By following these steps and comparing the FTE values shown in both CoreTime and Core Personnel, users can identify discrepancies and confirm that the pro-rata calculation reflects the employee's actual working arrangement.

After updating these values to eliminate any gaps between rows, users must save their changes and run the Validation function to confirm the configuration is correct. The document emphasizes that gaps between the To Months and From Months values directly prevent sick pay entitlements from generating properly, making this configuration check essential for maintaining accurate leave and pay administration.

ss: Carried forward annual leave has an expiry date set in CoreTime, and any unused days are automatically deducted from an employee's balance after that date passes. You can check the expiry date for carried forward days in Back Office by navigating to CoreTime > System Params > Balances > Calendars and reviewing the Expiry of Carried Forward Days section. The system calculates which days expire based on how many carried forward days were actually used before the expiry date—if an employee takes fewer days than they carried forward, the unused portion expires and is removed from their total balance. Open this document when you need to understand how carried forward leave expiry works, verify an employee's expiry date, or troubleshoot unexpected deductions from leave balances.
sl: This document explains how carried forward annual leave expiry works in the Access Group's Back Office system and provides guidance for checking and understanding when unused leave is deducted from employee balances. The document describes a specific process for locating expiry date information by navigating to CoreTime, selecting System Params, then Balances, and accessing Calendars to review the "Expiry of Carried Forward Days" section using the help symbol. It details how the system calculates expiry by comparing days taken against carried forward days, with no adjustment needed if all carried forward days are used, but unused days expiring after the set expiry date if days taken are insufficient. The document illustrates this calculation with a concrete example showing how 6 carried forward days with only 3 days taken before the expiry date results in 3 days expiring and being deducted from the total balance. A critical operational detail covered is that the system only removes expired days after the system calendar advances beyond the expiry date, meaning expiry actions are not immediate but occur when the calendar moves to the next period. This document serves HR administrators and payroll professionals who configure and manage annual leave entitlements in the Back Office system and need to understand when and how carried forward leave balances are automatically adjusted.

sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre explains how to resolve annual leave request approval issues in Access People XD when an employee's manager or workgroup assignment changes. To resolve these issues, users must verify that the new manager has the correct Manager Role Access configured in two locations: first in Access People XD BackOffice by navigating to CorePersonnel > Reference > Maintain Organisational Roles and querying the employee's Work Group, and second in Access People XD Portal through People Management > Data Centre > People Management > Maintain Organisational Roles. If the new manager lacks Manager Role Access for the relevant workgroup in either system, administrators must assign or set up this role to ensure leave requests route correctly. The document is designed for HR administrators and managers who need to troubleshoot leave approval workflow disruptions when organisational changes occur, and it references related error messages and issues such as access permission errors and email notification failures that may accompany these scenarios.

t: Unexplained absence generating when annual leave is recorded in Maintain Hours
s:

ss: When annual leave is recorded in Maintain Hours using CoreTime or the WFM Admin Dashboard, an unexplained absence may be generated if the Effect Basic setting is not enabled on the pay code. This occurs because without this setting, the system doesn't recognize the annual leave as time worked. You can resolve this issue by enabling the Effect Basic checkbox (in CoreTime's Pay Code General 2 tab) or the Effect Basic toggle (in WFM Configuration's Calculate Settings tab). Open this guide if you're experiencing unexplained absence flags appearing alongside recorded annual leave.
sl: This document explains how to resolve an issue in the Access Group's Maintain Hours system where an unexplained absence is incorrectly generated when annual leave is recorded on a particular day. The guide provides two separate resolution paths depending on whether users are working in Back Office or Portal environments. For Back Office users, the fix involves navigating to CoreTime > System Params > Pay Code, querying the specific pay code, selecting the General 2 tab, and enabling the Effect Basic checkbox before saving. Portal users follow a similar process by accessing the WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Configuration > Pay Codes, searching for the pay code, clicking View/Edit Pay Code, navigating to the Calculate Settings tab, and enabling the Effect Basic toggle. This document is designed for payroll administrators, human resources professionals, and system configurators who manage pay codes and leave settings within the Access Group platform and need to troubleshoot discrepancies between recorded annual leave and system-generated absence records.

ss: CoreTime's balance and pay code parameters control whether employees can book leave beyond their available entitlement or outside valid balance periods. When the "When Entitlement Exceeded" parameter is set to Allow or "Restrict Entry to Valid Balance Period" is set to No Restriction, employees can overbooking leave. Open this document if you need to prevent staff from booking annual leave they haven't accrued or during unauthorised periods by updating these settings in Back Office. You'll find step-by-step instructions for configuring both Balance Parameters and Pay Code settings to stop or warn on invalid leave entries.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre explains how to prevent employees from overbooking leave by correcting misconfigured system settings in the CoreTime module. The guide identifies two root causes of overbooking: the "When Entitlement Exceeded" parameter being set to Allow, and the "Restrict Entry to Valid Balance Period" parameter being set to No Restriction. To resolve this issue, users must navigate to Back Office, access CoreTime, and modify Balance Parameters by locating the "When Entitlement Exceeded" setting and changing it from Allow to Stop, then repeat this change in the Advanced Parameters section on the same screen. Additionally, users must update Pay Code settings by navigating to CoreTime's Pay Codes section, querying the annual leave Pay Code, and locating the "Restrict Entry to Valid Balance Period" parameter within General Parameter 3, which should be changed from No Restriction to either Stop (to completely prevent out-of-period bookings) or Warn (to display a warning while allowing the booking). The document is intended for HR administrators and system managers in organizations using Access Group's CoreTime software who need to configure leave management controls to enforce proper entitlement boundaries. sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre explains how to configure the system to allow employees to book holidays in the following year, which is restricted by default to the current balance year. t: Difference between PH FTE Entitlement and PH FTE Reserved on Balance
s:
Overview

When a Company Holiday Scheme is linked to a balance, the system manages Public Holiday (PH) adjustments through two key figures:

PH FTE Entitlement

PH FTE Reserved

These values ensure accurate public holiday calculations based on employee work patterns and Full-Time Equivalent (FTE) st...
ss: PH FTE Entitlement and PH FTE Reserved are two key figures that manage Public Holiday adjustments in your system when a Company Holiday Scheme is linked to a balance. PH FTE Entitlement represents the total Public Holiday days an employee is entitled to based on their Holiday Scheme and FTE percentage, while PH FTE Reserved shows the days they're rostered to work and have hours deducted from their leave balance. Open this document if you need to understand how the system calculates Public Holiday deductions, troubleshoot why certain Public Holiday dates aren't appearing in reserves, or verify that leave balance adjustments are correct based on employee work patterns and FTE status.
sl: This document explains how the Access Group system manages Public Holiday (PH) adjustments by tracking two interconnected figures—PH FTE Entitlement and PH FTE Reserved—when a Company Holiday Scheme is linked to a balance. PH FTE Entitlement represents the total number of Public Holiday days an employee is entitled to based on their assigned Holiday Scheme and FTE percentage, while PH FTE Reserved captures the number of Public Holiday days the employee is rostered to work and therefore has hours reserved for deduction from their leave balance. The system calculates the actual Public Holiday adjustment using the formula PH FTE Entitlement minus PH FTE Reserved, ensuring that only Public Holidays affecting an employee's actual work schedule are deducted. The calculation is dynamic and personalised, accounting for the employee's FTE percentage (for example, a 100% FTE employee receives 10 days of entitlement while an 80% FTE employee receives 8 days, assuming a 10-holiday scheme) and their rostered work pattern, meaning Public Holidays falling on scheduled rest days are not reserved for deduction. This document helps resolve scenarios where Public Holidays appear to be missing from PH FTE Reserved, typically because the employee was scheduled off on that date, which the system automatically ignores. The guidance applies to users managing leave balances and Public Holiday configurations in the Access Group system who need to understand why certain holidays are or are not being deducted from employee leave records.

t: How to remove (cancel) a leave request
s:
It is best practice not to delete an unprocessed leave request but to cancel it instead. This preserves the history but removes it from manager approval queues.

Employees can cancel their leave requests in PeopleXD only if the requests have not yet been actioned. Unactioned requests are those still...
ss: Cancelling a leave request in PeopleXD removes it from manager approval queues while preserving the request history—a best practice alternative to deleting requests. Employees can only cancel leave requests that haven't been actioned yet (those still awaiting manager or admin approval), while approved or rejected requests cannot be cancelled. Open this document if you need to withdraw a pending leave request you submitted, or if you want to understand why cancellation is preferable to deletion. The process takes just a few clicks from the Employee Dashboard's My Requests widget.
sl: This document provides guidance on canceling leave requests within the PeopleXD system, explaining why cancellation is preferable to deletion and when it can be performed. The document is designed for employees who need to remove unprocessed leave requests from their manager approval queues while maintaining an audit trail of the request history. Employees can only cancel leave requests that have not yet been actioned—meaning those still awaiting manager or admin approval—whereas approved or rejected requests cannot be canceled through the employee interface. The cancellation process is straightforward: employees navigate to the Employee Dashboard, access the My Requests widget, locate the leave request they wish to cancel, click the three-dot menu next to it, and select Cancel, which updates the request status to Cancelled. Once canceled, the request immediately disappears from the Managers' Approvals widget, preventing further action by managers. The document also addresses the scenario where an employee might want to fully delete a request rather than cancel it, advising that this action is not recommended and may require higher-level administrative permissions obtainable through system policies or support ticket submission. This resource is intended for employees managing their own leave requests and those experiencing issues with the cancellation process or related approval workflows.

sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving the "An error occurred retrieving the leave request" error that users encounter during bulk leave approval processes. The error typically stems from one of two root causes: either the user lacks the required permission to approve leave requests, or the leave request's associated pay code is missing a necessary process code configuration. To resolve permission issues, users must navigate to Portal > Admin Dashboard > Site Manager > Admin Settings, locate the setting cp_lv_req_process_role, and change its value from 'N' to 'Y' to grant the necessary approval permissions. For pay code configuration issues, administrators need to access WFM Admin Dashboard > Configuration > Pay Codes, query the problematic pay code, select Leave Request Settings, and assign both an appropriate Leave Request Process Code and Leave Request Cancel Code. The document notes an important limitation: only newly created leave requests will process correctly after assigning process codes; existing leave requests without the codes will continue to cause errors and must be either cancelled and resubmitted, cancelled by employees with absences recorded manually by managers/administrators, or alternatively approved through the back office via CoreTime > Time Management > Approve Leave Requests. This document is intended for portal administrators and managers responsible for configuring leave request workflows and resolving approval bottlenecks in workforce management systems.

sl: This document explains how the Bradford Factor score is calculated in the Access Group system and provides step-by-step instructions for correcting calculation errors. If the score is not calculating correctly, users should verify that the Bradford Factor is assigned to the employee's work group or employee level by navigating to Portal > WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Person Maintenance to query the employee and check their work group assignment, then go to WFM Configuration > Work Groups to update the Bradford Factor Rule parameter. ss: Absence Trigger Points in CorePortal may fail to send emails or notifications due to six common configuration or system issues. This document walks through each possible cause—including missing Rule Groupings, unconfigured Organisational Roles, known bugs in Reminder Rules, invalid log file paths, deactivated Trigger Points in CoreTime, and stopped scheduled database jobs—along with specific resolution steps for each. Open this guide when absence notifications aren't being delivered and you need to systematically troubleshoot the CorePortal and CoreTime setup.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving issues when Absence Trigger Points in CorePortal fail to send emails or notifications, presenting six potential causes and their corresponding solutions. The first cause involves ensuring that Trigger Point Rules are properly added to the correct Group ID or Grouping by navigating to Administrator Dashboard > Trigger Points > Rule Grouping in CorePortal and confirming the rule matches the company setup. The second cause addresses missing Organisational Role configuration, which requires users to navigate to Administrator Dashboard > Trigger Points > Rule Grouping > Notification Details > Organisational Roles and add or update relevant roles for notifications to function. The third cause covers a known system issue affecting Reminder Rules configured with "Days after the end date of Absence" or "Days after the start date of Absence" options, which was resolved in CorePortal version 22.0.13 and later. The fourth cause relates to an invalid log file directory path on the database server, requiring Support to run database scripts to correct it. The fifth cause involves Trigger Points not being activated within the CoreTime back office, which users can resolve by navigating to CoreTime > System Params > Reference A-C > Control Parameters, selecting the company, accessing Trigger Point Groups, and enabling the "Activate Trigger Points" checkbox. The sixth cause addresses instances where the scheduled database job responsible for sending trigger points has stopped, which only Support can resolve by restarting the job. This document is designed for system administrators, portal managers, and support personnel managing absence notifications and trigger point configurations in CorePortal and CoreTime systems.

This configuration is essential for organizations that need to enforce specific absence policies aligned with their company holiday calendar, ensuring that absence management respects organizational policies regarding public holidays and company-designated holidays.

sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving issues where annual leave days are not being automatically deducted from an employee's active balance in the Access Group HR system. The first potential cause is when absence dates fall outside the current open balance calendar period, requiring users to verify the date range aligns with the active balance period. The second cause involves work groups configured not to calculate clockings, which users can resolve by navigating to WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Configuration > Work Groups, selecting the relevant work group, and enabling the Calculate Clockings option. A third issue occurs when Work Pattern Default Hours are set to .00, requiring users to access WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Configuration > Work Patterns to add standard hours for the employee's work group. Additional causes include outdated system calendars that prevent overnight calculation jobs from processing absences, incorrect "Calculate to" parameters set to 'End of Input Period' instead of 'Today' (adjusted via CoreTime > System Params > General Parameters-1), and a known system issue affecting version 23 (resolved in CoreHR v23.0.7+). The document also addresses User Defined Periods Calendars, requiring users to mark completed monthly periods through CoreTime > System Params > Company > User Define Periods. HR administrators and payroll personnel who manage leave balances and system configuration would typically use this document when investigating why leave deductions are not processing correctly.

ss: User defined period calendars in CoreTime and WFM need to be extended regularly to ensure timesheets, payroll, and other time-related processes continue working correctly. This document covers how to extend your calendar in both Back Office (via System Params > Calendars) and Portal (via WFM Admin Dashboard), with steps to generate new periods based on your calendar type (weekly, fortnightly, or monthly). Open this guide when you need to add future periods to your calendar or when you're setting up payroll and timesheet processes for upcoming tax years. Keep in mind that your Weekly and Yearly calendars must also be extended to match your user defined calendar, or new periods won't generate properly.
sl: This document provides instructions for extending user-defined period calendars within Access Group's timesheet and payroll systems to ensure that time-related processes such as generating timesheets and running payroll continue to function correctly across all future periods. The document outlines specific period guidelines based on calendar type: weekly calendars typically contain 52 periods in a tax year (or 53 if the pay date falls on 5 April), fortnightly calendars have 26 periods, and monthly calendars always have 12 periods, with a critical note that weekly and yearly system calendars must be extended far enough to cover the periods in the user-defined calendar or new periods will not generate correctly. For Back Office users, the process involves navigating to CoreTime > System Params > Calendars > System Calendar, searching for the relevant company, selecting User Defined Periods and the calendar code, then clicking Generate Periods to enter a start date, select duration, and specify the number of periods. The document references related procedures including extending system calendars, rolling back user-defined periods, and completing balance period end processes.

ss: When entering a sickness absence in PeopleXD Workforce Management, this document explains how to resolve the error that appears when an employee lacks a valid work pattern or shift type for the absence dates. It covers three main causes: missing or inactive shift type assignments, no work pattern existing on the absence date, and insufficient user permissions (specifically the Ignore Data Entry Restriction setting). Follow the step-by-step instructions to check and update the employee's work schedule in People Management or the WFM Admin Dashboard, or enable the required permission for the user entering the absence. Open this article when you encounter this error while recording sickness absences or if absences fail to process due to scheduling gaps.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses a specific error in PeopleXD Workforce Management that prevents users from entering sickness absences when an employee lacks a valid work pattern or shift type for the relevant dates. The guide provides a systematic troubleshooting approach by identifying and resolving multiple root causes, with the primary issue being that employees must have both a shift type and work pattern assigned on the absence date for the system to process the entry. Users are instructed to navigate through the People Management widget, select Employees, then use the View/Edit and Change Work Schedule options to ensure the Date Effective setting covers the absence date, after which the shift type must be saved and verified as active. A secondary verification process involves accessing the WFM Admin Dashboard, navigating to Person Maintenance, and using the three-dot menu to View the employee's Work Schedule and confirm a shift or work pattern is visible on the specific absence date. The document also covers permission-related issues by explaining how to enable the Ignore Data Entry Restriction setting for users in either Back Office (through System Params and System Users) or the Portal (through WFM Admin Dashboard and WFM Configuration), as users must have the correct permissions to override data entry restrictions when entering absences. Additional troubleshooting steps address secondary potential issues including verification that sickness dates fall within employment dates, correct absence type configuration, proper user permissions, and whether the system calendar has been extended to cover the requested leave dates. This document is typically used by Workforce Management administrators and HR personnel who manage employee schedules and process absence requests when encountering this specific error condition.

t: Portal: Remove unapproved absences on the Maintain Hours screen
s:

ss: Unapproved absences appear on the Maintain Hours screen in CoreTime when employees belong to a work group with Calculate Clockings enabled but haven't recorded their shift clockings. You can resolve this by either disabling Calculate Clockings on the work group (if clocking in/out isn't required) or by enabling Always Remove Unapproved Absence on the relevant work pattern (if clocking is still needed). Open this document when you need to clean up unapproved absences from timesheets or want to prevent them from appearing in the future. The guide covers both prevention methods and how to recalculate existing timesheets to remove absences that are already recorded.
sl: This document provides guidance on resolving the issue of unapproved absences appearing on the Maintain Hours screen, which occurs when employees belong to a work group with Calculate Clockings enabled but have not recorded clockings for their scheduled shifts. The document presents two primary resolution paths: disabling the Calculate Clockings setting on the work group if employees do not need to clock in and out, or enabling the Always Remove Unapproved Absence setting on the relevant work pattern if clocking in and out is still required. To disable Calculate Clockings, users navigate from the dashboard menu to WFM Admin Dashboard, then to WFM Configuration and Work Groups, locate the relevant work group, and turn off the Calculate Clockings toggle before saving. Alternatively, to enable automatic removal of unapproved absences, users access WFM Admin Dashboard, navigate to WFM Configuration and Work Patterns, find the relevant work pattern, access the Absence tab, and enable the Always Remove Unapproved Absence setting. The document also addresses clearing existing unapproved absences by instructing users to recalculate timesheets through the Timesheet Input screen for affected employees, navigating to weeks containing unapproved absences, and clicking Calculate to remove them. This guidance is intended for workforce management administrators and HR personnel managing employee timesheets and clocking systems within the Access Group platform.

sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for managers who encounter the error "An error occurred retrieving the leave request" when attempting to action leave requests in the Access Group system. ss: Setting up New Years Leave Entitlements in PeopleXD enables employees to book holidays for the upcoming year while giving managers full visibility of current and future leave balances. Built-in validation automatically prevents leave requests from exceeding entitlements and adjusts for length of service and FTE changes. Open this document when you need to configure leave entitlements for a new year or troubleshoot why employees can't book leave in advance.
sl: This document explains how to set up New Years Leave Entitlements in PeopleXD, a workforce management system that enables employees to view and book leave across current and future years while providing managers with complete visibility of available entitlements. The document covers the process of adding new balance entitlements through the Entitlements Per Balance tab, where users select the Entitlement Level, Period, Affecting Element, and specify values for Days, Hours, and Occurrence, with the system automatically accounting for length of service and FTE changes through built-in validation checks. The document serves HR administrators, managers, and employees implementing or using the year-end leave entitlement transition feature in PeopleXD.

t: How to resolve 'rest day' errors when booking annual leave
s:
When booking annual leave in PeopleXD Workforce Management, you may see a "rest day" error. This happens when the employee is not scheduled to work on the selected date in Workforce Management.

Additional errors you might encounter include "0 Contracted Hours" and "Unable to Determine Absence Durat...
ss: When booking annual leave in PeopleXD Workforce Management, a "rest day" error blocks the request if the employee isn't scheduled to work on that date. This error—along with related issues like "0 Contracted Hours"—occurs because annual leave can only be applied to scheduled working days. Open the employee's roster, add a working shift to the selected date, save the changes, and resubmit the leave request. Use this guide if you're unable to book annual leave due to scheduling conflicts or need to update an employee's roster before processing their leave.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide to resolving "rest day" errors that occur when booking annual leave in PeopleXD Workforce Management, along with related scheduling errors such as "0 Contracted Hours" and "Unable to Determine Absence Duration." The error appears because PeopleXD only permits annual leave requests on dates where employees have scheduled working shifts in their roster, and the system blocks requests when a selected leave date is marked as a rest day. Common causes include missing working shifts in the employee's schedule, incorrect or missing working patterns, use of the wrong contract when employees have multiple contracts, outdated rosters in Workforce Management, or misconfigured bank holiday scheme settings. To resolve the issue, users must access the employee profile through PeopleXD by selecting Actions and clicking View Schedules to display the roster, then locate the problematic date, verify the correct contract is selected, and add an appropriate working shift or pattern to that date. After saving the updated schedule and confirming the shift appears on the selected date, users can return to the annual leave request, select the same date, and successfully submit the request. The document is designed for HR administrators and managers with permission to view and edit employee schedules in PeopleXD who need to troubleshoot booking issues and ensure employees have proper roster coverage before processing leave requests. If the error persists after updating the schedule, the document recommends checking Workforce Management synchronization or contacting system support, and emphasizes the importance of ensuring bank holiday schemes are configured correctly according to organizational policies.

It also covers best practices for navigation, filtering, and troubleshooting common problems with the Bulk Leave Approval process.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide to using the Bulk Leave Approval screen in PeopleXD, a centralized interface designed for managers and administrators to review, filter, and approve multiple leave requests simultaneously rather than processing them individually. The Bulk Leave Approval screen is primarily used by team managers handling departmental leave approvals and administrators managing organization-wide leave activity, allowing them to maintain visibility and consistency across leave management. The screen features a date range filtering capability where users select both a start date and end date to view all leave requests within that specific period, providing precise control over displayed data. The document addresses common issues such as discrepancies in the number of leave requests displayed, which typically stem from access configuration or filtering differences that can be resolved by reviewing user access settings in the WFM Admin Dashboard under WFM Configuration and WFM System User Configuration to verify correct Work Groups and Departments assignments. Users must always access the Bulk Leave Approval screen through the official WFM Admin Dashboard navigation path rather than alternative routes in Workforce Management, as different paths may apply varying rules or filters affecting results. The document recommends best practices including regular review of user access settings, consistent use of the correct navigation path for all updates, application of clear date ranges, and proper training on filter application to prevent missing or unexpected records. ss: Balance adjustments in CoreTime correct an employee's time or leave balance when discrepancies occur. Use this process when you need to add or remove hours from an employee's balance—for example, to fix an incorrect calculation or account for a special circumstance. Once saved, adjustments create an audit trail and cannot be deleted; to reverse an adjustment, you must enter an offsetting counter adjustment for the same balance period. Open this document if you're working in CoreTime's Time Management module and need step-by-step instructions for selecting an employee, choosing a balance code, and entering the adjustment amount with supporting narrative.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for back office staff to make balance adjustments in the CoreTime system to correct an employee's balance records. The process is accessed by navigating to CoreTime > Time Mgt > Balances > Balance Adjustments, where users select an employee and relevant balance code using person buttons to view the employee's current balances and adjustment history. Users must enter several key details including the adjustment period, the affecting element of the balance, the specific adjustment amount, and a narrative description for audit purposes before clicking Save. An important consideration is that saved balance adjustments cannot be deleted for auditing purposes; instead, users must process a counter adjustment with the opposite value (for example, entering -10 hours to reverse a +10 hour adjustment) to return a balance to its original value. When entering a period, the system automatically sets the date effective to today's date, but users making historical adjustments must manually set an appropriate date within the balance period being updated. This document is primarily used by back office administrators or payroll staff who need to correct employee balance records, such as vacation hours or leave entitlements, while maintaining a complete audit trail of all adjustments made to the system.

sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for creating and configuring a new balance in the CoreTime system, which is part of the Access Group's human resources management platform. ss: Leave balance entitlements may calculate incorrectly when appointment dates are out of sync in CorePersonnel or when an employee's position isn't configured in the Entitlement Per Balance settings within CoreTime. Use this guide if an employee's leave balance doesn't match their position history or company entitlement rules. Follow the troubleshooting steps to verify appointment start and end dates, set up the position in Entitlement Per Balance with the correct category and period, and trigger a balance recalculation to resolve the issue.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving incorrectly calculated leave balance entitlements in the Access Group system, which can stem from two distinct root causes. The first potential issue involves appointment start or end dates being out of sync within CorePersonnel, which can be diagnosed and corrected by navigating to CorePersonnel > Maintenance > Appointment History to verify and update the dates, followed by a balance recalculation. The second cause addresses situations where an employee's position has not been properly configured within the Entitlement Per Balance system, resolved by accessing CoreTime > System Params > Balances > Entitlement Per Balance and adding the employee position in the Category column alongside the corresponding period information. Users must input the entitlement values in days and hours within the Entitlement Per Balance configuration screen before saving the changes. This document is primarily used by human resources and payroll administrators who manage leave entitlements and need to reconcile discrepancies between expected and actual leave balances for individual employees. Following either correction procedure requires performing a balance recalculation for the affected employee to ensure the system updates with the corrected information. The document references related issues including pro-rating problems for departing employees, new starters receiving incorrect mid-year entitlements, and zero balances appearing for newly created leave types.

t: Length of Service not calculating correct entitlement for employees on Annual Leave Balance
s:
There are a few reasons how this could occur. To fix this, follow the steps below.

 

Condition 1

If the Length of Service Parameter is set to calculate on "Period Start", then it will give the LOS to any employee at the start of the balance calendar if they reach LOS entitlement within the balanc...
ss: Annual Leave Balance calculations in CoreTime may provide incorrect Length of Service (LOS) entitlements when the LOS parameter is configured incorrectly or when employee start date settings don't align with service history. This document covers three specific scenarios: when LOS is set to calculate on "Period Start" (requiring employee-level LOS assignment), when it's set to "Anniversary" (requiring correct Employee Start Date configuration), and when the Override Start Date field is used (requiring the Employee Start Date to be updated to "Continuous Date"). Open this guide if employees are receiving annual leave entitlements at the wrong time or in the wrong amount, or if you need to adjust LOS calculation settings in your Balance Parameters.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses issues where Length of Service (LOS) is not calculating correct annual leave entitlements for employees and provides three distinct scenarios with resolution steps for each. The first condition explains that when the Length of Service Parameter is set to "Period Start" in the Annual Leave Balance, employees receive their LOS entitlement at the start of the balance calendar year even if they don't reach the qualifying date until later in the year, requiring LOS to be assigned at the employee level through either CoreTime's Pers Data > Pers Maintenance > Balance Setup menu or the Portal's People Management/WFM Admin Dashboard using the 'Edit Setup' option. The second condition addresses the scenario where the Length of Service Parameter is set to "Calculate on Anniversary," which requires checking the Anniversary Date and the "Employee Start Date" field setting, and necessitates ensuring the correct Calculate On indicator is enabled in CoreTime > System Params > Balance > Balance Parameters > Length of Service by selecting from options including Anniversary, Period Start, Post Appointment Period Start, Post Appointment Anniversary, or Shift Type Anniversary before running a balance recalculation. The third condition covers situations where updating the 'Override Start Date' field automatically updates the 'Continuous Service Started' field to match, requiring administrators to change the 'Employee Start Date' setting to 'Continuance Date' in the Balance Parameters Length of Service section to ensure accurate calculations. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators, HR professionals, and system administrators working with the Access Group's CoreTime and Portal systems who need to troubleshoot and configure annual leave balance entitlements based on employee length of service metrics.

Access this feature through CoreTime > System Params > Balances > Calendars, where you can untick the closed period and save your changes. Open this guide when you need to reverse a closed balance period, but remember to only move the calendar backwards (never forward) and run a Balance Recalculation afterward to verify there are no errors. Use this process carefully and sparingly, as moving the calendar back too far can cause issues with your balance calculations.
sl: This document provides instructions for rolling back a closed calendar period in the CoreTime system to allow it to be reopened, which is useful when periods have been incorrectly closed and need correction. The process involves navigating to CoreTime > System Params > Balances > Calendars, then selecting the relevant balance from a dropdown menu and unticking the incorrectly closed period before saving changes. The document emphasizes a critical constraint that calendar periods should only be moved backwards and never advanced using this feature, as moving the calendar incorrectly could cause data integrity issues. Users are advised to exercise caution when rolling back periods and to avoid moving the calendar too far back, which could introduce errors into the system. After making any calendar changes, the document recommends performing a Balance Recalculation to verify the changes are working correctly and to identify any errors that may have resulted from the adjustment. If errors are discovered during or after the Balance Recalculation process, users should change the balance calendar back to its previous state. This document is primarily used by back office administrators or system managers who handle balance period management and need to correct calendar period closures in the CoreTime payroll or HR system.

Click View under the Employees option.

ss: Employee balances in People Management and WFM Admin can be created, adjusted, and recalculated to keep leave entitlements and other balance types accurate and current. Use this document to assign new balances to employees, make adjustments with effective dates and reasons, or manually recalculate balances when contract changes or entitlement code updates occur outside the standard overnight recalculation cycle. Open this guide when you need to modify an individual employee's balance record, correct a balance amount, or trigger an immediate recalculation after updating employee hours or contract details. The document covers the step-by-step process for both platforms and explains when manual recalculation is necessary versus relying on automatic overnight updates.
sl: This document provides administrators with comprehensive guidance on creating, adjusting, and recalculating employee leave balances through two primary interfaces: People Management and WFM Admin. For assigning new balances, administrators navigate to the Command Centre widget in People Management or WFM Person Maintenance in WFM Admin, then select the Balances tab and click Assign New Balance, where they must populate mandatory fields including Period, Type, Segment, and Balance Type (such as Annual Leave). To adjust existing balances, administrators access the Balances screen in either system, expand the 3-dot menu to select Balance Adjustment, and specify the Effective Date, Adjustment Type (such as Carried Forward), and Adjustment Amount, with optional reasons that will be visible to employees and tracked in Adjustment History. The document addresses manual recalculation procedures for situations where changes to entitlement codes or contract details occur after the Balance Period End process has run, allowing administrators to select a specific Period and trigger an immediate recalculation that the system would not otherwise update overnight. It also explains that annual leave entitlements automatically recalculate overnight based on updates to employee category or FTE, with the system using contract details such as weekly working hours to determine adjustments, though manual recalculation should be used when immediate updates are needed. The guidance emphasizes testing changes in UAT first, documenting adjustment reasons for audit trails, and using the Data Migration template for bulk balance management, while noting that contract or working hour modifications trigger pro-rated FTE adjustments based on the affected date range. This document is designed for system administrators and HR personnel responsible for managing employee leave entitlements and handling scenarios where automatic recalculation is insufficient.

sl: This document provides a comprehensive pre-checklist of five essential preparation tasks that must be completed before running the Balance Period End process in the Access Group's CoreTime and WFM systems to ensure smooth operation without errors. Future periods must be created before a period end can be run" and pay code entry warnings related to balance period boundaries.

Open this document if you need to fix incorrect leave balances for departing employees or configure pro-rating settings in CoreTime. To resolve this issue, users must navigate to CoreTime > System Params > Balances > Parameters, locate the relevant balance, access Advanced Parameters, and then click Advanced Pro Rata to enable the Apply Target End Date option before saving the changes. After updating this configuration setting, users must perform a balance recalculation by returning to CoreTime > System Params > Balances > Recalculate Balances, selecting the affected employee or employee group, and following the on-screen prompts to complete the recalculation process. This document is intended for HR administrators, payroll specialists, or system managers who manage leave and absence balances in Access Group's CoreTime system and need to ensure accurate pro-rata calculations for departing employees. The document also references related articles addressing similar pro-rata calculation issues, including scenarios involving new starters, mid-year FTE changes, and annual leave balance calculations.

Open this document when you need to set up or troubleshoot why an employee's holiday balance isn't automatically calculating on a pro-rata basis based on their start date or reduced working hours. This applies to basic balances that don't have automatic entitlement calculation configured by position or FTE.
sl: This document provides guidance on configuring and managing pro rata holiday entitlements in the Access Group's CoreTime system when employees start mid-year or experience changes to their full-time equivalent (FTE) status. It explains that balances configured to calculate entitlement based on position or FTE will automatically calculate the Starting Entitlement, but describes the manual steps required to pro rata a basic balance for mid-year starters. The process involves navigating to CoreTime > Time Mgt > Balances > Pro Rata Entitlements, locating the desired Balance Code on the list, and adding new entries using the Green Add button if necessary before saving changes. The document addresses a critical configuration requirement by instructing users to verify that the Adjustment Type is set to "Holiday" through CoreTime > Time Mgt > Balances > Parameters > Advanced Parameters > Advanced Pro Rata. It also requires enabling the "Calculate Service on Time in Company" parameter by accessing CoreTime > System Params > Balances > Entitlements per Balance, querying the balance, selecting General Parameters, and enabling this setting before saving. This guidance is essential for payroll administrators, HR professionals, and CoreTime system users who need to ensure employees receive correctly pro-rated holiday entitlements rather than full-year allocations when joining the organization mid-year or when their contracted hours change. The document also references related troubleshooting articles addressing scenarios where pro-rata calculations fail or new starters incorrectly receive full balance entitlements.

t: Balance hasn't updated fully after running balance period end
s:
After you run a balance period end, balances do not automatically update immediately. A balance re-calculation is required to finalise and update employee balances.

This re-calculation normally happens overnight via the scheduled balance re-calc job. However, you can also run it manually if you nee...
ss: Balance updates in WFM don't happen automatically after running a period end—you need to trigger a balance re-calculation to finalize employee balances. While the system normally recalculates balances overnight through a scheduled job, you can manually run the re-calculation immediately through WFM Admin > Balance Maintenance if you need updated balances sooner. Open this document if balances appear stuck or incomplete after a period end, or if you need to refresh balance figures urgently without waiting for the overnight process.
sl: This document explains why employee balances do not update immediately after running a balance period end and how to resolve this delay by performing a manual balance re-calculation. Normally, balances are recalculated automatically overnight through a scheduled balance re-calc job, but the document acknowledges that users may need balances to update sooner and provides instructions for manually triggering this process. To manually run the balance re-calculation, users must navigate to WFM Admin, select Balance Maintenance, query the specific balance requiring recalculation, select Balance Re-calculation, choose "Both" when prompted for the recalculation type, and click Recalculate. This manual process performs a bulk balance re-calculation that updates employee balances immediately rather than waiting for the overnight scheduled job. The document is primarily useful for payroll administrators, HR professionals, or workforce management staff who need to ensure employee balance information is current for reporting, compliance, or employee-facing purposes. It serves as a practical troubleshooting guide for situations where the automatic overnight recalculation is insufficient or where urgent balance updates are required before the next scheduled job runs.

ss: Leave balances in PeopleXD aren't reducing proportionally based on an employee's start date or leave date because their employee status (such as PP, PW, or ST) hasn't been configured in the Pro Rata Entitlements settings. Open this document if you need to fix pro rata leave calculations in CoreTime by adding missing employee statuses to the balance configuration and recalculating the affected employee's balance. This applies whether you're working in the Portal or Back-Office, and covers scenarios where employees join mid-year or leave during the balance year.
sl: This document addresses a common configuration issue in the Access Group system where leave balances fail to reduce proportionally based on an employee's start date or leave date, typically occurring because the balance has not been set up to recognize specific employee statuses such as PP, PW, or ST. The document provides a two-part resolution process beginning in the Portal interface, where users navigate to People Management or the WFM Admin Dashboard, access WFM Person Maintenance, query the employee record, and check the Balances section under Entitlement Basis to identify and note the employee's current status. The second part of the resolution takes place in the Back-Office CoreTime system, where administrators access System Params, select Balances, and then navigate to Pro Rata Entitlements to verify whether the specific Balance Code includes the employee status in question. If the Balance Code does not contain the required employee status, users must add a new row with both the Balance Code and Employee Status, then enable the Pro Rata Leave Date option and save the changes. Finally, users return to the Portal to recalculate the employee's balance by navigating back to the employee record and selecting the Recalculate function under Balances. This document is used by HR administrators and payroll professionals who manage leave entitlements and need to ensure that pro-rata calculations accurately reflect employees' tenure and employment status changes throughout the leave year.

t: How to limit days booked in a balance period
s:
You can control and limit how many days employees can book for Annual Leave or Flexi Time during a specific balance period by updating the calendar settings in CoreTime.

ss: CoreTime's calendar settings let you control and limit the number of days employees can book for Annual Leave or Flexi Time within a specific balance period. You can adjust booked day limits and statutory entitlement controls by accessing System Params, selecting Balances and Calendars, then updating the Limit Days field for your chosen period. Open this document when you need to prevent employees from booking more leave than allowed or when you're setting up leave restrictions for a new balance period.
sl: This document explains how to control and restrict the number of days that employees can book for Annual Leave or Flexi Time during a specific balance period by adjusting settings within the CoreTime system. The process involves navigating to CoreTime, accessing System Params, and then selecting the Balances section followed by Calendars to locate the relevant balance that requires updating. Users must search for the specific balance they want to modify and then adjust the controls for both Booked and Statutory Entitlement fields according to their requirements. The core task involves updating the Limit Days field for the relevant period or periods to set the maximum allowable days that can be booked during that balance period. After making the necessary changes to these configuration settings, users must click Save to apply and finalize the updates to the system. This document is primarily used by HR administrators, payroll managers, and system administrators who need to enforce leave booking restrictions and prevent employees from exceeding approved leave allocations during defined balance periods. The related articles suggest this functionality connects to broader leave management concerns, including preventing overbooking scenarios and managing balance period end processes.

t: Employee balance not appearing as expected after adding a new floating entitlement code
s:
If an employee’s balance isn’t displaying as expected after assigning a Floating Entitlement Code, it’s usually because the wrong code has been attached.

Why this happens

ss: When an employee's balance fails to display correctly after you assign a Floating Entitlement Code in CoreTime, it's typically due to an invalid or incorrect code attachment. This article walks you through removing the wrong code from the employee's Current Balances, then choosing the right correction method depending on whether new balances have been activated since the last Balance Period End. You'll also learn how to verify position-based entitlement parameters if your Floating Entitlements are tied to Position History. Open this if your employee balances aren't calculating as expected after setting up floating entitlement codes.
sl: This document provides guidance for resolving a common issue in CoreTime where an employee's balance fails to display correctly after a new Floating Entitlement Code has been assigned, with the root cause typically being an invalid or incorrect code attachment. The document outlines a step-by-step troubleshooting process beginning in CoreTime's Pers. Data > Person Maintenance section, where users navigate to Current Balances, select the affected balance, and remove the invalid Floating Entitlement Code before saving changes. After removing the incorrect code, users must decide on a correction strategy based on whether new balances have been activated since the last Balance Period End, with the option to roll back and re-run the balance period (via CoreTime > System Parameters > Balances > Calendars) if no new balances exist, or to manually adjust the employee's balance if new balances have already been activated. The document also addresses position-based floating entitlements by instructing users to verify that specific parameters are enabled in Back Office under CoreTime > System Params > Balances > Advance Parameters, specifically checking that "Populate Position History details" and "Calculate Entitlement Based on Position History" options are activated. This resource is intended for HR and payroll administrators who manage employee entitlements and balances within the CoreTime system and need to diagnose and correct balance-related discrepancies following entitlement code assignments.

Open this guide when you need to review past balance details for an employee or when the Reports option isn't visible in your WFM Admin Dashboard—it also includes steps to enable the necessary reporting permissions (WFM_REPORTS_ADMN or WFM_REPORTS_MGR) in Security settings.
sl: This document explains how to access and view historical balance information for employees across previous periods using two distinct methods within the Access Group system. The first option involves using the Insight Admin interface, where users navigate to the Balance History Report by searching for it in the report search bar and selecting the Person Balance History (Time) folder, then applying filters by employee name or number, balance type, and specific periods to retrieve closed period data. The second option utilizes the Balance Details Report in WFM Admin Dashboard, accessible through Reports and Report Type selection, where users input parameters including Balance Type, Start Period, End Period, Person, and Person Status before running the report. Access to these reports is role-based, requiring either WFM_REPORTS_MGR permissions for managers or WFM_REPORTS_ADMN permissions for administrators, which must be assigned through Security > User Management > Menu Profiles and verified before the Reports option becomes visible. The document serves HR administrators, payroll managers, and workforce management personnel who need to audit or review historical employee balance records for compliance, adjustment, or analytical purposes. If users cannot locate the Reports option after enabling permissions, the document provides troubleshooting steps including logging out and back in to refresh access, and emphasizes that all permission modifications should be carefully tested in a User Acceptance Testing (UAT) environment before deployment to the live system to ensure security and prevent disruptions.

t: New Starter Receiving Full Balance Entitlement Mid-Year
s:
You can fix employee balance calculation problems by checking key settings in CoreTime. This guide outlines four possible causes and provides step-by-step instructions to resolve each one. Following these steps ensures balances update correctly, reflecting accurate leave entitlements.

 

Common cau...
ss: CoreTime balance calculation problems can often be resolved by adjusting four key settings: enabling Populate Status/FTE Details, configuring Pro Rata Entitlements for employee status, setting Adjustment Type to "Holiday", and disabling the Use Hire/Leave dates option. This guide walks through step-by-step instructions for each of these CoreTime System Parameters adjustments, including where to navigate and what to verify. Open this document when employee leave entitlements are showing incorrect values or balances aren't updating as expected after configuration changes.
sl: This document is a troubleshooting guide for resolving employee leave balance calculation problems within the CoreTime system, specifically addressing scenarios where new starters or mid-year changes result in incorrect entitlement calculations. The guide identifies four primary causes of balance calculation errors: the Populate Status/FTE Details option not being enabled on Balance Parameters, the employee's Person Status lacking Pro Rata entitlement configuration, the Adjustment Type not being set to "Holiday," and the Use Hire/Leave dates setting being incorrectly enabled. For each cause, the document provides detailed step-by-step instructions requiring administrator access to CoreTime, including navigating to System Params > Balances and accessing either Parameters or Pro Rata Entitlements sections, then making the necessary configuration changes and recalculating balances. The Populate Status/FTE Details fix synchronizes employee status and full-time equivalent (FTE) details from Back Office to ensure accurate pro-rata calculations, with a note that enabling it will apply FTE deductions when FTE is below 100 percent. The Pro Rata Entitlements configuration requires selecting the Balance Code and Employee Status (such as Permanent) and setting the Pro Rata Leave Date field appropriately. This document is designed for HR administrators and system managers who need to correct mid-year hire entitlement issues or FTE-related balance adjustments, and it references related articles covering Length of Service calculations, pro-rating for employees leaving mid-year, and floating entitlement codes.

t: Deactivate or reactivate a balance for an employee
s:

ss: Enable or disable employee balances in PeopleXD using either the Portal or Back-Office system. This process covers toggling the Active indicator for specific balances in an employee's record, with different navigation steps depending on which system you're using. Open this document when you need to deactivate a balance temporarily or reactivate one that's been disabled, or if you're troubleshooting why a balance appears inactive (which may require checking the Category field in the employee's contract). After making changes in Back-Office, you'll also learn how to recalculate the balance in Core Time to ensure updates take effect.
sl: This document provides comprehensive instructions for deactivating and reactivating employee balances in both the Portal and Back-Office systems, serving HR administrators and payroll professionals who manage employee entitlements and leave balances. The document addresses a critical configuration consideration: the "Category" field in an employee's contract must be populated for balances to generate and display correctly, and balances may appear inactive if this field is empty. In the Portal environment, users navigate to People Management, use Employee Search to locate an employee, select Balances from the left menu, and use the ellipsis (...) menu next to the relevant balance to choose between Deactivate or Activate options. In Back-Office, the process involves navigating through Pers Data > Person Maintenance, searching for the employee (with an option to select All Employees for leavers), clicking Current Balances under Select Detail, and then toggling the Active indicator in the Balance Setup screen with automatic confirmation dialog handling. Following any balance deactivation or reactivation, users must perform a Balance Recalculation through Core Time > Time Mgt > Balance Recalculation, selecting both the employee and balance, and choosing "Both" to ensure changes are properly applied. The document emphasizes that appropriate permissions are required in both systems before making modifications, and notes that balances associated with ended appointments will automatically revert to inactive status after recalculation. The document also clarifies an important distinction: when navigating directly to Balance Setup, only the first balance displays by default, requiring manual selection of specific balances from the Current Balances list when employees have multiple balances.

t: System balance adjustments
s: Balances are automatically adjusted by the system in several situations, such as when a balance is activated, a new balance period starts, or employee working hours change. This article covers two common types of adjustments: FTE adjustments for part-time employees and Public Holiday (PH) adjustment...
ss: Automatic balance adjustments in PeopleXD occur when balances are activated, new balance periods start, or employee working hours change. This document explains two common adjustment types: FTE adjustments for part-time employees (based on their Absence FTE or base FTE) and Public Holiday adjustments that apply Reserved or Entitlement values depending on whether the employee is rostered to work or has a rest day on company holidays. Open this if you need to understand why an employee's leave or absence balance has changed automatically, or if you're troubleshooting balance discrepancies related to part-time status or public holiday schemes.
sl: This document explains the automatic balance adjustments that occur in the Access Group system under various triggering events, specifically focusing on two prevalent adjustment types: FTE adjustments for part-time employees and Public Holiday adjustments based on company holiday schemes. The FTE adjustment process applies to part-time employees and relies on their Absence FTE value, or their base FTE if Absence FTE is not configured, with instructions provided to view these details by navigating to the People Management Dashboard, selecting View beside Employees in the Command Centre, searching for the employee record, accessing the Contracts section, and opening Contract Information to review FTE details. Public Holiday adjustments are automatically applied when a company holiday scheme is assigned to a balance, with the scheme generating either Reserved or Entitlement adjustments during the balance period depending on the employee's schedule circumstances. Reserved adjustments appear as negative values when an employee is rostered to work on a company holiday, while Entitlement adjustments apply when the public holiday coincides with the employee's designated rest day. This document serves users responsible for managing employee time and attendance balances who need to understand how the system automatically recalculates entitlements based on employment contracts, working patterns, and company holiday policies, making it essential reading for HR administrators and payroll professionals handling balance assignments and adjustments mid-cycle or during balance period transitions.

t: Run the balance period end
s:
To close a balance period and move into the next one, you need to run a balance period end. 

 

Important considerations

Things to consider before running your balance period end:

Question
 
Answer

When can I run Period Year End?

 

Period Year End can only be run when the last week of the prev...
ss: Running a balance period end closes the current balance period in WFM and moves the system into the next one. Before you start, ensure the final week of the previous period is closed in WFM, your company calendar is extended through at least the end of the calendar year, and carry forward values are configured in the Balance Calendar. Open the WFM Admin Dashboard, navigate to Balance Maintenance, and use the Balance Period End tab to run the process once the system week has moved past your open period's end date. Use this when you're ready to transition between balance periods and need to finalize balances, calculate Length of Service updates, and prepare the next period for use.
sl: This document explains how to close out a balance period and transition to the next period in the WFM (Workforce Management) system by running a balance period end process. The document covers important pre-requisites and considerations, including that Period Year End can only be executed once the last week of the previous period has been closed in WFM (typically the first Monday of January), and that the company calendar and any user-defined calendars (UDCs) must be extended at minimum to the end of the calendar year or balance year if it runs mid-year. It details the step-by-step process to run balance period end: accessing the WFM Admin Dashboard, selecting the Balance Maintenance tab, clicking the three-dot menu next to the relevant balance, navigating to the Balance Period End tab, verifying the current period is correct, and clicking Run Period End followed by confirmation prompts. The document addresses specific timing considerations such as Length of Service (LOS) calculations occurring during the overnight calculation after Period Year End is run (meaning LOS additions will not be visible until the following day) and clarifies when carry forward values should be set during the previous year's Year End process to control which values transfer into the new balance year. The document also references related articles covering balance value limits, error messages about the last period on the balance calendar, back office prerequisites, and troubleshooting for incomplete balance updates after running period end. This resource is intended for payroll and workforce management administrators who need to close accounting or balance periods and manage the transition between fiscal periods in the system.
