ss: Advancing the system calendar in CoreTime without using the standard advance period function requires updating both Control Parameters and System Calendar in sync. This two-step process involves moving the current period forward in Control Parameters, then selecting the appropriate calendar period in System Calendar for your company. Use this workaround method only in emergency situations, as the standard week advance process in CoreTime is the recommended approach. You'll need to ensure both the Control Parameters and System Calendar remain synchronized to avoid processing issues.
sl: This document provides instructions for manually advancing the system calendar in CoreTime without using the standard advance period function, which is useful when the regular process cannot be used. The procedure consists of two mandatory steps that must be performed in sequence to keep the system synchronized: first, updating the Control Parameters current Period by navigating to CoreTime > System Params > Reference A-C > Control Parameters, selecting the appropriate Company via List of Values, and updating the Current Period field before saving; and second, advancing the System Calendar by going to CoreTime > System Params > Calendars > System Calendar, selecting the same Company, clicking Current Period, selecting the current Calendar Period checkbox (identifying the first uncompleted row), and saving the changes. The document emphasizes that the System Calendar and Control Parameters current Period must always remain in sync to prevent system inconsistencies. For users with User Defined Calendars, an alternative workaround is provided through the same System Calendar menu path, where users select the Calendar Code, mark completed periods by ticking the Completed button, and save the changes. A critical warning note indicates that this manual process should only be used as a workaround or emergency measure, with the standard CoreTime process being the recommended approach for regular calendar advancement. This document is primarily used by CoreTime administrators, payroll personnel, or support staff who need to troubleshoot calendar synchronization issues or handle exceptional scenarios where the automated advance period function is unavailable.

t: Configure shift types
s:
Learn how to configure shift types in Access WFM, including setting up working patterns, pay codes, and absence premiums.

 

Key Features of Shift Types
Cycle Shift

The Cycle Shift option ensures that the schedule repeats on the same weekly cycle. Enable this feature if you want the same work patt...
ss: Shift types in Access WFM define the working patterns, pay codes, and absence premiums assigned to employees. Use this guide to create new shift types (or copy existing ones), configure weekly schedules and daily hours, set thresholds and overtime allowances, and link absence premiums to pay codes. Open this document when you need to establish how shifts repeat—whether on a weekly cycle or custom periods—and want to ensure consistent scheduling across your workforce. This is essential setup work for anyone managing shift configuration in the WFM Admin Dashboard.
sl: This document provides comprehensive instructions for configuring shift types in Access WFM, covering the complete setup process from initial creation through detailed configuration of working patterns, pay codes, and absence premiums. The document begins by explaining key shift type features, specifically the Cycle Shift option which ensures schedules repeat on the same weekly cycle, and Sequence Number 1 which represents the weekly schedule from Sunday to Saturday. To create a new shift type, users navigate from the WFM Admin Dashboard to WFM Configuration, locate the Shift Type tile, and click Add to enter a unique code, name, and short name, with the option to copy an existing similar shift type instead using its three-dot menu. During initial setup, users must enable the Cycle Shift toggle for recurring weekly patterns (considered best practice to reduce maintenance) or disable it for period-based shifts, then enable the Active toggle and click OK. The Shift Patterns tab allows users to define specific work hours for each day of the week by selecting relevant hours from a dropdown menu and repeating this process for multiple shifts before saving. The General Parameters tab provides additional configuration options for thresholds, holiday adjustments, and overtime allowance settings. Finally, the Absence Premium tab enables users to set absence premiums and associate corresponding pay codes with shift types. This document is intended for workforce management administrators and supervisors who need to establish or modify shift scheduling configurations within their Access WFM system.

t: Reporting on Employee Shifts and Work Patterns
s:
You can report on shifts and patterns assigned to an employee using PeopleXD Insight, but there are some limitations you should be aware of.

What can you report on?

What

 

How

 

Notes

Returns all assigned shi...
ss: Reporting on employee shifts and work patterns uses PeopleXD Insight, specifically the Person Shift (Time) and Ct Shift Pattern (Data Validation) folders to pull shift assignments and linked patterns with daily breakdowns. This reporting tool helps you track all shifts assigned to an employee and understand how shift patterns are structured by day, though it has key limitations: you cannot filter for current shifts only, shift overrides are not included, and you'll need to manually order and filter results to find relevant data. Open this document when you need to generate shift or pattern reports in Insight, understand how pattern data is broken down, or troubleshoot why certain shift information isn't appearing in your reports.
sl: This document explains how to report on employee shifts and work patterns using PeopleXD Insight, including what data can be accessed and what limitations users should expect. The document describes specific reporting folders and methods: the Person Shift (Time) folder is used to report on shifts assigned to an employee, while the Ct Shift Pattern (Data Validation) folder shows patterns linked to those shifts with a daily breakdown of the pattern. Shift patterns are systematically broken down by day, with Pattern 1 representing the first day (typically Monday), Pattern 2 the second day (typically Tuesday), and so on. Three key limitations are highlighted: all shift records are returned rather than only the current shift, shift overrides and temporary override patterns are not included in reporting, and manual interpretation of results is required since there is no automatic filter for current shifts only. The document recommends ordering results by Date Effective (Descending) to display the most recent shifts at the top, helping users navigate the full dataset. This resource is intended for HR and workforce administrators who need to audit or analyze employee shift assignments and patterns within PeopleXD systems and should be consulted when troubleshooting shift-related issues or generating shift reports.

t: Set up new cycle shift type
s:
There are two different types of Shift Type - cycle Shift Types and calendar-based Shift Types. To set up a new cycle Shift Type, follow the steps below.

Portal

Click WFM Admin Dashboard, then click Config.

Enter the relevant details, then click OK.

Click Add, then...
ss: Setting up a cycle shift type in CoreTime or the WFM Admin Dashboard allows you to create rotating work patterns that span multiple weeks for your workforce. This process is essential when you need to define complex scheduling arrangements where employees work different shift patterns across consecutive weeks. Open this document when you're configuring a new repeating schedule that can't be captured with a single daily pattern, or when you need to assign default shift types to workgroups. Note that once a cycle shift type is assigned to employees or workgroups, it cannot be amended, so plan your pattern carefully before saving.
sl: This document provides instructions for creating a new cycle shift type within a workforce management system that supports two distinct shift type formats: cycle-based and calendar-based arrangements. The setup process varies depending on whether you are using the Portal interface or the Back Office system, with the Portal route requiring navigation through WFM Admin Dashboard > Config > Shift Type, while the Back Office method accesses the feature via CoreTime > System Params > Shift Type. In both interfaces, you must enter identifying information such as a code, name, and short name for the shift type, then configure the work patterns by defining sequence numbers and corresponding daily work arrangements across multiple weeks if the cycle spans longer than one week, using rest patterns to indicate non-working days. The document addresses a critical constraint: once a cycle shift type has been assigned to a workgroup or employee, it cannot be amended, and the system will highlight affected fields in yellow to prevent accidental modifications. Additionally, the document explains that default shift types can be assigned at the workgroup level, automatically applying to all members, though they can be overridden individually through the Person Maintenance screen, or alternatively assigned directly to each employee without a workgroup default. This guide is intended for workforce management administrators and HR personnel responsible for configuring shift schedules and managing shift type assignments across employees and workgroups.

t: Extend a standard shift type
s:
To extend a shift type, follow the steps below.

From the dashboard menu, click WFM Admin Dashboard, then click WFM Configuration. 

Click Shift Type, then next to the relevant shift click the three-dot menu.

Click View, then click Generate Periods and under Copy Range, enter the Period to copy (Fr...
ss: Extending shift types in the WFM Admin Dashboard allows you to copy existing shift patterns forward into new periods without manually recreating them. This process is useful when your shifts follow a repeating weekly pattern and you need to quickly generate future scheduling periods. You'll access this through WFM Configuration > Shift Type, then use the Generate Periods feature to specify which periods to copy and where to paste them. Use this guide when you've set up shift patterns that repeat consistently and want to extend them efficiently into upcoming timeframes.
sl: This document provides instructions for extending an existing shift type within the WFM (Workforce Management) system using the Access Group platform. The process begins by navigating from the dashboard menu to WFM Admin Dashboard, then selecting WFM Configuration and clicking on Shift Type to access the relevant shift configuration. Users locate their desired shift and access its options through a three-dot menu, then click View followed by Generate Periods to set up the extension parameters. The procedure involves specifying a Copy Range by entering the Period to copy (using From and To fields), followed by selecting a Paste Range where users enter the first new Period and the period to generate. After configuring these ranges, users click Ok and then Save to apply the changes and complete the shift extension. The document includes a helpful note clarifying that if a shift pattern repeats identically week to week, users should enter the last existing Period in both the 'Start Period' and 'End Period' fields to streamline the configuration. This guide is intended for WFM administrators and configuration managers who need to extend existing shift patterns in their workforce scheduling system without creating entirely new shift types.

t: How to restrict access to work patterns in the roster change screen in the Team Scheduler
s:
If you need to restrict a user’s ability to assign or view specific work patterns in the Roster Change screen of the Team Scheduler, you can do this by using Pattern Types in Back Office.

This process allows you to control which work patterns are available to each system user. Follow the steps belo...
ss: Restrict which work patterns users can assign or view in the Team Scheduler's Roster Change screen by setting up Pattern Type restrictions in CoreTime Back Office. This process involves creating a new pattern type code, assigning it to specific work patterns, and then attaching it to individual user accounts. Open this document when you need to limit roster access for certain team members or prevent users from selecting inappropriate shift patterns during scheduling.
sl: This document provides instructions for restricting user access to specific work patterns in the Roster Change screen within the Team Scheduler system using Pattern Types configuration in Back Office. The process involves three main sequential steps: first, creating a new pattern type code by navigating to CoreTime > System Params > Reference K-P > Pattern Types; second, assigning this pattern type to relevant work patterns through CoreTime > System Params > Work Patterns and setting the Pattern Type field in the Rostering section for each pattern; and third, allocating the pattern type to individual user accounts via CoreTime > System Params > System Users > Pattern Type Access, while ensuring the "No Pattern Type Restriction" option is not enabled for those users. This configuration controls which work patterns are visible and available to each system user when they access the Roster Change screen, preventing unauthorized viewing or assignment of restricted patterns. The document is primarily intended for administrators and system configurators who manage user permissions and work pattern availability in Team Scheduler environments. Related issues addressed include scenarios where users encounter errors stating "There are no patterns set up for this person" and problems with work pattern drop-down lists in both Portal and Back Office Shift Type functionality.

t: Create a work group in Back Office
s:
📌 Note: Plan your work groups before configuring. Break employees into blocks e.g. employees that do/do not generate timesheets, employees on the same shift type, employees expected to clock etc. Work Groups will fulfil the needs of a high % of employees.

ss: Work groups in CoreTime organize employees into logical blocks based on shared characteristics like timesheet generation, shift types, and payroll processing needs. Open this document when you need to set up a new work group in Back Office, configure which employees will have timesheets transferred to Core Pay or payroll interface files, and assign default holiday schemes and shift rosters. You'll use this process during initial system setup or whenever you need to create employee groupings that require consistent payroll, timekeeping, or scheduling rules. The document walks you through each configuration step, including options for waged employees whose hours feed into payroll versus salaried employees who don't.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for creating and configuring work groups in the Back Office system, which are used to organize employees into logical blocks based on characteristics such as timesheet generation requirements, shift types, or clocking expectations. The process begins by navigating to CoreTime > System Params > Work Groups, where administrators assign a meaningful code and description to the new work group and select default settings including Holiday Scheme and Shift Type, both of which can be overridden at the individual employee level if needed. The document addresses two distinct scenarios: Option A covers employees whose hours must transfer to payroll (such as waged staff), requiring selection of either Live Timesheets for direct Core Pay transfer or ASCII Timesheets for payroll interface files, along with activation of the Generate Timesheets indicator; Option B applies to non-payroll-tracked employees (such as salaried staff) where the Generate Timesheets indicator remains off. Additional configuration requirements include selecting appropriate Pay Frequency and Calculate Default Hours settings, designating a Working Time Directive Group from the applicable LOV, and enabling the Calculate Clockings checkbox in the General Parameters 2 section regardless of whether employees actually use clockings. This document is primarily used by Back Office administrators or HR personnel who need to establish standardized employee groupings for timesheet processing, payroll integration, and leave management, helping resolve issues such as hours not transferring to PeopleXD Payroll or missing public holidays in timesheets.

t: Configure work patterns
s:
You can configure Work Patterns in the WFM Admin Dashboard to define working hours and pay codes for your organisation. This guide provides step-by-step instructions to create a new Work Pattern and set standard hours accurately.

 

Steps to configure work patterns

Before you begin, ensure you hav...
ss: Work Patterns in the WFM Admin Dashboard let you define standard working hours and pay codes for your organisation. Use this guide when you need to create a new work pattern, set up standard hours accurately, and ensure those hours align with pay codes in your General Parameters. Open this if you're configuring workforce management settings, setting up employee schedules, or troubleshooting why hours aren't transferring correctly to PeopleXD Payroll. Follow the step-by-step instructions to add a work pattern code, populate mandatory fields, and configure standard hours.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on configuring Work Patterns within the WFM Admin Dashboard, enabling organizations to define working hours and pay codes for their workforce. The guide walks users through a specific step-by-step process that begins by accessing the WFM Admin Dashboard, navigating to WFM Configuration, and selecting the Work Patterns option to add a new work pattern. During configuration, users must enter a unique Code and Description, complete all mandatory fields in the work pattern details section, and activate the configuration by toggling on both the Active and Fill Basic Hours options before proceeding. After clicking OK, the Standard Hours configuration screen automatically opens, where users must enter the appropriate standard hours for the work pattern and save the settings. The document emphasizes a critical requirement that standard hours must align with default times and pay codes established in the General Parameters tab, including settings for early overtime, standard hours, and late overtime to maintain system consistency. This document is intended for WFM administrators and configuration managers who have been granted permission to manage configuration settings in the WFM Admin Dashboard and need to establish accurate working hour definitions that will subsequently transfer data to integrated systems like PeopleXD Payroll.

t: Configure breaks for a work pattern
s:
You can ensure your Work Patterns include the necessary breaks by reviewing and adding break details where missing. This guide walks you through the steps to verify and configure breaks in the Portal and Backoffice.

Check and add breaks to a Work Pattern in the Portal

ss: Work Patterns in the WFM Admin Dashboard and CoreTime require break configurations to ensure employees have scheduled break times and to prevent payroll or attendance calculation errors. This guide covers how to add and verify breaks in both the Portal (via WFM Admin Dashboard) and Backoffice (via CoreTime System Params). Open this document when you need to set up breaks for a Work Pattern, troubleshoot missing break times, or ensure compliance with break requirements before deploying schedules. You'll need WFM Admin or CoreTime modification permissions to complete these tasks.
sl: This document provides instructions for configuring and verifying breaks within work patterns using two different system interfaces: the Portal and Backoffice. The guide covers the complete process for the Portal route, which requires accessing the WFM Admin Dashboard, navigating to WFM Configuration, selecting the Work Patterns tile, using the search function to locate a specific work pattern, and then accessing the Breaks tab through the work pattern's 3-dot menu to add break details. For users working in Backoffice, the document outlines an alternative method through CoreTime, where administrators navigate to System Params, select Work Patterns, choose the desired pattern from the List Of Values (LOV), and add break details in the Breaks tab. Both processes require appropriate administrative permissions—specifically access to the WFM Admin Dashboard for Portal users and modification permissions in CoreTime for Backoffice users. The document addresses the critical business problem that omitting breaks from work patterns can result in employees lacking scheduled break times, which may negatively impact payroll calculations and attendance records. This guide is intended for workforce management administrators and system configurators responsible for maintaining accurate work pattern configurations across their organization.

t: Hours not calculating for a single employee on maintain hours
s:
There are 4 possible causes of this issue. To action this, see the resolutions below.

 

Employee has a Date Left entry

Hours will not calculate from this day forward.

Resolution: Confirm with HR team if the Date Left is correct. Remove or update if not.

Employee has a Start Date in advance of t...
ss: The Maintain Hours feature in CoreTime may fail to calculate hours for a single employee due to four common causes: an incorrect Date Left entry, a Start Date set in the future, misconfigured Work Patterns, or disabled overtime generation settings. Open this document if an employee's hours aren't appearing or calculating properly in Maintain Hours while other employees' hours process normally. The document walks through each potential cause and provides step-by-step resolutions, including how to verify employee dates with HR and configure Work Pattern settings in CoreTime's System Parameters. Use this guide when troubleshooting individual employee hour calculation issues before escalating to broader system problems.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving a specific issue where hours fail to calculate for an individual employee within the Maintain Hours function. The document identifies four distinct root causes and their corresponding resolutions: an incorrect or active Date Left entry that blocks hour calculations from that date forward, a Start Date configured in advance of the calculation period, an improperly configured Work Pattern for the relevant day or days, and a disabled Generate Overtime setting for the employee. To address Work Pattern configuration issues, users navigate to CoreTime, access System Params, select Work Patterns, query the employee's specific Work Pattern record, verify that Standard Hours are configured, and save any changes made. The document is designed for HR administrators and payroll professionals who manage employee hours and timekeeping data in the Access Group system, particularly when investigating why a single employee's hours are not appearing or calculating correctly in the Maintain Hours interface. By systematically checking each of these four potential causes and following the prescribed steps, users can identify and resolve the underlying reason preventing hours from being properly calculated and recorded for the affected employee.

t: Add a new department to your organisation's structure
s:
To reflect changes in your company, you can update your organisation structure, for example, to create a new department. To do this in PeopleXD Workforce Management, you need to create the relevant reference data, then update your structure setup.

🤓 Tip: You can also add new departments to your str...
ss: Adding a new department to your PeopleXD Workforce Management organisation structure requires two steps: first creating the department reference data through WFM Admin Dashboard, then adding it to your hierarchy via Data Centre Structure Setup. Open this document when your company has undergone restructuring or organizational changes that require a new department to be reflected in your system. The guide covers the specific menu navigation, field configuration, and toggle settings needed in both PeopleXD Workforce Management and People Management to complete the process.
sl: This document provides instructions for adding a new department to an organisation's structure within PeopleXD Workforce Management, covering both the creation of the department as reference data and its integration into the organisational hierarchy. The process begins in the WFM Admin Dashboard by navigating to WFM Configuration > Departments, where users click Add, complete the required fields, enable the Active toggle, and save the new department, with an optional Sensitive Unit toggle that requires granting additional access permissions. To make the newly created department accessible within the system, users must access the Data Centre from the dashboard menu, navigate to Structure Setup, locate the relevant structure's HIERARCHY, and expand it to find the appropriate hierarchy item. Once the correct hierarchy item is located, users access a three-dot menu to select Add, filter for linked items, search for the newly created reference data, and toggle on the Add to Hierarchy option before saving. The document notes that PeopleXD People Management offers an alternative method for adding new departments to an organisation structure. To enable department management functionality, system administrators must add specific menu options to user menu profiles, including CorePortal's Departments option and Web Services options such as Get analysiscode, Create bytype copy, Update bytype departments, and Delete bytype. This guide is intended for administrators and configuration managers responsible for maintaining and updating organisational structure within Access Group's PeopleXD workforce management system.

t: Set up menu profiles for team calendars and weekly work schedules
s:
Efficiently managing team calendars and timesheets in PeopleXD requires configuring the appropriate menu profiles and options. This guide provides step-by-step instructions for setting up these configurations for key functionalities such as Team Calendars and Weekly Work Schedule access.

ss: Menu profiles control which features employees and managers can access in PeopleXD, including Team Calendars and Weekly Work Schedules. This document walks you through configuring these profiles to enable Team Calendar functionality for both roles and activating specific menu options so employees can view their weekly work schedules directly in the Timesheets section. Open this guide when you're setting up PeopleXD access permissions and need to ensure your team can view calendars and timesheets without manual configuration for each user.
sl: This document provides configuration instructions for enabling Team Calendars and Weekly Work Schedule functionality within PeopleXD, a system used for managing team calendars and timesheets. The guide addresses two primary setup processes: configuring menu profiles to activate Team Calendars access for employees and managers, and enabling weekly work schedule visibility within the Timesheets section. For Team Calendars configuration, users are directed to reference the official Team Calendars Guide and navigate to the Menu Option Configuration section to identify the specific menu profiles and options required, then apply these settings to appropriate user roles. To enable weekly work schedule access in Employee Timesheets, administrators must open the Menu Profiles configuration tool in PeopleXD and add four specific menu options: MAIN_MENU.TIMESHEET_INPUT_WEEKLY_SCHEDULE_EMP, MAIN_MENU.TIMESHEET_INPUT_WEEKLY_SCHEDULE_EDIT, MAIN_MENU.TIMESHEET_INPUT_WEEKLY_SCHEDULE, and WS_TIMESHEETS_MENU.GET_WORKPATTERN_PROXY to an active menu profile. After adding these options, users must save the changes and assign the updated menu profile to relevant user groups to ensure employees can view and interact with their weekly schedules within the system. This document is typically used by PeopleXD administrators and system configuration managers who need to set up appropriate access controls and functionality for their organization's employees and managerial staff.

t: Manage work patterns, including deletion and inactivation?
s: Work patterns in PeopleXD are essential for defining employee schedules and operational workflows. However, there are specific limitations and processes to be aware of when managing these patterns. This provides an overview of how to handle work patterns, including setting them to inactive and under...
ss: Work patterns in PeopleXD define employee schedules and operational workflows, but they cannot be deleted once created. If you no longer need a work pattern, you must set it to inactive instead, which prevents it from being used in future scheduling while keeping it visible in the system for reference. Open this document when you need to deactivate an existing work pattern or understand why deletion isn't an option and what happens when you inactivate a pattern.
sl: This document provides guidance on managing work patterns in PeopleXD, a workforce management system, with specific focus on the permanent limitations around deletion and the inactivation process as the alternative solution. The document explains that work patterns cannot be deleted once created in PeopleXD, and instead users must set them to inactive status if they no longer need a pattern, which prevents future use while preserving historical data and references. To inactivate a work pattern, users navigate to the work pattern management section in PeopleXD, locate the desired pattern, and change its status to Inactive through the system interface. A key limitation emphasized throughout is that inactive work patterns remain permanently visible in the configuration or management interface and cannot be hidden, archived, or deleted, ensuring that all historical records stay accessible within the system. The document addresses common user scenarios such as accidentally created work patterns and clarifies in an FAQ section that no deletion option exists for resolving such mistakes, with inactivation being the only viable approach. This resource is intended for PeopleXD administrators and HR personnel responsible for scheduling configuration, operational workflow setup, and system maintenance, particularly those managing employee schedules and needing to maintain clean work pattern libraries while retaining audit trails.

t: Portal: Fix the work pattern drop-down list in Shift Type

ss: The work pattern drop-down list in Portal's Shift Type feature may not display available options when creating new shift types or assigning personal overrides. Use this document to enable No Data Entry Restriction or No Pattern Type Restriction for employees with MSS access type, which will restore the drop-down functionality and allow you to complete shift type setup and personal override assignments.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving issues with the work pattern drop-down list in Shift Type within the Portal component of the CoreTime system. The document addresses two distinct scenarios: the inability to select a work pattern when creating a new shift type, and the inability to assign a personal override to a shift type due to a blank drop-down list. For the first issue, users must navigate to Security > Setup > CoreTime System Users, query or create an employee record with Access Type: MSS, then enable the "No Data Entry Restriction" setting under Access Privileges. For the second issue, the same navigation path applies but instead requires enabling "No Pattern Type Restriction" under Pattern Type Access. A prerequisite for both fixes is ensuring that the employee has an existing CoreTime System User record with the appropriate Access Type designation, and creating one if necessary using the employee number as the username. The document is intended for Portal administrators or users with access to update security settings who need to grant proper permissions to employees experiencing drop-down list visibility problems in shift type configuration. Once the relevant restrictions are removed through these security configuration steps, the Work Pattern drop-down list should display available values correctly and allow personal overrides to be assigned as needed.

t: Back office: Fix the work pattern drop-down list in Shift Type
s:
In PeopleXD Workforce Management, the Work Pattern drop-down list in Shift Type may not work as expected when you are creating a new work pattern or assigning days to a shift type. You may also find that you cannot assign a personal override because the drop-down list has no values to display.

This...
ss: The Work Pattern drop-down list in PeopleXD Shift Type may fail to display values or allow personal overrides when an employee's CoreTime system user account lacks required access settings. This document covers how to fix the issue by enabling either "No Data Entry Restriction" (when creating new work patterns) or "No Pattern Type Restriction" (when assigning personal overrides) in CoreTime System Users. Open this if you're setting up shift types or personal overrides in PeopleXD and the Work Pattern drop-down appears empty or non-functional. You'll need access to update system parameters in Back office to apply these fixes.
sl: This document provides instructions for resolving issues with the Work Pattern drop-down list in the Shift Type section of PeopleXD Workforce Management, specifically when creating new work patterns or assigning personal overrides to shift types. The problem typically occurs when an employee's CoreTime system user account is missing required access settings, resulting in either an empty or non-functional drop-down list. The document addresses two distinct scenarios: first, when users cannot select a work pattern while setting up a shift type due to the "No Data Entry Restriction" setting not being enabled, and second, when users cannot assign a personal override because the "No Pattern Type Restriction" setting is not enabled. Both issues are resolved through the same navigation pathway in Back office—accessing CoreTime, navigating to System Params, then System Users—where administrators must query or create a system user record with Access Type: MSS and enable the appropriate restriction setting. The document emphasizes that system user accounts must exist before access privileges can be applied, and provides a tip highlighting this prerequisite step. Once the relevant restrictions are removed through these Back office configuration changes, the Work Pattern drop-down list should display available values correctly and allow personal override assignments as needed.

t: Portal: Add a personal override to work patterns from the People Management dashboard
s:

ss: Personal work pattern overrides in PeopleXD Workforce Management allow HR admins and managers to adjust employee schedules from the People Management dashboard in Portal. sl: This document provides instructions for HR administrators and managers in PeopleXD Workforce Management who need to grant employees the ability to have personal overrides applied to their work patterns through the People Management dashboard in Portal. This configuration change must be saved to take effect, and once completed, HR admins and managers will be able to add personal overrides to work patterns for that employee from the People Management dashboard. The document addresses a specific access control scenario where restricted pattern type settings would prevent personal overrides, and it helps resolve situations where managers need flexibility in applying work pattern exceptions to individual employees. Related resources are provided for troubleshooting common issues such as "There are no patterns set up for this person" errors and managing work pattern drop-down lists in both Portal and Back office environments.

sl: This document explains how HR administrators and managers can add a personal override to an employee's work pattern using PeopleXD Workforce Management's Back office system from the HR Administrator dashboard. t: Error – you are not allowed to modify this personal shift override
s:
If you see the error “You are not allowed to modify this personal shift override”, it means the system is preventing the override because the shift falls outside the current open calendar period.
Shift overrides can only be applied to shifts that fall within the current open period or in a future pe...
ss: Personal shift overrides in the scheduling system fail when you try to apply them to shifts outside the current open calendar period—typically shifts dated in the past or in closed periods. This error prevents overrides because the system only allows modifications to shifts within active or future periods. To resolve it, assign a new shift with a date effective that falls within the open period, then apply the override to that newly assigned shift. Check your system calendar's open period settings before attempting shift overrides to avoid errors and rework.
sl: This document provides guidance for resolving the error message "You are not allowed to modify this personal shift override," which occurs when users attempt to apply shift overrides to shifts that fall outside the current open calendar period in the system. The error arises specifically when the date effective on a shift is before the current open period on the system calendar, when the system calendar does not allow edits or overrides for past or closed periods, or when a personal shift override is being added to a shift that is no longer editable. To resolve this issue, users must navigate to the employee's profile and assign a new shift with a date effective that falls within or after the current open period, then save the new shift before applying the personal shift override to the newly assigned shift. The document emphasizes that the system fundamentally does not allow overrides on shifts dated before the current open period, and users should always ensure the date effective is within an open calendar period before applying overrides. For users who need to make changes to historical shifts, the document recommends contacting the system administrator to review calendar settings. This resource is primarily used by payroll, human resources, or shift management personnel who work within a workforce management system and frequently encounter restrictions when attempting to modify shift schedules.

t: Delete unused or mistakenly created shift types?
s: Managing shift types effectively is crucial for maintaining an organised workforce schedule. If you have unused or mistakenly created shift types in PeopleXD, you can delete them to keep your system clean and efficient. This article provides a step-by-step guide to deleting shift types, including pr...
ss: Keeping your PeopleXD shift types clean requires removing unused or mistakenly created entries that are no longer needed. You can delete a shift type only if it has never been assigned to any employees, and you must have the appropriate permissions in your user account. This guide walks you through locating the shift type in PeopleXD, accessing the delete option from the menu, and troubleshooting common issues like missing delete buttons or permission errors. Use this resource when you need to streamline your workforce management system by removing redundant shift configurations.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide for deleting unused or mistakenly created shift types in the PeopleXD workforce management system to maintain an organized and efficient schedule database. The document outlines two critical prerequisites that must be satisfied before deletion: the shift type must have no assignments to any employees or work groups (the system will block deletion if the shift has ever been used), and the user must possess the necessary permissions, which may require specific menu profiles or roles assigned by a system administrator. The deletion process itself is straightforward—users navigate to the shift types list, locate the target shift type, click the three-dot menu option beside it, select Delete, and confirm the deletion when prompted. The document addresses common troubleshooting scenarios, specifically explaining that the Delete option will only appear if the shift type remains unassigned to all employees, and that if the Delete option is not visible, users should verify both the unassigned status and their permission levels. For users who encounter permission-related issues preventing deletion, the document advises contacting the system administrator to update the user profile with the necessary access rights. This guide is primarily intended for PeopleXD administrators, managers, or designated users responsible for maintaining shift schedules and system configuration who need to clean up the shift type database after discovering unused or accidentally created entries.

t: Assign shifts to employees without fixed schedules in Workforce Management
s:
You can manage shifts for employees who do not have a fixed schedule in PeopleXD's Workforce Management module. Use REST shifts as a default placeholder, manually override shifts for specific working days, or configure Flexi Work Patterns for more advanced scheduling needs.

 

REST shifts as a defa...
ss: Workforce Management in PeopleXD allows you to schedule employees who don't have fixed shift patterns by using REST shifts as default placeholders and manually overriding them for specific working days. You can customize individual shifts directly in the Roster screen or Weekly Work Schedule, or set up Flexi Work Patterns for more complex scheduling needs where employees work flexible days without a fixed structure. Open this document if you need to assign shifts to casual, flexible, or variable-hour staff and want to understand your options for managing their schedules efficiently.
sl: This document provides guidance on managing shift assignments for employees without fixed schedules within PeopleXD's Workforce Management module, covering three distinct approaches to flexible scheduling. The document explains how to use REST shifts as a default placeholder for employees without fixed shift patterns, ensuring every employee always has a shift type assigned while allowing for manual adjustments as needed. For employees who require shifts on specific working days, the document outlines the manual override process: accessing either the Roster screen or the Weekly Work Schedule (found under Timesheet Input), selecting the employee, changing the default REST shift to the required working pattern for specified days, and clicking Save. For more complex scheduling scenarios where employees can work any five days out of seven without a predetermined structure, the document introduces Flexi Work Patterns as an advanced configuration option that provides greater control over flexible arrangements, though it notes that this feature requires additional setup coordinated with a system administrator using PeopleXD configuration guides. This document is primarily intended for workforce managers and schedulers who need to create and maintain rosters for employees with variable or non-fixed schedules, particularly those working in environments requiring day-to-day scheduling flexibility or complex work pattern arrangements.

t: Portal: Grant user access using System Users
s:

ss: Grant System Users access to work groups and departments in WFM so they can view employee calendars and relevant dashboards. Open this document when you need to set up or modify which work groups and departments a System User can access, or when configuring calendar viewing permissions. Note that the system cannot restrict calendar access alone; if a user has access to other dashboards like People Management or Payroll, they may also see sensitive information such as salary details.
sl: This document provides instructions for granting Portal users access to work groups and departments through system user configuration, which directly controls their permissions for viewing employee calendars based on assigned Work Group and Department combinations. The process involves two sequential steps: first adding work groups or departments to a user's profile, then granting access permissions through the WFM Admin Dashboard. To add work groups or departments for calendar access, administrators navigate from the dashboard menu to WFM Admin Dashboard, then WFM Configuration, select WFM System User Configuration, click the three-dot menu next to the relevant employee, select View/Edit and the company, then click Access Details to add the required work groups and departments before saving. Super users can grant access to all work groups and department combinations by following the same navigation path but selecting "Access All Groups / Departments" from the Actions menu under Access Details, which also applies to calendar viewing permissions. The document highlights a critical system limitation: the portal cannot restrict access solely to calendars, meaning users with access to other dashboards such as People Management or Payroll may view sensitive information like salary details, requiring administrators to control broader dashboard and data access permissions rather than relying on calendar-specific restrictions. This guide is essential for WFM administrators and super users who need to configure employee access levels and manage calendar visibility across departments and work groups in the workforce management system.

t: Configure user access privileges

Additional privileges govern specific capabilities such as approving hours, modifying clockings, accessing historical data, managing leave requests, and entering medical certificates. Open this document when setting up a new system user, troubleshooting access or visibility issues, or defining what actions specific team members are permitted to perform in your time and attendance system.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on configuring user access privileges in CoreTime, a workforce management and time and attendance system, covering both the Portal interface (WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Configuration > WFM System Users Configuration) and the Back Office system (CoreTime > System Params > System Users > Access Privileges). The document describes how administrators can enable, assign, and manage specific access privileges through the Access Privileges tab, including critical configuration for Team Area Access, which determines which employee data users can view in the Roster module, and menu profile options such as WRKMGMT_MENU.WRKMGMTVIEW that control editing capabilities. It details over twenty distinct access privileges that control user permissions across various functions, including HR User status for viewing HR-Only pay codes, approval and sign-off capabilities for hours worked, historical data entry and modification rights through features like Maintain Historical Clockings and Maintain Historical Hours (subject to open rolling periods), and administrative functions such as Leave Request Admin access and Medical Certificate entry. The document addresses common configuration problems such as users unable to see employee data in the Roster module due to missing team area assignments, and view-only access issues that can be resolved through menu profile adjustments. System administrators and HR personnel use this document to properly configure user permissions based on role requirements, ensuring users have appropriate access to work groups, departments, pay codes, and time and attendance functions while maintaining data security and approval workflows. Key indicators and toggles discussed include restrictions based on company assignment, automatic hour approval settings (which the document notes is not recommended), restrictions on modifying automated clockings versus view-only access, and the ability to override historical data entry restrictions or refresh work group/department access when employee assignments change.

ss: Prevent sick leave absences from being recorded on days directly before or after annual leave by configuring Adjoining Days Validation in CoreTime's Back Office Pay Codes settings. Use this feature when you need to enforce restrictions on specific pay codes so that users cannot book sick leave adjacent to annual leave days. Navigate to System Params, select your target pay code, enable Apply Validation under Adjoining Days Validation, and set the Warning Level to "Stop" to block the absence entry. This configuration helps maintain accurate leave records and prevents abuse of consecutive leave patterns.
sl: This document provides instructions for configuring a system restriction in Back Office that prevents sick leave absences from being recorded on days directly before or after annual leave by using Adjoining Days Validation settings. The process takes place within CoreTime's System Params section, specifically in the Pay Codes configuration area, where users navigate to select a specific pay code using the List icon in the Pay Code field. To implement this restriction, users must locate the Adjoining Days Validation section, check the Apply Validation box, and then select "Stop" from the Warning Level drop-down menu, which will block any attempted absence entry that violates the rule. The configuration requires a second step where users select additional pay codes from the Pay Code List icon—these represent the pay codes on which sick leave cannot be booked on adjoining days to the selected pay code. After configuring both the primary pay code and the adjoining restriction pay codes, users save the changes by clicking the Save icon to make the restriction active in the system. This document is typically used by Back Office administrators or payroll configuration staff who need to enforce organizational leave policies that prevent employees from booking sick leave immediately before or after scheduled annual leave, thereby closing a potential loophole in absence recording.

sl: This document explains how to customize the Admin Dashboard filter settings in the Access Group system to display different organizational categories instead of the default Work Group option. t: Create a Period Closure

ss: Period closure in Workforce Management (WFM) allows administrators to pre-book company shutdown periods—such as Christmas or summer closures—and automatically deduct the relevant leave from employee entitlements. Setting up a period closure requires four sequential steps: creating the closure with dates and pay code details, creating and configuring a criteria group to define which employees are affected, assigning that criteria group to the closure, and retrieving the employee list to confirm participation. Use this process when your organization needs to schedule planned closures and ensure leave is properly deducted from staff balances during those periods.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide for administrators to set up and manage period closures in Workforce Management (WFM), which allows pre-booking of company closure periods such as Christmas or summer shutdowns and automatically deducts relevant leave from staff entitlements. The document outlines four sequential steps that must be completed in order for the closure period to function correctly: creating a period closure through the WFM Admin Dashboard's Period Closure tab where administrators fill in closure details such as name, dates, and Pay Code; creating a Criteria Group by accessing the three-dot menu next to the relevant Period Closure, selecting Assign Criteria Groups and Manage Criteria Groups, then adding criteria with specific names and types before selecting required reference data and moving values to the Assigned column; assigning the Criteria Group by repeating the navigation to the Period Closure tab and three-dot menu, then clicking Assign New Group to select the required Criteria Group; and retrieving employees through the Retrieve Employees option in the three-dot menu to review the employee list and toggle the Exclude option to remove specific employees from the closure before clicking Assign. The document also references related troubleshooting articles addressing potential errors, such as the message "This is the last period on the balance calendar. Future periods must be created before a period end can be run," as well as guidance on extending the company period, PayWise+ balance issues from XD, and prerequisite steps for running balance period end. sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre provides a comprehensive guide for configuring and implementing Pay Code Groups in the WFM (Workforce Management) system, which controls employee access to specific pay codes for leave booking and payroll activities. The guide covers two primary processes: first, creating a Pay Code Group by navigating to the WFM Admin Dashboard, selecting WFM Configuration, clicking the Pay Groups tile, and then using the Add Group function to enter a Group Code and Description. Once a group is created, administrators add individual pay codes to it through the Add function, with the option to mark codes as View Only using a toggle switch, and can repeat this process to include multiple pay codes before saving. The document emphasizes an important distinction that creating a Pay Code Group does not automatically assign it to employees, requiring manual assignment as a separate step. To assign a Pay Code Group to an employee, users access the People Management Dashboard, use the Command Centre widget to locate employees, navigate to the Pay Codes Access Groups tab within an employee's profile, and select the group from a drop-down menu while specifying the Assignment Level as either Appointment (for role-specific assignment) or Person (for universal application). This document is primarily used by WFM administrators and HR personnel who need to control pay code visibility and access across their workforce to ensure employees can only book leave and perform payroll activities appropriate to their roles.

t: No Access to Company and Work-Groups on Calculate Hours
s:
If an employee cannot see Company and Work-Groups when using Calculate Hours, it is likely due to missing permissions.

Follow the steps below to check and resolve this.

 

Check and Update MSS Access Type

In Portal, go to the WFM Admin Dashboard.

Select WFM Configuration.

Click on WFM System Us...
ss: When employees can't see Company and Work-Groups in the Calculate Hours feature, it's usually caused by missing or incorrect permissions in WFM. To fix this, access the WFM Admin Dashboard in Portal, navigate to WFM System Users Configuration, and verify the employee has an MSS (Manager Self Service) Access Type with both "Allow Historical Calculation" and "Allow Future Calculation" enabled—create this access type if it doesn't exist. If you don't have permission to access WFM System Users Configuration yourself, enable the WFM_SYSTEM_USERS_CONFIG menu profile through User Management in Security. Once the correct access is assigned, employees will be able to view Company and Work-Groups in Calculate Hours.
sl: This document addresses a common access issue where employees cannot view Company and Work-Groups within the Calculate Hours function, typically caused by insufficient system permissions. The primary resolution process involves navigating to the Portal's WFM Admin Dashboard, accessing WFM Configuration, and then opening WFM System Users Configuration to query the employee's record and verify their access settings. If the employee has an MSS (Manager Self Service) Access Type assigned, administrators must ensure that both "Allow Historical Calculation" and "Allow Future Calculation" options are enabled; if MSS access is not assigned, it must be created with these same options enabled before saving. For users who lack permission to access WFM System Users Configuration themselves, the document provides an alternative procedure involving the Portal's Security section, User Management tools, and Menu Profiles, where administrators can search for and enable the WFM_SYSTEM_USERS_CONFIG menu profile before logging out and back in to refresh permissions. Once the correct MSS Access Type and calculation permissions are properly configured, employees will regain the ability to view Company and Work-Groups in the Calculate Hours interface. The document serves primarily system administrators, WFM (Workforce Management) configuration managers, and Portal security personnel who need to troubleshoot and resolve access restrictions for their employee base.

ss: Reason codes and reason code groups are configuration settings in CoreTime and the WFM Admin Dashboard that categorize and track the purposes behind employee absences, leave requests, and pay code usage. This document covers how to create individual reason codes, bundle them into reason code groups, and link those groups to specific pay codes in your system. Use this guide when you need to set up new absence categories, organize existing codes into logical groupings, or connect reason codes to your payroll and time and attendance processes.
sl: This document provides comprehensive instructions for setting up and managing reason codes and reason code groups within Access Group's CoreTime workforce management system, covering both back office and portal-based configuration methods. The document outlines four primary processes: creating reason code groups in the back office by navigating to CoreTime > System Params > Reference Q-Z > Reason Code Group and entering a unique code, description, and selecting relevant reason codes from a List of Values (LOV); creating individual reason codes through the WFM Admin Dashboard by accessing WFM Configuration > Reason Code and Groups > Reason Code tab and clicking Add; creating reason code groups in the portal via WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Configuration > Reason Code Groups tab, where users can add groups and assign multiple reason codes to each group; and applying configured reason code groups to specific pay codes by querying the relevant pay code, clicking View/Edit Pay Code, and adding the reason group in the Summary section. The procedures help resolve scenarios where users need to categorize absences, leaves, or pay adjustments with specific codes and groups for better workforce management tracking and reporting. This document is typically used by system administrators, payroll managers, and workforce management configuration specialists who need to establish and maintain the foundational reason code structure that employees and managers will later reference when creating leave requests or recording attendance-related activities within the system.

t: Portal Error: Entry/Modification/Deletion of the data during this period is restricted
s:
When deleting an absence record in the Portal for a historic period, you might see this error message:

'Entry/Modification/Deletion of the data during this period is restricted...'

This happens because the system is set to block changes to data from past periods to protect payroll integrity. Howev...
ss: Portal absence record deletions are blocked for historic periods by design to protect payroll integrity, triggering an "Entry/Modification/Deletion of the data during this period is restricted" error message. You can resolve this restriction by enabling the Ignore Data Entry Restriction access privilege for the user through WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Configuration > WFM System Users Configuration. Open this document when you need to delete past absence records in the Portal and encounter the data restriction error, or when you're configuring user permissions to allow historic data modifications. Note that deleting historic absence data can impact payroll records and reporting, so exercise caution when enabling this privilege.
sl: This document explains the error message "Entry/Modification/Deletion of the data during this period is restricted" that appears when users attempt to delete absence records from past periods in the Portal, and provides step-by-step instructions to resolve it. The error occurs as a system safeguard designed to protect payroll integrity by blocking modifications to historical data. To resolve this issue, administrators must enable the "Ignore Data Entry Restriction" access privilege for the affected user by navigating through WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Configuration > WFM System Users Configuration, locating the employee record, selecting View/Edit, accessing the Access Privileges section, and enabling the corresponding checkbox before saving changes. Once this privilege is activated, the user gains the ability to delete historic absence records in the Portal without encountering the restriction error. The document cautions that deleting historical data carries risks, as such deletions can negatively impact payroll records and reporting accuracy. This document is primarily used by WFM administrators and system managers who need to manage user access permissions and troubleshoot data entry restrictions for employees working with absence management in workforce management systems.

When populating Work Group details, users must enter a unique code and description, select the relevant Company from a dropdown menu, and complete all mandatory fields marked with an asterisk, while also enabling the Calculate Clockings and Active toggles before clicking OK to save. After the Work Group is created, users can access additional configuration options through tabs in the left-hand menu to further customize Scheduling rules, Overtime settings, Additional pay options, and Clocking behaviour according to organizational needs. You can process hours individually, for selected employees, or in bulk (up to 600 records at a time), with options to reject hours and add reasons or notes as needed. Open this document when you need step-by-step instructions for accessing the Sign Off Hours section, locating specific employees, and completing the approval and sign-off toggles. Use it as a reference if you're managing timesheet approvals or troubleshooting why the approve or sign-off buttons aren't appearing in your dashboard.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide for managers and administrators who need to approve and sign off employee hours within PeopleXD Workforce Management (WFM). The process is divided into two distinct stages: first reviewing and approving hours, then signing them off as a separate action. To approve hours, users navigate to the WFM Admin Dashboard via the dashboard menu, select Sign Off Hours and the relevant calendar, click Actions Required to find the employee, access the Sign Off Detail through the three-dot menu, and toggle the Approve or Reject option for each item while optionally adding reasons and narrative notes before saving. For signing off hours, administrators return to the WFM Admin Dashboard, select Sign Off Hours and the calendar, then proceed to the Pending Sign Off section where they can process individual employees by searching and using the three-dot menu, select multiple employees via checkboxes, or use the Bulk Sign Off feature to process up to 600 records at once. The document addresses common issues such as access permission errors and missing approval buttons, and references related troubleshooting articles covering problems like overtime hours not displaying and hours missing from the Manager Dashboard approval screens. t: How to activate or de-activate a workgroup
s:
You can activate or de-activate a workgroup by updating its status in the WFM Admin Dashboard. This controls whether the workgroup is available for use.

Note that a workgroup can only be activated or de-activated if there are no active employees assigned to it.

 

How to activate or de-activate a ...
ss: Workgroup activation and de-activation in the WFM Admin Dashboard controls whether a workgroup is available for scheduling and operations. Use this process when you need to enable or disable a workgroup's status through the WFM Configuration section. You can only change a workgroup's active status if there are no active employees currently assigned to it. Open this article when you're managing workgroup availability or need to remove a workgroup from active use.
sl: This document provides instructions for managing workgroup availability within the WFM Admin Dashboard by activating or deactivating workgroups based on organizational needs. The process is straightforward and involves navigating to the WFM Admin Dashboard, selecting WFM Configuration, clicking on Work Groups, querying the specific workgroup to be modified, and then toggling the Active indicator slider either ON to activate or OFF to deactivate the workgroup. A critical prerequisite for performing this action is that the workgroup must have no active employees assigned to it—this restriction prevents deactivation of workgroups that are currently in use, ensuring system integrity and preventing operational disruptions. The document is designed for WFM administrators and system managers who need to control workgroup availability as part of workforce management configuration and maintenance tasks. The related articles section references common issues and related configurations, such as managing leavers in CorePersonnel, configuring pay code groups, and handling employee access issues, suggesting this document fits within a broader suite of workforce management administrative procedures. This document helps resolve scenarios where administrators need to retire unused workgroups or temporarily disable them while maintaining active employee assignments elsewhere in the system.

t: How to extend the company period
s:

How to extend the company period

From the dashboard menu, click WFM Admin Dashboard.

Click WFM Configuration, then select Company and Ca...
ss: Extending a company period in WFM involves adding a new calendar period through the WFM Admin Dashboard to keep scheduling and payroll timelines running without gaps. You'll navigate to WFM Configuration, find the Company and Calendar Config section, and use the Generate Period function to create and save the new period. Open this document when you need to maintain continuous company operations across scheduling cycles or when your current calendar period is about to expire. This process ensures your payroll and workforce management systems stay aligned without interruption.
sl: This document explains how to extend a company period within the Access Group system by generating and adding a new calendar period, which prevents interruptions to the organization's scheduling and payroll operations. The process is accessed through the WFM Admin Dashboard, which users reach from the main dashboard menu by clicking WFM Admin Dashboard. Once in the dashboard, users navigate to WFM Configuration and select Company and Calendar Config to view the list of companies. Users then locate their relevant company and click the View/Edit button next to it to access the company's configuration settings. The next step involves clicking on Company Calendar Period, followed by clicking the Generate Period button to initiate the creation of a new period. Users must fill in the required information fields for the new period before clicking OK to save the changes and officially extend the company period. This document is typically used by workforce management administrators or system configuration staff who are responsible for maintaining accurate scheduling and payroll timelines. The related articles referenced suggest there are additional period extension scenarios, including user-defined period calendars, non-cycle shifts, system calendars in Portal, and preparatory steps for balance period end processes.

t: How to Set Up Auto Advance Periods
s:
The Auto Advance Periods feature ensures that your system calendars automatically stay up to date.
When enabled, the system will check if any calendars are in the past. If they are, it will automatically advance them by one period.

This helps prevent calendars from falling behind the actual date.

ss: Auto Advance Periods automatically keeps your WFM system calendars current by checking for outdated periods and advancing them by one period to prevent them from falling behind the actual date. You configure this feature in the WFM Admin Dashboard under WFM Configuration > Company and Calendar Config, where you set the day of the week and time you want the auto-advance to run. Open this document if you need to enable automatic calendar updates so your periods stay synchronized with real dates without manual intervention.
sl: This document provides instructions for configuring the Auto Advance Periods feature, which automatically maintains up-to-date system calendars by detecting and advancing any calendars that have fallen behind the current date. The setup process is straightforward and involves navigating through the WFM Admin Dashboard to access WFM Configuration, then locating and selecting the Company and Calendar Config tile followed by the Auto Advance Periods option. Users must click Add to create a new auto advance configuration, at which point a pop-up window prompts them to specify two key settings: the day of the week on which the automatic advancement should occur and the specific time the process should run. Once these parameters are selected and confirmed by clicking OK, the system will continuously monitor calendars and automatically advance any periods that fall into the past according to the configured schedule. This document is typically used by WFM (Workforce Management) administrators or system configuration personnel who need to ensure calendar accuracy and prevent operational delays caused by outdated period settings. The related articles referenced suggest this feature works within a broader system of calendar management tools, including options to extend user-defined periods, rollback system calendars, and complete period-end balance processes.

sl: This document provides a step-by-step guide for granting users access to the WFM Admin Dashboard through the Portal by updating their menu profiles. The process requires navigating to Security > User Management within the Portal interface, where administrators can search for and locate the specific user account that needs to be updated. Within Menu Profiles, users must search for WFM-related options and enable all menu profiles associated with WFM functionality. s:

ss: User defined periods in Access People XD's system calendar can be rolled back when a completed period needs to be reopened for data corrections or additional transactions. This process involves navigating to CoreTime, accessing System Calendars through System Params, and unchecking the Completed checkbox for the periods you want to reopen. Open this document when you need to reverse a period closure in your company's calendar or restore access to a period that was previously marked as finished.
sl: This document provides instructions for rolling back user-defined periods in Access People XD's system calendar when a completed period requires reopening for data corrections or additional transaction processing. The process is accessed by navigating to CoreTime in Access People XD, then proceeding through System Params to Calendars and selecting System Calendars. Users must identify the relevant company by clicking the question mark symbol and selecting from available options, then navigate to User Defined Periods and use another question mark symbol next to Calendar Code to select the specific calendar code requiring adjustment. The core task involves locating the completed periods in the displayed list and unchecking the Completed checkbox for the future periods that need to be rolled back. Once the necessary checkboxes have been unchecked, users must click Save to confirm and apply their changes to the system calendar. This document is intended for Access People XD users—typically payroll administrators or system managers—who need to reopen closed periods due to data errors, missing transactions, or other business requirements. The document also references related functionality including extending user-defined period calendars, rolling back calendar periods for balances, and advancing the system calendar without using the advance period function.

Without extending these calendars before year-end, you may encounter errors like "Failed Contact Support" when generating timesheets. Open this document if you need step-by-step instructions for adding the new year to your yearly calendar (via Calendar Years) and weekly calendar (via Generate Period). sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre explains how to extend the system calendar in PeopleXD to prevent errors such as "Failed Contact Support" when generating timesheets, and it covers the procedures for updating both yearly and weekly calendar types to cover the next calendar year. The document emphasizes that users should complete these extension steps before the start of the new year to avoid service interruptions. To extend the yearly calendar, users navigate to CoreTime > System Params > Calendars > System Calendars, enter the relevant company number, click Calendar Years, and then add the year, start date, and number of weeks in the next available row before saving. To extend the weekly calendar, users follow a similar navigation path (CoreTime > System Params > Calendars > System Calendars), enter the company number, and click Generate Period to specify the final week of the new year using the week number format (for example, 202552 for the last week of 2025) in the End Period field before clicking OK and Save. This guide is intended for back office administrators and configuration users who manage PeopleXD's timekeeping systems and need to ensure continuous calendar coverage across fiscal years. The document also references related processes including extending user-defined period calendars, generating timesheets, advancing the system calendar, completing balance period end procedures, and rolling back the system calendar.

t: Migration to the new PeopleXD Ideas Portal
s:
As part of our continued efforts to improve the way we collect and action feedback from our PeopleXD clients, we are migrating to a new Ideas Portal hosted within the Access Aha! environment.

 

This new portal provides a more modern interface, enhanced tracking features, and a stronger foundation ...
ss: The PeopleXD Ideas Portal is moving to a new platform hosted in Access Aha! on 30th June 2025, offering a modern interface with enhanced tracking and AI-assisted idea prioritisation. Ideas submitted in the last 12 months or with 10+ votes will automatically transfer to the new portal, while older ideas will be retained internally by the product team. Open this document if you need to access the new portal, understand what's changing from the legacy system, or find instructions for registering and submitting ideas. Use this guide if you're having trouble locating previously submitted ideas or need help logging in to the new portal.
sl: This document guides PeopleXD clients through the migration from a legacy Ideas Portal to a new portal hosted within the Access Aha! environment, which launches on 30th June 2025 when the old portal is permanently retired. The new portal offers a modern interface with enhanced tracking features, improved two-way communication capabilities, and AI-assisted idea prioritisation, serving as the single location for all PeopleXD idea submissions going forward. Ideas submitted in the last 12 months or containing 10 or more votes will be automatically transferred to the new portal, while older ideas meeting neither criterion will remain with the product team internally but won't appear in the portal. Users can access the new portal either by following an invitation email (automatically sent to those who submitted or voted on ideas in the past 12 months with pre-created accounts) or by manually registering on the site using the Sign up button and entering their work email address and name. Once registered, users can browse and vote on existing ideas, submit new ideas, and follow ideas to track their progress and status changes through the portal interface. The document addresses the troubleshooting scenario where users cannot locate previously submitted ideas by recommending they search with potentially modified titles or categories, or resubmit the idea as a new entry, and directs users experiencing technical issues to contact support through a case system or their customer success manager.
