t: Create a new team area
s:
You can create new team areas to organise your workforce structure within Workforce Management. Team areas help you group employees logically and manage scheduling more effectively. After creating a team area, you'll need to link it to a parent team before you can assign employees to it.

⚠️Importan...
ss: Creating team areas in Workforce Management helps you organize your workforce structure and manage scheduling more effectively by grouping employees logically. This process requires administrator permissions and involves two main steps: setting up the team area in WFM Configuration with a code and description, then linking it to a parent team so employees can be assigned to it. Open this document when you need to establish a new organizational grouping in your WFM Admin Dashboard or restructure how your workforce is divided across teams.
sl: This document provides instructions for creating and configuring new team areas within Workforce Management (WFM) to organize workforce structure and improve scheduling management. The document requires users to have appropriate administrator permissions to access the WFM Configuration area and describes a two-part process beginning with opening the WFM Admin Dashboard, navigating to WFM Configuration, selecting Team Area Structure, and clicking the Add Team Area button where users must enter a Code and Description before saving. The second part of the process involves linking the newly created team area to a parent team, which is a necessary step before employees can be assigned to the team area; this is accomplished by locating the parent team in Team Area Structure, clicking the three dots menu next to the team name, selecting Add Child Team, choosing the created team area from the Team Area drop-down menu, and saving the changes. The document addresses a common workflow scenario where administrators need to organize employees logically within the system and emphasizes that choosing clear and consistent naming formats for team area codes will facilitate future management. This guide is primarily intended for WFM administrators who are responsible for configuring organizational structure and managing the assignment of employees to appropriate team areas within the system.

t: Set up job title mappings in Workforce Management
s:
Job Title Mapping lets administrators group multiple job title variants under one standard reference title in Workforce Management. These variations often occur due to different employment types, legacy setups, or workforce pool structures.

Once configured, all mapped titles are treated as equivale...
ss: Job Title Mapping in Workforce Management lets you consolidate multiple job title variations—created by different employment types, legacy systems, or workforce structures—under a single standard reference title. Once configured, all mapped titles are treated as equivalent in Required vs Rostered calculations, giving you more accurate staffing coverage visibility across your workforce. Open this document if you need to group job title variants together in WFM, standardize how titles are counted in scheduling calculations, or manage title consolidation in the WFM Admin Dashboard. This feature is available to UK and Irish clients using Workforce Management.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide to configuring Job Title Mapping in Workforce Management, a feature that allows administrators to consolidate multiple job title variants into a single standard reference title for more accurate staffing analysis. The feature is available exclusively to UK and Irish clients and helps resolve inconsistencies that arise from different employment types, legacy system setups, or varied workforce pool structures. To access Job Title Mapping, users navigate to the WFM Admin Dashboard, select WFM Configuration from the left-hand navigation menu, then choose Roster Job Title Mapping under Roster Configuration Settings, or alternatively search for "mapping" in the search bar. The Job Title Mapping form contains two required fields: Job Title (the variant to be consolidated, selected from a dropdown list) and Mapped Job Title (the reference title that variants map to), with job title codes displayed beneath each title for reference. Creating a new mapping involves clicking Add, selecting the Job Title variant and its corresponding Mapped Job Title from dropdowns, then clicking OK, with the new mapping taking effect immediately. The document also covers deletion procedures, warning administrators that removing a mapping stops job titles from being grouped together and reverts Required vs Rostered calculations to treat each job title separately, requiring users to locate the mapping, select Delete on that row, and confirm with Yes. The underlying system references the menu option ROS_CONF_MENU.ROSTER_JOB_TITLE_MAPPING and includes webservice parent links for API integration with job title lookup and mapping operations.

t: Error: [Pay Code] must be entered in XXX days segments
s:

Query the Work Pattern.

Click Mis...
ss: Pay code entry in WFM requires requests to be submitted in specific day segments (full, half, quarter, or custom), and this error occurs when the balance setup or work pattern configuration doesn't match the leave request being submitted. Resolve this by checking three key areas: verifying the Work Pattern Full Day Value matches the Default Hours in WFM Configuration, ensuring the Balance Segment is set to 'None' instead of restricting segments, or confirming the employee's work pattern has sufficient Default Hours for the requested absence type. Open this document when you receive the error message "Pay Code must be entered in XXX days segments" and need step-by-step instructions to troubleshoot the underlying WFM Admin configuration or employee balance settings.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving the error message "[Pay Code] must be entered in XXX days segments" that users encounter in the Workforce Management (WFM) system. The document outlines three distinct causes and their corresponding solutions, each requiring navigation through the WFM Admin Dashboard to access different configuration areas. The first cause involves verifying Work Pattern settings by going to WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Configuration > Work Patterns, where users must confirm that the Full Day Value in Misc-1 matches the Default Hours of the work pattern, as misalignment can cause balances to reduce incorrectly (by 0.50 Days instead of 1 Day) and prevent leave approval. The second cause addresses Balance Segment configuration through WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Person Maintenance, where users query an employee, navigate to the Balance tab, and change the Balance Segment value from restricted day segments (full, half, or quarter day) to 'None' by selecting the edit option next to the required balance. The third cause occurs when employees attempt to book a Full Day absence but their assigned Work Pattern has Default Hours that are insufficient for a full day absence, requiring users to verify the employee's Work Pattern Default Hours in WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Configuration > Work Patterns. This document is primarily used by WFM administrators and payroll personnel who manage employee leave and absence requests, as well as by support staff troubleshooting approval issues in the Approve Leave Request screen.

sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving an error that occurs when attempting to record a specific pay code on a given date due to insufficient entitlement in the CoreTime system. ss: When employees see the error "You are not rostered to work on this day" while trying to apply for leave in CoreTime, it's usually caused by one of four configuration issues: missing shift assignments, incorrectly configured CoreTime periods, disabled Unrostered Booking functionality, or Bank Holiday Schemes missing the RFA (Record Future Absence) option. Open this document if you need to troubleshoot leave application errors or if employees are unable to request time off due to rostering problems. Each cause includes step-by-step instructions for fixing the underlying configuration in CoreTime, WFM Admin Dashboard, or System Calendars.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving the error message "You are not rostered to work on this day" when employees attempt to apply for leave in the CoreTime system. The document outlines four distinct causes and their corresponding resolutions that users should follow systematically to identify and fix the underlying issue. The first cause involves missing shift type assignments, which requires assigning a shift to the affected employee through CoreTime. The second cause relates to incorrectly configured CoreTime Periods, and its resolution involves navigating to CoreTime > System Params > Calendars > System Calendars, selecting the relevant company via the question mark symbol, editing the week in question to the correct date, and saving the changes. The third cause addresses misconfigured Unrostered Booking functionality, requiring users to access CoreTime > System Params > Reference A-C > Control Parameters, select the relevant company, locate Contract Hours under Select Detail, and enable both the Allow Functionality and Enable Functionality checkboxes. The fourth cause involves Bank Holiday Schemes lacking the RFA (Record Future Absence) option, which is resolved by navigating to the WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Configuration > Bank Holiday Schemes, accessing the relevant scheme's menu, clicking View, and toggling on the Allow RFA option next to the relevant bank holiday. Additionally, the document notes that the System Calendar must be extended through the day an employee is applying for leave. This troubleshooting guide is primarily intended for HR administrators, system configuration managers, and support personnel who manage leave requests and rostering settings within the CoreTime workforce management platform.

sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving the error message "This record cannot be edited as it is historical" that appears in the CoreTime timekeeping system, explaining that the error occurs when users lack specific privileges or when calendar settings are misconfigured. The document identifies three primary root causes: the 'Maintain Historical Hours' privilege not being enabled for a Manager's Org Role, a Work Group lacking user-defined calendar (UDC) settings, or a user missing both the 'Ignore Data Entry Restriction' and 'Maintain Historical Hours' privileges. To resolve these issues, the document provides step-by-step procedures for both the Back-Office and Portal interfaces, including navigating through CoreTime > System Params > System Users to query Org Roles or individual System Users and enabling the 'Maintain Historical Hours' checkbox. For Work Groups using user-defined calendars, users must enable the 'User Defined Calendar Group' parameter through CoreTime > System Params > Work Groups > General Parameters (in Back-Office) or through the WFM Admin Dashboard (in Portal). The document also specifies that when using UDC, the Data Entry Offset value in the System Calendar > User Defined Periods section must be set to a value greater than or equal to 0. Finally, for users needing to edit historical records, both 'Ignore Data Entry Restriction' and 'Maintain Historical Hours' privileges must be enabled through the Access Privileges section under System Users in either interface. This resource is intended for system administrators, managers, and HR personnel who manage timekeeping permissions and encounter restrictions when editing historical time entries or hours.

ss: When updating notification body text in trigger points, a 403 Forbidden error occurs if your text contains too many special characters, as ModSecurity blocks the submission for security protection. sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses a 403 Forbidden error that users encounter when attempting to update the notification body of a trigger point within the system. The error occurs due to ModSecurity, a security protection mechanism, which blocks submissions containing an excessive number of special characters in the text field being updated. The document explains that this security restriction cannot be modified or adjusted by users or administrators, as ModSecurity is a fundamental protective measure designed to safeguard the system from potential threats and maintain optimal performance. To resolve the issue, users are advised to either replace the problematic link with a different one or remove the link entirely from the notification body text. Additionally, simplifying the overall text content by reducing the density of special characters will help prevent the error from occurring during future trigger point notification body updates. This guidance is typically consulted by system administrators, configuration managers, or end-users who work with trigger points and notification settings and encounter this validation error when attempting to save their changes.

sl: This document provides guidance on configuring geofencing restrictions for employee clock-ins within the Access Group Portal system. t: Hours not calculating on Maintain Hours for all or a group of employees

t: Floating Entitlement for Re-Hired Employee is Incorrect
s:

When an employee is re-hired within the same Annual Leave period, their entitlement calculation may not prorate based on their new joining date. Instead, the system prorates the period during which the employee was not employed.

For example:

Annual Leave Balance period: 1st January to 31st...
ss: When a re-hired employee rejoins during the same Annual Leave period, PeopleXD may incorrectly calculate their entitlement by prorating the gap period when they were unemployed instead of from their new joining date. This results in an inaccurate leave balance that needs manual correction. Open this document if you need to fix an employee's Annual Leave balance after they've been rehired and their entitlement calculation appears wrong. The resolution involves using the People Management Dashboard to manually adjust the employee's balance with the correct effective date and adjustment amount.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses a specific calculation error that occurs when employees are re-hired within the same annual leave period in the system. The issue involves the system incorrectly prorating leave entitlements based on the gap period when an employee was not employed, rather than calculating entitlement from their new joining date; for example, if an employee rejoins on 19th September 2022 within an annual leave balance period running from 1st January to 31st December 2022, the system prorates from 13th May to 19th September instead of from the re-join date forward. The document provides a step-by-step resolution requiring users to navigate to People Management Dashboard > Command Centre, locate the employee through the View Employees option, access the Balances tab on the employee's record, and perform a manual balance adjustment via the 3-dot menu. The manual adjustment process requires entering specific details including the effective date, affecting element, adjustment amount, and reason for adjustment before saving the changes. This document is designed for payroll administrators, HR personnel, and system users within Access Group systems who need to correct leave entitlements for re-hired employees and understand that this workaround does not apply to Multi-Appointment clients. The resource also references related articles on length of service calculations, employee balance management, and floating entitlement configuration for users seeking additional context on entitlement administration.

sl: This document explains why managers receive an access error when attempting to view an employee's calendar in a system with separate calendar viewing mechanisms. The system provides two distinct calendar screens—Team Calendar and Employee Calendar—that operate independently and use different access control methods, meaning a manager may successfully view an employee on the Team Calendar but encounter access restrictions on the Employee Calendar. The Team Calendar determines visibility based on the organizational chart structure, while the Employee Calendar relies on specific portal parameters: cp_pers_maint_org_role and cp_pers_maint_org_group, which must be properly aligned to the manager's permissions. When these parameters are not configured correctly, the system displays the error message "You do not have access to this person's calendar." To troubleshoot this issue, administrators should navigate to the Admin Dashboard, select Site Manager, then Admin Settings, and search for the cp_pers_maint parameters to verify their values—for example, if cp_pers_maint_org_role is set to MGRESS and cp_pers_maint_org_group is set to WRKGRP, access is controlled by the manager's reporting relationship at the work group level. The resolution involves confirming the manager has the appropriate organizational role access for the employee's work group or updating the portal parameters and manager access levels to ensure proper alignment. This document is primarily used by system administrators and support staff responsible for configuring portal access and resolving manager access issues related to employee calendar visibility.

sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre explains the error message that appears when managers cannot access leave requests in the workforce management (WFM) system, identifying two root causes: missing Menu Profile access or incorrect Organisational Role (Org Role) access for the employee's Work Group. t: Bulk Leave Approval screen displays 'Nothing to See Here'
s:
If the Bulk Leave Approval screen shows 'Nothing to See Here', this usually means the user doesn’t have the correct level of Personnel Access. Even if the Menu Profile is assigned, without the right access level, the screen will not display any data.

⚠️Important: To follow these steps, you need Adm...
ss: The Bulk Leave Approval screen in PeopleXD displays "Nothing to See Here" when a user lacks the correct Personnel Access level, even if their Menu Profile is already assigned. This article explains how to grant the necessary access permissions using either the Portal or CorePersonnel Back-Office system. Open this document if managers or administrators cannot see leave data on the approval screen and need to troubleshoot access restrictions. Administrator permissions are required to update Personnel Access settings.
sl: This document provides guidance for resolving an issue where the Bulk Leave Approval screen displays "Nothing to See Here" instead of showing leave request data. The root cause is typically insufficient Personnel Access permissions, which prevents data from displaying even when the appropriate Menu Profile has been assigned to a user. The document outlines two parallel methods for updating Personnel Access: one through the Portal and another through the Back-Office system. In the Portal method, administrators navigate to Security > Set Up > System Users, select Personnel Access as the Security Type, and then enter the Username, Structure Code, and Access Level before enabling the desired access level and saving. The Back-Office approach follows a similar process but requires navigating to CorePersonnel > Reference > Reference Q–Z > System Users and selecting PERS as the Security Type instead. Both methods achieve the same result, allowing administrators to choose their preferred interface for granting the correct access level. The document emphasizes that Administrator permissions are required to complete these steps, making it a resource for system administrators or users with elevated privileges who need to troubleshoot leave approval visibility issues for other users.

t: Back Office: Manager unable to see employee on WFM but can see them on Manager Dashboard
s:
If a manager can view employees on the Manager Dashboard but not in WFM’s Team Scheduler, it usually means their Manager Role Access for the employee’s work group is missing or incomplete. This guide walks you through the necessary checks and updates in Back Office to fix this.

 

Verify Manager Ro...
ss: When a manager can see employees on the Manager Dashboard but not in WFM's Team Scheduler, the issue is usually missing or incomplete Manager Role Access in Back Office. This document guides you through checking and updating the manager's role assignments in CorePersonnel to ensure they have the correct access to the employee's work group. Use this guide when managers report they cannot view their team in the WFM Team Scheduler, even though employee data appears elsewhere in the system. After making updates, managers need to log out and back in to refresh their permissions.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving a specific visibility issue in Access Group's workforce management system where managers can access the Manager Dashboard but cannot view employees in WFM's Team Scheduler interface. The problem typically stems from incomplete or missing Manager Role Access permissions for the employee's work group within the Back Office system. The guide outlines two verification processes, both conducted within Back Office's CorePersonnel module: the first involves navigating to Reference > Maintain Organisational Roles, using the search function to locate the relevant work group, and confirming the manager has the appropriate Manager Role Access assignment; the second parallel process uses Reference > Maintain Organisational Roles by Person to search for the specific manager and verify their access rights to the employee's work group. If either verification reveals missing access, the document instructs users to assign or update the manager's role to include Manager Role Access for that work group. The document emphasizes that after making any role updates, managers must log out and log back in to refresh their system permissions and enable the visibility changes to take effect. This resource is intended for system administrators or Back Office users responsible for configuring manager access and permissions in workforce management systems.

t: How to Enable the Return to Work Interview Option
s:
For organisations that require formal Return to Work Interviews after employee absences, this feature ensures the interview step is built into the absence input process. This guide shows you how to enable the option within the relevant Pay Code.

Additionally, there are other methods to enable the R...
ss: The Return to Work Interview feature in PeopleXD ensures that formal interviews are automatically triggered when employees record absences, and this guide explains how to enable it through Pay Code configuration in the WFM Admin Dashboard. You'll configure the setting by navigating to your relevant Pay Code, accessing Absence Settings, and toggling on the Return to Work Interview option. This feature is essential if your organisation requires documented return-to-work conversations following employee time off. Open this guide when you need to set up or activate Return to Work Interviews for specific absence pay codes, keeping in mind the feature is only available on the desktop version of PeopleXD.
sl: This document provides instructions for organizations that need to implement formal Return to Work Interviews as part of their absence management process, explaining how to integrate this interview requirement into the absence input workflow. The guide covers multiple methods for enabling the Return to Work Interview feature, with primary focus on configuring it through Pay Codes, which is one of several approaches available depending on organizational needs. To enable this feature via Pay Code configuration, users navigate from the Dashboard menu to WFM Admin Dashboard, then select WFM Configuration, followed by Pay Codes, where they locate the relevant pay code and access View/Edit Pay Code through the three-dot menu. Once in the pay code settings, users navigate to the Absence Settings section and toggle on the Return to Work Interview option before saving their changes. The document addresses the practical limitation that the Return to Work Interview widget is only accessible through the desktop version of PeopleXD and is not currently available on the mobile app, which is important for organizations planning their implementation. This guide is primarily intended for HR administrators, workforce management configuration specialists, and organizational leaders who manage absence policies and need to enforce structured return to work procedures across their employee base.

t: Absence type not showing in employee calendar
s:

ss: Absence types may not appear in the employee calendar if their associated pay code isn't configured to display in WFM. Open this article if you need to check or update pay code settings in the WFM Admin Dashboard to ensure absences show correctly for specific user types (Admin, Manager, or Employee). You'll learn how to navigate Employee Calendar Configuration, search for the relevant pay code, and enable the appropriate toggles and display settings.
sl: This document addresses the common issue where absence types fail to display in employee calendars within an Access Group workforce management system, with the primary cause being misconfigured pay code display settings. The document provides a step-by-step troubleshooting process that requires users to navigate to the WFM Admin Dashboard, access WFM Configuration, and open the Employee Calendar Configuration tile to locate and modify the relevant pay code settings. Users must search for the specific pay code causing the display issue and ensure that the appropriate User Type toggles—including Admin, Manager, and Employee—are enabled according to organizational requirements. The configuration process also allows administrators to assign a color and calendar code to the pay code to further customize how the absence appears in the employee calendar interface. This document is primarily intended for WFM administrators and managers who need to troubleshoot absence visibility issues and configure system settings to ensure that all absence types display correctly for their employees. The article serves as a practical reference guide for resolving pay code configuration problems while also directing users to related resources covering work patterns, shift types, absence drop-down lists, and absence reason code configuration.

t: Portal: How to Make the Employee Calendar Visible for Managers
s:
For a manager to view their team’s Employee Calendar on the portal, specific organisational role access and menu profile permissions must be configured.

Assign the Organisational Role

Go to the People Management Dashboard.

Open the Data Center.

Select People Management.

Click Maintain Organisat...
ss: Employee Calendar visibility in the Portal requires two configuration steps: assigning the MGRESS organisational role to link managers with their work groups, and enabling the WFM_EMP_CALENDAR_MGR menu profile in user security settings. Open this guide if your managers cannot see their team's Employee Calendar on the Manager Dashboard, or if the calendar option is missing from their menu. You'll need access to the People Management Dashboard and Security section to complete both the organisational role assignment and menu profile enablement.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for enabling managers to view their team's Employee Calendar on the portal by configuring both organisational role access and menu profile permissions within the Access Group system. The process requires two distinct configuration tasks: first, assigning the MGRESS organisational role to the manager through the People Management Dashboard by navigating to Data Center > People Management > Maintain Organisational Roles by Person, then adding a new row with the role set to MGRESS, the Org Group set to Work Group, and the Org Group Item set to the specific workgroup the manager oversees. Second, the document explains how to enable the WFM_EMP_CALENDAR_MGR menu profile by accessing Security > User Management, querying the manager's user account, clicking Manage Account, navigating to Menu Profiles, and ensuring the WFM_EMP_CALENDAR_MGR profile is enabled. The document clarifies that both configurations are essential—the MGRESS role links the manager to their relevant Work Group to access employee calendars, while the WFM_EMP_CALENDAR_MGR menu profile must be enabled to display the calendar option on the Manager Dashboard itself. This guidance helps resolve scenarios where managers cannot view their team's Employee Calendar despite having appropriate access, and it references related troubleshooting articles for calendar configuration issues and access errors. The document is intended for system administrators or portal configuration specialists who need to set up manager access to employee calendars in workforce management systems.

t: Configure the Employee Calendar
s:
Set up the Employee Calendar to control how events, pay codes, and colours display for different user types in Workforce Management.

You can configure the Employee Calendar in Workforce Management to customise how calendar events display for your employees. This includes setting start days, choosin...
ss: The Employee Calendar in Workforce Management lets you control what events, pay codes, and colours display for different user types across your organisation. You can configure global settings like start days and calendar formats, then assign specific pay codes with colour-coding and choose which events each user type sees. Open this document when you need to customise calendar visibility and appearance to match your organisation's scheduling and payroll requirements, or when setting up pay code display rules for managers and employees.
sl: This document provides comprehensive instructions for configuring the Employee Calendar within Workforce Management to customize how events, pay codes, and colors display for different user types across an organization. The document guides administrators through three main configuration processes: first, setting up Global Calendar Settings by accessing drop-down menus to select the calendar Start Day, choose between Rolling months or Fixed months format, and use Colour selectors to set colors for different calendar sections. Second, administrators configure Pay Code Settings by clicking the Pay Code Settings tab, searching for specific pay codes, using toggles to enable visibility for particular user types, and assigning display colors to each pay code in the Colour column. Third, the document explains how to manage which pay codes and calendar events display for each user type by accessing the User Type Pay Codes tabs, using the Add function to directly assign additional pay codes for specific user types, and enabling Calendar Events for each user type. The document helps resolve scenarios where employees or managers need to see appropriate pay codes and calendar events based on their user type, with related issues including absences not displaying, missing work patterns, and manager visibility permissions. The configuration changes save automatically and immediately appear on the Employee Calendar once completed, ensuring that all selected user types view only the relevant pay codes and calendar events configured for their role.

t: Leavers appearing on manager’s Team Scheduler
s: You may notice that employees who have left the company still appear in a manager’s Team Scheduler. This usually happens when the System Calendar is not advanced on time, which interrupts the employee’s leaver process. You can fix this by verifying and updating the current period on the System Calen...
ss: When employees who have left your company still appear in a manager's Team Scheduler, it's typically because the System Calendar in Back-Office hasn't been advanced on time, which interrupts their leaver process. You can resolve this by accessing Back-Office, navigating to CoreTime > System Params > Calendars > System Calendar, and updating the current period to the correct date. This fix ensures the leaver process completes properly and departed employees are removed from the Team Scheduler. Open this document if you need to troubleshoot stale employee records showing up in scheduling or if the leaver offboarding process appears stuck.
sl: This document addresses the issue of former employees continuing to appear in a manager's Team Scheduler after they have left the company, explaining that this problem typically occurs when the System Calendar fails to advance on schedule, which interrupts the employee's leaver process. The document provides a step-by-step resolution procedure that involves accessing Back-Office and navigating to the System Calendar settings to verify and update the current period. Users must follow a specific menu path: Back-Office > CoreTime > System Params > Calendars > System Calendar, then enter the relevant Company Code and check the Current Period field to view the active calendar period. If the current period is found to be outdated, users must update it manually to ensure the leaver process completes correctly and the departed employees are removed from the Team Scheduler display. The document requires users to have appropriate permissions to access Back-Office and make modifications to the System Calendar configuration. This guidance is primarily intended for managers and Back-Office administrators who need to maintain accurate team scheduling information and manage the leaver workflow within the CoreTime system.

ss: The Manager Dashboard's Approve/Sign Off tab relies on configuration settings in both the Portal and Back Office to display employee hours. This document walks through troubleshooting steps including enabling Team Scheduler access, verifying Org Role and Org Group parameters, and checking CoreTime/CoreRoster system settings for the MSS Sign Off Summary Display. Open this if hours aren't appearing when you try to approve or sign off timesheets in the Manager Dashboard, or if you need to configure these features for your organization.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving an issue where hours data fails to appear in the Approve/Sign Off tab within the Manager Dashboard, a problem typically caused by incorrect configuration settings that require verification across both the Portal and Back Office systems. The document outlines a systematic diagnostic process beginning with checking access to Team Scheduler by navigating to the Calendar option in the Manager Dashboard and confirming that the Manager Toolbox - Team Scheduler option is enabled in the user's menu profile. It requires managers to verify Portal Parameters configuration by confirming that two specific settings—cp_app_signoff_org_group and cp_app_signoff_org_role—are correctly configured and that the logging-in user has appropriate access to the associated Org Groups. The troubleshooting steps also include accessing Back Office to navigate to either CoreTime or CoreRoster, selecting System Params, then Reference K-P, and opening the MSS Sign Off Summary Display screen to ensure the Base Hours On field is set to Pay Code Listing. Additional verification involves checking Global Parameters in Back Office under System Params, Reference D-J, and the CoreTime MSS tab to confirm that both Manager Toolbox Authorise Summary and Sign Off & Approval Allowed settings are properly configured. This document is primarily intended for managers and system administrators who encounter situations where expected timesheet hours data is not displaying in their approval workflow, and it references related troubleshooting articles covering access errors and paycode visibility issues.

This document walks you through enabling specific pay codes on the calendar and configuring visibility settings for different user types, including manager masking and calendar access controls. Open this guide when you need to set up or adjust calendar settings so that your team sees the right information in the format that works best for your organization.
sl: This document provides comprehensive instructions for customising the Team Calendar in the WFM (Workforce Management) system to align with organisational requirements. The configuration process begins by navigating to the Dashboard menu and selecting WFM Admin Dashboard, then accessing WFM Configuration followed by Team Calendar Configuration. Users can configure multiple foundational settings including the Calendar Start Day (selected from a drop-down menu), Work Schedule Colour, and Company Events Colour to control how calendar items appear to all system users. The document details a pay code configuration process that involves accessing the Pay Code Settings tab, searching for specific pay codes, and enabling relevant toggles for each pay code to be displayed on the calendar. Additionally, administrators can customise settings for different user types through dedicated tabs, including the ability to control which calendar events appear for specific users, apply manager masking settings to obscure manager absences with specified codes and descriptions, and manage Calendar Access Based On field settings to determine visibility of users when viewing the calendar. t: Allow users to enter clockings for employees in Time and Attendance
s:
Person Maintenance: Enable Maintain Clockings for employees

The Maintain Clockings parameter controls whether users can input or maintain clockings for a specific employee. If this is not enabled for an employee, no user—regardless of their own permissions—can modify that employee’s clockings.

 

...
ss: Enable employees' clockings to be entered and modified in CoreTime and WFM by configuring two essential settings: the Maintain Clockings parameter in Person Maintenance, and clocking privileges assigned to system users. This document covers the step-by-step process for both Portal and Back Office environments, including how to grant specific permissions like modifying automated clockings, maintaining historical clockings, moving clockings between days, and resetting clock types. Open this guide when you need to set up clocking entry capabilities for your team, troubleshoot why users can't modify clockings despite having permissions, or configure access controls for different clocking scenarios such as night shift adjustments or historical timesheet corrections.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on configuring clocking entry and maintenance capabilities in a Time and Attendance system, covering both the Portal and Back Office interfaces within CoreTime. It explains a two-tier permission structure: first, the Maintain Clockings parameter must be enabled for an employee in Person Maintenance (accessed via WFM Admin > Person Maintenance in Portal or CoreTime > Pers Data > Person Maintenance in Back Office), and second, individual users must be assigned appropriate clocking privileges through System Users Configuration. The document details four specific clocking privileges available to users: Modify Automated Clockings (for updating or deleting device-sourced and ESS clock-ins), Maintain Historical Clockings (for entering past week clockings marked with prefix H), Move Automated Clockings (for adjusting night shift times across days), and Reset Clock Types (for changing the clock type designation). It emphasizes that user privileges are ineffective without the employee-level Maintain Clockings parameter enabled, and conversely, that disabling this parameter completely prevents all clocking modifications regardless of user permissions. The document also clarifies that users without any clocking privileges enabled can still input or modify manual clock times marked with prefix M, so administrators must disable Maintain Clockings at the employee level in Person Maintenance to fully restrict clocking access. This document is used by system administrators and HR personnel who need to configure time and attendance permissions and manage which users can enter, modify, or delete employee clockings, and it helps resolve errors related to clocking restrictions and maintain clocking indicators.

t: Assign menu profiles to users
s:
Menu profiles control user access to system functionality in PeopleXD. Users require at least one menu profile to access the system. The Security dashboard serves as the central hub for managing user access, roles, and menu profiles, providing a streamlined approach to access management.

 

 You ca...
ss: Menu profiles in PeopleXD control which system functionality each user can access, and every user needs at least one profile assigned to use the system. You can assign multiple profiles to a single user depending on their role—for example, an employee profile for the Employee Dashboard, a manager profile for the Manager Dashboard, and an HR admin profile for the People Management Dashboard. Open this document if you need to assign or remove menu profiles for individual users through the Security dashboard's User Management section, or if you want to set up automated profile assignments using the Menu Profile Matrix based on organizational roles or employee registration. The document also covers best practices for managing access and the specific menu permissions required to perform these tasks.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on assigning menu profiles to users within the PeopleXD system, explaining that menu profiles control user access to system functionality and that every user requires at least one profile to access the system. The document describes the central role of the Security dashboard in managing user access, roles, and menu profiles, and details the step-by-step process for assigning profiles: navigating from the dashboard menu to Security, then User Management, searching for the user in the System Users widget, clicking the three-dot menu to select Manage Account, and accessing the Menu Profiles section where administrators can toggle the Active switch to assign or remove profiles. It explains that users can be assigned multiple profiles depending on their organizational role, such as an Employee Dashboard profile, Manager Dashboard profile, or People Management Dashboard profile for HR administrators. The document also covers the Menu Profile Matrix feature, which automates profile assignments to employee groups based on two assignment types: Employee Organisation Role (where profiles are assigned based on matching organizational roles through a nightly process) and Employee Account Provisioning (where profiles are assigned during self-registration if contract requirements are met). Additionally, the document specifies that administrators must have the menu options "Menu Profiles - View Only" and "Menu Profiles - Update" within the Security system, and optionally need HR_CONFIGURATION_MENU.EMPLOYEE_MANAGER_REQUESTS for Employee and Manager Requests functionality and the $_R00T menu profile for full system access. Security and system administrators use this document to understand how to configure user access controls, implement best practices such as regularly reviewing roles, using descriptive profile names, limiting sensitive feature access, and documenting changes for audit purposes.

sl: This document provides instructions for editing the email notifications that are automatically sent when annual leave requests are submitted, approved, or rejected within an HR management system. t: Manage outstanding notifications

ss: Outstanding notifications in PeopleXD accumulate over time and can clutter your Notification Centre Management screen, particularly for employees who have been absent or off work. Use this process when you need to clear down outdated notifications or remove notifications for employees on extended leave. sl: This document guides administrators on how to view and manage outstanding notifications within the PeopleXD system, providing a practical solution for clearing outdated notifications or removing notifications for users who have been absent from work for extended periods. The process involves navigating to the Administrator Dashboard from the dashboard menu, then accessing the Notification Centre Management screen by clicking Site Manager and selecting the Open option next to Notification Centre Management. Once in the Notification Centre Management interface, administrators can apply filters based on criteria such as notification type or date to narrow down the notifications they wish to manage. After identifying the relevant notifications through these filters, administrators can select multiple notifications and use the Hide Notifications button to remove them from view. The document is designed for system administrators responsible for maintaining the notification system and ensuring that notification backlogs do not accumulate, and it references related articles covering notification configuration, email notification issues, and payroll integration concerns that may contextually relate to notification management in PeopleXD.

sl: This document provides instructions for accessing and configuring Notification Centre Management within an organization's administrator interface, primarily through the Site Manager widget located on the Site Management tab of the Administrator Dashboard. t: Pay code did not transfer to payroll and is missing from payslips
s:
If a pay code is missing from payroll and doesn’t show on payslips, it’s often because the Payroll Indicator is set to Non Payroll. You can check and update this setting in Back Office to resolve the issue.

This article explains how to check the configuration and correct it if needed.

 

Check the...
ss: Pay codes that don't appear on payslips are often configured with the Payroll Indicator set to "Non Payroll" instead of an active payroll option. Use CoreTime's System Params to locate the pay code, check the Payroll Indicator field under Pay In section on the Calculate/Pay tab, and change it from Non Payroll to the correct setting. Open this article when a pay code has been created in CoreTime but isn't transferring to PeopleXD Payroll or showing on employee payslips.
sl: This document provides guidance for resolving a common payroll configuration issue where pay codes fail to transfer to payroll and subsequently do not appear on employee payslips. The primary cause of this problem is typically the Payroll Indicator setting being configured as "Non Payroll" rather than an active payroll option. To diagnose and fix this issue, users navigate through CoreTime by accessing System Params, selecting Pay Codes, searching for the affected pay code, and clicking Calculate/Pay to view the configuration details. Within the Pay In section of this screen, users must locate the Payroll Indicator field and verify its current setting. If the Payroll Indicator is set to Non Payroll, users must change it to the correct option that will allow the pay code to transfer to payroll processing. After making this configuration change, users must click Save to confirm the update, and then reprocess the payroll to verify that the pay code now correctly appears on employee payslips. This document is intended for payroll administrators, HR staff, or system users responsible for configuring pay codes and managing payroll integrations within the Access Group's CoreTime and PeopleXD Payroll systems.

t: Pay code not calculating when running a future calculation
s:

ss: When running a future calculation in CoreTime and the Portal, some pay codes may fail to calculate because the Allow Future Calculation option isn't enabled. This document walks you through enabling this setting in both CoreTime's System Params and the WFM Admin Dashboard to resolve the issue. Open this if pay codes aren't calculating during future calculation runs or if you need to configure pay code settings to support future-dated calculations.
sl: This document addresses a common issue where certain pay codes fail to calculate properly when users run a future calculation in the system. The problem typically occurs because the Allow Future Calculation option has not been enabled for the affected pay code, and the resolution requires updates in two separate system locations. To fix this issue, users must first access CoreTime, navigate to System Params > Pay Codes, query the specific pay code that failed to calculate, open the General 4 tab, and enable the Allow Future Calculation option before saving the changes. Additionally, users must update the same pay code settings in the Portal by logging in, accessing the WFM Admin Dashboard, selecting Paycodes, and using the three-dot menu next to the relevant pay code to select View/Edit, then enabling the Future Calculation option under the Input Validation menu on the left side. This dual-location configuration is necessary because the system requires the setting to be activated in both CoreTime and the Portal for future calculations to process correctly. The document is primarily used by payroll administrators, system configuration specialists, or HR personnel who manage pay code settings and need to troubleshoot calculation failures during future pay period processing.

t: Error: The new pay code not in pay code group (pay code group name)
s:

To resolve this issue, you need to add the missing pay code to the correct pay code group in the WFM Admin Dashbo...
ss: Pay code configuration errors in the WFM Admin Dashboard occur when a pay code hasn't been added to its required Personalised Pay Code Group (PPCG). This document walks you through resolving the "pay code not in pay code group" error by navigating to WFM Configuration, locating the correct Pay Code Group, and adding the missing pay code. Open this guide when you encounter this error message and need step-by-step instructions to update your pay code group settings.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre explains the error message "The new pay code not in pay code group (pay code group name)" and provides step-by-step instructions to resolve it. The error occurs when a pay code has not been included in the required Personalised Pay Code Group (PPCG) within the system. To fix this issue, users must navigate to the WFM Admin Dashboard and access the WFM Configuration section, then select Pay Code Groups to locate the specific pay code group mentioned in the error message. The resolution involves querying the relevant pay code group, adding the missing pay code to it, and clicking Save to apply the changes. Once the pay code has been successfully added and saved, the error will no longer appear when users attempt to use that pay code. This document is typically used by WFM (Workforce Management) administrators or HR personnel who manage pay code configurations and employee pay code group assignments within the Access Group system, particularly when implementing new pay codes or troubleshooting configuration issues.

t: Pay code not calculating on rest days
s:
If a pay code is not calculating on rest days, it’s usually because the correct configuration is missing in the Rest Day Absences settings.

You can resolve this by updating the pay code in the WFM Admin Dashboard and linking it to the Global Rest Day Absence Pay Code.

 

How to enable a pay code t...
ss: Pay codes that aren't calculating on rest days usually lack the correct configuration in the Rest Day Absences settings within the WFM Admin Dashboard. You can fix this by accessing the Pay Codes section, selecting the relevant pay code, enabling "Apply Work Pattern Default Hours" under Rest Day Absences, and linking it to the Global Rest Day Absence Pay Code. Open this document if a pay code is showing zero or incorrect values on scheduled rest days, or if you need to configure a pay code to properly account for rest day absences in your payroll.
sl: This document addresses the issue of pay codes failing to calculate on rest days and provides the configuration solution needed to resolve it. The problem typically stems from missing or incorrect settings in the Rest Day Absences configuration area within the system. The document guides users through accessing the WFM Admin Dashboard from the dashboard menu, then navigating to WFM Configuration and selecting Pay Codes to locate the pay code that requires adjustment. Users must click the three-dot menu next to the relevant pay code, select View/Edit Pay Code, and then access the Rest Day Absences section from the left-hand menu. The resolution involves enabling the "Apply Work Pattern Default Hours" option and ensuring the Global Rest Day Absence Pay Code field is set to reference the same pay code being configured. After saving these changes, the pay code will function correctly and calculate properly on rest days. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators, HR personnel, or WFM (Workforce Management) configuration specialists who manage pay code settings and need to troubleshoot calculation issues related to rest day absences.

t: Stop pay code calculating on rest days
s:
You can stop a pay code from calculating on rest days by disabling specific parameters in both Back Office and Portal. This guide walks you through the steps to update the pay code configuration correctly.

Update pay code configuration in Back Office

Before starting, ensure you have the necessary ...
ss: Stop a pay code from calculating on rest days by disabling the Apply Work Pattern Default Hours parameter and removing it from the Global Rest Day Absence Pay Code list in both CoreTime Back Office and the WFM Admin Dashboard. This guide walks you through the configuration steps needed in each system to prevent unwanted pay code calculations during rest periods. Open this article if you're managing pay code settings and need to ensure specific codes don't apply to rest days, or if pay codes are calculating when they shouldn't be on non-working days.
sl: This document provides instructions for configuring pay codes to prevent them from calculating on rest days within the Access Group time and attendance system, addressing a common configuration need for payroll and absence management. The guide requires users to have appropriate permissions to access CoreTime and modify system parameters, and it covers two parallel configuration processes that must be completed in both the Back Office and Portal environments. In Back Office, users navigate through CoreTime to System Params and Pay Codes, where they query the relevant pay code, access the Rest Day Absences tab, disable the Apply Work Pattern Default Hours parameter, and remove the pay code from the Global Rest Day Absence Pay Code list before saving. The same configuration steps are then repeated in the Portal environment by accessing the WFM Admin Dashboard, selecting WFM Configuration, navigating to Pay Codes, and performing identical actions on the Rest Day Absences tab. This dual-system approach ensures consistent pay code behavior across both the backend system and the user-facing portal. The document is designed for payroll administrators, HR professionals, and system configuration specialists who need to manage how pay codes interact with rest day scheduling and absence calculations.

t: Error: Pay Code must be entered in full day segments – Timesheet Claim
s:
This error occurs when submitting a timesheet claim against a balance that is incorrectly configured to require full day segments.

 

Root Cause

At the employee level, the Balance Segment validation is set to enforce full day segments. This prevents partial day entries (e.g., 3 hours) from being p...
ss: Pay codes configured with full day segment validation in CoreTime will trigger an error when employees try to submit timesheet claims for partial day hours (like 3 hours). This happens because the Balance Segment setting at the employee level is enforcing full day entries only. Open this document if you're receiving a "Pay Code must be entered in full day segments" error and need to reconfigure the balance settings to allow partial day claims. The fix involves accessing CoreTime's Person Maintenance section and changing the Balance Segment setting from full day to "None" for the affected pay code.
sl: This document explains how to resolve a timesheet submission error that occurs when a pay code is configured to require full day entries, preventing employees from submitting partial day claims such as 3-hour segments. The root cause is an incorrect Balance Segment validation setting at the employee level that enforces full day segments for the affected balance. To fix this issue, users must navigate to CoreTime, access Person Data, select Person Maintenance, locate the specific employee, click on Current Balances, and identify the Balance associated with the problematic pay code. Within the Balance configuration, users must change the Balance Segment drop-down field from its current setting to "None," then save the changes. By setting Balance Segment to None, the system removes the full day requirement restriction, allowing employees to submit timesheet claims for partial day hours without encountering the error. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators, human resources personnel, or CoreTime system administrators who manage employee timesheet submissions and need to troubleshoot configuration issues that prevent valid partial day claims from being processed.

t: How to Assign Non Group Payroll Codes (NGPC) to Employees or Work Groups
s:
Purpose

Non Group Payroll Codes (NGPC) are used to control which payroll codes are excluded or skipped when generating timesheets for specific employees or groups.

⚠️ Important: Assigning an NGPC directly to a Work Group will impact all employees in that group. If you have a mix of salaried and no...
ss: Non Group Payroll Codes (NGPC) control which payroll codes are excluded when generating timesheets in CoreTime and WFM, allowing you to skip specific pay codes for individual employees or entire work groups. You can assign NGPCs at the employee level through the WFM Admin Dashboard's Person Maintenance section, or apply them to an entire work group through Configuration—though employee-level assignment is recommended if your work group contains a mix of salaried and non-salaried staff. Open this document if you need to prevent certain payroll codes from appearing on timesheets, troubleshoot why specific codes are missing from an employee's timesheet, or configure payroll code exclusions in your CoreTime system.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on managing Non Group Payroll Codes (NGPC), which are used to control which payroll codes are excluded or skipped when generating timesheets for specific employees or work groups. The document emphasizes that assigning an NGPC directly to a Work Group will impact all employees in that group, and recommends assigning NGPCs at the employee level when work groups contain a mix of salaried and non-salaried employees. For viewing and managing NGPCs, users navigate through the Back Office by accessing CoreTime, then System Params, selecting Ref D to J, and opening the Group Non Payroll Codes Menu to query and modify pay codes through the Payroll Codes – Group Non Payroll Code Details screen. The recommended process for assigning an NGPC to an individual employee involves using the WFM Admin Dashboard's Person Maintenance feature, where users search for the employee, access their Work Group Override settings, and assign the NGPC through the ellipsis menu option. For situations where all employees in a work group require the same NGPC, users can assign it at the group level by navigating to Configuration > Work Groups in the WFM Admin Dashboard and assigning the NGPC through the Group Codes section. This document is intended for payroll administrators, HR personnel, and system configurators who need to manage timesheet generation and payroll code exclusions across their workforce, particularly when dealing with heterogeneous work groups or specific employee-level payroll requirements.

t: Pay code not appearing on the create leave request screen drop-down
s:
If you cannot see a specific pay code when creating a leave request, there are three common causes to check. Each cause has a corresponding resolution that you can apply both in the back-office system and the portal to restore visibility of the pay code.

 

Cause 1: Pay code is not marked as an All...
ss: When creating a leave request in CoreTime or CorePortal, a pay code may not appear in the drop-down menu due to one of three common causes: the pay code isn't enabled for leave requests, the employee hasn't been assigned to a personalised pay code group, or the pay code is marked as HR Only. This document walks you through identifying which cause applies and provides step-by-step instructions to fix the issue in both the back-office CoreTime system and the WFM Admin Dashboard portal. Open this guide when employees report missing pay codes on their leave request screens or when you're troubleshooting leave request configuration issues.
sl: This document provides a troubleshooting guide for resolving the issue of pay codes not appearing in the drop-down menu when creating leave requests within CoreTime (back-office system) and CorePortal (the portal interface). The document identifies three primary causes for this problem and provides step-by-step resolution instructions for each cause in both systems. The first cause addresses pay codes that lack the "Allow Leave Requests" setting enabled, requiring users to navigate to System Params > Pay Codes > General Parameters-1 in CoreTime or WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Configuration > Pay Codes > Leave Request Settings in the portal, with additional parameters like "Allow Future Absences" and "Allow Absence Details" also needing to be enabled for full visibility across CorePortal screens. The second cause covers situations where employees have not been assigned a personalised pay code group, requiring administrators to access either Pers Data > Pers Maintenance > Personal Groups tab in CoreTime or WFM Person Maintenance > Personal Groups tab in the portal. The third cause involves pay codes configured as "HR Only," which restricts their visibility to general users and can be disabled via System Params > Pay Codes > General Parameters-1 in CoreTime or WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Configuration > Pay Codes > Summary tab in the portal. The document also includes instructions for granting access to the Pay Codes screen through the Security > User Management menu by enabling the WFM_PAY_CODES_ADMIN menu profile. This resource is intended for HR administrators, system administrators, and WFM (Workforce Management) personnel who manage leave request configurations and employee pay code assignments.

t: An employee's hours haven't transferred to PeopleXD Payroll
s:
If you've linked PeopleXD Workforce Management to PeopleXD Payroll, but the hours worked aren't transferring for an employee, there are several factors that could be causing this.

 

To resolve this, check each of the following in order.

 

Hours aren’t signed off

In order for the timesheets to s...
ss: When employee hours linked between PeopleXD Workforce Management and PeopleXD Payroll don't transfer to payroll, several configuration or setup issues could be blocking the transfer. This document walks through nine common causes—including unsigned timesheets, employee paid in advance, missing shift assignments, Non Generate Timesheets settings, and CorePay setup—with step-by-step instructions to fix each one. Open this if hours aren't appearing in PeopleXD Payroll after you've set up the WFM-to-Payroll connection and need to troubleshoot why the sync failed.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving issues when employee hours fail to transfer from PeopleXD Workforce Management to PeopleXD Payroll after linking the two systems. It presents a systematic checklist of nine specific scenarios and their corresponding resolutions that payroll and workforce administrators should investigate in sequence. The document addresses common configuration issues such as hours not being signed off in the timesheets, employees being marked with the "Non Generate Timesheets" setting in the WFM Admin Dashboard, and pay codes incorrectly configured as "Group Non Payroll" codes within CoreTime's System Params section. Additional scenarios covered include work groups not having the "Generate Timesheets" toggle enabled in WFM Configuration, employees not existing in CorePay, hours being processed against incorrect payroll periods through the System Calendars interface, and employees lacking assigned work patterns or shifts. The document includes detailed step-by-step navigation paths for each resolution, such as accessing the three-dot menu next to employee names or work groups and toggling specific settings like "Non Generate Timesheets" and "Generate Timesheets." This resource is designed for payroll managers, payroll administrators, and workforce management coordinators who manage the integration between these two systems and need to diagnose why expected hour transfers have failed.

t: Add or remove a pay code as an affecting code on a balance
s:
In PeopleXD Workforce Management, pay codes represent specific types of employee compensation or time entries. For example, regular hours, overtime, sick leave, or bonuses. 

 

When you set a pay code as an affecting code on a balance, it means that the value of that pay code directly influences th...
ss: In PeopleXD Workforce Management, pay codes like regular hours, overtime, and sick leave can be set as "affecting codes" that directly influence balance calculations. This document walks you through adding or removing pay codes as affecting codes on a balance within CoreTime's System Parameters and Balance Parameters sections. Open this guide when you need to control which pay codes impact your employee balance values, or when you're troubleshooting unexpected balance calculations. Note that removing an affecting code impacts balance values across all employees and periods, so this is an important system-level configuration task.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre provides instructions for managing pay code configurations within PeopleXD Workforce Management, specifically how to add or remove pay codes as affecting codes on employee balances. Pay codes in this system represent types of compensation or time entries such as regular hours, overtime, sick leave, or bonuses, and when designated as an affecting code, they directly influence how a particular balance is calculated. To add a pay code as an affecting code, users navigate to CoreTime > System Params > Balances > Balance Parameters, select the relevant balance from the list of values, click Affecting Codes to select the pay code, configure the affecting element and multiplier settings, then save the changes. The removal process follows the same navigation path through CoreTime > System Params > Balances > Balance Parameters, but instead requires users to select the pay code and click Delete before saving, with an important caveat that this action will impact balance values across all employees and all periods. This document is typically used by payroll administrators, system configurators, or workforce management specialists who need to adjust how specific pay codes influence balance calculations in their organization. The document also references related articles covering balance creation, unexpected balance appearance issues, mid-year entitlements for new starters, and leave overbooking prevention, indicating it is part of a broader suite of balance and pay code management documentation.

t: Fix approval access error for paycodes in Portal
s:
You may see the message ‘You do not have the required access for Approval of [paycode] on [date]’ when trying to approve hours in Portal. This happens when your System User account doesn’t have the correct permissions enabled.
Once the correct privileges are switched on, you’ll be able to approve ho...
ss: Portal displays an "You do not have the required access for Approval of [paycode]" error when your System User account lacks the correct approval permissions for hours. This issue is resolved by enabling the Approve Hours and Sign-Off Hours toggles in WFM System Users Configuration within the WFM Admin Dashboard. Use this guide when you're unable to approve employee hours in Portal due to missing access privileges. The fix involves a WFM administrator updating your account permissions rather than a user-side workaround.
sl: This document addresses a specific access permission error that users encounter when attempting to approve hours in Portal, manifesting as the message "You do not have the required access for Approval of [paycode] on [date]." The root cause of this error is that the System User account lacks the necessary permissions configured in the system, preventing approval functionality despite the user's role or responsibilities. The document provides step-by-step instructions to resolve this issue by navigating through WFM Admin Dashboard and accessing the WFM Configuration menu, then locating WFM System Users Configuration to identify and modify the affected user's settings. Within the System Users Configuration interface, users must locate the specific employee account using the three-dots menu option and select View/Edit to access the Access Privileges settings panel. The resolution involves enabling two critical toggles: the "Approve Hours" toggle and the "Sign-Off Hours" toggle, which grant the necessary permissions to approve and sign off on hours respectively. Once these access privileges are activated, the user will be able to approve hours in Portal without encountering the access restriction error. This document is typically used by administrators or managers who manage system permissions in the WFM (Workforce Management) platform and need to troubleshoot approval access issues for their team members, particularly in contexts where payroll data transfers to PeopleXD Payroll.

ss: When users in PeopleXD Workforce Management encounter an "access for Approval of paycode" error, it's because their System User account lacks the required Approve Hours permission. This error prevents managers and administrators from approving or signing off hours in the Portal or WFM Admin Dashboard. Open this document if you need to grant a user permission to approve hours—you'll find step-by-step instructions to enable the Approve Hours and Sign-Off Hours toggles in WFM System Users Configuration.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre explains how to resolve a specific access error in PeopleXD Workforce Management that prevents users from approving or signing off on hours. The error message "You do not have the required access for Approval of paycode on date" occurs when a user's System User account lacks the necessary Approve Hours permission within the application's Portal or WFM Admin Dashboard interface. The document identifies the root cause as missing System User Access Privileges and provides a step-by-step solution accessible through the WFM Admin Dashboard menu path: WFM Configuration > WFM System Users Configuration. To resolve the issue, administrators must locate the affected user via the three-dots menu, select View/Edit, navigate to Access Privileges, and then enable both the Approve Hours and Sign-Off Hours toggles for that user. This document is typically used by WFM administrators or supervisors who manage workforce management permissions and need to grant approval capabilities to team members in PeopleXD Workforce Management. The guide is part of a broader help center resource that covers related access issues and bulk approval processes, making it a focused reference for a common permission configuration problem.

s:
The WFM year end tasks screen eliminates guesswork by giving system administrators a centralised view of all tasks and actions needed to keep the WFM system up to date.

 

WFM year end tasks screen
