ss: WFM year end tasks is a centralised screen in the WFM Admin Dashboard that gives system administrators a complete view of all tasks and actions needed to maintain the system at year end. Use this feature to review action-required tasks for active companies, calendars, and schemes, create custom checklist items, and configure email notifications and thresholds for year-end reminders. Open this guide when you need to set up year-end processes, adjust notification timing (default 30-day threshold), or assign the required menu profiles to users who manage WFM year-end activities. The screen eliminates guesswork by consolidating balance period end tasks, shift extensions, and other maintenance activities in one place.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on using the WFM Year End Tasks screen, a centralised feature within the WFM Admin Dashboard that helps system administrators manage all necessary year-end maintenance activities and configuration changes. The document explains how to access the screen, view required actions for each active company, calendar, or scheme, and extend them as needed through the three-dot menu options. It describes how administrators can create custom year-end tasks by clicking Add Check List Item on the WFM Year End Tasks screen, entering the task name, description, due date and comments, and then manually marking items as complete when finished. The document details the configuration of three email parameters—ct_year_end_email_fromn (email subject), ct_year_end_email_frome (sender address), and ct_year_end_email_to (recipient inbox address)—which are set through the Administrator Dashboard's Site Manager and Admin Settings using the ct_year_end search term. It explains how to adjust the notification threshold in WFM Configuration's General Settings, where administrators can modify the Year End Limit from its default 30-day setting to match their organisation's timing requirements. Before accessing the WFM year-end tasks functionality, the document specifies that six specific menu profiles must be assigned: WFM_YEAR_END, WFM_COMPANY_SETTING_ADMIN, WFM_BANK_HOLIDAY_CONFIG, WFM_BALANCE_CONFIGURATION, WFM_BALANCE_ADMIN, and WFM_SHIFTS_TYPES. This guide is intended for WFM system administrators responsible for preparing the workforce management system for a new year and ensuring timely notifications are sent for critical year-end maintenance tasks.

t: Enable co-workers' leave and absence viewing on the Native App
s:
You can allow employees to view co-workers' leave and absence information on the Native App by enabling specific menu options in their menu profile. This is done in Security > Menu Profiles in Back Office.

Once enabled, users will be able to view co-workers’ leave directly in the app.

How to enabl...
ss: Configure employee access to view co-workers' leave and absence information in the Native App by enabling specific menu options in Back Office Security settings. This process involves querying the relevant menu profile (such as COREPORTAL_EMPLOYEE) and enabling the WS_LEAVE_MENU.GET_COWORKERS and WS_SHIFTS_MENU.GET_COWORKERS options. Open this document when you need to grant employees visibility of their team's leave schedules or when setting up menu permissions for new user profiles in the Native App.
sl: This document explains how to enable co-workers' leave and absence viewing functionality on the Native App by configuring specific menu options within user profiles in the Back Office system. The process is managed through the Security > Menu Profiles section, where administrators query the relevant menu profile (such as COREPORTAL_EMPLOYEE) and locate two specific menu options: WS_LEAVE_MENU.GET_COWORKERS and WS_SHIFTS_MENU.GET_COWORKERS. Both of these options must be enabled by selecting their corresponding checkboxes to grant users the ability to view leave and absence information for their co-workers directly within the Native App. After making these configuration changes, affected users must log out and log back in to the Native App to ensure the new permissions take effect immediately. This document is primarily used by system administrators or HR personnel responsible for configuring user access and permissions in the Native App, particularly when implementing visibility of team leave schedules across their organization. The guide also references related issues including error messages when retrieving leave requests, time display problems on leave screens, issues with booking annual leave, absence calculation problems on rest days, and manager-specific document upload restrictions.

t: Add cycle stages to an appraisal
s:
Once you've created an appraisal in PeopleXD Talent, to add a cycle stage, follow the steps below.

Next to the relevant appraisal, click the three-dot menu.

Click + Add a New Stage then enter the details of the stage.

Turn on the Activate Stage toggle then click Save.

Once you've done this, you ...
ss: Adding cycle stages in PeopleXD Talent lets you structure the phases of your appraisal process—such as planning, review, and feedback stages. You'll open this guide when you're setting up a new appraisal cycle and need to define the individual stages employees will progress through. The process involves creating a stage, activating it, and then adding specific steps within each stage. It's important to activate stages before you activate the overall appraisal cycle, since only active stages can be assigned to employees.
sl: This document provides instructions for adding cycle stages to an appraisal within PeopleXD Talent, a talent management system. The process involves locating the relevant appraisal and accessing the three-dot menu next to it, then clicking the "+ Add a New Stage" option to enter the stage details. A critical configuration step is toggling on the "Activate Stage" setting before saving, as only stages marked as active can be assigned to employees. Users must enable the Active Stage toggle for each stage before activating the appraisal cycle itself, as enabling it after activation will not add the stage to the cycle. After saving a stage, users can subsequently add individual steps to that stage to build out the appraisal workflow. This document is primarily used by HR administrators and appraisal managers who are setting up or configuring appraisal cycles in PeopleXD Talent and need to establish the structural stages that will guide employees through the appraisal process. The document references related processes including creating appraisal cycles, creating objective cycles, managing active appraisal cycles, and handling appraisal cycle assignments for new starters.

t: Amend an existing appraisal
s:
There may be times when an appraisal reaches the end of the workflow, but you need to make an update. In CorePortal, you can reopen or adjust reviews without disrupting the whole process.

 

To do this, follow the steps below.

In CorePortal, click Talent Admin Dashboard.

Click Appraisals then, fo...
ss: Amending appraisals in CorePortal allows you to reopen or adjust employee reviews after they've progressed through the workflow without starting the entire process over. Use the Talent Admin Dashboard to access appraisals, find the employee's review, and choose actions like sending it back to the employee or manager, marking it as HR reviewed, or deleting it entirely. Open this guide when you need to make changes to a completed or in-progress appraisal, correct employee information, or route a review back through the approval chain.
sl: This document provides guidance on modifying appraisals that have already progressed through their workflow in CorePortal, addressing the common situation where updates are needed after an appraisal has reached completion. The document outlines the specific navigation path required to access amendment functionality: users must go to the Talent Admin Dashboard, select Appraisals, click the three-dot menu next to the relevant appraisal, then choose Admin Options followed by Manage Review. Once in the Manage Review screen, users can search for the specific employee whose appraisal requires adjustment. The document describes four key actions available through the Actions drop-down menu: Send Back To Employee, Send Back to Manager, Mark as HR Reviewed, and Delete Review, each allowing different types of modifications or status changes to the appraisal. This process is designed to accommodate late-stage changes without requiring the entire appraisal workflow to be restarted, making it useful for HR administrators and managers who need flexibility in handling completed or near-completed appraisals. The document is intended for CorePortal users with admin-level access who manage appraisal cycles and employee performance reviews.

t: Disable the password authentication for signing off on a review
s:
By default in PeopleXD Talent, you need to enter a password in order to sign off a review or appraisal. To disable the password authentication, you can enable the pdp_simple_sign_off parameter.

 

To do this, follow the steps below.

In portal, click Administrator Dashboard.

Click the Site Manager...
ss: In PeopleXD Talent, password authentication is required by default when signing off on reviews and appraisals. If you want to remove this password requirement and allow simple sign-offs without authentication, you'll need to enable the pdp_simple_sign_off parameter through Administrator settings. Open this document if you're managing PeopleXD configuration and need to streamline your review sign-off process by disabling password prompts. This is a quick administrative task that takes just a few clicks in the Site Manager.
sl: This document provides instructions for disabling password authentication when signing off on reviews or appraisals in PeopleXD Talent, a system that by default requires users to enter a password to complete this action. The document describes a straightforward configuration process that involves navigating to the Administrator Dashboard in the portal, then accessing the Site Manager tab and clicking Admin Settings to locate the relevant configuration option. The key setting administrators need to modify is the pdp_simple_sign_off parameter, which must be set to the value "Y" to disable password authentication for sign-offs. This configuration is particularly useful for organizations that want to streamline the review sign-off process by removing the password requirement barrier while maintaining the ability to complete reviews and appraisals. The document is primarily targeted at system administrators or those with access to portal administration settings who have responsibility for configuring PeopleXD Talent to match their organization's security and workflow requirements. By following these steps, administrators can simplify the user experience for employees and managers who need to sign off on performance reviews without compromising the core functionality of the review and appraisal system.

t: Appraisal cycle not auto-assigned to new starters
s:
If you've added a new employee to PeopleXD, but they haven't been auto-assigned to an appraisal cycle, you need to check the appraisal configuration.

 

To do this, follow the steps below.

Click Talent Dashboard then click the Appraisals tab.

Next to the relevant appraisal, click the three-dot me...
ss: When you add a new employee to PeopleXD but they're not automatically assigned to an appraisal cycle, you'll need to adjust the appraisal configuration settings. This document walks you through accessing the Talent Dashboard, editing the relevant appraisal, and configuring the auto-assignment criteria—specifically the "Number of Days" value that controls how long CorePortal continues assigning the appraisal to new starters. Open this if new employees aren't appearing in appraisal cycles automatically, or if you need to adjust how long the system should keep auto-assigning employees after a cycle begins.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for PeopleXD users who have created new employee records but notice those employees are not automatically assigned to appraisal cycles. The document walks through a specific process accessed via the Talent Dashboard's Appraisals tab, where users locate the relevant appraisal, click the three-dot menu, and select Edit (confirming any active appraisal warnings). The core steps involve navigating to Actions and selecting both Assign and Assign Criteria Group to configure the auto-assignment behavior. The document explains a critical configuration setting called "Number of Days," which determines the duration over which CorePortal continues to auto-assign the appraisal to new starters after the cycle begins; for example, setting this to 365 days ensures new employees are assigned throughout a full-year cycle, while entering 1 means the auto-assignment job runs only once on the first day after activation and then ceases. This document is primarily used by HR administrators and talent managers who are setting up or managing appraisal cycles in PeopleXD and need to ensure that new hires are properly enrolled in performance management processes.

ss: The Additional Details settings in PeopleXD let you control which employees are included in appraisals based on their probation expiry date or start date. You can exclude employees still on probation, include only those in probation, or automatically assign appraisals to employees whose probation or start dates fall within a specified number of days from the appraisal start date. Open this document if you're setting up an appraisal cycle and need to ensure new starters or employees finishing probation are automatically included or excluded from reviews based on their employment status.
sl: This document explains the Additional Details settings feature that controls which employees are included in appraisal assignments based on their probation status and employment start dates. The feature provides four configurable options accessed during appraisal assignment: users can exclude employees with future probation expiry dates, include only those with future probation expiry dates, or set up automatic assignment rules based on probation expiry or start dates occurring within a specified number of days. The automatic assignment options use a daily system check that compares employee profile data against a configurable Number of Days field to determine eligibility. These settings help resolve scenarios where new starters or employees finishing probation might be missed from relevant appraisal cycles, either because they were not yet added to the system when the appraisal was initially assigned or because their employment status has changed since the appraisal began. The document is typically used by HR administrators, appraisal managers, or system configurators who need to ensure appropriate employee inclusion in performance review cycles while managing probationary periods and onboarding timelines. The related articles reference "Appraisal cycle not auto-assigned to new starters" and "360 Reviews aren't being assigned to all employees," indicating this document addresses common issues with incomplete appraisal assignments.

t: Manage criteria groups
s:
You can use criteria groups in PeopleXD to group employees based on reference data in their employee records. For example, you can group all employees in a particular department.

 

You can then use these criteria groups when you assign objective or appraisal cycles to employees.

 

Assign criteri...
ss: Criteria groups in PeopleXD let you organize employees by reference data from their employee records, such as department or other attributes. You can create new criteria groups or activate existing ones, then assign them to appraisal cycles, objective cycles, and individual objectives in the Talent Dashboard. Open this document when you need to group employees for performance management purposes or when assigning appraisals and objectives to multiple staff members at once based on shared characteristics.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre explains how to use criteria groups in PeopleXD to organize employees based on reference data stored in their employee records, such as departmental assignment, and then leverage these groups when distributing objective or appraisal cycles. The document provides step-by-step instructions for assigning criteria groups across three different contexts within the Talent Dashboard: assigning an appraisal cycle (via the Appraisals tab by selecting the three-dot menu, then Assign > Actions > Assign Criteria Group), assigning an objective cycle (via the Objective cycles tab using the three-dot menu and Edit function), and assigning a set objective (via the Objective cycles tab by navigating through the Edit menu to the Types step). For creating new criteria groups, users access the Assignment screen, click Add Group, enter a group name, and then select relevant reference data from the left-hand menu before moving desired attributes to the Assigned column using the arrow button. sl: This document provides comprehensive instructions for configuring custom workflows and statuses within objective cycles in the Talent Dashboard, enabling managers to approve objectives at various stages and allowing employees to track progress using customized status labels. The setup process begins by navigating to Talent Dashboard > Objective cycles, selecting the relevant cycle via the three-dot menu, choosing Edit to access the Types step of the wizard, then enabling the Custom Workflow and Statuses indicator in the Key Fields tab before proceeding through the Workflow & Status Setup wizard. The system includes customizable workflow statuses that cannot be deactivated but can have their display names changed via the Custom Description field to alter how they appear to users. For objective progress tracking, administrators can assign either an existing group of custom workflow statuses or create a new group by clicking Manage Statuses, specifying a title, selecting Status as the Rating Type, and configuring individual statuses with numeric ratings for display order, custom descriptions for display names, color selections, and active status toggles. s:

ss: When printing a review in your system, a 404: Not Found error typically occurs due to special characters, unexpected spaces, or blank lines in objective text fields or other review fields. To fix this issue, back up the affected fields, clear them completely, and attempt to print again—if successful, you can then reintroduce the backed-up content one field at a time to identify the problematic field. Open this document if you're unable to print reviews and need to troubleshoot formatting errors that are blocking the print function.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses the "Error: 404: Not Found" message that users encounter when attempting to print reviews within the system. The error typically stems from formatting issues in the review's text fields, specifically the presence of special characters in objective text fields or other review text fields, as well as problematic spacing such as spaces in empty fields or double blank lines at the end of text entries. To resolve this issue, users should first back up the data contained in the affected fields and then clear all text fields to blank values before attempting to print the review again. If the review prints successfully after clearing the fields, users can systematically re-add the backed-up information one field at a time to identify which specific field caused the original error, or alternatively re-enter the information while carefully avoiding special characters and extra spaces. This document is primarily used by Access Group system users who encounter print failures related to review documents and need to troubleshoot and resolve formatting-related errors affecting system functionality.

ss: The Available Employees list in 360 reviews shows which employees are eligible to participate based on their assignment group—whether that's specific departments, the entire company, or another grouping. Use this information to verify that the right people are included in your review cycle before assignments go out. sl: This document explains the composition of the Available Employees list within a 360 review system, specifically detailing which employees appear in the list based on their assignment group membership. The Available Employees list dynamically populates with all employees who share the same assignment group designated for the review, ensuring that only relevant personnel are included in the review scope. The document illustrates three specific scenarios: when a review is assigned to multiple departments (such as Department A and Department B), the list displays all employees with active appointments in those departments; when a review is assigned at the company level, all active employees company-wide appear on the list; and when an employee holds multiple appointments within the assignment group, that employee appears on the list multiple times, with one entry per appointment to reflect their different roles. This approach ensures transparency about who is included in a review before it is distributed and helps users understand the scope of their review assignment based on organizational structure and employment status. The document serves as a reference guide for administrators and managers setting up or managing 360 reviews, helping them verify that the correct pool of employees has been identified for their review cycles.

The document describes the process for manually assigning individual employees after the main assignment is complete by using the Admin Options function. If certain employees do not meet the date criteria for a particular 360 Review, the document advises creating a separate review instance to include them rather than forcing them into an ineligible assignment. t: Applicant Cleardown overview
s:
In PeopleXD Recruitment, you can use the Applicant Cleardown feature to automate the removal or anonymisation of applicant details. This process runs nightly and targets closed vacancies with a closed date older than six or twelve months.

 

The Applicant Cleardown process doesn't apply to successf...
ss: Applicant Cleardown in PeopleXD Recruitment automates the removal or anonymisation of applicant details from closed vacancies on a nightly schedule. You can configure the process to clear data from vacancies closed more than 6 or 12 months ago, though successful applicants and those with active applications elsewhere are protected from deletion. Open this document when you need to set up or manage automated applicant data cleanup in your recruitment system, or to understand how unsuccessful applicants' records are handled during the cleardown process.
sl: The Applicant Cleardown overview document describes an automated feature in PeopleXD Recruitment that removes or anonymises applicant details on a nightly schedule for closed vacancies. The process targets vacancies with a closed status and a closing date that is older than either six or twelve months, depending on the configuration selected. Successful applicants are protected from cleardown if they appear on the Successful Applicants screen with an accepted job offer or if an HR record has been created following their hire. For unsuccessful applicants, the system deletes their application for that specific vacancy; however, if they have other active applications, their applicant record and those applications remain intact, while applicants with no other active applications have their entire record deleted. To configure the Applicant Cleardown process, users navigate from the Recruitment Dashboard to the Toolbox tab, open the My Recruit Toolbox widget, and access Applicant Cleardown to select from three options via the "Clear down data after" dropdown menu: "Do not clear" (default, no data removal), "6 Months" (clears data from vacancies closed over six months ago), or "12 Months" (clears data from vacancies closed over twelve months ago). This document is designed for recruitment administrators and HR professionals who need to manage applicant data retention policies and comply with data protection requirements while preserving records of successful hires and active candidates.

t: Forgot Password Email Not Sending on E-Recruitment
s:
Cause 1: E-Recruitment Web Parameters not configured correctly for the Forget Password option
Cause 2: Email has been sent. Email is being filtered by the client's email
Cause 3: Applicant has two email addresses associated with their Applicant ID. Email will not fire unless the correct email addres...
ss: The E-Recruitment system's password reset functionality relies on correct configuration of email parameters in Back Office and proper email delivery settings. This document helps troubleshoot situations where applicants don't receive the "Forgot Password" email, covering four common causes: misconfigured E-Recruitment Web Parameters, emails filtered to spam folders, applicants having multiple email addresses on file, or missing Recruitment accounts. Open this if users report they cannot reset their e-Recruitment passwords due to missing reset emails, or if you need to verify email parameter settings in CorePersonnel or EMS Parameter Maintenance.
sl: This document provides diagnostic guidance for troubleshooting situations where the "Forgot Password" email feature fails to send in the E-Recruitment system. The document identifies four primary causes: misconfigured E-Recruitment Web Parameters, emails being filtered by client email systems, applicants having multiple email addresses associated with their Applicant ID, or the absence of a valid Recruitment account linked to the applicant's email address. To address configuration issues, administrators should navigate in Back Office to CorePersonnel > Recruitment > Recruitment Reference > E-Recruitment Web Parameters, select the Email Parameters tab, and verify that the Reset Password parameter is populated with both an Email Subject and Email Body. For email filtering problems, users should first check their spam folder, then access either the Portal's Data Centre to search for EMS Parameter Maintenance or navigate through Back Office via CoreHR > Event Management > EMS Parameter Maintenance to ensure the EMS Username field matches the Administrator Email field (both should be peoplexd@accessacloud.com). If the first two resolutions do not resolve the issue, applicants should attempt to register a new account using the email address for which they are trying to reset the password, or users should raise a new support case online referencing this article. This document is primarily used by E-Recruitment administrators, system support teams, and help desk personnel who need to resolve password reset email delivery failures for applicants.

t: Applicant is unable to apply for internal vacancy
s:
If you have an applicant that's unable to apply for an internal vacancy, it may be due to the internal email extension not being configured. To resolve this, advise the applicant to apply using their work email address.
​
You need to configure the work email address extension that appears after the ...
ss: When applicants can't submit applications for internal vacancies in e-Recruitment, the issue is often a missing internal email extension configuration. Resolve this by ensuring the work email address extension (the domain after the @ symbol) is properly set up in the Email Extension screen under Personnel > Recruitment > Reference > E-Recruitment web Parameters. Open this article if applicants are receiving errors or unable to complete their internal vacancy applications, or if you need to configure the internal email domain for your recruitment system.
sl: This document explains how to resolve an issue where applicants cannot apply for internal vacancies within the Access Group recruitment system, typically caused by improper configuration of the internal email extension. The document outlines a specific configuration process that administrators must follow to enable applicants to submit applications using their work email addresses. The configuration requires navigating through the system menu path: Personnel > Recruitment > Reference > E-Recruitment web Parameters, then accessing the General Parameters Tab and selecting the Email Extension option. The key configuration step involves populating the Internal Email Extension field with the appropriate work email domain (such as @work.com) that appears after the @ symbol in email addresses. Once this email extension is properly configured, applicants will be able to submit applications for internal vacancies without encountering errors. This document is primarily intended for HR administrators, recruiters, or system configurators who manage the e-Recruitment module and need to troubleshoot application submission issues for internal job candidates. The document references related troubleshooting articles covering related e-Recruitment problems such as vacancy visibility issues, email address changes in Core e-Recruit, missing email notifications, and application errors.

If you need to verify whether an applicant's email address is missing from their application record, support can run scripts to investigate the issue. Open this if an applicant reports they've applied but aren't receiving confirmation emails, or if you suspect email address data wasn't captured during the application process.
sl: This document addresses the issue of applicants or users failing to enter their email address correctly during the vacancy application process in the Access Group e-Recruitment system. The document explains that this is a common problem that can occur when applying for a position, preventing successful submission of an application. When this issue is encountered, support staff can investigate by running scripts to verify whether the email address was properly entered into the system. Users who suspect they have experienced this problem are instructed to raise a support case with the Access Group Help Centre to request the diagnostic check. The document also references three related articles that cover adjacent issues: problems with unlinking applicants who are already recruited or appointed, difficulties modifying email addresses or usernames within the Core e-Recruit system, and delivery failures when applicants use Hotmail email addresses. This troubleshooting guide is primarily intended for recruitment administrators, hiring managers, or applicants experiencing submission failures due to email entry problems, and serves as a first point of reference before contacting technical support for resolution.

t: Generate and merge applications
s:
Generating and Merging in Portal:
Generating:

Click Recruitment

Query a Vacancy

Click Actions, View applicants

Click Actions once more and select Generate Applications

Select all or some of the applications you wish to generate

Click Actions

Click Generate Applications.

A message will appear...
ss: The recruitment application process in Access Group's Portal and Back Office systems allows you to generate individual PDFs that combine all documents for single applications, or merge applications to create one PDF containing all applicants for a vacancy. You can perform both tasks from either the Portal recruitment area or CorePersonnel Back Office by querying a vacancy, selecting applicants, and clicking the relevant action button. Open this document when you need to create consolidated application documents for review, storage, or distribution purposes, or when you're troubleshooting issues with generating or merging applicant files. The system submits these jobs in the background and notifies you by email when complete, then displays the completion date and time for easy access to the generated PDFs.
sl: This document provides comprehensive instructions for generating and merging applications within the Access Group recruitment system, covering both Portal and Back Office interfaces. The generating process combines all documents associated with individual applications into single PDF documents, while the merging process creates a combined PDF containing all applications for a specific competition or vacancy. In the Portal interface, users access these functions by navigating to Recruitment, querying a vacancy, selecting View applicants, and then choosing either Generate Applications or Merge Applications from the Actions menu, with the option to process all or selected applications. In the Back Office system, users navigate through CorePersonnel > Recruitment > Maintenance > Applicant Status to access the Generate Applications Screen, where they can select applicants and initiate generation or merging tasks. Both processes operate asynchronously, submitting jobs that trigger email notifications to recipients upon completion, with the completion date and time displayed on screen (and accessible by double-clicking to open the resulting PDF in a new browser window). The document addresses potential issues such as needing to exit and reopen screens for dates to display properly, and references related articles covering applicant cleardown, email notifications, and troubleshooting scenarios like merge failures in the Vacancy Maintenance screen. This resource is designed for recruitment administrators and hiring managers who need to prepare application documentation for review, comparison, or archival purposes within the system.

t: Delete an individual application Back Office
s:

Search for the applicant and drill down into their record

In the Select Detail box press 02 - Vacancy Detail

Hig...
ss: Deleting individual applications from vacancies in CorePersonnel's Recruitment module requires navigating to the Applicant Detail section and locating the specific application you want to remove. This process guides you through finding the applicant record, accessing their vacancy details, and using the Delete option while providing a deletion reason for audit purposes. Open this document when you need to remove a single applicant's application from a job posting or when an application needs to be withdrawn from the recruitment process in Back Office.
sl: This document provides instructions for removing an individual job application from a vacancy within the CorePersonnel system's back office environment. The process begins by navigating to CorePersonnel, then selecting Recruitment, followed by Recruitment Maintenance, and finally Applicant Detail to locate the specific applicant whose application needs to be deleted. Once the applicant record is accessed through a search and drill-down function, users must select option "02 - Vacancy Detail" from the Select Detail box to view the relevant vacancy information. The next step involves highlighting the specific application intended for deletion and scrolling horizontally across the page to locate the Delete option. Upon selecting Delete, the system requires users to enter a deletion reason and confirm the action to complete the removal process. This document is intended for back office recruitment administrators or HR personnel who need to manage applicant records and remove applications from active vacancies within CorePersonnel. The related articles section indicates this document is part of a broader suite of recruitment management guides covering application handling, email notification issues, and form configuration tasks.

t: Unable to Merge Applications in 'Vacancy Maintenance' screen
s: The process runs out of memory when trying to merge a large number of applications simultaneously. The number of applications it is possible to merge at the same time will depend on how many documents per employee (CV, qualifications, images) are included. It is possible to generate a larger number ...
ss: The Vacancy Maintenance screen's merge applications function can run out of memory when processing large batches of applications simultaneously, particularly when employee records contain multiple documents like CVs, qualifications, or large image files. The number of applications you can merge at once depends on the volume and size of attached documents per employee—fewer applications with heavy documentation, more applications with minimal attachments. If you encounter merge failures or slowdowns, break the merge process into smaller batches of approximately 20 applicants at a time. Open this document if you're experiencing performance issues or errors when merging multiple applications in your recruitment workflow.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses a specific technical issue encountered when using the Vacancy Maintenance screen to merge multiple applications simultaneously. The core problem involves a memory constraint that occurs during the application merging process, particularly when attempting to combine large numbers of applicants at once. The severity of this issue is directly proportional to the volume of supplementary documents associated with each employee, such as CVs, qualifications, and images, as well as the file sizes of those documents—systems can process more applicants when documents are minimal but face constraints with larger or numerous files. Rather than attempting to merge all applications at one time, the recommended solution is to break the merging task into smaller batches of approximately 20 applicants per merge operation, adjusting the batch size based on the specific document load and system capacity. This document is particularly relevant for recruitment administrators or HR professionals who regularly work within the Vacancy Maintenance screen and need to consolidate applicant information. The guidance provided helps users understand both the root cause of the memory limitation and a practical workaround to successfully complete application merging tasks without system failures.

t: Link an applicant to internal record/employee
s:
In order to link an applicant to an employee record please follow the below instructions:

Navigate to Recruitment, Applicants

Search for the applicant

Click on the three dot ellipsis, View details

Select the Applicant Link at top right

On the left, in the Employee Link, search for employee

Sel...
ss: Linking an applicant to an employee record in the Recruitment module allows you to connect a job applicant with their corresponding employee profile in the system. Use this process when you've hired an applicant and need to establish the relationship between their recruitment record and their new employee record. If the employee name doesn't appear in the initial search, the system can find duplicate applicant numbers and link them automatically. Open this document when onboarding new hires or reconciling applicant and employee records in PeopleXD Recruitment.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for linking an applicant record to an existing employee record within the Access Group recruitment system. Users navigate to Recruitment, Applicants, search for the target applicant, and access their details via the three-dot ellipsis menu, then select the Applicant Link button at the top right of the screen. The linking process involves searching for the employee in the Employee Link field on the left side of the interface, selecting the matching employee, and confirming when the system prompts completion. The document addresses a specific error scenario where an employee name cannot be found in the initial search, which typically indicates that another applicant number is already assigned to that employee. To resolve this, users can search for the employee again using the Applicant Link field on the right-hand side, and if a duplicate applicant number appears, the system will automatically link both applicant numbers together and simultaneously link the associated employee record on the left side. This document is primarily used by recruitment administrators or HR staff who need to consolidate applicant records with their corresponding employee profiles during the hiring process.

t: Remove an application from recruitment Back Office
s:
To remove an application from Recruitment, follow the steps below. 

Set the applicant's status in the competition they have applied for to a unique status that no other applicant in any competition is currently on.

Select Recruitment, Recruitment Maintenance, Applicant Clear Down

In Start Date fi...
ss: Removing an applicant from Recruitment in the Back Office requires using the Applicant Clear Down function to delete their application record. First, assign the applicant a unique status code that no other applicant currently holds, then navigate to Recruitment Maintenance and run the Clear Down Applicants Report with the competition dates and status filter. You'll preview the report to confirm only the correct applicant is selected, then switch to Update mode to permanently remove the application from the system. Use this process when you need to fully delete an applicant's record from a recruitment competition.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for removing an application from the Recruitment module within the Access Group Back Office system. The process requires users to navigate to Recruitment > Recruitment Maintenance > Applicant Clear Down, where they must input specific competition dates and applicant status information to identify and remove the target application. Users must first assign the applicant a unique status code that no other applicant in any competition currently holds, then enter the competition's start date and today's date in the respective Start Date and End Date fields, followed by entering that unique status code in the Applicant Status field. The procedure includes a built-in safety mechanism requiring users to initially run the clear down process in Preview mode using the Submit Clear Down Applicants Report button to review results and confirm only the intended applicant record appears before proceeding. Once verification is complete, users must change the Mode Indicator from Preview to Update and submit the report again to finalize the application removal. This document is typically used by Recruitment Back Office administrators or staff who need to remove individual applicant records from the system, serving as an alternative to other deletion methods referenced in the related articles section.

t: Applicant offer details are incorrect
s:
Please amend the employee status back to the status it was prior to the offer and then update the applicant status to the offer again and make them a new offer.
Updating the original offer will not update the values held.
ss: When an applicant's offer details contain incorrect information in PeopleXD, you'll need to revert the employee status to its previous state before amending and reissuing the offer. This process is necessary because updating an existing offer won't automatically correct the values already recorded in the system. Open this document if you've discovered errors in offer details after they've been created and need step-by-step instructions to fix them without carrying forward the incorrect information.
sl: This document provides guidance on resolving issues when applicant offer details contain incorrect information within a recruitment or applicant management system. The resolution process requires a specific sequence of steps: first amending the employee status back to its previous state before the offer was made, then updating the applicant status to the offer stage again, and finally creating a new offer for the applicant. The document clarifies an important system behavior, noting that simply updating the original offer will not automatically update the values held in the system, meaning a complete refresh of the offer is necessary rather than a simple edit. This guidance is particularly relevant for HR administrators or recruitment staff who discover discrepancies in applicant offer information after an offer has been generated. The document addresses a common scenario where incorrect details may have been captured during the initial offer creation, requiring remediation through status reversion and offer recreation rather than direct modification. Users following this procedure should understand that the system requires the full workflow cycle rather than in-place updates to properly correct offer-related data.

t: Applicant country populated by the system
s:
This issue commonly occurs because every employee and applicant needs to be linked to an address template in order to be able to view them. These templates are linked to country codes.
If there is no country on the application, the system selects the country from the template that has the most recen...
ss: The applicant country field in PeopleXD Portal is automatically populated based on address templates linked to country codes, which every employee and applicant requires to view addresses. If an application lacks a country value, the system defaults to the country from the template with the most recent effective date. You'll need to configure the Portal parameter cp_volc_default_country with a valid country code through Administrator Dashboard > Site Manager > Admin Settings, or alternatively add country codes to address types in CorePersonnel Reference if the parameter alone doesn't resolve the issue. Open this document when applicants aren't displaying the correct country or when you're troubleshooting missing country population during application processing.
sl: This document addresses a common system issue where employees and applicants cannot be properly displayed because they lack the necessary country linkage required for address template visibility. The problem typically occurs when an application has no country specified, causing the system to default to the country from the address template with the most recent date_effective value. The document provides two solutions: the first involves configuring the Portal parameter cp_volc_default_country, which requires navigating to Administrator Dashboard > Site Manager > Admin Settings, searching for the parameter, editing it, entering a valid country code, and saving the changes. If this initial approach does not resolve the issue, users must add the country code directly to address types by accessing CorePersonnel > Reference > Reference A-C > Address Type Codes, then adding a new layout with an effective date later than the current date, selecting the country, ensuring the correct Address Type is assigned to Default Home Address, and adding a mandatory Country line before saving. This document is designed for system administrators or configuration personnel who manage Portal settings and address template configurations and need to troubleshoot applicant visibility issues related to missing or incorrect country assignments in the Access Group recruitment or HR system.

Open this document if an applicant needs to log in for the first time using a temporary password, or if you're supporting a candidate through their initial account setup. This is particularly useful when troubleshooting login issues or when applicants report they've received a temporary password but aren't sure how to proceed.
sl: This document provides instructions for resetting passwords for candidates and applicants within the Access Group system, specifically guiding users through the initial login process when a temporary password has been issued. The process requires applicants to navigate to the login screen and enter both their username and the temporary password they have received via email or other communication channels. Once applicants successfully log in using the temporary credentials, they are able to change the password to a permanent one of their own choosing, allowing them to customize their account access. The document addresses common scenarios where applicants need to regain access to their accounts or establish their initial login credentials after being added to the system. This resource is typically used by recruitment administrators, hiring managers, or support staff who need to help candidates troubleshoot login issues or understand the password reset workflow. The document also references related help articles covering related issues such as forgot password emails not sending in the E-Recruitment system, password change procedures for the agency portal back office, and email delivery problems specifically affecting Hotmail addresses, indicating it is part of a broader support documentation set for Access Group's recruitment platform.

t: Recruitment user getting the error 'Invalid Login Credentials' when registering on the recruitment website
s:
This error displays when the email address the user is trying to register the account with is already in use.

 

Resolution 1

The user will need to register the account using a different email address

Resolution 2

The user can navigate to the Login section of the recruitment site

From here they...
ss: When registering on the recruitment website, the "Invalid Login Credentials" error occurs because the email address you're trying to use is already associated with an existing account. You can resolve this by either registering with a different email address, or by using the Forgotten Password option on the Login section to unlock and reset the password for your existing account. Open this article if you're unable to complete registration due to email address conflicts or if you need to regain access to an existing recruitment account.
sl: This Access Group Help Centre document addresses the "Invalid Login Credentials" error that recruitment website users encounter during account registration. The error occurs specifically when a user attempts to register using an email address that is already associated with an existing account in the system. The document provides two distinct resolution paths for affected users. The first resolution directs users to simply register their account using a different email address instead of the one causing the conflict. The second resolution guides users through a password recovery process by navigating to the Login section of the recruitment site, selecting the Forgotten Password option, entering their email details when prompted, and then following a reset link sent to that email address to unlock the account and create a new password. This document is primarily useful for recruitment administrators, help desk staff, or end users who encounter this registration error and need to either use an alternative email or regain access to an existing account. The guide also references related articles on email delivery issues and data removal requests for users seeking additional support with recruitment site access.

The process involves navigating to the agency record and entering a new password, which the user will be prompted to change again on their next login. Open this guide if you're managing agency access and password resets from the back office administrator side.
sl: This document provides back office instructions for resetting or changing passwords for agencies within the Access Group portal system. The process involves navigating through specific menu sections: starting from Available Products, selecting CorePersonnel, then proceeding to Recruitment, followed by Recruitment Reference, and finally Recruitment Agencies. Once in the Recruitment Agencies section, administrators locate the specific agency record and enter a new password in the Login Password field before confirming the change by clicking Ok. An important operational note is that users will be prompted to reset their password again upon their first login after a password change has been made in the back office, ensuring security protocols are maintained. This document is typically used by back office administrators or agency managers who have the authority to manage agency portal access and credentials within the Core Personnel and Recruitment modules. The guide addresses the scenario where an agency's password needs to be updated or reset, whether due to forgotten credentials or routine password management procedures. Related support articles referenced in the document cover additional password-related issues such as forgot password emails not being sent in e-Recruitment and problems changing e-Recruitment email addresses or usernames in Core e-Recruit.

t: Unable to change e-Recruitment email address / username in Core e-Recruit
s:
This issue usually occurs because the Change E-recruitment Email Address / Username functionality is not enabled.

 

Step 1: Turn on Change Email Address Option

This will change the email address for the applicant for their applicant recruitment account - Switch on this option if you want to allow...
ss: Core e-Recruit applicants cannot change their email address or username because the functionality is typically disabled by default. This document walks through enabling the Change Email Address option in the Recruitment Admin portal, configuring the verification email alert that applicants receive after updating their email, and ensuring the required URL parameters are properly set in Core Personnel. Open this guide if your users are unable to modify their e-Recruitment email address for notifications and future applications, or if you need to set up the email change verification process.
sl: This document provides a step-by-step resolution guide for enabling users to change their email addresses and usernames in Core e-Recruitment when the functionality is disabled by default. The document describes three main configuration steps: first, enabling the Change Email Address option by navigating to Portal > Recruitment > Toolbox > Recruitment Admin > My Account and selecting specific fields including "Allowed change email address," "Change email section heading," "Old Email Address," "New Email Address," "Confirm Email Address," and various error message fields, with optional password requirement configuration. The second step involves configuring an automated Change Email Address Alert by navigating to Core back office through CorePersonnel > Recruitment > Recruitment Reference > E-Recruitment Web Parameters > Email Parameters > Applicant Email Change, where administrators can customize the verification email message sent to applicants after they update their address. The third step requires validating that the Applicant_Change_Email_URL parameter is properly populated with a valid URL in the Web Parameters section of the same menu path. This document is typically used by e-Recruitment administrators or Portal configuration managers who need to troubleshoot why applicants cannot modify their email addresses in the recruitment system. The guide also clarifies that internal applicants will always use their PeopleXD system email address and must create a new external applicant account if they wish to apply using a different email address.

t: Add Questions to an Existing Question Profile
s:
The Current Questions tab is where Questionnaires for the Vacancy can be configured.
In PORTAL:

Login to the Portal as Recruitment Admin

Vacancies Widget, Select Vacancy, Edit Vacancy

Vacancy Details, Current Questions

As well as assigning question categories that have been pre-populated in the ...
ss: The Current Questions tab in PeopleXD's recruitment portal lets you configure questionnaires for specific vacancies by adding custom questions beyond pre-populated question categories. When setting up questions, you'll define the answer type, sequence number, and flags like Active, Mandatory, and Private status to control how and when candidates see each question. Open this document if you need to add, activate, or manage interview or screening questions for a particular vacancy in the Portal's Vacancies Widget.
sl: This document provides instructions for adding custom questions to questionnaires associated with job vacancies within an e-Recruitment system. The primary process takes place in the Portal interface, accessible to users logged in as Recruitment Admin, where they navigate through the Vacancies Widget, select a specific Vacancy, choose Edit Vacancy, and then access the Vacancy Details section to reach the Current Questions tab. Users can add pre-configured question categories or create new custom questions by clicking the Add Question button, at which point they must enter the question text and select an appropriate Answer Type, with certain answer types requiring additional configuration such as designating an Unsuitable Answer for Yes/No questions. Each question requires configuration of a Sequence number to determine display order, and users must set status indicators including Active (to make the question available for use), Mandatory, and Private flags according to their requirements. After saving the question, users can manage existing questions through the Cog Wheel menu option next to each question to Activate/Deactivate it or view its complete details. The document also references the back-office configuration pathway through Core Personnel > Recruitment > Recruitment Reference > Question Category for accessing and managing question profiles at the system administration level. This document is primarily used by Recruitment Administrators who need to customize vacancy questionnaires with vacancy-specific questions beyond the standard pre-populated question categories.

t: Making a recruitment application form section mandatory
s:
In order to make this change you need to carry out the following steps:

Navigate to the Recruitment Dashboard

Select Toolbox, Open Recruitment Admin

On the screen that appears select a company from the Company Dropdown Menu

Select E-Recruitment Form from the Form Type Dropdown Menu

From the For...
ss: Recruitment application forms in the E-Recruitment system can be configured to require candidates to complete specific sections before submitting. You'll access the Recruitment Dashboard and Recruitment Admin toolbox to select your company and application form, then edit individual sections to make them mandatory. Depending on the section type, you can enable a mandatory indicator, require all questionnaire questions to be answered, or set a minimum number of entries for sections like References or Qualifications. Open this document when you need to enforce completion of particular form fields to ensure applicants provide essential information before progressing.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for making recruitment application form sections mandatory within the Access Group's recruitment system. Users navigate to the Recruitment Dashboard, access Toolbox and select Open Recruitment Admin, then proceed through a series of dropdown menus to locate and edit the desired application form by selecting a company from the Company Dropdown Menu, choosing E-Recruitment Form from the Form Type Dropdown Menu, and selecting the specific form from the Form Profile Dropdown Menu. Once the form is selected and Edit Profile is chosen, users can make individual sections mandatory by selecting Edit on the target section. The system offers three different methods for enforcing mandatory status depending on the section type: enabling a mandatory indicator for standard sections, enabling the All Questions Must Be Answered Indicator specifically for Questionnaire sections, or entering a minimum value of 1 or greater in the Min Number of Rows field for sections that allow multiple entries such as References and Qualifications. This document is primarily used by recruitment administrators and HR personnel who manage e-recruitment forms and need to enforce applicant compliance with required application sections. The related articles referenced suggest this functionality is part of a broader e-recruitment management system within the Access Group's Core e-Recruit application, which also handles tasks like question profile management, application removal, and form customization.

t: Amend applicant status codes
s:
Note: The below configuration changes will impact the system on a Global Level. As always if any configuration changes are to be made this needs to be completed first on a Test environment and confirmed to be working as expected before promoting to the Live Environment.
​
The Applicant Status Code i...
ss: Applicant Status Codes in CorePersonnel track candidates through recruitment stages like Applied, Offer, Acceptance, and Panel. Use this document when you need to create, modify, or configure these status codes in your recruitment process, particularly if you're setting up new statuses or linking them to specific indicators. You'll access this configuration through CorePersonnel > Reference > Applicant Status, and any changes must be tested in your Test environment before promoting to Live. This is essential for managing candidate progression and converting accepted applicants into employees.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on managing Applicant Status Codes within a recruitment system, which are essential for tracking applicants through various stages of the recruitment process. The document explains how to access these codes through the CorePersonnel menu by navigating to Reference, A-C, then Applicant Status, and describes five key status indicators: Applicant Applied (the default initial status for all applicants), Applicant Offer (assigned when an applicant is identified as successful), Applicant Acceptance (indicating a successful applicant has accepted the offer), Applicant Panel (for applicants placed on panels), and Online Enquiry Update (enabling interviewers to make online enquiries). Each of these indicators must be linked to one of the Applicant Status types, with AP - Applicant Applied being a mandatory record that cannot be removed. The document provides step-by-step instructions for inserting new records, including selecting Edit Mode, pressing the Green Plus icon on the toolbar, adding necessary details, optionally ticking indicators, clicking Save, and returning to the Main Menu via the Red Door icon. Importantly, the Applicant Acceptance Status is specifically required for successfully promoting an applicant to employee status. The document emphasizes that any configuration changes made to these codes will impact the system at a global level and must first be tested in a test environment before being promoted to the live environment. This document is primarily used by recruitment administrators and HR personnel responsible for configuring and maintaining the recruitment process workflow.

ss: Killer Questions in your Recruitment module allow you to set mandatory screening criteria that automatically disqualify applicants who answer incorrectly, helping you filter candidates at the vacancy level before they complete their full application. You'll use this feature through Portal by navigating to Recruitment > Toolbox > Recruitment Admin, then editing specific questions in your Application form's Questionnaire section to mark them as Killer Questions. Open this guide when you need to create hard-stop screening questions that prevent unsuitable candidates from progressing in your recruitment process.
sl: This document explains how to configure Killer Questions in a recruitment system, a feature that allows recruiters to automatically prevent applicants from proceeding if they provide certain answers. The document describes a specific process that can only be implemented at the vacancy level within the Portal system. To set up a Killer Question, users must navigate through the Portal menu path: Recruitment > Toolbox > Recruitment Admin, then select the Application form and expand the Questionnaire Section. Once in the Questionnaire Section, users locate the particular question they wish to convert to a Killer Question and click Edit on that question row. Within the question editing interface, users update the configuration option to designate which answer choice will stop the applicant from completing their application. This document is targeted at recruitment administrators or hiring managers who manage application forms and want to filter out applicants who provide disqualifying answers to specific screening questions. The feature helps automate the candidate screening process by removing unsuitable applicants before they fully complete their applications, saving time in the recruitment workflow.

ss: Managing vacancy questions in CorePortal's Vacancies Widget lets you add multiple answers beyond the standard 5-answer limit by navigating to a specific vacancy's details and editing the current questions section. Open this document when you need to expand answer options for recruitment screening questions or customize the question set for a specific vacancy.
sl: This document provides instructions for Recruitment Admins who need to expand the number of answers available for vacancy questions beyond the default limit of 5 using the CorePortal system. The process involves navigating through a specific menu path: logging into CorePortal as a Recruitment Admin, accessing the Vacancies Widget, selecting the relevant Vacancy, choosing Edit Vacancy, clicking on Vacancy Details, and then selecting Edit Current Questions. The document clarifies an important limitation: while users cannot directly edit or modify existing questions, they can deactivate questions using the active indicator field and add new questions as needed to accommodate additional answers. However, there is a critical constraint that prevents deactivation of questions if applicants have already submitted responses to those questions, which administrators must consider when managing question sets. This guidance is specifically designed for Recruitment Admins responsible for configuring and maintaining vacancy postings within the CorePortal recruitment module.

ss: Managing applicant statuses in the Recruitment dashboard allows you to create and configure custom status codes that track candidates through your hiring process. Open this guide when you need to establish status workflows, customize how candidates are notified of updates, or modify existing applicant status settings in your recruitment system.
sl: This document provides instructions for managing applicant statuses within a recruitment system, offering both video and step-by-step written guidance for users who need to create and configure these statuses. The core process involves accessing the Recruitment dashboard, navigating to the Toolbox tab, and using the Applicant Status option to add new statuses by entering a code and description while enabling the Active toggle. Once a status is created, users can expand the three-dot menu on the relevant status to access Status Details, where they can enable required toggles to customize the status behavior according to their needs. The document also covers email template configuration, which allows users to customize communications by accessing the Email Template option from the three-dot menu and entering custom subject lines and message bodies before saving. This functionality is particularly useful for organizations that need to maintain consistent communication with applicants at different stages of the recruitment process. The document appears designed for recruitment administrators or HR professionals who manage applicant workflows and need to ensure proper status tracking and automated email notifications are functioning correctly within their recruitment system.

sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving issues where applicant emails, particularly status update emails, fail to reach recipients through PeopleXD Recruitment despite appearing as sent in the email queue. The document outlines a specific configuration process that users access by navigating to the Administrator Dashboard from the dashboard menu, then opening Admin Settings via the Site Manager widget. The resolution involves locating and updating two configuration settings: cp_recruit_emailN and cp_recruit_emailE, both of which should be set to peoplexd@accessacloud.com. The document also requires users to verify that the EMS Username and Administrator Email fields contain matching values as part of the setup process. Additionally, users must navigate to the Document and Email Templates section and access the Email From Configuration tab to set the Recruitment Email Address to peoplexd@accessacloud.com. This document is typically used by administrators or support personnel managing PeopleXD Recruitment systems who need to diagnose and fix email delivery failures affecting applicant communications. The guide serves as a reference for ensuring proper email configuration within the system's administrative settings.

ss: Automatic email notifications are sent to applicants when their status is updated in the Recruitment module, provided the status has the 'Email Template after status change' indicator enabled. Open this document when you need to set up status-triggered emails, customize email templates, or understand how to send notifications when updating an individual applicant's status from the View Applicants screen. Note that emails only generate when status changes are made through the View Applicants screen, not through bulk update or other recruitment screens.
sl: This document provides comprehensive instructions for configuring and executing automated email notifications triggered by applicant status changes within a recruitment system. The feature works by enabling the 'Email Template after status change' indicator on specific applicant statuses, which is configured by navigating to the Recruitment Dashboard, accessing the My Recruitment Toolbox widget, opening Applicant Status, expanding the 3-dot menu to select Status Details, toggling on the Email Template after status change option, and saving changes. Users must then configure the email template itself by selecting Email Template from the same 3-dot menu, customizing the template content, and saving it. To generate an actual email notification, recruiters navigate from the Recruitment Dashboard to the Vacancies widget, expand Actions, select View Applicants for the applicable vacancy, then expand the applicant's 3-dot menu and choose Edit Status to update the status. Once the status is updated and confirmed with OK, an Email Template window automatically appears where the applicant's email address is pre-populated from their application, allowing users to modify the subject line, message body, attach documents if needed, and click Send. A critical limitation is that this automated email feature only functions when the Applicant Status is changed on the View Applicants screen for individual applicants; it will not generate emails when status updates occur on other screens such as Bulk Update, Interview Panel, Schedules, or Assign Applicants. This document is typically used by recruitment administrators and hiring managers who need to maintain communication with candidates throughout the application and hiring process.

t: Applicant not receiving alerts when new job is advertised
s:
If you clients aren't receiving job alerts, it's caused by an issue with the timing of the 2 Create and Send DBA Jobs in relation to these notifications.

Version 24 and above

We've made improvements in version 24 and above, where a new parameter sends emails immediately after notifications are cre...
ss: Job alerts in e-Recruitment aren't reaching applicants due to timing issues between the Create and Send DBA Jobs and notification processes. In version 24 and above, enable the "Send emails to applicants immediately after notifications have been created" parameter in Personnel > Recruitment > Recruitment parameters > Client parameters > Applicant Notifications to resolve this. For version 23 and below, you'll need to raise a support case with details about the affected vacancy, applicant, and previous successful notifications. Open this article if applicants aren't receiving job alerts despite being signed up for new vacancy notifications.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses the issue of applicants not receiving job alerts when new positions are advertised, diagnosing the problem as a timing issue between the two "Create and Send DBA Jobs" processes and notification delivery. For users running version 24 and above, the document provides a straightforward configuration solution: navigate to Personnel > Recruitment > Recruitment parameters > Client parameters, then enable the "Send emails to applicants immediately after notifications have been created" option within the Applicant Notifications section to ensure immediate email delivery. For users operating version 23 and below, the document directs them to raise a support case online while referencing the article title and providing three specific pieces of information: a new vacancy opened since the issue was reported, an applicant signed up for relevant events who should have received the alert, and an example of a previously successful "Jobs by Email / New Vacancy Notification" message. The document serves IT administrators, recruitment managers, and support staff who manage e-Recruitment system configurations and need to troubleshoot notification delivery failures affecting job seekers in the system. This guidance ensures that applicants subscribed to job alerts receive timely notifications when positions matching their criteria are advertised, maintaining the effectiveness of the recruitment notification process.

ss: Email notifications for job vacancies in eRecruitment require configuration at both the system level and user level. Administrators must enable the "Applicant Notifications" parameter in Recruitment Parameters, while applicants must activate "Switch on Email Notifications" in their My Account settings and select at least one vacancy alert preference (such as job titles, departments, or vacancy types). Open this document if applicants are not receiving vacancy alerts despite being registered in the system, or if you need to troubleshoot notification settings in eRecruitment.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving issues where applicants are not receiving email notifications for job vacancies in an Access Group recruitment system. It outlines a two-level configuration process: first, administrators must navigate to Recruitment > Reference > Recruitment Parameters > Client Parameter and ensure the checkbox for 'Applicant Notifications - Send emails to applicants immediately after notifications have been created' is enabled. Second, applicants must log into eRecruitment, access their My Account section, and activate the 'Switch on Email Notifications' checkbox. The document specifies that applicants must also tick at least one notification preference parameter—either 'Notify me when vacancies are closing,' 'new,' or 'unsubmitted'—to receive alerts. For applicants preferring consolidated communication, the 'Send one notification daily' option can be enabled to batch all vacancy notifications into a single email. Additionally, applicants have granular control over which types of vacancies trigger notifications through reference type filters in their My Account settings, such as job titles, departments, and vacancy types, which are customized per client. Applicants must select at least one of these reference type options and can use CTRL+Click to select multiple criteria in order to activate vacancy alerts. This document is essential for HR administrators, recruitment managers, and applicants troubleshooting notification delivery issues within the eRecruitment platform.

sl: This document addresses the issue of emails failing to deliver to Hotmail email addresses, a problem that typically stems from incorrect configuration settings in the system. The guide provides step-by-step instructions to resolve the issue by navigating to the EMS Parameter Maintenance screen, which is accessed through the Data Centre by clicking View All and then searching for and opening EMS Parameter Maintenance. The core problem occurs when the EMS Username field does not match the Administrator Email field—both should be set to peoplexd@accessacloud.com—and when these fields are misaligned, Hotmail classifies outgoing emails as junk mail, preventing them from reaching applicants' inboxes. This document is particularly relevant for administrators and support personnel managing the PeopleXD Recruitment system who encounter delivery failures specifically to Hotmail recipients. The document also cross-references related issues such as forgot password emails not sending in E-Recruitment and problems with changing e-Recruitment email addresses or usernames in the Core e-Recruit module, indicating this is part of a broader troubleshooting framework for the PeopleXD email and recruitment system.

sl: This document explains how to configure email notifications in the Back Office system that alert users when applicant application data has been successfully generated and merged into PDF format. sl: This document provides guidance on configuring internal vacancies in Volcanic so that they can be published and made visible to external candidates. The document addresses the specific scenario where recruitment teams need to ensure that vacancies marked as internal are properly configured to allow external visibility, which requires this particular setting to be enabled. By toggling on the Internal checkbox in the Discipline settings, users can control whether vacancies initially posted for internal candidates will also be accessible to external job seekers. The document is primarily intended for Volcanic administrators or recruitment team members responsible for managing vacancy visibility and access permissions within the system. Visual screenshots are included in the document to illustrate exactly where the Internal checkbox is located and how to interact with it, making the configuration process straightforward for users unfamiliar with this menu path.

s:

If there is a large number of these either in the description or on other free text fields, this can cause the system to reject the export.
