There might be an issue w...
ss: The Broadbean job posting integration in PeopleXD can fail during vacancy exports due to two main issues: special characters (trademark symbols, ampersands, hyphens) in job descriptions or free text fields that cause the system to reject the export, or invalid Broadbean API credentials stored in PeopleXD. Open this document when you encounter an error message referencing Broadbean integration and need to troubleshoot why job postings aren't syncing. You'll find guidance on reviewing job descriptions for problematic characters and instructions for contacting PeopleXD Support with the necessary credential parameters and debug logs to resolve authentication issues.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving integration errors that occur when exporting job vacancies to Broadbean, a job distribution platform integrated with the XD recruitment system. The document identifies two primary causes of export failures: the first relates to problematic characters and symbols in the Job Description field or other free text fields, such as trademark symbols, ampersands, and hyphens, which can cause the system to reject the export if they appear in large quantities. The second cause involves credential or authentication issues with the Broadbean connection parameters stored in XD, specifically the cp_bb_username, cp_bb_password, and cp_bb_apikey settings located in Admin Settings. When credential issues are suspected, users should contact Broadbean directly with the parameter values and error details extracted from the system's debug logs to diagnose the connection problem. The document advises users experiencing export failures to raise a support case with PeopleXD Support, providing the affected competition details and authorizing the support team to test the export process to Broadbean in order to generate and review logs that confirm the root cause of the error.

ss: Volcanic Custom Mapping in My Recruit Toolbox lets you control which fields from PeopleXD are sent to Volcanic as custom fields, such as automatically selecting the correct application form for each vacancy. You can map up to 5 custom fields using hierarchy fields or the new 'Recruitment Custom' field, and migrating customers can use this feature to replace their previously fixed custom fields. To set this up, you'll add reference data in PeopleXD under People Management > Reference Data > Recruitment Custom Data, ensure matching custom categories exist in Volcanic, and configure application forms in Volcanic to use 'Custom Category Options'. Open this document when you need to configure the Volcanic integration to automatically route job applications to the right form based on custom field values.
sl: This document explains how to configure the Volcanic Custom Mapping feature within My Recruit Toolbox, which allows users to specify which fields are transmitted to Volcanic as custom fields, such as automatically selecting the appropriate Volcanic application form for each vacancy. The integration supports a maximum of 5 custom fields, and users can select from any hierarchy fields plus a new 'Recruitment Custom' field option. For customers migrating from the previous system that used fixed custom fields, this new screen provides flexibility to choose which fields to use for the integration going forward. To implement job advert custom fields, users must first add reference data in PeopleXD by navigating to People Management > Reference Data > Recruitment Custom Data, and ensure matching custom categories are configured in Volcanic. Within Volcanic itself, administrators create application forms and link them to the PeopleXD custom fields by setting usage conditions on the application form to 'Custom Category Options'. To access both the Volcanic Custom Mapping option and the Job Advert Field Configuration screen, specific menu options must be enabled on user profiles: the Job Advert Field Configuration menu (ID: MAIN_MENU.APPLICANTCLEARDOWN) and the Volcanic Custom Mapping menu (ID: MAIN_MENU.VOLCANICMAPPING), both within the CorePortal system. This document is primarily used by recruitment administrators and system configurators who need to establish the integration between PeopleXD and Volcanic to customize how candidate application data flows between the two platforms.

t: Process a Right To Be Forgotten Request
s: GDPR gives individuals the right to ask organisations to delete their personal data. For example, if a candidate has registered on an organisation's website e.g. Careers Portal, or has submitted an application but been unsuccessful, they may request the right to be forgotten. The Right To Be Forgott...
ss: Processing Right To Be Forgotten requests in PeopleXD Recruitment allows you to delete candidate personal data in compliance with GDPR regulations. Use this process when applicants request data deletion—such as unsuccessful candidates or those who registered on your Careers Portal. Navigate to the My Recruit Toolbox widget on the Recruitment Dashboard, search for the candidate by name or email, and confirm deletion; note that only candidates without employee records and no accepted applications are eligible. The deletion removes all candidate data from PeopleXD ATS and eRecruitment, though data in the Volcanic-powered Careers Website and merged PDF packs require separate manual deletion.
sl: This document explains how to process Right to Be Forgotten requests in PeopleXD Recruitment, a feature that enables organizations to comply with GDPR regulations by deleting personal data for candidates who request it, such as unsuccessful applicants or those who registered on a Careers Portal. The process involves navigating to the My Recruit Toolbox widget on the Recruitment Dashboard, clicking Open on Right To Be Forgotten, searching for the applicant by name, applicant number, or email address, clicking Delete on the relevant row, and confirming the deletion by clicking Yes. Only eligible candidates appear on the Right To Be Forgotten screen—specifically those without an employee record (applicant record with a personnel number) and those without another application at the accepted stage. When a request is processed, the system deletes all candidate data held within the PeopleXD ATS (Portal View of PeopleXD Recruitment), the Generated PDF View of the Candidate Application, and candidate data held within the eRecruitment website, though data in the new Careers Website powered by Volcanic and merged PDF packs are not automatically deleted but can be removed separately. To access this feature, users must have specific menu options enabled on their profile: Delete rtbf (WS_RECRUITMENT_MENU.DELETE_RTBF) and Get rtbf (WS_RECRUITMENT_MENU.GET_RTBF) under Web Services, and Recruitment - Right to be forgotten (MAIN_MENU.RIGHTTOBEFORGOTTEN) under CorePortal. This document is used by recruitment administrators and HR personnel who need to fulfill legal deletion requests while ensuring data compliance across multiple integrated systems.

sl: This document explains how to report on applicant source information within PeopleXD Insight, enabling recruitment administrators to track which recruitment channels applicants used to apply. The document serves recruitment teams and managers who regularly need visibility into staff request activity and approval statuses, and it references related support articles for related tasks such as editing individual staff requests, managing access permissions, and troubleshooting missing buttons in the Back Office interface.

t: Report on internal/external for applicants
s:
There are 2 columns that can be used in Insight for reporting the type of applicant.
​
The first is Applicant type from Recruitment Applicant master. This will report on the applicants current status which include internal/external. If an applicant is External and they are hired after completing rec...
ss: Use the Applicant type and Application type columns in Insight to distinguish between internal and external applicants in your recruitment reporting. Applicant type tracks an applicant's current status in the Recruitment Applicant master, updating from External to Internal once they're hired. Application type reports their status for each specific job competition, which remains External even after hire until they apply for a new internal role. Choose Applicant type for overall applicant classification and Application type when you need to analyze recruitment activity by individual competition.
sl: This document explains two distinct reporting columns available in Insight for categorizing applicants as internal or external. The first column, Applicant type, is sourced from the Recruitment Applicant master and reflects an applicant's current overall status; when an external applicant is hired through recruitment, their status automatically changes to Internal. The second column, Application type, tracks the internal/external status specific to individual job applications rather than the applicant's overall record, meaning an applicant hired in one recruitment cycle remains marked as External for that particular competition unless they subsequently apply for another internal vacancy. Understanding the difference between these two columns is critical for accurate reporting, as they capture different aspects of applicant classification—one showing current global status and the other preserving historical application-level data. This document serves recruitment administrators and reporting users who need to distinguish between applicants' overall employment classification and their status within specific recruitment competitions. The guide references related functionality including applicant cleardown processes, applicant status email generation, internal vacancy application issues, and applicant source field reporting.

t: Getting 'Error(s) has been found while sanitizing data, further information available in logs'
s:
Error about sanitizing data is caused by ModSecurity. ModSecurity is an Application Firewall that filters, monitors, and blocks HTTP traffic to and from a web application. By inspecting HTTP traffic, it can prevent attacks stemming from webion, and security misconfigurations.
Items that are likely t...
ss: When entering data into the Access Group Portal, ModSecurity (an application firewall) blocks certain characters and text patterns to prevent security vulnerabilities, which triggers a "sanitizing data" error message. Common triggers include special characters like !=, <>, /bold, certain SQL-related terms, very long URLs, and hidden formatting characters copied from Word documents. Open this document when you encounter a sanitizing data error and need to identify which specific text or element is causing the block and learn how to reformat it. The troubleshooting steps guide you through isolating the problematic content by testing sections incrementally, rewording flagged terms, shortening URLs, or typing text directly in the Portal instead of copying from external sources.
sl: This document explains the root cause and resolution steps for the "Error(s) has been found while sanitizing data" message that users encounter in the Access Group system. The error is triggered by ModSecurity, an Application Firewall that inspects and filters HTTP traffic to the web application to prevent security threats such as SQL injection, cross-site scripting (XSS), and file inclusion attacks. Certain characters and syntax patterns are likely to trigger the firewall's blocking mechanism, including SRC, Style, !=, <>, and /bold formatting, though the document notes this is not an exhaustive list. Long URLs are also flagged as potential security risks and the document recommends using an online URL shortening service such as https://www.shorturl.at/ to resolve this issue. The document advises against copying and pasting text directly from Word documents into the Portal, as Word may contain hidden whitespace and non-Unicode characters that trigger the firewall; instead, users should type text directly into the Portal and apply formatting there. To troubleshoot, users should systematically copy and paste paragraphs into the portal to identify the problematic content, then type the text word-by-word while saving after every two or three words, and be aware that common words like "from" and "create" can sometimes trigger the error and may require rewording. This guidance is intended for Portal users who encounter data sanitization errors during normal data entry and submission workflows.

t: Error - 'Unable to Un-link Applicant as Applicant or Matched Applicant is currently Recruited or Appointed to a Post'

ss: The CorePersonnel system prevents unlinking an applicant when the associated Personnel Number has already been appointed or commenced in a post. Open this article when you're unable to unlink an applicant in your recruitment workflow and receive an error message about the applicant or matched applicant being recruited or appointed to a post.
sl: This document explains the error that occurs when users attempt to unlink an applicant in the recruitment system but cannot do so because the associated Personnel No in CorePersonnel has already been appointed or commenced in a Post. The resolution process involves multiple steps that require both system support intervention and manual user actions within the recruitment interface. First, users must raise a new support case online referencing this article's title and providing specific details about the Personnel No and the Post that needs to be reverted to remove the employee attachment. Support staff will then execute database scripts to address the underlying data issue. Once support completes their work, users should unlink the Personnel No from the Applicant No using the standard unlinking procedure, followed by consulting the related PeopleXD People Management article titled "Deleting an employee set up in error when updating the incorrectly created Personnel No" to properly correct the mistakenly created Personnel record. After these steps are completed, users will be able to link the existing Applicant to the correct Personnel No, resolving the recruitment record linking issue. This document is primarily used by recruitment administrators or HR personnel who encounter obstacles when managing applicant records that have been inadvertently linked to active employee positions.

This document is primarily useful for erecruit administrators and form editors who encounter this validation error while attempting to save or modify form content, helping them understand that they must remove or avoid pasting HTML code into text fields to successfully complete their edits.

Open this document if you need to troubleshoot why Application Details appear empty or inaccessible, or if you need instructions on attaching an application form to enable managers to view applicant responses.
sl: This document addresses a specific issue where managers cannot view application details for applicants who have applied for a vacancy in the Access Group recruitment system. The problem occurs when the Default Application Form field is left blank in the Recruitment Dashboard under Vacancies > Edit Vacancy > Vacancy Details 1, which means no application form has been attached to that vacancy. When a manager attempts to select Application Details for an applicant, the application form will not display because there is no form linked to the vacancy, and this is confirmed as expected system behavior rather than a malfunction. To resolve this issue and enable managers to view application details, administrators must attach an application form to the vacancy through the Vacancy Details configuration screen. The document also references a specific menu item that must be active to support this functionality: Menu option reference no - 593867830 (MAIN_MENU.VIEW_APPLICANTS_APPLICATION_DETAILS), which managers need enabled in order to access applicant application details. This guidance is primarily intended for recruitment administrators and hiring managers who encounter situations where application form content fails to appear when reviewing applicant submissions. The Restriction Active parameter must be enabled when the Creator Role is in use and disabled when it is not being utilized, ensuring the permission rules function as intended. If the required organisational role is not yet assigned to a user, administrators must assign the relevant role through the organization's role assignment process. This document is primarily used by system administrators and recruiters who need to set up or troubleshoot staff request creation access, particularly when the Create Staff Request button is missing or when controlling who can initiate staffing requests across the organization.

ss: Vacancy visibility in CorePortal is controlled by the "Vacancy Restriction Override" menu item setting within user menu profiles. When this setting is enabled, users can view vacancies and applicant details even if they're not authorized in the vacancy's restriction configuration. If you need to prevent unauthorized users from accessing specific vacancies, you'll need to disable this menu item so that only users selected in the Authorization screen can view restricted vacancies. Open this document when you discover users viewing vacancies they shouldn't have access to or when you need to enforce vacancy visibility restrictions.
sl: This document explains a specific access control issue in the CorePortal recruitment system where users can view vacancies they should not have permission to access. The root cause is that users have the menu item "CorePortal - Vacancy Restriction Override" (System=CorePortal) enabled in one of their assigned menu profiles, which bypasses the normal vacancy restriction configuration settings. When this menu item is ticked, affected users gain the ability to open and view restricted vacancies and access associated details through the Applicant Details screens, regardless of whether they are listed in the Authorization screen. To properly enforce vacancy restrictions and prevent unauthorized users from viewing confidential or restricted vacancies, administrators must disable the "CorePortal - Vacancy Restriction Override" menu item for those users. This document is typically used by recruitment administrators and system configurators who manage portal access permissions and need to troubleshoot why vacancy visibility controls are not working as expected. The document references the CorePortal system and its authorization and menu profile configuration mechanisms as the primary areas where access control is managed.

Open this document when users report missing vacancies or when you need to troubleshoot recruitment visibility problems.
sl: This document addresses the issue of users being unable to view some or all vacancies in the Vacancies tab within CorePortal, which can occur due to insufficient user access permissions or system timeout problems caused by excessive open vacancies. The document provides two distinct resolution paths depending on the root cause: first, it explains how to check and modify user access through the back office system by navigating to CorePersonnel > Reference > Reference Q-Z > System Users, then searching for the user's personnel number and managing their Security Type settings under REC - Recruitment Access. Alternatively, users can manage recruitment access via the portal by accessing the People Management dashboard, navigating to Data Centre > View All, locating HR user access, and enabling or disabling the relevant recruitment access options for the employee. For issues related to CorePortal timing out due to excessive open vacancies, the document recommends closing older open vacancies through the back office to improve system performance. This document is designed for HR administrators, recruitment managers, and CorePersonnel system users who need to troubleshoot vacancy visibility issues for themselves or other employees within their organization. ss: When a vacancy isn't displaying in the recruitment portal, it's typically caused by missing access permissions for the HR Admin user. Check whether the HR Admin has been granted "Recruitment Access" for the relevant department in CoreHR Back Office or through the People management dashboard's HR User access settings. If the department is marked as sensitive, you'll also need to grant "Sensitive Department Access" separately using the same tools. This document walks you through both permission checks and how to enable access in either CoreHR or the portal interface.
sl: This document explains how to resolve the issue of vacancies not displaying in the recruitment portal admin section, identifying two root causes related to user access permissions in a CoreHR system. The first cause occurs when an HR Admin user lacks access to the relevant department for the Recruitment Access Security Type, while the second cause occurs when the department is classified as sensitive and the user lacks Sensitive Department Access permissions. To resolve the first issue, administrators can navigate to CoreHR Back Office through CorePersonnel > Reference > Reference Q-Z > System Users, ensure the Portal Account option is selected, locate the HR Admin user by personnel number, and enable "Access granted" for the required department under Recruitment Access security types; this same task can alternatively be completed from the People Management Dashboard by accessing Data Centre > View all > search access > HR User access. To resolve the second issue involving sensitive departments, administrators must access System Users in CoreHR Back Office, select Sensitive Department as the Security Type, grant access to the appropriate department, and save the changes—with the caveat that if the department does not appear in the list, it is not classified as a sensitive department. The same Sensitive Department Access permissions can be managed through the Portal's People Management Dashboard using the equivalent path of Data Centre > View all > search access > HR User access. This document is intended for HR administrators and system administrators who manage recruitment portal access and user permissions within the CoreHR system and need to troubleshoot visibility issues with job vacancies.

ss: When a newly created vacancy isn't displaying in the system, it's typically due to incomplete mandatory setup steps. sl: This document addresses the problem of newly created vacancies failing to appear in the system, which typically occurs when required setup steps have not been fully completed. Additionally, users should verify that the restricted indicator has not been activated, as this setting can prevent vacancy visibility. The document is designed for recruitment staff or administrators who create new job vacancies and need to troubleshoot why their newly created vacancies are not appearing to recruiters or candidates. By systematically checking each of these mandatory requirements, users can identify which step was missed and complete it to make the vacancy visible in the system. sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving issues when competitions cannot be located in the Competition Detail Screen within CorePersonnel's recruitment module. It identifies seven distinct causes of this problem, ranging from missing configuration data to access permission issues, and provides specific resolutions for each scenario. For the most straightforward causes, users can resolve the issue independently by navigating to specific menu paths such as Personnel > Reference Q-Z > System Users to grant Recruitment access to a department, or Personnel > Recruitment > Reference > Recruitment User Profile to assign Post Administrator privileges. Other causes require administrative intervention, such as when a Competition's start date was not entered during creation, when the Restricted option was enabled on the Competition Detail screen (accessed via Personnel > Recruitment > Maintenance > Competition Detail), or when the Post Administrator has been removed from the system. Two causes—invalid characters in the "Unsuitable Answer Option" database field and improperly configured Internal, External, and Recruitment Open Times that are not set at 15-minute intervals—require users to submit support cases with reference to this article title. This document is typically used by recruitment administrators and Personnel module users who encounter visibility or access issues when attempting to view or manage competition records in the system.

s:

Employees can be added to these Talent Pools in HR Admin, from a given Date Added. An employee can be a member of many Talent Pools if ...
ss: Talent Pools in Recruitment let you organize and group employees and applicants based on your organization's needs, with each person able to belong to multiple pools. You can assign employees to Talent Pools in HR Admin with a start date, and these assignments automatically display in Recruitment when those employees apply for vacancies. Open this document to learn how to view which Talent Pools an employee belongs to and when they were added, using the employee dashboard in the system. Talent Pool memberships are managed at the person level rather than tied to specific contracts or positions.
sl: This document explains what Talent Pools are in the Access Group recruitment system and how to view them for individual employees. Talent Pools and Talent Pool Categories are configurable features in the Recruitment module that allow organizations to define and group sets of employees or applicants according to their specific requirements. Employees can be added to Talent Pools in HR Admin with a specified Date Added field, and a single employee can belong to multiple Talent Pools simultaneously. When an employee who is a member of a Talent Pool applies for a vacancy through Recruitment, an applicant record is created and that Talent Pool membership becomes visible to recruitment administrators in the relevant Talent Pool options within the Recruitment module. Importantly, Talent Pools are managed at the Person level on the system, meaning they are directly associated with employee or applicant records rather than linked to Post Appointments or Contracts. To view an employee's Talent Pool assignments, users click the ellipsis icon next to the employee record, select View Dashboard, navigate to the second page of the dashboard, and click on the Talent Pool option, which displays both the total number of assigned pools and a detailed list showing each pool membership along with the date the employee was added. This functionality is particularly useful for recruitment administrators and HR professionals who need to review candidate pools and manage talent strategically across the organization.

This is particularly relevant for users managing expense claims who need to understand that changing the trip report cost centre alone is insufficient—each individual expense item must also be updated to ensure consistency. ss: Use this resource to find the correct benefit in kind (BIK) tax rates when calculating taxable vehicle values for employees. The document provides separate lookup tables based on vehicle registration date and CO2 emissions or engine capacity, with rates that vary by tax year from 2021/22 through 2026/27. sl: This document provides the current benefit in kind (BIK) rate tables used to calculate vehicle cash equivalent values for tax purposes, with rates loaded automatically as part of the year end software delivery. The document is organized into four distinct vehicle categories: cars first registered on or after 6 April 2020, cars first registered before 6 April 2020, cars registered on or after 1 January 1998 without an approved CO2 emissions figure, and all cars registered before 1 January 1998. For vehicles registered from 6 April 2020 onwards, BIK rates are determined by CO2 emissions (g/km) and electric range (miles), with separate percentage rates provided for the tax years 2023/24, 2024/25, 2025/26, and 2026/27, ranging from 2% for zero-emission vehicles to a maximum of 37% for high-emission vehicles. A critical note indicates that a 4% diesel car tax supplement applies to non-RDE2 compliant diesel vehicles, capped at a maximum of 37%. For pre-6 April 2020 vehicles, the rates table covers tax years 2021/22 through 2024/25 using the same CO2 and electric range parameters. For older vehicles without approved CO2 figures or registered before 1998, BIK rates are determined solely by engine capacity in cubic centimeters, with percentages ranging from 24% for engines under 1400cc to 37% for engines over 2000cc and all rotary engines. This document serves payroll and HR professionals who need to accurately determine taxable benefits on company cars and those configuring vehicle benefit calculations within the Access Group payroll system.

ss: The 'Available From' date for company cars in Core Expense's car administration centre may disappear after processing your Year End Rollover—this occurs because the system automatically clears this field when no 'Available To' date is set, then resets it to the start of the new tax year. During Year End Rollover, several car BIK values reset including the Available From date, Days car unavailable, and Dates Free Fuel Provided. Open this document if your company car's Available From date has vanished after year end processing and you need to understand why the system clears and recalculates this field automatically. This explains the expected behaviour and clarifies when to manually input Available To dates versus when the system handles dates automatically.
sl: This document explains a specific data behavior in Core Expense's car administration center that occurs when users process their Year End Rollover, particularly addressing why the 'Available From' date field disappears from company car records. During the Year End Rollover process, three car benefit-in-kind (BIK) values reset automatically: Available From (available_from), Days car unavailable (days_car_unavailable), and Dates Free Fuel Provided (dates_free_fuel_prov). The document clarifies that when the Expense Year End is completed, the system automatically clears the Available From date whenever no 'Available To' date is populated, and subsequently sets the Available From date to the start of the new tax year to eliminate manual data entry requirements at the beginning of each tax year. In contrast, the Available To date is intentionally preserved during Year End Rollover; if an Available To date exists, it indicates the car has been returned and the record is complete, and new Available To dates should only be entered when a car is actually returned. Users managing company car records in Core Expense's car administration center who conduct year-end processes need this information to understand expected system behavior and to know when to create new records for vehicles that become available again by updating the Vehicle Cash Equivalent field.

For expense codes classified under the Travel and Subsistence category, the configuration requires an additional step of selecting a subcategory to ensure proper categorization. Users need to repeat this assignment process for all expense codes that should be included in the final ERR report, then click OK to save the changes. This configuration task is one component of a broader ERR setup procedure that also requires users to configure expense company parameters, claimant parameters, expense group parameters, and load digital certificates before the system is ready to generate and transfer reports. The document is intended for back office administrators or finance personnel responsible for implementing Enhanced Reporting Requirements compliance within their organization.

sl: This document provides instructions for loading ROS Digital Certificates required for Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) functionality in PeopleXD Payroll and PeopleXD Expense systems. The document explains that ERR is an additional permission layer under the employer ROS certificate that Revenue automatically applies to employer certificates and can be assigned to sub-certificates through the ROS permissions screen. It addresses deployment scenarios specific to whether PeopleXD Payroll and PeopleXD Expense operate on the same database or separate databases, requiring users to upload the ERR digital certificate in both systems only when they run independently. The main process involves navigating to Expense > Update > Enhanced Reporting Requirements > 05 - Load Digital Certificate, then entering the company code in the Expense Company field, selecting the relevant company tax registration from a dropdown menu, entering the certificate password, and browsing to select the .p12 file downloaded from ROS. A critical prerequisite highlighted is that the digital certificate file must have a .p12 file extension; otherwise, PeopleXD Expense cannot recognize it. This document is intended for payroll administrators, finance teams, and system users who manage employer tax compliance and need to configure ERR permissions for multiple companies within their PeopleXD systems. The document serves as part of a broader ERR configuration workflow and references related articles covering ERR run checks, file transfers to Revenue, and parameter configuration for both claimants and expense groups.

ss: Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) is a Revenue compliance process that requires you to submit employee payment details starting January 2024. This checklist guides you through the four key stages: granting user access to ERR screens, configuring your software, retrieving ERNs post year-end, generating the ERR file, and transferring it to Revenue. sl: This document is a checklist designed to guide users through the implementation of Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR), a mandatory reporting process introduced by Revenue starting in January 2024 that requires submission of employee payment details. The checklist breaks down ERR processing into four distinct stages: granting user access to ERR screens during the pre-year-end phase, configuring the software before year-end, and then post-year-end activities that include retrieving ERNs (Employee Reference Numbers), generating the ERR file, and transferring the completed ERR file to Revenue. Several configuration parameters must be established prior to submission, specifically relating to expense codes, expense company settings, claimant details, and expense groups, along with the loading of digital certificates required for the ERR process. This checklist is intended for payroll and HR professionals responsible for managing employee payment reporting and compliance with Irish Revenue requirements, and it serves as a starting point before users consult the more detailed ERR FAQs article and related configuration guides also provided by the Access Group Help Centre.

Within this screen, users can update three key fields: the Exclude Claimant checkbox to remove specific employees from expense ERR returns; the Company Tax Registration field to input a Company Tax Registration Number Override that takes precedence over company-level settings; and the Employment ID field to record an override when submitting ERR returns for a different employment ID than the one currently registered with revenue. The document addresses a specific configuration scenario where employees need to be excluded from ERR submissions, and notes that exclusions for Payroll ERR returns must be configured separately on the ERR Employee Parameters screen within the Payroll system. ss: The Check ERR Run process validates Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) submission files in your back office when you've submitted multiple ERR files for the same period. It retrieves overall ERR totals for that period so you can reconcile your submissions and identify any errors in the expenses through the generated JSON file. Use this process when you need to verify the status of your ERR submissions—whether they're completed with valid expenses, completed with errors requiring correction in PeopleXD Payroll, or still pending validation at Revenue. Open this guide when you're ready to run the Check ERR Run from the Expense > Update > Enhanced Reporting Requirements menu.
sl: This document provides guidance on the Check ERR Run process, which is used when organizations have submitted multiple Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) submission files for the same period and need to reconcile the overall ERR totals for that period. The process is accessed through the back office by navigating to Expense > Update > Enhanced Reporting Requirements, then selecting "Check ERR Run" from the Generate/Transfer drop-down menu. Users must select the relevant company from the Company Tax Registration drop-down menu, enter a run reference in the Run Reference field, choose a file generation location, and click Check Expense Run to generate the response file. The Check ERR Run process produces a response file that assigns each expense one of three statuses: "Completed - all valid expenses" indicates successful validation and completion; "Completed - invalid expenses" means errors exist that can be reviewed in the generated JSON file and must be corrected in PeopleXD Payroll before generating and transferring a new ERR file to Revenue; and "Pending" indicates the submission is awaiting validation at Revenue. This document is primarily used by finance and payroll professionals who manage ERR submissions and need to verify the accuracy and status of their expense data before final submission to tax authorities.

t: Transfer the (ERR) file to Revenue
s:
In every expense run where you've processed ERR qualifying payments, you need to report the values to Revenue on or before the date you pay the employees.

Once you've generated the file in PeopleXD Expense, to transfer it to Revenue, follow the steps below in back office.

ss: Transferring ERR (Enhanced Reporting Requirements) submission files from PeopleXD Expense to Revenue is a compliance requirement you must complete on or before the date you pay employees for expense runs with qualifying payments. This process involves navigating to the Enhanced Reporting Requirements section in back office, selecting your expense company and groups, and uploading the generated file to Revenue. After transfer, you'll receive a status update (Acknowledged, Rejected, or Pending) and can use the Run Check function if needed to request updates without re-submitting. Once the transfer is confirmed and any corrections are processed, you must mark the submission as confirmed in the system to complete the compliance task.
sl: This document provides instructions for transferring Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) files to Revenue through the PeopleXD Expense system's back office, a mandatory process that must be completed on or before the date employees are paid for each expense run containing ERR-qualifying payments. The transfer process involves navigating to Expense > Update > Enhanced Reporting Requirements, selecting "Transfer Submission Files" from the Generate/Transfer dropdown menu, entering the relevant expense company code, selecting the Transfer File checkbox for each applicable expense group, choosing a save location via Browse, and then clicking Transfer to send the file to Revenue. After submission, the Status column displays one of three responses: "Acknowledged" indicates successful receipt by Revenue, "Rejected" means Revenue has declined the file with a stated reason, or "Pending" signifies the file has been transferred but not yet processed—and in the Pending status, users should click Run Check to request an update rather than re-generating and re-transferring the file. For situations involving multiple submissions in the same period, such as original and correction submissions, the document recommends completing a Check ERR Run process before proceeding to the confirmation stage. The confirmation process requires returning to Expense > Update > Enhanced Reporting Requirements, selecting "Transfer Submission Files," entering the expense company code, selecting the Confirmed checkbox for the relevant submission, and clicking Save followed by Yes to finalize the transfer. This document is designed for payroll and expense administrators who need to ensure compliance with Revenue reporting requirements and manage the submission lifecycle within the PeopleXD system.

ss: When you amend an employee's pay date after submitting an ERR file to Revenue, you need to generate a Full Resubmission File in back office to report those changes. You can generate this file at the expense group or individual employee level for either the current period or a previous period. The Full Resubmission File only includes amendments made since Revenue accepted your original ERR file, so if you haven't submitted a normal file yet, you'll need to do that instead. Open this guide when you've made pay date changes and need to resubmit your ERR data to ensure Revenue has your updated information.
sl: This document provides instructions for generating a Full Resubmission ERR (Enhanced Reporting Requirements) file in the back office system when an employee's pay date has been amended after the original ERR file was already submitted to Revenue. The file can be generated at either the expense group level or for individual employees, and it contains only amendments made since Revenue accepted the normal ERR file for that period. For the current period, users navigate to Expense > Update > Enhanced Reporting Requirements, select Generate Submission File from the Generate/Transfer dropdown, then choose Full Resubmission from the Submission Type dropdown, enter the expense group code, and optionally specify a Company Tax Registration Number and individual employee reference in the Claimant field. For previous periods, the process is similar but requires selecting the Previous Run Number checkbox in the 02 - Expense Group Parameters section and selecting Normal Submission instead of Full Resubmission from the Submission Type dropdown. The document notes that if no normal file was previously submitted, users should submit a normal file instead of following these steps. An Override Payment Date field is available in both processes to adjust dates if needed before generating the file. This document is typically used by back office administrators and payroll personnel who manage expense groups and need to correct and resubmit employee pay information to the tax authority after initial submission.

s:
The ERN provides non-payroll systems with the employment ID information Revenue holds on individual employees.

You don't have PeopleXD Payroll or

You have PeopleXD Payroll held on a different database to PeopleXD Expense.

ss: The ERN (Employment Reference Number) process enables PeopleXD Expense to retrieve and sync employment ID information from Revenue for employees, which is essential when you don't have PeopleXD Payroll or when your Payroll and Expense systems use different databases. Open this document when you need to generate ERN certificates, retrieve them from Revenue via ROS, upload Revenue responses back into PeopleXD, and update employee records with the latest employment information. The guide walks through each step including generating claimant ERNs, submitting files to Revenue, loading responses, and maintaining records to ensure duplicate entries are cleared. You won't need this process if your PeopleXD Payroll and Expense already share the same database, as employment IDs sync automatically.
sl: This document provides instructions for retrieving and uploading Employment Reference Numbers (ERNs) in PeopleXD Expense, which supplies non-payroll systems with employment ID information held by Revenue for individual employees. Users need to retrieve and upload ERNs if they lack PeopleXD Payroll entirely or if their PeopleXD Payroll database is separate from their PeopleXD Expense database, though the process is unnecessary when both systems share the same database. The document outlines a four-part workflow beginning with generating claimant ERNs by navigating to Expense > Reference > Reference CC > Claimant Bulk ERN, selecting Generate Claimant ERN, choosing a company via the Tax Register Number dropdown, and saving the file to a location of choice. The second phase involves retrieving the ERN file from Revenue by logging into ROS, selecting "Request ERN's by file upload," uploading the previously generated file, entering credentials, and signing and submitting the request. The third phase requires uploading Revenue's response file back into PeopleXD Expense through the same menu path (Expense > Reference > Reference CC > Claimant Bulk ERN), selecting Upload Revenue Response, and locating the response file on the user's computer. The final phase includes maintaining and updating claimant ERN records through the Maintain Claimant ERN and Update ERN Details options accessed via the same menu structure, which generates and uploads employment IDs for new or existing employees, along with a Cleardown Records function to remove duplicates if multiple ERN requests are run without completing the update process. This document is primarily used by PeopleXD Expense administrators or finance teams responsible for managing employee reference data and ensuring compliance with Revenue requirements.

Once configured, when generating Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) Submission files, both the Company Tax Registration Number and the Payroll Company name will appear in the drop-down list, allowing users to select the appropriate Company Tax Registration Number to generate files using the Expense digital certificate instead of the Payroll certificate. This document is primarily used by finance or HR administrators who manage multiple digital certificates across different modules within the Access Group system and need to maintain separate credentials for Payroll and Expense functions for Enhanced Reporting Requirements submissions.

sl: This document provides instructions for generating Delete Submission Files in PeopleXD Expense for Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR), which are required in three specific scenarios: when an employee or expense group was incorrectly included in a submission, when a submission file was generated and transferred twice for the same period by mistake, or when deleting a submission file for a previous period. The process involves accessing the back office, navigating to Expense > Update > Enhanced Reporting Requirements, and selecting Generate Submission File from the Generate/Transfer dropdown menu, followed by selecting Delete Submission from the Submission Type dropdown. Users must enter the relevant expense group code and decide whether to leave the Company Tax Reg Number field blank to generate output files for all associated company TRNs and employees within the expense group, or select a specific company TRN to generate a single file. The instructions vary slightly depending on the scenario: for individual employees returned in error, users enter the employee reference in the Claimant field and can optionally override the payment date; for expense groups returned in error or duplicate files, users select where to save the file using Browse; and for previous periods, users must first enable the Previous Run Number checkbox in the Expense Group Parameters section before generating the deletion file. After generating the Delete Submission File, users must transfer it to Revenue following the standard transfer process, which is referenced in the related articles section alongside additional resources for ERR configuration and management.

Second, they must go to Reference > Reference S-Z > User Maintenance, add a new entry with the ORACLE Username field populated, and critically set the Approval Indicator field to "A" to enable approval permissions. The document assumes that back office user setup has already been completed; if not, users must complete that prerequisite configuration first. This guide is intended for system administrators or managers who manage back office user permissions and need to grant or restore claim approval capabilities to team members, serving as a troubleshooting resource for access control issues within the expense management system.

ss: FRM-41214 error appears during expense run validation in CoreExpense Back Office when the system detects that a process has already been executed. If any required process steps are missing from the log, you'll need to complete them before closing out the expense run. Open this document when you encounter validation errors and need to verify which expense processes have already run and identify what's still pending.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for the FRM-41214 error that occurs on the expense run validation detail screen in Back Office, typically caused by an expense process that has already been executed. Users can verify whether a process has previously run by navigating to Back Office, selecting CoreExpense, then accessing Tools > Process Logs to search for their specific expense group and current run number. The document outlines seven key processes that should appear in the process log when an expense run progresses normally: Submitted EXP4000 (displayed after generating payment claims), Validation Complete (shown when the validation run process executes), Paypath Generated (appearing after the create paypath data process), SP Timesheets Passed (an optional process visible only if the organization uses it), Complete Update (displayed when running the complete cheque update), Ledger INT (shown during Interface processing), and Update Submitted (appearing after the validation process completes). If any of these expected processes are missing from the log, the user must manually complete those missing steps in order to successfully close the expense run. This document is intended for Back Office users and finance teams managing expense runs who encounter validation errors and need to diagnose whether processes have been properly completed in sequence.

The document serves as a troubleshooting resource for resolving approval bottlenecks caused by exceeding the system's line-item capacity, helping users understand both why the error occurs and what corrective action is required to proceed with the expense approval process.

The document also instructs users to verify the employee's effective salary date by accessing CorePersonnel > Maintenance > Personnel Profile, selecting the employee from the Personnel No field, and reviewing Salary Details from the Select Detail dropdown to confirm the appointment is active. A critical constraint mentioned is that if the effective date is in the future, the claimant cannot be created yet. If these troubleshooting steps do not resolve the issue, users are directed to raise a new case online while referencing the article title and providing specific claimant details including the Expense Group, Input Location, Pay Method, Scale Code, and Scale Class. This document is primarily used by back office administrators or support staff who manage claimant setup and configuration within the Access Group expense management system.

ss: When submitting an expense item in CoreExpense, you may encounter a form error due to special characters in your receipt filename or because Duplicate Detection is disabled in back office. sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses the "Error: Please review the form for errors" message that users encounter when attempting to submit expense items in the CoreExpense system. The error stems from two primary causes: improper receipt file naming conventions or the disabling of the duplicate items detection feature in back office. For receipt file name issues, users must remove special characters such as apostrophes from the filename before uploading, as the system does not accept special characters in receipt filenames. For duplicate item problems, administrators need to enable the Duplicate Detection option in back office, which can be configured to identify duplicate entries based on date, time, or cost centre criteria, preventing employees from submitting multiple expense items with identical values. The configuration process involves navigating to CoreExpense > Reference > Reference S-Z > System Parameters, then selecting the appropriate Duplicate Detection option under the Common Tab. This document is primarily used by expense system administrators and finance teams who manage the CoreExpense back office settings, as well as employees who encounter submission errors and need to correct their receipt file naming or understand why duplicate submissions are being rejected.

The resolution involves checking employee setup, contacting support to have the affected employee's claim removed from the expense run, and then revalidating and regenerating the ERR file.
sl: This document addresses a specific error message—"Error calling py_err.payroll_submission Employee ALL at location L error ORA-01403: no data found"—that occurs when users attempt to submit an ERR file within an expense management system. The error stems from underlying issues with employee data, typically caused by modifications made to employee records during an active expense run, such as changes to an employee's expense group or pay group assignments. To diagnose the problem, users should first check for newly added employees in the expense run to verify they have been properly configured as claimants, and then review whether any existing employees have had their expense group or pay group altered during the current run. Once the problematic employee or employees have been identified, users must raise a support case online, referencing the article title and the affected employee number, after which the support team will remove the employee's claim from the expense run. Following the removal of the expense trip and associated claim data, users should run the validation process again and then regenerate the ERR file. This document is intended for payroll and expense management administrators or finance professionals who work with ERR file submissions and need to resolve data integrity issues that prevent successful payroll processing.

ss: Use this document to bulk upload P11D tax benefit details for multiple employees via CSV file in Core Expense. sl: This document explains how to perform bulk updates to employee P11D tax benefit details using a CSV file upload process within the Core Expense system. The document specifies critical formatting requirements, including populating the sections column for every entry, configuring your computer to use commas as list delimiters, and entering car numbers sequentially in column 32 AF (with at least 1 required, and odd-numbered cars appearing in the Car1 column while even-numbered cars appear in Car2). If the exception report reveals errors, users must amend the incorrect records in the CSV file and repeat the upload process until no errors exist; successful uploads with no errors produce no report, indicating the data has loaded correctly. The system allows multiple CSV uploads per company (with each new upload overwriting the previous one), maintains historical data by year so prior years remain accessible, and the uploaded data can be viewed on the Create/Maintain P11D Details screen where it is labeled with the data source "UPLOAD." Additional specifications include treating cash equivalents for vans and van fuel as separate records, using specific XML transfer values for Section M (M4-M9 for Class 1A items and M10-M15 for non-qualifying Class 1A items), and ensuring M3 Tax Paid is mandatory if other values do not exist, all following the HMRC PAYE internet submissions schema for 2020 to 2021.

sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for situations where the generate payment claim process in Core Expense fails to complete successfully, leaving expense trips showing as approved rather than processed into payment claims. sl: This document addresses a common issue that occurs when the "Generate Payment Claims" function fails to work properly during expense run processing in the Access Group system. The generate payment claims process is designed to automatically move all trips with an "approved" status to "processed" status while simultaneously creating a corresponding claim for each trip. When this function malfunctions, trips fail to move to the processed status and no claims are generated, indicating an underlying data quality problem with one or more trips in the expense run. Users encountering this issue should raise a support case and reference this article, providing the expense group identifier and run number to enable support analysts to investigate the logs and identify which specific trip contains the problematic data. The document assumes users are already in the process of running expense claims and have encountered this failure scenario, making it relevant for finance or payroll team members responsible for processing employee expenses. Related articles referenced suggest additional troubleshooting steps are available, including guidance on removing trips from claims and comparing expense run reports, though the primary resolution path involves contacting support for technical investigation of the underlying data issues.

ss: When an employee repays an advance outside the system, you need to clear the outstanding balance by entering a trip expense equal to the advance amount. sl: This document provides guidance on clearing down advances that have been repaid outside of the system in Access Group's expense management software. The core procedure involves entering a trip to match the value of the advance amount for the specific claimant, which allows the system to properly reconcile the external payment. When the expense run is subsequently executed, the system will process this entry so that no additional payment is issued to the claimant and the outstanding advance balance is automatically set to zero. The document is intended for finance teams, managers, or system administrators who manage employee advances and expense reimbursements and encounter situations where advances have been settled through manual or external payment methods rather than through standard system processes. By following this recommended procedure, users can maintain accurate advance tracking and prevent double payments or discrepancies in expense reporting. The document also references related issues such as mileage rate calculation problems, advance input during expense runs, payment status anomalies, and advances showing as outstanding despite being recouped, indicating it is part of a broader troubleshooting resource for expense management challenges.

The document is designed for back office users who need to correct or undo a validation step in the expense run workflow, particularly in scenarios where validation was completed prematurely or incorrectly.

To resolve the problem, users must manually run the Complete Cheque Update by going to Back Office, CoreExpense, Update, and selecting Complete Cheque Update. In this screen, users enter their Expense Group while the Cheque Date, Current Run Number, and New Run Number auto-populate; they should verify the Current Run Number is correct before clicking OK to complete the process. This document is intended for Back Office administrators and expense managers who need to troubleshoot expense claim status issues and ensure that all expense runs are fully processed through to completion.

sl: This document explains a common issue in the Access Group system where advance payments fail to link automatically to expense claims, specifically due to timing misalignment between when the advance was set up and when trip expenses were entered. The core problem occurs when an advance has a repayment date set in the future; in this scenario, any expenses that are entered before the advance's repayment date will not be applied to clear down the advance balance. Only expenses that are recorded on or after the future repayment date will be used to offset and reduce the outstanding advance amount. This document is intended for finance and expense management users who are troubleshooting why their advance payments are not automatically linking to submitted expense claims in the system. The guidance helps users understand the date-based logic governing advance reconciliation and provides context for resolving situations where advances remain uncleared despite expense submissions. t: Payments by company have a status of processed and not paid
s:
If an expense claim still shows as PROCESSED after the expense run it was included in has been finalized, this is because the claims are set as Payment by Company.
​
When claims are set to Payment by Company, it means that payment was made using a company credit card and the claimant will not be rei...
ss: Expense claims marked as "Payment by Company" remain stuck in PROCESSED status even after the expense run is finalized, because these claims represent company credit card payments with no reimbursement owed to the employee. When payment is made by company card, the claim value shows as 0.00 since no reimbursement is due, which prevents the system from recognizing a payment transaction. If all expense items on a claim are set to "Paid by Company," the entire claim stays PROCESSED; if only some items are company-paid, those individual line items remain at 0.00 while the overall claim can advance to PAID status. Open this document if your expense claims aren't progressing past PROCESSED status after finalization and you need to understand why company-paid expenses behave differently in the reimbursement workflow.
sl: This document explains why expense claims may remain stuck with a PROCESSED status even after their expense run has been finalized, specifically addressing the Payment by Company configuration in the expense claims system. When claims are set to Payment by Company, it indicates that expenses were charged to a company credit card rather than being reimbursed to the employee, which is why the system displays a claim value of 0.00 and does not progress the status beyond PROCESSED. The document clarifies that the system does not recognize a payment transaction when using Payment by Company because the claimant receives no reimbursement, causing the status to remain unchanged after the expense run completes. It distinguishes between two scenarios: if all expense items on a report are marked as Paid by Company, the entire claim status will not advance past PROCESSED, whereas if only some items are marked Paid by Company while others are set for reimbursement, only those specific line items will show as 0 and the overall trip status will progress to PAID. This documentation is intended for employees or finance administrators who manage expense claims and encounter unexpectedly stalled claim statuses, helping them understand the relationship between the Payment by Company setting and status progression within the expense management system. The document references the broader Expense run process as related material for additional context on how expenses are processed and finalized.

t: SQL Training Guide — Oracle SQL Developer for HR Systems
s: A comprehensive reference guide for querying PeopleXD using Oracle SQL Developer. Covers SELECT statements, WHERE clauses, JOINs, aggregation, and Oxford HR-specific context. Suitable for beginners and as an ongoing reference.

t: HOW TO — Add a Pay Code to the HR Report Suite SQL
s: Step-by-step guide for adding a new pay code to the hard-coded pay code filter in the HR Report Suite .RDL files using Visual Studio 2017 via CONNECT Remote Services. Covers the full process from OSM Change Request through to LIVE deployment and sign-off.

t: HOW TO — Raise a Change Request for HR Reporting (OSM)
s: Guide to raising OSM Change Requests for HR Reporting SQL and report file changes at the University of Oxford. Covers the 14-section CR format, key fields, the CR template location, and how the OSM Change ID links back to the report files.

t: HOW TO: Create a Non-Payroll Company & Link the Org Hierarchy — Colleges & Halls UOXU
s: Step-by-step guide for setting up a non-payroll organisation structure in PeopleXD (UOXU, Company 90) for Colleges & Halls. Covers creating the company, pay group, hierarchy reference data, Pay Administered By codes, and linking the hierarchy. Status: draft — some screenshots pending live UOXU configuration.
